(C) The homeowner has not availed himself or herself of the exemption in this paragraph on more than two structures more than once during any three-year period.
rules.notes: The 'more than two structures more than once during any three-year period' wording is ambiguous; confirm interpretation before hard-coding.

rules.title: Nonprofit assisting mutual self-help owner-builders exempt
rules.plain_english: A nonprofit corporation helping an owner-builder who participates in a mutual self-help housing program is exempt.

parameters.exempt: nonprofit corporation providing assistance to an owner-builder (HSC 50692(a))

rules.applies_to: Affordable housing nonprofits
rules.quote: A nonprofit corporation providing assistance to an owner-builder, as defined in subdivision (a) of Section 50692 of the Health and Safety Code, who is participating in a mutual self-help housing program, as defined in Section 50078 of the Health and Safety Code.

rules.title: Owner-builder sale within 1 year presumed built for sale
rules.plain_english: If an owner-builder sells or offers to sell a structure within one year after completion, the law presumes it was built for sale (the owner can try to rebut this). Selling or offering five or more structures within one year after completion is conclusive proof they were built for sale.

parameters.presumption: structure undertaken for purposes of sale (defeats 7044 exemptions that require no sale intent)

rules.applies_to: Owner-builders selling completed structures
rules.quote: proof of the sale or offering for sale of a structure by or for the owner-builder within one year after completion of the structure constitutes a rebuttable presumption affecting the burden of proof that the structure was undertaken for purposes of sale.
rules.notes: Conclusive presumption text: 'Proof of the sale or offering for sale of five or more structures by the owner-builder within one year after completion constitutes a conclusive presumption that the structures were undertaken for purposes of sale.'

rules.title: Injunctions against unlicensed, non-exempt owner-builders
rules.plain_english: Licensed contractors, contractor associations, labor organizations, affected consumers, district attorneys or the Attorney General can sue for an injunction against an owner-builder who is neither licensed nor exempt, without proving irreparable injury. The prevailing party (plaintiff or defendant) gets attorney's fees and costs.

parameters.defendant: owner-builder who is neither licensed nor exempt
parameters.attorney_fees: prevailing party (plaintiff or defendant) recovers attorney's fees and all costs

rules.applies_to: Owner-builders; competing contractors
rules.quote: any licensed contractor or association of contractors, labor organization, consumer affected by the violation, district attorney, or the Attorney General shall be entitled to seek injunctive relief prohibiting any violation of this chapter by an owner-builder who is neither licensed nor exempted from licensure under this chapter.
rules.notes: Two-way fee shifting creates risk for plaintiffs who lose.

rules.title: Real estate licensees exempt only within real estate scope
rules.plain_english: Real estate licensees acting within their real estate license are exempt, but neither a real estate licensee nor a property manager may act as a contractor without a CSLB license.

parameters.exempt: real estate licensee acting within course and scope of license (B&P 10000 et seq.)
not_authorized_without_cslb_license: real estate licensee acting as contractor

rules.applies_to: Real estate agents/brokers and property managers
rules.quote: However, nothing in this section shall authorize a real estate licensee or a property manager to act in the capacity of a contractor unless licensed by the board.
rules.notes: Property managers arranging and overseeing repairs should check B&P 7026.1(a)(2) consultant rules too.

rules.title: Surety completing a bonded contract is exempt
rules.plain_english: An admitted surety insurer that hires a contractor to complete a contract it bonded (performance or completion bond) is exempt, as long as all actual construction is done by licensed contractors.

parameters.condition_1: surety engages a contractor to complete a contract on which it issued a performance or completion bond
parameters.condition_2: all actual construction work performed by duly licensed contractors

rules.applies_to: Sureties and completion contractors; owners after contractor default
rules.quote: This chapter does not apply to an admitted surety insurer whenever that surety insurer engages a contractor to undertake the completion of a contract on which a performance or completion bond was issued by the surety insurer, provided all actual construction work is performed by duly licensed contractors.

rules.title: Finished products not fixed to structure; non-installing suppliers exempt
rules.plain_english: Selling or installing finished products that do not become a fixed part of the structure is exempt, as are suppliers/manufacturers that do not install or contract to install. But installed carpets, mobilehomes and mobilehome accessory structures are not 'finished products', and installing home improvement goods is covered by the license law.

exempt: sale or installation of finished products, materials, or merchandise that do not become a fixed part of the structure
material supplier or manufacturer who does not install or contract for installation

rules.applies_to: Suppliers, manufacturers, retailers offering installation
rules.quote: This chapter does not apply to the sale or installation of any finished products, materials, or articles of merchandise that do not become a fixed part of the structure, nor shall it apply to a material supplier or manufacturer furnishing finished products, materials, or articles of merchandise who does not install or contract for the installation of those items.
rules.notes: Second paragraph: 'This chapter shall apply to the installation of home improvement goods, as defined in Section 7151.'

rules.title: Personal property work exempt (not mobilehomes)
rules.plain_english: Work on personal property is exempt, but mobilehomes and mobilehome accessory structures are not treated as personal property for this exemption.

parameters.exempt: construction, alteration, improvement, or repair of personal property

rules.applies_to: Persons working on movable property
rules.quote: This chapter does not apply to any construction, alteration, improvement, or repair of personal property. The term “personal property” shall not include mobilehomes or mobilehome accessory structures as defined in Section 7026.2.

rules.title: Minor work exemption: under $1,000 total and no building permit
rules.plain_english: No license is needed for casual, minor work on one project if the total price of all contracts for labor, materials and everything else is under $1,000 and the work does not require a building permit.

parameters.aggregation: all contracts on one undertaking or project
parameters.test: aggregate_price < 1000 AND NOT permit_required AND NOT part_of_larger_operation AND NOT split_to_evade AND NOT advertises_as_contractor AND NOT employs_others

rules.applies_to: Handypersons and owners hiring for small jobs
rules.quote: This chapter does not apply to a work or operation on one undertaking or project by one or more contracts if the aggregate contract price for labor, materials, and all other items is less than one thousand dollars ($1,000), that work or operation being considered of casual, minor, or inconsequential nature, and the work or operation does not require a building permit.
rules.effective: January 1, 2025 (Stats 2024 ch 240, AB 2622); further amended effective January 1, 2026 (Stats 2025 ch 67, AB 1170)
rules.notes: Strictly less than $1,000; $1,000.00 exactly requires a license. Previous threshold ($500) is not stated in this text.

rules.title: Minor work exemption: no splitting or parts of larger jobs
rules.plain_english: The under-$1,000 exemption does not apply if the work is part of a larger operation (by the same or a different contractor), or if the job is broken into contracts under $1,000 to evade the law or otherwise.

disqualifiers: work is only part of a larger or major operation, whether by same or different contractor
operation divided into contracts under $1,000 for purpose of evasion or otherwise

rules.applies_to: Unlicensed persons relying on the minor-work exemption; owners hiring them
rules.quote: This section does not apply in a case wherein the work of construction is only a part of a larger or major operation, whether undertaken by the same or a different contractor, or in which a division of the operation is made in contracts of amounts less than one thousand dollars ($1,000) for the purpose of evasion of this chapter or otherwise.
rules.notes: Tool check: sum all contracts/invoices with the same person on the same project; flag multiple sub-$1,000 contracts.

rules.title: Minor work exemption lost if you advertise as contractor or employ others
rules.plain_english: The under-$1,000 exemption does not apply to anyone who advertises or uses signs/cards suggesting they are a contractor or qualified to be one, or who employs anyone else to do or help with the work.

disqualifiers: advertises or puts out sign, card or device indicating the person is a contractor or qualified to engage in contracting
employs another person to perform or assist in performing the work

rules.applies_to: Unlicensed handypersons
rules.quote: This section does not apply to a person who does either of the following: (1) Advertises or puts out a sign or card or other device that might indicate to the public that the person is a contractor or that the person is qualified to engage in the business of a contractor. (2) Employs another person to perform, or assist in performing, the work or operation.
rules.notes: Compare B&P 7027.2 (unlicensed ads for <$1,000 work allowed only with a 'not licensed' statement).

rules.title: Agricultural, district ditch and rural fire-prevention work exempt
rules.plain_english: Work incidental to building/repairing irrigation and drainage ditches of irrigation or reclamation districts, farming, dairying, agriculture, viticulture, horticulture, livestock or poultry raising, and rural land clearing for fire prevention is exempt, except when done by a licensee. Water well work is not exempt.

exempt_activities: construction/repair of irrigation and drainage ditches of regularly constituted irrigation or reclamation districts
clearing or other work on land in rural districts for fire prevention
parameters.exemption_lost_if: performed by a licensee under the chapter
parameters.not_exempt: water well drilling, digging, boring, constructing, deepening, repairing, reperforating, or abandoning

rules.applies_to: Farmers, ranchers, rural landowners, districts
rules.quote: This chapter does not apply to any construction or operation incidental to the construction and repair of irrigation and drainage ditches of regularly constituted irrigation districts, reclamation districts, or to farming, dairying, agriculture, viticulture, horticulture, or stock or poultry raising
rules.notes: Text: '... or clearing or other work upon the land in rural districts for fire prevention purposes, except when performed by a licensee under this chapter.'

rules.title: Mural artists exempt (not painted wall signs)
rules.plain_english: An artist who draws, paints, applies, executes, restores or conserves a mural under an agreement with someone who can legally authorize it does not need a contractor's license. A 'mural' is a unique hand-made work of fine art directly on walls, ceilings or fixtures; painted wall signs are not murals.

parameters.exempt: artist who draws, paints, applies, executes, restores, or conserves a mural
parameters.condition: agreement with a person who could legally authorize the work
parameters.mural_definition: unique work of fine art protected by copyright, trademark, label, or patent, drawn or painted by hand directly onto interior or exterior walls, ceilings, fixtures, or other appurtenances

rules.applies_to: Mural artists; owners commissioning murals
rules.quote: This chapter does not apply to an artist who draws, paints, applies, executes, restores, or conserves a mural pursuant to an agreement with a person who could legally authorize the work.
rules.notes: Painted wall signs remain covered (e.g., sign/painting classifications).

rules.title: Architects, engineers, pest control operators, geologists exempt within practice
rules.plain_english: Licensed architects and registered civil/professional engineers acting solely in their professional capacity, licensed structural pest control operators within their license, and licensees under the Geologist and Geophysicist Act within its scope are exempt.
rules.applies_to: Design professionals and pest control operators
rules.quote: This chapter does not apply to a licensed architect or a registered civil or professional engineer acting solely in his or her professional capacity or to a licensed structural pest control operator acting within the scope of his or her license or a licensee operating within the scope of the Geologist and Geophysicist Act.
rules.notes: Design-build or construction management beyond professional services may require a CSLB license.

rules.title: Material suppliers who don't install are exempt
rules.plain_english: A person who only furnishes materials or supplies, without fabricating them into or consuming them in the contractor's work, is exempt.

parameters.exempt: person who only furnishes materials or supplies
parameters.condition: does not fabricate them into, or consume them in the performance of, the work

rules.applies_to: Material suppliers
rules.quote: This chapter does not apply to any person who only furnishes materials or supplies without fabricating them into, or consuming them in the performance of, the work of the contractor.

rules.title: Wage employees exempt (3-part test)
rules.plain_english: A worker is exempt as an employee only if they are paid wages as their sole compensation, do not customarily run an independent business, and have no right to control how the work is done to determine its final results. This exemption does not apply to home improvement salespersons (Article 10).

conditions_all: does not customarily engage in an independently established business
does not have right to control or discretion as to manner of performance so as to determine final results
parameters.not_applicable_to: Article 10 (B&P 7150 et seq.) home improvement business, e.g., salespersons

rules.applies_to: Contractors classifying workers; owners using workers directly
rules.quote: Except as provided in Article 10 (commencing with Section 7150), this chapter does not apply to any person who engages in the activities herein regulated as an employee who receives wages as his or her sole compensation, does not customarily engage in an independently established business, and does not have the right to control or discretion as to the manner of performance
rules.notes: Workers paid by the job/1099 who control the means of work are likely 'contractors' needing a license. Labor Code worker-classification tests are separate.

rules.title: Licensed alarm company operators exempt for alarm work
rules.plain_english: A person holding an alarm company operator's license (B&P 7590 et seq.) is exempt for installing, maintaining, monitoring, selling, altering or servicing alarm systems.

parameters.exempt: holder of alarm company operator's license (B&P Chapter 11.6)
parameters.of: alarm systems as defined in B&P 7590.1

rules.applies_to: Alarm companies
rules.quote: This chapter does not apply to any person who performs work in the installation, maintenance, monitoring, selling, alteration, or servicing of alarm systems, as defined in Section 7590.1, and who holds an alarm company operator’s license issued pursuant to Chapter 11.6 (commencing with Section 7590).

rules.title: Registered satellite antenna installers exempt (residential)
rules.plain_english: A person registered under B&P Chapter 20 whose only activity is installing satellite antenna systems on residential structures or property is exempt from the licensing provisions.

parameters.exempt: person registered under B&P Chapter 20 (commencing with 9800)
parameters.condition: activities consist only of installing satellite antenna systems

rules.applies_to: Satellite antenna installers
rules.quote: The licensing provisions of this chapter do not apply to any person registered under Chapter 20 (commencing with Section 9800) if that person’s activities consist only of installing satellite antenna systems on residential structures or property.

rules.title: Three branches of contracting (A, B/B-2, C)
rules.plain_english: For licensing classification, contracting is divided into general engineering contracting (A), general building contracting (B), residential remodeling contracting, and specialty contracting (C).
rules.applies_to: All contractors and owners choosing a contractor
rules.quote: For the purpose of classification, the contracting business includes any or all of the following branches: (a) General engineering contracting. (b) (1) General building contracting. (2) Residential remodeling contracting. (c) Specialty contracting.
rules.notes: Letter codes A, B, B-2 and C are not printed in this section; residential remodeling is defined in B&P 7057.5 (outside this chunk).

rules.title: General engineering (A) contractor scope
rules.plain_english: A general engineering contractor's main business is fixed works requiring specialized engineering knowledge, such as irrigation, water supply, flood control, harbors, dams, railroads, highways, streets, tunnels, airports, sewers, bridges, pipelines, parks, refineries and plants, power plants, mines, earthmoving, excavating, grading, trenching, paving and related concrete work.

parameters.principal_business: fixed works requiring specialized engineering knowledge and skill
listed_works: levees, river control and reclamation works
sewers and sewage disposal plants and systems
bridges, overpasses, underpasses and similar works
pipelines for petroleum and other liquid or gaseous substances
parks, playgrounds and other recreational works
refineries, chemical plants and similar industrial plants
powerhouses, powerplants and other utility plants and installations
excavating, grading, trenching, paving and surfacing work
cement and concrete works in connection with the above

rules.applies_to: A-licensed contractors; owners of infrastructure projects
rules.quote: A general engineering contractor is a contractor whose principal contracting business is in connection with fixed works requiring specialized engineering knowledge and skill, including the following divisions or subjects:
rules.notes: Letter code 'A' not printed in this section.

rules.title: General building (B) contractor: two unrelated trades
rules.plain_english: A general building contractor's main business is structures for sheltering people, animals or property that require at least two unrelated building trades or crafts, or supervising all or part of such work. Someone who only supplies materials is not a general building contractor.

parameters.structure_purpose: support, shelter, and enclosure of persons, animals, chattels, or movable property
parameters.includes: doing or superintending the whole or any part thereof
parameters.excludes: material suppliers under B&P 7045 who do not fabricate or consume materials in the work

rules.applies_to: B-licensed contractors and owners hiring GCs
rules.quote: a general building contractor is a contractor whose principal contracting business is in connection with any structure built, being built, or to be built, for the support, shelter, and enclosure of persons, animals, chattels, or movable property of any kind, requiring in its construction the use of at least two unrelated building trades or crafts
rules.notes: Section 7057 appears on PDF page 271, just past the nominal end of this chunk.

rules.title: B contractor prime/sub limits: two unrelated trades besides framing/carpentry
rules.plain_english: A B contractor may take any framing or carpentry job. For other trades, a B may take a prime contract only if the job requires at least two unrelated trades other than framing/carpentry, or the B holds the specialty license, or subcontracts that work to a properly licensed contractor. A B may take a subcontract for other trades only if it requires two unrelated trades other than framing/carpentry, or the B holds the specialty license. Framing/carpentry never counts toward the two trades.

prime_contract_other_trades_allowed_if_a: requires >= 2 unrelated building trades or crafts other than framing or carpentry
B holds the appropriate specialty classification
B subcontracts with an appropriately licensed contractor to perform the work
subcontract_other_trades_allowed_if_any: requires >= 2 unrelated trades or crafts other than framing or carpentry
B holds the appropriate specialty classification

rules.applies_to: B general building contractors; owners and GCs awarding work to B contractors
rules.quote: a general building contractor shall not take a prime contract for any project involving trades other than framing or carpentry unless the prime contract requires at least two unrelated building trades or crafts other than framing or carpentry, or unless the general building contractor holds the appropriate license classification or subcontracts with an appropriately licensed contractor
rules.notes: Tool check: count distinct unrelated trades in scope excluding framing/carpentry; if < 2, B needs matching C classification (prime: or a licensed sub; subcontract: own classification only).

rules.title: B contractor: fire protection and well drilling need license or sub
rules.plain_english: A B general building contractor may not contract for a project that includes a fire protection system or C-57 well drilling unless it holds that classification or subcontracts the work to a properly licensed contractor.

allowed_if_any: B subcontracts with the appropriately licensed contractor

rules.applies_to: B general building contractors
rules.quote: A general building contractor shall not contract for any project that includes a fire protection system as provided for in Section 7026.12 or 7026.13, or the “C-57” Well Drilling classification as provided for in Section 13750.5 of the Water Code, unless the general building contractor holds the appropriate license classification, or subcontracts with the appropriately licensed contractor.
rules.notes: Applies even when the project otherwise meets the two-unrelated-trades test.

rules.title: Satellite antenna installers registered under B&P 9800 exempt
rules.plain_english: A person registered under the electronic and appliance repair dealer law (B&P 9800 et seq.) does not need a contractor license if all they do is install satellite antenna systems on homes or residential property.

parameters.exempt_activity: installing satellite antenna systems on residential structures or property only

rules.applies_to: Satellite antenna installers working on residential property
rules.quote: The licensing provisions of this chapter do not apply to any person registered under Chapter 20 (commencing with Section 9800) if that person’s activities consist only of installing satellite antenna systems on residential structures or property.
rules.notes: Exemption is lost if the person does any other construction work. Commercial structures are not covered.

rules.title: Four branches of contracting: A, B, B-2, C
rules.plain_english: For licensing, California contracting is split into general engineering (A), general building (B), residential remodeling (B-2) and specialty (C) contracting. Every license classification falls into one of these branches.
rules.applies_to: All contractors and license applicants
rules.quote: For the purpose of classification, the contracting business includes any or all of the following branches: (a) General engineering contracting. (b) (1) General building contracting. (2) Residential remodeling contracting. (c) Specialty contracting.
rules.notes: The B-2 code appears in 7057.5(d). The letter codes A, B and C are standard CSLB usage from the regulations (16 CCR), not stated in this section.

rules.title: General engineering contractor (A) scope
rules.plain_english: A general engineering contractor's main business is fixed works that need specialized engineering knowledge, such as roads, bridges, pipelines, sewers, dams, utilities, grading, paving and related concrete work.

fixed_works_examples: sewers and sewage disposal plants and systems
bridges, overpasses, underpasses and similar works
pipelines for petroleum and other liquid or gaseous substances
parks, playgrounds and other recreational works
refineries, chemical plants and similar industrial plants
powerhouses, powerplants and other utility plants and installations
excavating, grading, trenching, paving and surfacing
cement and concrete works in connection with the above fixed works

rules.applies_to: Contractors holding or seeking the A classification; owners choosing a contractor for engineering works
rules.quote: A general engineering contractor is a contractor whose principal contracting business is in connection with fixed works requiring specialized engineering knowledge and skill, including the following divisions or subjects: irrigation, drainage, water power, water supply, flood control, inland waterways, harbors, docks and wharves, shipyards and ports, dams and hydroelectric projects
rules.notes: Excavating, grading, trenching, paving and concrete fall in A scope only when connected with the listed fixed works.

rules.title: General building contractor (B) definition: two or more unrelated trades
rules.plain_english: A general building contractor builds or superintends structures for sheltering people, animals or property, where the work uses at least two unrelated building trades. Someone who only supplies materials without installing them is not a B contractor.

parameters.structure_purpose: support, shelter, and enclosure of persons, animals, chattels, or movable property
parameters.excludes: material suppliers under B&P 7045 who do not fabricate or install the materials

rules.applies_to: B license holders and applicants
rules.quote: a general building contractor is a contractor whose principal contracting business is in connection with any structure built, being built, or to be built, for the support, shelter, and enclosure of persons, animals, chattels, or movable property of any kind, requiring in its construction the use of at least two unrelated building trades or crafts,

rules.title: B contractor prime contracts need 2+ unrelated trades besides framing/carpentry
rules.plain_english: A B contractor may take a prime contract for framing or carpentry alone. For any other prime contract, the job must involve at least two unrelated trades other than framing and carpentry, unless the B contractor holds the specialty license for the work or subcontracts it to a properly licensed contractor.

alternatives_if_below_minimum: B contractor holds the appropriate specialty classification
B contractor subcontracts the work to an appropriately licensed contractor

rules.applies_to: B general building contractors taking prime contracts
rules.quote: a general building contractor shall not take a prime contract for any project involving trades other than framing or carpentry unless the prime contract requires at least two unrelated building trades or crafts other than framing or carpentry, or unless the general building contractor holds the appropriate license classification or subcontracts with an appropriately licensed contractor
rules.notes: Check: count distinct unrelated trades in the contract scope, excluding framing and carpentry; if fewer than 2, require a matching specialty license or a licensed subcontractor for each trade.

rules.title: B contractor subcontracts need 2+ unrelated trades or the specialty license
rules.plain_english: A B contractor may take a subcontract for framing or carpentry. For any other subcontract, the subcontract must involve at least two unrelated trades other than framing and carpentry, or the B contractor must hold the specialty license itself. Sub-subcontracting does not cure this.

alternatives_if_below_minimum: B contractor holds the appropriate specialty classification

rules.applies_to: B general building contractors taking subcontracts
rules.quote: A general building contractor shall not take a subcontract involving trades other than framing or carpentry, unless the subcontract requires at least two unrelated trades or crafts other than framing or carpentry, or unless the general building contractor holds the appropriate license classification.
rules.notes: Unlike the prime-contract rule, the subcontract rule offers no option to pass the work to another licensed subcontractor.

rules.title: B contractor may not contract fire protection or C-57 well drilling without license or licensed sub
rules.plain_english: A B contractor cannot contract for a project that includes a fire protection system or C-57 well drilling unless it holds that classification or subcontracts that work to a contractor who does.
rules.applies_to: B general building contractors
rules.quote: A general building contractor shall not contract for any project that includes a fire protection system as provided for in Section 7026.12 or 7026.13, or the “C-57” Well Drilling classification as provided for in Section 13750.5 of the Water Code, unless the general building contractor holds the appropriate license classification, or subcontracts with the appropriately licensed contractor.
rules.notes: Fire protection work is normally C-16.

rules.title: B-2 residential remodeling contractor scope
rules.plain_english: A B-2 contractor improves existing wood-frame homes on jobs that use at least three unrelated trades in one contract, such as drywall, flooring, painting, tile, siding, roof repair, or replacing electrical, plumbing and mechanical fixtures. The B-2 may do the work itself or subcontract any trade to licensed subs.

example_trades: installing/repairing/replacing electrical fixtures (dimmers, fans, lights, outlets, switches)
installing/repairing/replacing plumbing fixtures (faucets, sinks, toilets, tubs)
installing/repairing/replacing mechanical fixtures (air filters, air delivery and return grills, preassembled exhaust fans)

rules.applies_to: B-2 license holders and applicants; homeowners hiring remodelers
rules.quote: A residential remodeling contractor is a contractor whose principal contracting business is in connection with any project to make improvements to, on, or in an existing residential wood frame structure, and the project requires the use of at least three unrelated building trades or crafts for a single contract.
rules.notes: New construction and non-wood-frame structures are outside B-2 scope. The trade list is non-exhaustive ('may include, but is not limited to').

rules.title: B-2 contract must include three or more unrelated trades
rules.plain_english: A B-2 contractor may not take a contract unless it includes at least three unrelated trades.
rules.applies_to: B-2 residential remodeling contractors
rules.quote: A residential remodeling contractor shall not take a contract unless the contract includes three or more unrelated trades or crafts.
rules.notes: Check per contract, not per project.

rules.title: B-2 may not contract C-16, C-22 or C-57 work without license or licensed sub
rules.plain_english: A B-2 contractor cannot contract for a job that includes fire protection (C-16), asbestos abatement (C-22) or well drilling (C-57) unless it holds that license or subcontracts that work to a contractor who does.
rules.applies_to: B-2 residential remodeling contractors
rules.quote: A residential remodeling contractor shall not contract for a project that includes the following trades or crafts unless the contractor holds the appropriate license classification or subcontracts with an appropriately licensed contractor: (A) C-16 Fire Protection. (B) C-22 Asbestos Abatement. (C) C-57 Well Drilling.

rules.title: B-2 may not contract structural changes to load-bearing elements
rules.plain_english: A B-2 contractor cannot contract to make structural changes to load-bearing parts of an existing building, such as footings, foundations, bearing walls, partitions or roof structures. Unlike the other B-2 limits, there is no subcontracting exception.
rules.applies_to: B-2 residential remodeling contractors
rules.quote: A residential remodeling contractor shall not contract to make structural changes to load bearing portions of an existing structure, including, but not limited to, footings, foundations, load bearing walls, partitions, and roof structures.
rules.notes: A job that needs load-bearing structural work requires a B (or other suitable) license, not a B-2.

rules.title: B-2 limits on electrical, mechanical and plumbing systems
rules.plain_english: A B-2 contractor cannot contract to install, replace, substantially alter or extend electrical, mechanical or plumbing systems unless it holds the license or subcontracts to a licensed contractor. It may make minor alterations to existing systems to install, repair or replace fixtures, as long as the contract uses at least three unrelated trades.

parameters.restricted_work: install, replace, substantially alter, or extend electrical, mechanical, or plumbing systems or their component parts

minor_alteration_exception.purpose: installing, repairing, or replacing electrical, mechanical and plumbing fixtures

rules.applies_to: B-2 residential remodeling contractors
rules.quote: The residential remodeling contractor shall not contract to install, replace, substantially alter, or extend electrical, mechanical, or plumbing systems or their component parts, or the mechanisms or devices that are part of those systems, unless the residential remodeling contractor holds the appropriate license classification or subcontracts with an appropriately licensed contractor.
rules.notes: CSLB may further define 'minor alterations' by regulation (7057.5(c)(3)(C)); check current 16 CCR for the definition.

rules.title: Specialty contractor (C) definition
rules.plain_english: A specialty contractor does construction work in a specialized trade. Specialty work includes servicing or testing fire extinguishing systems, laying carpet and resilient flooring, and setting up or removing roadway work zones, lane closures, flagging and traffic diversions.

included_operations: servicing or testing fire extinguishing systems
installation and laying of carpets, linoleum, and resilient floor covering
preparing or removing roadway construction zones, lane closures, flagging, or traffic diversions on roadways, including public streets, highways, or any public conveyance

rules.applies_to: C license holders and applicants
rules.quote: A specialty contractor is a contractor whose operations involve the performance of construction work requiring special skill and whose principal contracting business involves the use of specialized building trades or crafts.
rules.notes: Traffic control and flagging companies need a contractor license under 7058(d).

rules.title: Asbestos work of 100 sq ft or more needs C-22 or asbestos certification
rules.plain_english: A contractor may not do asbestos-related work involving 100 square feet or more of asbestos-containing material unless it holds the C-22 Asbestos Abatement license or its qualifier has passed the asbestos certification exam. Installing, maintaining or repairing asbestos cement pipe or sheets, vinyl asbestos flooring, or asbestos bituminous or resinous materials does not require the certification exam.

parameters.measure: surface area of asbestos containing materials

rules.applies_to: Any contractor disturbing asbestos-containing materials
rules.quote: A contractor shall not engage in asbestos-related work, as defined in Section 6501.8 of the Labor Code, that involves 100 square feet or more of surface area of asbestos containing materials, unless the contractor holds a C-22 Asbestos Abatement classification or the qualifier for the license passes an asbestos certification examination.
rules.notes: CSLB may require updated asbestos certification exams based on new health and safety information. DOSH registration is also required (see asbestos-cert-dosh-registration-90-days).

rules.title: All initial license applicants must complete the asbestos open-book exam
rules.plain_english: Every applicant for an initial contractor license must complete CSLB's open-book asbestos exam and submit it before the license is issued.

parameters.who: all applicants for an initial contractor license
parameters.due: prior to issuance of the license

rules.applies_to: All initial license applicants
rules.quote: All applicants for an initial contractor license shall complete the open book examination and, prior to the issuance of a contractor’s license, submit it to the board electronically or by mail if the applicant elects to use the hard-copy format.
rules.notes: This is separate from the asbestos certification exam for 100+ sq ft work.

rules.title: Register with Cal/OSHA (DOSH) within 90 days of passing asbestos certification
rules.plain_english: After passing the asbestos certification exam, the contractor must register with the Division of Occupational Safety and Health within 90 days of being notified. If it misses the deadline, CSLB may require it to retake the exam and pay the test fees again.

parameters.trigger: date contractor is notified of passing the asbestos certification exam
parameters.agency: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Labor Code 6501.5)
parameters.consequence_if_missed: board may require reexamination; test fees apply
parameters.exception: certification may issue without DOSH registration if contractor states in writing it does not perform asbestos-related work

rules.applies_to: Contractors obtaining asbestos certification
rules.quote: The contractor shall register with the division within 90 days from the date the contractor is notified of the passage of the certification examination. The board may require a reexamination if the contractor fails to register within 90 days following issuance of the notification.

rules.title: Show current DOSH asbestos registration at license renewal
rules.plain_english: A contractor certified for asbestos work that actually does asbestos-related work must show proof of current DOSH registration when it renews its contractor license.

parameters.document: proof of current DOSH asbestos registration (Labor Code 6501.5)
parameters.condition: contractor is asbestos-certified and engages in asbestos-related work

rules.applies_to: Asbestos-certified contractors performing asbestos-related work
rules.quote: Any contractor who is certified to engage in asbestos-related work shall present proof of current registration with the division pursuant to Section 6501.5 of the Labor Code upon application for renewal of the contractor’s license, if the contractor engages in asbestos-related work, as defined in Section 6501.8 of the Labor Code.

rules.title: Non-certified contractor may bid asbestos projects if a qualified contractor does the asbestos work
rules.plain_english: A contractor without asbestos certification can still bid on and contract for a project that includes asbestos work, as long as the asbestos work itself is done by a C-22 contractor or a contractor that is certified and registered with DOSH.

parameters.condition: asbestos-related work performed by a C-22 holder or a certified and DOSH-registered contractor

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors on projects with asbestos-related work
rules.quote: A contractor who is not certified pursuant to this section may bid on and contract to perform a project involving asbestos-related work as long as the asbestos-related work is performed by a contractor who holds the C-22 Asbestos Abatement classification or is certified and registered pursuant to this section and Section 6501.5 of the Labor Code.
rules.notes: The book also cross-references H&S Code 25914-25914.3 (separate asbestos/hazardous removal contracts), which are in the Appendix and not covered here.

rules.title: Hazardous substance removal or remedial action needs HAZ certification
rules.plain_english: A contractor may not do a hazardous substance removal or remedial action unless its qualifier has passed the hazardous substance certification exam. The rule covers digging into the earth and removing the dug material at a listed state (DTSC) or federal Superfund (NPL) site, but not asbestos work or highway spill cleanup.

parameters.required: qualifier passed approved hazardous substance certification examination
parameters.covered_activity: removal or remedial action (H&S Code 78000 et seq.) requiring digging into the surface of the earth and removing dug material
covered_sites: site listed under H&S Code 78760 et seq.
excluded: hazardous substance spill on a highway

rules.applies_to: Contractors doing excavation and removal at listed hazardous substance sites
rules.quote: No contractor may engage in a removal or remedial action, as defined in subdivision (d), unless the qualifier for the license has passed an approved hazardous substance certification examination.
rules.notes: CSLB may require updated certification exams of current certificate holders.

rules.title: Installing or removing underground storage tanks needs HAZ certification
rules.plain_english: A contractor may not install or remove an underground storage tank unless it has passed the hazardous substance certification exam. A non-certified contractor may bid on or contract for the tank work if a certified contractor does it.

parameters.covered_activity: installation or removal of an underground storage tank (H&S Code 25281(y))
parameters.condition_for_noncertified: work performed by a certified contractor

rules.applies_to: Contractors installing or removing underground storage tanks
rules.quote: A contractor may not install or remove an underground storage tank, unless the contractor has passed the hazardous substance certification examination developed pursuant to this section. (2) A contractor who is not certified may bid on or contract for the installation or removal of an underground tank, if the work is performed by a contractor who is certified pursuant to this section.
rules.effective: Amended by Stats 2022 ch 258 (AB 2327), effective January 1, 2023; book history line reads 'operative effective 1/1/2024'

rules.title: Specialty contractors may do other trades only if incidental and supplemental
rules.plain_english: A specialty contractor may take a contract involving several trades, but work outside its own classification must be incidental and supplemental to the work in the trade it is licensed for.

parameters.out_of_class_work_allowed_if: incidental and supplemental to the licensed craft

rules.applies_to: C specialty contractors
rules.quote: Nothing contained in this section shall prohibit a specialty contractor from taking and executing a contract involving the use of two or more crafts or trades, if the performance of the work in the crafts or trades, other than in which they are licensed, is incidental and supplemental to the performance of the work in the craft for which the specialty contractor is licensed.
rules.notes: 'Incidental and supplemental' is defined further in CSLB regulations (16 CCR 831), not in this text. CSLB may limit a licensee's field and scope to its classifications.

rules.title: Additional classifications: application fee only, no extra license fee
rules.plain_english: A licensee may hold more than one classification if it qualifies for each. Adding a classification requires an application and the application fee, but there is no extra license fee for it.
rules.applies_to: Licensees adding classifications
rules.quote: The application shall be in a form as prescribed by the registrar and shall be accompanied by the application fee fixed by this chapter. No license fee shall be charged for an additional classification or classifications.
rules.notes: The fee amount is set in the fee article (B&P 7137), outside this chunk.

rules.title: Public works: specialty prime only if its class is a majority of the project
rules.plain_english: On public works, the awarding agency decides which license class is needed to bid and perform. It may never award a prime contract to a specialty contractor whose classification covers less than a majority of the project, and a specialty prime's work outside its class must go to licensed subcontractors under the Subletting and Subcontracting Fair Practices Act.

parameters.out_of_specialty_work: performed by licensed subcontractor per Public Contract Code 4100 et seq., except incidental and supplemental work under 7059(a)

rules.applies_to: Public agencies awarding contracts; specialty contractors bidding public works
rules.quote: In no case shall the awarding authority award a prime contract to a specialty contractor whose classification constitutes less than a majority of the project. When a specialty contractor is authorized to bid a project, all work to be performed outside of their license specialty, except work authorized by subdivision (a), shall be performed by a licensed subcontractor
rules.notes: The text does not say how to measure 'majority' (likely by contract value; not stated). Awarding authorities may not set their own contractor qualification regulations (7059(b)(2)).

rules.title: Business name must match classifications and entity type; one name per license
rules.plain_english: A licensee may not use a business name that implies classifications it does not hold or that does not fit its entity type (for example 'Inc.' on a sole owner license). It also may not do business under more than one name per license.
rules.applies_to: All licensees (advertising, contracts, letterhead, trucks)
rules.quote: A licensee shall not use any business name that indicates the licensee is qualified to perform work in classifications other than those issued for that license, or any business name that is incompatible with the type of business entity licensed. (b) A licensee shall not conduct business under more than one name for each license.
rules.notes: Name changes go through the CSLB change process (see notify-changes-90-days).

rules.title: Who can be licensed; officers and members must be listed as personnel of record
rules.plain_english: Licenses are issued to sole owners, partnerships, corporations, LLCs and participating tribes. Every officer, member, responsible manager or director of a corporation or LLC, and every partner of a partnership, must be listed on the application as personnel of record.
rules.applies_to: License applicants
rules.quote: Contractors’ licenses are to be issued to individual owners, partnerships, corporations, limited liability companies, and participating tribes, in accordance with this chapter. (A) Every person who is an officer, member, responsible manager, or director of a corporation or limited liability company seeking licensure under this chapter shall be listed on the application

rules.title: Corporations and LLCs must give their Secretary of State ID; tribal businesses must verify status
rules.plain_english: A corporation or LLC (domestic or foreign) applying for a license must give its California Secretary of State identification number. A tribal business must provide proof of its tribal status, such as a charter resolution, articles or bylaws, or a federal tribe listing.

tribal_verification_examples: enacted resolution ratifying charter under Section 17 of the Indian Reorganization Act
enacted resolution authorizing the tribally chartered corporation under tribal law
current federal list of recognized tribes or tribal leadership directory (25 U.S.C. 5131) or BIA website

rules.applies_to: Corporation, LLC and tribal business applicants
rules.quote: A corporation or limited liability company, whether foreign or domestic, seeking licensure under this chapter shall provide its identification number issued by the Secretary of State.

rules.title: Who may serve as qualifying individual for each entity type
rules.plain_english: Each license is qualified by a person who has the knowledge and experience. A sole owner qualifies personally or through an RME. A partnership uses a general partner or RME. A corporation or tribe uses an RMO or RME. An LLC uses an RMO, responsible managing manager, responsible managing member or RME.
rules.applies_to: All license applicants and licensees
rules.quote: If a corporation, or any other combination or organization, it shall qualify by the appearance of a responsible managing officer or responsible managing employee who is qualified for the same license classification as the classification being applied for.
rules.effective: Amended effective September 28, 2021 (AB 830); 7065 amended effective January 1, 2025

rules.title: No exam if qualifier passed or qualified in same class within prior 5 years
rules.plain_english: A qualifying individual does not have to retake the exam if, within the 5 years before applying, they passed the exam for the same classification or served as qualifier for a license in good standing in that classification.

parameters.measured_from: date of application
exempt_if_any: qualifier personally passed written exam for same classification
qualifier served as qualifying individual for a licensee in good standing in same classification at any time in the period

rules.applies_to: Qualifying individuals on new applications
rules.quote: No examination shall be required of a qualifying individual if, within the five-year period immediately preceding the application for licensure, the qualifying individual has either personally passed the written examination for the same classification being applied for, or has served as the qualifying individual for a licensee whose license was in good standing
rules.notes: Mandatory ('shall'), unlike the discretionary waivers in 7065.1.

rules.title: Limited specialty classification: no trade exam
rules.plain_english: Applicants for the limited specialty classification do not take a trade exam.
rules.applies_to: Limited specialty license applicants
rules.quote: Notwithstanding Section 7065, no trade examination shall be required of an applicant for the limited specialty license classification.
rules.notes: Only the trade exam is waived; the text does not waive the law and business exam. The limited specialty is the C-61 class under CSLB regulations (not stated here).

rules.title: Exam waiver: listed personnel of a licensee for 5 of the past 7 years
rules.plain_english: CSLB may waive the exam if the qualifier was listed as personnel of record of an active licensee in good standing in the same classification for 5 of the 7 years before applying, and the licensee was actively doing construction in that classification.

conditions: listed on CSLB records as personnel of a licensee
license active and in good standing
same classification applied for
licensee actively engaged in construction in that classification during the period

rules.applies_to: Qualifying individuals seeking an exam waiver
rules.quote: The qualifying individual has, for five of the seven years immediately preceding the application for licensure, been listed on the official records of the board as a member of the personnel of any licensee who held a license, which was active and in good standing, in the same classification being applied for,
rules.notes: Waiver is discretionary ('may waive').

rules.title: Exam waiver: family member continuing a family business
rules.plain_english: CSLB may waive the exam for an immediate family member of a licensee whose individual license was active and in good standing for 5 of the last 7 years, if the family member worked in the business for 5 of those 7 years, the license is needed to keep the family business going after the licensee's absence or death, and they apply in the same classifications.

conditions: immediate family member of an individual licensee
license needed to continue family business on absence or death of licensee
new license in same classifications

rules.applies_to: Family members of individual licensees
rules.quote: The qualifying individual has been actively engaged in the licensee’s business for five of the seven years immediately preceding the application for licensure. (2) The license is required to continue the existing family business in the event of the absence or death of the licensee.
rules.notes: 'Immediate family member' is defined for license-number reissuance in 7075.1(d); 7065.1 does not define it.

rules.title: Exam waiver: corporation/LLC employee replacing its qualifier
rules.plain_english: CSLB may waive the exam for a corporation or LLC employee (including officers and managers) who is replacing the company's qualifier, if the employee worked there in a supervisory role in the same classifications for 5 of the last 7 years, the company held an active license in good standing in those classifications for 5 of the last 7 years, and the company has not used this waiver in the past 5 years.
rules.applies_to: Corporations and LLCs replacing a qualifier
rules.quote: For five of the seven years immediately preceding the application for licensure, the qualifying individual has been continually employed by the corporation or limited liability company in a supervisory capacity in the same classifications being applied for.

rules.title: Exam waiver: former California licensee who contracted for the U.S. government
rules.plain_english: CSLB may waive the exam for an applicant who previously held a valid California contractor license and has been working as a contractor for the U.S. government in a license-exempt position.

conditions: previously held a valid California contractor license
acting as a contractor for the United States government in a license-exempt position

rules.applies_to: Former California licensees doing federal work
rules.quote: the registrar may waive the examination for a contractor’s license if the applicant has previously held a valid contractor’s license in this state and has been acting in the capacity of a contractor for the United States government in a position exempt from licensure under this chapter.

rules.title: Adding a classification without exam: 5 of 7 years plus 4 years of experience in last 10
rules.plain_english: A licensee can add a classification without an exam if its qualifier was listed as personnel of an active licensee in good standing for 5 of the last 7 years, and has at least 4 years of journeyman, foreman, supervisor or contractor experience in the new classification within the last 10 years. The new class must be closely related to existing classes, or the qualifier must be with an A or B contractor for whom the class is a significant part of the business.

relatedness_test: qualifier associated with licensed A or B contractor and class is a significant component of its business

rules.applies_to: Licensees adding a classification
rules.quote: The qualifying individual for the applicant has had within the last 10 years immediately preceding the filing of the application, not less than four years experience as a journeyman, foreman, supervising employee, or contractor in the classification within which the licensee intends to engage in the additional classification as a contractor.
rules.notes: Requires a 'conclusive showing' of experience satisfactory to the registrar. At least 3% of these applications get a full investigation.

rules.title: Reciprocity: trade exam waivable with 5 years good standing in a reciprocal state
rules.plain_english: CSLB may accept an out-of-state contractor's qualifications in a similar classification if that state gives California licensees the same treatment and has equal or stricter standards. The trade exam may be waived if the other state certifies in writing that the license has been in good standing for the previous 5 years.

parameters.document: written certification from the other state
conditions: licensed in similar classification in other state
other state reciprocates for California licensees
other state's standards at least equal (case-by-case)

rules.applies_to: Out-of-state licensed contractors applying in California
rules.quote: The registrar may waive the trade examination for that applicant if the applicant provides written certification from that other state in which he or she is licensed, that the applicant’s license has been in good standing for the previous five years.
rules.notes: Only the trade exam is mentioned; the law and business exam is not waived by this section.

rules.title: No license to or through a minor without a court-appointed guardian
rules.plain_english: A minor cannot be licensed, and no partnership, corporation, LLC or other business with a minor as a partner, officer, director, manager or RME can be licensed, unless a court has appointed a guardian for the minor.

applies_if_minor_is: holder of any responsible official position
parameters.exception: guardian appointed by court of competent jurisdiction

rules.applies_to: All applicants
rules.quote: No license shall be issued to a minor, nor to any partnership a partner of which is a minor, nor to any corporation any officer, director or responsible managing employee of which is a minor, nor to any limited liability company any officer, manager, or responsible managing employee of which is a minor

rules.title: Applications must be signed by applicant and qualifier; e-signatures allowed
rules.plain_english: Every original, renewal, reinstatement or reissuance application, active or inactive, must be on the CSLB form with the fee, and must be signed by both the applicant and the qualifying individual. CSLB may accept electronic filing and digital signatures.
rules.applies_to: All applicants and licensees
rules.quote: Every application form for an original license, for renewal thereof, for reinstatement or for reissuance, including both active and inactive licenses, shall be signed by both the applicant and by the person qualifying on behalf of an individual or firm as referred to in Section 7068.1.

rules.title: Applicants must show trade experience and knowledge of building, safety, health and lien laws
rules.plain_english: Applicants must show knowledge and experience in the classification and general knowledge of California building, safety, health and lien laws and contracting business principles. The written exam includes questions on state law and the contracting business, and an applicant qualifying through an RME must also show this law and business knowledge.

required_knowledge: trade knowledge and experience in classification

rules.applies_to: All license applicants
rules.quote: The board shall require an applicant to show the degree of knowledge and experience in the classification applied for, and the general knowledge of the building, safety, health, and lien laws of the state and of the administrative principles of the contracting business that the board deems necessary for the safety and protection of the public.
rules.notes: The years of experience needed are set by CSLB regulation (16 CCR 825), not in this text.

rules.title: RME must be a permanent employee working 32 hrs/week or 80% of business hours
rules.plain_english: A responsible managing employee must be a permanent, bona fide employee who is actively engaged in the work they qualify for. Actively engaged means working 32 hours a week, or 80% of the hours the business is open each week, whichever is less.

parameters.rule: required_hours = min(32, 0.80 * business_operating_hours_per_week)
parameters.employment_type: permanently employed by the applicant (bona fide employee)

rules.applies_to: Licensees qualified by a responsible managing employee (RME)
rules.quote: “Bona fide employee of the applicant” means an employee who is permanently employed by the applicant. (B) “Actively engaged” means working 32 hours per week, or 80 percent of the total hours per week that the applicant’s business is in operation, whichever is less.
rules.notes: Useful check for HR/payroll: RME timesheets should meet the computed minimum.

rules.title: Qualifier may not hold another active license (except under 7068.1)
rules.plain_english: A person serving as qualifier for a licensee may not hold any other active contractor license at the same time, except as allowed by the multiple-license rules in 7068.1.

parameters.exception: B&P 7068.1 (20% common ownership, subsidiary/joint venture, or same majority officers; max 3 firms per year)

rules.applies_to: Qualifying individuals
rules.quote: Except in accordance with Section 7068.1, no person qualifying on behalf of an individual or firm under paragraph (1), (2), (3), or (4) of subdivision (b) shall hold any other active contractor’s license while acting in the capacity of a qualifying individual pursuant to this section.

rules.title: Qualifier must file a statement verifying their role at each renewal
rules.plain_english: At every renewal, the current qualifying individual must file a CSLB form confirming they still serve as the licensee's qualifier.

parameters.document: statement on registrar form verifying capacity as qualifying individual

rules.applies_to: All licensees at renewal
rules.quote: At the time of application for renewal of a license, the current qualifying individual shall file a statement with the registrar, on a form prescribed by the registrar, verifying their capacity as a qualifying individual to the licensee.

rules.title: Experience claims must be verified by a qualified, responsible person
rules.plain_english: An applicant's claimed experience must be certified by a qualified and responsible person, and CSLB randomly audits a share of these statements. Experience gained in other states counts only if it was gained lawfully in that state.
rules.applies_to: All license applicants
rules.quote: Statements made by or on behalf of an applicant as to the applicant’s experience in the classification applied for shall be verified by a qualified and responsible person.
rules.notes: The audit percentage is set by regulation, not stated here. Unlicensed out-of-state work where a license was required may not count.

rules.title: Qualifier must exercise supervision and control of construction operations
rules.plain_english: The qualifying individual is responsible for supervising and controlling the company's construction work so it complies with the license law. That means supervising operations, making technical and administrative decisions, checking jobs for workmanship, or supervising job sites, or monitoring and being available to people they delegate to. Applicants must describe the qualifier's duties in detail.

parameters.supervision_and_control: direct supervision or control, or monitoring and being available to assist others to whom direct supervision and control has been delegated
direct_supervision_or_control_any_of: managing construction activities by making technical and administrative decisions
parameters.required_document: detailed information on qualifier duties and responsibilities (7068.1(d))

rules.applies_to: Qualifying individuals and the licensees they qualify
rules.quote: The person qualifying on behalf of an individual or firm under paragraph (1), (2), (3), or (4) of subdivision (b) of Section 7068 shall be responsible for exercising supervision and control of their employer’s or principal’s construction operations to secure compliance with this chapter and the rules and regulations of the board.
rules.notes: 'Firm' covers partnerships, limited partnerships, corporations, LLCs and other organizations.

rules.title: Qualifying more than one firm needs 20% common ownership, subsidiary/JV, or same majority officers
rules.plain_english: A qualifier may qualify an additional firm only if at least 20% of the equity of each firm is under common ownership, the additional firm is a subsidiary (at least 20% owned) or joint venture of the first, or a majority of the partners, officers or managers are the same.

allowed_if_any: at least 20% common ownership of equity of each firm
additional firm is a subsidiary (>=20% equity owned) or joint venture of the first
majority of partners, officers, or managers are the same

rules.applies_to: Qualifying individuals serving more than one licensee
rules.quote: There is a common ownership of at least 20 percent of the equity of each individual or firm for which the person acts in a qualifying capacity. (2) The additional firm is a subsidiary of or a joint venture with the first. “Subsidiary,” as used in this subdivision, means any firm at least 20 percent of the equity of which is owned by the other firm.
rules.notes: Changes to this multiple-license exemption must be reported to CSLB within 90 days (7083).

rules.title: A qualifier may qualify no more than three firms in any one-year period
rules.plain_english: Even when the ownership tests are met, one person can serve as qualifier for no more than three firms in any one-year period.
rules.applies_to: Qualifying individuals
rules.quote: Notwithstanding paragraphs (1) to (3), inclusive, of subdivision (a), a qualifying individual may act as the qualifier for no more than three firms in any one-year period.
rules.notes: Count all firms qualified during any rolling 12-month window.

rules.title: Qualifier rule violations: misdemeanor, up to 6 months jail and $3,000-$5,000 fine
rules.plain_english: Breaking the qualifier rules (for example, being an absentee qualifier or qualifying too many firms) is cause for discipline and a misdemeanor punishable by up to 6 months in county jail, a fine of $3,000 to $5,000, or both.
rules.applies_to: Qualifying individuals and licensees
rules.quote: Violation of this section shall constitute a cause for disciplinary action and shall be punishable as a misdemeanor by imprisonment in a county jail not to exceed six months, by a fine of not less than three thousand dollars ($3,000), but not to exceed five thousand dollars ($5,000), or by both the fine and imprisonment.

rules.title: Report qualifier departure to CSLB in writing within 90 days
rules.plain_english: When the RMO, RME, responsible managing member or manager leaves, the licensee or the qualifier must notify CSLB in writing within 90 days. If no one notifies CSLB in time, the license is suspended (or the classification removed) and the qualifier removed as of the date CSLB receives the notice, and the late notice is grounds for discipline.

parameters.trigger: date of qualifier disassociation
parameters.consequence_if_late: automatic suspension or classification removal, effective date written notice received at CSLB headquarters; grounds for discipline

rules.applies_to: All licensees with an RMO, RME, responsible managing member or responsible managing manager
rules.quote: If the responsible managing officer, responsible managing employee, responsible managing member, or responsible managing manager disassociates from the licensed entity, the licensee or the qualifier shall notify the registrar in writing within 90 days after the date of disassociation.

rules.title: Replace a departed qualifier within 90 days or the license is suspended
rules.plain_english: The licensee has 90 days from the qualifier's departure to replace them by filing an application and fee naming a new qualifier. If not replaced in time, the license is automatically suspended (or the classification removed) at the end of the 90 days.

parameters.trigger: date of qualifier disassociation
parameters.required_filing: application to replace qualifier plus fee
parameters.consequence_if_missed: automatic suspension of license or removal of classification at day 90

rules.applies_to: Licensees whose qualifier leaves
rules.quote: The licensee shall have 90 days after the date of disassociation in which to replace the qualifier. Upon failure to replace the qualifier within 90 days after the date of disassociation, the license shall be automatically suspended or the classification removed at the end of the 90 days.
rules.notes: If the departed person qualified only one of several classifications, that classification is removed instead of the whole license being suspended.

rules.title: Departing qualifier stays responsible until the later of departure or CSLB's receipt of notice
rules.plain_english: A qualifier remains responsible for the licensee's construction operations until the later of the date they left or the date CSLB receives written notice. Qualifiers should send their own notice promptly.
rules.applies_to: Qualifying individuals leaving a licensee
rules.quote: The person qualifying on behalf of a licensee under Section 7068 shall be responsible for the licensee's construction operations until the date of disassociation or the date the board receives the written notification of disassociation, whichever is later.

rules.title: One 90-day extension to replace a qualifier (180-day cap for date disputes or death)
rules.plain_english: For good cause, CSLB may grant one 90-day extension to replace a qualifier if the licensee disputes the departure date, the qualifier died, or processing was delayed by CSLB or another agency. The petition must arrive within 90 days of the departure, death or delay, and a replacement application must already be on file. For date disputes or death, the total time to replace is capped at 180 days.

parameters.petition_trigger: date of disassociation, death, or delay
grounds: processing delay outside applicant's control caused by CSLB or another state or federal agency
parameters.prerequisite: application to replace qualifier on file

rules.applies_to: Licensees replacing a qualifier
rules.quote: The petition shall only be considered if an application to replace the qualifier as prescribed by the registrar is on file with the board. Under the circumstances described in subparagraphs (A) and (B) of paragraph (1), the licensee shall have no more than a total of 180 days after the date of disassociation or death in which to replace the qualifier.
rules.notes: The text sets no 180-day cap for the agency-delay ground.

rules.title: Taking or obtaining a CSLB exam for someone else is a misdemeanor
rules.plain_english: It is a misdemeanor for anyone other than the named examinee to take the qualifying exam for an applicant, or for anyone without authorization to obtain and give another person the exam or any part of it.

prohibited_acts: taking the qualifying exam on behalf of an applicant
obtaining and providing the exam or any part of it to another without authorization

rules.applies_to: Applicants, examinees and anyone else
rules.quote: It is a misdemeanor for any person other than the examinee named in the application to take the qualifying examination on behalf of an applicant for a contractor’s license.
rules.notes: No specific fine is stated in these sections.

rules.title: Applicant and all officers, partners, managers and RMEs must be free of B&P 480 grounds
rules.plain_english: The applicant and each officer, director, partner, manager, associate and RME must not have committed acts or crimes that are grounds for denial under B&P 480. For entity applicants, the license is refused if any officer, director, partner, LLC manager or member fails the non-experience qualifications.

parameters.standard: no acts or crimes that are grounds for denial under B&P 480

rules.applies_to: All applicants and their personnel of record
rules.quote: An applicant, and each officer, director, partner, manager, associate, and responsible managing employee thereof, shall not have committed acts or crimes that are grounds for denial of licensure under Section 480.
rules.notes: B&P 480 limits (look-back periods, rehabilitation) appear in an earlier section of the book.

rules.title: Applicants must submit fingerprints for DOJ and FBI background checks
rules.plain_english: Applicants must provide a full set of fingerprints, electronically (Live Scan) if available, for California DOJ and FBI criminal history checks. CSLB may also receive later arrest information.

parameters.format: electronic if readily available; alternatives require registrar approval

rules.applies_to: All license applicants
rules.quote: As part of an application for a contractor’s license, the board shall require an applicant to furnish a full set of fingerprints for purposes of conducting a criminal history record check.
rules.notes: This subdivision says only 'an applicant'. Whether each officer, partner and qualifier must also be fingerprinted is not stated here (7069(a) does screen all of them), so confirm current CSLB practice.

rules.title: Proof of arrest disposition due within 90 days when CSLB asks
rules.plain_english: If CSLB learns a member of a licensee's personnel or a home improvement salesperson was arrested, it may demand proof of how the case ended, such as certified court records. The proof must reach CSLB within 90 days of the disposition or 90 days of CSLB's demand, whichever is later. Failing to comply is cause for discipline.

who: personnel of record of a licensee

rules.applies_to: Licensee personnel and registered home improvement salespersons
rules.quote: Any proof required by this section shall be received by the registrar within 90 days of the date of the disposition, or within 90 days of the registrar’s demand for information if that date is later.
rules.notes: The demand is sent by first-class mail to the last official address of record, so keeping the address current matters.

rules.title: After a denial, reapply no earlier than one year unless CSLB sets an earlier date
rules.plain_english: An applicant must show it was never denied a license or had one revoked for reasons that bar the new license. When CSLB denies an application, the earliest reapplication date is one year from the decision or notice, unless CSLB sets an earlier date.

parameters.trigger: effective date of denial decision or service of notice under B&P 485(b)

rules.applies_to: Denied applicants
rules.quote: inform the applicant of the earliest date that the applicant may reapply for a license, which shall be one year from the effective date of the decision or service of notice under subdivision (b) of Section 485, unless the board prescribes an earlier date.
rules.notes: For crime-related denials, 7073(b) caps the wait at 5 years; see denial-crime-reapply-max-5-years.

rules.title: Licensee entering the military: name a designee within 30 days
rules.plain_english: A licensee entering the U.S. armed forces may name responsible managing person(s) to run the business until one year after discharge. The license stays in force for 30 days after entry, and the designees must be reported to CSLB before those 30 days end. Renewal fees must still be paid.

parameters.designee_report_deadline: before expiration of 30 days after entry into armed forces

rules.applies_to: Licensees entering military service
rules.quote: Any license shall remain in full force and effect for 30 days after the entrance of the licensee into the armed forces, but he shall prior to the expiration of such 30-day period provide the registrar with the name or names of the persons so designated to conduct his business.

rules.title: License bonds: admitted surety bond or cash/cashier's check deposit only (no CDs)
rules.plain_english: Required license bonds must be either a bond from an admitted surety insurer or a deposit of cash or a cashier's check with CSLB under CCP 995.710(a)(1). Certificates of deposit and other alternatives are not accepted. CSLB stopped accepting other alternatives on January 1, 2019, and existing ones had to be replaced by January 1, 2020.

allowed_forms: bond executed by admitted surety insurer
lawful money or cashier's check deposited with registrar (CCP 995.710(a)(1))

rules.applies_to: All licensees subject to bond requirements
rules.quote: Notwithstanding Article 7 (commencing with Section 995.710) of Chapter 2 of Title 14 of Part 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, no other method of deposit, including, but not limited to, a certificate of deposit, shall satisfy a bond requirement under this article.
rules.notes: The 2026 amendment (AB 521) touches this section; the book does not mark which subdivisions changed.

rules.title: Cash bond deposits are frozen once CSLB is notified of a lawsuit; shared pro rata if short
rules.plain_english: If CSLB gets written notice of a civil action against a cash deposit given in place of a bond, none of it is released except as a court orders. If the deposit cannot pay all adjudicated claims in full, it is split among claimants in proportion to their claims. CSLB charges no legal fees against it.

parameters.freeze_trigger: written notice to CSLB of civil action against the deposit

rules.applies_to: Licensees with cash deposits in lieu of bond; claimants
rules.quote: If the board is notified, in writing, of a civil action against the deposit authorized under this section, the deposit or any portion thereof shall not be released for any purpose, except as determined by the court.

rules.title: Non-wage claims against cash deposits: 3-year deadline
rules.plain_english: A non-wage claim against a cash deposit given in place of a contractor's or qualifier's bond must be filed within 3 years after the license period in which the act happened ends, or within 3 years of the license being inactivated, canceled or revoked, whichever comes first. For a deposit in place of a disciplinary bond, a third deadline also applies: 3 years after the last date the deposit was required.

parameters.deadline_rule: earliest of: (expiration of license period in which act occurred + 3 years), (date license inactivated/canceled/revoked + 3 years), and for disciplinary-bond deposits (last date deposit required + 3 years)
applies_to_deposits: in lieu of qualifying individual bond
parameters.covers: alternatives filed before 2019-01-01 and cash/cashier's check deposits after 2019-01-01

rules.applies_to: Claimants against contractor cash deposits; licensees
rules.quote: against a deposit given in lieu of a contractor’s bond or bond of a qualifying individual filed by an active licensee shall be brought within three years after the expiration of the license period during which the act or omission occurred, or within three years of the date the license of the active licensee was inactivated, canceled, or revoked by the board, whichever occurs first.
rules.notes: Surety bonds have a 2-year deadline (7071.11(c)); cash deposits have 3 years.

rules.title: Wage and fringe benefit claims against bonds or deposits: 6 months from discovery, 2-year outside limit
rules.plain_english: A claim against a contractor bond or cash deposit for unpaid wages or fringe benefits must be brought within 6 months after the delinquency is discovered. A civil action may never be filed more than 2 years after the wages or contributions were due.
rules.applies_to: Employees, union trust funds and licensees
