rules.quote: A claim to recover wages or fringe benefits shall be brought within six months from the date that the wage or fringe benefit delinquencies were discovered, but in no event shall a civil action thereon be brought later than two years from the date the wage or fringe benefit contributions were due.
rules.notes: Identical wording appears in both sections, one for cash deposits and one for surety bonds.

rules.title: Wage claims against cash deposits go to the Labor Commissioner; 10-day and 60-day payment windows
rules.plain_english: Employee wage and fringe claims against a cash deposit are filed with the Labor Commissioner, who holds a hearing. CSLB waits 10 days after the findings before paying. If a party gives notice that it will seek judicial review and files suit, payment waits for the court. If no action is filed within 60 days of the findings, CSLB pays the claimant.

parameters.judicial_review_notice: written notice of intent to seek review under Gov Code 11523, filed with registrar and commissioner within the 10 days

rules.applies_to: Licensees with cash deposits; employees and employee organizations
rules.quote: The registrar shall not make payment from the deposit on the basis of findings by the commissioner for a period of 10 days following determination of the findings.

rules.title: Who the contractor's bond protects
rules.plain_english: The contractor's bond protects: homeowners hurt by license-law violations on home improvement to their own home; owners building a single-family home not meant for sale; anyone hurt by willful and deliberate violations or fraud; employees owed wages; and trust funds or others owed fringe benefits.

beneficiaries: homeowner contracting for home improvement on personal family residence
property owner contracting for construction of single-family dwelling not intended or offered for sale when damages incurred
person damaged by willful and deliberate violation or by fraud in execution or performance of a construction contract
employee damaged by failure to pay wages
person or entity (including Civil Code 8024(b) laborer) damaged by failure to pay fringe benefits, public or private work

rules.applies_to: Licensees, homeowners, owners, employees, trust funds
rules.quote: The contractor’s bond shall be for the benefit of the following: (a) A homeowner contracting for home improvement upon the homeowner’s personal family residence damaged as a result of a violation of this chapter by the licensee. (b) A property owner contracting for the construction of a single-family dwelling who is damaged as a result of a violation of this chapter by the licensee.
rules.notes: Fringe benefit damages are limited to actual employer payments owed (e.g., Labor Code 1773.1 payments).

rules.title: Contractor's bond: $25,000
rules.plain_english: To get, reinstate, reactivate, renew or keep a license, every licensee must have a $25,000 contractor's bond on file with CSLB. No bond is needed while the license is inactive.
rules.applies_to: All active licensees and applicants
rules.quote: The board shall require as a condition precedent to the issuance, reinstatement, reactivation, renewal, or continued maintenance of a license, that the applicant or licensee file or have on file a contractor’s bond in the sum of twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000).
rules.notes: The earlier version of 7071.6 was repealed January 1, 2023 and replaced by this one; the book does not print the earlier amount.

rules.title: Non-homeowner claims against the $25,000 bond capped at $7,500 total
rules.plain_english: Claimants other than homeowners doing home improvement on their own residence can collect no more than $7,500 in total from the contractor's bond (or the qualifier's bond). The rest is reserved for those homeowners, who can recover up to the full bond.

parameters.homeowner_beneficiary: 7071.5(a) homeowner, home improvement on personal family residence

rules.applies_to: Bond claimants and sureties
rules.quote: Excluding the claims brought by the beneficiaries specified in subdivision (a) of Section 7071.5, the aggregate liability of a surety on claims brought against a bond required by this section shall not exceed the sum of seven thousand five hundred dollars ($7,500).
rules.notes: reserved_for_homeowners_usd is computed (25,000 - 7,500). Wage and fringe claims have a separate $4,000 aggregate cap (7071.11(a)).

rules.title: Applicants with past unlicensed-contracting violations may need a $50,000 bond
rules.plain_english: CSLB may require an applicant to post twice the normal contractor's bond, until first renewal, if the applicant was convicted of unlicensed contracting (7028) or got a final citation for it (7028.7), and the violation caused substantial injury to the public.

conditions_all: convicted under B&P 7028 or cited under B&P 7028.7
citation (if any) is a final order of the registrar
violation caused substantial injury to the public

rules.applies_to: Applicants with prior unlicensed contracting violations
rules.quote: the board may require an applicant to post a contractor’s bond in twice the amount required pursuant to subdivision (a) until the time that the license is renewed, under the following conditions: (1) The applicant has either been convicted of a violation of Section 7028 or has been cited pursuant to Section 7028.7.
rules.notes: amount_usd is computed as 2 x $25,000.

rules.title: LLC licensees: extra $100,000 worker protection bond
rules.plain_english: An LLC licensee must also keep a $100,000 surety bond protecting workers owed wages, interest on wages or fringe benefits. If the LLC is party to a collective bargaining agreement, the bond also covers welfare, pension and apprenticeship fund contributions. It is not required while the license is inactive.
rules.applies_to: LLC licensees
rules.quote: The board shall require, as a condition precedent to the issuance, reissuance, reinstatement, reactivation, renewal, or continued valid use of a limited liability company license, that the applicant or licensee file or have on file a surety bond in the sum of one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000).

rules.title: File a bond within 90 days of its effective date for retroactive reinstatement
rules.plain_english: CSLB accepts a contractor's, LLC, disciplinary or qualifier bond as of the effective date on the bond if it receives the bond within 90 days of that date, and reinstates the license back to that date. A bond received later is still accepted as of its effective date only if the licensee shows the gap was beyond its control.

parameters.trigger: effective date shown on bond
parameters.result_if_timely: accepted as of bond effective date; license reinstated retroactively if otherwise eligible
parameters.late_exception: showing on registrar form that lapse was due to circumstances beyond licensee's control

rules.applies_to: Licensees replacing or reinstating bonds
rules.quote: the registrar shall accept a bond required by Section 7071.6, 7071.6.5, 7071.8, or 7071.9 as of the effective date shown on the bond, if the bond is received by the registrar within 90 days after that date, and shall reinstate the license to which the bond pertains, if otherwise eligible, retroactive to the effective date of the bond.
rules.notes: Tool idea: alert when a replacement bond has not been filed within 90 days of its effective date.

rules.title: Disciplinary bond: $25,000 to $250,000 after suspension or revocation
rules.plain_english: A person or firm tied to a suspended or revoked license (including the qualifier at the time, and officers who knew or took part) must post a disciplinary bond to get, renew or restore a license, change officers, lift a suspension, or keep using a license under stayed discipline. CSLB sets the amount by how serious the violation was, from $25,000 up to 10 times the contractor's bond.

subject_persons: person whose license was suspended or revoked
qualifier at any time cause for discipline occurred (knowledge not required)
officer, director, manager, partner or personnel of record who knew of or participated in the act
firm whose existing or new personnel had a license suspended or revoked
firm whose personnel held such a role at a disciplined licensee and knew of or participated in the act
triggers: change of officers or members of corporation or LLC
continued valid use of license under stayed discipline

rules.applies_to: Disciplined licensees and their personnel, including new firms they join
rules.quote: that the applicant or licensee file or have on file a contractor’s bond in a sum to be fixed by the registrar based upon the seriousness of the violation, but which sum shall not be less than twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000) nor more than 10 times that amount required by Section 7071.6.
rules.notes: max_usd is computed as 10 x the $25,000 bond in 7071.6. Wage and fringe claims against this bond are not subject to the $4,000 cap in 7071.11(a).

rules.title: Disciplinary bond stays on file at least 2 years of active, good-standing license time
rules.plain_english: A disciplinary bond must stay on file for at least 2 years, plus any extra time CSLB sets. The clock runs only while the license is current, active and in good standing, so inactive or suspended time does not count.
rules.applies_to: Licensees subject to a disciplinary bond
rules.quote: The bond shall remain on file with the registrar for a period of at least two years and for any additional time that the registrar determines. The bond period shall run only while the license is current, active, and in good standing,
rules.notes: Calculation: release no earlier than 2 calendar years of qualifying status after the start date (add years, not a fixed 730 days, so a leap day does not end the period early), excluding periods when the license is not current, active and in good standing; the registrar may require more time.
rules.correction: Notes computed the release date as start + 730 days. The text says 'at least two years' of current, active, good-standing time, and 730 days falls one day short when the period includes February 29. Notes changed to count two calendar years of qualifying status.

rules.title: Qualifier's bond: $25,000 when the qualifier is not the owner or a general partner
rules.plain_english: If the qualifier (RMO, RME, etc.) is not the sole owner, a general partner or a joint licensee, they must file their own $25,000 qualifying individual bond in addition to the contractor's bond. It protects the same people as the contractor's bond, and non-homeowner claims are capped at $7,500. Tribes are exempt.

parameters.required_when: qualifier is not proprietor, general partner, or joint licensee
parameters.beneficiaries: same five categories as contractor's bond (7071.10)
exempt: RMO owning >=10% of voting stock (with certification)
LLC qualifier owning >=10% membership interest (with certification)

rules.applies_to: Licensees qualified by an RMO, RME, responsible managing member or manager
rules.quote: If the qualifying individual, as referred to in Sections 7068 and 7068.1, is neither the proprietor, a general partner, nor a joint licensee, the qualifying individual shall file or have on file a qualifying individual’s bond as provided in Section 7071.10 in the sum of twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000).

rules.title: Qualifier bond waived for RMO with 10%+ voting stock or LLC qualifier with 10%+ membership
rules.plain_english: An RMO who owns at least 10% of the corporation's voting stock, or an LLC qualifier who owns at least 10% of the membership interest, does not need a qualifying individual bond if they certify that on the CSLB form. Changes to this exemption must be reported within 90 days.
rules.applies_to: Corporate RMOs and LLC qualifiers
rules.quote: The responsible managing officer of a corporation shall not be required to file or have on file a qualifying individual’s bond, if the responsible managing officer owns 10 percent or more of the voting stock of the corporation and certifies to that fact on a form prescribed by the registrar.
rules.notes: Corporate exemption is based on voting stock; the LLC exemption is based on membership interest.

rules.title: Wage and fringe claims against a license bond capped at $4,000 total
rules.plain_english: Total surety liability for wage and fringe benefit claims against a license bond (other than a disciplinary bond) is capped at $4,000. If the bond cannot pay all claims, it is split among claimants in proportion to their claims.
rules.applies_to: Employees, trust funds, sureties, licensees
rules.quote: The aggregate liability of a surety on a claim for wages and fringe benefits brought against a bond required by this article, other than a bond required by Section 7071.8, shall not exceed the sum of four thousand dollars ($4,000).
rules.notes: Read literally, the cap covers every bond in this article except the 7071.8 disciplinary bond, which would include the $100,000 LLC worker bond (7071.6.5). That outcome sits uneasily with the LLC bond's purpose of protecting workers. Confirm with CSLB or counsel before applying the $4,000 cap to the LLC bond.

rules.title: No renewal while a judgment or admitted claim above the bond amount is unpaid
rules.plain_english: A license cannot be renewed, reissued or reinstated while a judgment or admitted claim larger than the bond amount is still unpaid.

parameters.condition: judgment or admitted claim exceeding bond amount remains unsatisfied

rules.applies_to: Licensees with bond claims
rules.quote: No license may be renewed, reissued, or reinstated while a judgment or admitted claim in excess of the amount of the bond remains unsatisfied.

rules.title: Non-wage claims against a surety license bond: 2-year deadline
rules.plain_english: A non-wage claim against a license bond must be filed within 2 years after the end of the license period in which the act happened. If the license was inactivated, canceled or revoked, the 2 years run from the date it would have expired. For a disciplinary bond, the deadline is the earlier of that date or 2 years after the bond was last required. Judgment bonds are excluded.

parameters.rule_active_license: expiration of license period in which act or omission occurred + 2 years
parameters.rule_inactivated_canceled_revoked: date license would have expired + 2 years (act must predate inactivation/cancellation/revocation)
parameters.rule_disciplinary_bond: earliest of the applicable rule above and (last date disciplinary bond required + 2 years)

rules.applies_to: Bond claimants (homeowners, owners, others) and licensees
rules.quote: Within two years after the expiration of the license period during which the act or omission occurred. The provisions of this paragraph shall be applicable only if the license has not been inactivated, canceled, or revoked during the license period for which the bond was posted and accepted by the registrar as specified under Section 7071.7.
rules.notes: Needs the license expiration date (from CSLB records) to compute.

rules.title: Surety must report bond payments to CSLB within 30 days
rules.plain_english: When a surety pays a claim on a license bond, it must notify CSLB within 30 days by declaration. The notice gives the contractor's name and license number, bond number, amount paid, legal basis, payees, whether it was a good faith payment, and whether the licensee protested.

parameters.trigger: surety payment on bond claim (court or otherwise)
contents: whether payment was good faith action

rules.applies_to: Sureties; licensees whose bonds are paid out
rules.quote: Whenever the surety makes payment on a claim against a bond required by this article, whether or not payment is made through a court action or otherwise, the surety shall, within 30 days of the payment, provide notice to the registrar.

rules.title: Licensee gets at least 15 days to protest a good-faith bond payment
rules.plain_english: Before a surety settles a claim through a good faith payment, the licensee has at least 15 days to send a written protest telling the surety not to pay and giving a specific, reasonable basis for opposing it. If the licensee protests, CSLB must investigate, and must file disciplinary action if there is evidence the surety sustained a loss from a good faith payment made to mitigate damages of a person covered by B&P 7071.5.

protest_must_include: instruction not to pay from the bond
specific and reasonable basis for opposition
parameters.board_action_on_protest: board shall investigate; board shall file disciplinary action if evidence surety sustained a loss from a good faith payment made to mitigate damages of a 7071.5 beneficiary

rules.applies_to: Licensees facing bond claims
rules.quote: Prior to the settlement of a claim through a good faith payment by the surety, a licensee shall have not less than 15 days in which to provide a written protest.
rules.correction: plain_english said CSLB 'may discipline' after a protest. 7071.11(f)(1) says the board 'shall investigate the matter and file disciplinary action' if there is evidence the surety sustained a loss from a good faith payment made to mitigate damages of a 7071.5 beneficiary. plain_english fixed and a board_action_on_protest parameter added.

rules.title: No protest: reimburse the surety within 90 days of CSLB notice or license is suspended
rules.plain_english: If the licensee does not protest, it has 90 days from CSLB's notice to prove it repaid the surety, plus any judgment or admitted claim above the bond. Otherwise the license is suspended by law at day 90, and the suspension is shown publicly indefinitely as a failure to settle final liabilities.

parameters.trigger: date of CSLB notification
proof_required: payment of actual amount owed to surety
payment of any judgment or admitted claim exceeding bond (if applicable)
parameters.consequence: automatic suspension at end of 90 days; disclosed indefinitely as failure to settle outstanding final liabilities

rules.applies_to: Licensees whose surety paid a claim without protest
rules.quote: A licensee that fails to file a protest as specified in this subdivision shall have 90 days from the date of notification by the board to submit proof of payment of the actual amount owed to the surety and, if applicable, proof of payment of any judgment or admitted claim in excess of the amount of the bond or, by operation of law, the license shall be suspended at the end of the 90 days.

rules.title: Unreimbursed surety blocks renewal of the license and other licenses with the same personnel
rules.plain_english: While a surety remains unreimbursed for a bond loss, the license and any other license listing any of the same personnel of record cannot be renewed, reissued or reinstated.

scope: any other license listing any of the same personnel of record
parameters.condition: surety unreimbursed for loss or expense on the bond

rules.applies_to: Licensees and their officers, partners and qualifiers
rules.quote: During any period in which a surety remains unreimbursed for a loss or expense sustained on a bond issued pursuant to this article, the license for which the bond was issued, and any other license on which any member of the licensee’s personnel of record has also been listed, may not be renewed, reissued, or reinstated

rules.title: Payment plan (accord) with the surety: breaking it means automatic suspension
rules.plain_english: Instead of paying the surety in full, a licensee may give CSLB a notarized copy of an accord (settlement agreement) with the surety. If it fails to follow the accord, the license is automatically suspended and can only be renewed or reinstated after proof all debts are paid.

parameters.document: notarized copy of accord with surety
parameters.consequence_of_breach: automatic suspension by operation of law
parameters.reinstatement_requires: proof of satisfaction of all debts

rules.applies_to: Licensees owing a surety
rules.quote: The licensee may provide the board with a notarized copy of an accord, reached with the surety to satisfy the debt in lieu of full payment. By operation of law, failure to abide by the accord shall result in the automatic suspension of a license to which this section applies.

rules.title: Do not mention the license bond in advertising or solicitations
rules.plain_english: A contractor may not mention any CSLB-required bond in its advertising, sales pitches or other presentations to the public. Doing so is grounds for license suspension.

parameters.prohibited_content: reference to any bond required to be filed under the Contractors State License Law

rules.applies_to: All licensees (ads, websites, proposals, trucks, social media)
rules.quote: Any reference by a contractor in his advertising, soliciting, or other presentments to the public to any bond required to be filed pursuant to this chapter is a ground for the suspension of the license of such contractor.
rules.notes: Useful check for marketing copy: flag phrases like 'bonded' that refer to the license bond. Whether a generic 'licensed and bonded' tagline counts is not addressed in the text; treat it as a risk.

rules.title: Denying a license bond for race, religion, color, national origin, ancestry or sex: actual damages plus $250
rules.plain_english: No applicant or licensee may be denied a contractor's license bond solely because of race, religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry or sex. Whoever does so owes actual damages plus $250 for each offense.
rules.applies_to: Sureties and bond producers; licensees and applicants
rules.quote: Whoever denies a contractor’s license bond solely on the grounds specified herein is liable for each and every such offense for the actual damages, and two hundred fifty dollars ($250) in addition thereto, suffered by the licensee or applicant for a license.

rules.title: Failing to keep a sufficient bond: suspension or revocation
rules.plain_english: If a licensee does not keep a sufficient required bond on file, the license can be suspended or revoked under CCP 996.020.

parameters.consequence: license subject to suspension or revocation

rules.applies_to: All bonded licensees
rules.quote: If a licensee fails to maintain a sufficient bond required by this article, the license is subject to suspension or revocation pursuant to Section 996.020 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
rules.notes: Track bond expiration and cancellation notices; see bond-retroactive-acceptance-90-days for the reinstatement window.

rules.title: Applicant with unpaid construction judgment must post a judgment bond within 90 days
rules.plain_english: An applicant (for a new license, renewal, reinstatement or change of personnel) found to have an unpaid final judgment for failing to pay a contractor, sub, consumer, supplier or employee must file a bond equal to the unpaid judgment(s) within 90 days of CSLB's notice, or the application is void. The bond is in addition to the contractor's bond and stays on file at least one year. A notarized accord with the judgment creditor or a cash deposit can be used instead.

parameters.trigger: date of CSLB notification
parameters.bond_amount: equal to the unsatisfied final judgment(s)
parameters.removal: proof of satisfaction of all debts
alternatives: notarized copy of accord with judgment creditor
lawful money or cashier's check deposit (CCP 995.710(a)(1))
applies_to_applications: change of officers or other personnel of record

rules.applies_to: Applicants and licensees with unsatisfied construction-related judgments
rules.quote: The applicant shall have 90 days from the date of notification by the board to file the bond or the application shall become void and the applicant shall reapply for issuance, reinstatement, or reactivation of a license.
rules.notes: CSLB acts on notice from anyone who knows of the judgment and shows proof of it (7071.17(h)).

rules.title: Application must state under penalty of perjury whether there are unpaid construction judgments
rules.plain_english: The application for issuance, reinstatement or reactivation includes a statement under penalty of perjury about unpaid judgments owed to contractors, subs, consumers, suppliers or employees. If the statement is false, the license is suspended back to its issue date until the bond, proof of payment, or notarized accord is filed.

parameters.document: penalty-of-perjury statement on application re unsatisfied judgments
parameters.consequence_if_falsified: license retroactively suspended to date of issuance until bond, satisfaction of judgment, or notarized accord filed

rules.applies_to: All applicants
rules.quote: if it is found that the applicant falsified the statement then the license will be retroactively suspended to the date of issuance and the license will stay suspended until the bond, satisfaction of judgment, or notarized copy of any accord applicable under this section is filed.

rules.title: Report any unsatisfied final judgment to CSLB within 90 days
rules.plain_english: Every licensee must tell CSLB in writing about any unsatisfied final judgment against it. If it does not report within 90 days, the license is automatically suspended when CSLB finds out, and stays suspended until it proves the judgment is paid or files a notarized accord. Failing to report is also cause for discipline, even if the debt was later discharged in bankruptcy.

parameters.trigger: imposition of unsatisfied final judgment
parameters.consequence_if_late: automatic suspension on date registrar learns of judgment; lifted only on proof of satisfaction or notarized accord; cause for discipline

rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.quote: all licensees shall notify the registrar in writing of any unsatisfied final judgment imposed on the licensee. If the licensee fails to notify the registrar in writing within 90 days, the license shall be automatically suspended on the date that the registrar is informed, or is made aware of the unsatisfied final judgment.
rules.notes: Limited to judgments substantially related to construction activities or license duties (7071.17(e)).

rules.title: Licensee who reports a judgment must post a judgment bond within 90 days of CSLB notice
rules.plain_english: A licensee that reports an unsatisfied judgment on time must keep a bond equal to all unpaid judgments to stay licensed. It has 90 days from CSLB's notice to file the bond (or a notarized accord), or the license is automatically suspended.

parameters.trigger: date of CSLB notification
parameters.bond_amount: sum of all unsatisfied judgments covered by 7071.17
parameters.alternative: notarized copy of accord with each judgment creditor
parameters.consequence_if_missed: automatic suspension at end of 90 days

rules.applies_to: Licensees with unsatisfied construction-related judgments
rules.quote: The licensee has 90 days from the date of notification by the board to file the bond or at the end of the 90 days the license shall be automatically suspended. In lieu of filing the bond required by this section, the licensee may provide the board with a notarized copy of any accord reached with any individual holding an unsatisfied final judgment.

rules.title: Judgment bond rule: construction-related judgments only; arbitration awards count; bankruptcy discharge excluded
rules.plain_english: The judgment bond rules cover only judgments substantially related to the licensee's construction work or license duties. A final arbitration award counts as a judgment once the time to challenge it has passed with no petition pending. Debts discharged in bankruptcy are generally excluded.

parameters.covered_judgments: substantially related to construction activities or to qualifications, functions or duties of the license
parameters.judgment_includes: final arbitration award after time to petition for trial de novo or to vacate/correct has expired with no petition pending
parameters.excluded: financial obligations discharged in bankruptcy (except as otherwise provided)

rules.applies_to: Licensees and applicants with judgments
rules.quote: This section applies only with respect to an unsatisfied final judgment that is substantially related to the construction activities of a licensee licensed under this chapter, or to the qualifications, functions, or duties of the license.
rules.notes: Bankruptcy discharge does not excuse a failure to report the judgment (7071.17(l)).

rules.title: Judgment bond: lapse means suspension; may be reduced at renewal on partial payment
rules.plain_english: If the judgment bond lapses or the licensee breaks the accord, the license is automatically suspended and is reinstated only on proof all debts are paid or a notarized accord is filed. The bond stays in full force until the debt is paid. At renewal, CSLB may reduce it to the unpaid balance on proof of partial payment, and may remove it once all debts are paid.

parameters.lapse_consequence: automatic suspension by operation of law
reinstatement_requires: proof of satisfaction of all debts
parameters.removal: proof of satisfaction of all debts

rules.applies_to: Licensees with judgment bonds
rules.quote: If, at the time of renewal, the licensee submits proof of partial satisfaction of the financial obligations covered by this section, the board may authorize the bond to be reduced to the amount of the unsatisfied portion of the outstanding judgment. When the licensee submits proof of satisfaction of all debts, the bond requirement may be removed.

rules.title: Unpaid judgment bars the licensee's qualifier and personnel from other licenses
rules.plain_english: When a judgment is entered against a licensee or its personnel, the qualifier and personnel of record at the time of the work are barred from serving on any license until the judgment is paid. Any other license with the same personnel is suspended until the judgment is paid, the debtor's license is reinstated, or those people leave that company.

parameters.barred_persons: qualifying person and personnel of record at time of activities underlying the judgment
parameters.other_licenses_effect: suspended until judgment debtor license reinstated, judgment satisfied, or shared personnel disassociate

rules.applies_to: Officers, partners, qualifiers and any company that shares them
rules.quote: If a judgment is entered against a licensee or any personnel of record of a licensee, then a qualifying person or personnel of record of the licensee at the time of the activities on which the judgment is based shall be automatically prohibited from serving as a qualifying individual or other personnel of record on any license until the judgment is satisfied.
rules.notes: Due diligence check before hiring a qualifier or adding an officer: search CSLB records for unsatisfied judgments tied to that person.

rules.title: Report felony or related criminal convictions to CSLB within 90 days
rules.plain_english: A licensee must report to CSLB in writing within 90 days after learning of its conviction for any felony, or for any other crime substantially related to a contractor's qualifications, functions or duties.

parameters.trigger: licensee obtains knowledge of the conviction
reportable_events: conviction of licensee for any felony
conviction for any other crime substantially related to qualifications, functions, and duties of a licensed contractor

rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.quote: a licensee shall report to the registrar in writing the occurrence of any of the following within 90 days after the licensee obtains knowledge of the event: (1) The conviction of the licensee for any felony. (2) The conviction of the licensee for any other crime that is substantially related to the qualifications, functions, and duties of a licensed contractor.

rules.title: LLC licensees: liability insurance of $1M aggregate, more with more than 5 personnel, max $5M
rules.plain_english: An LLC licensee must carry liability insurance for claims from its contracting work, on top of its bonds. The aggregate limit must be at least $1 million if 5 or fewer people are listed as personnel of record. With more than 5, it must add $100,000 per person listed, but never more than $5 million per policy period.
rules.applies_to: LLC licensees
rules.quote: For a limited liability company licensee with five or fewer persons listed on the members of the personnel of record, the aggregate limit shall not be less than one million dollars ($1,000,000). (2) For a limited liability company licensee with more than five persons listed on the members of the personnel of record, an additional one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000) of insurance
rules.notes: The statute says an additional $100,000 'for each person listed on the personnel of record'. The law book's own Chapter 3 summary (PDF page 43) reads it as 'for each additional member of the personnel of record, not to exceed $5 million total', which is the formula used here (only persons above five count). The $5M cap is reduced by amounts paid in defending, settling or discharging claims.

rules.title: LLC insurance: claims-made or occurrence, policy period of 12 months or less, licensed or surplus line insurer
rules.plain_english: The LLC liability policy may be claims-made or occurrence. The coverage period must be a policy year or other period of no more than 12 months, the insurer must be licensed in California or an eligible surplus line insurer, and deductibles or self-insured retentions are allowed.
rules.applies_to: LLC licensees and their insurance brokers
rules.quote: For purposes of this section, “designated period” means a policy year or any other period designated in the policy that is not greater than 12 months. Any policy or policies secured to satisfy the requirements of this section shall be written by an insurer or insurers duly licensed by this state or an eligible surplus line insurer,

rules.title: Exhausted LLC policy limit must be restored by the next policy period or the license is suspended
rules.plain_english: If claims use up the LLC's aggregate limit, it does not have to buy more coverage for that period. But the full required limit must be restored by the start of the next period, or the license is suspended by law until it is. CSLB may post the depleted amount on the license record.

parameters.deadline: commencement date of next designated period
parameters.consequence_if_missed: suspension by operation of law until compliance

rules.applies_to: LLC licensees
rules.quote: the aggregate limit of liability coverage (coverage limit) required by this section shall be reinstated by not later than the commencement date of the next designated period, and the license of any licensee that fails to comply with this provision shall be suspended by operation of law until the date that the licensee complies with the coverage limit requirements of this section.

rules.title: Dissolving LLC must keep 3 years of extended reporting (tail) coverage
rules.plain_english: When an LLC licensee dissolves and winds up, it must keep or buy an extended reporting period endorsement (tail) at the full required aggregate limit for at least 3 years, if the insurer reasonably offers one.

parameters.trigger: dissolution and winding up of LLC
parameters.coverage_amount: maximum total aggregate limit required by 7071.19
parameters.condition: if reasonably available from insurer

rules.applies_to: LLC licensees that dissolve
rules.quote: the company shall, with respect to any insurance policy or policies then maintained pursuant to this section, maintain or obtain an extended reporting period endorsement or equivalent provision in the maximum total aggregate limit of liability required to comply with this section for a minimum of three years if reasonably available from the insurer.

rules.title: LLC must file proof of insurance (Certificate of Liability Insurance) with CSLB
rules.plain_english: Before an LLC license is issued, reinstated or reactivated, the LLC must give CSLB proof it meets the insurance requirement, including a Certificate of Liability Insurance signed by the insurer's authorized agent or employee. The insurer (or surplus line broker) reports policy details to CSLB, and CSLB may post the insurer, policy numbers and limits online.

parameters.document: Certificate of Liability Insurance signed by authorized agent or employee of insurer
parameters.due: prior to issuance, reinstatement, or reactivation
insurer_reports: date and amount of claim payments

rules.applies_to: LLC licensees
rules.quote: For any insurance policy secured by a licensee in satisfaction of this section, a Certificate of Liability Insurance, signed by an authorized agent or employee of the insurer, shall be submitted electronically or otherwise to the registrar.

rules.title: Report $1M+ multifamily rental load-bearing defect judgments or settlements within 90 days
rules.plain_english: A licensee must report to CSLB in writing within 90 days of learning of a judgment, signed settlement or arbitration award of $1 million or more against it in an action filed on or after Jan 1, 2019, if all criteria are met: it alleges fraud, negligence, breach of contract or warranty or similar; it involves a load-bearing failure or substantial risk of one in a multifamily rental residential building caused by the licensee's work; and, if a civil action, it was designated a complex case. Late or missing reports are grounds for discipline, but not criminal penalties.

parameters.trigger: licensee has knowledge of final judgment, executed settlement agreement, or final arbitration award
all_criteria_required: alleges fraud, deceit, negligence, breach of contract or express/implied warranty, misrepresentation, incompetence, recklessness, wrongful death, or strict liability while acting as contractor
failure or substantial risk of failure in load bearing portions of multifamily rental residential structure
caused by licensee's construction, repair, alteration, improvement, moving, wrecking or demolishing of the structure, personally or through others
if civil action: designated complex case under CRC 3.400-3.403 for construction defect or related insurance coverage
parameters.excluded: residential construction subject to Civil Code 895 et seq. (SB 800)
parameters.penalty: grounds for disciplinary action; no criminal penalties
parameters.confidentiality: report does not violate a confidential settlement agreement (7071.22(b))

rules.applies_to: Licensees (and former licensees/personnel per 7071.22(a)) building or repairing multifamily rental housing
rules.quote: A licensee shall report to the registrar in writing within 90 days after the licensee has knowledge of any civil action resulting in a final judgment, executed settlement agreement, or final arbitration award in which the licensee is named as a defendant or cross-defendant, filed on or after January 1, 2019, that meets all of the following criteria:
rules.notes: CSLB returns the report with no action if it finds no violation, the public interest is served, or discipline is unnecessary; a returned report is deemed a complaint resolved in the licensee's favor.

rules.title: Multi-defendant defect cases: every contractor apportioned $15,000+ must report
rules.plain_english: When more than one contractor is named in a reportable multifamily defect action, every contractor apportioned liability by the court or by agreement must report it, except contractors assigned less than $15,000.

parameters.applies_when: more than one contractor named as defendant or cross-defendant in action meeting 7071.20 criteria

rules.applies_to: General and specialty contractors named in multifamily defect actions
rules.quote: all contractors who are apportioned any liability either by the court or pursuant to an agreement between parties, shall report the action pursuant to subdivision (a). This subdivision does not apply to a contractor who is named as a defendant or cross-defendant, but is assigned liability of less than fifteen thousand dollars ($15,000) in the action.

rules.title: Required contents of a 7071.20 defect report
rules.plain_english: The report must be signed by the licensee and give the license number and the facts of the event. If a court was involved, it must also list the case title, court or agency name, docket number, claim or file number, and the date of the event.
rules.applies_to: Licensees filing 7071.20 reports
rules.quote: shall be signed by the licensee and shall set forth the license number of the licensee and the facts that constitute the reportable event. If the reportable event involves the action of a court, the report shall also set forth the following: (1) The title of the matter. (2) The court or agency name. (3) The docket number. (4) The claim or file number.
rules.notes: Good candidate for a generated report form.

rules.title: Contractor's CGL, defect or professional liability insurer reports qualifying payments within 30 days
rules.plain_english: An insurer that pays all or part of a judgment, settlement or award meeting the 7071.20 criteria must report it to CSLB within 30 days, with the licensee's name and license number, claim number, total amount, amount the insurer paid, and the payee.

parameters.who: insurer providing commercial general liability, construction defect, or professional liability insurance
parameters.trigger: insurer payment (all or part) of qualifying judgment, settlement, or award

rules.applies_to: Insurers of licensees; licensees (their insurer's report may trigger CSLB review)
rules.quote: An insurer providing a licensee commercial general liability insurance, construction defect insurance, or professional liability insurance shall report to the registrar within 30 days of all or a portion of the insurer’s payment of a civil action judgment, settlement payment, or arbitration award, that meets all of the requirements of Section 7071.20,
rules.notes: The licensee's own 90-day duty (7071.20) applies regardless of the insurer report.

rules.title: CSLB notifies within 15 days of approval; license issues when the initial fee is paid
rules.plain_english: Within 15 days after approving an application, CSLB notifies the applicant that the license can be issued once the initial license fee is paid, and issues the license when the fee is paid.

parameters.trigger: approval of application
parameters.next_step: pay initial license fee (Article 8, B&P 7135 et seq.)

rules.applies_to: Approved applicants
rules.quote: the registrar, within 15 days after approval of the application, shall notify the applicant that a license may be issued to him on payment of the initial license fee provided in Article 8 (commencing at Section 7135), and, when the initial license fee is paid, shall issue a license to him
rules.notes: Applicant must pay the initial license fee within 90 days of notice or the application is void (7074(a)(2)).

rules.title: Return pocket license cards within 5 days of suspension, revocation, denial of renewal or departure
rules.plain_english: All pocket license cards must be returned to CSLB within 5 days of a suspension, revocation or denial of renewal. When a partner, officer or manager leaves a company, they surrender their card to the company, and the company must mail or deliver it to CSLB within 5 days.

triggers: cardholder leaves non-individual licensee (deadline runs after surrender to licensee)

rules.applies_to: Licensees and their partners, officers and managers
rules.quote: All cards issued shall be surrendered upon the suspension, revocation, or denial of renewal of the license, and shall be mailed or delivered to the board within five days of the suspension, revocation, or denial.

rules.title: Crime-based denial: CSLB sets a reapply date no more than 5 years out
rules.plain_english: CSLB may deny an application for failing to follow its rules or on B&P 480 grounds. If the denial is for a crime substantially related to contracting, CSLB must state the earliest date the applicant can reapply, no more than 5 years after the decision, and all evidence of rehabilitation is considered on reapplication.

parameters.trigger: effective date of decision or service of notice under B&P 485(b)
grounds_for_denial: failure to comply with CSLB rule or regulation

rules.applies_to: Applicants denied for crimes
rules.quote: The date set by the registrar shall not be more than five years from the effective date of the decision or service of notice under subdivision (b) of Section 485.

rules.title: Probationary license instead of denial; 30 days to show cause before revocation
rules.plain_english: Instead of denying an application, CSLB may issue a probationary license with conditions. If problems come up during probation, CSLB notifies the licensee to show cause within 30 days why the license should not be revoked, and the license cannot be renewed while proceedings are pending.

parameters.procedure: Administrative Procedure Act (Gov Code 11500 et seq.)

rules.applies_to: Applicants with criminal or compliance history
rules.quote: In lieu of denying licensure as authorized under this section, the registrar may issue an applicant a probationary license with terms and conditions.

rules.title: Application voids if the exam is not passed within 18 months of acceptance
rules.plain_english: An application for an original license, added classification or new qualifier becomes void if the applicant or examinee does not pass the exam within 18 months after CSLB accepts the application. A new application and fee are then required.

parameters.trigger: date application deemed acceptable by CSLB
parameters.consequence: application void; reapplication fee required; voided application not returned

rules.applies_to: License applicants and examinees
rules.quote: The applicant or the examinee for the applicant has failed to achieve a passing grade in the qualifying examination within 18 months after the application has been deemed acceptable by the board.

rules.title: Application voids if the fee, bond or documents are not filed within 90 days of notice
rules.plain_english: An application becomes void if, after notice, the applicant does not pay the initial license fee within 90 days, does not file the required bond (or cash deposit) or other documents within 90 days, or does not return a rejected application within 90 days. It is also void if withdrawn or denied after disciplinary proceedings.

triggers.item: file bond, cash/cashier's check deposit, or other required documents
return application rejected as insufficient or incomplete
triggers.clock_starts: date of original notice or rejection

rules.applies_to: License applicants
rules.quote: (2) The applicant for an original license, after having been notified to do so, fails to pay the initial license fee within 90 days from the date of the notice. (3) The applicant, after having been notified to do so, fails to file within 90 days from the date of the notice any bond or lawful money or cashier’s check deposited

rules.title: Void date extendable up to 90 days, or one free exam reschedule, for emergencies
rules.plain_english: If a medical emergency or other circumstance beyond the applicant's control caused a missed step or exam, and it is documented, CSLB may extend the void date by up to 90 days or let the applicant reschedule one exam without a fee.
rules.applies_to: License applicants
rules.quote: The void date on an application may be extended up to 90 days or one examination may be rescheduled without a fee upon documented evidence by the applicant that the failure to complete the application process or to appear for an examination was due to a medical emergency or other circumstance beyond the control of the applicant.
rules.notes: Extension and free reschedule are alternatives ('or').

rules.title: Display the license at the main office; show proof on demand
rules.plain_english: The license certificate must be displayed at the licensee's main office or chief place of business, and the licensee must show proof of a current license and renewal on request.

parameters.display_location: main office or chief place of business

rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.quote: The license shall be displayed in the licensee’s main office or chief place of business. Satisfactory evidence of the possession of a license and the current renewal thereof shall be provided by the licensee upon demand.

rules.title: Licenses cannot be transferred, sold or loaned
rules.plain_english: No license of any type or classification can be transferred to another person or entity under any circumstances. Buying a company does not carry over its license unless a reissuance rule below applies.
rules.applies_to: All licensees; buyers of contracting businesses
rules.quote: No license, regardless of type or classification, shall be transferable to any other person or entity under any circumstances.

rules.title: When a license number can be reissued or moved to a new entity
rules.plain_english: A canceled, revoked, suspended or long-expired license number can be reissued to the same individual, to the same partnership with unchanged partners, or to the same corporation or LLC with unchanged Secretary of State status. It can move to a new entity for parent/subsidiary mergers, domestic/foreign conversions, a family member or family-formed company continuing a deceased or absent licensee's business, a corporation or LLC in which the individual licensee holds more than 50% of the voting power, or an LLC formed by a corporation with the same personnel.

reissue_same_holder: partnership with no change in partners or structure
corporation with no change in SOS status
LLC with no change in SOS status
reassign_new_entity: corporation/LLC: parent merged or created subsidiary, subsidiary merged into parent, or domestic/foreign filing change, continuing the business
individual immediate family member of deceased or absent individual licensee
corporation/LLC created by immediate family to continue deceased or absent individual licensee's business
corporation/LLC formed by individual licensee holding >50% of voting power directly or indirectly
LLC formed by corporation to continue its business after corporate license cancellation, same personnel

rules.applies_to: Licensees restructuring, converting to a corporation or LLC, or continuing a family business
rules.quote: To a corporation or limited liability company when the corporation or limited liability company is formed by an individual licensee and the individual licensee maintains ownership directly or indirectly of shares or membership interests evidencing more than 50 percent of the voting power.
rules.notes: Reissuance after expiration applies only beyond the renewal period in B&P 7141 (outside this chunk).

rules.title: Sole owner dies: license canceled; family may request a continuance within 90 days
rules.plain_english: An individual license is canceled when the licensee dies. An immediate family member may request in writing, within 90 days of the death, a continuance to finish jobs in progress and take new work for a limited time. CSLB may require the bonds within 90 days of its notice, and the family member must get their own license to keep contracting after that.

parameters.trigger: death of individual licensee
continuance_scope: undertake new work for a reasonable time set by CSLB rule

rules.applies_to: Families of deceased sole-owner licensees; owners with jobs in progress
rules.quote: An immediate member of the family of the deceased licensee may request a continuance of the license to complete projects in progress and undertake new work for a reasonable amount of time to be determined by rules of the board. The request for a continuance must be made in writing and received at the board’s headquarters office within 90 days after the death.
rules.notes: Continuance length is set by CSLB regulation, not stated here.

rules.title: General partner dies: partnership license canceled; notify CSLB and request continuance within 90 days
rules.plain_english: A partnership license is canceled when a general partner dies. The remaining partners must notify CSLB in writing within 90 days (a late notice is grounds for discipline) and may request a continuance within 90 days to finish projects and take new work for a limited time. They must get a new license to keep contracting after the continuance ends.

parameters.trigger: death of a general partner
continuance_scope: undertake new work for reasonable time

rules.applies_to: Partnership licensees
rules.quote: A partnership license shall be canceled upon the death of a general partner. The remaining partner or partners shall notify the registrar in writing within 90 days of the death of a general partner. Failure to notify the registrar within 90 days of the death is grounds for disciplinary action.

rules.title: General partner leaves or partnership dissolves: license canceled; 90-day notice
rules.plain_english: A partnership license is canceled when a general partner leaves or the partnership dissolves. Notice is due in writing within 90 days. If late, cancellation takes effect on the date CSLB receives notice, and the late notice is grounds for discipline. A continuance (requested within 90 days) covers only projects contracted before the departure; new work needs a new license.

parameters.late_notice_consequence: cancellation effective date written notice received at CSLB HQ; grounds for discipline
parameters.continuance_scope: only projects contracted for or in progress before disassociation/dissolution

rules.applies_to: Partnership licensees
rules.quote: A partnership license shall be canceled upon the disassociation of a general partner or upon the dissolution of the partnership. The disassociating partner or the remaining partner or partners shall notify the registrar in writing within 90 days of the disassociation of a general partner or dissolution of the partnership.

rules.title: Limited partner dies or leaves: notify within 90 days; sole limited partner must be replaced within 90 days
rules.plain_english: General partners must notify CSLB in writing within 90 days when a limited partner dies or leaves. This does not affect the license unless the partnership had only one limited partner; then the license is canceled unless a new limited partner is added within 90 days. A continuance may be requested within 90 days if canceled.

parameters.replacement_needed_if: partnership license had only one limited partner
parameters.late_notice_consequence: grounds for discipline; for disassociation, effective date becomes date notice received

rules.applies_to: Limited partnership licensees
rules.quote: The death of a limited partner will not affect the partnership license unless the partnership license has only one limited partner. In this case, the license will be canceled upon the death of the limited partner unless a new limited partner is added to the license within 90 days of the death.

rules.title: Joint venture license canceled when a member license ends or the JV dissolves; 90-day notice
rules.plain_english: A joint venture license is canceled if any member entity's license is canceled, revoked or disassociated, or the JV dissolves. CSLB must be notified in writing within 90 days. Late notice makes cancellation effective on receipt and is grounds for discipline. Remaining members may request a continuance within 90 days, but only to finish existing projects.

triggers: cancellation, revocation, or disassociation of any member entity license
parameters.late_notice_consequence: cancellation effective date written notice received; grounds for discipline
parameters.continuance_scope: projects contracted for or in progress before disassociation/dissolution

rules.applies_to: Joint venture licensees
rules.quote: A joint venture license shall be canceled upon the cancellation, revocation, or disassociation of any of its entity licenses or upon the dissolution of the joint venture. The registrar shall be notified in writing within 90 days of the disassociation of a joint venture entity or dissolution of the joint venture.
rules.notes: A JV license depends on every member license staying active; track all of them.

rules.title: Corporation or LLC dissolves, merges or surrenders: license canceled; notify within 90 days
rules.plain_english: A corporation or LLC license is canceled when the company dissolves, merges or surrenders its right to do business in California. The company must notify CSLB in writing within 90 days. If late, cancellation is effective when CSLB receives notice. If the company never notifies, CSLB cancels the license 60 days after it discovers the change in corporate or Secretary of State records. Late notice is grounds for discipline.

triggers: surrender of right to do business in California
parameters.late_notice_consequence: cancellation effective date written notice received; grounds for discipline

rules.applies_to: Corporation and LLC licensees (including after mergers and acquisitions)
rules.quote: A corporation license shall be canceled upon the corporation’s dissolution, merger, or surrender of its right to do business in this state. The corporation or participating tribe shall notify the registrar in writing within 90 days of the dissolution, merger, or surrender.
rules.notes: Unlike partnerships, the text gives no continuance for corporations or LLCs. See license-number-reissue-reassignment for merger cases.

rules.title: Dispute a cancellation date within 90 days of CSLB's notice
rules.plain_english: A licensee that disputes the cancellation date may petition CSLB, showing good cause. The petition must be received within 90 days of CSLB's official cancellation notice.

parameters.trigger: date of CSLB official notice of cancellation
parameters.standard: good cause

rules.applies_to: Licensees with canceled licenses
rules.quote: The registrar shall review and accept the petition of a licensee who disputes the date of cancellation upon a showing of good cause. This petition shall be received within 90 days of the board’s official notice of cancellation.

rules.title: Voluntary surrender cancels the license immediately with no refund
rules.plain_english: A license voluntarily surrendered is canceled as soon as CSLB receives the request, with no refund of fees. To get it back, the licensee must pay all fees and meet every requirement for an original license.

parameters.cancellation_effective: upon receipt of request by registrar
parameters.reinstatement_requires: all fees and qualifications for an original license

rules.applies_to: Licensees surrendering licenses
rules.quote: Upon the voluntary surrender of a license by a licensee, the registrar shall order the license canceled. Cancellation will be effected upon receipt of the request by the registrar. No refund will be made of any fee which a licensee may have paid prior to the surrender of the license.
rules.notes: Inactivation (7076.5) is usually the better option if the business may resume.

rules.title: Corporation or LLC not in good standing with the Secretary of State: suspended 30 days after CSLB notice
rules.plain_english: If a corporation or LLC licensee is not registered and in good standing with the Secretary of State, CSLB sends written notice, and the license is automatically suspended 30 days later unless the company proves good standing. It can be reinstated at any time with proof.

parameters.trigger: date of CSLB written notice of SOS non-good-standing
parameters.consequence: automatic suspension by operation of law
parameters.cure: proof satisfactory to registrar of SOS registration and good standing (any time)

rules.applies_to: Corporation and LLC licensees
rules.quote: The registrar shall notify the licensee in writing of its failure to be registered and in good standing with the Secretary of State and that the licensee shall be suspended 30 days from the date of the notice if the licensee does not provide proof satisfactory to the registrar that it is properly registered and in good standing with the Secretary of State.
rules.notes: SOS suspension often follows Franchise Tax Board issues; monitor SOS status regularly.

rules.title: LLC suspended for Secretary of State status: managers and officers personally liable up to $1M each
rules.plain_english: If an LLC license is suspended for not being in good standing with the Secretary of State, each person identified in B&P 7028.5 is personally liable up to $1 million each for third-party damages from licensed work done during the suspension, unless there was substantial compliance with licensing requirements.

parameters.scope: damages to third parties from any act or contract requiring a license

rules.applies_to: LLC licensees and their managers, officers and members
rules.quote: Where the license of a limited liability company is suspended pursuant to subdivision (a), each person within the company identified in Section 7028.5 shall be personally liable up to one million dollars ($1,000,000) each for damages resulting to third parties in connection with the company’s performance, during the period of suspension, of any act or contract where a license is required
rules.notes: Who 7028.5 covers is described in an earlier section of the book, not this chunk.

rules.title: Inactive license: no contracting until reactivated; valid 4 years from due date
rules.plain_english: A licensee not doing licensed work may inactivate by filing a CSLB form with its current license certificate (or a replacement fee if lost). While inactive it cannot contract until it reactivates. Inactive licenses are valid for 4 years from their due date.

to_inactivate: current active license certificate (or replacement fee if lost)

rules.applies_to: Licensees not currently contracting
rules.quote: The holder of an inactive license shall not be entitled to practice as a contractor until their license is reactivated. (b) Any licensed contractor who is not engaged in work or activities which require a contractor’s license may apply for an inactive license. (c) Inactive licenses shall be valid for a period of four years from their due date.
rules.notes: Contracting on an inactive license is unlicensed contracting. The 2026 amendment (SB 861) changed this section; the book does not mark which subdivisions changed.

rules.title: Inactive license: no bond, qualifier or workers' comp requirements
rules.plain_english: While a license is inactive, the contractor's bond, disciplinary bond, qualifier bond, qualifier requirement and workers' compensation requirements do not apply. A new applicant may ask for the license to be issued inactive, unless it is subject to a disciplinary bond.
rules.applies_to: Inactive licensees and new applicants
rules.quote: During the period that an existing license is inactive, no bonding requirement pursuant to Section 7071.6, 7071.8, or 7071.9, qualifier requirement pursuant to Section 7068, or workers’ compensation requirements pursuant to Section 7125 shall apply.
rules.notes: Reactivation requires restoring all of these.

rules.title: Inactive license: renew on schedule; reactivate by paying the full active fee (no exam)
rules.plain_english: An inactive license must still be renewed on each renewal date with the inactive renewal fee. To reactivate, file an application, pay the full active renewal fee and meet all other requirements (bond, qualifier, workers' comp). No exam is needed. No refund is given for fees paid before inactivation, and CSLB may still discipline an inactive licensee.

parameters.inactive_renewal: each established renewal date with inactive renewal fee

rules.applies_to: Inactive licensees
rules.quote: An inactive license may be reactivated by submitting an application acceptable to the registrar, by paying the full renewal fee for an active license and by fulfilling all other requirements of this chapter. No examination shall be required to reactivate an inactive license.
rules.notes: Fee amounts are in B&P 7137 (outside this chunk).

rules.title: Every original license is probationary until first renewal
rules.plain_english: Every new license (not added classifications) is probationary until its first renewal. If CSLB learns of grounds for denial, suspension or revocation during that time, it may order the licensee to show cause within 30 days why the license should not be revoked, and the license cannot be renewed while proceedings are pending.
rules.applies_to: Newly licensed contractors
rules.quote: Every original license, except an additional classification issued pursuant to Section 7059, shall be a probationary license until such time as the license is renewed.

rules.title: Report any change to license record information within 90 days
rules.plain_english: Licensees must notify CSLB in writing on its form within 90 days of any change to their recorded information, including business address, personnel, business name, qualifier bond exemption or multiple-license exemption. If late, the change takes effect only on the date CSLB receives notice, and the late notice is grounds for discipline.

parameters.trigger: date of change
parameters.late_consequence: change effective date notice received at CSLB HQ; grounds for disciplinary action

rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.quote: licensees shall notify the registrar, on a form prescribed by the registrar, in writing within 90 days of any change to information recorded under this chapter. This notification requirement shall include, but not be limited to, changes in business address, personnel, business name, qualifying individual bond exemption pursuant to Section 7071.9,
rules.notes: Good candidate for a change-tracking reminder.

rules.title: Expired, suspended or canceled licensees must keep their address current for 5 years
rules.plain_english: A licensee whose license is expired or suspended (but renewable) or canceled must report address changes in writing within 90 days and keep a current address of record for 5 years after the license expires or is canceled.
rules.applies_to: Former and lapsed licensees
rules.quote: A licensee whose license is expired or suspended, and is renewable under Section 7141, or whose license is canceled, shall notify the registrar in writing of a change of address of record within 90 days, and shall maintain a current address of record during the five-year period immediately following the expiration or cancellation of the license.

rules.title: Report a valid email address at application and renewal; CSLB email is presumed delivered
rules.plain_english: Applicants must give CSLB their email address (if they have one) when applying, and licensees and registrants must give it at renewal. The email is not a public record. Email CSLB sends to that address is presumed delivered, so monitor it.

parameters.valid_email_definition: address at which person currently receives email when the application, registration or renewal is submitted

rules.applies_to: All applicants, registrants and licensees with email
rules.quote: An applicant for licensure or registration that has a valid email address shall report to the board that email address at the time of application. (b) A registrant or licensee that has a valid email address shall report that email address to the board at the time of renewal.
rules.notes: Because of the delivery presumption, a CSLB notice sent by email may be treated as received when sent, which could start deadlines that run from 'notice'. This is an inference; the text does not say so directly.

rules.title: CSLB arbitration (optional) for complaints with damages over the bond amount and under $50,000
rules.plain_english: After investigating a complaint involving certain violations (B&P 7107, 7109, 7110, 7113, 7119, 7120) or any construction contract dispute, CSLB may send it to arbitration if both sides agree and the damages are 'material', meaning more than the $25,000 bond amount but less than $50,000. Other conditions: arbitration serves the public better than discipline, the licensee was in good standing with no history of similar violations or pending discipline, the parties have no private arbitration agreement, and they were advised of Civil Code 2855. The arbitrator's award is treated as a CSLB order.

covered_violations: any complaint arising from a contract involving works of improvement
conditions: evidence of material damages
arbitration better serves public interest than discipline
no history of repeated or similar violations
licensee in good standing at time of violation
no outstanding disciplinary actions
no prior private arbitration agreement
parties advised of Civil Code 2855

rules.applies_to: Licensees and owners/consumers with CSLB complaints
rules.quote: For the purposes of paragraph (1), “material damages” means damages greater than the amount of the bond required under subdivision (a) of Section 7071.6, but less than fifty thousand dollars ($50,000).
rules.notes: The $25,000 lower bound is the current 7071.6(a) bond amount; it moves if the bond amount changes. A contract with a private arbitration clause takes the dispute out of this program.

rules.title: CSLB arbitration is mandatory when damages or contract price are at or below the bond amount
rules.plain_english: When a possible violation exists and the contract price or the damages claimed are at or below the bond amount ($25,000), CSLB must refer the complaint to arbitration if the public-interest, good-standing, no-history, no-pending-discipline and no-private-arbitration conditions are met. The licensee's consent is not required.

parameters.measure: contract price or demand for damages

rules.applies_to: Licensees and owners/consumers with smaller CSLB complaints
rules.quote: In all cases in which a possible violation of the sections set forth in paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) exists and the contract price, or the demand for damages is equal to or less than the amount of the bond required under Section 7071.6, but, regardless of the contract price, the complaint shall be referred to arbitration,
rules.notes: The printed text looks garbled or incomplete ('but, regardless of the contract price,' runs straight into 'the complaint shall be referred'); the official statute likely limits the demand for damages to the bond amount regardless of contract price. Verify against the official code before coding this threshold.

rules.title: Return the CSLB arbitration agreement or notice within 30 calendar days
rules.plain_english: Once CSLB offers arbitration, both parties must return the 'agreement to arbitrate' (optional cases) or the 'notice to arbitrate' (mandatory cases) within 30 calendar days of the mailing date. In mandatory cases, a complainant who does not return it has the complaint closed, but a licensee who does not return it can still be sent to arbitration and bound by an enforceable award.

parameters.trigger: date CSLB mails the agreement or notice
parameters.licensee_failure_mandatory_case: arbitration and award enforcement may proceed anyway
parties_informed_of: consequences of administrative arbitration vs judicial remedies
right to retain counsel at own expense

rules.applies_to: Licensees and complainants in CSLB arbitration
rules.quote: This agreement shall be returned to the registrar within 30 calendar days of the date that the agreement is mailed by the registrar. The return of this agreement by the parties shall authorize the registrar to proceed with administrative arbitration.
rules.notes: Calendar days, not business days.

rules.title: Strike and rank the arbitrator list within 7 days or accept all names
rules.plain_english: In CSLB arbitration, each party gets the same list of possible arbitrators and has 7 days from the mailing date to cross off objectionable names, rank the rest and return it. If a party does not return the list in time, every name on it is treated as acceptable. CSLB pays the arbitration fee from the Contractors License Fund.

parameters.trigger: mailing date of arbitrator list
agreement_must_include: names, addresses, phone numbers of parties
amount in dollars or other remedy sought

rules.applies_to: Licensees and complainants in CSLB arbitration
rules.quote: Each party to the dispute shall have seven days from the mailing date in which to cross off any names to which it objects, number the remaining names to indicate the order of preference, and return the list to the board or appointed arbitration association. If a party does not return the list within the time specified, all persons named in the list are acceptable.
rules.notes: The chunk ends partway through 7085.5(b)(1); the remaining arbitration rules are in the next chunk.

rules.title: Small-dollar complaints must go to CSLB arbitration
rules.plain_english: If a complaint alleges a possible violation of the sections listed in B&P 7085(a)(1) (7107, 7109, 7110, 7113, 7119 or 7120) and the contract price or the damages demanded is at or below the contractor bond amount required by B&P 7071.6 ($25,000), CSLB must refer the complaint to its arbitration program (mandatory arbitration).

parameters.trigger: possible violation of the sections listed in B&P 7085(a)(1)
parameters.threshold_test: contract price OR demand for damages <= bond amount required under B&P 7071.6
parameters.result: complaint shall be referred to arbitration
parameters.bond_amount_source: B&P 7071.6(a): contractor's bond "in the sum of twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000)" (2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF page 295)

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and complainants (owners) in CSLB complaints
rules.quote: In all cases in which a possible violation of the sections set forth in paragraph (1) of subdivision (a) exists and the contract price, or the demand for damages is equal to or less than the amount of the bond required under Section 7071.6, but, regardless of the contract price, the complaint shall be referred to arbitration
rules.notes: The 7071.6 bond is $25,000 (PDF page 295), so mandatory referral applies at or below $25,000. The sections in 7085(a)(1) are 7107, 7109, 7110, 7113, 7119 and 7120 (PDF page 324). For voluntary arbitration under 7085(a), "material damages" means more than the 7071.6(a) bond amount but less than $50,000. The printed sentence is ambiguous ("but, regardless of the contract price"); read with the full statute.
rules.correction: No error. Added bond_amount_usd = 25000 from B&P 7071.6(a) (PDF page 295) and the 7085(a)(1) section list (PDF page 324) so the threshold can be computed; the original note said the amount was not on these pages. plain_english updated on 2026-11-27 to name the sections and the $25,000 bond amount.

rules.title: Arbitrator's award is a CSLB registrar order
rules.plain_english: An award issued by a CSLB arbitrator counts as an order of the Registrar, so ignoring it has licensing consequences (see automatic suspension under B&P 7085.6).
rules.applies_to: Licensees and complainants in CSLB arbitration
rules.quote: An arbitrator may render an award and that award shall be deemed to be an order of the registrar.

rules.title: Return voluntary agreement to arbitrate within 30 calendar days
rules.plain_english: When CSLB decides a dispute is suitable for voluntary arbitration under B&P 7085(a), it mails an agreement to arbitrate to both the owner and the contractor. It must be returned within 30 calendar days of the mailing date; returning it authorizes CSLB to proceed. CSLB must also explain the consequences of choosing arbitration over court and that parties may hire counsel at their own expense.

parameters.start_event: date registrar mails the agreement to arbitrate
parameters.effect_of_return: authorizes registrar to proceed with administrative arbitration

rules.applies_to: Owners/complainants and licensed contractors in voluntary CSLB arbitration (B&P 7085(a) cases)
rules.quote: The registrar shall forward an “agreement to arbitrate” to the complainant and the licensee. This agreement shall be returned to the registrar within 30 calendar days of the date that the agreement is mailed by the registrar.
rules.notes: Voluntary track. For the mandatory track (7085(b)) see B&P 7085.4(b).

rules.title: Mandatory arbitration notice: 30 days; complainant non-return closes complaint
rules.plain_english: In mandatory arbitration cases, CSLB mails a notice to arbitrate to both parties, due back within 30 calendar days of mailing. If the owner/complainant does not return it, the complaint is closed. If the contractor does not return it, CSLB can still send the case to arbitration and enforce the award.

parameters.start_event: date registrar mails the notice to arbitrate
parameters.licensee_failure_to_return: does not stop referral to arbitration or enforcement of award under B&P 7085.6 (contested or noncontested hearing)

rules.applies_to: Owners/complainants and licensed contractors in mandatory CSLB arbitration (B&P 7085(b) cases)
rules.quote: This notice shall be returned to the registrar within 30 calendar days of the date that the notice is mailed by the registrar. The complainant’s failure to return an executed copy of the notice shall result in the closure of the complaint.
rules.notes: Contractor non-response is not a defense; the hearing can proceed and the award is enforceable.

rules.title: Required contents of a CSLB agreement to arbitrate; board pays fee
rules.plain_english: Every CSLB agreement to arbitrate must list each party's name, address and phone number, the issue in dispute, and the dollar amount or other remedy sought. The arbitration fee is paid by CSLB from the Contractors License Fund, not by the parties.

required_fields: amount in dollars or other remedy sought

rules.applies_to: Parties to CSLB arbitration
rules.quote: All “agreements to arbitrate” shall include the names, addresses, and telephone numbers of the parties to the dispute, the issue in dispute, and the amount in dollars or any other remedy sought. The appropriate fee shall be paid by the board from the Contractors License Fund.

rules.title: Strike and rank arbitrator list within 7 days
rules.plain_english: Each party gets the same list of possible arbitrators and has 7 days from the mailing date to cross off objectionable names, rank the rest, and return it. If you do not return it on time, every name on the list is treated as acceptable to you. One arbitrator hears the case unless CSLB or the association directs more.

parameters.start_event: mailing date of the arbitrator list
parameters.default_if_not_returned: all persons on list deemed acceptable
parameters.mandatory_cases: in B&P 7085(b) cases the board/association may appoint the arbitrator directly (7085.5(b)(2))

rules.applies_to: Parties to voluntary CSLB arbitration
rules.quote: Each party to the dispute shall have seven days from the mailing date in which to cross off any names to which it objects, number the remaining names to indicate the order of preference, and return the list to the board or appointed arbitration association. If a party does not return the list within the time specified, all persons named in the list are acceptable.
rules.notes: Statute does not say calendar vs. working days for this 7-day period; treat as calendar days conservatively.

rules.title: Arbitrator must have no interest and must disclose bias
rules.plain_english: A person with a financial or personal interest in the outcome cannot be the arbitrator. Before accepting, the arbitrator must disclose anything that could delay the hearing or suggest bias; CSLB or the association then replaces the arbitrator or asks the parties for comment, and its disqualification decision is conclusive.
