rules.quote: In the case of outstanding final liabilities assessed by the State Board of Equalization, this section shall not apply to any outstanding final liability if the licensee has entered into an installment payment agreement for that liability with the State Board of Equalization and is in compliance with the terms of that agreement.
rules.notes: The text grants this exception only for BOE liabilities. It does not state a similar exception for DIR, EDD or FTB debts.

rules.title: Home improvement article: 'person' = natural persons; senior citizen = age 65+
rules.plain_english: In the home improvement article, 'person' means only individuals (natural persons), and a 'senior citizen' is anyone 65 or older. Senior buyers get a five-day instead of three-day right to cancel.

parameters.person: natural persons only (overrides B&P 7025 definition for Article 10)

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts and salespersons (Article 10)
rules.quote: (a) “Person” as used in this article is limited to natural persons, notwithstanding the definition of person in Section 7025. (b) “Senior citizen” means an individual who is 65 years of age or older.
rules.notes: Contract software should capture whether any buyer is 65+ to select the 5-day cancellation notice.

rules.title: Home improvement contractor (incl. pool contractors) must meet Article 10
rules.plain_english: Any licensed contractor, including a swimming pool contractor, who does home improvement work full time or part time is a home improvement contractor and must meet every requirement in Article 10.
rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors doing residential home improvement work
rules.quote: A home improvement contractor, including a swimming pool contractor, is a contractor as defined and licensed under this chapter who is engaged in the business of home improvement either full time or part time. A home improvement contractor shall satisfy all requirements imposed by this article.

rules.title: What counts as 'home improvement' (incl. disaster rebuilds)
rules.plain_english: Home improvement means repairing, remodeling, altering, converting, modernizing or adding to residential property, plus rebuilding homes damaged in a declared natural disaster. It includes work like driveways, pools, spas, patios, solar, landscaping, fences, porches, garages and basements, and installing home improvement goods or services.

activities: reconstruction/restoration/rebuilding of residential property damaged or destroyed by a declared natural disaster
disaster_declaration_triggers: Governor state of emergency under Gov. Code 8625
Presidential emergency or major disaster declaration
examples: swimming pools, spas and hot tubs
other improvements of structures or land adjacent to a dwelling house

rules.applies_to: Classifying whether a residential job is home improvement (triggers B&P 7159 contract rules)
rules.quote: “Home improvement” means the repairing, remodeling, altering, converting, or modernizing of, or adding to, residential property, as well as the reconstruction, restoration, or rebuilding of a residential property that is damaged or destroyed by a natural disaster for which a state of emergency is proclaimed by the Governor
rules.notes: New single-family home construction for an owner is covered separately by B&P 7164.

rules.title: Home improvement goods or services
rules.plain_english: Home improvement goods and services are goods and services bought in connection with improving real property, such as carpeting, texture coating, fencing, AC or heating equipment and termite extermination. Goods affixed so they become part of the property count even if removable.
rules.applies_to: Sellers and installers of residential goods and services
rules.quote: Such home improvement goods and services include, but are not limited to, carpeting, texture coating, fencing, air conditioning or heating equipment, and termite extermination. Home improvement goods include goods which are to be so affixed to real property as to become a part of real property whether or not severable therefrom.

rules.title: Solar energy system: residential, 1 kW to 5 MW AC
rules.plain_english: For home improvement and solar disclosure rules, a solar energy system is a residential solar electric device producing at least 1 kW and no more than 5 MW AC peak that meets Public Resources Code 25782 eligibility criteria.

parameters.primary_purpose: collection and distribution of solar energy for generation of electricity

rules.applies_to: Residential solar installers and sellers
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 388 and 431
rules.quote: “solar energy system” means a solar energy device to be installed on a residential building or residential property that has the primary purpose of providing for the collection and distribution of solar energy for the generation of electricity, that produces at least one kilowatt, and not more than five megawatts, alternating current rated peak electricity
rules.notes: 7169(g) uses 'installed on a residential building' (text truncated at end of this chunk).

rules.title: Home improvement contract: oral or written, owner or tenant
rules.plain_english: A home improvement contract is any agreement, oral or written or in several documents, between a contractor and an owner, or a contractor and a tenant (in any size building), for home improvement work, including all labor, services and materials. Agreements by any salesperson with an owner or tenant to sell, install or furnish home improvement goods or services also count.

counterparties: tenant (regardless of number of units in building)
parameters.also_covers: agreements by a salesperson (registered or not) with owner or tenant for sale/installation/furnishing of home improvement goods or services

rules.applies_to: Residential contractors and salespersons
rules.quote: “Home improvement contract” means an agreement, whether oral or written, or contained in one or more documents, between a contractor and an owner or between a contractor and a tenant, regardless of the number of residence or dwelling units contained in the building in which the tenant resides
rules.notes: B&P 7159(b) adds the over-$500 aggregate price threshold for the B&P 7159 contract requirements.

rules.title: Home Improvement Salesperson (HIS) registration required
rules.plain_english: Anyone who solicits, sells, negotiates or signs home improvement contracts (including pools, spas and hot tubs) on behalf of a licensed contractor must be registered with CSLB as a Home Improvement Salesperson.
rules.applies_to: Sales staff of home improvement contractors
rules.quote: A home improvement salesperson shall register with the board in order to engage in the business of, or act in the capacity of, a home improvement salesperson.
rules.effective: Section amended effective January 1, 2026 (Stats 2025 ch 592, SB 861)
rules.notes: The book's history line shows a 2026 amendment but does not say which subdivision changed.

rules.title: HIS must disclose contractor's business name and license number first
rules.plain_english: Before soliciting or selling, a home improvement salesperson must tell the owner or tenant the business name and license number of the contractor they represent for that deal. An HIS may work for more than one contractor. Failing to disclose is grounds for discipline.

parameters.timing: before engaging in any soliciting, selling, negotiating or executing of contracts
parameters.violation: cause for disciplinary action under B&P 7155

rules.applies_to: Registered home improvement salespersons
rules.quote: However, prior to engaging in any activity described in subdivision (a) of this section, a home improvement salesperson shall identify to the owner or tenant the business name and license number of the contractor they are representing for the purposes of that transaction. Failure to do so is a cause of disciplinary action within the meaning of Section 7155.

rules.title: Who does not need HIS registration
rules.plain_english: Officers of a licensed corporation, managers/members/officers of a licensed LLC, general partners, and the qualifier do not need HIS registration, but only if they are personnel of record on that license at the time of the sale. Retail-store salespeople (buyer-initiated, fixed location), appointment setters, and service repairpersons limited to the requested repair are also exempt.

exempt_persons: officer of record of a licensed corporation
manager, member or officer of record of a licensed LLC
general partner listed on the license record of a licensed partnership
salesperson whose sales come from buyer-initiated negotiations at a fixed-location general merchandise retail establishment
person contacting buyers only to schedule appointments for a registered HIS
bona fide service repairperson employed by a licensed contractor, limited to the service/repair/emergency repair initially requested
parameters.condition_for_first_four: listed as personnel of record for the licensee responsible for the transaction at the time of the sales transaction

rules.applies_to: Contractors deciding who must register as HIS
rules.quote: The exemption to registration provided under paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) of subdivision (d) shall apply only to those individuals who, at the time of the sales transaction, are listed as personnel of record for the licensee responsible for soliciting, negotiating, or contracting for a service or improvement that is subject to regulation under this article.
rules.notes: Subdivision (e) names paragraphs (1)-(3); the qualifier is paragraph (3), so the personnel-of-record condition covers officers/LLC managers/members, general partners and qualifiers.

rules.title: Selling home improvement without HIS registration is a misdemeanor
rules.plain_english: It is a misdemeanor to work as a salesperson for a home improvement contractor, or to sell home improvement goods or services, without a current and valid HIS registration at the time of the sale. CSLB may also issue a citation.

parameters.offense: acting as home improvement salesperson without current valid registration at time of sales transaction

rules.applies_to: Unregistered salespersons
rules.quote: It is a misdemeanor for any person to engage in the occupation of salesperson for one or more home improvement contractors within this state without having, at the time of the sales transaction, a current and valid home improvement salesperson registration issued by the registrar.
rules.notes: The contractor who employs an unregistered salesperson is also subject to discipline (B&P 7154(d)).

rules.title: Security interest unenforceable if sale made by unregistered salesperson
rules.plain_english: If the home improvement contract was solicited by someone who was not a registered (or exempt) salesperson when the homeowner signed, any security interest the contractor took to secure payment cannot be enforced.

parameters.test_time: when the homeowner signs the home improvement contract

rules.applies_to: Contractors taking security interests on home improvement jobs
rules.quote: Any security interest taken by a contractor, to secure any payment for the performance of any act or conduct described in Section 7151 ... is unenforceable if the person soliciting the act or contract was not a duly registered salesperson or was not exempt from registration pursuant to Section 7152 at the time the homeowner signs the home improvement contract solicited by the salesperson.

rules.title: HIS application: written form, fee and fingerprints
rules.plain_english: A salesperson applies for HIS registration in writing on CSLB's form with the required fee and must submit fingerprints (electronically where available) for DOJ and FBI criminal history checks. CSLB may deny registration on B&P 480 grounds.

required: full set of fingerprints (electronic where readily available)

rules.applies_to: Home improvement salesperson applicants
rules.quote: As part of an application for a home improvement salesperson, the board shall require an applicant to furnish a full set of fingerprints for purposes of conducting criminal history record checks.
rules.notes: Fee amount is not stated in this excerpt.

rules.title: HIS registration expires two years from last day of month issued
rules.plain_english: A Home Improvement Salesperson registration expires two years after the last day of the month it was issued, and after renewal, two years from the date it last expired.

parameters.anchor_original: last day of the month in which the registration was issued
parameters.anchor_renewed: date on which the renewed registration last expired

rules.applies_to: Registered home improvement salespersons and their employers
rules.quote: All home improvement salesperson registrations issued under the provisions of this article shall expire two years from the last day of the month in which the registration was issued, or two years from the date on which the renewed registration last expired.
rules.notes: Employers should track each salesperson's expiration date; selling with an expired registration is a misdemeanor (B&P 7153).

rules.title: Renew HIS registration before it expires
rules.plain_english: To renew an unexpired HIS registration, file the CSLB renewal form and pay the renewal fee before expiration; the renewal runs two more years.

requirements: renewal form
renewal fee

rules.applies_to: Registered home improvement salespersons
rules.quote: To renew a home improvement salesperson registration, which has not expired, the registrant shall before the time at which the registration would otherwise expire, apply for renewal on a form prescribed by the registrar and pay a renewal fee prescribed by this chapter.

rules.title: Late HIS renewal: within 3 years with 50% penalty
rules.plain_english: An HIS renewal is delinquent if not postmarked or electronically received by the expiration date. A registration can still be renewed within three years after expiration by paying the renewal fee plus a penalty equal to 50% of the renewal fee. After three years, a new application is required.

parameters.after_window: new application for registration under B&P 7153.1

rules.applies_to: Home improvement salespersons with expired registrations
rules.quote: A registration may, however, still be renewed at any time within three years after its expiration upon the filing of an application for renewal on a form prescribed by the registrar and the payment of the renewal fee prescribed by this chapter and a delinquent renewal penalty equal to 50 percent of the renewal fee.
rules.notes: Renewal fee amount is not in this excerpt.

rules.title: Rejected HIS renewal: 90 days to return; 90-day petition window
rules.plain_english: If an HIS renewal is rejected as incomplete, the registrant must return it within 90 days of rejection or it is abandoned (a new application is then required). A good-cause petition disputing abandonment must be received within 90 days of the abandonment date.

parameters.measured_from: original date of rejection
parameters.consequence: application and fee deemed abandoned; new application under B&P 7153.1

rules.applies_to: Home improvement salespersons
rules.quote: If a registrant fails to return the application rejected for insufficiency or incompleteness within 90 days from the original date of rejection, the application and fee shall be deemed abandoned.

rules.title: Notify CSLB before a registered salesperson starts work
rules.plain_english: A home improvement contractor must file CSLB's form reporting the employment of a registered salesperson, including the salesperson's name and registration number, before the salesperson begins working for the contractor.

parameters.deadline: before the home improvement salesperson begins work for the contractor
parameters.electronic_filing: allowed if board implements system under B&P 7156.6

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors employing salespersons
rules.quote: A home improvement contractor licensed under this chapter shall notify the registrar in writing, on a form prescribed by the registrar, about the employment of a registered home improvement salesperson ... The form shall be submitted prior to the home improvement salesperson beginning work for the contractor.
rules.notes: Until CSLB has received this notice, the salesperson may not guide an owner in selecting a contractor (B&P 7156(c)).

rules.title: Notify CSLB within 90 days after a salesperson leaves
rules.plain_english: A home improvement contractor must notify CSLB on its form, with the salesperson's name and registration number, within 90 days after a registered salesperson stops working for the contractor.

parameters.measured_from: date the salesperson ceases to be employed

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors
rules.quote: The form shall be submitted within 90 days after the home improvement salesperson ceases to be employed by the contractor.

rules.title: Contractor discipline for not reporting salespersons or using unregistered ones
rules.plain_english: A contractor who fails to file the salesperson hire or termination notices, or who uses an unregistered person to sell home improvement contracts, is subject to CSLB discipline.

violations: employing unregistered person to sell home improvement contracts

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors
rules.quote: A home improvement contractor who employs a person to sell home improvement contracts while that person is not registered by the registrar as a home improvement salesperson as provided in this article, is subject to disciplinary action by the registrar.

rules.title: HIS registration may be suspended or revoked for violations
rules.plain_english: Any violation of the contractors law by a home improvement salesperson is cause for discipline; CSLB may suspend or revoke the registration through Administrative Procedure Act proceedings.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement salespersons
rules.quote: Violation of any provision of this chapter by a home improvement salesperson constitutes cause for disciplinary action. The registrar may suspend or revoke the registration of the home improvement salesperson if he or she is found to be in violation.

rules.title: Contractor disciplined for its salesperson's violations, even without knowledge
rules.plain_english: If a home improvement salesperson violates the law, the contractor who employed them at the time can be disciplined too, whether or not the contractor knew about or took part in the violation.

parameters.liable_party: contractor employing the salesperson at the time of the violation

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors employing salespersons
rules.quote: Violations of any provisions of this chapter by a home improvement salesperson likewise constitute cause for disciplinary action against the contractor, by whom he or she was employed at the time the violation occurred, whether or not the contractor had knowledge of or participated in the act or omission constituting violations of this chapter.

rules.title: Salesperson must account for and remit all payments to employing contractor
rules.plain_english: A home improvement salesperson who fails to account for or turn over to the employing contractor any payment received on a job commits a misdemeanor and is subject to discipline.

parameters.duty: account for and remit every payment received to the employing contractor
parameters.violation: misdemeanor and cause for disciplinary action

rules.applies_to: Home improvement salespersons
rules.quote: For any home improvement salesperson to fail to account for or to remit to their employing contractor any payment received in connection with any home improvement transaction or any other transaction involving a work of improvement.

rules.title: Contract form must disclose the employing contractor's name
rules.plain_english: Any contract form used by a salesperson or anyone else for a home improvement or other construction job must show the name of the contractor principal who employs that person. Using a form without it is a misdemeanor.

parameters.required_field: name of the contractor principal by whom the person is employed
parameters.violation: misdemeanor and cause for disciplinary action

rules.applies_to: All contract forms used for home improvement and other works of improvement
rules.quote: For any person to use a contract form in connection with any home improvement transaction or any other transaction involving a work of improvement if the form fails to disclose the name of the contractor principal by whom the person is employed.

rules.title: Salesperson may not guide contractor selection before CSLB has the hire notice
rules.plain_english: A home improvement salesperson may not assist, recommend or guide an owner or tenant in choosing a contractor until CSLB has received the contractor's notice of employment for that salesperson.

parameters.blocked_until: Board has received employment notification under B&P 7154(a)
parameters.violation: misdemeanor and cause for disciplinary action

rules.applies_to: Home improvement salespersons and their employers
rules.quote: For any home improvement salesperson to assist, recommend, select, or otherwise guide an owner or tenant in the selection of a contractor for the performance or sale of home improvement goods or services if notification of employment by the home improvement contractor, as required by subdivision (a) of Section 7154, has not been received by the Board.
rules.notes: Note the trigger is CSLB's receipt, not the contractor's mailing date.

rules.title: Electronic filing of HIS applications, renewals and employment notices
rules.plain_english: CSLB may accept HIS applications, renewals and the contractor's salesperson hire/termination notices electronically; once regulations take effect, an electronic submission satisfies the requirement.

parameters.condition: board implements system and adopts regulations on form and manner

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors and salespersons
rules.quote: Upon the effective date of the regulations, the electronic submission of an initial registration application, a renewal application, or the electronic transmission of a notice required by Section 7154 shall satisfy the requirements of this article.
rules.notes: Whether CSLB's regulations are in effect is not stated in this excerpt.

rules.title: No paying owners for referrals or placing business with others
rules.plain_english: As an inducement to sign a home improvement or other construction contract, no one may promise or offer an owner or tenant money, credit or a reward for referring or placing home improvement business with others. Violation is a misdemeanor and grounds for discipline.

parameters.prohibited: promise or offer to pay, credit or allow compensation or reward to owner for procurement or placing of home improvement business with others
parameters.exception: promotional gifts under B&P 7157(b)
parameters.violation: misdemeanor and cause for disciplinary action

rules.applies_to: Contractors, salespersons and anyone inducing a contract
rules.quote: Except as otherwise provided in subdivision (b), as a part of or in connection with the inducement to enter into any home improvement contract or other contract, which may be performed by a contractor, no person may promise or offer to pay, credit, or allow to any owner, compensation or reward for the procurement or placing of home improvement business with others.
rules.notes: Referral-reward marketing programs aimed at homeowners should be screened against this rule.

rules.title: Promotional gifts to prospects limited to $5, one per transaction
rules.plain_english: A contractor, agent or salesperson may give a prospective customer a promotional gift only if it is worth $5 or less, is not conditioned on signing a contract, and only one gift is given per transaction.

parameters.condition: gift not conditioned on obtaining a contract
parameters.gift_type: tangible items for advertising or sales promotion

rules.applies_to: Contractors, agents and salespersons marketing home improvement work
rules.quote: A contractor or his or her agent or salesperson may give tangible items to prospective customers for advertising or sales promotion purposes where the gift is not conditioned upon obtaining a contract for home improvement work if the gift does not exceed a value of five dollars ($5) and only one such gift is given in connection with any one transaction.

rules.title: Salesperson/agent may be paid only by the contractor they represent
rules.plain_english: A salesperson or contractor's agent may not accept any compensation on a job from anyone other than the contractor they represent, and may not make payments on the sale to anyone other than their employer.

parameters.accept_compensation_only_from: the contractor represented in the transaction
parameters.violation: misdemeanor and cause for disciplinary action

rules.applies_to: Salespersons and contractor agents
rules.quote: No salesperson or contractor’s agent may accept any compensation of any kind, for or on account of a home improvement transaction, or any other transaction involving a work of improvement, from any person other than the contractor whom he or she represents with respect to the transaction

rules.title: Contractor may not pay unlicensed contractors or salespersons for work
rules.plain_english: A contractor may not pay or credit any compensation to another contractor or salesperson who is not a licensee for construction work or services, unless that person is exempt from licensing or the transaction is not subject to the licensing law. Violation is a misdemeanor.

parameters.prohibited: paying, crediting or allowing consideration to a non-licensee contractor or salesperson for work of improvement or services
exceptions: recipient/payer not subject to or exempt from licensing requirements
transaction not subject to the chapter
parameters.violation: misdemeanor and cause for disciplinary action

rules.applies_to: All contractors (not only home improvement)
rules.quote: No contractor shall pay, credit, or allow any consideration or compensation of any kind to any other contractor or salesperson other than a licensee for or on account of the performance of any work of improvement or services, including, but not limited to, home improvement work or services
rules.notes: Useful check for AP/subcontractor payment workflows: verify sub's license status before paying.

rules.title: Using a false completion certificate to get paid or financed
rules.plain_english: Knowingly using a false completion certificate (work not substantially complete) to assign or negotiate the right to the owner's payment, or to get credit or a loan, is a misdemeanor punishable by a $500 to $5,000 fine and/or 1 month to 1 year in county jail.

elements: knowledge document is false
performance not substantially completed
used in assignment/negotiation of right to owner payment or to obtain credit/loan

rules.applies_to: Anyone using completion certificates for any work of improvement
rules.quote: shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and subject to a fine of not less than five hundred dollars ($500) nor more than five thousand dollars ($5,000), or to imprisonment in the county jail for a term of not less than one month nor more than one year, or both.

rules.title: Disaster-repair fraud with false completion certificate: restitution + fine up to $25,000
rules.plain_english: If a false completion certificate is used in a scheme to defraud an owner over natural-disaster repairs, the court must order full restitution based on ability to pay and may add a fine of $500 to $25,000.

parameters.restitution: full restitution, based on defendant's ability to pay
disaster_triggers: Presidential emergency or major disaster declaration

rules.applies_to: Contractors doing natural-disaster repair work
rules.quote: In addition to full restitution, and imprisonment authorized by subdivision (a), the court may impose a fine of not less than five hundred dollars ($500) nor more than twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000), based upon the defendant’s ability to pay.

rules.title: When B&P 7159 home improvement contract rules do not apply
rules.plain_english: B&P 7159 does not apply to compliant service and repair contracts (7159.10-7159.14), to fire alarms sold with an alarm system where all costs to make the fire alarm operable are $500 or less and 7159.9 is followed, or to alarm monitoring charges.

exemptions.type: fire alarm sold with alarm system (B&P 7590.1)
exemptions.cost_basis: all costs to make fire alarm system operable incl. sale and installation

exemptions.type: burglar or fire alarm monitoring costs

rules.applies_to: Residential contractors choosing which contract form applies
rules.quote: This section does not apply to the sale, installation, and servicing of a fire alarm sold in conjunction with an alarm system, as defined in Section 7590.1, if all costs attributable to making the fire alarm system operable, including sale and installation costs, do not exceed five hundred dollars ($500), and the licensee complies with the requirements set forth in Section 7159.9.

rules.title: Missing HIC information is cause for discipline; prime contractor responsible for completion
rules.plain_english: Failing to include any required information, notice or disclosure in a home improvement contract, or otherwise violating 7159, is grounds for CSLB discipline. The prime/direct contractor is responsible for completing the project per the contract, plans and specs, but subs and salespersons can also be disciplined. If the Notice of Cancellation is missing, the buyer may complain to CSLB.

parameters.missing_notice_of_cancellation_remedy: buyer may file complaint with CSLB

rules.applies_to: All home improvement contractors, subcontractors and salespersons
rules.quote: For purposes of administrative discipline under this chapter, the prime or direct contractor is responsible for completion of the project in accordance with the home improvement contract, plans, and specifications.

rules.title: Home improvement contract rules apply when aggregate price exceeds $500
rules.plain_english: B&P 7159's contract requirements apply to home improvement agreements between a contractor and an owner or tenant when the total price in one or more contracts, including labor, services and materials, is more than $500. Agreements by a salesperson with an owner or tenant for home improvement goods or services are also covered.

parameters.aggregation: aggregate contract price specified in one or more improvement contracts, including all labor, services and materials furnished by the contractor

rules.applies_to: Residential home improvement contracts
rules.quote: if the aggregate contract price specified in one or more improvement contracts, including all labor, services, and materials to be furnished by the contractor, exceeds five hundred dollars ($500).
rules.notes: Splitting a job into multiple contracts does not avoid the threshold because the price is aggregated. Service and repair contracts of $750 or less that meet 7159.10 use the separate service-and-repair form.
rules.correction: Note said service and repair contracts are "under $750". B&P 7159.10(a)(1)(A) and 7159.14(a)(1) say "$750 or less", so a $750 contract still qualifies. Note fixed. The $500 "exceeds" threshold itself is correct.

rules.title: HIC must be legible; at least 10-point text and 10-point bold headings
rules.plain_english: Every home improvement contract must be legible. Printed forms must use at least 10-point type for text and at least 10-point bold type for headings, unless a larger size is required for a specific notice.
rules.applies_to: All home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: Unless a larger typeface is specified in this article, text in any printed form shall be in at least 10-point typeface and the headings shall be in at least 10-point boldface type.
rules.notes: Several notices require 12-point bold (entitled-to-copy statement, downpayment and progress payment statements, right-to-cancel notices, CSLB information notice at 12-point).

rules.title: Give buyer a signed and dated copy before any work starts
rules.plain_english: Before starting any work, the contractor must give the buyer a copy of the contract signed and dated by both the contractor and the buyer. The buyer's cancellation rights begin when they receive this copy.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors
rules.quote: Before any work is started, the contractor shall give the buyer a copy of the contract that is signed and dated by both the contractor and the buyer. The buyer’s receipt of the copy of the contract initiates the buyer’s rights to cancel the contract pursuant to Sections 1689.5 to 1689.14, inclusive, of the Civil Code.
rules.notes: Software should record the date the buyer received the signed copy, because the 3/5/7 business-day cancellation period runs from it.

rules.title: First page must show buyer's signing date and contractor contact for cancellation
rules.plain_english: Page one of the contract, in type at least as large as the body text, must show the date the buyer signed, and the contractor's name, address and email address for sending the Notice of Cancellation, introduced by a statement that the notice may be sent there. It must also show a phone number for help locating and filling out the Notice of Cancellation.

required_items: date the buyer signed the contract
contractor name, address and email address for Notice of Cancellation
statement immediately preceding it advising that the Notice of Cancellation may be sent to the contractor at that address or email address
telephone number of contractor or contractor's representative to assist with the Notice of Cancellation

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: The name, address, and email address of the contractor to whom the applicable “Notice of Cancellation” is to be sent, immediately preceded by a statement advising the buyer that the “Notice of Cancellation” may be sent to the contractor at the address or email address noted on the contract.
rules.effective: Section amended effective January 1, 2026 (Stats 2025 ch 348 AB 1327 and ch 585 SB 517)
rules.notes: The text says 'both of the following' but lists three items (i)-(iii); include all three. The email address and email cancellation language appear in the 2026 text; the book does not say exactly which words the 2026 amendments added.

rules.title: Contract must promise unconditional lien release after each payment
rules.plain_english: The contract must state that after satisfactory payment for any portion of the work, and before any further payment, the contractor will give the owner a full and unconditional release from any lien claim or mechanics lien (Civil Code 8400 and 8404) for that paid portion.

parameters.trigger: satisfactory payment for any portion of work
parameters.timing: before any further payment is made

rules.applies_to: Home improvement and swimming pool contracts
rules.quote: The contract shall include a statement that, upon satisfactory payment being made for any portion of the work performed, the contractor, prior to any further payment being made, shall furnish to the person contracting for the home improvement or swimming pool work a full and unconditional release from any potential lien claimant claim or mechanics lien
rules.notes: For pool contracts, substantial noncompliance with this paragraph voids the contract (B&P 7167).

rules.title: Change-order form must be part of the contract
rules.plain_english: A change-order form for changes or extra work must be incorporated into the contract. A change order becomes part of the contract only if it is written and signed by both parties before the changed work begins.

valid_only_if: signed before commencement of work covered by the change order

rules.applies_to: Home improvement and swimming pool contracts
rules.quote: A change-order form for changes or extra work shall be incorporated into the contract and shall become part of the contract only if it is in writing and signed by the parties prior to the commencement of any work covered by a change order.
rules.notes: Pool contracts that do not substantially comply are void (B&P 7167), but the contractor may still recover in quantum meruit for this paragraph.

rules.title: Notice of owner's right to require performance and payment bond
rules.plain_english: Near the owner's and contractor's signatures, the contract must state that the owner or tenant has the right to require the contractor to have a performance and payment bond.

parameters.placement: in close proximity to the signatures of owner and contractor
parameters.content: owner or tenant has right to require contractor to have a performance and payment bond

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: The contract shall contain, in close proximity to the signatures of the owner and contractor, a notice stating that the owner or tenant has the right to require the contractor to have a performance and payment bond.
rules.notes: No exact wording is prescribed.

rules.title: Subcontractor Yes/No checkbox and disclaimer, repeated on each change order
rules.plain_english: The contract must state whether subcontractors will be used, with Yes/No checkboxes. If Yes, it must include a disclaimer that a list of subcontractors (names, contact info, license numbers and classifications) will be provided on request, and the same disclaimer must appear on every change order.

parameters.if_yes_required_text: One or more subcontractors will be used on this project, and the contractor is aware that a list of subcontractors is required to be provided, upon request, along with the names, contact information, license number, and classification of those subcontractors.

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500 and their change orders
rules.quote: “One or more subcontractors will be used on this project, and the contractor is aware that a list of subcontractors is required to be provided, upon request, along with the names, contact information, license number, and classification of those subcontractors.”
rules.notes: Software should keep a subcontractor roster per job (name, contact, license number, classification) ready to produce on request.

rules.title: Contractor may have no interest in the joint control it furnishes
rules.plain_english: If the contract provides for the contractor to furnish joint control (a funds-control arrangement), the contractor must not have any financial or other interest in that joint control.

parameters.applies_when: contract provides for contractor to furnish joint control

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors using joint control
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 399 and 411
rules.quote: If the contract provides for a contractor to furnish joint control, the contractor shall not have any financial or other interest in the joint control.

rules.title: Contract and all changes must be written and signed before work
rules.plain_english: A home improvement contract and every change to it must be in writing and signed by the parties before work on the contract or change order begins, and must include the items listed in 7159(d).

parameters.timing: prior to commencement of work covered by the contract or applicable change order

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: A home improvement contract and any changes to the contract shall be in writing and signed by the parties to the contract prior to the commencement of work covered by the contract or an applicable change order

rules.title: Contract must show contractor name, address, license no., and salesperson registration
rules.plain_english: The contract must list the contractor's name, business address and license number, and, if a home improvement salesperson solicited or negotiated the deal, the salesperson's name and registration number.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: (1) The name, business address, and license number of the contractor. (2) If applicable, the name and registration number of the home improvement salesperson that solicited or negotiated the contract.

rules.title: Contract heading 'Home Improvement' in 10-point bold
rules.plain_english: The contract form must carry the heading 'Home Improvement' in at least 10-point bold type to identify the contract type.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: The following heading on the contract form that identifies the type of contract in at least 10-point boldface type: “Home Improvement.”

rules.title: 12-point bold 'entitled to a completely filled in copy' statement
rules.plain_english: The contract must include, in at least 12-point bold type, the statement that the buyer is entitled to a completely filled-in copy signed by both parties before any work starts.

parameters.required_text: You are entitled to a completely filled in copy of this agreement, signed by both you and the contractor, before any work may be started.

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: The following statement in at least 12-point boldface type: “You are entitled to a completely filled in copy of this agreement, signed by both you and the contractor, before any work may be started.”

rules.title: 'Contract Price' heading with full price in dollars and cents
rules.plain_english: The contract must have the heading 'Contract Price' followed by the amount in dollars and cents. The contract amount must include the entire cost (profit, labor and materials) but exclude finance charges.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 399 and 410
rules.quote: The contract shall be in writing and shall include the agreed contract amount in dollars and cents. The contract amount shall include the entire cost of the contract, including profit, labor, and materials, but excluding finance charges.
rules.notes: Violating 7159.5(a)(1) is also a misdemeanor (7159.5(b)(1)).

rules.title: 'Finance Charge' heading, stated separately from contract price
rules.plain_english: If a finance charge will be charged, the contract must show the heading 'Finance Charge' followed by the amount in dollars and cents, separate from the contract amount.

parameters.condition: a finance charge will be charged

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts with contractor financing
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 400 and 410
rules.quote: If a finance charge will be charged, the heading: “Finance Charge,” followed by the amount in dollars and cents. The finance charge is to be set out separately from the contract amount.

rules.title: Project description and significant materials/equipment; pool plan and scale drawing
rules.plain_english: The contract must have the heading 'Description of the Project and Description of the Significant Materials to be Used and Equipment to be Installed' followed by those descriptions. Swimming pool contracts must also include a plan and scale drawing showing shape, size, dimensions and construction and equipment specs.

rules.notes: Pool contracts not substantially complying with this paragraph are void and unenforceable by the contractor (B&P 7167).

rules.title: 'Downpayment' heading and 12-point bold downpayment limit statement
rules.plain_english: If a downpayment is charged, the contract must show the heading 'Downpayment', a space with the actual downpayment amount, and the 12-point bold statement that the downpayment may not exceed $1,000 or 10% of the contract price, whichever is less.

rules.title: Downpayment cap: lesser of $1,000 or 10% of contract amount
rules.plain_english: On a home improvement contract, any downpayment may not be more than $1,000 or 10% of the contract amount, whichever is less. Taking more is a misdemeanor and grounds for discipline, unless the contractor has a registrar-approved bond or joint control covering full performance and payment.

parameters.contract_amount_basis: entire contract amount incl. profit, labor, materials; excluding finance charges

rules.title: 'Schedule of Progress Payments' with dollar amounts tied to work, plus 12-point bold statement
rules.plain_english: If payments other than the downpayment are due before completion, the contract must include a 'Schedule of Progress Payments' with each payment in dollars and cents tied to specific work, services, materials and equipment, plus a required 12-point bold statement that collecting payment for work not yet done or materials not yet delivered is against the law.

references materials and equipment to be supplied

IT IS AGAINST THE LAW FOR A CONTRACTOR TO COLLECT PAYMENT FOR WORK NOT YET COMPLETED, OR FOR MATERIALS NOT YET DELIVERED. HOWEVER, A CONTRACTOR MAY REQUIRE A DOWNPAYMENT.

rules.title: Workers' Compensation Insurance notice
rules.plain_english: The contract must include a notice headed 'Workers' Compensation Insurance' stating either that the contractor has no employees and is exempt, or that it carries workers' comp for all employees. It may be an attachment if the contract says so.

options.B_carries_wc: (The name on the license or ‘This contractor’) carries workers’ compensation insurance for all employees.

rules.title: Notice to buyer about extra/change-order work
rules.plain_english: The contract must tell the buyer that (A) they cannot require extra or change-order work without written authorization before it starts, (B) a change order is not enforceable unless it states scope, price change, and effect on progress payments or completion date in writing before the work starts, and (C) the contractor's noncompliance does not bar recovery for work done under unjust-enrichment remedies.

required_statements: buyer may not require extra or change-order work without written authorization prior to commencement of that work
change order not enforceable against buyer unless it identifies in writing, before the work: scope of work; amount added or subtracted; effect on progress payments or completion date
contractor's failure to comply does not preclude recovery for work performed under legal or equitable remedies preventing unjust enrichment

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: A statement informing the buyer that extra work or a change order is not enforceable against a buyer unless the change order also identifies all of the following in writing prior to the commencement of work covered by the new change order: (i) The scope of work encompassed by the order. (ii) The amount to be added or subtracted from the contract.
rules.notes: No exact wording prescribed; content must cover these three statements.

rules.title: Mechanics Lien Warning (home improvement contract version)
rules.plain_english: Every home improvement contract must include the statutory 'Mechanics Lien Warning' explaining liens, 20-day preliminary notices, how to protect against liens with a subcontractor/supplier list and joint checks, and CSLB contact information.

parameters.required_text:
MECHANICS LIEN WARNING:
Anyone who helps improve your property, but who is not paid, may record what is called a mechanics lien on your property. A mechanics lien is a claim, like a mortgage or home equity loan, made against your property and recorded with the county recorder.
Even if you pay your contractor in full, unpaid subcontractors, suppliers, and laborers who helped to improve your property may record mechanics liens and sue you in court to foreclose the lien. If a court finds the lien is valid, you could be forced to pay twice or have a court officer sell your home to pay the lien. Liens can also affect your credit.
To preserve their right to record a lien, each subcontractor and material supplier must provide you with a document called a ‘Preliminary Notice.’ This notice is not a lien. The purpose of the notice is to let you know that the person who sends you the notice has the right to record a lien on your property if they are not paid.
BE CAREFUL. The Preliminary Notice can be sent up to 20 days after the subcontractor starts work or the supplier provides material. This can be a big problem if you pay your contractor before you have received the Preliminary Notices.
You will not get Preliminary Notices from your prime contractor or from laborers who work on your project. The law assumes that you already know they are improving your property.
PROTECT YOURSELF FROM LIENS. You can protect yourself from liens by getting a list from your contractor of all the subcontractors and material suppliers that work on your project. Find out from your contractor when these subcontractors started work and when these suppliers delivered goods or materials. Then wait 20 days, paying attention to the Preliminary Notices you receive.
PAY WITH JOINT CHECKS. One way to protect yourself is to pay with a joint check. When your contractor tells you it is time to pay for the work of a subcontractor or supplier who has provided you with a Preliminary Notice, write a joint check payable to both the contractor and the subcontractor or material supplier.
For other ways to prevent liens, visit CSLB’s internet website at www.cslb.ca.gov or call CSLB at 800-321-CSLB (2752).
REMEMBER, IF YOU DO NOTHING, YOU RISK HAVING A LIEN PLACED ON YOUR HOME. This can mean that you may have to pay twice, or face the forced sale of your home to pay what you owe.

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500 (except bonded contractors under 7159.5(a)(8))
rules.quote: BE CAREFUL. The Preliminary Notice can be sent up to 20 days after the subcontractor starts work or the supplier provides material. This can be a big problem if you pay your contractor before you have received the Preliminary Notices.
rules.notes: In the book the phone number line is printed as '800-321-CSLB (2752) .REMEMBER' (typesetting); the period placement here is normalized. The B&P 7164 single-family-dwelling version has slightly different wording.

rules.title: 'Information about the Contractors State License Board (CSLB)' notice in 12-point
rules.plain_english: Every home improvement contract must include the prescribed CSLB information notice in at least 12-point type, telling the buyer to use licensed contractors, that complaints are usually due within four years, and how to contact CSLB.

parameters.required_text:
Information about the Contractors State License Board (CSLB): CSLB is the state consumer protection agency that licenses and regulates construction contractors.
Contact CSLB for information about the licensed contractor you are considering, including information about disclosable complaints, disciplinary actions, and civil judgments that are reported to CSLB.
Use only licensed contractors. If you file a complaint against a licensed contractor within the legal deadline (usually four years), CSLB has authority to investigate the complaint. If you use an unlicensed contractor, CSLB may not be able to help you resolve your complaint. Your only remedy may be in civil court, and you may be liable for damages arising out of any injuries to the unlicensed contractor or the unlicensed contractor’s employees.
For more information:
Visit CSLB’s internet website at www.cslb.ca.gov
Call CSLB at 800-321-CSLB (2752)
Write CSLB at P.O. Box 26000, Sacramento, CA 95826.

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500
rules.quote: Use only licensed contractors. If you file a complaint against a licensed contractor within the legal deadline (usually four years), CSLB has authority to investigate the complaint.
rules.notes: Bold is not required for this notice; 12-point is.

rules.title: 'Three-Day Right to Cancel' notice (five-day for seniors)
rules.plain_english: Unless the contract was negotiated at the contractor's place of business, is a disaster-repair contract (7-day notice), or is by an alarm company licensee following Civil Code 1689.5-1689.7, the buyer must get the prescribed 'Three-Day Right to Cancel' notice; for a buyer 65 or older it becomes the 'Five-Day Right to Cancel'. The buyer can cancel by email, mail, fax or delivery by midnight of the 3rd (or 5th) business day after receiving the signed contract.

parameters.deadline_rule: midnight of the Nth business day after buyer received a signed and dated copy of the contract including this notice
cancel_methods: delivery to contractor's place of business
exceptions: negotiated at the contractor's place of business
subject to the Seven-Day Right to Cancel (disaster repair)
Alarm Company Act licensee complying with Civil Code 1689.5, 1689.6 and 1689.7
parameters.required_text:
Three-Day Right to Cancel
You, the buyer, have the right to cancel this contract within three business days. You may cancel by emailing, mailing, faxing, or delivering a written notice to the contractor at the contractor’s place of business by midnight of the third business day after you received a signed and dated copy of the contract that includes this notice. Include your name, your address, and the date you received the signed copy of the contract and this notice.
If you cancel, the contractor must return to you anything you paid within 10 days of receiving the notice of cancellation. For your part, you must make available to the contractor at your residence, in substantially as good condition as you received them, goods delivered to you under this contract or sale. Or, you may, if you wish, comply with the contractor’s instructions on how to return the goods at the contractor’s expense and risk. If you do make the goods available to the contractor and the contractor does not pick them up within 20 days of the date of your notice of cancellation, you may keep them without any further obligation. If you fail to make the goods available to the contractor, or if you agree to return the goods to the contractor and fail to do so, then you remain liable for performance of all obligations under the contract.
parameters.senior_substitution: replace “three” with “five” and “third” with “fifth” (title becomes Five-Day Right to Cancel)

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts over $500 not excepted

You may cancel by emailing, mailing, faxing, or delivering a written notice to the contractor at the contractor’s place of business by midnight of the third business day after you received a signed and dated copy of the contract that includes this notice.
rules.effective: Section amended effective January 1, 2026; five-day senior right applies to contracts entered into on or after January 1, 2021

The notice may be attached instead if the contract has a 12-point bold checkbox statement the buyer initials.

rules.title: Completed 'Notice of Cancellation' form in duplicate, easily detachable
rules.plain_english: The right-to-cancel notice must be accompanied by a completed 'Notice of Cancellation' form in duplicate, attached to the contract and easily detachable, in the same language as the contract, with the transaction date, seller name, seller's business address and cancellation deadline filled in.

parameters.language: same as used in the contract
fill_in_fields: address of seller's place of business
parameters.required_text:
Notice of Cancellation
[enter date of transaction] (Date)
You may cancel this transaction, without any penalty or obligation, within three business days from the above date.
If you cancel, any property traded in, any payments made by you under the contract or sale, and any negotiable instrument executed by you will be returned within 10 days following receipt by the seller of your cancellation notice, and any security interest arising out of the transaction will be canceled.
If you cancel, you must make available to the seller at your residence, in substantially as good condition as when received, any goods delivered to you under this contract or sale, or you may, if you wish, comply with the instructions of the seller regarding the return shipment of the goods at the seller’s expense and risk.
If you do make the goods available to the seller and the seller does not pick them up within 20 days of the date of your notice of cancellation, you may retain or dispose of the goods without any further obligation. If you fail to make the goods available to the seller, or if you agree to return the goods to the seller and fail to do so, then you remain liable for performance of all obligations under the contract.
To cancel this transaction, mail or deliver a signed and dated copy of this cancellation notice, or any other written notice, or send a telegram to [name of seller], at [address of seller’s place of business] not later than midnight of [Date].
I hereby cancel this transaction. [Date]
[Buyer’s signature]

You may cancel by emailing, mailing, faxing, or delivering a written notice to the contractor at the contractor’s place of business by midnight of the seventh business day after you received a signed and dated copy of the contract that includes this notice. For your part, you must make available to the contractor at your residence, in substantially as good condition as you received them, goods delivered to you under this contract or sale. Or, you may, if you wish, comply with the contractor’s instructions on how to return the goods at the contractor’s expense and risk. If you do make the goods available to the contractor and the contractor does not pick them up within 20 days of the date of your notice of cancellation, you may keep them without any further obligation. If you fail to make the goods available to the contractor, or if you agree to return the goods to the contractor and fail to do so, then you remain liable for performance of all obligations under the contract.

rules.title: After cancellation: refund within 10 days; goods kept if not picked up in 20 days

rules.title: Door-to-door sale secured by lien on home: 18-point bold warning on separate page
rules.plain_english: If a door-to-door home improvement goods or services contract includes or is secured by a lien on real property, it must come with a separate, signed and dated 18-point bold 'WARNING TO BUYER' page stating the home is being put up as security. The buyer gets a copy at signing. Without it, the security interest is void.

parameters.required_text: WARNING TO BUYER: IF YOU SIGN THE CONTRACT WHICH ACCOMPANIES THIS NOTICE, YOU WILL BE PUTTING UP YOUR HOME AS SECURITY. THIS MEANS THAT YOUR HOME COULD BE SOLD WITHOUT YOUR PERMISSION AND WITHOUT ANY COURT ACTION IF YOU MISS ANY PAYMENT REQUIRED BY THIS CONTRACT.
exclusions: contracts subject to Civil Code 1801 et seq. (Unruh Act)
mechanics liens under Civil Code 8400 et seq.

rules.quote: “WARNING TO BUYER: IF YOU SIGN THE CONTRACT WHICH ACCOMPANIES THIS NOTICE, YOU WILL BE PUTTING UP YOUR HOME AS SECURITY. THIS MEANS THAT YOUR HOME COULD BE SOLD WITHOUT YOUR PERMISSION AND WITHOUT ANY COURT ACTION IF YOU MISS ANY PAYMENT REQUIRED BY THIS CONTRACT.”
rules.notes: The 'Unruh Act' label for Civil Code 1801 et seq. is a common name, not stated in the text.

rules.title: No security interest in real property on contracts of $5,000 or less
rules.plain_english: A home improvement goods or services contract worth $5,000 or less may not include a security interest in real property, other than a mechanics lien or interest arising by law. Any such lien is void.

parameters.prohibited: security interest in real property
allowed: other interest arising by operation of law

rules.applies_to: Home improvement goods or services contracts
rules.quote: No home improvement goods or services contract of a value of five thousand dollars ($5,000) or less shall provide for a security interest in real property, except for a mechanic’s lien or other interest in property that arises by operation of law. Any lien in violation of this subdivision is void and unenforceable.

rules.title: Mortgage-funded jobs over $5,000: lender pays by borrower/joint check or escrow
rules.plain_english: When proceeds of a loan secured by a mortgage on real property fund a home improvement contract over $5,000, the lender may pay the contractor only by an instrument payable to the borrower or jointly to the borrower and contractor, or, if the borrower chooses, through a third-party escrow under a written agreement signed by borrower, lender and contractor before disbursement.

third-party escrow at borrower's election, per written agreement signed by borrower, lender and contractor prior to disbursement

rules.title: 7159.2 violations: actual damages, treble contract price, $5,000 senior/disabled award, attorney fees
rules.plain_english: Violating 7159.2 makes the violator liable for the borrower's actual damages. Intentional or pattern violations add liability of three times the contract price. Seniors or disabled persons may also be awarded up to $5,000, and a prevailing plaintiff gets court costs and attorney's fees.
