rules.title: Furnish unconditional lien releases on request; owner may withhold payment until received
rules.plain_english: After each payment by the owner and before any further payment, the contractor must, if asked, obtain and give the owner full and unconditional lien releases for the paid portion of the work. The owner may withhold all further payments until those releases are provided.

parameters.trigger: any payment by the person contracting for home improvement
parameters.release_type: full and unconditional release from any potential lien claimant claim or mechanics lien (Civil Code 8400, 8404)

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors and owners
rules.quote: Upon any payment by the person contracting for home improvement, and prior to any further payment being made, the contractor shall, if requested, obtain and furnish to the person a full and unconditional release from any potential lien claimant claim or mechanics lien ... The person contracting for home improvement may withhold all further payments until these releases are furnished.
rules.notes: Releases must cover subs and suppliers ('any potential lien claimant'), not just the prime.

rules.title: Salesperson commission paid pro rata with contractor's payment schedule
rules.plain_english: If the contract provides for paying a salesperson's commission out of the contract price, the commission must be paid pro rata, in proportion to the payments made to the contractor under the payment schedule.

parameters.rule: commission paid in proportion to schedule of payments made to contractor by disbursing party

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts paying salesperson commissions from the contract price
rules.quote: If the contract provides for a payment of a salesperson’s commission out of the contract price, that payment shall be made on a pro rata basis in proportion to the schedule of payments made to the contractor by the disbursing party in accordance with paragraph (4).
rules.notes: The formula is an interpretation of 'pro rata'; the statute gives no formula.

rules.title: Bonded/joint-control contractors exempt from downpayment and progress-payment limits
rules.plain_english: A contractor that furnishes a registrar-approved performance and payment bond, lien and completion bond, bond equivalent or joint control covering full performance and payment is exempt from the downpayment cap, progress-payment schedule and no-payment-ahead rules, may accept payment before completion, and need not include the downpayment statement, progress-payment details or Mechanics Lien Warning. A licensee must be actively licensed for at least two years before applying for a blanket performance and payment bond approval.

exempt_from: B&P 7159.5(a)(5) no payment ahead of work
parameters.blanket_bond_regulation: 16 CCR 858.2 as it read on January 1, 2016

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors using blanket bonds or joint control
rules.quote: Notwithstanding any other law, a licensee shall be licensed in this state in an active status for not less than two years prior to submitting an Application for Approval of Blanket Performance and Payment Bond as provided in Section 858.2 of Title 16 of the California Code of Regulations as it read on January 1, 2016.
rules.notes: Bond amounts are not stated in this excerpt.

rules.title: Unwritten contract, excess downpayment or payment ahead of work: misdemeanor $100-$5,000
rules.plain_english: Violating the written-contract/price rule, the downpayment cap, or the no-payment-ahead-of-work rule is a misdemeanor punishable by a $100 to $5,000 fine and/or up to one year in county jail. In a declared natural-disaster area, the court must impose the maximum fine.

parameters.disaster_area_rule: court shall impose the maximum fine ($5,000)
disaster_triggers: Presidential emergency or major disaster declaration

rules.applies_to: Licensees, persons required to be licensed, agents and salespersons
rules.quote: A violation of paragraph (1), (3), or (5) of subdivision (a) by a licensee or a person subject to be licensed under this chapter, or by their agent or salesperson, is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not less than one hundred dollars ($100) nor more than five thousand dollars ($5,000), or by imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding one year, or by both that fine and imprisonment.
rules.effective: Operative July 1, 2021; amended effective January 1, 2022 and 2023

rules.title: Criminal filing deadline for HIC violations: 4 years (unlicensed) / 2 years (licensed)
rules.plain_english: Criminal charges for 7159.5 violations must be filed within four years for an unlicensed person who should be licensed, or within two years for a licensee, counted from the contract date, or from the buyer's first payment if the contract was not written. These limits do not apply to CSLB administrative actions.

parameters.measured_from: date of the contract; if not in writing, date buyer makes first payment

rules.applies_to: Contractors facing prosecution for home improvement contract violations
rules.quote: An indictment or information against a person who is licensed under this chapter shall be brought, or a criminal complaint filed, for a violation of this section ... within two years from the date of the contract or, if the contract is not reduced to writing, from the date the buyer makes the first payment to the contractor.

rules.title: Disaster-repair fraud under 7159.5: full restitution plus fine $500-$25,000
rules.plain_english: A person who violates 7159.5 in a scheme to defraud an owner or tenant over natural-disaster repairs must pay full restitution (based on ability to pay) and may be fined $500 to $25,000 on top of jail.

parameters.restitution: full, based on ability to pay

rules.applies_to: Contractors doing natural-disaster repairs
rules.quote: In addition to full restitution, and imprisonment authorized by this section, the court may impose a fine of not less than five hundred dollars ($500) nor more than twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000), based upon the defendant’s ability to pay.

rules.title: Change order enforceable only if it states scope, price change and schedule/payment effect
rules.plain_english: An extra-work or change order cannot be enforced against the buyer unless it states the scope of work, the amount added or subtracted, and the effect on progress payments or the completion date. The buyer cannot require extra work without written authorization. The contractor can still seek payment for work done under unjust-enrichment remedies.

required_change_order_fields: scope of work encompassed by the order
amount to be added or subtracted from the contract
effect on progress payments or completion date

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors and buyers
rules.quote: An extra work or change order is not enforceable against a buyer unless the change order sets forth all of the following: (1) The scope of work encompassed by the order. (2) The amount to be added or subtracted from the contract. (3) The effect the order will make in the progress payments or the completion date.
rules.notes: Combine with 7159(c)(5)/(d): change orders must also be signed before the changed work begins, and if subs are used, carry the subcontractor disclaimer (7159(c)(7)(C)).

rules.title: Fire alarm (<= $500) exemption: certification statement, address, contractor data, copies
rules.plain_english: To use the 7159 exemption for a fire alarm sold with an alarm system, the licensee must follow the alarm contract rules (B&P 7599.54) and Civil Code 1689.5-1689.7, sign a certification that all costs to make the fire alarm operable are $500 or less, include the residence address and the contractor's name, business address and license number, and give the customer exact copies.

parameters.required_certification_text: All costs attributable to making the fire alarm system operable for the residence identified by this document, including sale and installation costs, do not exceed five hundred dollars ($500).
parameters.separate_document_certification_text: I certify that all statements and representations made by me in this document are true and accurate.
required_fields: contractor name, business address and license number as in CSLB records
parameters.copies: exact copy of all documents to the party contracting for installation

rules.applies_to: Licensees selling/installing fire alarms with alarm systems
rules.quote: “All costs attributable to making the fire alarm system operable for the residence identified by this document, including sale and installation costs, do not exceed five hundred dollars ($500).”

rules.title: Keep fire alarm exemption documents 5 years; produce within 30 days
rules.plain_english: All fire alarm exemption documents must be kept for five years and given to CSLB within 30 days of a written request. Failing to produce them is cause for discipline and creates a presumption that 7159 was violated.

parameters.measured_from: board's written request
failure_consequences: presumption of violation of B&P 7159 unless rebutted within board's timeframe

rules.applies_to: Licensees using the fire alarm exemption
rules.quote: All documents required pursuant to this section shall be retained by the licensee for a period of five years in accordance with the provisions of Section 7111, and shall be made available to the board within 30 days of a written request.

rules.title: Service and repair contract: <= $750, buyer-initiated, no upsell, no payment until done
rules.plain_english: A service and repair contract is a home improvement agreement of $750 or less where the buyer called the contractor, the contractor sells only what is reasonably needed to fix that problem, and no payment is due or accepted until the work is completed (the problem fully corrected and, if applicable, approved by the building department).

conditions: buyer initiated contact to request the work
no goods/services beyond those reasonably necessary for the particular problem
no payment due or accepted until work completed
parameters.work_completed_definition: all conditions that caused the call fully corrected and, if applicable, building department accepted and approved the corrective work

rules.applies_to: Residential service and repair work
rules.quote: (A) The contract amount is seven hundred fifty dollars ($750) or less. (B) The prospective buyer initiated contact with the contractor to request the work. ... (D) No payment is due, or accepted by the contractor, until the work is completed.
rules.notes: Contract selector logic: if all four conditions are true -> service and repair form; otherwise -> the full 7159(c), (d) and (e) requirements and Civil Code 1689.6/1689.7 rescission rights apply regardless of the aggregate contract price, for any contract written under 7159.10(a) or presented as a service and repair contract (7159.10(b)). A contract never presented as service and repair falls under 7159 only if over $500 (7159(b)).
rules.correction: Note said a non-conforming contract goes to the full 7159 contract "(if over $500) per 7159.10(b)". 7159.10(b) says the 7159(c)-(e) requirements apply "regardless of the aggregate contract price" to any contract written or presented as a service and repair contract. Note fixed. The four conditions and $750 cap are correct.

rules.title: Non-conforming 'service and repair' contract must meet full HIC rules regardless of price
rules.plain_english: If a contract is presented as a service and repair contract but does not meet all four conditions, the full home improvement contract requirements of 7159(c), (d) and (e), including cancellation rights, apply regardless of the contract price. If it does conform, only the 7159.10 requirements apply.

parameters.if_nonconforming: B&P 7159(c), (d), (e) apply plus Civil Code 1689.6/1689.7 rescission rights
parameters.if_conforming: only B&P 7159.10 notices and requirements apply

rules.applies_to: Contractors using service and repair contracts
rules.quote: unless all of the conforming requirements for service and repair contracts specified in subdivision (a) are met, the contract requirements for home improvements set forth in subdivisions (c), (d), and (e) of Section 7159 shall be applicable, including any rights to rescind the contract as set forth in Section 1689.6 or 1689.7 of the Civil Code, regardless of the aggregate contract price.

rules.title: Service and repair: written, same language, legible, 10-point, copy before work
rules.plain_english: A service and repair contract, its changes and attachments must be in writing, signed or acknowledged, and in the same language as the oral sales pitch; legible; at least 10-point text with 10-point bold headings; and the buyer must get a copy signed and dated by both sides before work starts.

parameters.language: same as principally used in oral sales presentation

rules.applies_to: Service and repair contracts
rules.quote: Before any work is started, the contractor shall give the buyer a copy of the contract signed and dated by the buyer and by the contractor or the contractor’s representative.

rules.title: Service and repair: contractor name, address, license number and signing date
rules.plain_english: A service and repair contract must show the contractor's name, business address and license number, and the date the contract was signed.
rules.applies_to: Service and repair contracts
rules.quote: (5) The name, business address, and license number of the contractor. (6) The date the contract was signed.

rules.title: Service and repair: CGL and workers' comp notices
rules.plain_english: Service and repair contracts need a notice headed 'Commercial General Liability Insurance (CGL)' and one headed 'Workers' Compensation Insurance', each followed by whichever listed statement is both relevant and correct. The statements are close to the home improvement contract notices but not word for word the same, so use the service and repair wording in B&P 7159.10(d)(7)-(8). Either notice may be an attachment if the contract says it is attached.

cgl_options: carries CGL written by (insurer); call (insurer) at ___
LLC carrying liability insurance or other security; call (insurer/trust company/bank) at ___
wc_options: has no employees and is exempt from workers’ compensation requirements
carries workers’ compensation insurance for all employees
parameters.cgl_attachment_statement: A notice concerning commercial general liability insurance is attached to this contract.
parameters.wc_attachment_statement: A notice concerning workers’ compensation insurance is attached to this contract.

cgl_options_exact.A: (The name on the license or ‘This contractor’) does not carry commercial general liability insurance.
cgl_options_exact.B: (The name on the license or ‘This contractor’) carries commercial general liability insurance written by (the insurance company). You may call the (insurance company) at _________ to check the contractor’s insurance coverage.
cgl_options_exact.C: (The name on the license or ‘This contractor’) is self-insured.
cgl_options_exact.D: (The name on the license or ‘This contractor’) is a limited liability company that carries liability insurance or maintains other security as required by law. You may call (the insurance company or trust company or bank) at ____ to check on the contractor’s insurance coverage or security.

wc_options_exact.A: (The name on the license or ‘This contractor’) has no employees and is exempt from workers’ compensation requirements.
wc_options_exact.B: (The name on the license or ‘This contractor’) carries workers’ compensation insurance for all employees.

parameters.cgl_selection_rule: whichever statement is both relevant and correct
parameters.wc_selection_rule: whichever statement is both relevant and correct

rules.applies_to: Service and repair contracts
rules.quote: The notice shall include the heading “Workers’ Compensation Insurance” followed by whichever of the following statements is both relevant and correct:
rules.notes: Option wording is nearly the same as B&P 7159(e)(1)-(2), with two differences: 7159.10(d)(7)(B) reads 'You may call the (insurance company) at ___' (7159(e)(1)(B) has '(the insurance company)'), and 7159.10(d)(8) picks the workers' comp statement that is 'both relevant and correct' (7159(e)(2): 'correct'). Use cgl_options_exact / wc_options_exact for service and repair contracts.
rules.correction: Note said the option wording is exactly the same as 7159(e)(1)-(2). It is not quite: 7159.10(d)(7)(B) says "You may call the (insurance company)" and 7159.10(d)(8) uses "both relevant and correct". Added the exact 7159.10 option texts and selection rules to parameters and fixed the note. plain_english reworded on 2026-11-27: it no longer says the notices are the same as the home improvement ones.

rules.title: 'Service and Repair' heading in 10-point bold
rules.plain_english: The contract must identify its type with the notice 'Service and Repair' in at least 10-point bold type.
rules.applies_to: Service and repair contracts
rules.quote: Notice of the type of contract in at least 10-point boldface type: “Service and Repair.”

rules.title: Signed 12-point bold 'Notice to the Buyer' listing the four service and repair conditions
rules.plain_english: A service and repair contract must include a 12-point bold notice, signed and dated by the buyer, stating the four legal requirements: price no more than $750, buyer initiated contact, no upselling, and no payment until the work is completed.

parameters.required_text: Notice to the Buyer: The law requires that service and repair contracts must meet all of the following requirements: (A) The price must be no more than seven hundred and fifty dollars ($750). (B) You, the buyer, must have initiated contact with the contractor to request the work. (C) The contractor must not sell you goods or services beyond those reasonably necessary to take care of the particular problem that caused you to contact the contractor. (D) No payment is due and the contractor may not accept any payment until the work is completed.

rules.applies_to: Service and repair contracts
rules.quote: A notice in at least 12-point boldface type, signed and dated by the buyer: Notice to the Buyer: The law requires that service and repair contracts must meet all of the following requirements: (A) The price must be no more than seven hundred and fifty dollars ($750).

rules.title: Service and repair: 12-point bold 'entitled to a completely filled in and signed copy' notice
rules.plain_english: The service and repair contract must include the 12-point bold notice that the buyer is entitled to a completely filled in and signed copy before work begins.

parameters.required_text: Notice to the Buyer: You are entitled to a completely filled in and signed copy of this agreement before any work may be started.

rules.applies_to: Service and repair contracts
rules.quote: “Notice to the Buyer: You are entitled to a completely filled in and signed copy of this agreement before any work may be started.”

rules.title: Service and repair: incorporated documents, 'Contract Price', 'Finance Charge' headings
rules.plain_english: If applicable, list incorporated documents under 'List of Documents to be Incorporated into the Contract'. For a fixed price, show 'Contract Price' in dollars and cents; any finance charge goes under a separate 'Finance Charge' heading.

headings.documents: List of Documents to be Incorporated into the Contract

rules.applies_to: Service and repair contracts
rules.quote: Where the contract is a fixed contract amount, the heading: “Contract Price” followed by the amount of the contract in dollars and cents.

rules.title: Time-and-materials service contracts: 'Estimated Contract Price', rate, increments; cannot exceed estimate without written OK
rules.plain_english: A time-and-materials service and repair contract must show 'Estimated Contract Price' in dollars and cents, the set rate, the estimated cost of materials, how time is counted (e.g., quarter-hours), and a statement that the actual amount may not exceed the estimate without the buyer's written authorization.

required_disclosures: estimated contract amount in dollars and cents
time increment (e.g., quarter hours, half hours, hours)
parameters.required_text: The actual contract amount of a time and materials contract may not exceed the estimated contract amount without written authorization from the buyer.
parameters.rule: actual_amount <= estimated_amount unless buyer written authorization

rules.applies_to: Time-and-materials service and repair contracts
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 416 and 419
rules.quote: The contract must also disclose how time will be computed, for example, in increments of quarter hours, half hours, or hours, and the statement: “The actual contract amount of a time and materials contract may not exceed the estimated contract amount without written authorization from the buyer.”
rules.notes: Even with authorization, exceeding $750 takes the contract outside the service and repair category (7159.14(a)(1)).

rules.title: Service and repair: project, materials and equipment description
rules.plain_english: The contract must include the heading 'Description of the Project and Materials to be Used and Equipment to be Installed' followed by those descriptions.

parameters.required_heading: Description of the Project and Materials to be Used and Equipment to be Installed

rules.applies_to: Service and repair contracts
rules.quote: The heading: “Description of the Project and Materials to be Used and Equipment to be Installed” followed by a description of the project and materials to be used and equipment to be installed.

rules.title: Offer replaced parts to customer; 'OK for contractor to take replaced parts' checkbox
rules.plain_english: The service and repair contractor must offer the customer any parts replaced. The contract must include the prescribed statement and a checkbox labeled 'OK for contractor to take replaced parts' for the customer to initial if they do not want them.

parameters.required_text: The law requires that the contractor offer you any parts that were replaced during the service call. If you do not want the parts, initial the checkbox labeled ‘OK for contractor to take replaced parts.’
parameters.checkbox_label: OK for contractor to take replaced parts.
parameters.duty: offer customer any parts that were replaced

rules.applies_to: Service and repair contracts
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 417 and 420
rules.quote: “The law requires that the contractor offer you any parts that were replaced during the service call. If you do not want the parts, initial the checkbox labeled ‘OK for contractor to take replaced parts.’”

rules.title: Only one service charge (incl. trip or inspection fee); disclose in ads and on the call
rules.plain_english: A service and repair contractor may charge only one service charge, which includes trip charges and inspection fees. If one is charged, the contract must show 'Amount of Service Charge' with the required statement, every advertisement must disclose that there is a service charge, and the amount must be disclosed when the customer calls.

parameters.required_text: You may be charged only one service charge, including any trip charge or inspection fee.
parameters.advertising_disclosure: all advertisements must disclose that there is a service charge
parameters.call_disclosure: disclose amount of service charge when customer initiates the call

rules.applies_to: Service and repair contractors
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 417 and 419-420
rules.quote: A service and repair contractor charging a service charge shall disclose in all advertisements that there is a service charge and, when the customer initiates the call for service, shall disclose the amount of the service charge.
rules.notes: Ad-copy checker: any ad by a contractor that charges a service charge must mention it.

rules.title: 'Your Rights to Cancel Before Work Begins' notice (3/5/7 business days for listed reasons)
rules.plain_english: Service and repair contracts must include, next to the buyer's signature, the 12-point bold 'YOUR RIGHTS TO CANCEL BEFORE WORK BEGINS' notice, signed and dated by the buyer. The buyer may cancel until they have the signed copy and work starts; after work starts they may still cancel within 3 business days (7 for declared-disaster repairs, 5 for seniors) if the price exceeds $750, they did not initiate contact, they were upsold, or payment was due or accepted before completion.

parameters.placement: immediate proximity to space reserved for buyer's signature
parameters.cancel_before_work: until buyer receives signed and dated copy AND contractor starts work
post_start_cancel_reasons: price incl. labor and materials over $750
contractor sold goods/services beyond those reasonably necessary
payment was due or money accepted before work complete
parameters.required_text:
YOUR RIGHTS TO CANCEL BEFORE WORK BEGINS
(A) You, the buyer, have the right to cancel this contract until:
1. You receive a copy of this contract signed and dated by you and the contractor; and
2. The contractor starts work.
(B) However, even if the work has begun you, the buyer, may still cancel the contract for any of the reasons specified in items 1 through 4 of this paragraph. If any of these reasons occur, you may cancel the contract within three business days of signing the contract for normal service and repairs, or within seven business days of signing a contract to repair or correct conditions resulting from any sudden or catastrophic event for which a state of emergency has been declared by the President of the United States or the Governor, or for which a local emergency has been declared by the executive officer or governing body of any city, county, or city and county:
1. You may cancel the contract if the price, including all labor and materials, is more than seven hundred fifty dollars ($750).
2. You may cancel the contract if you did not initiate the contact with the contractor to request the work.
3. You may cancel the contract if the contractor sold you goods or services beyond those reasonably necessary to take care of the particular problem that caused you to contact the contractor.
4. You may cancel the contract if the payment was due or the contractor accepted any money before the work was complete.
(C) If any of these reasons for canceling occurred, you may cancel the contract as specified under paragraph (B) above by e-mailing, mailing, faxing, or delivering a written notice to the contractor at the contractor’s place of business within three business days or, if applicable, seven business days of the date you received a signed and dated copy of this contract. Include your name, your address, and the date you received a signed copy of the contract and this notice.
If you cancel, the contractor must return to you anything you paid within 10 days of receiving the notice of cancellation. For your part, you must make available to the contractor at your residence, in substantially as good condition as you received it, any goods delivered to you under this contract. Or, you may, if you wish, comply with the contractor’s instructions on how to return the goods at the contractor’s expense and risk. If you make the goods available to the contractor and the contractor does not pick them up within 20 days of the date of your notice of cancellation, you may keep them without any further obligation. If you fail to make the goods available to the contractor, or if you agree to return the goods to the contractor and fail to do so, then you remain liable for performance of all obligations under the contract.
parameters.senior_substitution: references to “three” changed to “five” for a senior citizen buyer

rules.applies_to: Service and repair contracts
rules.quote: (A) You, the buyer, have the right to cancel this contract until: 1. You receive a copy of this contract signed and dated by you and the contractor; and 2. The contractor starts work.
rules.effective: Five-day senior right applies to contracts entered into on or after January 1, 2021
rules.notes: Note an inconsistency in the statutory text: (B) counts days from 'signing the contract' while (C) counts from 'the date you received a signed and dated copy'. A conservative calculator uses the later of the two dates (interpretation).

rules.title: Service and repair cancel notice may be attached with checkbox; alarm operator exemption
rules.plain_english: The service and repair right-to-cancel notice may be an attachment if the contract has a 12-point bold checkbox statement the buyer initials. The notice requirement does not apply to alarm company operators who comply with Civil Code 1689.5-1689.7.

parameters.checkbox_text_standard: The law requires that the contractor give you a notice explaining your right to cancel. Initial the checkbox if the contractor has given you a ‘Notice of Your Right to Cancel.’
parameters.checkbox_text_disaster: The law requires that the contractor give you a notice explaining your right to cancel contracts for the repair or restoration of residential premises damaged by a disaster. Initial the checkbox if the contractor has given you a ‘Notice of Your Right to Cancel.’
parameters.exempt: alarm company operator licensees (B&P 7590 et seq.) complying with Civil Code 1689.5, 1689.6, 1689.7

rules.applies_to: Service and repair contracts
rules.quote: “The law requires that the contractor give you a notice explaining your right to cancel. Initial the checkbox if the contractor has given you a ‘Notice of Your Right to Cancel.’”

rules.title: Bona fide service repairperson may sign service and repair contract for contractor
rules.plain_english: A bona fide service repairperson employed by a licensed contractor, or a subcontractor hired by a licensed contractor, may enter into a service and repair contract on that contractor's behalf.

authorized_signers: bona fide service repairperson employed by licensed contractor

rules.applies_to: Service and repair contractors
rules.quote: A bona fide service repairperson employed by a licensed contractor or subcontractor hired by a licensed contractor may enter into a service and repair contract on behalf of that contractor.

rules.title: Service and repair substantive rules: $750 cap, written amount, payment only after completion, lien releases
rules.plain_english: A service and repair contract may not exceed $750; must be written with a fixed or estimated amount including profit, labor and materials (excluding finance charges); requires buyer-initiated contact and no upselling; payment is not due before completion; and on request after any payment the contractor must furnish an unconditional lien release. Any violation of 7159.10 or 7159.14 is cause for discipline.

parameters.lien_release_on_request: full and unconditional release (Civil Code 8400, 8404) for portion paid

rules.applies_to: Service and repair contractors
rules.quote: (1) The contract shall not exceed seven hundred fifty dollars ($750). (2) The contract shall be in writing and shall state the agreed contract amount, which may be stated as either a fixed contract amount in dollars and cents or, if a time and materials formula is used, as an estimated contract amount in dollars and cents.

rules.title: Service and repair violations: misdemeanor $100-$5,000; 4-year/2-year filing deadlines
rules.plain_english: Violating the $750 cap, written-amount, entire-cost, T&M estimate, buyer-initiated, no-upsell or single-service-charge rules is a misdemeanor with a $100 to $5,000 fine and/or up to one year in jail. Charges must be filed within four years (unlicensed) or two years (licensed) from the contract date or first payment; administrative actions are not limited.

parameters.sol_measured_from: date of contract; if unwritten, date of buyer's first payment

rules.applies_to: Service and repair contractors, agents and salespersons
rules.quote: A violation of paragraph (1), (2), (3), (4), (5), (6), or (8) of subdivision (a) ... is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not less than one hundred dollars ($100) nor more than five thousand dollars ($5,000), or by imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding one year, or by both that fine and imprisonment.
rules.notes: Paragraph (7) (payment before completion) is not in the misdemeanor list but is cause for discipline.

rules.title: Service and repair disaster fraud: full restitution plus fine $500-$25,000
rules.plain_english: A person who violates 7159.14 in a scheme to defraud an owner or tenant over natural-disaster repairs must pay full restitution and may be fined $500 to $25,000 in addition to jail.

parameters.restitution: full, based on ability to pay

rules.applies_to: Service and repair contractors in disaster areas
rules.quote: In addition to full restitution, and imprisonment authorized by this section, the court may impose a fine of not less than five hundred dollars ($500) nor more than twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000), based upon the defendant’s ability to pay.

rules.title: Owner induced by knowing false statements may recover $500 penalty plus fees and damages
rules.plain_english: Anyone induced to contract for construction work (including home improvement) by knowingly false or fraudulent statements may sue the contractor or solicitor for a $500 penalty plus reasonable attorney's fees, on top of any damages.
rules.applies_to: Contractors and solicitors; owners as plaintiffs
rules.quote: Any person who is induced to contract for a work of improvement, including but not limited to a home improvement, in reliance on false or fraudulent representations or false statements knowingly made, may sue and recover from such contractor or solicitor a penalty of five hundred dollars ($500), plus reasonable attorney’s fees, in addition to any damages sustained

rules.title: False advertising, misrepresentation, bait advertising and document fraud are misdemeanors
rules.plain_english: It is a misdemeanor and grounds for discipline to use false or misleading advertising, make substantial misrepresentations or false promises to get a contract, commit fraud in contract or loan documents, prepare a note or trust deed for more than the job's price, or advertise work or prices you do not intend to honor. Ads that comply with FTC rules are not deemed false.

prohibited_acts: false, misleading or deceptive advertising as inducement for a contract
substantial misrepresentation in procuring a contract or false promise likely to induce
fraud in execution or material alteration of contract, trust deed, mortgage, promissory note or other document
preparing/accepting trust deed, mortgage, note or other evidence of debt knowing it states a greater obligation than the consideration (which may be a time sale price)
publishing false/deceptive/misleading advertising or advertising work/prices with intent not to accept contracts for that work or price
parameters.safe_harbor: advertisement subject to and complying with FTC rules, regulations or guides

rules.applies_to: All contractors (home improvement and other works of improvement)

rules.title: Mechanics Lien Warning (single-family dwelling contract version)
rules.plain_english: Single-family home construction contracts must include the 'Mechanics Lien Warning' statement in the 7164 wording, which differs slightly from the home improvement version.

parameters.required_text:
MECHANICS LIEN WARNING:
Anyone who helps improve your property, but who is not paid, may record what is called a mechanics lien on your property. A mechanics lien is a claim, like a mortgage or home equity loan, made against your property and recorded with the county recorder.
Even if you pay your contractor in full, unpaid subcontractors, suppliers, and laborers who helped to improve your property may record mechanics liens and sue you in court to foreclose the lien. If a court finds the lien is valid, you could be forced to pay twice or have a court officer sell your home to pay the lien. Liens can also affect your credit.
To preserve their right to record a lien, each subcontractor and material supplier must provide you with a document called a ‘Preliminary Notice.’ This notice is not a lien. The purpose of the notice is to let you know that the person who sends you the notice has the right to record a lien on your property if he or she is not paid.
BE CAREFUL. The Preliminary Notice can be sent up to 20 days after the subcontractor starts work or the supplier provides material. This can be a big problem if you pay your contractor before you have received the Preliminary Notices.
You will not get Preliminary Notices from your prime contractor or other persons you contract with directly or from laborers who work on your project. The law assumes that you already know they are improving your property.
PROTECT YOURSELF FROM LIENS. You can protect yourself from liens by getting a list from your contractor of all the subcontractors and material suppliers that work on your project. Find out from your contractor when these subcontractors started work and when these suppliers delivered goods or materials. Then wait 20 days, paying attention to the Preliminary Notices you receive.
PAY WITH JOINT CHECKS. One way to protect yourself is to pay with a joint check. When your contractor tells you it is time to pay for the work of a subcontractor or supplier who has provided you with a Preliminary Notice, write a joint check payable to both the contractor and the subcontractor or material supplier.
For other ways to prevent liens, visit CSLB’s Web site at www.cslb.ca.gov or call CSLB at 800-321-CSLB (2752).
REMEMBER, IF YOU DO NOTHING, YOU RISK HAVING A LIEN PLACED ON YOUR HOME. This can mean that you may have to pay twice, or face the forced sale of your home to pay what you owe.

rules.applies_to: Single-family dwelling construction contracts (owner retains 1+ year)
rules.quote: You will not get Preliminary Notices from your prime contractor or other persons you contract with directly or from laborers who work on your project. The law assumes that you already know they are improving your property.
rules.notes: Differences from the 7159(e)(4) version: 'if he or she is not paid', 'or other persons you contract with directly', and 'CSLB’s Web site'. Use the correct version per contract type.

rules.title: Single-family dwelling contract: legible, describe incorporated documents, signed copy before work

rules.title: Single-family dwelling contract: bond notice in 10-point bold or all caps near signatures
rules.plain_english: Near the owner's and contractor's signatures, the single-family home contract must state, in at least 10-point bold or all capital letters, that the owner can require the contractor to have a performance and payment bond and that the owner may pay for the bond.

rules.title: Lender-financed pool: conditions to start before loan rescission period ends
rules.plain_english: For a pool financed by a third-party lender, work may start before the loan rescission period ends only if the lender has agreed in writing to finance the maximum estimated cost, provided written TILA loan terms, agreed to hold the offer at least 15 days after excavation is complete (and to lend a lesser amount on same or better terms if cost is lower), and the buyer, at least three business days after receiving these writings, signs a separate request to start.

parameters.required_text:
NOTICE
Under the law, this contract is not enforceable until:
(1) A third party agrees to make a loan to finance the construction cost of the swimming pool;
(2) You agree to accept the loan; and
(3) You do not cancel the loan within the period prescribed for cancellation under the federal Truth in Lending Act or Regulation Z (usually three business days after the loan is consummated).
Until the cancellation period is over, the contractor cannot deliver any materials or perform any services except preliminary services for which no mechanic’s lien can be claimed.
However, as an alternative to the above, you can ask the contractor to start work and deliver materials before the cancellation period on the loan is over if all of the following have occurred:
(1) The lender has agreed, in writing, to provide you with financing for up to the maximum estimated construction cost of the swimming pool.
(2) The lender has provided you with a written copy of the terms and conditions of a loan for the maximum estimated cost, including the annual percentage rate, the finance charge, the amount financed, the total of payments, the payment schedule, and a description of the security interest to be taken by the lender.
(3) The lender has agreed in writing to offer these terms and conditions for a period not less than 15 days following completion of the excavation of the swimming pool.
(4) Three business days have passed since you received the writing mentioned in paragraphs (1), (2), and (3), and you then sign a copy of this form to request that the contractor begin construction of the swimming pool before the cancellation period on your loan is over.
The first day you can sign the request for the contractor to begin construction of the swimming pool is [contractor to insert third business day after buyer receives writings described in subdivisions (a), (b), and (c)]
If you sign this request, the contractor will be permitted to immediately begin performance of the contract, and if the contractor is not paid in accordance with the terms of the contract, he or she may file a lien against your property for the value of the labor and materials provided. [This paragraph shall be printed in 12-point type.]
REQUEST
I/we request that the contractor immediately start construction of the swimming pool.
[Date]
Buyer(s)

rules.notes: Article 11 applies only to asbestos abatement projects involving 100 sq ft or more of ACM surface area (7189.5).

rules.title: Contractor may take up to 12 asbestos bulk samples without consultant certification
rules.plain_english: A licensed contractor or registered asbestos abatement contractor does not need asbestos consultant certification to take no more than 12 bulk samples of suspected asbestos material that will be removed, repaired or disturbed on a residential construction project, but only for bid preparation, checking its own employees' exposure, or confirming an abatement contract was completed. The person sampling must be an AHERA-certified building inspector.

parameters.setting: construction project in a residential dwelling
parameters.material: suspected asbestos-containing material required to be removed, repaired, or disturbed
permitted_purposes: evaluating exposure to its own employees during construction or asbestos abatement
determining for its own purposes or for communicating whether an asbestos abatement contract has been satisfactorily completed
parameters.sampler_qualification: certified building inspector under AHERA, 40 CFR 763, appendix C to subpart E

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and registered asbestos abatement contractors on residential projects
rules.quote: Certification as an asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician shall not be required when a licensed contractor or registered asbestos abatement contractor takes no more than 12 bulk samples of suspected asbestos-containing material that is required to be removed, repaired, or disturbed as part of a construction project in a residential dwelling
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255; amended Stats 1996 ch 526 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Text does not state the consequence beyond 12 samples; by implication the exemption is lost and consultant certification rules apply. The same 12-sample exemption also applies to the 7187 conflict-of-interest rule.
rules.correction: No error. 12-sample limit, residential-dwelling setting, three permitted purposes and AHERA building-inspector requirement confirmed; the same exemption is restated in 7187. The quote spans the page 432/433 break ("re-/moved"), which is the only reason it does not machine-match.

rules.title: Contractors may not do asbestos risk assessment or clearance air monitoring
rules.plain_english: A licensed contractor or asbestos abatement contractor may not provide professional asbestos health and safety services, perform asbestos risk assessments, or (unless another law allows) perform clearance air monitoring after abatement. Those are consultant functions.

prohibited_activities: clearance air monitoring following asbestos abatement, unless otherwise permitted by law

rules.applies_to: All licensed contractors and asbestos abatement contractors
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 433 and 437
rules.quote: No licensed contractor or asbestos abatement contractor may provide professional health and safety services or perform any asbestos risk assessment. ... nor does it permit a licensed contractor or asbestos abatement contractor to perform clearance air monitoring following asbestos abatement, unless otherwise permitted by law.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255; amended Stats 1996 ch 526 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Clearance air monitoring must be done by an independent certified asbestos consultant/technician.

rules.title: Asbestos bid may report sampling results; contractor may charge for bid prep
rules.plain_english: An asbestos abatement bid may state the results and locations of asbestos sampling and how the asbestos will be abated, and the contractor may charge for bid preparation, including lab analysis costs.

bid_may_include: how the asbestos will be abated
parameters.may_charge_for: bid preparation, including cost of laboratory analysis of asbestos-containing material

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors and asbestos abatement contractors bidding abatement work
rules.source: 2026 CSLB Law Book, PDF pages 433 and 437
rules.quote: A bid for asbestos abatement may communicate the results and location of sampling for the presence of asbestos and how the asbestos will be abated. ... A licensed contractor or asbestos abatement contractor may seek compensation for bid preparation, including the cost of laboratory analysis of asbestos-containing material.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255; amended Stats 1996 ch 526 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Bid template field: sampling results, sample locations, abatement method; optional bid-prep/lab fee line item.

rules.title: Building owner must hire DOSH-certified asbestos consultant
rules.plain_english: When a building owner or operator hires someone for asbestos consulting or site surveillance technician work, the owner must contract with a DOSH-certified person.

parameters.trigger: engaging asbestos consulting or site surveillance technician services (B&P 7181/7182) after 1992-07-01
parameters.must_hire: person certified by DOSH under Labor Code 9021.5(b) regulations

rules.applies_to: Building owners/operators (project owners) on asbestos projects
rules.quote: When a building owner or operator engages the services of a person to perform asbestos consulting or site surveillance technician activities as defined in Sections 7181 and 7182 after July 1, 1992, the building owner or operator shall contract with a person who is certified by the Division of Occupational Safety and Health
rules.notes: Owner-side compliance check: verify consultant's DOSH certification card before contracting.

rules.title: Definition: asbestos consultant
rules.plain_english: An asbestos consultant is anyone who contracts to provide professional health and safety services for asbestos-containing material, including building inspections, abatement design, contract administration, supervising site surveillance technicians, sampling, asbestos management plans and clearance air monitoring.
rules.applies_to: Classifying asbestos-related service roles on a project
rules.quote: An “asbestos consultant,” as used in this chapter, means any person who contracts to provide professional health and safety services relating to asbestos-containing material ... including building inspections, abatement project design, contract administration, supervision of site surveillance technicians
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)

rules.title: Definition: site surveillance technician
rules.plain_english: A site surveillance technician is an independent on-site representative of an asbestos consultant who monitors others' abatement work, does area and personnel air monitoring, and performs building surveys and contract administration at the consultant's direction.

parameters.role: independent onsite representative of an asbestos consultant
duties: monitors asbestos abatement activities of others
asbestos air monitoring for area and personnel samples
building surveys and contract administration at direction of an asbestos consultant

rules.applies_to: Classifying asbestos-related service roles on a project
rules.quote: A “site surveillance technician” means any person who acts as an independent onsite representative of an asbestos consultant who monitors the asbestos abatement activities of others, provides asbestos air monitoring services for area and personnel samples, and performs building surveys and contract administration at the direction of an asbestos consultant.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)

rules.title: DOSH asbestos certification: 15-day completeness notice, 45-day issuance
rules.plain_english: DOSH must tell an asbestos consultant/technician applicant within 15 days of receipt whether the application is complete or deficient, and must issue the certification card within 45 days after a complete application is filed. If it misses these deadlines, it must issue a provisional card.

parameters.issue_card_from: date of filing of completed application
parameters.if_deadline_missed: provisional certification card issued until procedures completed

rules.applies_to: Applicants for DOSH asbestos consultant / site surveillance technician certification
rules.quote: Within 15 days of receipt of an application for certification pursuant to this article, the division shall inform the applicant in writing either (1) that the application is complete and accepted, or (2) that it is deficient ... Within 45 days of the date of filing of a completed application, the division shall issue
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Agency deadline; useful for scheduling when a company's staff must get certified before a project.

rules.title: DOSH must revoke asbestos certification for fraud or gross/repeated negligence
rules.plain_english: DOSH must revoke an asbestos consultant's or technician's certification if it was obtained under false pretenses, or if the holder acted with gross negligence or fraud, or committed repeated negligent acts (after an Administrative Procedure Act hearing).

parameters.procedure: Government Code 11500 et seq. (Administrative Procedure Act)

rules.applies_to: DOSH-certified asbestos consultants and site surveillance technicians
rules.quote: In the event the division determines that a certified asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician obtained certification under false pretenses, or that a certified asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician acted in a grossly negligent or fraudulent manner, or engaged in repeated acts of negligence, the division shall revoke that person’s certification.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)

rules.title: Asbestos consultant qualification: experience/education ladder + AHERA + exam
rules.plain_english: To be a certified asbestos consultant you need one of: 1 year asbestos experience + BS in engineering/architecture/industrial hygiene/construction management/related science; 2 years + any bachelor's; 3 years + related AA; or 4 years + high school diploma. You also need a valid federal AHERA certificate for the work type and must pass a DOSH exam.

experience_education_options.education: bachelor of science in engineering, architecture, industrial hygiene, construction management, or related biological or physical science
associate of arts in engineering, architecture, industrial hygiene, construction management, or related biological or physical science

also_required: valid federal AHERA certificate (15 USC 2641 et seq.) for the type of work, or DOSH-determined equivalent
passing score on DOSH-approved or DOSH-administered examination
exam_subjects: OSHA, DOSH, EPA, air district and DHS regulatory requirements
state-of-the-art abatement and control work procedures
AHERA training for inspectors, management planners, supervisors
industrial hygiene sampling methodology and recordkeeping

rules.applies_to: Individuals seeking asbestos consultant certification
rules.quote: (1) One year of asbestos-related experience, and a bachelor of science degree in engineering, architecture, industrial hygiene, construction management, or a related biological or physical science. (2) Two years of asbestos-related experience, and a bachelor’s degree.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)

rules.title: Site surveillance technician qualification: 6 months + HS + AHERA + exam
rules.plain_english: A certified site surveillance technician needs 6 months of asbestos experience under an asbestos consultant's supervision, a high school diploma or equivalent, a valid AHERA certificate, and a passing DOSH exam score.

parameters.experience_condition: under the supervision of an asbestos consultant
parameters.federal_certificate: valid AHERA certificate for type of work, or equivalent
parameters.exam: passing score on DOSH-approved/administered exam (5 subject areas)

rules.applies_to: Individuals seeking site surveillance technician certification
rules.quote: (a) Having six months of asbestos-related experience under the supervision of an asbestos consultant. (b) Possession of a high school diploma or equivalent.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)

rules.title: Owner's asbestos consultant cannot have an interest in the abatement contractor
rules.plain_english: When a building owner hires an asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician, that consultant may not have any financial or ownership interest in the asbestos abatement contractor hired for the same project. A contractor may still hire its own consultant for its workers' health and safety.

parameters.trigger: building owner or operator contracts with asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician
parameters.prohibited: consultant/technician has any financial or proprietary interest in an asbestos abatement contractor hired for the same project
parameters.exception_contractor_hire: contractor may hire a consultant to provide health and safety services for the contractor's personnel
parameters.exception_bulk_samples: does not apply to contractor taking <= 12 bulk samples in residential dwelling for the listed purposes

rules.applies_to: Building owners, asbestos consultants/technicians, and asbestos abatement contractors on the same project
rules.quote: that asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician shall not have any financial or proprietary interest in an asbestos abatement contractor hired for the same project. However, this section shall not preclude the hiring of a consultant by a contractor for the purpose of providing health and safety services for the personnel of the contractor.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255; amended Stats 1996 ch 526 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Legislative intent: consultant work (clearance air monitoring, design, contract administration) must reflect independent professional judgment.

rules.title: Penalties: uncertified asbestos consulting or conflict of interest
rules.plain_english: Practicing as an asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician without certification, or violating the conflict-of-interest rule, is an infraction on a first conviction ($1,000-$3,000 fine). A later conviction is a misdemeanor: certification must be revoked or suspended, and the fine is $3,000-$5,000 and/or up to one year in county jail.

violations: practicing as asbestos consultant or site surveillance technician without DOSH certification

rules.applies_to: Uncertified asbestos consultants/technicians and consultants with conflicts of interest
rules.quote: (a) Conviction of a first offense is an infraction punishable by a fine of not less than one thousand dollars ($1,000) or more than three thousand dollars ($3,000).
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Subsection (b) text in the book reads 'a fine not not less than three thousand dollars ($3,000) or more than five thousand dollars ($5,000), or imprisonment in the county jail not exceeding one year, or both' (typo 'not not' is in the source).
rules.correction: No error. $1,000-$3,000 infraction (first offense) and $3,000-$5,000 and/or up to 1 year county jail misdemeanor with mandatory revocation or suspension (subsequent offense) confirmed; the "not not" typo is in the book.

rules.title: Asbestos consultant rules apply at 100+ sq ft of ACM
rules.plain_english: The asbestos consultant certification article applies to asbestos abatement projects involving 100 square feet or more of asbestos-containing material surface area.
rules.applies_to: Asbestos abatement projects (owners, consultants, contractors)
rules.quote: This article shall apply to asbestos abatement projects within the meaning of asbestos-related work as defined in Section 6501.8 of the Labor Code, and which involves 100 square feet or more of surface area of asbestos containing material.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Below 100 sq ft, Article 11 (B&P 7180-7189.7) does not apply; other Cal/OSHA asbestos rules may still apply.

rules.title: State agencies may use their own DOSH-certified staff as asbestos consultants
rules.plain_english: State agencies need not hire outside asbestos consultants if their own assigned employees are DOSH-certified; where feasible, the state should use associate or senior industrial hygienists. Attorneys giving asbestos legal advice to owners need not be certified.

parameters.condition: state employees performing B&P 7181/7182 activities must be DOSH-certified
parameters.attorney_exemption: attorneys providing asbestos legal advice to building owners/operators need not be certified (7189.7(b))

rules.applies_to: State agencies as owners of state-owned or leased buildings
rules.quote: Nothing in this article shall be construed to require agencies of the state to contract with asbestos consultants or site surveillance technicians who are not employees of the state as long as employees of the state who are assigned to perform the activities described in Sections 7181 and 7182 have been certified by the division
rules.effective: Added Stats 1990 ch 1255 (no effective date printed)

rules.title: No public official's name in ads without written authorization
rules.plain_english: A licensed contractor may not use the name or position of a public official (local or state agency member, officer, employee, or consultant) in advertising or promotional material without that official's written authorization.

parameters.requires: written authorization of the public official
parameters.public_official_definition: member, officer, employee, or consultant of a local government agency (Gov Code 82041) or state agency (Gov Code 82049)

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees' advertising
rules.quote: The name or position of a public official may not be used in an advertisement or any promotional material by a person licensed under this chapter, without the written authorization of the public official.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1994 ch 1135 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Book cross-references Civil Code 1770 (Unfair Practices) in the Appendix.

rules.title: Required disclaimer when an authorized public official appears in ads
rules.plain_english: If a printed ad uses a public official's name or position with written authorization, it must include a disclaimer in at least 10-point roman boldface, in a contrasting color, set apart from other text, stating the official does not endorse the product/service in an official capacity. Broadcast ads must read the statement aloud clearly.

parameters.trigger: printed advertisement/promotional material uses public official's name or position with written authorization
parameters.color: contrasts with background so as to be easily legible
parameters.placement: set apart from any other printed matter
parameters.disclaimer_template: The name of {public_official_name} does not imply that {public_official_name} endorses this product or service in {his_or_her} official capacity and does not imply an endorsement by any governmental entity.
parameters.broadcast_requirement: statement read in a clearly audible tone of voice

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees' advertising that names a public official
rules.quote: The disclaimer shall consist of a statement that reads “The name of (specify name of public official) does not imply that (specify name of public official) endorses this product or service in (his or her) official capacity and does not imply an endorsement by any governmental entity.”
rules.effective: Added Stats 1994 ch 1135 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Ad-copy generator can fill the template automatically.
rules.correction: No error. At-least-10-point roman boldface, contrasting color, set apart, and the disclaimer wording (template matches the statute once the placeholders are filled) confirmed.

rules.title: Residential (1-4 unit) arbitration clause must be titled ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES
rules.plain_english: If a contract for work on residential property with four or fewer units has an arbitration clause, it must be clearly titled 'ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES'. In a printed contract it must be in at least 10-point roman boldface, or contrasting red print in at least 8-point roman boldface; in a typed contract, in capital letters.

parameters.trigger: contract for work on residential property contains an arbitration provision between the principals
printed_contract_format_options: contrasting red print in at least 8-point roman boldface type

rules.applies_to: Contractors whose contracts for work on 1-4 unit residential property include arbitration
rules.quote: If a contract for work on residential property with four or fewer units contains a provision for arbitration of a dispute between the principals in the transaction, the provision shall be clearly titled “ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES.”
rules.effective: Added Stats 1994 ch 1135 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Applies to any contract for work on such property (not only home improvement contracts).

rules.title: Mandatory arbitration NOTICE text and initial line
rules.plain_english: Right after the arbitration clause and immediately before the space where the parties initial agreement or refusal, the contract must print the statutory NOTICE (giving up court/jury trial, discovery and appeal rights) and the statement 'WE HAVE READ AND UNDERSTAND...'. Same formatting rules: 10-pt roman bold or red 8-pt roman bold if printed; capitals if typed.

parameters.placement: immediately following the arbitration provision and immediately before the line or space for parties to indicate assent or nonassent
parameters.notice_text: NOTICE: BY INITIALING IN THE SPACE BELOW YOU ARE AGREEING TO HAVE ANY DISPUTE ARISING OUT OF THE MATTERS INCLUDED IN THE ‘ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES’ PROVISION DECIDED BY NEUTRAL ARBITRATION AS PROVIDED BY CALIFORNIA LAW AND YOU ARE GIVING UP ANY RIGHTS YOU MIGHT POSSESS TO HAVE THE DISPUTE LITIGATED IN A COURT OR JURY TRIAL. BY INITIALING IN THE SPACE BELOW YOU ARE GIVING UP YOUR JUDICIAL RIGHTS TO DISCOVERY AND APPEAL, UNLESS THOSE RIGHTS ARE SPECIFICALLY INCLUDED IN THE ‘ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES’ PROVISION. IF YOU REFUSE TO SUBMIT TO ARBITRATION AFTER AGREEING TO THIS PROVISION, YOU MAY BE COMPELLED TO ARBITRATE UNDER THE AUTHORITY OF THE BUSINESS AND PROFESSIONS CODE OR OTHER APPLICABLE LAWS. YOUR AGREEMENT TO THIS ARBITRATION PROVISION IS VOLUNTARY.
parameters.acknowledgment_text: WE HAVE READ AND UNDERSTAND THE FOREGOING AND AGREE TO SUBMIT DISPUTES ARISING OUT OF THE MATTERS INCLUDED IN THE ‘ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES’ PROVISION TO NEUTRAL ARBITRATION.
printed_contract_format_options: contrasting red print in at least 8-point roman boldface type

rules.applies_to: Contracts for work on residential property with 4 or fewer units that include arbitration
rules.quote: NOTICE: BY INITIALING IN THE SPACE BELOW YOU ARE AGREEING TO HAVE ANY DISPUTE ARISING OUT OF THE MATTERS INCLUDED IN THE ‘ARBITRATION OF DISPUTES’ PROVISION DECIDED BY NEUTRAL ARBITRATION AS PROVIDED BY CALIFORNIA LAW AND YOU ARE GIVING UP ANY RIGHTS YOU MIGHT POSSESS TO HAVE THE DISPUTE LITIGATED IN A COURT OR JURY TRIAL.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1994 ch 1135 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Full notice text is in parameters.notice_text (dehyphenated from the printed line breaks). Generator should reproduce it word-for-word.
rules.correction: No error. notice_text and acknowledgment_text were matched word for word against the book (after removing line-end hyphens); placement and 10-pt bold / 8-pt red bold / capitals format confirmed.

rules.title: Noncompliant residential arbitration clause may not be enforceable against anyone but the contractor
rules.plain_english: An arbitration clause in a contract for work on 1-4 unit residential property that doesn't meet the title, notice and formatting rules may not be enforceable against anyone except the licensee. The statute implies, but does not say outright, that the contractor can still be held to it. CSLB can still investigate and discipline.

parameters.trigger: arbitration provision fails B&P 7191 requirements
parameters.consequence: may not be enforceable against any person other than the licensee

rules.applies_to: Contractors using arbitration clauses on 1-4 unit residential work
rules.quote: A provision for arbitration of a dispute between a principal in a contract for work on a residential property with four or fewer units that does not comply with this section may not be enforceable against any person other than the licensee.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1994 ch 1135 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Contract checker should flag missing title, missing notice, wrong font size/color, or missing initial line. Statute wording is "may not be enforceable against any person other than the licensee"; enforceability against the licensee is implied, not stated.
rules.correction: No error. The statute says the clause "may not be enforceable against any person other than the licensee"; still_enforceable_against = licensee is the implied reading, not express text. title and plain_english reworded on 2026-11-27 so the implied reading is not stated as express text.

rules.title: Definition: home inspection and home inspector
rules.plain_english: A home inspection is a noninvasive, physical, paid examination of the mechanical, electrical, plumbing, structural and essential components of a 1-4 unit residence done in connection with a property transfer, to find material defects. Any consultation called a home inspection (or similar) counts. A home inspector is anyone who performs one.

parameters.trigger: in connection with a transfer of real property (see 7195(e))
parameters.includes: any consultation represented to be a home inspection or any confusingly similar term
parameters.home_inspector: any individual who performs a home inspection

rules.applies_to: Contractors or firms offering pre-sale/transfer inspections of 1-4 unit homes
rules.quote: “Home inspection” is a noninvasive, physical examination, performed for a fee in connection with a transfer, as defined in subdivision (e), of real property, of the mechanical, electrical, or plumbing systems or the structural and essential components of a residential dwelling of one to four units designed to identify material defects in those systems, structures, and components.
rules.notes: Chapter 9.3 does not create a CSLB license for home inspectors; it sets duties and unfair practices.

rules.title: Definition: transfer (triggers home inspection rules)
rules.plain_english: A 'transfer' means a sale, exchange, installment land sales contract, lease with option to purchase, any other option to purchase, or ground lease coupled with improvements, of real property or a residential stock cooperative with 1 to 4 dwelling units.

transfer_types: lease with an option to purchase
parameters.property: real property or residential stock cooperative

rules.applies_to: Determining whether an inspection is a regulated home inspection
rules.quote: “Transfer” is a transfer by sale, exchange, installment land sales contract, as defined in Section 2985 of the Civil Code, lease with an option to purchase, any other option to purchase, or ground lease coupled with improvements, of real property or residential stock cooperative, improved with or consisting of not less than one nor more than four dwelling units.

rules.title: Home inspection of pool/spa must report drowning prevention features
rules.plain_english: When a property with a pool or spa is transferred, the home inspection must check which of the seven drowning prevention safety features listed in Health & Safety Code 115922(a) are present, and the report must identify them and specifically state if the pool or spa has fewer than two.

parameters.trigger: transfer of real property with a swimming pool or spa
parameters.report_must_identify: which, if any, of the seven features the pool or spa is equipped with
parameters.flag_statement: report shall specifically state if the pool or spa has fewer than two listed features

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors (including contractors performing home inspections) on 1-4 unit homes with pools/spas
rules.quote: In a dwelling with a pool or spa, the “home inspection report” shall identify which, if any, of the seven drowning prevention safety features listed in subdivision (a) of Section 115922 of the Health and Safety Code the pool or spa is equipped with and shall specifically state if the pool or spa has fewer than two of the listed drowning prevention safety features.
rules.notes: The seven features themselves are listed in H&S 115922(a), not in this chunk.

rules.title: Optional energy-efficiency items in a home inspection
rules.plain_english: If the client asks, a home inspection may include an energy-efficiency inspection covering items such as insulation R-values, window panes and frames, HVAC and water heating, appliance age and fuel type, fans, thermostats, air leakage areas, and window solar control.

parameters.trigger: requested by the client
optional_items: noninvasive inspection of insulation R-values in attics, roofs, walls, floors, ducts
number of window glass panes and frame types
heating and cooling equipment and water heating systems
age and fuel type of major appliances
type of thermostat and other systems
general integrity and potential leakage areas of walls, window areas, doors, duct systems
solar control efficiency of existing windows

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors
rules.quote: “Home inspection,” if requested by the client, may include an inspection of energy efficiency.
rules.notes: Checklist generator input.

rules.title: Definition: material defect
rules.plain_english: A material defect is a condition that significantly affects the value, desirability, habitability or safety of the dwelling. Style or aesthetics do not make something defective.
rules.applies_to: Home inspection reports
rules.quote: A “material defect” is a condition that significantly affects the value, desirability, habitability, or safety of the dwelling. Style or aesthetics shall not be considered in determining whether a system, structure, or component is defective.

rules.title: Home inspection report contents
rules.plain_english: A home inspection report is a written, paid report issued after the inspection that clearly describes the inspected systems, structures and components, any material defects found, and recommendations (including referrals for evaluation by appropriate persons).

must_include: description and identification of the inspected systems, structures, or components
recommendations regarding conditions observed or recommendations for evaluation by appropriate persons
pool/spa: drowning prevention features identified; statement if fewer than two

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors
rules.quote: A “home inspection report” is a written report prepared for a fee and issued after a home inspection. The report clearly describes and identifies the inspected systems, structures, or components of the dwelling, any material defects identified, and any recommendations regarding the conditions observed or recommendations for evaluation by appropriate persons.
rules.notes: Report template generator input.

rules.title: Optional landscape irrigation inspection report contents
rules.plain_english: A home inspection report on a parcel with an owner-controlled in-ground irrigation system may include an irrigation inspection report (by the home inspector or a certified landscape irrigation auditor) covering the controller, activation of each turf zone noting valve/piping/head malfunctions, overspray onto hardscape, runoff and ponding during a stated number of minutes, and any limits due to snow, ice or site conditions. No watering-restriction penalty may be imposed for running the system for the inspection.

parameters.trigger: parcel with in-ground landscape irrigation system under exclusive control of owner or occupant
report_contents_if_provided: examination of irrigation controller, noting observable defects in installation or operation
activation of each zone/circuit to turf grass, noting malfunctions of irrigation valve, visible supply piping, sprinkler heads and stems
observation during operation (minutes specified in report) of spray to hardscape, surface runoff, ponding
notation whether inspection limited by snow, ice, or other site conditions
parameters.watering_restriction_sanction_shield: no state/local agency or water purveyor sanction for operating system for the inspection (7195.5(b))

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors and landscape irrigation auditors; owners/occupants
rules.quote: a home inspection report on a dwelling unit prepared pursuant to this chapter on a parcel containing an in-ground landscape irrigation system, the operation of which is under the exclusive control of the owner or occupant of the dwelling, may include an irrigation system inspection report, prepared by either a home inspector or certified landscape irrigation auditor
rules.notes: Home inspectors are also encouraged (not required) to provide information on water-efficient irrigation (7195.5(c)).

rules.title: Home inspector may not give a property valuation opinion
rules.plain_english: A home inspector may not give an opinion of the property's value.

parameters.prohibited: opinion of valuation on a property

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors
rules.quote: A home inspector shall not give an opinion of valuation on a property.

rules.title: Home inspector standard of care: reasonably prudent home inspector
rules.plain_english: A home inspector who is not a licensed general contractor, structural pest control operator, architect, or registered professional engineer must perform inspections with the care a reasonably prudent home inspector would use. This duty cannot be waived by contract.

parameters.standard: degree of care a reasonably prudent home inspector would exercise

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors who are not GC/SPCO/architect/PE
rules.quote: It is the duty of a home inspector who is not licensed as a general contractor, structural pest control operator, or architect, or registered as a professional engineer to conduct a home inspection with the degree of care that a reasonably prudent home inspector would exercise.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1996 ch 338 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Licensed general contractors doing home inspections are presumably held to their own professional standard; the text does not state it.

rules.title: Home inspectors not exempt from contractor/engineer/architect licensing
rules.plain_english: A home inspector who is not a registered engineer may not perform analysis that amounts to civil, electrical or mechanical engineering, and being a home inspector does not exempt anyone from the Contractors License Law, architect, engineer, structural pest control or appraiser licensing laws.

not_exempt_from: Contractors State License Law (B&P 7000 et seq.)
Structural Pest Control Act (B&P 8500 et seq.)
Real Estate Appraisers law (B&P 11300 et seq.)

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors; contractors who also inspect
rules.quote: Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to allow home inspectors who are not registered engineers to perform any analysis of the systems, components, or structural integrity of a dwelling that would constitute the practice of civil, electrical, or mechanical engineering, or to exempt a home inspector from Chapter 3
rules.notes: Any repair work a home inspector performs still requires a CSLB license (subject to 7197 limits).

rules.title: Who the home inspector chapter does not cover; appraisers barred from inspecting
rules.plain_english: The home inspector chapter does not apply to registered engineers, licensed land surveyors, or licensed architects acting under their licenses, and does not change real estate licensees' or sellers' disclosure duties. A licensed real estate appraiser doing an appraisal may not also act as a home inspector, except as required by law or regulation standards.

parameters.condition: acting pursuant to their professional registration or license
parameters.appraiser_bar: licensed real estate appraiser performing an appraisal shall not engage in home inspection activity, except as required to comply with standards in law or regulation

rules.applies_to: Engineers, surveyors, architects, appraisers, real estate licensees
rules.quote: This chapter does not apply to a registered engineer, licensed land surveyor, or licensed architect acting pursuant to their professional registration or license

rules.title: Yellow CSST gas tubing: required notice in home inspection report
rules.plain_english: If a home inspector sees any shade of yellow corrugated stainless steel tubing (CSST gas line), the report must note it and include a statutory notice that proper bonding and grounding can only be determined by a licensed electrical contractor.

parameters.trigger: home inspector observes any shade of yellow corrugated stainless steel tubing
parameters.notice_text: Manufacturers of yellow corrugated stainless steel tubing believe that yellow corrugated stainless steel tubing is safer if properly bonded and grounded as required by the manufacturer’s installation instructions. Proper bonding and grounding of this product can only be determined by a licensed electrical contractor.
parameters.csst_definition: flexible stainless steel pipe used to supply natural gas and propane in residential, commercial, and industrial structures

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors; refers owners to C-10 electrical contractors
