rules.quote: Manufacturers of yellow corrugated stainless steel tubing believe that yellow corrugated stainless steel tubing is safer if properly bonded and grounded as required by the manufacturer’s installation instructions. Proper bonding and grounding of this product can only be determined by a licensed electrical contractor.
rules.notes: Lead source for electrical (C-10) bonding/grounding work.
rules.correction: No error. Notice text matched word for word; effective January 1, 2019 (Stats 2018 ch 225) confirmed.

rules.title: Home inspector/company may not do paid repairs within 12 months of its report
rules.plain_english: It is an unfair business practice for a home inspector, the inspector's employer, or an affiliated company to perform or offer to perform, for an extra fee, repairs on a structure for which it prepared a home inspection report in the past 12 months. Exceptions exist for home warranty repairs, structural pest control repairs, C-39 roof certifications and C-36 sewer laterals (with conditions).

parameters.measured_from: date home inspection report was prepared
covered_parties: company controlled by a company that also has a financial interest in a company employing a home inspector
parameters.prohibited: perform or offer to perform, for an additional fee, any repairs to a structure on which the inspector or inspector's company prepared a home inspection report
exceptions: home protection company affiliated with/retaining inspector, repairs under home protection contract claims (7197(b))
structural pest control operator repairs under B&P 8505 after a structural pest inspection (7197(c))
C-39 roofing contractor roof-certification repairs meeting 7197(d) conditions
C-36 plumbing contractor sewer lateral repairs with 7197(e) disclosure

rules.applies_to: Contractors and companies that also perform home inspections
rules.quote: (1) To perform or offer to perform, for an additional fee, any repairs to a structure on which the inspector, or the inspector’s company, has prepared a home inspection report in the past 12 months.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1996 ch 338; amended effective January 1, 2018 and January 1, 2022
rules.notes: A CRM can block repair quotes on addresses where the company issued a home inspection report < 12 months earlier.

rules.title: Home inspector may not inspect property it has an interest in
rules.plain_english: A home inspector or the inspector's company may not inspect for a fee any property in which it has a financial interest or any interest in the transfer.

parameters.prohibited: inspect for a fee any property in which inspector/company has any financial interest or interest in the transfer

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors and their companies/affiliates
rules.quote: (2) Inspect for a fee any property in which the inspector, or the inspector’s company, has any financial interest or any interest in the transfer of the property.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1996 ch 338; amended effective January 1, 2018 and January 1, 2022

rules.title: No referral payments to owners, brokers or agents
rules.plain_english: A home inspector or inspection company may not offer or give any compensation, inducement or reward to the property owner, broker or agent for referring business.

parameters.prohibited: any compensation, inducement, or reward for referral of business

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors and their companies/affiliates
rules.quote: (3) To offer or deliver any compensation, inducement, or reward to the owner of the inspected property, the broker, or agent, for the referral of any business to the inspector or the inspection company.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1996 ch 338; amended effective January 1, 2018 and January 1, 2022

rules.title: No contingent-fee home inspections
rules.plain_english: A home inspector may not accept an engagement where the job or the fee depends on the report's conclusions, pre-set findings, or the close of escrow.
rules.applies_to: Home inspectors and their companies/affiliates
rules.quote: (4) Accept an engagement to make an inspection or to prepare a report in which the employment itself or the fee payable for the inspection is contingent upon the conclusions in the report, preestablished findings, or the close of escrow.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1996 ch 338; amended effective January 1, 2018 and January 1, 2022

rules.title: C-39 roofer may repair after roof certification inspection if conditions met
rules.plain_english: A C-39 roofing contractor whose company also does the home inspection may still repair the roof for a roof certification if: different employees do the home and roof inspections; the roof inspection is ordered before or with the home inspection (or finished before it starts); and before the consumer authorizes the home inspection, the consumer gets a consumer disclosure with three specific statements.

conditions_all_required: different employees perform the home inspection and the roof inspection
roof inspection ordered prior to or at the same time as the home inspection, or completed before commencement of the home inspection
consumer disclosure provided before consumer authorizes the home inspection
disclosure_statements: The same company that performs the roof inspection and roof repairs will perform the home inspection on the same property.

Any repairs that are authorized by the consumer are for the repairs identified in the roofing contractor’s roof inspection report and no repairs identified in the home inspection are authorized or allowed as specified in the roof inspection.
The consumer has the right to seek a second opinion.
parameters.disclosure_timing: before the consumer authorizes the home inspection
parameters.roof_certification_definition: written statement by licensed C-39 who inspected the roof, made any necessary repairs, and warrants the roof is free of leaks at time of certification and should perform as designed for the specified term

rules.applies_to: C-39 roofing contractors whose company also performs home inspections
rules.quote: (1) Different employees perform the home inspection and the roof inspection. (2) The roof inspection is ordered prior to, or at the same time as, the home inspection, or the roof inspection is completed before the commencement of the home inspection.
rules.effective: Amended effective January 1, 2018 (Stats 2017 ch 508) and January 1, 2022
rules.notes: Disclosure statements copied from 7197(d)(3)(A)-(C); a generator can produce the disclosure form and a workflow can check timing and employee separation. The statute does not say the disclosure must be in writing; giving it in writing is prudent for proof.
rules.correction: plain_english said the consumer must get a "written disclosure"; 7197(d)(3) only says "a consumer disclosure" (no writing requirement stated). Removed "written". Conditions and the three disclosure statements match word for word (the printed (d)(3)(B) reads "authorized or allowed as specified", without the "except" used in 7197(e)(2)).

rules.title: C-36 plumber may repair sewer lateral after inspection with disclosure
rules.plain_english: A C-36 plumbing contractor whose company also does the home inspection may repair a sewer lateral it inspected if, before the consumer authorizes the home inspection, the consumer gets a disclosure with three specific notifications.

parameters.work: repairs pursuant to inspection of sewer lateral pipe connecting a residence or business to a sewer system
parameters.disclosure_timing: before the consumer authorizes the home inspection
disclosure_statements: The same company that performs the sewer lateral inspection and the sewer lateral repairs will perform the home inspection on the same property.

Any repairs that are authorized by the consumer are for the repairs identified in the sewer lateral inspection report and no repairs identified in the home inspection report are authorized or allowed except as specified in the sewer lateral inspection report.
The consumer has the right to seek a second opinion on the sewer lateral inspection.

rules.applies_to: C-36 plumbing contractors whose company also performs home inspections
rules.quote: (1) The same company that performs the sewer lateral inspection and the sewer lateral repairs will perform the home inspection on the same property.
rules.notes: Unlike the C-39 exception, no separate-employee or timing-of-order condition is stated.
rules.correction: No error. All three disclosure statements matched word for word.

rules.title: Home inspection contracts cannot waive duty or cap liability at the fee
rules.plain_english: Contract terms that waive the home inspector's duty of care or limit the inspector's liability to the cost of the inspection report are void as against public policy.

invalid_clauses: waiver of the B&P 7196 duty of care
limitation of home inspector liability to the cost of the home inspection report
parameters.effect: contrary to public policy and invalid

rules.applies_to: Home inspection agreements
rules.quote: Contractual provisions that purport to waive the duty owed pursuant to Section 7196, or limit the liability of the home inspector to the cost of the home inspection report, are contrary to public policy and invalid.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1996 ch 338 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Contract checker can flag these clauses.

rules.title: 4-year limit to sue over a home inspection report
rules.plain_english: A lawsuit for breach of duty arising from a home inspection report must be started within four years from the date of the inspection.

parameters.measured_from: date of the inspection
parameters.claim: breach of duty arising from a home inspection report

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors and their clients (buyers, owners)
rules.quote: The time for commencement of a legal action for breach of duty arising from a home inspection report shall not exceed four years from the date of the inspection.
rules.effective: Added Stats 1996 ch 338 (no effective date printed)
rules.notes: Record-retention tool: keep inspection records at least 4 years from inspection date.

rules.title: HERS California home energy audit with home inspection, on request
rules.plain_english: If the client asks, a home inspection may come with a HERS California home energy audit. The HERS report must meet California Energy Commission standards (20 CCR 1670 et seq.), and the audit may be done by a home inspector who meets those requirements.

parameters.trigger: client requests
parameters.audit: Home Energy Rating System (HERS) California home energy audit
parameters.standards: Energy Commission HERS regs, Title 20 CCR Division 2, Chapter 4, Article 8 (section 1670 et seq.)
parameters.performer: home inspector meeting 20 CCR 1670 et seq. requirements

rules.applies_to: Home inspectors offering HERS audits
rules.quote: If the client requests a HERS California home energy audit, the HERS California home inspection report accompanying any home inspection report defined in subdivision (c) of Section 7195 shall comply with the standards and requirements established by the Energy Commission for HERS California home energy audits

rules.title: Statutes control over regulations not yet updated
rules.plain_english: CSLB regulations interpret the statutes; if a law changed and the regulation was not yet updated, the law still controls.

parameters.applies_when: rules and regulations not yet corrected to reflect changes in law

rules.applies_to: Any compliance tool using 16 CCR rules
rules.citation: CSLB Law Book Chapter 9 introduction (16 CCR Division 8)
rules.quote: Laws take precedence and are in effect, even if the affected rules and regulations have not been corrected to reflect any changes in the law.
rules.notes: Editorial statement in the book, not a regulation itself.

rules.title: Definition: battery energy storage system (stayed)
rules.plain_english: A battery energy storage system is one or more devices assembled together that store energy to supply electricity later. This definition's effective date was temporarily stayed when the book was printed.

parameters.definition: one or more devices, assembled together, capable of storing energy in order to supply electrical energy at a future time
parameters.status: effective date temporarily stayed at time of printing

rules.applies_to: C-10, C-46 and other contractors installing batteries
rules.quote: For purposes of this division, “battery energy storage system” means one or more devices, assembled together, capable of storing energy in order to supply electrical energy at a future time.
rules.effective: Effective date temporarily stayed at time of printing
rules.notes: Check current status with CSLB before relying on it; tied to C-10 and C-46 BESS rules.

rules.title: CSLB application fees
rules.plain_english: CSLB application fees: original license (one classification) $450; each extra classification with the original application $150; additional classification later (B&P 7059) $230; replacing the qualifier (RMO/RME etc.) $230; adding non-qualifying personnel $125; asbestos certification exam $125; hazardous substance removal certification exam $125.
rules.applies_to: License applicants and licensees
rules.quote: (1) An application for an original license in a single classification is $450. (2) An application for each additional classification applied for in connection with an original license is $150. (3) An application for each additional classification pursuant to Business and Professions Code Section 7059 is $230.
rules.notes: Qualifier replacement covers RMO, RMM, responsible managing member, or RME (B&P 7068.2).
rules.correction: No error. All seven amounts match 811(a) and the base amounts in B&P 7137(a)(1)(A)-(G).

rules.title: CSLB exam rescheduling fee $100
rules.plain_english: Rescheduling a CSLB exam (original license, added class, qualifier change, asbestos or hazardous substance certification) costs $100. Scheduling or rescheduling an exam required as a probation condition also costs $100.
rules.applies_to: Exam applicants and licensees on probation
rules.quote: (2) Scheduling or rescheduling an examination for a licensee who is required to take the examination as a condition of probation is $100.

rules.title: CSLB initial license and HIS registration fees
rules.plain_english: Initial license fee: $200 for an individual owner (active or inactive); $350 for a partnership, corporation, LLC or joint venture. Home improvement salesperson registration: $200. A U.S. Armed Forces veteran (including the National Guard or Reserve) who was not dishonorably discharged pays half (B&P 7137(a)(3)(D)).

parameters.veteran_fee_reduction_condition: applicant is a veteran of the U.S. Armed Forces (incl. National Guard or Reserve) and was not dishonorably discharged; proof by driver license/ID marked "Veteran" or DD214 long form (B&P 7137(a)(3)(D), PDF page 375)

rules.applies_to: New licensees and HIS registrants
rules.quote: (1) The initial license fee for an active or inactive license for an individual owner is $200. (2) The initial license fee for an active or inactive license for a partnership, corporation, limited liability company, or joint venture is $350. (3) The registration fee for a home improvement salesperson is $200.
rules.notes: Initial license fee is in addition to the application fee in 811(a). B&P 7137(a)(3)(D) halves these initial fees for qualifying veterans.
rules.correction: No error in the amounts. Added: B&P 7137(a)(3)(D) requires a 50% reduction of these initial license/registration fees for an applicant who is a U.S. Armed Forces veteran (incl. National Guard/Reserve) not dishonorably discharged; 811(c) does not repeat this. plain_english updated on 2026-11-27 to add the veteran reduction.

rules.title: CSLB license and HIS renewal fees
rules.plain_english: Renewal fees: individual owner active $450, inactive $300; partnership/corporation/LLC/joint venture active $700, inactive $500; home improvement salesperson registration renewal $200. Renewing after the license expires adds a delinquency fee of 50% of the renewal fee (B&P 7137(a)(5)), and C-10 contractors pay an extra $20 with an active renewal (B&P 7137(a)(6)(A)).
rules.applies_to: Licensees and HIS registrants renewing
rules.quote: (1) The renewal fee for an active license for an individual owner is $450. (2) The renewal fee for an inactive license for an individual owner is $300. (3) The renewal fee for an active license for a partnership, corporation, limited liability company, or joint venture is $700.
rules.notes: Delinquency fee = 50% of the renewal fee if renewed after expiration (B&P 7137(a)(5)); C-10 holders pay an extra $20 with an active renewal (B&P 7137(a)(6)(A)). Renewal period length is set in B&P 7140 (not in this chunk).
rules.correction: No error in the amounts. Added from B&P 7137: delinquency fee = 50% of the renewal fee when renewed after expiration (7137(a)(5)); C-10 licensees pay an extra $20 with an active renewal (7137(a)(6)(A)). plain_english updated on 2026-11-27 to add the delinquency fee and the C-10 $20 fee.

rules.title: Business name change fee $100
rules.plain_english: Changing the business name recorded on a CSLB license costs $100.
rules.applies_to: Licensees changing their recorded business name
rules.quote: (1) The fee to change the business name of a license as it is recorded under Chapter 9 of Division 3 of the Business and Professions Code is $100.
rules.notes: Regulation 812 (dishonored check service charge) is repealed, but B&P 7137(a)(6)(F) still sets a $25 charge per dishonored check (PDF page 377). Statute allows the name-change fee to rise to $125 (7137(a)(6)(E)).
rules.correction: No error. $100 confirmed (statute allows up to $125). Note refined: regulation 812 is repealed, but B&P 7137(a)(6)(F) still sets a $25 dishonored-check charge.

rules.title: Rejected application abandoned if not returned within 90 days
rules.plain_english: A non-renewal application that CSLB rejected as insufficient or incomplete is considered abandoned if the applicant does not return it within 90 days from the original rejection notice (the Registrar may extend for good cause). An abandoned application cannot be reinstated; you must file a new one with a new fee.

parameters.measured_from: date of original notice of rejection
parameters.applies_to: all applications other than renewal applications
parameters.extension: Registrar may extend for good cause
parameters.consequence: application deemed abandoned; cannot be reinstated; must file new application with required fee

rules.applies_to: License, classification, qualifier and HIS applicants
rules.quote: An application, other than a renewal application, shall be deemed abandoned whenever an applicant fails to return an application rejected for insufficiency or incompleteness within 90 days from date of original notice of rejection. This 90-day period may be extended by the Registrar for good cause.
rules.notes: Deadline calculator: rejection_notice_date + 90 days.

rules.title: License application: experience record, prior license history, signed under perjury
rules.plain_english: The CSLB license application asks each member of the applicant's personnel for the qualifier's construction experience and whether anyone involved ever had a license refused or revoked, and must be signed under penalty of perjury by each member of the personnel.

information_required: record of previous construction experience of the personnel member who will qualify
whether applicant, any personnel, or known associates in contracting ever had a professional or vocational license refused or revoked
parameters.signature: each member of the personnel of the applicant, under penalty of perjury
parameters.experience_record_exemption: Registrar may exempt applicants eligible for exam waiver (B&P 7065.1) or not required to test (B&P 7065)

rules.applies_to: Original license applicants
rules.quote: (b) The application shall be signed, under penalty of perjury, by each member of the personnel of the applicant.
rules.notes: Registrar may require any other information needed to determine qualifications.

rules.title: Corporations must certify Secretary of State filings
rules.plain_english: A domestic or foreign corporation applying for a license must complete a Registrar-prescribed certification showing it has met California Secretary of State filing requirements (Corporations Code 200 and 2105).

parameters.required: certification prescribed by Registrar showing Secretary of State filing requirements fulfilled

rules.applies_to: Corporate license applicants
rules.quote: A foreign or domestic corporation, applying for a license, shall complete a certification as prescribed by the Registrar, showing that it has fulfilled the filing requirements of the California Secretary of State as set out in Sections 200 and 2105 of the Corporations Code.
rules.notes: Corp Code 2105 is the foreign-corporation qualification statement.

rules.title: Claimed experience must be documented; at least 3% field-investigated
rules.plain_english: All experience claimed on a license application must be supportable by documentation satisfactory to CSLB, and CSLB conducts a comprehensive field investigation of at least 3% of applications.

parameters.documentation_standard: all claimed experience supportable by documentation satisfactory to the Board

rules.applies_to: License applicants and their qualifiers
rules.quote: the Registrar shall conduct a comprehensive field investigation of a minimum of 3% of all such applications. ... All claimed experience shall be supportable by documentation satisfactory to the Board.
rules.notes: Employee experience-tracking tools should retain proof (pay records, project lists, employer letters).

rules.title: License experience: 4 years within the last 10 years in the class
rules.plain_english: Every license applicant needs at least four years of experience as a journeyman, foreman, supervising employee or contractor in the specific classification, within the 10 years immediately before filing. A journeyman is a fully qualified worker who can work without supervision, or who completed an apprenticeship.

parameters.journeyman_definition: experienced worker fully qualified (not a trainee) able to perform the trade without supervision, or one who has completed an apprenticeship program

rules.applies_to: Qualifying individuals for all contractor license applications
rules.quote: Every applicant for a contractor’s license must have had, within the last 10 years immediately preceding the filing of the application, not less than four years experience as a journeyman, foreman, supervising employee or contractor in the particular class within which the applicant intends to engage as a contractor.
rules.notes: See 825(b)-(e) for former-qualifier, military, training credit and qualifier rules; 826 allows equivalent experience.

rules.title: Former qualifier in same class: no 10-year lookback
rules.plain_english: Someone who was previously the qualifier on a license in the same classification can count experience without the 10-year time limit.

parameters.condition: applicant formerly a qualifier on a license in the same classification

rules.applies_to: Former qualifiers re-applying in same classification
rules.quote: An applicant who was formerly a qualifier on a license in the same classification applied for may compute experience without regard to the ten-year limitation.

rules.title: Military service during National Emergency extends 10-year window
rules.plain_english: Time served in the U.S. armed forces during a National Emergency can be added to the 10-year experience window.

parameters.extension: length of U.S. armed forces service during a National Emergency added to the 10 years

rules.applies_to: License applicants with military service
rules.quote: An applicant shall not be jeopardized in computing time for service in the armed forces of the United States during a National Emergency and the length of service may be added to the 10 years mentioned above.
rules.notes: Calculator: lookback_years = 10 + years_of_qualifying_service.

rules.title: School training/apprenticeship counts for at most 3 years
rules.plain_english: Accredited school training or a completed approved apprenticeship in the trade counts as experience, but never for more than 3 of the 4 required years.

creditable: acceptable training in an accredited school
completion of approved apprenticeship program (Labor Code 3070 et seq.) or Registrar-approved equivalent
parameters.must_be_in: the construction trade for which application is made

rules.applies_to: License applicants
rules.quote: In no case, however, will such training or completion of an approved apprenticeship program count for more than 3 years of the experience.
rules.notes: Therefore at least 1 year must be practical experience.

rules.title: Experience must be held by the qualifier, who takes the exam
rules.plain_english: The required experience must belong to one member of the applicant entity or its responsible managing employee, and that person must take the exam.

parameters.experience_holder: one member of the applicant entity or a responsible managing employee
parameters.exam_taker: the same member or responsible managing employee

rules.applies_to: All license applicants (individuals and entities)
rules.quote: The required experience shall be possessed by one member of the applicant entity or by a responsible managing employee therefore, and the member or responsible managing employee shall be required to take the examination.

rules.title: C-47 applicants must submit HUD installer training certificate
rules.plain_english: Since September 30, 2021, a C-47 General Manufactured Housing applicant must complete HUD-compliant initial installer training (24 CFR 3286.308(a)) from a HUD-confirmed trainer and submit the Certificate of Completion of Training with the application; without it the application is incomplete.

parameters.proof_document: Certificate of Completion of Training (24 CFR 3286.303(c))
parameters.trainer: qualified trainer confirmed by HUD under 24 CFR 3286.301 et seq.

rules.applies_to: C-47 license applicants
rules.quote: An application submitted without the certificate prescribed by this subdivision is not complete within the meaning of section 7072 of the Business and Professions Code.
rules.notes: In addition to the 825 experience requirement.

rules.title: Registrar may accept equivalent knowledge/training
rules.plain_english: CSLB's Registrar may decide that an applicant lacking the exact experience in 16 CCR 825 has comparable knowledge, training or experience that is equivalent.
rules.applies_to: License applicants short of the 825 experience
rules.quote: The Registrar may determine that an applicant who does not have the specific experience required in Section 825 has some comparable knowledge, training, and/or experience which is equivalent to the required experience.

rules.title: CSLB processing deadlines: applications requiring exam
rules.plain_english: For applications that require an exam (original license, added class, replacement qualifier), CSLB must: say within 60 days of receipt if it is complete (and referred to exam) or deficient; decide within 5 days on a resubmitted application; decide licensure within 115 days after referral to exam (once exam passed and bonds/fees/documents filed); decide within 45 days after a later exam is passed; and may add 60 days if the application must be investigated.
rules.applies_to: Applicants for original license, additional classification, or qualifier replacement with exam
rules.quote: (1) The Board shall inform an applicant in writing within 60 days of receipt whether the application is complete and has been referred for examination or is deficient and what specific information is required.
rules.notes: Board-side deadlines; useful for estimating when a company can start contracting in a new classification.

rules.title: Historical CSLB processing times (with exam)
rules.plain_english: CSLB's printed past-two-year processing times for applications with exam: original license 11 / 253 / 726 days (min/median/max); additional classification 20 / 96 / 617 days; qualifier replacement 20 / 78 / 428 days. These include time the applicant was responsible for.

parameters.basis: Board's past two years performance (as printed in regulation)

rules.applies_to: Planning for license/classification timelines
rules.quote: These periods include not only the Board’s processing time, but also the time for which the applicant is responsible: e.g., the return of a rejected application, failure of and/or failure to appear at examinations, filing of the required bond(s) and fee.
rules.notes: Figures are historical statistics embedded in the regulation, not legal deadlines; the reference period is not dated in the text and may be outdated.
rules.correction: No error. All nine min/median/max figures match.

rules.title: CSLB processing deadlines: applications not requiring exam
rules.plain_english: For applications without exam (B&P 7065 or 7065.1 waivers): CSLB must say within 50 days of receipt whether complete and what is required; decide within 5 days on a resubmitted application; and decide licensure within 15 days after acceptable bonds and documents are filed. The 50-day period can be extended 60 days for investigation.

applies_to_types: replacement of qualifying person without exam

rules.applies_to: Applicants under B&P 7065 or 7065.1 (no exam)
rules.quote: (3) Once the applicant has filed acceptable bond(s) and other documents required by Division 3 of the Business and Professions Code, the Board shall decide within 15 days whether the applicant meets the requirements for licensure.

rules.title: Historical CSLB processing times (without exam)
rules.plain_english: CSLB's printed past-two-year processing times without exam: original license 1 / 48 / 349 days (min/median/max); additional classification 24 / 58.5 / 358 days; qualifier replacement 1 / 29 / 253 days. These include applicant-caused time.

parameters.basis: Board's past two years performance (as printed in regulation)

rules.applies_to: Planning for license/classification timelines
rules.quote: These periods include not only the Board’s processing time, but also the time for which the applicant is responsible: e.g., return of a rejected application and filing of the required bond(s) and fee.
rules.notes: Historical statistics, not legal deadlines; reference period not dated.
rules.correction: No error. All nine min/median/max figures match (incl. 58.5-day median).

rules.title: Home improvement salesperson registration processing
rules.plain_english: CSLB must tell an HIS applicant within 30 days of receipt whether the application is deficient or the registration is issued, and decide within 5 days after a corrected application is returned. These periods can be extended 5 weeks if paid by personal or company check, or 60 days if investigation is needed. Historical times: 1 / 8 / 53 days (min/median/max).

parameters.completed_application_definition: acceptable form plus all required information, documentation and fee

rules.applies_to: Home improvement salesperson (HIS) applicants and the contractors who employ them
rules.quote: (c) The time periods outlined in (a) and (b) may be extended by 5 weeks if the fee is in the form of a personal or company check, or by 60 days if an application requires investigation to determine if a statement of issues must be filed.
rules.notes: Onboarding tool: budget up to ~30 days (plus extensions) before a new salesperson can sell home improvement contracts.

rules.title: Licensees may not contract outside their classifications
rules.plain_english: Every license is classified as Class A (general engineering), Class B (general building), or a specialty (C) class. A contractor licensed in one classification may not contract in another classification's field unless also licensed in it or the work is incidental and supplemental (16 CCR 831).

parameters.rule: no contracting in field of another classification unless also licensed in it or permitted by 16 CCR 831

rules.applies_to: All licensed contractors
rules.quote: (b) Contractors licensed in one classification shall be prohibited from contracting in the field of any other classification unless they are also licensed in that classification or are permitted to do so by Section 831.
rules.notes: Core check for bid/contract scope vs. license classes held.

rules.title: Incidental and supplemental work: essential to licensed work
rules.plain_english: Work in another classification is 'incidental and supplemental' to a specialty contractor's licensed work if it is essential to accomplish the licensed work. The specialty contractor may do it with its own employees or subcontract it.

parameters.test: work in other classification is essential to accomplish the work in which the contractor is classified

rules.applies_to: Specialty (C) contractors
rules.quote: For purposes of Section 7059, work in other classifications is “incidental and supplemental” to the work for which a specialty contractor is licensed if that work is essential to accomplish the work in which the contractor is classified. A specialty contractor may use subcontractors to complete the incidental and supplemental work, or they may use their own employees to do so.
rules.notes: Subcontracting incidental work still requires the sub to hold the proper class (general CSLB rules).

rules.title: List of CSLB specialty (C) classifications
rules.plain_english: CSLB specialty classes are: C-2 Insulation/Acoustical, C-4 Boiler/Hot Water/Steam, C-5 Framing/Rough Carpentry, C-6 Cabinet/Millwork/Finish Carpentry, C-7 Low Voltage, C-8 Concrete, C-9 Drywall, C-10 Electrical, C-11 Elevator, C-12 Earthwork/Paving, C-13 Fencing, C-15 Flooring, C-16 Fire Protection, C-17 Glazing, C-20 HVAC, C-21 Building Moving/Demolition, C-22 Asbestos Abatement, C-23 Ornamental Metal, C-27 Landscaping, C-28 Lock/Security, C-29 Masonry, C-31 Traffic Control, C-32 Parking/Highway Improvement, C-33 Painting, C-34 Pipeline, C-35 Lathing/Plastering, C-36 Plumbing, C-38 Refrigeration, C-39 Roofing, C-42 Sanitation, C-43 Sheet Metal, C-45 Sign, C-46 Solar, C-47 Manufactured Housing, C-49 Tree/Palm, C-50 Reinforcing Steel, C-51 Structural Steel, C-53 Swimming Pool, C-54 Tile, C-55 Water Conditioning, C-57 Well Drilling, C-60 Welding, C-61 Limited Specialty. Specialty contractors must work to the standards of their trade.

classes.C-4: Boiler, Hot Water Heating and Steam Fitting
classes.C-6: Cabinet, Mill Work and Finish Carpentry
classes.C-20: Warm-Air Heating, Ventilating and Air Conditioning

parameters.performance_standard: art, experience, science and skill necessary to satisfactorily organize, administer, construct and complete projects, in accordance with the standards of their trade

rules.applies_to: All specialty contractors; scope-to-license matching
rules.quote: Specialty contractors shall perform their trade using the art, experience, science and skill necessary to satisfactorily organize, administer, construct and complete projects under their classification, in accordance with the standards of their trade.
rules.notes: Class A and Class B are defined in B&P 7056/7057 (not in this chunk). C-61 has many CSLB-designated subcategories (D-codes) not listed here.

rules.title: C-2 Insulation and Acoustical scope
rules.plain_english: C-2 contractors install any insulating media and preformed architectural acoustical materials for temperature and/or sound control.
rules.applies_to: Insulation and acoustical work
rules.quote: An insulation and acoustical contractor installs any insulating media and preformed architectural acoustical materials for the purpose of temperature and/or sound control.

rules.title: C-4 Boiler, Hot-Water Heating and Steam Fitting scope
rules.plain_english: C-4 contractors install, service and repair power boilers, hot-water heating systems and steam fitting, including fire-tube and water-tube boilers, low-pressure hot-water boilers, piping, valves, gauges, pumps, radiators, convectors, fuel oil tanks/lines, chimneys, flues, heat insulation and associated equipment including solar heating equipment.

scope_includes: fire-tube and water-tube steel power boilers
solar heating equipment associated with these systems

rules.applies_to: Boiler and hydronic/steam heating work
rules.quote: A boiler, hot-water heating and steam fitting contractor installs, services and repairs power boiler installations, hot-water heating systems and steam fitting ... and all other equipment, including solar heating equipment, associated with these systems.

rules.title: C-5 Framing and Rough Carpentry scope
rules.plain_english: C-5 contractors do form work, framing and rough carpentry for framed structures, including sub-flooring, siding, exterior staircases and railings, overhead doors, roof decking, truss members and sheathing.
rules.applies_to: Framing and rough carpentry work
rules.quote: A framing and rough carpentry contractor performs any form work, framing or rough carpentry necessary to construct framed structures; installs or repairs individual components of framing systems and performs any rough carpentry or associated work

rules.title: C-6 Cabinet, Millwork and Finish Carpentry scope
rules.plain_english: C-6 contractors make cabinets, cases, sashes, doors, trims, nonbearing partitions and other finish carpentry from wood or other products, and place, erect and finish them in structures.

scope_includes: placing, erecting and finishing cabinets and millwork in structures

rules.applies_to: Cabinet and finish carpentry work
rules.quote: A cabinet, millwork and finish carpentry contractor makes cabinets, cases, sashes, doors, trims, nonbearing partitions and other items of ... This contractor also places, erects, and finishes such cabinets and millwork in structures.

rules.title: C-7 Low Voltage Systems: energy-limited, max 91 volts, no fire alarms
rules.plain_english: C-7 contractors install, service and maintain energy-limited communication and low voltage systems not exceeding 91 volts (phone, sound, cable TV, CCTV, satellite dishes, instrumentation and temperature controls, low voltage landscape lighting). Low voltage fire alarm systems are excluded.
rules.applies_to: Low voltage and communications work
rules.quote: A communication and low voltage contractor installs, services and maintains all types of communication and low voltage systems which are energy limited and do not exceed 91 volts. ... Low voltage fire alarm systems are specifically not included in this section.
rules.notes: Scope check: system voltage > 91 V or fire alarm requires another class (e.g., C-10).

rules.title: C-8 Concrete scope
rules.plain_english: C-8 contractors form, pour, place, finish and install mass, pavement, flat and other concrete work and set screeds. The class does not cover contractors whose only business is plaster coatings or placing reinforcing steel.

scope_includes: forming, pouring, placing, finishing, installing mass, pavement, flat and other concrete work
placing and setting screeds for pavements or flatwork
scope_excludes: contractors whose sole business is application of plaster coatings
contractors whose sole business is placing/erecting reinforcing steel or bars

rules.applies_to: Concrete work
rules.quote: A concrete contractor forms, pours, places, finishes and installs specified mass, pavement, flat and other concrete work; and places and sets screeds for pavements or flatwork.

rules.title: C-9 Drywall scope
rules.plain_english: C-9 contractors lay out and install gypsum wallboard and assemblies, including nonstructural metal framing, and do taping and texturing.
rules.applies_to: Drywall work
rules.quote: A drywall contractor lays out and installs gypsum wall board and gypsum wallboard assemblies including nonstructural metal framing members, and performs the taping and texturing operations including the applications of compounds that adhere to wall board to produce a continuous smooth or textured surface.

rules.title: C-10 Electrical scope (includes batteries and PV; stayed amendment)
rules.plain_english: C-10 contractors place, install, erect or connect any electrical wires, fixtures, appliances, apparatus, raceways, conduits, battery energy storage systems, photovoltaic solar systems or parts thereof that generate, transmit, transform or use electricity.

parameters.status: effective date temporarily stayed at time of printing (amended text)

rules.applies_to: Electrical, PV and battery storage work
rules.quote: An electrical contractor places, installs, erects or connects any electrical wires, fixtures, appliances, apparatus, raceways, conduits, battery energy storage systems, photovoltaic solar energy systems or any part thereof, which generate, transmit, transform or utilize electrical energy in any form or for any purpose.
rules.effective: Effective date temporarily stayed at time of printing
rules.notes: The explicit battery/PV language is part of a stayed amendment; verify current status with CSLB.

rules.title: C-11 Elevator scope
rules.plain_english: C-11 contractors fabricate, erect, install and repair elevators, including sheave beams, motors, cables, guides, cabs, counterweights, doors (including sidewalk elevator doors), controls and signal systems for electric, hydraulic and manual elevators.
rules.applies_to: Elevator work
rules.quote: An elevator contractor fabricates, erects, installs and repairs elevators, including sheave beams, motors, sheaves, cable and wire rope, guides, cab, counterweights, doors (including sidewalk elevator doors), automatic and manual controls, signal systems

rules.title: C-12 Earthwork and Paving scope
rules.plain_english: C-12 contractors dig, move and place earth materials for cuts, fills, excavations, grades, trenches, backfill and incidental tunnels (including use of explosives), and mix, fabricate and place paving and other surfacing.

scope_includes: use of explosives for these purposes
mixing, fabricating and placing paving and surfacing materials

rules.applies_to: Earthwork, grading and paving
rules.quote: An earthwork and paving contractor digs, moves, and places material forming the surface of the earth, other than water, in such a manner that a cut, fill, excavation, grade, trench, backfill, or tunnel (if incidental thereto) can be executed, including the use of explosives for these purposes.

rules.title: C-13 Fencing scope (excludes masonry walls)
rules.plain_english: C-13 contractors build and repair all types of fences, corrals, runs, railings, cribs, game court enclosures, guard rails and barriers, playground equipment, backstops, posts, flagpoles and gates, but not masonry walls.
rules.applies_to: Fencing work
rules.quote: A fencing contractor constructs, erects, alters, or repairs all types of fences, corrals, runs, railings, cribs, game court enclosures, guard rails and barriers, playground game equipment, backstops, posts, flagpoles, and gates, excluding masonry walls.
rules.notes: Masonry walls require C-29 (or B).

rules.title: C-15 Flooring and Floor Covering scope (excludes ceramic tile)
rules.plain_english: C-15 contractors prepare surfaces and install carpet, resilient sheet and tile, wood floors (including finishing and repair) and other flooring materials, except ceramic tile.

scope_includes: wood floors and flooring including finishing and repairing

rules.applies_to: Flooring work
rules.quote: A flooring and floor covering contractor prepares any surface for the installation of flooring and floor coverings, and installs carpet, resilient sheet goods, resilient tile, wood floors and flooring (including the finishing and repairing thereof), and any other materials established as flooring and floor covering material, except ceramic tile.
rules.notes: Ceramic tile requires C-54.

rules.title: C-16 Fire Protection scope (excludes electrical alarms)
rules.plain_english: C-16 contractors lay out, fabricate and install all types of fire protection systems and associated equipment, excluding electrical alarm systems.

scope_includes: all types of fire protection systems

rules.applies_to: Fire sprinkler / fire protection work
rules.quote: A fire protection contractor lays out, fabricates and installs all types of fire protection systems; including all the equipment associated with these systems, excluding electrical alarm systems.

rules.title: C-17 Glazing scope
rules.plain_english: C-17 contractors select, cut, assemble and install all glass, mirrored glass and glass substitutes, and fabricate and glaze frames, panels, sashes and doors.

scope_includes: fabrication and glazing of frames, panels, sashes and doors

rules.applies_to: Glazing work
rules.quote: A glazing contractor selects, cuts, assembles and/or installs all makes and kinds of glass, glass work, mirrored glass, and glass substitute materials for glazing; executes the fabrication and glazing of frames, panels, sashes and doors; and/or installs these items in any structure.

rules.title: C-20 Warm-Air Heating, Ventilating and Air-Conditioning scope
rules.plain_english: C-20 contractors fabricate, install, maintain, service and repair warm-air heating systems, water heating heat pumps, ventilating and air-conditioning systems with their ducts, registers, flues, controls and filters, including solar-powered HVAC.

scope_includes: ventilating systems with blowers and plenum chambers

rules.applies_to: HVAC work
rules.quote: A warm-air heating, ventilating and air-conditioning contractor fabricates, installs, maintains, services and repairs warm-air heating systems and water heating heat pumps, complete with warm-air appliances
rules.notes: Refrigeration below 50 F is C-38.

rules.title: C-21 Building Moving/Demolition scope
rules.plain_english: C-21 contractors raise, lower, crib, underpin, demolish, and move or remove structures and their foundations, but not alterations, additions, repairs or rehabilitation of the parts of a structure that stay.

scope_includes: moving or removing structures including foundations
scope_excludes: alterations, additions, repairs or rehabilitation of permanently retained portions

rules.applies_to: Demolition and building moving
rules.quote: A building moving/demolition contractor raises, lowers, cribs, underpins, demolishes and moves or removes structures, including their foundations. This classification does not include the alterations, additions, repairs or rehabilitation of the permanently retained portions of such structures.

rules.title: C-22 Asbestos Abatement scope; DOSH rules govern work and documents
rules.plain_english: C-22 contractors perform asbestos abatement (containment, encapsulation, removal and disposal of asbestos-containing construction materials) in and on buildings. All work and documentation must follow DOSH (Cal/OSHA) regulations. C-22 does not include rebuilding retained portions or hazardous substance removal.

scope_includes: disposal of asbestos containing construction materials (Labor Code 6501.8)
scope_excludes: addition to or alteration, repair, or rehabilitation of permanently retained portions of buildings/structures

rules.applies_to: Asbestos abatement work
rules.quote: An asbestos abatement contractor performs abatement, including containment, encapsulation, or removal, and disposal of asbestos containing construction materials, as defined in Section 6501.8 of the Labor Code, in and on buildings and structures.
rules.notes: Hazardous substance removal requires separate HAZ certification (B&P 7058.7).

rules.title: C-22: DOSH registration; proof within 90 days or automatic suspension
rules.plain_english: CSLB will not issue a C-22 unless the applicant is registered with DOSH (Labor Code 6501.5) or has a registration application pending, and all C-22 holders must complete DOSH registration training (8 CCR 1529). Within 90 days after the license issues, the contractor must give CSLB proof of DOSH registration; no asbestos work or documentation may be done until then. Missing the 90 days automatically suspends the license or removes the C-22 class.

parameters.pre_issuance_requirement: registered with DOSH under Labor Code 6501.5 or active DOSH registration application in process
parameters.proof_deadline_from: issuance of asbestos abatement contractor license
parameters.consequence_if_missed: automatic suspension of license or removal of C-22 classification at end of 90 days

rules.applies_to: C-22 applicants and licensees
rules.citation: 16 CCR 832.22(b)-(c); B&P 7180(b) (Labor Code 6501.5 registration still required)
rules.quote: Failure of a licensee to provide proof of current registration with DOSH within 90 days after issuance shall result in the automatic suspension of the license or removal of the C-22—asbestos abatement contractor classification at the end of the 90 days.
rules.notes: Deadline calculator: license_issue_date + 90 days; block scheduling asbestos jobs until proof is submitted.

rules.title: C-22 experience: 4 years in last 10 performing asbestos abatement
rules.plain_english: A C-22 applicant needs at least 4 years in the 10 years before applying performing asbestos abatement as a journeyman, foreman, supervisor or contractor for: a licensed C-22 (or asbestos-certified) DOSH-registered contractor, an out-of-state/federal licensed abatement contractor, a regulated utility, a state or federal government division, or the U.S. armed forces.

qualifying_employers: licensed contractor with C-22 or asbestos certification (B&P 7058.5) and DOSH registration
asbestos abatement contractor licensed in another state or federal jurisdiction
utility company operating under state or federal regulatory agency
division of a state or the federal government

rules.applies_to: C-22 applicants
rules.quote: Every applicant for the C-22—asbestos abatement contractor classification must have had, within the last 10 years immediately preceding the filing of the application, not less than four years of experience performing asbestos abatement duties as a journeyman,

rules.title: C-22 renewal requires current DOSH registration on file
rules.plain_english: A C-22 license can only be renewed if the licensee has proof of current DOSH registration on file with CSLB.

parameters.renewal_precondition: proof of current DOSH registration (Labor Code 6501.5) on file

rules.applies_to: C-22 licensees renewing
rules.quote: The Board shall require as a condition precedent to the renewal of an asbestos abatement contractor license that the licensee have on file proof of current registration with DOSH pursuant to Section 6501.5 of the Labor Code.
rules.notes: Track DOSH registration expiration alongside CSLB renewal date.

rules.title: C-23 Ornamental Metal scope
rules.plain_english: C-23 contractors fabricate and install sheet, rolled and cast metals (brass, bronze, copper, iron, stainless, steel, etc.) for architectural treatment and ornamental decoration, but not sheet metal contractor work.

scope_includes: assembling, casting, cutting, shaping, stamping, forging, welding, fabricating and installing metals for architectural treatment and ornamental decoration
scope_excludes: work of a sheet metal contractor

rules.applies_to: Ornamental metal work
rules.quote: This classification does not include the work of a sheet metal contractor.

rules.title: C-27 Landscaping scope
rules.plain_english: C-27 contractors construct, maintain, repair, install, or subcontract landscape systems and facilities for gardens and grounds, and prepare and grade land for architectural, horticultural and decorative treatment.

scope_includes: construct, maintain, repair, install, or subcontract landscape systems and facilities
public and private gardens and grounds
preparing and grading plots for architectural, horticultural and decorative treatment

rules.applies_to: Landscaping work
rules.quote: A landscape contractor constructs, maintains, repairs, installs, or subcontracts the development of landscape systems and facilities for public and private gardens and other areas which are designed to aesthetically, architecturally, horticulturally, or functionally improve the grounds within or surrounding a structure or a tract or plot of land.

rules.title: C-28 Lock and Security Equipment scope (excludes fire alarms)
rules.plain_english: C-28 contractors install and repair doors and door assemblies, gates, locks, panic and fire-rated exit devices, door/gate operators, jail locking devices, built-in safes and vaults, master key systems, window guards, security doors, card/electronic access control, detectors and related control computers. Fire alarm systems are excluded.

scope_includes: panic and fire rated exit devices
manual and automatic gate and door closures and releases
card activated and electronic access control systems

rules.applies_to: Locks, access control and security equipment work
rules.quote: A lock and security equipment contractor evaluates, sets up, installs, maintains and repairs all doors and door assemblies, gates, locks and locking devices, panic and fire rated exit devices ... Fire alarm systems are specifically not included in this section.

rules.title: C-29 Masonry scope
rules.plain_english: C-29 contractors install concrete units, clay products, block, stone, terra cotta and refractory brick, including load-bearing and non-load-bearing masonry walls and fences, ceramic veneer and thin brick, masonry paving, and incidental waterproofing, cleaning and caulking.

scope_includes: concrete units and baked clay products
structural load bearing and non-load bearing masonry walls and fences
ceramic veneer (not tile) and thin brick
clear waterproofing, cleaning and caulking incidental to masonry

rules.applies_to: Masonry work
rules.quote: A masonry contractor installs concrete units and baked clay products; concrete, glass and clay block; natural and manufactured stone; terra cotta; and fire brick or other material for refractory work.

rules.title: C-31 Construction Zone Traffic Control scope
rules.plain_english: C-31 contractors set up or remove lane closures, flagging or traffic diversions on roadways using portable devices like cones, delineators, barricades, sign stands, flashing beacons, arrow trailers and changeable message signs.
rules.applies_to: Construction zone traffic control
rules.quote: A construction zone traffic control contractor prepares or removes lane closures, flagging or traffic diversions, utilizing portable devices, such as cones, delineators, barricades, sign stands, flashing beacons, flashing arrow trailers, and changeable message signs, on roadways

rules.title: C-32 Parking and Highway Improvement scope (no re-paving)
rules.plain_english: C-32 contractors apply protective coatings and install vehicle stops, guard rails, striping, buttons, markers, signs and arrows on game courts, parking lots, airports and roads, including surface prep for coatings, but not re-paving.

scope_includes: signs and arrows on horizontal surfaces
surfaces: highway or roadway (concrete, asphalt or similar)

rules.applies_to: Striping, sealcoat and parking improvements
rules.quote: This classification includes the surface preparatory work necessary for the application of protective coatings but does not include the re-paving of these surfaces.
rules.notes: Re-paving requires C-12 or A.

rules.title: C-33 Painting and Decorating scope
rules.plain_english: C-33 contractors prepare surfaces (scraping, sandblasting, etc.) and apply paints, papers, textures, fabrics, stains, varnishes, sealers, waxes, adhesives and similar materials to structures for decorating, protecting, fireproofing and waterproofing.

scope_includes: surface preparation by scraping, sandblasting or other means

rules.applies_to: Painting and wallcovering
rules.quote: A painting and decorating contractor prepares by scraping, sandblasting or other means and applies any of the following: paints, papers, textures, fabrics, pigments, oils, turpentines, japans, driers, thinners, varnishes, shellacs, stains, fillers, waxes, adhesives

rules.title: C-34 Pipeline scope
rules.plain_english: C-34 contractors fabricate and install pipelines for water, gas, petroleum or other materials, including protective coatings and the trenching, boring, shoring, backfilling, compacting, paving and surfacing needed to complete them.

scope_includes: pipelines for conveyance of fluids (water, gas, petroleum)
pipelines for containment or protection of other material
trenching, boring, shoring, backfilling, compacting, paving and surfacing necessary to complete installation

rules.applies_to: Pipeline work
rules.quote: A pipeline contractor fabricates and installs pipelines for the conveyance of fluids, such as water, gas, or petroleum, or for the containment or protection of any other material, including the application of protective coatings or systems and the trenching, boring, shoring, backfilling, compacting, paving and surfacing necessary to complete the installation of such pipelines.

rules.title: C-35 Lathing and Plastering scope
rules.plain_english: C-35 contractors apply plaster and cement coatings (troweled or sprayed, including soundproofing and fireproofing) and install lath, metal studs, channel work and other plaster bases.

scope_includes: plaster/cement/lime surface coatings applied by trowel or spray
wood and metal lath and other plaster bases
channel work and metal studs for lathing and solid plaster partitions

rules.applies_to: Lath and plaster/stucco work
rules.quote: This classification includes the channel work and metal studs for the support of metal or any other lathing material and for solid plaster partitions.

rules.title: C-36 Plumbing scope
rules.plain_english: C-36 contractors provide safe water supply and fluid waste disposal, including on-site waste systems, gas/liquid/medical gas piping and tanks, gas appliances and flues (not forced warm air units), water and gas piping from the owner's side of the meter, water heaters including solar, and maintenance of safety devices like gas earthquake valves and backflow preventers.

scope_includes: complete removal of waste; construction and connection of on-site waste disposal systems
piping, storage tanks and venting for gases and liquids incl. vacuum, compressed air, medical/dental/commercial/industrial gases
gas appliances, flues and gas connections incl. suspended space heating units
water and gas piping from property owner's side of utility meter to structure
equipment to heat water or fluids, incl. solar equipment
maintenance and replacement of above and of gas earthquake valves, gas control valves, backflow preventers, water conditioning equipment, regulating valves

rules.applies_to: Plumbing work
rules.quote: (d) Water and gas piping from the property owner’s side of the utility meter to the structure or fixed works;

rules.title: C-38 Refrigeration: temperatures below 50 F (10 C)
rules.plain_english: C-38 contractors build, install, maintain and repair refrigerators, refrigerated rooms and spaces, insulation, AC units, ducts, blowers and controls for controlling air, liquid or gas temperatures below 50 degrees F (10 degrees C).
rules.applies_to: Refrigeration work
rules.quote: units, ducts, blowers, registers, humidity and thermostatic controls for the control of air, liquid, and/or gas temperatures below fifty degrees Fahrenheit (50°), or ten degrees Celsius (10°).
rules.notes: Scope check: design temperature < 50 F -> C-38; comfort cooling -> C-20.

rules.title: C-39 Roofing scope
rules.plain_english: C-39 contractors install and repair surfaces that seal, waterproof and weatherproof structures, using asphalt, pitch, tar, felt, glass fabric, urethane foam, metal roofing, shakes, shingles, tile, slate and other roofing or membrane materials.

materials: other roofing, waterproofing, weatherproofing or membrane materials

rules.applies_to: Roofing and waterproofing
rules.quote: A roofing contractor installs products and repairs surfaces that seal, waterproof and weatherproof structures.

rules.title: C-42 Sanitation System scope
rules.plain_english: C-42 contractors fabricate and install cesspools, septic tanks, storm drains and other sewage disposal and drain structures, including laying the associated pipe.

scope_includes: other sewage disposal and drain structures
cast-iron, steel, concrete, vitreous and non-vitreous pipe and related hardware

rules.applies_to: Septic, sewer and storm drain work
rules.quote: A sanitation system contractor fabricates and installs cesspools, septic tanks, storm drains, and other sewage disposal and drain structures.

rules.title: C-43 Sheet Metal scope
rules.plain_english: C-43 contractors fabricate and install sheet metal such as cornices, flashings, gutters, leaders, pans, kitchen equipment, ductwork (including insulation), patented chimneys, metal flues and metal roofing.
rules.applies_to: Sheet metal work
rules.quote: A sheet metal contractor selects, cuts, shapes, fabricates and installs sheet metal such as cornices, flashings, gutters, leaders, pans, kitchen equipment, duct work (including insulation, patented chimneys, metal flues, metal roofing systems and any other installations requiring sheet metal).

rules.title: C-45 Sign scope (includes sign wiring)
rules.plain_english: C-45 contractors fabricate, install and erect electrical signs (including their wiring) and non-electrical signs such as pole signs, building-mounted signs, painted wall signs and sign modifications.

scope_includes: electrical signs including wiring of such signs

rules.applies_to: Sign work
rules.quote: A sign contractor fabricates, installs, and erects electrical signs, including the wiring of such electrical signs, and non-electrical signs

rules.title: C-46 Solar: batteries only as incidental to PV and up to 80 kWh (stayed)
rules.plain_english: C-46 contractors install, modify, maintain and repair thermal and PV solar systems and may not do other building trades except as required for the solar install. A battery energy storage system is not part of a PV system; a C-46 may install a battery only as incidental and supplemental to a PV installation and only if the battery is rated 80 kWh or less.

parameters.other_trades_allowed: only when required to install a thermal or PV system
parameters.bess_allowed_if: installed as incidental and supplemental to installation of a PV system
parameters.status: effective date temporarily stayed at time of printing

rules.applies_to: Solar contractors installing PV and battery storage
rules.quote: a licensee classified in this section may install a battery energy storage system as “incidental and supplemental” to the installation of a photovoltaic solar energy system if the battery energy storage system does not exceed a rating of 80 kilowatt-hours (kWh).
rules.effective: Effective date temporarily stayed at time of printing
rules.notes: Verify current status with CSLB; standalone battery retrofits or batteries > 80 kWh would need C-10 (or other appropriate class) under this text.
rules.correction: No error. 80 kWh limit and the "effective date temporarily stayed at time of printing" flag confirmed.

rules.title: C-47 General Manufactured Housing scope
rules.plain_english: C-47 contractors install, alter, repair or prepare for moving manufactured homes, mobilehomes and multifamily manufactured homes, including accessory structures and foundations, and may connect gas, water, sewer and electric utilities on a single-family individual site placement. RVs, commercial coaches and factory-built housing are excluded.

parameters.utility_services_allowed: connection of gas, water, sewer, and electrical utilities on a single-family individual site placement

rules.applies_to: Manufactured housing installers
rules.quote: A general manufactured housing contractor may provide utility services on a single-family individual site placement. Utility services mean the connection of gas, water, sewer, and electrical utilities to the home.
rules.notes: See 825.5 for HUD installer training requirement.

rules.title: C-49 Tree and Palm scope (operative Jan 1, 2024)
rules.plain_english: Since January 1, 2024, C-49 contractors plant, maintain and remove trees and palms, including pruning, stump grinding and guying. No license is needed for incidental pruning or guying of planted trees by a nurseryperson, or incidental pruning by a gardener (B&P 7026.1).

license_not_required_for: incidental pruning of trees or guying of planted trees and limbs by a nurseryperson
incidental pruning of trees by a gardener (B&P 7026.1)

rules.applies_to: Tree service work
rules.quote: (a) A tree and palm contractor plants, maintains, and removes trees and palms. The duties include pruning, stump grinding, and tree, palm, or limb guying. (b) Effective January 1, 2024, this regulation shall become operative.

rules.title: C-50 Reinforcing Steel scope
rules.plain_english: C-50 contractors fabricate, place and tie steel mesh or reinforcing bars of any profile used to reinforce concrete.

scope_includes: fabricate, place and tie steel mesh
steel reinforcing bars (rods) of any profile, perimeter, or cross-section for reinforcing concrete

rules.applies_to: Rebar work
rules.quote: A reinforcing steel contractor fabricates, places and ties steel mesh or steel reinforcing bars (rods), of any profile, perimeter, or cross-section, that are or may be used to reinforce concrete structures.

rules.title: C-51 Structural Steel scope
rules.plain_english: C-51 contractors fabricate and erect structural steel shapes and plates used as structural members, including riveting, welding, rigging and metal roofing systems needed for that work.

scope_includes: fabricate and erect structural steel shapes and plates
metal roofing systems necessary to perform this work

rules.applies_to: Structural steel work
rules.quote: A structural steel contractor fabricates and erects structural steel shapes and plates, of any profile, perimeter or cross-section, that are or may be used as structural members for buildings and structures, including the riveting, welding, rigging, and metal roofing systems necessary to perform this work.

rules.title: C-53 Swimming Pool scope
rules.plain_english: C-53 contractors build swimming pools, spas and hot tubs, including solar heating equipment, using the trades necessary for that construction.

scope_includes: trades or skills necessary for such construction

rules.applies_to: Pool and spa construction
rules.quote: A swimming pool contractor constructs swimming pools, spas or hot tubs, including installation of solar heating equipment using those trades or skills necessary for such construction.

rules.title: C-54 Tile (Ceramic and Mosaic) scope
rules.plain_english: C-54 contractors prepare surfaces and install glazed wall, ceramic, mosaic, quarry, paver, faience, glass mosaic and stone tile, thin brick-look tile, and natural or simulated stone slabs for tubs, showers and interior horizontal surfaces, excluding hollow or structural partition tile.

scope_includes: glazed wall, ceramic, mosaic, quarry, paver, faience, glass mosaic and stone tiles
thin tile that resembles full brick
natural or simulated stone slabs for bathtubs, showers and horizontal surfaces inside buildings

rules.applies_to: Tile and stone slab work

rules.title: Disciplinary guideline: All other violations
rules.plain_english: Under CSLB's Disciplinary Guidelines, a license disciplined for any violation not specifically listed faces a minimum penalty of 5 day suspension, stayed, 1 year probation and a maximum of revocation. If warranted CSLB may add actual suspension of 5 days or more, restitution, plus probation terms and investigation/enforcement costs.

parameters.violation_title: All Other Violations
optional_terms_if_warranted: Actual suspension of 5 days or more.
Standard terms and conditions in cases of probation. (See page 566.)
If not taken within the past 5 years, take and pass the CSLB law and business examination.
Take and pass a course in Contractors License Law or a course related to construction law at an accredited community college. All courses must be approved in advance by the Registrar.
If not taken within the past 5 years, take and pass the CSLB trade examination.
Take and pass a vocational course(s) related to the trade(s) employed on the project. All courses must be approved in advance by the Registrar.
Submit copies of construction contracts to the Registrar upon demand during the probation period.
Make restitution
Pay CSLB investigation and enforcement costs.

rules.title: Standard probation terms in every CSLB probation
rules.plain_english: Every probation order requires the contractor to obey all laws governing contractors, have personnel of record appear for interviews with the Regional Deputy on request, and submit documents about its construction operations on demand. Violating probation lets the Registrar revoke probation and impose the stayed penalty (without a hearing if restitution is not paid); completing probation fully restores the license.

terms: obey all federal, state and local laws governing licensed contractors
respondent and personnel of record appear in person for interviews with Regional Deputy on request and reasonable notice
license fully restored on successful completion
violation: after notice and opportunity to be heard, Registrar may revoke probation and impose stayed order
failure to comply with restitution order: Registrar may impose stayed order without hearing
submit copies of documents directly related to construction operations on demand

rules.title: Commercial General Liability insurance disclosure must accompany every home improvement bid and contract
rules.plain_english: Every estimate or bid meant to lead to a home improvement contract, and every home improvement contract, must be accompanied by CSLB's 'Information About Commercial General Liability Insurance - Home Improvement' statement, checked to show whether the contractor carries CGL insurance and, if so, the insurer's name and phone number. Heading at least 14-point, questions at least 12-point, comments in at least 11-point italics.

fill_in_fields: contractor's name (does not carry / carries CGL)
parameters.template_text: Information About Commercial General Liability Insurance Home Improvement Pursuant to California Business & Professions Code § 7159.3 (SB 2029), home improvement contractors must provide this notice and disclose whether or not they carry commercial general liability insurance. Did your contractor tell you whether he or she carries Commercial General Liability Insurance? Home improvement contractors are required by law to tell you whether or not they carry Commercial General Liability Insurance. This written statement must accompany the bid, if there is one, and the contract. What does this insurance cover? Commercial General Liability Insurance can protect against third-party bodily injury and accidental property damage. It is not intended to cover the work the contractor performs. Is this insurance required? No. But the Contractors State License Board strongly recommends that all contractors carry it. The Board cautions you to evaluate the risk to your family and property when you hire a contractor who is not insured. Ask yourself, if something went wrong, would this contractor be able to cover losses ordinarily covered by insurance? How can you make sure the contractor is insured? If he or she is insured, your contractor is required to provide you with the name and telephone number of the insurance company. Check with the insurance company to verify that the contractor’s insurance coverage will cover your project. What about a contractor who is self-insured? A self-insured contractor has made a business decision to be personally responsible for losses that would ordinarily be covered by insurance. Before contracting with a self-insured contractor, ask yourself, if something went wrong, would this contractor be able to cover losses ordinarily covered by insurance? ■ _______________ does not carry Commercial General Liability (CONTRACTOR’S NAME) Insurance. ■ _______________ carries Commercial General Liability (CONTRACTOR’S NAME) Insurance. The insurance company is ____________________________ (COMPANY NAME) You may call the insurance company at ___________________ (TELEPHONE NUMBER) to verify coverage. For more information about Commercial General Liability Insurance, contact the Contractors State License Board at www.cslb.ca.gov or call 800-321-CSLB (2752). (This form meets the requirements of Rule 872 and Sections 7159.3 and 7164, Business and Professions Code.)

rules.title: Order of correction may be met by hiring another licensee or paying the owner

rules.title: How CSLB sets the time allowed to correct

rules.title: Request extension to correct in writing before the deadline
rules.plain_english: If conditions beyond the contractor's control prevent finishing corrections on time despite diligent effort, the contractor may request more time, in writing, before the correction deadline expires. If no request is made before the deadline, failing to correct on time is a violation even if good cause existed.

rules.correction: parameters.statute_overlay_from_2026_07_01 applied B&P 7099.2(b)(1) $500-$8,000 to 7125.4. That cannot be right: 7099.2(b)(1) yields 'except as otherwise provided by this chapter', B&P 7125.4(a) (PDF p. 370) sets $10,000 (sole owner) / $20,000 (entity) minimums per violation, and 16 CCR 884(a)/(c) allow up to $30,000 for 7125.4. Removed the overlay and replaced it with bp_7099_2_general_range_not_applicable. Also narrowed the overlay trigger: the book ties the $10,000/$20,000 minimums to a licensee 'found to have employed workers without maintaining workers' compensation coverage', not to a false exemption filing alone.

rules.title: Contest a CSLB citation within 15 days after service (statute), not 15 working days from receipt (regulation)
rules.plain_english: To contest a CSLB citation issued under B&P 7099, file a written request with the Registrar within 15 days after the citation is served. The regulation (16 CCR 885) says 15 working days from receipt, and B&P 7099.3/7099.4 say 15 working days from service. But B&P 7099.8(a) applies 'notwithstanding any other law' and requires the written hearing request within 15 days after service. Use the 15-calendar-day period counted from the service date to be safe. Instead of (or as well as) a hearing, you can request an informal citation conference within the same 15 days. If you miss the deadline, the citation becomes a final order that no court or agency can review (B&P 7099.4).

parameters.file_with: Registrar (written request for administrative hearing per B&P 7099.5); alternatively a written request for an informal citation conference to the chief of the enforcement division or designee (B&P 7099.8(b)(1))

rules.title: How CSLB serves a citation
rules.plain_english: CSLB serves citations by the method in Government Code 11505(c) and also sends a copy by regular mail. A citation of an unlicensed person under B&P 7028.7 may be served by certified mail at the person's last known business or residence address (B&P 7028.8). The contest deadline runs from service, not receipt: 15 days after service under B&P 7099.8(a).

rules.title: Penalty: disclosure violation (B&P 7030.1)
rules.plain_english: A contractor whose license was suspended or revoked two or more times within eight years must disclose that history before contracting for work on residential property with four or fewer units (B&P 7030.1). The statute fixes the penalty: $1,000 for the first violation, $2,500 for the second, and $5,000 plus a one-year suspension for the third; a fourth means revocation. The 884(a) table prints a $1,000 to $8,000 range.

rules.quote: Primary accessible path of travel shall include a primary entrance to the building or facility; toilet and bathing facilities serving the area; drinking fountains serving the area; public telephones serving the area, and signs.

rules.title: 2026 path-of-travel valuation threshold: $209,208
rules.plain_english: For 2026 the state 'valuation threshold' is $209,208. If the adjusted construction cost of your alteration is at or below this amount, path-of-travel upgrades are capped at 20% of that cost (CBC 11B-202.4 Exception 8). Above it, full path-of-travel compliance is required unless the building department grants an unreasonable hardship.

confirmed_by: City of San Diego Form DS-2123 (January 2026): '$209,208.00 2026 Valuation Threshold'

LADBS Counter Plan Check Correction Sheet (2020 LABC)
San Diego Accessibility Guide for Small Businesses (June 2015) and LADBS PC/DAD/App.20 (Rev. 1/26/15)

rules.applies_to: Alterations, structural repairs and additions to existing buildings and facilities covered by CBC Chapter 11B in California (commercial tenant improvements, public accommodations, public buildings)
