rules.title: At or below the threshold, path-of-travel spending is capped at 20% of adjusted construction cost
rules.plain_english: If the adjusted construction cost is at or below the valuation threshold ($209,208 in 2026), you do not have to spend more than 20% of that cost on path-of-travel upgrades. Example: a $150,000 adjusted cost means up to $30,000 of path-of-travel work, spent in the priority order.
rules.applies_to: Alterations, structural repairs and additions to existing buildings and facilities covered by CBC Chapter 11B in California (commercial tenant improvements, public accommodations, public buildings)
rules.source: https://www.sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/dsdds2123.pdf (City of San Diego Form DS-2123 'Determination of Unreasonable Hardship Exception to Accessibility Requirements' (January 2026); PDF page 3; page 3, 'For Department Use Only'); also https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/counter-plan-corrections-sheet.pdf (Section H, item 3)
rules.quote: The adjusted construction cost is less than or equal to the current valuation threshold. The elements noted in this application shall comply with accessibility requirements of California Building Code Chapter 11B and shown on the approved construction plans. The cost of compliance with Section 11B-202.4 need not exceed 20 percent (20%) of the adjusted construction cost of alterations, structural repairs or additions.
rules.notes: City of San Diego Form DS-2123 (January 2026), 'For Department Use Only' determination. LADBS states the same rule: 'When the adjusted construction cost is less than or equal to the current valuation threshold ... the cost of compliance shall be limited to 20 percent of the adjusted construction cost of alterations, structural repairs or additions' (Counter Plan Check Correction Sheet, Section H, item 3). The CBC text itself was not fetched.

rules.title: Above the threshold: full path-of-travel compliance, or hardship with at least 20% spent
rules.plain_english: If the adjusted construction cost is more than the valuation threshold, the path of travel must be brought into full compliance. Only if the building department finds an 'unreasonable hardship' can you do less, and then access must be provided by equivalent facilitation or as far as possible, spending no less than 20% of the adjusted construction cost.

if_unreasonable_hardship_granted.method: equivalent facilitation or to the extent possible without unreasonable hardship

rules.applies_to: Alterations, structural repairs and additions to existing buildings and facilities covered by CBC Chapter 11B in California (commercial tenant improvements, public accommodations, public buildings)
rules.source: https://www.sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/legacy/development-services/pdf/industry/smallbusaccess.pdf (City of San Diego DSD 'Accessibility Guide for Small Businesses' (Second Edition, June 2015; based on the 2013 CBC); PDF page 10; section 5.1.1, item 2); also https://www.sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/dsdds2123.pdf (PDF page 3)
rules.quote: compliance of the path of travel elements, as identified above shall be provided by equivalent facilitation or to the extent possible without creating an unreasonable hardship; but in no case shall the cost of compliance be less than 20% of the adjusted construction cost of alterations, structural repairs or additions.
rules.notes: Quoted from the City of San Diego Accessibility Guide for Small Businesses (June 2015, restating the 2013 CBC); the 2025 CBC text was not fetched. The City's current Form DS-2123 (January 2026) carries the same outcomes: 'REQUEST DENIED. The adjusted construction cost exceeds the current valuation threshold. The cost of compliance is determined NOT to be an unreasonable hardship' or 'REQUEST GRANTED ... Compliance will be provided as noted on this application by equivalent facilitation and full compliance.' Search-result excerpts of the current CBC (not read) carry the same 'in no case ... less than 20 percent' wording.

rules.title: Adjusted construction cost excludes path-of-travel work but not work in the altered area
rules.plain_english: When you compute the 'adjusted construction cost' for the 20% test, leave out the cost of the path-of-travel upgrades themselves. You may not leave out the cost of making the altered area itself accessible.

exclude_from_adjusted_cost: cost of alterations to path of travel elements required by 11B-202.4
do_not_exclude: cost of making the area of alterations or remodel accessible

rules.applies_to: Alterations, structural repairs and additions to existing buildings and facilities covered by CBC Chapter 11B in California (commercial tenant improvements, public accommodations, public buildings)
rules.source: https://www.sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/dsdds2123.pdf (City of San Diego Form DS-2123 'Determination of Unreasonable Hardship Exception to Accessibility Requirements' (January 2026); PDF page 2; Section IV footnotes 2 and 3)
rules.quote: For this exception, the adjusted construction cost of alterations, structural repairs or additions shall not include the cost of alterations to the path of travel elements required to comply with Section 11B-202.4.
rules.notes: Form DS-2123 footnote 2; footnote 3 adds: 'The cost of making the area of alterations or remodel accessible is not allowed to be excluded.' LADBS states the same exclusion (Counter Plan Check Correction Sheet, Section H, NOTE).

rules.title: Add the last 3 years of alterations on the same path that skipped path-of-travel upgrades
rules.plain_english: Owners cannot avoid path-of-travel upgrades by splitting work into small permits. The adjusted construction cost includes the cost of all alterations in the preceding three years, to this area and to other areas on the same path of travel, that did not provide an accessible path of travel.

parameters.include: construction cost of all prior alterations (preceding 3 years) to the proposed area and all areas on the same path of travel that did not provide an accessible path of travel

form_math.B: total cost of alterations, preceding 3-year period
form_math.compliance_percent: (A / (B + C)) * 100, A = amount spent on accessible elements

rules.applies_to: Alterations, structural repairs and additions to existing buildings and facilities covered by CBC Chapter 11B in California (commercial tenant improvements, public accommodations, public buildings)
rules.source: https://www.sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/dsdds2123.pdf (City of San Diego Form DS-2123 'Determination of Unreasonable Hardship Exception to Accessibility Requirements' (January 2026); PDF page 2; Section IV footnote 1)
rules.quote: The cost of alterations for the preceding three years includes the cost of construction of all alterations which did not provide an accessible path of travel to the area of the proposed alteration.
rules.notes: San Diego DS-2123 Section III asks for 'all improvements to the proposed area and all areas on the same path of travel with their construction cost for the preceding three years'. LADBS PC/DAD/App.20 states the same three-year rule.

rules.title: Spend capped path-of-travel money in priority order: entrance, route, restroom, phones, fountains, other
rules.plain_english: When the 20% cap applies, spend the money first on an accessible entrance, then an accessible route to the altered area, then at least one accessible restroom for each sex (or a unisex restroom), then telephones, then drinking fountains, then other items such as parking, storage and alarms.

priority_order: accessible route to the altered area
at least one accessible restroom for each sex (a unisex restroom is listed as an alternative on the San Diego guide and LADBS App.20 form)
when possible, additional accessible elements such as parking, storage and alarms

rules.applies_to: Alterations, structural repairs and additions to existing buildings and facilities covered by CBC Chapter 11B in California (commercial tenant improvements, public accommodations, public buildings)
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/counter-plan-corrections-sheet.pdf (LADBS Counter Plan Check Correction Sheet PC/STR/Corr.Lst.058, effective 1-1-2026, revised 4-3-2026; PDF page 8; Section H, item 4)
rules.quote: In choosing which accessible elements to provide, priority should be given to those elements that will provide the greatest access in the following order: a. An accessible entrance; b. An accessible route to the altered area; c. At least one accessible restroom for each sex; d. Accessible telephones; e. Accessible drinking fountains; and f. When possible, additional accessible elements such as parking, storage and alarms.
rules.notes: LADBS counter sheet wording. The San Diego Accessibility Guide (2015) lists item 3 as 'At least one accessible restroom for each sex or an unisex toilet facility' and adds signs to item 6; the LADBS Summary of Accessibility Upgrades form lists 'Accessible restroom for each sex or a unisex restroom'. Current 2025 CBC wording of this item was not read.

rules.title: Los Angeles: submit the Summary of Accessibility Upgrades form when using the 20% exception
rules.plain_english: In the City of Los Angeles, if the project is below the valuation threshold and not every path-of-travel element will be brought up to code, submit LADBS's 'Summary of Accessibility Upgrades' form showing what will be upgraded and what it costs. LADBS also requires an Unreasonable Hardship request to be prepared and submitted for approval.

parameters.form: LADBS Summary of Accessibility Upgrades for Commercial Projects (IB/P/BC 2026-076)
parameters.when: adjusted construction cost <= valuation threshold and not all path-of-travel elements will comply
parameters.also_required: request for Unreasonable Hardship submitted to LADBS for review and approval (counter sheet, Section H, item 3)

rules.applies_to: Commercial alterations permitted by the Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety (LADBS)
rules.citation: CBC 11B-202.4 Exception 8; LADBS CL-BC-2026-026 items A.3-A.4
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-026-Acc_Commercial.pdf (LADBS Commercial Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-026, effective 01/01/2026, revised 09/23/2026; PDF page 2; Section A, item 3)

The older LADBS form PC/DAD/App.20 (Rev. 1/26/15) shows the layout: cost of features provided (A) / adjusted cost of proposed construction (B) = percentage upgrades provided. rules.title: San Diego: request Exception 8 on Form DS-2123, signed by owner or design professional
rules.plain_english: In the City of San Diego, the 20% exception or a hardship finding is requested on Form DS-2123. It lists each path-of-travel element, whether it complies, its cost and what you will spend, plus 3 years of prior work, and must be signed and certified by the owner, architect or design professional.

elements_listed: route to the altered area (doors, corridor, elevator/platform lift, ramps, stairways)
parking (ramp on aisle, curb ramp, re-striping, detectable warnings)

rules.applies_to: Alterations permitted by the City of San Diego Development Services Department
rules.citation: CBC 11B-202.4 Exception 8; City of San Diego Form DS-2123
rules.source: https://www.sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/dsdds2123.pdf (City of San Diego Form DS-2123 'Determination of Unreasonable Hardship Exception to Accessibility Requirements' (January 2026); PDF page 2; applicant certification)
rules.quote: I, the undersigned, hereby request that the above-referenced project be granted exception from the accessibility requirements of the California Building Code, Chapter 11B, Section 11B-202.4, Exception 8. I certify that the information provided on this application is true and correct.
rules.notes: Form dated January 2026 (DS-2123 (01-26)).

rules.title: San Diego: a granted unreasonable hardship must be ratified through the appeals process before approval
rules.plain_english: In San Diego, when the cost is above the threshold and the City grants an unreasonable hardship, that finding must be ratified through the appeals process before the project is approved, and you must submit plans showing how access is provided.

parameters.applies_when: adjusted_construction_cost > valuation_threshold and unreasonable hardship granted
parameters.step: Appeals Action Ratification ruling before project approval
parameters.submit: copy of the construction plans showing how accessibility of noted elements is provided

rules.applies_to: Alterations permitted by the City of San Diego Development Services Department
rules.citation: CBC 11B-202.4 Exception 8; City of San Diego Form DS-2123
rules.source: https://www.sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/dsdds2123.pdf (City of San Diego Form DS-2123 'Determination of Unreasonable Hardship Exception to Accessibility Requirements' (January 2026); PDF page 3)
rules.quote: This finding shall be ratified through the appeals process prior to the approval of this project.
rules.notes: Form DS-2123 page 3 ('REQUEST GRANTED') and page 4 ('Appeals Action Ratification Ruling').

rules.title: The valuation threshold resets every January 1 using a construction cost index
rules.plain_english: The valuation threshold is good for one calendar year. DSA resets it on January 1 by scaling a 1981 baseline by the ratio of the current January construction cost index to the January 1981 index. Always use the figure in effect when the project is submitted.
rules.applies_to: Alterations, structural repairs and additions to existing buildings and facilities covered by CBC Chapter 11B in California (commercial tenant improvements, public accommodations, public buildings)
rules.citation: CBC 11B-202.4 Exception 8 and CBC definition of valuation threshold (as explained by the City of San Diego)
rules.source: https://www.sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/legacy/development-services/pdf/industry/smallbusaccess.pdf (City of San Diego DSD 'Accessibility Guide for Small Businesses' (Second Edition, June 2015; based on the 2013 CBC); PDF page 36; FAQ 14); also https://www.sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/dsdds2123.pdf (footnote 4)
rules.quote: The current valuation threshold is determined by multiplying the baseline valuation threshold by a ratio of the current year’s January Average Construction Cost Index (CCI) to the baseline January 1981 CCI. The current valuation threshold is established on the first day of January of every year by the California Division of State Architect.
rules.notes: The baseline dollar amount and index publisher are not stated in the documents read (a search excerpt of the DSA page, not read, describes a $50,000 January 1981 base and the ENR 20 Cities index). Form DS-2123 footnote 4 confirms the one-year validity and January 1 adjustment.

rules.title: Parking lot resurfacing or restriping alone does not trigger path-of-travel upgrades
rules.plain_english: Resurfacing or restriping an existing parking lot is limited to the work itself; it does not trigger the 11B-202.4 path-of-travel upgrades. The restriped spaces themselves still have to meet current accessible parking rules.

parameters.scope_limited_to: actual scope of work of the project

rules.applies_to: Contractors resurfacing or restriping existing parking lots in California
rules.citation: CBC 11B-202.4 (exception for parking lot resurfacing/restriping, as described by CCDA)
rules.source: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/2024/CCDA%20Guide%20to%20Accessible%20Parking%20Construction%20Industry.pdf (California Commission on Disability Access, 'A Guide to Accessible Parking for the Construction Industry' (CBC 2022 Edition, publication 05-15-2024), hosted by CSLB; PDF page 8; 'Maintenance and Alterations')
rules.quote: However, alterations of existing parking lots by resurfacing and/or restriping shall be limited to the actual scope of work of the project and shall not be required to comply with CBC 11B-202.4.
rules.notes: CCDA guide based on the 2022 CBC; the guide says it 'will not be updated unless there are relevant changes to the code'. The exception number in the 2025 CBC was not read. The guide advises checking with the AHJ.

rules.title: Public housing and publicly funded multifamily go under Chapter 11B (existing ones use 11B-202.4)
rules.plain_english: Multifamily housing that is public housing or publicly funded is reviewed under Chapter 11B (DSA rules), not only Chapter 11A. New publicly funded multifamily follows Chapter 11B; alterations to existing publicly funded multifamily trigger the 11B-202.4 path-of-travel rule.
rules.applies_to: Publicly funded multifamily housing and public housing projects in California
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-027-Acc_Residential.pdf (LADBS Residential Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-027, effective 01/01/2026, revised 08/21/2026; PDF page 2; Section A, items 4-6)
rules.quote: 4. Public housing as defined in Chapter 2 of this code is subject to provisions of the Division of the State Architect (DSA-AC) in Chapter 11B. (1101A.1) 5. Newly constructed publicly funded multifamily dwellings are subject to the provisions of Chapter 11B. (1101A.1) 6. Existing publicly funded multifamily dwellings are subject to provisions of Section 11B-202.4.
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC Residential Accessibility checklist, which restates CBC Chapter 11A (HCD 1-AC) sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). CBC text itself not fetched (dgs.ca.gov, hcd.ca.gov and codes.iccsafe.org are not reachable from this session).

rules.title: Changes in level: 1/4 in. vertical OK, 1/4-1/2 in. beveled 1:2, over 1/2 in. ramped
rules.plain_english: Floor level changes up to 1/4 inch may be vertical. Between 1/4 and 1/2 inch they must be beveled no steeper than 1:2. Anything over 1/2 inch must be a ramp or curb ramp.
rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-026-Acc_Commercial.pdf (LADBS Commercial Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-026, effective 01/01/2026, revised 09/23/2026; PDF page 3; Section B, item 1)
rules.quote: Changes in level of 1/4 inch high maximum shall be permitted to be vertical and without edge treatment. (11B-303.2) b. Changes in level between 1/4 inch high minimum and 1/2 inch high maximum shall be beveled with a slope not steeper than 1:2. (11B-303.3) c. Changes in level greater than 1/2 inch high shall be ramped, and shall comply with Section 11B-405 or 11B-406.
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC plan check checklist, which restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS.

rules.title: Wheelchair turning space: 60-inch circle or 60-inch T-shape
rules.plain_english: Where a turning space is required, provide either a 60-inch diameter circle or a T-shaped space inside a 60-inch square with 36-inch-wide arms and base.
rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-026-Acc_Commercial.pdf (LADBS Commercial Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-026, effective 01/01/2026, revised 09/23/2026; PDF page 3; Section B, item 2)
rules.quote: A T-shaped space within a 60 inch square minimum with arms and base 36 inches wide minimum. Each arm of the T shall be clear of obstructions 12 inches minimum in each direction and the base shall be clear of obstructions 24 inches minimum.
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC plan check checklist, which restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS. Item 2a on the same page: 'A 60-inch diameter circle (11B-304.3.1)'.

rules.title: Door clear width 32 in. minimum (36 in. where the opening is over 24 in. deep)
rules.plain_english: Accessible door openings need at least 32 inches of clear width. If the opening is more than 24 inches deep, it needs 36 inches.

parameters.strike_side_clearance_note: LADBS item 26 also asks to dimension 18 in. interior and 24 in. exterior strike-side clearance

rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-026-Acc_Commercial.pdf (LADBS Commercial Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-026, effective 01/01/2026, revised 09/23/2026; PDF page 6; Section C, item 24)
rules.quote: Door openings shall provide a clear width of 32 inches minimum. Openings more than 24 inches deep shall provide a clear opening of 36 inches minimum.
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC plan check checklist, which restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS. The 2010 ADA Standards 404.2.3 set the same 32/36-inch figures.

rules.title: Ramps: max slope 1:12, cross slope 1:48, 48 in. clear width, 30 in. max rise per run
rules.plain_english: Ramp runs can be no steeper than 1:12 (8.33%) with cross slope no more than 1:48 (2.083%). Under CBC 11B the clear width is at least 48 inches, each run rises no more than 30 inches, and every run needs a landing at top and bottom.

parameters.landings: top and bottom of each ramp run

rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-026-Acc_Commercial.pdf (LADBS Commercial Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-026, effective 01/01/2026, revised 09/23/2026; PDF page 7; Section C, item 32)
rules.quote: Ramp runs shall not exceed a running slope of 1:12 (8.33%) and cross slopes of ramp runs shall not be steeper than 1:48 (2.083%).
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC plan check checklist, which restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS. Same page: 'The clear width of a ramp run shall be 48 inches minimum. (11B-405.5)'; 'The rise for any ramp run shall be 30 inches maximum. (11B-405.6)'; 'Ramps shall have landings at the top and the bottom of each ramp run. (11B-405.7)'.

rules.title: Site path of travel: 48 in. walkway, 5% max running slope, 2% max cross slope
rules.plain_english: LADBS asks site plans to show the accessible path of travel as a walkway at least 48 inches wide, no steeper than 5% in the direction of travel and no more than 2% cross slope; steeper walks become ramps.
rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-026-Acc_Commercial.pdf (LADBS Commercial Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-026, effective 01/01/2026, revised 09/23/2026; PDF page 5; Section C, item 12)
rules.quote: On the site plan, show and define the required accessible path of travel: 48 in minimum width walkway, 5% maximum slope in the direction of travel, 2% maximum cross-slope.
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC plan check checklist, which restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS.

rules.title: Big floors (over 10,000 sq ft): accessible vertical access within 200 ft of each stair or escalator
rules.plain_english: In buildings where elevators are required and any floor exceeds 10,000 square feet, provide a ramp, elevator or lift within 200 feet of travel of each stair and escalator. In existing buildings this applies to each newly built stair or escalator.
rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-026-Acc_Commercial.pdf (LADBS Commercial Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-026, effective 01/01/2026, revised 09/23/2026; PDF page 4; Section C, items 5-6)
rules.quote: in new construction of buildings where elevators are required by 11B-206.2.3 Multi-Story Buildings and Facilities, and which exceed 10,000 square feet on any floor, an accessible means of vertical access via ramp, elevator or lift shall be provided within 200 feet of travel of each stair and each escalator.
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC plan check checklist, which restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS. Item 6 on the same page applies the rule to existing buildings when a new stair or escalator is built.

rules.title: Count required accessible parking separately for each parking lot or structure
rules.plain_english: The number of accessible spaces is figured separately for each parking facility on a site, not from the site's total. Patient and visitor parking for hospital outpatient facilities (including free-standing buildings giving a hospital's outpatient clinical services) needs 10% accessible; patient and visitor parking for rehabilitation facilities specializing in conditions that affect mobility, and for outpatient physical therapy facilities, needs 20%.

parameters.general_table: CBC Table 11B-208.2 (see ada-cbc-11b-208-2-table; same rows as the federal table)
parameters.hospital_outpatient_scope: patient and visitor parking serving hospital outpatient facilities and free-standing buildings providing outpatient clinical services of a hospital
parameters.rehab_scope: patient and visitor parking serving rehabilitation facilities specializing in treating conditions that affect mobility, and outpatient physical therapy facilities

rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-026-Acc_Commercial.pdf (LADBS Commercial Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-026, effective 01/01/2026, revised 09/23/2026; PDF page 8; Section D, items 1-4)
rules.quote: The number of parking spaces required to be accessible is to be calculated separately for each parking facility; the required number is not based on the total number of parking spaces provided in all of the parking facilities provided on site.
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC plan check checklist, which restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS. Same page: 'Ten percent of patient and visitor parking spaces provided to serve hospital outpatient facilities' and 'Twenty percent ... rehabilitation facilities ... and outpatient physical therapy facilities'; item 1: EVCS are not parking spaces (see 11B-228.3).
rules.correction: Fractions and per-facility counting confirmed. Scope corrected: the 20% rate is only for rehabilitation facilities 'specializing in treating conditions that affect mobility' and outpatient physical therapy facilities (CL-BC-2026-026 item D.4), and the 10% rate covers 'free-standing buildings providing outpatient clinical services of a hospital' (item D.3); both apply to patient and visitor spaces only. plain_english rewritten and parameters hospital_outpatient_scope and rehab_scope added. general_table updated to point to the CBC table read from LADBS P/BC 2026-084.

rules.title: One in every six accessible spaces (minimum one) must be van accessible
rules.plain_english: Of the required accessible parking spaces, one in every six (or fraction of six), and at least one, must be van accessible and signed 'van accessible'. The LADBS checklist says van spaces are served by a 96-inch aisle on the passenger side; the CBC text LADBS prints in P/BC 2026-084 allows a 12-ft van space with a 5-ft aisle or a 9-ft van space with an 8-ft (96-inch) aisle. The 9 ft + 8 ft layout meets both.

parameters.van_ratio: 1 per 6 required accessible spaces or fraction
parameters.aisle_side: opposite the driver's side when entering forward
parameters.aisle_width_conflict: CL-BC-2026-026 item D.6 states a 96-inch aisle for van spaces; LADBS P/BC 2026-084 (eff. 01-01-2026) prints 11B-208.2.4 without an aisle width and 11B-502.2 / 11B-502.3.1 allowing a 144-inch van space with a 60-inch aisle, or a 108-inch van space with a 96-inch aisle

rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-026-Acc_Commercial.pdf (LADBS Commercial Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-026, effective 01/01/2026, revised 09/23/2026; PDF page 8; Section D, item 6)
rules.quote: One in every six or fraction of six parking spaces required by Section 11B-208.2 Minimum Number, but not less than one, shall be served by an access aisle 96 inches wide minimum placed on the side opposite the driver’s side when the vehicle is going forward into the parking space and shall be designated “van accessible”.
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC plan check checklist, which restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS. For CBC 11A covered multifamily parking the ratio is one in every eight (see ada-cbc-11a-1109a-8-6-van-1-in-8). [Review 2026-11-25: LADBS Information Bulletin P/BC 2026-084 'Accessibility Details for Parking' (eff. 01-01-2026, rev. 11-23-2025), PDF p.2, restates 11B-208.2.4 as 'For every six or fraction of six parking spaces required by Section 11B-208.2 to comply with Section 11B-502, at least one shall be a van parking space complying with Section 11B-502.' (no aisle width), and PDF pp.3-4 restate 11B-502.2 (van 144 in, or 108 in with a 96 in aisle) and 11B-502.3.1 (aisles 60 in minimum). The checklist item's 96-inch wording conflicts with that text.]
rules.correction: Ratio (one in six or fraction, minimum one), designation and passenger-side aisle confirmed. The 96-inch aisle is stated by the checklist only: the CBC text restated in LADBS P/BC 2026-084 allows a 12-ft van space with a 60-inch aisle. plain_english rewritten to state both, and parameter aisle_width_conflict added.

rules.title: Accessible stalls: 18 ft long; car 9 ft wide; van 12 ft (5 ft aisle) or 9 ft (8 ft aisle); aisles 5 ft
rules.plain_english: Accessible car spaces are at least 9 feet wide and 18 feet long. Van spaces are 12 feet wide with a 5-foot aisle, or 9 feet wide with an 8-foot aisle. Access aisles are at least 5 feet wide and two spaces may share one aisle.
rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-026-Acc_Commercial.pdf (LADBS Commercial Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-026, effective 01/01/2026, revised 09/23/2026; PDF page 8; Section D, items 10-13)
rules.quote: Dimension minimum 12-foot wide accessible van parking space with minimum 5-foot wide access aisle. Van parking spaces shall be permitted to be minimum 9 feet wide where access aisle is 8-foot wide minimum.
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC plan check checklist, which restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS. Same page items 10, 11 and 13: 'Dimension minimum 18-foot long car and van accessible parking space(s)'; 'Dimension minimum 9-foot width at accessible car parking space'; 'Car and van stall access aisle shall be 5 foot wide minimum'. California is stricter than the federal 96-inch car space (2010 ADA Standards 502.2).

rules.title: Access aisle marking: blue border, hatching 36 in. on center, 'NO PARKING' in 12 in. letters
rules.plain_english: Paint a blue border around each access aisle, hatch inside it with lines no more than 36 inches on center, and paint 'NO PARKING' in white letters at least 12 inches high visible from the drive aisle.
rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-026-Acc_Commercial.pdf (LADBS Commercial Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-026, effective 01/01/2026, revised 09/23/2026; PDF page 9; Section D, item 14)
rules.quote: Access aisles shall be marked with a blue painted borderline around their perimeter. The area within the blue borderlines shall be marked with hatched lines a maximum of 36 inches on center in a color contrasting with that of the aisle surface, preferably blue or white. The words "NO PARKING" shall be painted on the surface within each access aisle in white letters a minimum of 12 inches in height and located to be visible from the adjacent vehicular way.
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC plan check checklist, which restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS.

rules.title: Accessible parking signs: ISA, 'van accessible', 60 in. to bottom, 70 sq in reflective, 'Minimum Fine $250'
rules.plain_english: Each accessible stall needs a reflective sign of at least 70 square inches with the International Symbol of Accessibility, mounted with its bottom at least 60 inches above grade. Van stalls add 'van accessible'. A sign or added language below the symbol must say 'Minimum Fine $250'.

parameters.required_text: Minimum Fine $250

rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-026-Acc_Commercial.pdf (LADBS Commercial Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-026, effective 01/01/2026, revised 09/23/2026; PDF page 9; Section D, items 17-20)
rules.quote: Additional language or an additional sign below the International Symbol of Accessibility shall state “Minimum Fine $250.”
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC plan check checklist, which restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS. Same pages: van signs 'shall be 60 inches minimum above the finish floor or ground surface measured to the bottom of the sign' (11B-502.6) and signs 'shall be reflectorized with a minimum area of 70 square inches' (11B-502.6.1).

rules.title: Tow-away sign at lot entrances or next to accessible stalls: 17x22 in., 1 in. letters
rules.plain_english: Post a tow-away warning sign at each entrance to an off-street lot or next to the accessible stalls. It must be at least 17 by 22 inches, with 1-inch letters, using the required wording and the tow company's address and phone number.

parameters.location: each entrance to off-street parking facility, or immediately adjacent to on-site accessible parking and visible from each space
fill_in: where towed vehicles may be reclaimed

rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-026-Acc_Commercial.pdf (LADBS Commercial Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-026, effective 01/01/2026, revised 09/23/2026; PDF page 9; Section D, item 23)
rules.quote: "Unauthorized vehicles parked in designated accessible spaces not displaying distinguishing placards or special license plates issued for persons with disabilities will be towed away at the owner’s expense. Towed vehicles may be reclaimed at:
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC plan check checklist, which restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS. Same item: 'The additional sign shall not be less than 17 inches wide by 22 inches high' and 'Blank spaces shall be filled in with appropriate information as a permanent part of the sign.'

rules.title: Accessible parking vertical clearance: 8 ft 2 in. at stalls and along one vehicle route
rules.plain_english: Garages and covered parking must give at least 8 feet 2 inches of headroom at accessible spaces and along at least one vehicle route to them from the site entrances and exits.

parameters.where: accessible parking spaces and at least one vehicle access route to them from site entrances and exits

rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-026-Acc_Commercial.pdf (LADBS Commercial Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-026, effective 01/01/2026, revised 09/23/2026; PDF page 9; Section D, item 16)
rules.quote: Clearly show minimum vertical clearance of 8 feet 2 inches at accessible parking spaces and along at least one vehicle access route to such spaces from site entrances and exits.
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC plan check checklist, which restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS. The CBC 11A covered multifamily rule is the same height (1109A.8.1).

rules.title: Paint a 36x36 in. International Symbol of Accessibility in each accessible stall
rules.plain_english: Each accessible car and van stall needs the International Symbol of Accessibility painted on the surface, at least 36 by 36 inches, centered within 6 inches of the stall centerline at the end of the space.

schemes: stall outlined or painted blue with white or contrasting symbol

rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-026-Acc_Commercial.pdf (LADBS Commercial Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-026, effective 01/01/2026, revised 09/23/2026; PDF page 9; Section D, item 22)
rules.quote: in white on a blue background a minimum 36 inches wide by 36 inches high. The centerline of the International Symbol of Accessibility shall be a maximum of 6 inches from the centerline of the parking space
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC plan check checklist, which restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS.

rules.title: Unisex (single-user) toilet room limits: 1 lavatory, max 2 water closets or 1 WC + 1 urinal, privacy latch
rules.plain_english: A unisex toilet room may have only one lavatory and either up to two water closets (no urinal) or one water closet and one urinal. Unisex bathing rooms have one shower (or shower and tub), one lavatory and one water closet. Doors need privacy latches.

bathing_room_fixtures: one shower or one shower and one bathtub

rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-026-Acc_Commercial.pdf (LADBS Commercial Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-026, effective 01/01/2026, revised 09/23/2026; PDF page 11; Section E, item 18)
rules.quote: Unisex toilet rooms shall contain not more than one lavatory, and not more than two water closets without urinals or one water closet and one urinal. Unisex bathing rooms shall contain one shower or one shower and one bathtub, one lavatory, and one water closet. Doors to unisex toilet rooms and unisex bathing rooms shall have privacy latches.
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC plan check checklist, which restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS.

rules.title: Drinking fountains: provide at least two (one wheelchair-height, one standing-height)
rules.plain_english: Where drinking fountains are provided, there must be at least two: one meeting the wheelchair (forward approach) requirements and one for standing persons.

parameters.over_minimum: 50 percent of the total (item 2; text continues on the sheet)

rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-026-Acc_Commercial.pdf (LADBS Commercial Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-026, effective 01/01/2026, revised 09/23/2026; PDF page 10; Section E, item 1)
rules.quote: No fewer than two drinking fountains shall be provided. When provided, one drinking fountain shall comply with 11B-602.1 through 11B-602.6, 11B-602.8 and 11B-602.9 and one drinking fountain shall comply with 11B-602.7 and 11B-602.9.
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC plan check checklist, which restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS. Drinking fountains serving the altered area are also a path-of-travel element under 11B-202.4.

rules.title: Sales and service counters: a 36 in. long section no higher than 34 in.
rules.plain_english: Every type of sales or service counter needs an accessible section at least 36 inches long and no more than 34 inches high, with a parallel-approach clear floor space (or knee and toe space for a forward approach).
rules.applies_to: Retail (Group M) and business (Group B) occupancies with sales or service counters in California
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-032-Acc_Grp_B_M_Occupancies.pdf (LADBS Group B and Group M Occupancies accessibility checklist (LABC 2026), CL-BC-2026-032; PDF page 5; Section D, item 7)
rules.quote: a. A portion of the counter surface that is 36 inches long minimum and 34 inches high maximum above the finish floor shall be provided. A clear floor or ground space complying with 11B-305 shall be positioned for a parallel approach adjacent to the 36-inch minimum length of counter.
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC plan check checklist, which restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS. Same checklist item D.6.b: check-out aisle 'counter surface height shall be 38 inches maximum'.

rules.title: Employee workstations: only limited 11B sections apply inside the workstation
rules.plain_english: Inside employee workstations only these CBC sections apply: 11B-207.1, 11B-215.3, 11B-302 (floor surfaces), 11B-303 (changes in level), 11B-308.1.1 and 11B-308.1.2 (parts of the reach-range rules) and 11B-404.2.3 (door clear width). LADBS still asks for an accessible route to the workstation, and common-use circulation paths within workstations must comply with 11B-206.2.8.
rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-026-Acc_Commercial.pdf (LADBS Commercial Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-026, effective 01/01/2026, revised 09/23/2026; PDF page 6; Section C, item 17)
rules.quote: Spaces and elements within employee workstations shall only be required to comply with Sections 11B-207.1, 11B-215.3, 11B-302, 11B-303, 11B-308.1.1, 11B-308.1.2 and 11B-404.2.3.
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC plan check checklist, which restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS.
rules.correction: Quote, parameters and citation confirmed. plain_english corrected: it described the listed sections as 'approach, enter and exit; floor surfaces; changes in level; certain reach ranges; door width', but 'approach, enter and exit' is not one of the listed CBC sections (it is the federal 203.9 wording) and the list omitted 11B-207.1 and 11B-215.3. Rewritten to list the sections exactly as LADBS states them.

rules.title: Detectable warnings: 36 in. deep at curb ramps, yellow, 6-8 in. from curb face
rules.plain_english: Curb ramps need yellow truncated-dome detectable warnings 36 inches deep across the full ramp width. On perpendicular curb ramps the edge nearest the curb is 6 to 8 inches from the curb face line. Walks that cross vehicle routes need a continuous 36-inch-wide warning strip.
rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-026-Acc_Commercial.pdf (LADBS Commercial Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-026, effective 01/01/2026, revised 09/23/2026; PDF page 4; Section C, item 10)
rules.quote: Curb ramps shall have detectable warnings that extend 36 inches in the direction of travel for the full width of the ramp run less than 2 inches maximum on each side, excluding any flared sides.
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC plan check checklist, which restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS. Same item g: 'Detectable warning surfaces shall be yellow and approximate 33538 of SAE AMS-STD-595A.'

rules.title: Curb ramps: max 1:12, 48x48 in. turning space at bottom, blended transitions max 1:20
rules.plain_english: Curb ramp runs can be no steeper than 1:12 (flares no steeper than 1:10). Provide a 48 by 48 inch turning space at the bottom sloped no more than 1:48. Blended transitions can be no steeper than 1:20.
rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-026-Acc_Commercial.pdf (LADBS Commercial Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-026, effective 01/01/2026, revised 09/23/2026; PDF page 5; Section C, item 11)
rules.quote: A turning space 48 inches minimum by 48 inches minimum shall be provided at the bottom of the curb ramp. The slope of the turning space in all directions shall be 1:48 maximum (2.083%).
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC plan check checklist, which restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS. Same item: 'Perpendicular ramp runs shall have a running slope not steeper than 1:12 (8.33%).' and 'Blended transition ramps shall have a running slope not steeper than 1:20 (5%).'

rules.title: Public housing: at least 5% mobility units and 2% communication units (minimum one each)
rules.plain_english: New public housing must make at least 5% of dwelling units (at least one) fully accessible mobility units and at least 2% (at least one) communication-feature units. Buildings with three or more units also need adaptable units.

parameters.formula: mobility_units = max(1, ceil(0.05 * total_units)); communication_units = max(1, ceil(0.02 * total_units))

rules.applies_to: New construction of public housing (housing built or altered by, for, or on behalf of a public entity) in California
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-036-Acc_Public_Housing.pdf (LADBS Public Housing Accessibility checklist (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-036, effective 01/01/2026; PDF page 2; Section B, item 2.a)
rules.quote: Mobility Units. In facilities with residential dwelling units, at least 5 percent, but no fewer than one unit, of the total number of residential dwelling units shall provide mobility features complying with 11B-809.2 through 11B-809.4 and shall be on an accessible route as required by 11B-206.
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC Public Housing checklist, which restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS. Same page: 'at least 2 percent, but no fewer than one unit ... shall provide communication features complying with 11B-809.5'. The ceil() rounding is inferred from 'at least'.

rules.title: What counts as 'public housing' under CBC 11B
rules.plain_english: 'Public housing' means housing built or altered by, for or on behalf of a public entity, or under a public entity's housing program, including 1-2 family homes, buildings with three or more units, shelters and group homes, short-stay lodging and school housing.

includes: one- or two-family dwelling units or congregate residences
buildings or complexes with three or more residential dwelling units
homeless shelters, group homes, halfway houses and similar social service establishments
transient lodging of not more than 30 days
housing at a place of education

rules.applies_to: Housing projects for or funded by public entities in California
rules.citation: CBC Chapter 2, Section 202 'Public Housing' (as quoted by LADBS)
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-036-Acc_Public_Housing.pdf (LADBS Public Housing Accessibility checklist (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-036, effective 01/01/2026; PDF page 1; Section B, item 1)
rules.quote: Public Housing. Housing facilities constructed or altered by, for, or on behalf of a public entity, or constructed or altered as part of a public entity’s program to provide housing pursuant to United States Code of Federal Regulations, 28 CFR Part 35, Section 35.102(a), including but not limited to the following:
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC Public Housing checklist, which restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS.

rules.title: CBC 11A applies to new covered multifamily dwellings, new common areas, qualifying additions and gut rehabs
rules.plain_english: Chapter 11A housing accessibility applies to all newly built covered multifamily dwellings, new common-use areas serving new or existing covered dwellings, additions that by themselves meet the covered-dwelling definition, and buildings gutted down to the exterior shell, which count as new buildings.

applies_to: new common use areas serving existing covered multifamily dwellings
additions where the addition alone meets the definition of a covered multifamily dwelling

rules.title: 11A parking: 2% of covered units (1 per facility type minimum); 5% of unassigned spaces

Stall and aisle slopes may not exceed 1/4 inch per foot (2.083%), and garages need 8 feet 2 inches of headroom to accessible spaces.

rules.correction: The 1-in-8 ratio, minimum one, 17 ft width, 12+5 / 9+8 options, passenger-side aisle and 18 ft length are confirmed. Corrected parameters: van_ratio 'one in every eight accessible spaces (fraction rule not stated)'; formula_literal_minimum 'max(1, floor(accessible_spaces / 8))'; formula_conservative 'max(1, ceil(accessible_spaces / 8))'; fraction_rounding_stated false. plain_english updated on 2026-11-27 to say the text does not state how a partial group of eight is counted and that rounding up is the conservative reading.

rules.title: 11A site: an accessible route from transit stops, accessible parking, loading zones and the street to the entrance
rules.plain_english: Provide at least one accessible route on the site from public transit stops, accessible parking and passenger loading zones, and public streets or sidewalks to the accessible building entrance. If there are several routes, all must be accessible.

parameters.not_for: multi-story dwelling units in nonelevator buildings (except as provided in 1102A.3.1)

rules.title: City plan check does not certify ADA or Fair Housing Act compliance
rules.plain_english: California building departments check Title 24 (CBC 11A/11B) only. They are not delegated authority to review or inspect for the federal ADA or Fair Housing Act, so the owner and design team remain responsible wherever federal rules are stricter, even after permits and final inspection.
rules.applies_to: Owners, designers and contractors on California projects subject to the ADA or Fair Housing Act
rules.citation: LADBS CL-BC-2026-026 Section II.1; CL-BC-2026-027 Section II.1
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-026-Acc_Commercial.pdf (LADBS Commercial Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-026, effective 01/01/2026, revised 09/23/2026; PDF page 1; Section II, item 1)
rules.quote: Please be aware that the owner(s) of this building and his/her consultants are responsible for compliance with the most current Federal Regulations contained in the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) and Fair Housing Act (FHA). Where the ADA & FHA requirements exceed those contained in Title 24, Part 2, it is the owner’s responsibility and consultants to ensure compliance with the most current ADA & FHA regulations, as the County/City is not delegated the authority to plan review or inspect projects for ADA & FHA compliance.
rules.notes: Federal counterpart: a state or local compliance determination 'is not conclusive in enforcement proceedings' under the Fair Housing Amendments Act (24 CFR 100.205(h); see ada-fha-local-approval-not-conclusive).

rules.title: Certified Access Specialist (CASp): a DSA-certified inspector who issues reports and inspection certificates
rules.plain_english: A CASp is a person certified by the Division of the State Architect. A CASp can review plans, inspect a facility for state and federal accessibility compliance, write accessibility reports, and issue CASp Inspection Reports and Disability Access Inspection Certificates under Civil Code 55.53. Some building departments use CASp-certified inspectors.

issue CASp Inspection Reports and Disability Access Inspection Certificates (Civil Code 55.53)

rules.title: Required CASp statement in commercial leases
rules.plain_english: Commercial leases must include a standard statement: a CASp can inspect the premises; state law does not require it, but the landlord cannot prohibit the tenant from getting one; and the parties must agree on timing, who pays for the inspection and who pays for repairs.

parameters.statement_text: A Certified Access Specialist (CASp) can inspect the subject premises and determine whether the subject premises comply with all of the applicable construction-related accessibility standards under state law. Although state law does not require a CASp inspection of the subject premises, the commercial property owner or lessor may not prohibit the lessee or tenant from obtaining a CASp inspection of the subject premises for the occupancy or potential occupancy of the lessee or tenant, if requested by the lessee or tenant. The parties shall mutually agree on the arrangements for the time and manner of the CASp inspection, the payment of the fee for the CASp inspection, and the cost of making any repairs necessary to correct violations of construction-related accessibility standards within the premises.
parties_must_agree_on: cost of repairs within the premises

rules.notes: Stated by the City of San Diego Treasurer: 'From January 1, 2013, through December 31, 2017, cities and counties were required to collect a state-mandated fee of $1.00 ... Assembly Bill 1379 ... increased the fee from $1.00 to $4.00 effective January 1, 2018'. The split between the city/county and the state Disability Access and Education Revolving Fund was not read (non-official search excerpts conflict), so it is not given.
rules.correction: $4.00 fee, 2013/2018 history, AB 2164 repeal and 'indefinitely' confirmed. The San Diego example (total $38) was incomplete: the $34 business tax applies only to businesses with 12 or fewer employees, and since July 1, 2025 mail applications also owe a per-employee Minimum Wage Enforcement Fee, which the two City pages state differently ($1.47 on btaxhow, $2.82 on btaxfees). Corrected example_san_diego_mail_application_usd to add business_tax_applies_to, plus_per_employee_minimum_wage_enforcement_fee_usd and the conflict.

rules.title: Business license applicants must receive disability access information (AB 3002)
rules.plain_english: Since January 1, 2019, business owners must receive information on disability access requirements and available resources. The City of San Diego gives this notice to business tax applicants and points them to DSA, the Department of Rehabilitation and the California Commission on Disability Access.

parameters.content: information regarding disability access requirements and available resources

rules.applies_to: California cities and counties issuing business licenses; business owners receiving them
rules.citation: AB 3002 (Stats. 2018), as described by the City of San Diego
rules.source: https://www.sandiego.gov/treasurer/taxesfees/btax/btaxfees (City of San Diego Office of the City Treasurer, Business Tax Rates and Fees page (fetched 2026-11-25); section 'Senate Bill 1186 - State Mandated Fee' and 'Notice to Business Owners')
rules.quote: Additionally, Assembly Bill 3002 , effective January 1, 2019, requires that business owners receive information regarding disability access requirements and available resources.
rules.notes: The codified section and the DSA model notice (dgs.ca.gov) were not read, so the statute's exact delivery trigger and which agency must deliver it are not stated here.

rules.title: ADA: altered portions of a facility must be accessible to the maximum extent feasible
rules.plain_english: Under the federal ADA, any alteration of a public accommodation or commercial facility after January 26, 1992 must make the altered portions readily accessible to people with disabilities, including wheelchair users, to the maximum extent feasible.

parameters.standard: maximum extent feasible

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California
rules.quote: Any alteration to a place of public accommodation or a commercial facility, after January 26, 1992, shall be made so as to ensure that, to the maximum extent feasible, the altered portions of the facility are readily accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities, including individuals who use wheelchairs.

rules.title: ADA: what counts as an alteration (maintenance, reroofing, painting, asbestos and MEP work usually do not)
rules.plain_english: Remodeling, renovation, reconstruction, structural changes and moving walls or full-height partitions are alterations. Normal maintenance, reroofing, painting or wallpapering, asbestos removal, and mechanical or electrical changes are not, unless they affect the usability of the building.

alterations_include: changes or rearrangement in structural parts or elements
changes or rearrangement in the plan configuration of walls and full-height partitions
not_alterations_unless_usability_affecte: changes to mechanical and electrical systems

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California
rules.quote: Normal maintenance, reroofing, painting or wallpapering, asbestos removal, or changes to mechanical and electrical systems are not alterations unless they affect the usability of the building or facility.

rules.title: ADA: altering a primary function area triggers an accessible path of travel, restrooms, phones and fountains
rules.plain_english: When an alteration affects an area containing a primary function, the path of travel to it and the restrooms, telephones and drinking fountains serving it must also be made accessible, unless the cost is disproportionate (over 20% of the alteration cost).

parameters.trigger: alteration that affects or could affect usability of or access to an area containing a primary function
must_make_accessible: path of travel to the altered area
drinking fountains serving the altered area

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California
rules.quote: An alteration that affects or could affect the usability of or access to an area of a facility that contains a primary function shall be made so as to ensure that, to the maximum extent feasible, the path of travel to the altered area and the restrooms, telephones, and drinking fountains serving the altered area, are readily accessible to and usable by individuals with disabilities, including individuals who use wheelchairs, unless the cost and scope of such alterations is disproportionate to the cost of the overall alteration.

rules.title: ADA: 'primary function' areas vs. areas that are not (mechanical rooms, corridors, restrooms, etc.)
rules.plain_english: A primary function is a major activity the facility is for, such as a bank lobby, a cafeteria dining area, meeting rooms, offices and work areas. Mechanical rooms, boiler rooms, storage, employee lounges and locker rooms, janitor closets, entrances, corridors and restrooms are not primary function areas.

examples_primary: customer services lobby of a bank
meeting rooms in a conference center

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California
rules.quote: Mechanical rooms, boiler rooms, supply storage rooms, employee lounges or locker rooms, janitorial closets, entrances, corridors, and restrooms are not areas containing a primary function.

rules.title: ADA: window, hardware, controls, outlet and signage alterations do not trigger path of travel
rules.plain_english: Altering only windows, hardware, controls, electrical outlets or signage is not treated as an alteration affecting a primary function area, so it does not trigger the path-of-travel obligation.
rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California
rules.quote: For the purposes of this section, alterations to windows, hardware, controls, electrical outlets, and signage shall not be deemed to be alterations that affect the usability of or access to an area containing a primary function.

rules.title: ADA: a tenant's alterations in its own space do not create a path-of-travel duty for the landlord
rules.plain_english: If a tenant alters areas only it occupies, that does not make the landlord responsible for path-of-travel work in areas the landlord controls, as long as the landlord is not otherwise altering those areas.

parameters.unless: landlord-controlled areas are otherwise being altered

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California
rules.quote: If a tenant is making alterations as defined in § 36.402 that would trigger the requirements of this section, those alterations by the tenant in areas that only the tenant occupies do not trigger a path of travel obligation upon the landlord with respect to areas of the facility under the landlord's authority, if those areas are not otherwise being altered.
rules.notes: The tenant's own path-of-travel obligation within its control is not removed by this provision.

rules.title: ADA: what the 'path of travel' includes
rules.plain_english: The path of travel is the continuous, unobstructed pedestrian route to approach, enter and exit the altered area, connecting it to sidewalks, streets and parking, the facility entrance and other parts of the facility. It also includes the restrooms, telephones and drinking fountains serving the area.

may_consist_of: curb ramps and other pedestrian ramps
clear floor paths through lobbies, corridors, rooms
also_includes: drinking fountains serving the altered area

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California
rules.quote: A “path of travel” includes a continuous, unobstructed way of pedestrian passage by means of which the altered area may be approached, entered, and exited, and which connects the altered area with an exterior approach (including sidewalks, streets, and parking areas), an entrance to the facility, and other parts of the facility.

rules.title: ADA: path-of-travel cost over 20% of the primary-function alteration is disproportionate
rules.plain_english: Federally, path-of-travel work is 'disproportionate' when it costs more than 20% of the cost of the alteration to the primary function area. Up to 20% must be spent. Unlike California, there is no dollar valuation threshold.

parameters.base: cost of the alteration to the primary function area

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California
rules.quote: Alterations made to provide an accessible path of travel to the altered area will be deemed disproportionate to the overall alteration when the cost exceeds 20% of the cost of the alteration to the primary function area.
rules.notes: California's CBC 11B-202.4 Exception 8 applies the 20% cap only at or below the DSA valuation threshold ($209,208 in 2026); a California project must satisfy both rules.

rules.title: ADA: costs that count toward the 20% (entrance/route, restrooms, phones, fountains)
rules.plain_english: Costs that may count toward the 20% path-of-travel spend include an accessible entrance and route (widening doors, ramps), restroom work (grab bars, larger stalls, pipe insulation, accessible faucets), accessible telephones (lowering, amplification, TTY), and relocating an inaccessible drinking fountain.

countable_costs: accessible entrance and accessible route (e.g., widening doorways, installing ramps)
restrooms (grab bars, enlarging toilet stalls, insulating pipes, accessible faucet controls)
telephones (relocating to accessible height, amplification devices, TTY)

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California
rules.quote: Costs associated with providing an accessible entrance and an accessible route to the altered area, for example, the cost of widening doorways or installing ramps;

rules.title: ADA: when costs are disproportionate, provide as much access as possible in priority order
rules.plain_english: If full path-of-travel access would be disproportionate, you must still provide what you can within the limit, in this order: entrance, route to the altered area, at least one accessible restroom for each sex or a single unisex restroom, telephones, drinking fountains, then parking, storage and alarms.

priority_order: accessible route to the altered area
at least one accessible restroom for each sex or a single unisex restroom
when possible, additional elements such as parking, storage, and alarms

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California
rules.quote: When the cost of alterations necessary to make the path of travel to the altered area fully accessible is disproportionate to the cost of the overall alteration, the path of travel shall be made accessible to the extent that it can be made accessible without incurring disproportionate costs.

rules.title: ADA: no splitting jobs; 3-year aggregation of alterations without path-of-travel work
rules.plain_english: You cannot dodge the path-of-travel duty with a series of small jobs. If an area was altered without an accessible path of travel and more work on that area or the same path happens within three years, the total cost over the preceding three years is used for the 20% test (only alterations after January 26, 1992 count).

parameters.aggregate: total cost of alterations to primary function areas on that path of travel during the preceding three years

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California
rules.quote: If an area containing a primary function has been altered without providing an accessible path of travel to that area, and subsequent alterations of that area, or a different area on the same path of travel, are undertaken within three years of the original alteration, the total cost of alterations to the primary function areas on that path of travel during the preceding three year period shall be considered in determining whether the cost of making that path of travel accessible is disproportionate.

rules.title: ADA: path-of-travel elements built to the 1991 Standards need not be retrofitted to 2010 changes
rules.plain_english: If path-of-travel elements were built or altered to the 1991 ADA Standards, a later primary-function alteration does not require retrofitting them just to meet the incremental changes in the 2010 Standards.

parameters.applies_to: required elements of a path of travel already compliant with 1991 Standards

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California
rules.quote: If a private entity has constructed or altered required elements of a path of travel at a place of public accommodation or commercial facility in accordance with the specifications in the 1991 Standards, the private entity is not required to retrofit such elements to reflect the incremental changes in the 2010 Standards solely because of an alteration to a primary function area served by that path of travel.
rules.notes: California CBC rules apply separately and may still require upgrades.

rules.title: ADA Title II (public agencies): same 20% path-of-travel disproportionality test
rules.plain_english: For buildings of state and local governments, the path-of-travel rule is the same: path-of-travel cost over 20% of the primary-function alteration cost is disproportionate. Restrooms are not primary function areas unless restrooms are the main purpose (such as highway rest stops).

parameters.base: cost of the alteration to the primary function area
parameters.restrooms_primary_function_only_if: provision of restrooms is a primary purpose of the area (e.g., highway rest stops)

rules.applies_to: Facilities built or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of state and local government entities (ADA Title II)
rules.quote: Alterations made to provide an accessible path of travel to the altered area will be deemed disproportionate to the overall alteration when the cost exceeds 20% of the cost of the alteration to the primary function area.
rules.notes: Relevant to contractors on public works alterations (cities, counties, school districts, state agencies).

rules.title: ADA Title II: 3-year aggregation counts only alterations on or after March 15, 2011
rules.plain_english: For public agency facilities, the three-year aggregation of small alterations counts only alterations made on or after March 15, 2011.
rules.applies_to: Facilities built or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of state and local government entities (ADA Title II)
rules.quote: Only alterations undertaken on or after March 15, 2011 shall be considered in determining if the cost of providing an accessible path of travel is disproportionate to the overall cost of the alterations.

rules.title: ADA Title II: path-of-travel elements built to 1991 Standards or UFAS before 3/15/2012 need not be retrofitted
rules.plain_english: A public agency that built or altered path-of-travel elements to the 1991 Standards or UFAS before March 15, 2012 does not have to retrofit them to the 2010 Standards just because a primary function area served by that path is altered.
rules.applies_to: Facilities built or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of state and local government entities (ADA Title II)
rules.quote: If a public entity has constructed or altered required elements of a path of travel in accordance with the specifications in either the 1991 Standards or the Uniform Federal Accessibility Standards before March 15, 2012, the public entity is not required to retrofit such elements to reflect incremental changes in the 2010 Standards solely because of an alteration to a primary function area served by that path of travel.

rules.title: ADA Title II: alterations done only for program access do not trigger path of travel
rules.plain_english: When a public agency alters a facility solely to meet its program accessibility duty, the path-of-travel rule does not apply to that work.

parameters.pot_applies_only_to: alterations undertaken solely for purposes other than program accessibility (28 CFR 35.150)

rules.applies_to: Facilities built or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of state and local government entities (ADA Title II)
rules.quote: The path of travel requirements of § 35.151(b)(4) shall apply only to alterations undertaken solely for purposes other than to meet the program accessibility requirements of § 35.150.

rules.title: ADA Title III: 2010 Standards apply to permits certified complete (or work started) on or after March 15, 2012
rules.plain_english: New construction and alterations must follow the 2010 ADA Standards if the last building permit application was certified complete (or received) on or after March 15, 2012, or, with no permit, if physical work started on or after that date.

parameters.date_test: last permit application certified complete (or received); if no permit, start of physical construction
parameters.start_excludes: ceremonial groundbreaking or razing of structures prior to site preparation
