rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California
rules.quote: New construction and alterations subject to §§ 36.401 or 36.402 shall comply with the 2010 Standards if the date when the last application for a building permit or permit extension is certified to be complete by a State, county, or local government (or, in those jurisdictions where the government does not certify completion of applications, if the date when the last application for a building permit or permit extension is received by the State, county, or local government) is on or after March 15, 2012, or if no permit is required, if the start of physical construction or alterations occurs on or after March 15, 2012.

rules.title: ADA Title II: public projects starting physical construction on or after March 15, 2012 use the 2010 Standards
rules.plain_english: For state and local government facilities, construction or alterations that physically start on or after March 15, 2012 must comply with the 2010 ADA Standards.

parameters.date_test: commencement of physical construction or alterations
parameters.start_excludes: ceremonial groundbreaking or razing of structures prior to site preparation

rules.applies_to: Facilities built or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of state and local government entities (ADA Title II)
rules.quote: If physical construction or alterations commence on or after March 15, 2012, then new construction and alterations subject to this section shall comply with the 2010 Standards.

rules.title: ADA: new facilities for first occupancy after January 26, 1993 must be fully accessible
rules.plain_english: New public accommodations and commercial facilities first occupied after January 26, 1993 must be designed and built readily accessible. That covers buildings whose last permit application was certified complete after January 26, 1992 and whose first certificate of occupancy was issued after January 26, 1993.
rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California
rules.quote: For purposes of this section, a facility is designed and constructed for first occupancy after January 26, 1993, only—

rules.title: ADA new construction: 'structurally impracticable' only in rare cases where terrain prevents access
rules.plain_english: Full compliance in new construction is excused only where it is structurally impracticable, which happens only in rare cases where unique terrain prevents accessibility features. Everything that can be made accessible still must be.

parameters.standard: unique characteristics of terrain prevent incorporation of accessibility features

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California
rules.quote: Full compliance with the requirements of this section is not required where an entity can demonstrate that it is structurally impracticable to meet the requirements. Full compliance will be considered structurally impracticable only in those rare circumstances when the unique characteristics of terrain prevent the incorporation of accessibility features.

rules.title: ADA elevator exemption: under 3 stories or under 3,000 sq ft per story (not for shopping centers, medical offices, transit)
rules.plain_english: Federally, an elevator is not required in an altered facility that is less than three stories or has less than 3,000 square feet per story, unless it houses a shopping center or mall (5+ sales or rental establishments), a health care provider's professional office, or a transit station or airport terminal. California CBC 11B has its own rules.

exemption_not_available_for: shopping center or mall (5 or more sales or rental establishments)
professional office of a health care provider
terminal, depot or station for specified public transportation

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California
rules.quote: This section does not require the installation of an elevator in an altered facility that is less than three stories or has less than 3,000 square feet per story, except with respect to any facility that houses a shopping center, a shopping mall, the professional office of a health care provider, a terminal, depot, or other station used for specified public transportation, or an airport passenger terminal.
rules.notes: Floors above or below an accessible ground floor must still meet all other requirements (36.404(b)). CBC 11B-206.2.3 has separate California exceptions (not read here).

rules.title: ADA: 'to the maximum extent feasible' means provide all the access the existing building allows
rules.plain_english: Where the nature of an existing building makes full compliance virtually impossible in a planned alteration, the work must still provide the maximum physical accessibility feasible. Any altered feature that can be made accessible must be, and if wheelchair access is not feasible, access must still be provided for people with other disabilities.

parameters.applies_when: nature of existing facility makes full compliance virtually impossible
parameters.requirement: maximum physical accessibility feasible; every altered feature that can be made accessible must be
parameters.fallback: access for persons with other disabilities (crutches, impaired vision or hearing, other impairments)

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California
rules.quote: The phrase “to the maximum extent feasible,” as used in this section, applies to the occasional case where the nature of an existing facility makes it virtually impossible to comply fully with applicable accessibility standards through a planned alteration. In these circumstances, the alteration shall provide the maximum physical accessibility feasible.

rules.title: ADA: pre-2012 work that never met the 1991 Standards must now be fixed to the 2010 Standards
rules.plain_english: New construction or alterations built before March 15, 2012 that did not comply with the 1991 Standards must, on or after March 15, 2012, be made accessible under the 2010 Standards. Correcting old non-compliant work means building to the 2010 Standards.

parameters.condition: does not comply with the 1991 Standards

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California
rules.quote: Newly constructed or altered facilities or elements covered by §§ 36.401 or 36.402 that were constructed or altered before March 15, 2012 and that do not comply with the 1991 Standards shall, on or after March 15, 2012, be made accessible in accordance with the 2010 Standards.
rules.notes: Title II counterpart: 28 CFR 35.151(c)(5)(ii) (1991 Standards or UFAS).

rules.title: ADA: existing public accommodations must remove barriers where readily achievable
rules.plain_english: Businesses open to the public must remove architectural barriers in existing facilities when it is readily achievable, meaning easy to do without much difficulty or expense, even with no remodel planned. Examples include ramps, curb cuts, widening doors, grab bars and accessible parking spaces.

parameters.standard: readily achievable (easily accomplishable and able to be carried out without much difficulty or expense)
priorities: access from public sidewalks, parking or public transportation
areas where goods and services are available

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation (ADA Title III) in existing facilities
rules.quote: A public accommodation shall remove architectural barriers in existing facilities, including communication barriers that are structural in nature, where such removal is readily achievable, i.e., easily accomplishable and able to be carried out without much difficulty or expense.

rules.title: ADA: barrier-removal work must meet alteration standards but does not trigger path of travel
rules.plain_english: Barrier-removal projects must meet the alteration standards for each element altered, but the path-of-travel requirement does not apply to work done only for barrier removal. Elements that comply with the 1991 Standards and have not been altered since March 15, 2012 need not be changed to the 2010 Standards.

parameters.safe_harbor: unaltered elements complying with 1991 Standards (not altered on or after 2012-03-15)

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation (ADA Title III) in existing facilities
rules.quote: The path of travel requirements of § 36.403 shall not apply to measures taken solely to comply with the barrier removal requirements of this section.

rules.title: ADA Title III civil penalty (DOJ suit): up to $118,225 first violation, $236,451 subsequent
rules.plain_english: In a Justice Department lawsuit, a court may assess a civil penalty against a public accommodation of up to $118,225 for a first violation and up to $236,451 for any later violation (amounts for penalties assessed after July 3, 2025).

parameters.multiple_acts_in_one_action: counted as a single violation (28 CFR 36.504(b))

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California
rules.quote: 42 U.S.C. 12188(b)(2)(C)(i) Americans With Disabilities Act; Public accommodations for individuals with disabilities, first violation 28 CFR 36.504(a)(3)(i) 115,231 118,225
rules.notes: Row of 28 CFR 85.5 table 1 (columns: U.S.C. citation, penalty name, CFR citation, amount assessed after 2/12/2024, amount assessed after July 3, 2025). The subsequent-violation row reads '... subsequent violation 28 CFR 36.504(a)(3)(ii) 230,464 236,451'. Courts consider good-faith efforts (36.504(d)). These penalties are assessed in civil actions by the Attorney General under 28 CFR 36.503.

rules.title: ADA Standards: scaffolding, hoists, material storage, construction trailers and crew toilets are exempt
rules.plain_english: Structures and sites directly tied to construction work, such as scaffolding, bridging, materials hoists, materials storage and construction trailers, do not have to be accessible or on an accessible route. Portable toilets used only by construction personnel do not have to be accessible.

exempt: portable toilet units provided exclusively for construction personnel

rules.applies_to: Contractors' temporary jobsite facilities (ADA 2010 Standards scoping)
rules.citation: 2010 ADA Standards 203.2 (36 CFR part 1191, App. B)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-36/part-1191 (eCFR 36 CFR part 1191, Appendix B (ADA Chapters 1-2) and Appendix D (Chapters 3-10) (version 2026-11-23); Appendix B, 203.2)
rules.quote: 203.2 Construction Sites. Structures and sites directly associated with the actual processes of construction, including but not limited to, scaffolding, bridging, materials hoists, materials storage, and construction trailers shall not be required to comply with these requirements or to be on an accessible route. Portable toilet units provided for use exclusively by construction personnel on a construction site shall not be required to comply with 213 or to be on an accessible route.
rules.notes: Text read from the eCFR edition of 36 CFR part 1191 current on 2026-11-23. Under 28 CFR 36.104 and 35.104 the 2010 ADA Standards consist of the 2004 ADAAG (36 CFR part 1191 Appendices B and D, 2009 edition) plus DOJ subpart D rules; if the Access Board has amended this provision since 2009, the DOJ-adopted 2009 text controls. The exemption is limited to structures and sites directly associated with the actual processes of construction; portable toilets are exempt only when exclusively for construction personnel.

rules.title: ADA Standards: altered elements must comply; exceptions for unaltered circulation and technical infeasibility
rules.plain_english: Each altered element or space must comply. An accessible route to it is not required if the circulation path is not altered (unless the primary-function rule applies). Where full compliance is technically infeasible, comply to the maximum extent feasible.

exceptions: circulation path not altered -> accessible route not required unless 202.4 applies
technically infeasible -> maximum extent feasible
residential dwelling units not required to be accessible are exempt

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California; Facilities built or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of state and local government entities (ADA Title II)
rules.citation: 2010 ADA Standards 202.3 (36 CFR part 1191, App. B)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-36/part-1191 (eCFR 36 CFR part 1191, Appendix B (ADA Chapters 1-2) and Appendix D (Chapters 3-10) (version 2026-11-23); Appendix B, 202.3)
rules.quote: 202.3 Alterations. Where existing elements or spaces are altered, each altered element or space shall comply with the applicable requirements of Chapter 2. Exceptions: 1. Unless required by 202.4, where elements or spaces are altered and the circulation path to the altered element or space is not altered, an accessible route shall not be required.
rules.notes: Text read from the eCFR edition of 36 CFR part 1191 current on 2026-11-23. Under 28 CFR 36.104 and 35.104 the 2010 ADA Standards consist of the 2004 ADAAG (36 CFR part 1191 Appendices B and D, 2009 edition) plus DOJ subpart D rules; if the Access Board has amended this provision since 2009, the DOJ-adopted 2009 text controls.

rules.title: ADA Standards: an alteration may never reduce accessibility below new-construction requirements
rules.plain_english: You cannot alter a building in a way that makes it less accessible than new-construction rules require at the time of the alteration, for example by removing a compliant ramp or narrowing an accessible door.

parameters.prohibited: alteration that decreases accessibility below new construction requirements at time of alteration
parameters.max_requirement: an alteration does not require more than new construction (202.3.2)

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California; Facilities built or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of state and local government entities (ADA Title II)
rules.citation: 2010 ADA Standards 202.3.1 (36 CFR part 1191, App. B)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-36/part-1191 (eCFR 36 CFR part 1191, Appendix B (ADA Chapters 1-2) and Appendix D (Chapters 3-10) (version 2026-11-23); Appendix B, 202.3.1-202.3.2)
rules.quote: 202.3.1 Prohibited Reduction in Access. An alteration that decreases or has the effect of decreasing the accessibility of a building or facility below the requirements for new construction at the time of the alteration is prohibited.
rules.notes: Text read from the eCFR edition of 36 CFR part 1191 current on 2026-11-23. Under 28 CFR 36.104 and 35.104 the 2010 ADA Standards consist of the 2004 ADAAG (36 CFR part 1191 Appendices B and D, 2009 edition) plus DOJ subpart D rules; if the Access Board has amended this provision since 2009, the DOJ-adopted 2009 text controls.

rules.title: ADA Standards: primary-function path-of-travel rule does not apply to residential dwelling units
rules.plain_english: The 2010 ADA Standards' primary-function path-of-travel rule (202.4) does not apply to residential dwelling units.
rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California; Facilities built or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of state and local government entities (ADA Title II)
rules.citation: 2010 ADA Standards 202.4 Exception (36 CFR part 1191, App. B)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-36/part-1191 (eCFR 36 CFR part 1191, Appendix B (ADA Chapters 1-2) and Appendix D (Chapters 3-10) (version 2026-11-23); Appendix B, 202.4)
rules.quote: Exception: Residential dwelling units shall not be required to comply with 202.4.
rules.notes: Text read from the eCFR edition of 36 CFR part 1191 current on 2026-11-23. Under 28 CFR 36.104 and 35.104 the 2010 ADA Standards consist of the 2004 ADAAG (36 CFR part 1191 Appendices B and D, 2009 edition) plus DOJ subpart D rules; if the Access Board has amended this provision since 2009, the DOJ-adopted 2009 text controls.

rules.title: ADA Standards Table 208.2: minimum accessible parking spaces by lot size
rules.plain_english: Federal minimum accessible spaces per parking facility: 1-25 spaces: 1; 26-50: 2; 51-75: 3; 76-100: 4; 101-150: 5; 151-200: 6; 201-300: 7; 301-400: 8; 401-500: 9; 501-1000: 2% of total; over 1000: 20 plus 1 per 100 over 1000. One in six must be van spaces. Count each parking facility separately.

table.required: 20 plus 1 for each 100, or fraction thereof, over 1000

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California; Facilities built or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of state and local government entities (ADA Title II)
rules.citation: 2010 ADA Standards 208.2, Table 208.2, 208.2.4 (36 CFR part 1191, App. B)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-36/part-1191 (eCFR 36 CFR part 1191, Appendix B (ADA Chapters 1-2) and Appendix D (Chapters 3-10) (version 2026-11-23); Appendix B, 208.2)
rules.quote: 208.2 Minimum Number. Parking spaces complying with 502 shall be provided in accordance with Table 208.2 except as required by 208.2.1, 208.2.2, and 208.2.3. Where more than one parking facility is provided on a site, the number of accessible spaces provided on the site shall be calculated according to the number of spaces required for each parking facility.
rules.notes: Text read from the eCFR edition of 36 CFR part 1191 current on 2026-11-23. Under 28 CFR 36.104 and 35.104 the 2010 ADA Standards consist of the 2004 ADAAG (36 CFR part 1191 Appendices B and D, 2009 edition) plus DOJ subpart D rules; if the Access Board has amended this provision since 2009, the DOJ-adopted 2009 text controls. The ceil() rounding for the 2% row is inferred, not stated in the table. CBC Table 11B-208.2, as restated by LADBS P/BC 2026-084 (eff. 01-01-2026), has the same rows (see ada-cbc-11b-208-2-table).

rules.title: ADA Standards: at least one van space for every six accessible spaces
rules.plain_english: For every six accessible parking spaces (or fraction of six), at least one must be a van space.
rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California; Facilities built or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of state and local government entities (ADA Title II)
rules.citation: 2010 ADA Standards 208.2.4 (36 CFR part 1191, App. B)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-36/part-1191 (eCFR 36 CFR part 1191, Appendix B (ADA Chapters 1-2) and Appendix D (Chapters 3-10) (version 2026-11-23); Appendix B, 208.2.4)
rules.quote: 208.2.4 Van Parking Spaces. For every six or fraction of six parking spaces required by 208.2 to comply with 502, at least one shall be a van parking space complying with 502.
rules.notes: Text read from the eCFR edition of 36 CFR part 1191 current on 2026-11-23. Under 28 CFR 36.104 and 35.104 the 2010 ADA Standards consist of the 2004 ADAAG (36 CFR part 1191 Appendices B and D, 2009 edition) plus DOJ subpart D rules; if the Access Board has amended this provision since 2009, the DOJ-adopted 2009 text controls.

rules.title: ADA Standards: car spaces 96 in. wide, van spaces 132 in. (or 96 in. with 96 in. aisle), aisles 60 in.
rules.plain_english: Federal accessible car spaces are at least 96 inches wide and van spaces 132 inches, or 96 inches if the aisle is 96 inches. Access aisles are at least 60 inches wide. California's 11B dimensions are larger and also apply.
rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California; Facilities built or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of state and local government entities (ADA Title II)
rules.citation: 2010 ADA Standards 502.2, 502.3.1 (36 CFR part 1191, App. D)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-36/part-1191 (eCFR 36 CFR part 1191, Appendix B (ADA Chapters 1-2) and Appendix D (Chapters 3-10) (version 2026-11-23); Appendix D, 502.2-502.3)
rules.quote: 502.2 Vehicle Spaces. Car parking spaces shall be 96 inches (2440 mm) wide minimum and van parking spaces shall be 132 inches (3350 mm) wide minimum, shall be marked to define the width, and shall have an adjacent access aisle complying with 502.3.
rules.notes: Text read from the eCFR edition of 36 CFR part 1191 current on 2026-11-23. Under 28 CFR 36.104 and 35.104 the 2010 ADA Standards consist of the 2004 ADAAG (36 CFR part 1191 Appendices B and D, 2009 edition) plus DOJ subpart D rules; if the Access Board has amended this provision since 2009, the DOJ-adopted 2009 text controls. CBC 11B-502 (as cited by LADBS): car 9 ft, van 12 ft with 5 ft aisle or 9 ft with 8 ft aisle.

rules.title: ADA Standards: at least 60% of public entrances must be accessible
rules.plain_english: Federally at least 60% of all public entrances must be accessible, in addition to specific entrances such as those from parking structures and tunnels. Check CBC 11B for California's entrance rules.
rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California; Facilities built or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of state and local government entities (ADA Title II)
rules.citation: 2010 ADA Standards 206.4.1 (36 CFR part 1191, App. B)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-36/part-1191 (eCFR 36 CFR part 1191, Appendix B (ADA Chapters 1-2) and Appendix D (Chapters 3-10) (version 2026-11-23); Appendix B, 206.4.1)
rules.quote: 206.4.1 Public Entrances. In addition to entrances required by 206.4.2 through 206.4.9, at least 60 percent of all public entrances shall comply with 404.
rules.notes: Text read from the eCFR edition of 36 CFR part 1191 current on 2026-11-23. Under 28 CFR 36.104 and 35.104 the 2010 ADA Standards consist of the 2004 ADAAG (36 CFR part 1191 Appendices B and D, 2009 edition) plus DOJ subpart D rules; if the Access Board has amended this provision since 2009, the DOJ-adopted 2009 text controls. The ceil() rounding is inferred from 'at least'. LADBS asks new buildings to 'detail compliance at all entrances and exterior ground-floor exits' (CL-BC-2026-026 item C.15, citing 11B-206.4.1).

rules.title: ADA Standards: raised employee work areas under 300 sq ft (7 in. or more up) are exempt
rules.plain_english: Employee work areas need only allow people with disabilities to approach, enter and exit (plus a few listed items). Work areas under 300 square feet that are raised 7 inches or more because the function requires it are exempt.

parameters.condition: elevation essential to the function; not raised courtroom stations

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California; Facilities built or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of state and local government entities (ADA Title II)
rules.citation: 2010 ADA Standards 203.9 (36 CFR part 1191, App. B)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-36/part-1191 (eCFR 36 CFR part 1191, Appendix B (ADA Chapters 1-2) and Appendix D (Chapters 3-10) (version 2026-11-23); Appendix B, 203.9)
rules.quote: Employee work areas, or portions of employee work areas, other than raised courtroom stations, that are less than 300 square feet (28 m 2 ) and elevated 7 inches (180 mm) or more above the finish floor or ground where the elevation is essential to the function of the space shall not be required to comply with these requirements or to be on an accessible route.
rules.notes: Text read from the eCFR edition of 36 CFR part 1191 current on 2026-11-23. Under 28 CFR 36.104 and 35.104 the 2010 ADA Standards consist of the 2004 ADAAG (36 CFR part 1191 Appendices B and D, 2009 edition) plus DOJ subpart D rules; if the Access Board has amended this provision since 2009, the DOJ-adopted 2009 text controls. CBC 11B-203.9 (LADBS) lists the California sections that apply within workstations.

rules.title: ADA Standards: if altering restrooms is technically infeasible, one unisex room on the same floor can substitute
rules.plain_english: In an alteration where making the existing toilet or bathing rooms comply is technically infeasible, you may instead provide a single accessible unisex toilet or bathing room in the same area and on the same floor.

parameters.condition: technically infeasible to comply with 603 in an alteration
parameters.substitute: single unisex toilet or bathing room complying with 213.2.1
parameters.location: same area and same floor as existing inaccessible rooms

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California; Facilities built or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of state and local government entities (ADA Title II)
rules.citation: 2010 ADA Standards 213.2 Exception 1 (36 CFR part 1191, App. B)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-36/part-1191 (eCFR 36 CFR part 1191, Appendix B (ADA Chapters 1-2) and Appendix D (Chapters 3-10) (version 2026-11-23); Appendix B, 213.2)
rules.quote: 1. In alterations where it is technically infeasible to comply with 603, altering existing toilet or bathing rooms shall not be required where a single unisex toilet room or bathing room complying with 213.2.1 is provided and located in the same area and on the same floor as existing inaccessible toilet or bathing rooms.
rules.notes: Text read from the eCFR edition of 36 CFR part 1191 current on 2026-11-23. Under 28 CFR 36.104 and 35.104 the 2010 ADA Standards consist of the 2004 ADAAG (36 CFR part 1191 Appendices B and D, 2009 edition) plus DOJ subpart D rules; if the Access Board has amended this provision since 2009, the DOJ-adopted 2009 text controls.

rules.title: ADA Standards: steeper ramps allowed in existing buildings only for short rises (1:10 up to 6 in., 1:8 up to 3 in.)
rules.plain_english: In existing sites and buildings, where space is too tight for a 1:12 ramp, a ramp may be steeper: up to 1:10 for a rise of no more than 6 inches, or up to 1:8 for a rise of no more than 3 inches. Steeper than 1:8 is never allowed.

parameters.condition: necessary due to space limitations

rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California; Facilities built or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of state and local government entities (ADA Title II)
rules.citation: 2010 ADA Standards 405.2 Exception 1 and Table 405.2 (36 CFR part 1191, App. D)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-36/part-1191 (eCFR 36 CFR part 1191, Appendix B (ADA Chapters 1-2) and Appendix D (Chapters 3-10) (version 2026-11-23); Appendix D, 405.2)
rules.quote: Table 405.2—Maximum Ramp Slope and Rise for Existing Sites, Buildings, and Facilities Slope 1 Maximum rise Steeper than 1:10 but not steeper than 1:8 3 inches (75 mm). Steeper than 1:12 but not steeper than 1:10 6 inches (150 mm). 1 A slope steeper than 1:8 is prohibited.
rules.notes: Text read from the eCFR edition of 36 CFR part 1191 current on 2026-11-23. Under 28 CFR 36.104 and 35.104 the 2010 ADA Standards consist of the 2004 ADAAG (36 CFR part 1191 Appendices B and D, 2009 edition) plus DOJ subpart D rules; if the Access Board has amended this provision since 2009, the DOJ-adopted 2009 text controls. Whether CBC 11B allows the same steeper slopes was not read; California projects must also meet CBC 11B-405.

rules.title: ADA Standards: accessible route clear width 36 in. (32 in. allowed for 24 in. max)
rules.plain_english: Federal accessible routes must be at least 36 inches clear, narrowing to 32 inches for no more than 24 inches at a time with 48-inch-long full-width segments between. The CBC site walkway target used by LADBS is 48 inches.
rules.applies_to: Places of public accommodation and commercial facilities (ADA Title III), nationwide including California; Facilities built or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of state and local government entities (ADA Title II)
rules.citation: 2010 ADA Standards 403.5.1 (36 CFR part 1191, App. D)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-36/part-1191 (eCFR 36 CFR part 1191, Appendix B (ADA Chapters 1-2) and Appendix D (Chapters 3-10) (version 2026-11-23); Appendix D, 403.5.1)
rules.quote: 403.5.1 Clear Width. Except as provided in 403.5.2 and 403.5.3, the clear width of walking surfaces shall be 36 inches (915 mm) minimum.
rules.notes: Text read from the eCFR edition of 36 CFR part 1191 current on 2026-11-23. Under 28 CFR 36.104 and 35.104 the 2010 ADA Standards consist of the 2004 ADAAG (36 CFR part 1191 Appendices B and D, 2009 edition) plus DOJ subpart D rules; if the Access Board has amended this provision since 2009, the DOJ-adopted 2009 text controls.

rules.title: Fair Housing Act: covered multifamily = 4+ unit buildings with an elevator, and ground-floor units in other 4+ unit buildings
rules.plain_english: Federal Fair Housing Act design rules cover every unit in buildings of 4 or more units that have an elevator, and the ground-floor units in buildings of 4 or more units without an elevator.
rules.applies_to: Covered multifamily dwellings (4+ units) designed and constructed for first occupancy after March 13, 1991: developers, architects, and builders/contractors
rules.quote: Covered multifamily dwellings means buildings consisting of 4 or more dwelling units if such buildings have one or more elevators; and ground floor dwelling units in other buildings consisting of 4 or more dwelling units.
rules.notes: California CBC Chapter 11A applies in addition; its unit-count thresholds were not read.

rules.title: Fair Housing Act: 'first occupancy' and 'ground floor' definitions
rules.plain_english: 'First occupancy' means a building never before used for any purpose. A 'ground floor' is any floor with a building entrance on an accessible route; a building can have more than one ground floor.

parameters.first_occupancy: building never before used for any purpose
parameters.ground_floor: floor with a building entrance on an accessible route

rules.applies_to: Covered multifamily dwellings (4+ units) designed and constructed for first occupancy after March 13, 1991: developers, architects, and builders/contractors
rules.quote: First occupancy means a building that has never before been used for any purpose. Ground floor means a floor of a building with a building entrance on an accessible route. A building may have more than one ground floor.

rules.title: Fair Housing Act design rules apply to first occupancy after March 13, 1991 (permit date test June 15, 1990)
rules.plain_english: The federal design and construction rules apply to covered multifamily housing first occupied after March 13, 1991. A building is treated as pre-1991 if it was occupied by March 13, 1991, or its last building permit (or renewal) was issued on or before June 15, 1990.
rules.applies_to: Covered multifamily dwellings (4+ units) designed and constructed for first occupancy after March 13, 1991: developers, architects, and builders/contractors
rules.quote: For purposes of this section, a covered multifamily dwelling shall be deemed to be designed and constructed for first occupancy on or before March 13, 1991, if the dwelling is occupied by that date, or if the last building permit or renewal thereof for the dwelling is issued by a State, County or local government on or before June 15, 1990.

rules.title: Fair Housing Act: at least one building entrance on an accessible route unless terrain makes it impractical
rules.plain_english: Covered multifamily buildings must have at least one building entrance on an accessible route unless terrain or unusual site characteristics make it impractical. The designer and builder must prove impracticality.

parameters.exception: impractical because of terrain or unusual characteristics of the site
parameters.burden_of_proof: person(s) who designed or constructed the housing

rules.applies_to: Covered multifamily dwellings (4+ units) designed and constructed for first occupancy after March 13, 1991: developers, architects, and builders/contractors
rules.quote: Covered multifamily dwellings for first occupancy after March 13, 1991 shall be designed and constructed to have at least one building entrance on an accessible route unless it is impractical to do so because of the terrain or unusual characteristics of the site.
rules.notes: Same subsection: 'The burden of establishing impracticality because of terrain or unusual site characteristics is on the person or persons who designed or constructed the housing facility.' Example (3) in 100.205(b): building fewer units to keep an accessible entrance is not 'impractical'.

rules.title: Fair Housing Act: accessible public and common use areas, and doors wide enough for wheelchairs
rules.plain_english: In covered multifamily buildings with a building entrance on an accessible route, the public and common use areas (for example hallways, lounges, lobbies, laundry rooms, refuse rooms, mail rooms, recreational areas and passageways) must be accessible, and all doors into and within the premises must be wide enough for wheelchair users.

requirements: public and common use areas readily accessible to and usable by persons with disabilities
all doors into and within all premises sufficiently wide for wheelchair passage

rules.applies_to: Covered multifamily dwellings (4+ units) designed and constructed for first occupancy after March 13, 1991: developers, architects, and builders/contractors
rules.quote: (1) The public and common use areas are readily accessible to and usable by handicapped persons; (2) All the doors designed to allow passage into and within all premises are sufficiently wide to allow passage by handicapped persons in wheelchairs; and
rules.notes: 'Common use areas' include hallways, lounges, lobbies, laundry rooms, refuse rooms, mail rooms, recreational areas and passageways (24 CFR 100.201).
rules.correction: Quote, parameters and citation confirmed. plain_english listed 'parking' as a common use area; the 24 CFR 100.201 definition read lists hallways, lounges, lobbies, laundry rooms, refuse rooms, mail rooms, recreational areas and passageways, and does not name parking. plain_english rewritten to the listed examples.

rules.title: Fair Housing Act: adaptable unit features (route, controls, grab bar backing, usable kitchens and baths)
rules.plain_english: Every covered dwelling unit needs an accessible route into and through the unit; switches, outlets, thermostats and other controls in accessible locations; wall reinforcement in bathrooms for future grab bars at the toilet, tub, shower and shower seat; and kitchens and bathrooms where a wheelchair user can maneuver.

unit_features: accessible route into and through the unit
light switches, electrical outlets, thermostats and other environmental controls in accessible locations
bathroom wall reinforcement for later grab bars around toilet, tub, shower stall and shower seat
usable kitchens and bathrooms for wheelchair maneuvering
parameters.framing_trade_note: grab bar backing must be installed during framing

rules.applies_to: Covered multifamily dwellings (4+ units) designed and constructed for first occupancy after March 13, 1991: developers, architects, and builders/contractors
rules.quote: (3) All premises within covered multifamily dwelling units contain the following features of adaptable design: (i) An accessible route into and through the covered dwelling unit; (ii) Light switches, electrical outlets, thermostats, and other environmental controls in accessible locations; (iii) Reinforcements in bathroom walls to allow later installation of grab bars around the toilet, tub, shower, stall and shower seat, where such facilities are provided; and (iv) Usable kitchens and bathrooms such that an individual in a wheelchair can maneuver about the space.
rules.notes: The 'framing_trade_note' parameter is a practical reading of (iii), not regulatory text.

rules.title: Fair Housing Act safe harbors: ICC/ANSI A117.1, HUD Guidelines and Design Manual, listed IBC editions
rules.plain_english: Designing to one of HUD's recognized safe harbors satisfies the federal design rules: the listed ICC/ANSI A117.1 editions (for unit features), the 1991 Fair Housing Accessibility Guidelines with the 1994 Q&A, the HUD Fair Housing Act Design Manual, or the 2000 (with 2001 supplement), 2003, 2006, 2009, 2012, 2015 or 2018 IBC as specified.

other_safe_harbors: Fair Housing Accessibility Guidelines (March 6, 1991) with June 28, 1994 Q&A supplement
Fair Housing Act Design Manual (HUD 1996, updated 1998)
2000 ICC Code Requirements for Housing Accessibility (CRHA)
parameters.conditions: adopted without modification or waiver of the Fair Housing provisions, interpreted with the matching IBC Commentary where stated

rules.applies_to: Covered multifamily dwellings (4+ units) designed and constructed for first occupancy after March 13, 1991: developers, architects, and builders/contractors
rules.quote: Compliance with the appropriate requirements of ICC A117.1-2009, ICC/ANSI A117.1-2003, ICC/ANSI A117.1-1998, CABO/ANSI A117.1-1992, or ANSI A117.1-1986 (all incorporated by reference, see § 100.201a), or suffices to satisfy the requirements of paragraph (c)(3) of this section.
rules.notes: The CBC is not listed as a HUD safe harbor; compliance with a duly enacted state law that includes the federal requirements satisfies them (100.205(f)), but see 100.205(h).

rules.title: Fair Housing Act: a building department's approval does not prove federal compliance
rules.plain_english: A city or state plan review or inspection that finds a building compliant is not conclusive if HUD or DOJ later enforces the Fair Housing Act. States may require more access than the federal rule.
rules.applies_to: Covered multifamily dwellings (4+ units) designed and constructed for first occupancy after March 13, 1991: developers, architects, and builders/contractors
rules.quote: Determinations of compliance or noncompliance by a State or a unit of general local government under paragraph (f) or (g) of this section are not conclusive in enforcement proceedings under the Fair Housing Amendments Act.
rules.notes: 100.205(i): the subpart does not limit state or local laws requiring greater access.

rules.title: Fair Housing Act: landlords must allow tenant-paid accessibility modifications
rules.plain_english: A landlord may not refuse a tenant with a disability permission to make reasonable modifications at the tenant's expense. For interior changes the landlord may require restoration at move-out where reasonable, may ask for a description of the work and assurance it will be done in a workmanlike manner with any required permits, but may not raise the security deposit.

landlord_may_require: restoration of interior where reasonable (reasonable wear and tear excepted)
interest-bearing escrow for restoration costs where necessary

rules.applies_to: Landlords of dwellings and contractors hired by tenants to make accessibility modifications
rules.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person to refuse to permit, at the expense of a handicapped person, reasonable modifications of existing premises, occupied or to be occupied by a handicapped person, if the proposed modifications may be necessary to afford the handicapped person full enjoyment of the premises of a dwelling.
rules.notes: Effective date not stated in the text read (the regulation cites 54 FR 3283, Jan. 23, 1989); the rule text is from 24 CFR 100.203 as of 2026-11-23. Example (1): landlord may not require removal of blocking added for grab bars.

rules.title: Fair Housing Act HUD (ALJ) civil penalties: up to $26,262 / $65,653 / $131,308 per practice
rules.plain_english: In a HUD administrative case, the judge can assess for each separate discriminatory housing practice up to $26,262 with no prior violation, $65,653 with one prior adjudication in 5 years, and $131,308 with two or more prior adjudications in 7 years.

parameters.per: separate and distinct discriminatory housing practice

rules.applies_to: Covered multifamily dwellings (4+ units) designed and constructed for first occupancy after March 13, 1991: developers, architects, and builders/contractors
rules.quote: (1) $26,262, if the respondent has not been adjudged in any administrative hearing or civil action permitted under the Fair Housing Act or any State or local fair housing law, or in any licensing or regulatory proceeding conducted by a Federal, State, or local governmental agency, to have committed any prior discriminatory housing practice.
rules.notes: Amounts as shown in eCFR on 2026-11-23 (latest amendment cited: 90 FR 24748, June 12, 2025). The eCFR point-in-time text shows these amounts in force from 2025-07-14; through 2025-07-13 the section read $25,597 / $63,991 / $127,983. No 2026 adjustment appears in eCFR as of 2026-11-23. HUD adjusts these amounts for inflation; check for a later adjustment.
rules.correction: Amounts $26,262 / $65,653 / $131,308 confirmed. The effective date was wrong: 2025-06-12 is the Federal Register publication date. In the eCFR point-in-time text, 180.671(a) still reads $25,597 / $63,991 / $127,983 through 2025-07-13 (the 2025-06-12 version only adds a link to the pending amendment) and the new amounts first appear on 2025-07-14. Corrected effective to 2025-07-14 and added parameters effective_per_ecfr and prior_amounts_usd (through 2025-07-13).

rules.title: Fair Housing Act DOJ pattern-or-practice civil penalty: up to $131,308 first, $262,614 subsequent
rules.plain_english: In a Justice Department Fair Housing Act civil action, the court can assess a civil penalty of up to $131,308 for a first violation and $262,614 for a subsequent violation (penalties assessed after July 3, 2025).
rules.applies_to: Covered multifamily dwellings (4+ units) designed and constructed for first occupancy after March 13, 1991: developers, architects, and builders/contractors
rules.quote: 42 U.S.C. 3614(d)(1)(C)(i) Fair Housing Act of 1968; first violation 28 CFR 85.3(b)(3)(i) 127,983 131,308
rules.notes: Row of 28 CFR 85.5 table 1; subsequent-violation row: '... subsequent violation 28 CFR 85.3(b)(3)(ii) 255,964 262,614'.

rules.title: CBC Table 11B-208.2: minimum accessible parking spaces per parking facility
rules.plain_english: Count accessible parking for each lot or garage from CBC Table 11B-208.2: 1 for 1-25 spaces, 2 for 26-50, 3 for 51-75, 4 for 76-100, 5 for 101-150, 6 for 151-200, 7 for 201-300, 8 for 301-400, 9 for 401-500, 2 percent of the total for 501-1,000, and 20 plus 1 for each 100 (or fraction) over 1,000. Hospital outpatient, mobility-rehabilitation and residential parking follow their own rules.

table.required: 20 plus 1 for each 100, or fraction thereof, over 1000

rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/accessible-details-for-parking.pdf (LADBS Information Bulletin P/BC 2026-084 'Accessibility Details for Parking', effective 01-01-2026, revised 11-23-2025; PDF page 1; 11B-208.2 Minimum number and Table 11B-208.2)
rules.quote: Parking spaces complying with Section 11B-502 shall be provided in accordance with Table 11B-208.2 except as required by Sections 11B-208.2.1, 11B-208.2.2 and 11B-208.2.3. Where more than one parking facility is provided on a site, the number of accessible spaces provided on the site shall be calculated according to the number of spaces required for each parking facility.
rules.notes: Quoted from an LADBS 2026 LABC document that restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS. The table printed on the same page matches federal Table 208.2 row for row. The rounding of the 2 percent row is not stated; CCDA's parking guide says CBC 11B-104 calls for always rounding up when calculating percentages for numbers of facilities.

rules.title: Bus, truck, delivery and impound parking is exempt from the accessible parking count
rules.plain_english: Parking spaces used only for buses, trucks, other delivery vehicles or vehicle impound do not have to meet CBC 11B-208, as long as a lot the public uses has an accessible passenger drop-off and loading zone (CBC 11B-503). EV charging spaces are not parking spaces for this count either.

parameters.proviso: lots accessed by the public provide a passenger drop-off and loading zone complying with 11B-503

rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/accessible-details-for-parking.pdf (LADBS Information Bulletin P/BC 2026-084 'Accessibility Details for Parking', effective 01-01-2026, revised 11-23-2025; PDF page 1; 11B-208.1 General, Exception 1)
rules.quote: Parking spaces used exclusively for buses, trucks, other delivery vehicles or vehicular impound shall not be required to comply with Section 11B-208 provided that lots accessed by the public are provided with a passenger drop-off and loading zone complying with Section 11B-503.
rules.notes: Quoted from an LADBS 2026 LABC document that restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS. Same page, 11B-208.1: 'electric vehicle charging stations are not parking spaces'.

rules.title: Measure accessible stall and aisle widths from the centerline of the stripes
rules.plain_english: Where accessible parking spaces and aisles are striped, measure their widths from the centerline of the stripes. Only where a space or aisle is not next to another space or aisle may the full width of its outside line be included.

parameters.exception: space or aisle not adjacent to another space or aisle: full line width may be included

rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/accessible-details-for-parking.pdf (LADBS Information Bulletin P/BC 2026-084 'Accessibility Details for Parking', effective 01-01-2026, revised 11-23-2025; PDF page 3; 11B-502.1 General and Exception)
rules.quote: Where parking spaces are marked with lines, width measurements of parking spaces and access aisles shall be made from the centerline of the markings.
rules.notes: Quoted from an LADBS 2026 LABC document that restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS.

rules.title: Accessible parking spaces and aisles: slopes no steeper than 1:48, aisle level with the space
rules.plain_english: Accessible parking spaces and their access aisles may not slope more than 1:48 (2.083%) in any direction, the aisle must be at the same level as the space, and changes in level and detectable warnings are not allowed in them.
rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/accessible-details-for-parking.pdf (LADBS Information Bulletin P/BC 2026-084 'Accessibility Details for Parking', effective 01-01-2026, revised 11-23-2025; PDF page 4; 11B-502.4 Floor or ground surfaces)
rules.quote: Parking spaces and access aisles serving them shall comply with Section 11B-302. Access aisles shall be at the same level as the parking spaces they serve. Changes in level, slopes exceeding 1:48, and detectable warnings shall not be permitted.
rules.notes: Quoted from an LADBS 2026 LABC document that restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS. 1:48 = 2.083% (arithmetic); the CBC 11A figure is the same (1109A.8.3).

rules.title: Existing multistory garages: 80 in clearance allowed at car (not van) accessible spaces
rules.plain_english: In an existing multistory parking facility, accessible car spaces, their aisles and the vehicle routes to them need 80 inches of vertical clearance instead of 98, and any existing clearance between 80 and 98 inches must be kept. Van spaces, their aisles and routes still need 98 inches.

parameters.not_for: van parking spaces, their access aisles and vehicular routes serving them

rules.applies_to: Existing multistory parking facilities serving public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B)
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/accessible-details-for-parking.pdf (LADBS Information Bulletin P/BC 2026-084 'Accessibility Details for Parking', effective 01-01-2026, revised 11-23-2025; PDF page 4; 11B-502.5 Vertical clearance and Exception)
rules.quote: In existing multistory parking facilities, car parking spaces, access aisles and vehicular routes serving them shall provide a vertical clearance of 80 inches (2032 mm) minimum. Existing vertical clearance in excess of 80 inches (2032 mm) and less than 98 inches (2489 mm) shall be maintained. This exception shall not apply to van parking spaces, access aisles or vehicular routes serving them.
rules.notes: Quoted from an LADBS 2026 LABC document that restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS. The rule itself on the same page: 'Parking spaces, access aisles and vehicular routes serving them shall provide a vertical clearance of 98 inches (2489 mm) minimum.'

rules.title: Accessible parking signs in a walk or other circulation path: bottom at 80 in minimum
rules.plain_english: An accessible parking sign normally has its bottom at least 60 inches above the ground, but a sign located within a circulation path (a walk or other pedestrian route) must have its bottom at least 80 inches above the walking surface.
rules.applies_to: Alterations, additions, structural repairs and new construction of public accommodations, commercial buildings and public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B), including tenant improvements
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/accessible-details-for-parking.pdf (LADBS Information Bulletin P/BC 2026-084 'Accessibility Details for Parking', effective 01-01-2026, revised 11-23-2025; PDF page 4; 11B-502.6 Identification, Exception)
rules.quote: Signs located within a circulation path shall be a minimum of 80 inches (2032 mm) above the finish floor or ground surface measured to the bottom of the sign.
rules.notes: Quoted from an LADBS 2026 LABC document that restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS. The CBC 11A parking sign rule is the same height on accessible routes (CL-BC-2026-027 item 26, 1109A.8.8.1).

rules.title: Accessible EV charging stations: CBC Table 11B-228.3.2.1 (public and common use)
rules.plain_english: EV charging spaces are not counted as parking; accessible EV charging stations are required separately. For public or common-use chargers, each combination of charging level and connector type is its own facility, and Table 11B-228.3.2.1 sets how many must be van accessible, standard accessible and ambulatory. Private chargers for one driver and fleet-only chargers are exempt from the count.

parameters.facility_is: each combination of charging level and EV connector type
exempt: not available to the general public and designated for an individual EV driver
not available to the general public and serving only fleet vehicles
parameters.multi_vehicle_charger: counts as the number of vehicles it can charge at once
parameters.existing_facilities: count includes both existing and new EVCS when new ones are added

rules.applies_to: Public-use and common-use electric vehicle charging stations at facilities covered by CBC Chapter 11B in California
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms/pc17/accessible-details-for-parking.pdf (LADBS Information Bulletin P/BC 2026-084 'Accessibility Details for Parking', effective 01-01-2026, revised 11-23-2025; PDF page 7; 11B-228.3.2 and 11B-228.3.2.1; Table 11B-228.3.2.1 on PDF page 8)
rules.quote: Where EVCS are provided for public use or common use, EVCS complying with Section 11B-812 shall be provided in accordance with Table 11B-228.3.2.1.
rules.notes: Quoted from an LADBS 2026 LABC document that restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS. Same page: 'Each combination of charging level (such as: AC Level 1, AC Level 2, DC Fast Charge) and EV connector type shall be considered as a facility.' Table row '101 and over': '1, plus 1 for each 300, or fraction thereof, over 100' (van accessible), '3, plus 1 for each 60, or fraction thereof, over 100' (standard), '3, plus 1 for each 50, or fraction thereof, over 100' (ambulatory). Vehicle space sizes (11B-812.6) are not used by the tools.

rules.title: CBC 11A accessible parking signs: 70 sq in, 60 in to the bottom, 80 in on accessible routes
rules.plain_english: Each accessible space reserved for persons with disabilities in covered multifamily parking gets a reflective International Symbol of Accessibility sign of at least 70 square inches, bottom at least 60 inches above the ground, or 80 inches where the sign is on an accessible route. Van spaces add 'Van Accessible'. Unassigned accessible spaces need the signs; where parking is assigned, the 1109A.8.8 signs are not required.
rules.applies_to: Parking serving covered multifamily dwellings in California (CBC 11A)
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-027-Acc_Residential.pdf (LADBS Residential Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-027, effective 01/01/2026, revised 08/21/2026; PDF page 5; Section B, items 26-28; items 16-17 on PDF page 4)
rules.quote: The sign shall not be smaller than 70 square inches in area, and shall be posted 60 inches minimum above the finish floor or ground surface, measured to the bottom of the sign. Signs located on accessible routes shall be posted at a minimum height of 80 inches above the finish floor or ground surface of the accessible route, measured to the bottom of the sign.
rules.notes: Quoted from the LADBS 2026 LABC Residential Accessibility checklist, which restates CBC Chapter 11A (HCD 1-AC) sections for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). CBC text itself not fetched. Item 16 (1109A.4): 'When assigned parking is provided, signage as required by Section 1109A.8.8 shall not be required.' Item 17 (1109A.5, unassigned parking): 'Accessible parking spaces shall be provided with signage as required by Section 1109A.8.8.' Item 28: van spaces have an additional sign or language stating 'Van Accessible' below the symbol.

rules.title: Public housing alterations: vacated buildings over 15 units need 5% mobility and 2% communication units
rules.plain_english: When a public housing building with more than 15 units is vacated to be altered, at least 5% of its units must get mobility features on an accessible route and at least 2% communication features. Where a unit's bathroom or kitchen is substantially altered and at least one other room is altered, that unit counts toward the new-construction numbers. Adaptable-unit standards do not apply to altering units first occupied on or before March 13, 1991.

parameters.unit_trigger: bathroom or kitchen substantially altered and at least one other room altered

rules.applies_to: Alterations of public housing (housing built or altered by, for, or on behalf of a public entity) in California
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-036-Acc_Public_Housing.pdf (LADBS Public Housing Accessibility checklist (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-036, effective 01/01/2026, revised 08/21/2026; PDF page 3; Section B, item 2.c.i-iii)
rules.quote: Where a building is vacated for the purposes of alteration, and the altered building contains more than 15 residential dwelling units, at least 5 percent of the residential dwelling units shall comply with Sections 11B-809.2 through 11B-809.4 and shall be on an accessible route as required by Section 11B-206. In addition, at least 2 percent of the residential dwelling units shall comply with Section 11B-809.5.
rules.notes: Quoted from an LADBS 2026 LABC document that restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS. Each item carries a '- see exception' note whose text the checklist does not print; the rounding of the percentages is not stated (ceil is used as for 11B-233.3.1).

rules.title: California new buildings: every entrance and exterior ground-floor exit must be accessible
rules.plain_english: For a new building, LADBS plan check asks for accessible-door compliance (CBC 11B-404) at all entrances and exterior ground-floor exits, citing CBC 11B-206.4.1. This is stricter than the federal rule of 60% of public entrances.

parameters.entrances_required_to_comply: all entrances and exterior ground-floor exits

rules.applies_to: New buildings that are public accommodations, commercial buildings or public buildings in California (CBC Chapter 11B)
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/forms_and_publications/publications/checklists/building-code/2026/CL-BC-2026-026-Acc_Commercial.pdf (LADBS Commercial Accessibility Plan Check Correction Sheets (2026 LABC), CL-BC-2026-026, effective 01/01/2026, revised 09/23/2026; PDF page 5; Section C, item 15)
rules.quote: For the new building proposed, detail compliance at all entrances and exterior ground-floor exits to buildings and facilities in compliance with 11B-404 Doors, Doorways, and Gates.
rules.notes: Quoted from an LADBS 2026 LABC document that restates CBC (Title 24 Part 2) Chapter 11B for the 2025 CBC cycle (effective 2026-01-01). The CBC text itself (codes.iccsafe.org, dgs.ca.gov) could not be fetched from this session, so the section number is as cited by LADBS. The item restates the CBC requirement as a plan-check correction, not the code text.

rules.title: Title II: windows, hardware, controls, outlets and signage do not trigger path of travel
rules.plain_english: For a state or local government facility, altering windows, hardware, controls, electrical outlets or signage is not an alteration that affects a primary function area, so it does not trigger the federal path-of-travel rule.
rules.applies_to: Facilities built or altered by, on behalf of, or for the use of state and local government entities (ADA Title II)
rules.quote: For the purposes of this section, alterations to windows, hardware, controls, electrical outlets, and signage shall not be deemed to be alterations that affect the usability of or access to an area containing a primary function.
rules.notes: Read from the eCFR versioner API full text of 28 CFR part 35 as of 2026-11-23 (the www.ecfr.gov HTML page redirects to a bot check, which was not bypassed). Same wording as the Title III rule, 28 CFR 36.403(c)(2).

rules.title: Off-road diesel rule covers vehicles of 25 hp or more
rules.plain_english: CARB's off-road diesel fleet rule applies to anyone who owns or operates in California a self-propelled off-road diesel vehicle (excavator, loader, dozer, backhoe, crane, forklift and the like) with an engine of 25 horsepower or more, including rented and leased machines. Two-engine cranes, drill rigs and similar vehicles with a 50 bhp or larger auxiliary engine are also covered.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 3, §2449(b)(1)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 3)
rules.quote: Except as provided in subsection (b)(2) below, this regulation applies to any person, business, or government agency who owns or operates within California any vehicles with a diesel-fueled or alternative diesel fueled off-road compression-ignition engine with maximum power (max hp) of 25 horsepower (hp) or greater provided that the vehicle cannot be registered and driven safely on-road or was not designed to be driven on-road, even if it has been modified so that it can be driven safely on-road.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. Exempt: vehicles used solely for agriculture, personal-use vehicles, vehicles awaiting sale (2449(e)(10)-(11)); emergency-only, snow-removal and over-half-agricultural vehicles still report and label.
rules.correction: effective changed from 2008-01-01 to 2008. CARB's overview fact sheet says only that the original regulation 'became effective in 2008', and none of the sources read gives a day; 2008-01-01 was not in any source. Applicability text, 25 hp threshold and 50 bhp two-engine auxiliary threshold confirmed in the Final Regulation Order 2449(b)(1)-(2).

rules.title: Off-road fleet size: small up to 2,500 hp, medium 2,501-5,000 hp, large over 5,000 hp
rules.plain_english: Fleet size is set by adding the horsepower of every off-road diesel vehicle under common ownership or control. Over 5,000 hp is a large fleet, 2,500 hp or less is a small fleet, and anything in between is medium. All state and federal government fleets count as large, whatever their size.

always_small: local municipality fleet in a low-population county
parameters.basis: total max hp under common ownership or control

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 11, §2449(c)(28)(A)-(C)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 11)
rules.quote: “Large fleet” – A fleet with a total max hp (as defined below) greater than 5,000 hp. [...] (B) “Medium fleet” – A fleet that is not a small or large fleet. (C) “Small fleet” – A fleet with total max hp of less than or equal to 2,500 hp that is owned by a business, non-profit organization, or local municipality, a local municipality fleet in a low population county irrespective of total max hp, a non-profit training center irrespective of total max hp, or a captive attainment area fleet irrespective of total max hp.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. CARB's Nov. 2025 booklet (Table 1) restates small < 2,500 hp, medium 2,501-5,000 hp, large > 5,000 hp. An optional 'ultra-small' path exists for fleets of 500 hp or less (see air-ord-optional-schedule-500hp).

rules.title: Low-use, snow-removal and emergency-only vehicles are left out of fleet horsepower
rules.plain_english: When adding up fleet horsepower to find the fleet size, leave out permanent low-use vehicles, dedicated snow-removal vehicles and vehicles used only for emergency work.

excluded_from_total_hp: vehicles used solely for emergency operations

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 18, §2449(c)(64)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 17)
rules.quote: “Total maximum power” (total max hp) means the sum of the max hp for all of a fleet’s engines that are subject to this regulation. Permanent and year-by-year low-use vehicles, dedicated snow-removal vehicles, and vehicles used solely for emergency operations shall not be included in the sum.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. Electric vehicles also need not be included when determining fleet size (2449(d)(1)(B)3.).

rules.title: Fleet includes every company under the same owners or managers
rules.plain_english: Vehicles owned by different companies still count as one fleet if the same people manage them day to day, or the same majority stockholders control the companies. You cannot split equipment into separate LLCs to stay a small fleet.

aggregates_entities_with: corporations controlled by the same majority stockholders

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 7, §2449(c)(10)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 7)
rules.quote: “Common ownership or control” means being owned or managed day to day by the same person, corporation, partnership, or association. Vehicles managed by the same directors, officers, or managers, or by corporations controlled by the same majority stockholders are considered to be under common ownership or control even if their title is held by different business entities.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: Rentals under 1 year stay in the rental company's fleet
rules.plain_english: A machine rented or leased for less than one year belongs to the rental company's fleet for CARB purposes. A lease of one year or more can move the machine into the renter's fleet, but only if the written lease says so.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 10, §2449(c)(27)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 10)
rules.quote: “Rental or Leased Fleets” – Vehicles that are owned by a rental or leasing company and that are leased by the same lessee for a period of one year or more may be excluded from the rental company fleet and included in the fleet of the lessee only if such arrangement is delineated in the written lease agreement. Vehicles that are rented or leased for a period of less than one year must be included in the fleet of the rental or leasing company.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.
rules.correction: Replaced short_term_rental_max_days_exclusive = 365 with short_term_rental_less_than_years = 1. The regulation says 'less than one year'; 365 days does not appear in the text and is wrong in a leap year. Other parameters confirmed.

rules.title: Captive attainment area: fleets that work only in 21 cleaner-air counties
rules.plain_english: A fleet that works only in the listed rural counties is a 'captive attainment area fleet'. It is treated as a small fleet whatever its size, uses green EIN labels, and its vehicles are exempt from the renewable diesel requirement while working there.

parameters.partial_county: Sonoma (North Coast Air Basin portion only)

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF pages 6-7, §2449(c)(6)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 6)
rules.quote: “Captive attainment area fleet” means a fleet or fleet portion, as defined under section 2449(c)(24), in which all of the vehicles in the fleet or fleet portion operate exclusively within the following counties: Alpine, Colusa, Del Norte, Glenn, Humboldt, Lake, Lassen, Mendocino, Modoc, Monterey, Plumas, San Benito, San Luis Obispo, Santa Barbara, Santa Cruz, Shasta, Sierra, Siskiyou, Trinity, Tehama, Yuba, and the portion of Sonoma County that lies within the boundaries of the North Coast Air Basin.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. Fleets owned by the United States, the State of California or their agencies are large fleets and are never part of a captive attainment area fleet (2449(c)(6)); that sentence does not cover local municipality fleets. The renewable diesel exemption is 2449.1(f)(2)(A); the green label is 2449(f)(1)(B)1.

rules.title: Off-road diesel equipment may not idle more than 5 minutes
rules.plain_english: No off-road diesel machine may idle for more than five minutes in a row. Exceptions: waiting in a work queue, safety checks, servicing, idling needed to do the machine's work (such as running a crane), warming up to operating temperature, and idling needed for safe operation. For a rented machine, the renter is responsible, and the rental agreement must say so.

exceptions: queuing
safety check
testing/servicing/repair/diagnostics
work the vehicle was designed for (e.g., crane)
warm-up to operating temperature
safe operation
parameters.waiver: Executive Officer may grant a written waiver on justification

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 26, §2449(d)(2)(A)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 26)
rules.quote: No vehicle or engines subject to this regulation may idle for more than five consecutive minutes. Idling of a vehicle that is owned by a rental company is the responsibility of the renter or lessee, and the rental agreement shall so indicate. The idling limit does not apply to: 1. idling when queuing, 2. idling to verify that the vehicle is in safe operating condition, 3. idling for testing, servicing, repairing or diagnostic purposes, 4. idling necessary to accomplish work for which the vehicle was designed (such as operating a crane), 5. idling required to bring the machine system to operating temperature, and 6. idling necessary to ensure safe operation of the vehicle.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. The idling limit took effect when the original regulation was certified by the Secretary of State (2449(d)(2)); CARB's overview fact sheet says the regulation 'became effective in 2008'; the exact day was not read. The jobsite sign required of prime contractors repeats the 5-minute limit.

rules.title: Waiting in line before the workday starts is not 'queuing'
rules.plain_english: The idling exception for queuing covers stop-and-go waiting in a work line when shutting off is not practical. Sitting in line with the engine running before the workday or site opens is not queuing, so the 5-minute limit applies.

parameters.queuing_excludes: waiting motionless in line before the start of a workday or opening of a location

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 15, §2449(c)(47)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 15)
rules.quote: “Queuing” means the intermittent starting and stopping of a vehicle while the driver, in the normal course of doing business, is waiting to perform work or a service, and when shutting the vehicle engine off would impede the progress of the queue and is not practicable. Queuing does not include the time a driver may wait motionless in line in anticipation of the start of a workday or opening of a location where work or a service will be performed.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: Medium and large fleets need a written idling policy
rules.plain_english: Medium and large off-road fleets must have a written idling policy, give it to their equipment operators, and tell them idling is limited to five minutes.

parameters.policy_content: idling limited to five consecutive minutes or less

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 26, §2449(d)(2)(B)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 26)
rules.quote: As of March 1, 2009, medium and large fleets must also have a written idling policy that is made available to operators of the vehicles and informs them that idling is limited to five consecutive minutes or less.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. Initial reporting asks whether the fleet has an idling policy documented and available to employees (2449(g)(1)(A)14.).

rules.title: Equipment rental agreements must put idling responsibility on the renter
rules.plain_english: If you rent out off-road diesel equipment, the rental agreement must state that the renter is responsible for complying with the 5-minute idling limit.

parameters.clause_subject: renter or lessee responsible for idling limit

rules.applies_to: Rental and leasing companies that rent off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more for use in California, and contractors who rent them
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 26, §2449(d)(2)(A)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 26)
