rules.quote: Idling of a vehicle that is owned by a rental company is the responsibility of the renter or lessee, and the rental agreement shall so indicate.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: A small fleet that grows has two years to meet medium or large fleet rules
rules.plain_english: If a small fleet grows into a medium or large fleet, it must meet the bigger fleet's requirements on the compliance date two years after the year it grew. A medium fleet that becomes large also gets two years. A fleet that shrinks may follow either its old or new size on the next compliance date.

parameters.shrink: may meet either the old or the new size requirements on the next compliance date

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 27, §2449(d)(3)(A)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 26)
rules.quote: Small fleets that become medium or large fleets must meet the medium or large fleet requirements, respectively, on the compliance date in section 2449.1 two years subsequent to the year they became a medium or large fleet.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: New fleets: report vehicles to CARB within 30 days
rules.plain_english: A business that buys its first off-road diesel vehicles, or brings them into California for the first time, must report them to CARB (in DOORS) within 30 days, and immediately meets the idling and adding-vehicle rules.

parameters.trigger: purchase of vehicles or bringing them into California

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 28, §2449(d)(4)(C)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 28)
rules.quote: New and newly reported fleets must comply with the idling requirements in section 2449(d)(2) and the adding vehicle requirements in section 2449(d)(6) immediately upon purchasing vehicles subject to the regulation, upon bringing such vehicles into the State, or upon reporting the fleet to CARB for the first time, whichever occurs first. New and newly reported fleets must report vehicles subject to the regulation to CARB within 30 days of purchasing or bringing such vehicles into the State, in accordance with the requirements in section 2449(g).
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.
rules.correction: verbatim_quote re-based on the Final Regulation Order wording ('newly reported' without the hyphen the 15-day text had); source_location now cites the Final Regulation Order. The 30-day reporting deadline and the immediate idling/adding-vehicle duties are unchanged and confirmed; 2449(g)(3) (30 days) also confirmed.

rules.title: No fleet may add a Tier 0 off-road vehicle
rules.plain_english: No off-road fleet may add (buy, lease long-term or bring in) a vehicle with an uncontrolled Tier 0 engine. In the amended regulation this general ban took effect when U.S. EPA authorized it, which CARB dates January 10, 2025. Since January 1, 2024 fleets also may not add a Tier 0 vehicle designated for snow removal, emergency work or Job Corps.

parameters.general_ban_effective: upon U.S. EPA authorization of the regulation (2449(d)(6)(A))

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF pages 30-31, §2449(d)(6)(A), (H)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF pages 29-30)
rules.quote: Ban on adding Tier 0s – Effective upon U.S. EPA issuing authorization for this regulation, a fleet may not add a vehicle with a Tier 0 engine to its fleet. The engine tier must be Tier 1 or higher. [...] (H) Ban on adding Tier 0s to special provisions – Beginning January 1, 2024, for large, medium, and small fleets, a fleet may not add a vehicle with a Tier 0 engine to its fleet as a vehicle designated as a dedicated snow removal vehicle, a vehicle used for emergency operations, or a Job Corps vehicle, as described in section 2449(e).
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. Tier 1 and Tier 2 additions were already banned (large/medium 2013/2018; small 2016/2023). CARB's booklet (offroad_booklet_11.17.25.pdf) describes the general Tier 0 adding ban as effective January 1, 2014; the adopted 2449(d)(6)(A) text ties it to U.S. EPA authorization (January 10, 2025).
rules.correction: Added general_ban_effective and us_epa_authorization_date. The rule's only date (2024-01-01) is for the special-provision ban in (d)(6)(H); the general Tier 0 adding ban in (d)(6)(A) of the Final Regulation Order is 'Effective upon U.S. EPA issuing authorization for this regulation', which CARB's July 21, 2025 enforcement notice dates January 10, 2025. CARB's booklet states the Tier 0 adding ban was 'Effective January 1, 2014' (pre-2022 text); the regulation text controls. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: Since 2024 no fleet may add a Tier 3 off-road vehicle
rules.plain_english: Starting January 1, 2024, no off-road fleet of any size may add a vehicle with a Tier 3 engine. Anything added must be at least Tier 4 interim.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 30, §2449(d)(6)(D)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 30)
rules.quote: Ban on adding Tier 3s – Beginning January 1, 2024, for large, medium, and small fleets, a fleet may not add a vehicle with a Tier 3 engine to its fleet. The engine tier must be Tier 4 interim or higher.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. CARB's July 21, 2025 enforcement notice says enforcement of the expanded adding-vehicle requirement began January 11, 2025.

rules.title: Tier 4 interim additions banned: large/medium since 2024, small fleets from 2028
rules.plain_english: Large and medium fleets may add only Tier 4 final (or cleaner) off-road vehicles since January 1, 2024. Small fleets may still add Tier 4 interim vehicles until December 31, 2027; from January 1, 2028 they too may add only Tier 4 final.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 30, §2449(d)(6)(E)-(F)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 30)
rules.quote: Ban on adding Tier 4 interims – Beginning January 1, 2024, for large and medium fleets, and January 1, 2028, for small fleets, a fleet may not add a vehicle with a Tier 4 interim engine to its fleet. The engine tier must be Tier 4 final or higher. [...] Instead, beginning January 1, 2035, a fleet that chooses to comply with the requirements of 2449(e)(16) may not add a vehicle with a Tier 4 interim engine to its fleet.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. 2449(e)(9) lets CARB grant an extension to add Tier 4 interim vehicles when Tier 4 final vehicles are not available.

rules.title: On-road-engine off-road vehicles added must have a 2007 or newer engine
rules.plain_english: For vehicles powered by an on-road truck engine (such as workover rigs and some two-engine vehicles), large and medium fleets may add only 2007-or-newer engines since 2024; small fleets from January 1, 2028.

parameters.banned: model year 2006 or earlier on-road engine

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF pages 30-31, §2449(d)(6)(G)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 30)
rules.quote: Ban on adding vehicles powered by model year 2006 or earlier on-road engines – Beginning January 1, 2024, for large and medium fleets, and January 1, 2028, for small fleets, a fleet may not add a vehicle powered by a model year 2006 or earlier on-road engine to its fleet.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. Fleets of 500 hp or less are small fleets for this ban. The adopted text lets them substitute only the Tier 4 interim adding date ((d)(6)(F), 2035) and the Tier 2 phase-out date (2449.1(c)(5)); (d)(6)(G) has no 500 hp exception. CARB's overview fact sheet (rev. Jan. 2024, Table 2) shows 2035 for 'On-road <2006' under the ultra-small option, but that fact sheet states it does not alter the regulation, and the July 2025 enforcement notice does not address on-road engines.
rules.correction: effective_by_fleet_size.optional_500hp_or_less changed from 2035-01-01 to 2028-01-01. In the Final Regulation Order, 2449(d)(6)(G) bans adding MY2006-or-earlier on-road engines for small fleets from January 1, 2028, with no carve-out. The 500 hp-or-less carve-outs in (d)(6)(F) and in the last paragraphs of 2449(e)(16) cover only the Tier 4 interim adding ban and the Tier 2 phase-out. The 2035 figure appears only in CARB's overview fact sheet Table 2, which conflicts with the adopted text; it is not in the enforcement notice.

rules.title: Large fleets: Tier 0 banned 2024, Tier 1 from 2026, Tier 2 from 2028
rules.plain_english: A large off-road fleet (over 5,000 hp) may not operate in California any Tier 0 vehicle (or 1994-and-older on-road engine) since 2024, any Tier 1 vehicle (or 1999-and-older on-road engine) since January 1, 2026, and any Tier 2 vehicle (or 2003-and-older on-road engine) from January 1, 2028.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 80, §2449.1(c)(1)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 77)
rules.quote: (A) Beginning January 1, 2024, a large fleet shall not operate any vehicle with a Tier 0 engine or a model year 1994 or earlier on-road engine in California. (B) Beginning January 1, 2026, a large fleet shall not operate any vehicle with a Tier 1 engine or a model year 1999 or earlier on-road engine in California. (C) Beginning January 1, 2028, a large fleet shall not operate any vehicle with a Tier 2 engine or a model year 2003 or earlier on-road engine in California.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. Phase-out is met by retiring, selling, repowering or designating the vehicle permanent low-use.

rules.title: Medium fleets: Tier 0 banned 2026, Tier 1 from 2028, Tier 2 from 2030
rules.plain_english: A medium off-road fleet (2,501-5,000 hp) may not operate any Tier 0 vehicle (or 1994-and-older on-road engine) since January 1, 2026, any Tier 1 (or 1999-and-older) from January 1, 2028, and any Tier 2 (or 2003-and-older) from January 1, 2030.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 80, §2449.1(c)(2)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 77)
rules.quote: (A) Beginning January 1, 2026, a medium fleet shall not operate any vehicle with a Tier 0 engine or a model year 1994 or earlier on-road engine in California. (B) Beginning January 1, 2028, a medium fleet shall not operate any vehicle with a Tier 1 engine or a model year 1999 or earlier on-road engine in California. (C) Beginning on January 1, 2030, a medium fleet shall not operate a vehicle with a Tier 2 engine or a model year 2003 or earlier on-road engine in California.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: Small fleets: Tier 0 banned 2028, Tier 1 from 2030, Tier 2 from 2032
rules.plain_english: A small off-road fleet (2,500 hp or less) may not operate any Tier 0 vehicle (or 1994-and-older on-road engine) from January 1, 2028, any Tier 1 (or 1999-and-older) from January 1, 2030, and any Tier 2 (or 2003-and-older) from January 1, 2032.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 80, §2449.1(c)(3)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 77)
rules.quote: (A) Beginning on January 1, 2028, a small fleet shall not operate a vehicle with a Tier 0 engine or a model year 1994 or earlier on-road engine in California. (B) Beginning on January 1, 2030, a small fleet shall not operate a vehicle with a Tier 1 engine or a model year 1999 or earlier on-road engine in California. (C) Beginning January 1, 2032, a small fleet shall not operate any vehicle with a Tier 2 engine or a model year 2003 or earlier on-road engine in California.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. Fleets of 500 hp or less on the optional schedule follow the same Tier 0/Tier 1 dates but get until 2036 for Tier 2 (air-ord-tier2-phaseout-500hp-2036).

rules.title: Permanent low-use and Job Corps vehicles: Tier 0 banned from 2036
rules.plain_english: Vehicles designated permanent low-use (or Job Corps) are spared the normal phase-out dates, but from January 1, 2036 even they may not be Tier 0 (or have a 1994-or-older on-road engine).
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 81, §2449.1(c)(4)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 77)
rules.quote: Beginning on January 1, 2036, a fleet shall not operate a vehicle designated as permanent low-use or as a Job Corps vehicle with a Tier 0 engine or a model year 1994 or earlier on-road engine in California.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.
rules.correction: verbatim_quote re-based on the Final Regulation Order wording ('Job Corps' where the 15-day text had 'jobs corps'); source_location now cites the Final Regulation Order. The 2036-01-01 date, Tier 0 and MY1994 on-road limits are unchanged and confirmed.

rules.title: Fleets of 500 hp or less on the optional schedule: Tier 2 banned from 2036
rules.plain_english: A fleet with 500 hp or less that chose the optional compliance schedule is not held to the small-fleet 2032 Tier 2 date; instead it may not operate Tier 2 vehicles (or 2003-and-older on-road engines) from January 1, 2036.

parameters.condition: fleet elects 2449(e)(16) optional schedule

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 81, §2449.1(c)(5)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 78)
rules.quote: Fleets that choose to comply with the requirements of 2449(e)(16) are not subject to the small fleet Tier 2 engine phase-out requirements in section 2449.1(c)(3)(C) above. Instead, beginning January 1, 2036, these fleets shall not operate a vehicle with a Tier 2 engine or a model year 2003 or earlier on-road engine in California.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: Fleets of 500 hp or less: 75% of horsepower Tier 2 or better by Jan. 1, 2026
rules.plain_english: A very small fleet (500 hp or less in total) may follow a simpler schedule instead of the small fleet average/BACT rules: at least 25% of its horsepower in Tier 2-or-better engines by 2019, 50% by 2022, 75% by January 1, 2026 and 100% by January 1, 2029. Every vehicle counts; no exemptions apply. A fleet that grows past 500 hp must switch to the small fleet rules.
rules.applies_to: Owners of off-road diesel fleets with 500 total max hp or less
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF pages 43-44, §2449(e)(16), Table 1); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF pages 39-40)
rules.quote: Fleets with 500 hp or less total max hp may meet the optional compliance schedule listed below in Table 1 instead of the small fleet requirements in 2449.1(a)(2) and 2449.1(b). [...] 2026 75 2029 100 [...] If a fleet grows larger than 500 hp, that fleet must begin meeting the fleet average or BACT requirements for small fleets on the next compliance date for the applicable fleet size category.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. Table 1 columns: compliance date (January 1 of year) and percent of fleet hp that must have a Tier 2 or higher engine (2019: 25; 2022: 50; 2026: 75; 2029: 100).

rules.title: Designate special-provision vehicles by Dec. 31 before the phase-out year
rules.plain_english: A vehicle you want treated as a special-provision vehicle (low-use, emergency, snow removal and similar) to avoid a Tier phase-out must be designated by December 31 of the year before that phase-out takes effect for your fleet.

parameters.designate_by: December 31 of the year before the applicable Tier phase-out effective date

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 79, §2449.1(c)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 76)
rules.quote: Any special provision vehicle, as described in section 2449(e), with an engine that is subject to these Tier phase-outs must be designated as a special provision vehicle by December 31 of the year prior to the Tier phase-out’s effective date for that vehicle and fleet.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: Each zero-emission machine added delays one Tier 1/Tier 2 phase-out by 2 years
rules.plain_english: For each zero-emission off-road vehicle (25 hp or more, similar size class) a fleet adds on or after January 1, 2024, it may keep one existing Tier 1 or Tier 2 vehicle two extra years past its phase-out date. The older vehicle must have been reported to CARB before January 1, 2023, and both vehicles must be reported by December 31 of the year before the phase-out.

parameters.report_by: December 31 of the year before the phase-out

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF pages 81-82, §2449.1(d)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF pages 78-79)
rules.quote: For each zero-emission vehicle a fleet adds to its fleet on or after January 1, 2024, the fleet may delay the Tier phase-out in section 2449.1(c) for one existing vehicle with a Tier 1 or Tier 2 engine in its fleet for two years, if all of the following conditions are met during those two years: [...] The vehicle with a Tier 1 or Tier 2 engine must have been reported to CARB as being in the fleet prior to January 1, 2023, to be eligible for the delay of the Tier phase-out.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: Off-road fleets: annual DOORS reporting due March 1 through 2036
rules.plain_english: Every off-road fleet must review and update its CARB (DOORS) report by March 1 each year, showing each vehicle as of December 31 of the prior year. Large fleets report through 2036, medium 2016-2036, small 2018-2036. A fleet with permanent or year-by-year low-use vehicles must keep reporting those vehicles every year for as long as it owns or operates them, even after 2036.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 52, §2449(g)(2)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 48)
rules.quote: The reporting date for all fleets is March 1. Fleet owners must report information regarding each vehicle subject to this regulation as it was on December 31 of the year prior to the reporting year [...] Large fleets must report annually each year from 2012 to 2036. Medium fleets must report annually each year 2016 to 2036. Small fleets must report annually each year from 2018 to 2036. [...] Any fleet that operates permanent or year-by-year low-use vehicles must continue to report annually for each permanent or year-by-year low-use vehicle for as long as the fleet owns or operates the vehicle.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. Fleets with low-use vehicles keep reporting annually as long as they own them.
rules.correction: Review 2026-11-25: added low_use_vehicles_report_while_owned: low-use vehicles keep annual reporting after 2036 for as long as the fleet owns or operates them (2449(g)(2)). Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: Annual Responsible Official Affirmation of Reporting (ROAR)
rules.plain_english: With each annual report, a responsible official (or a designated official, with a signed designation letter from the responsible official attached the first time) must sign an affirmation that the report is accurate and the fleet complies. Captive attainment area fleets must also certify that their vehicles did not operate outside the listed counties in the prior year.

parameters.submission: DOORS or paper/electronic form approved by the Executive Officer

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 52, §2449(g)(2)(A)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 48)
rules.quote: Each year that annual reporting is required, a fleet shall submit to CARB an affirmation, signed by a responsible official or a designated official that the information reported is accurate and that the fleet is in compliance with the regulation.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. The 15-day text's sentence deeming everything submitted under 2449(g) to be under penalty of perjury is not in the Final Regulation Order (deleted before adoption), so it is not used.
rules.correction: Removed under_penalty_of_perjury and the quoted sentence 'All information and documentation submitted to CARB under section 2449(g) is deemed to be submitted under the penalty of perjury.' That sentence is in the 15-day text but not in the adopted Final Regulation Order: a word-level diff shows it deleted, and 'perjury' appears in the order only in the SOON section. Replaced electronic_option 'e-ROAR in DOORS' ('e-ROAR' is not in any text read) with submission 'DOORS or paper/electronic form approved by the Executive Officer' (2449(g)(2)(A); CARB booklet: 'using DOORS or forms available on CARB's website'). Added the designation-letter and captive-fleet certification duties stated in 2449(g)(2)(A). Citation narrowed to 2449(g)(2)(A); plain_english updated.

rules.title: Annual renewable diesel affirmation
rules.plain_english: Since 2024, each annual report must include an affirmation signed by the responsible or designated official that the fleet met the renewable diesel (R99/R100) requirement.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 55, §2449(g)(2)(D)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 51)
rules.quote: Beginning January 1, 2024, in each year that annual reporting is required, a fleet shall submit to CARB an affirmation signed by its responsible official or designated official that the fleet complied with the performance requirements outlined in section 2449.1(f).
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: Report a sold off-road vehicle to CARB within 30 days
rules.plain_english: Anyone selling an off-road diesel vehicle in California must tell CARB within 30 days of the sale (the annual report counts if it falls within those 30 days). Once you update DOORS, the buyer can add it to their fleet.

parameters.trigger: date the vehicle was sold

rules.applies_to: Anyone selling an off-road diesel vehicle of 25 hp or more in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 55, §2449(g)(4)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 52)
rules.quote: Any person selling a vehicle with an engine subject to this regulation in California must notify CARB within 30 days from the date the vehicle was sold.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: Off-road vehicle bill of sale must carry CARB's disclosure statement
rules.plain_english: When you sell an off-road diesel vehicle in California, the bill of sale must include CARB's exact disclosure sentence, and you must keep proof you gave it for three years.

parameters.text: When operated in California, any off-road diesel vehicle may be subject to the California Air Resources Board In-Use Off-road Diesel Vehicle Regulation. It therefore could be subject to retrofit or accelerated turnover requirements to reduce emissions of air pollutants. For more information, please visit the California Air Resources Board website at http://www.arb.ca.gov/msprog/ordiesel/ordiesel.htm.

rules.applies_to: Anyone selling an off-road diesel vehicle of 25 hp or more in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 63, §2449(l)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF pages 59-60)
rules.quote: Any person selling a vehicle with an engine subject to this regulation in California must provide the following disclosure in writing to the buyer on the bill of sale, “When operated in California, any off-road diesel vehicle may be subject to the California Air Resources Board In-Use Off-road Diesel Vehicle Regulation. It therefore could be subject to retrofit or accelerated turnover [...] requirements to reduce emissions of air pollutants. For more information, please visit the California Air Resources Board website at http://www.arb.ca.gov/msprog/ordiesel/ordiesel.htm.”
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. Three-year record retention for the disclosure: 2449(h)(11).

rules.title: Apply for a CARB EIN within 30 days of adding a vehicle
rules.plain_english: When you buy an off-road diesel vehicle or bring one into California, you have 30 days to apply to CARB for an Equipment Identification Number (EIN), or to report the purchase if it already has one.

submission: mail: CARB MSCD (In-Use Off-road Diesel), P.O. Box 2815, Sacramento, CA 95812

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF pages 44-45, §2449(f)(1)(A)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 41)
rules.quote: if a fleet owner adds a vehicle to his California fleet or brings a vehicle into California from outside the State, the fleet owner has 30 days from the date of purchase or the date the vehicle enters California to apply to CARB for an EIN or, if the vehicle already has an EIN, to inform CARB of the purchase using forms approved by the Executive Officer for submittal of required reporting information.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: Put the EIN on the vehicle within 30 days of receiving it
rules.plain_english: Within 30 days of getting the EIN from CARB, permanently paint or affix it on the vehicle. CARB does not supply labels.

parameters.trigger: receipt of CARB-issued EIN

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 45, §2449(f)(1)(B)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 41)
rules.quote: Within 30 days of receipt of the CARB-issued EIN, fleet owners shall permanently affix or paint the EIN(s) on the vehicle in clear view according to the following specification:
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. CARB's booklet: 'CARB does not issue EIN labels'.

rules.title: EIN label: white on red, both sides, about 5 ft up, letters 3 in tall
rules.plain_english: The EIN must be white on a red background (green for captive attainment area fleets), on both outside sides of the vehicle about 5 feet above the ground, with each character at least 3 inches high and 1.5 inches wide, and stay legible for the life of the vehicle.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 45, §2449(f)(1)(B)1.-3.); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 42)
rules.quote: 1. The EIN shall be white on a red background, unless the vehicle is part of a captive attainment area fleet, in which case the EIN shall be white on a green background. 2. The EIN shall be located in clear view on both sides of the outside of the vehicle approximately 5 feet above the ground, or, if the vehicle is not 5 feet tall, lower on the vehicle. 3. Each character shall be at least 3 inches (7.6 centimeters) in height and 1.5 inches (3.8 centimeters) in width.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: Missing engine emission label: contact the manufacturer within 10 days
rules.plain_english: If an engine's emission control label becomes unreadable, contact the engine manufacturer within 10 days to get a replacement affixed. If the manufacturer cannot do it within 30 days, ask for a replacement label to be sent and put it on right away.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 46, §2449(f)(2)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 42)
rules.quote: If a fleet observes that the emission control label is no longer visible or readable for any reason, the fleet must contact the manufacturer within 10 days and request a replacement emission control label be affixed by the manufacturer. If the manufacturer is unable to affix the label within 30 days of the fleet’s request, then the fleet must request a replacement emission control label be sent to the fleet.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: Off-road fleet records: kept in California, produced within 5 business days
rules.plain_english: Keep copies of everything reported to CARB plus the required records (bills of sale, VDECS, approvals, fuel purchases) at a location in California, and hand them to CARB within five business days of a request.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 57, §2449(h)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 53)
rules.quote: Fleet owners must maintain copies of the information reported under section 2449(g), as well as the records described in section 2449(h) below, and provide them to an agent or employee of CARB within five business days upon request. Records must be kept at a location within the State of California.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: Keep off-road fleet records while you own the fleet (until Jan. 1, 2037)
rules.plain_english: Keep each vehicle's and the fleet's records as long as you have the fleet, or until January 1, 2037 if that comes first. When you sell a vehicle or the whole fleet, pass the records to the buyer.

parameters.retain_until: earlier of: while the owner has a fleet, or 2037-01-01

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 59, §2449(h)(11)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 55)
rules.quote: Each fleet owner shall maintain the records for each vehicle subject to the regulation and for the overall fleet as long as the owner has a fleet or until January 1, 2037, whichever is earlier.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: Off-road fleets must buy and use R99 or R100 renewable diesel
rules.plain_english: Since January 1, 2024, every off-road fleet must buy R99 or R100 renewable diesel and use it in all its covered off-road vehicles in California, including rented equipment, unless an exemption applies.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 88, §2449.1(f)(1)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 85)
rules.quote: Beginning January 1, 2024, all fleets subject to this regulation are required to procure R99 or R100 renewable diesel and use this fuel in all vehicles subject to this regulation, including rental equipment, when operating them in California, subject to the exemptions provided in section 2449.1(f)(2) below.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. Category 'prohibition' is used for the bar on fueling with conventional diesel.

rules.title: Renewable diesel exemptions: captive counties, all-Tier-4F fleets, cold weather below 20 F
rules.plain_english: The R99/R100 requirement does not apply to captive attainment area fleets (or vehicles while in those counties), fleets made up entirely of Tier 4 final, 2010+ on-road or zero-emission vehicles, and during cold weather: in places where the January 10th-percentile low is below 20 F, from November through February (winter fuel may be bought from October 15); or for days when it drops, or is forecast within 14 days to drop, below 20 F.

exempt_fleets: captive attainment area fleet or vehicle operating in a listed county
fleet entirely Tier 4 final, MY2010+ on-road, or zero-emission

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF pages 88-89, §2449.1(f)(2)(B)-(C)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 86)
rules.quote: Any fleet or fleet portion that is comprised entirely of vehicles with Tier 4 final engines, model year 2010 or newer on-road engines, or zero-emission vehicles; [...] Any fleet, fleet portion, or vehicle that is located or operated in a location where the 10th percentile minimum ambient air low temperature in January drops below 20 degrees Fahrenheit (20⁰ F) is exempt from the renewable diesel requirements in section 2449.1(f)(1) solely for the months of November, December, January, and February.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: Cold-weather renewable diesel exemption: report by April 30 or within 2 weeks
rules.plain_english: A fleet that uses the seasonal cold-weather exemption must report its location, the January 10th-percentile low and the fuel volumes to CARB by April 30. A fleet that uses the short cold-snap exemption must report location, fuel volumes and daily temperatures within two weeks after the cold period ends.

submit_to: mail: CARB MSCD (In-Use Off-Road Diesel), P.O. Box 2815, Sacramento, CA 95812

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 56, §2449(g)(5)(A)-(B)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF pages 52-53)
rules.quote: Fleets that use the exemption described in section 2449.1(f)(2)(C) must report to CARB the location of the fleet or fleet operations, the 10th percentile minimum ambient air low temperature in January for that location, and the volumes of renewable diesel and volumes of low temperature-specific diesel procured and used during October, November, December, January, and February, including composition, if known, by April 30 after each period the exemption is used. [...] (B) Fleets that use the exemption described in section 2449.1(f)(2)(D) must report to CARB, within two weeks of the end of such use,
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: No renewable diesel available: document quarterly attempts to buy it
rules.plain_english: If part of a fleet cannot get R99/R100 through its normal fueling, those vehicles may use other diesel only if the fleet keeps records: how it normally fuels, its attempts to get renewable diesel (at least quarterly or whenever vehicles move to a new job site), and proof it was unavailable, such as supplier messages or station maps. Preferring a particular supplier or brand does not count.

parameters.retry_frequency: at least quarterly or when vehicles move to a new job site
records: evidence of inability to procure (fuel provider communications, bids, maps)

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF pages 89-90, §2449.1(f)(3)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF pages 86-87)
rules.quote: If a portion of a fleet is unable to procure R99 or R100 renewable diesel through its normal refueling methods, where a fleet’s preference for a specific distributor or a specific brand is not considered a necessary component of its normal refueling method, those vehicles for which R99 or R100 renewable diesel could not be procured are not required to comply with Section 2449.1(f)(1) if the fleet maintains documentation, [...] (B) A description of the fleet’s attempts to obtain R99 or R100 renewable diesel and continued attempts to obtain R99 or R100 renewable diesel, at a minimum, on a quarterly basis or when vehicles move to a new job site; and
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: Keep renewable diesel purchase records 3 years
rules.plain_english: Keep fuel receipts, purchase orders or fueling contracts showing the date and volume of renewable diesel bought, for three calendar years after each purchase. Also keep the documentation required when R99/R100 could not be obtained.

parameters.also_keep: documentation under 2449.1(f)(3) where R99/R100 could not be procured

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 59, §2449(h)(10)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 55)
rules.quote: These documents must show the date and volumes of fuel purchased and could include receipts of fuel purchases, purchase orders, or fueling contracts. Each fleet owner shall maintain the records required under this provision for three calendar years from the date the transaction is completed.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.
rules.correction: Removed per_vehicle_tracking_required = false and the plain-English sentence 'Records are kept for the fleet, not per vehicle.' Neither 2449(h)(10) nor 2449.1(f) says this. Added also_keep for the 2449.1(f)(3) records that (h)(10) cross-references. The 3-calendar-year retention and the date/volume content are confirmed.

rules.title: Rental contracts must require the renter to use renewable diesel
rules.plain_english: Companies that rent out off-road diesel equipment must put language in the rental contract requiring the renter to follow the renewable diesel rule. With that language, the rental company is not liable for the renter's fuel. If CARB asks, the rental company must give CARB the renter's name and contact information within 5 days.

parameters.clause: renter must comply with 2449.1(f) renewable diesel requirements

rules.applies_to: Rental fleets that rent off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more, and contractors who rent them
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 90, §2449.1(f)(4)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 87)
rules.quote: Fleets that provide for rent vehicles subject to this regulation to other entities must include language in their rental contract that the recipient of the rented vehicle (renter) must comply with the renewable diesel requirements in section 2449.1(f). [...] then the rental fleet must disclose the relevant renter’s company name and business contact information to CARB within 5 days of CARB’s request.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. The text says '5 days', not business days.

rules.title: Permanent low-use vehicle: under 200 hours a year
rules.plain_english: A vehicle designated permanent low-use must run less than 200 hours each calendar year (or, since 2024, average 200 hours or less over three years if used only in California by one owner). It needs a working non-resettable hour meter, is left out of fleet horsepower and the fleet average, but must still be reported, labeled and meet the idling limit and the 2036 Tier 0 ban.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF pages 13-14, §2449(c)(43)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF pages 13-14)
rules.quote: “Permanent low-use vehicle” means a vehicle that a fleet owner has designated as operating less than 200 hours a calendar year, for all years subsequent to the designation. [...] (F) Three-year rolling average – Beginning January 1, 2024, a vehicle operated only in California for three consecutive years and owned by the same owner during that entire period, may be considered permanent low-use if it is operated an average of 200 or fewer hours per year during that consecutive three-year period
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. The year-by-year low-use option ended January 1, 2024 (2449(e)(7)).

rules.title: Low-use vehicles: hour meter reading within 30 days of Jan. 1, with dated photo
rules.plain_english: For each permanent low-use vehicle, report the hour meter reading taken within 30 days of December 31 (January 1 for the first year), and keep a date-stamped photo of the meter (or a signed written log if no camera or military security bars photos).

parameters.alternative: signed, dated written log with EIN and reading

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF pages 53-54, §2449(g)(2)(C)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF pages 49-50)
rules.quote: A date stamped photograph of the engine hour meter at the time of the reading being gathered for reporting must be documented and maintained in accordance with the recordkeeping requirements in section 2449(h). [...] For vehicles that fleet owners intend to designate as permanent low-use vehicles, report one engine hour meter reading that is taken within 30 days of January 1 of the current year. For each year thereafter, report the engine hour meter reading that is taken within 30 days of December 31 of the prior year.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: Primes and public agencies must get the fleet's CARB Certificate before contracting
rules.plain_english: Before signing or renewing a contract with any equipment fleet (and its listed subcontractors) on a project using off-road diesel equipment, the prime contractor or public works awarding body must obtain a copy of the fleet's valid CARB Certificate of Reported Compliance. No valid certificate, no contract.

parameters.obtain_before: entering into a new or renewed contract

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors (and, where stated, public works awarding bodies) on California projects where off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operate and public works awarding bodies
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 59, §2449(i)(1)-(2)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 56)
rules.quote: Beginning January 1, 2024, prime contractors and public works awarding bodies are subject to the requirements in section 2449(i)(1) – (4) below. (1) For a project involving the use of vehicles subject to this regulation, the prime contractor or public works awarding body, as applicable, must obtain copies of the valid Certificates of Reported Compliance, as described in section 2449(n), for the fleet selected for the contract and their listed subcontractors, if applicable, prior to entering into a new or renewed contract with that fleet. (2) No prime contractor or public works awarding body, as applicable, shall enter into a contract with a fleet for which it does not have a valid Certificate of Reported Compliance for the fleet and its listed subcontractors, if applicable, prior to entering into a new or renewed contract with that fleet.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. CARB's booklet and overview fact sheet both restate that neither a prime contractor nor a public works awarding body may award a contract or hire a fleet without a valid Certificate.
rules.correction: verbatim_quote re-based on the Final Regulation Order wording ('a valid Certificate' where the 15-day text had 'a valid Certificates'); source_location now cites the Final Regulation Order. The notes claimed CARB's booklet said a prime need not obtain a certificate from a company with no off-road diesel equipment. The booklet does not say that, and the claim was otherwise sourced only from search excerpts, so it was removed. Parameters confirmed.

rules.title: Keep fleet compliance certificates 3 years after the project ends
rules.plain_english: Prime contractors and public works awarding bodies must keep the Certificates of Reported Compliance they collected for a project for three years after the project is completed, and give them to CARB within five business days if asked.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors (and, where stated, public works awarding bodies) on California projects where off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operate and public works awarding bodies
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 60, §2449(i)(3)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 56)
rules.quote: The Certificates of Reported Compliance received by the prime contractor or public works awarding body, as applicable, for a project must be retained for three years after that project’s completion. Upon request by CARB, these records must be provided to CARB within five business days of the request.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: Emergency projects: no certificate needed, but keep emergency records
rules.plain_english: For true emergency projects, primes and public agencies do not need the fleet certificates, but must keep records showing the equipment was used only for the emergency: a description, the location, the dates, and the fleet's attestation. Routine maintenance or construction is not an emergency.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors (and, where stated, public works awarding bodies) on California projects where off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operate and public works awarding bodies
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 60, §2449(i)(4)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 56)
rules.quote: Situations in which prime contractors or public works awarding bodies, as applicable, are contracting for projects that are considered emergency operations, as defined in section 2449(c)(18), are exempt from the requirements in section 2449(i)(1)-(3), but must still retain records verifying vehicles subject to the regulation that are operating on the emergency operations project are actually being operated on the project for emergency operations only. These records must include a description of the emergency, the address or a description of the specific location of the emergency, the dates on which the emergency operations were performed, and an attestation by the fleet that the vehicles are operated on the project for emergency operations only.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. 2449(c)(18): 'Routine maintenance or construction to prevent public health risks does not constitute emergency operations.'

rules.title: Primes: collect new fleet certificates between March 1 and June 1 each year
rules.plain_english: For every fleet with an ongoing contract on March 1, the prime contractor must collect that fleet's new valid Certificate for the current year between March 1 and June 1. Contracts may not be structured to dodge this.

parameters.applies_to: fleets with an ongoing contract as of March 1

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors (and, where stated, public works awarding bodies) on California projects where off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operate
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 60, §2449(j)(1)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 57)
rules.quote: Between March 1 and June 1 of each year, a prime contractor must collect new valid Certificates of Reported Compliance for the current compliance year, as defined in section 2449(n), from all fleets that have an ongoing contract with the prime contractor as of March 1 of that year. Prime contractors must not write contracts to evade this requirement.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: Primes may allow only certified fleets on their job sites
rules.plain_english: A prime contractor may allow only fleets that hold a valid CARB Certificate of Reported Compliance to work on its job sites.

parameters.allowed_on_site: fleets with valid Certificate of Reported Compliance

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors (and, where stated, public works awarding bodies) on California projects where off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operate
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 60, §2449(j)(2)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 57)
rules.quote: Prime contractors shall only allow fleets with valid Certificates of Reported Compliance on the prime contractor’s job sites.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: Primes must report uncertified fleets or noncompliant machines within 5 business days
rules.plain_english: If a prime contractor finds that a fleet working for it lacks a valid certificate, or sees a noncompliant off-road vehicle on its job site, it must report it to CARB within 5 business days (online complaint form or email), giving the date, the fleet's responsible party, address, email and phone if known, DOORS fleet ID if known, the job site location, and whether it is still operating.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors (and, where stated, public works awarding bodies) on California projects where off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operate
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 60, §2449(j)(3)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 57)
rules.quote: then the prime contractor must report the following information to CARB at https://calepacomplaints.secure.force.com/complaints/Complaint, or email dieselcomplaints@arb.ca.gov, for each fleet without a valid Certificate of Reported Compliance or each noncompliant vehicle, as applicable, within five business days of such discovery:
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. CARB's July 2025 enforcement notice gives the email as diesel.complaints@arb.ca.gov.
rules.correction: verbatim_quote re-based on the Final Regulation Order wording ('five business days' where the 15-day text had '5 business days'); source_location now cites the Final Regulation Order. The 5-business-day deadline, the reporting channels and fields (A)-(H) are unchanged and confirmed. The enforcement notice gives the email as diesel.complaints@arb.ca.gov, while the regulation text gives dieselcomplaints@arb.ca.gov; both are kept as stated.

rules.title: Primes must immediately tell CARB who is responsible for each machine on site
rules.plain_english: When CARB asks, the prime contractor must immediately give CARB the name and contact information of the responsible party for every off-road diesel vehicle on the job site.

parameters.information: name and contact information of each responsible party

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors (and, where stated, public works awarding bodies) on California projects where off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operate
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 61, §2449(j)(4)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 58)
rules.quote: Upon request by CARB, the prime contractor must immediately disclose to CARB the name and contact information of each responsible party for all vehicles subject to this regulation operating at the job site or for the prime contractor.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: Primes must post CARB's off-road regulation sign on jobs lasting 8+ days
rules.plain_english: On any project where off-road diesel equipment will run 8 or more calendar days, the prime contractor must post CARB's sign (exact wording set by the rule) by the 8th calendar day after the first machine starts. Lettering must be larger than 14-point, posted where employee notices go or where employees walk, and where the public can see it if possible. Projects of 7 days or less are exempt.

location: where notices to employees are customarily posted
sections: Who does the In-Use Off-Road Regulation Apply to?

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors (and, where stated, public works awarding bodies) on California projects where off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operate
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 61, §2449(j)(5)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 58)
rules.quote: The prime contractor shall prominently display signage for any project where vehicles subject to this regulation will operate for 8 calendar days or more. The signage must be posted by the eighth calendar day from which the first vehicle operates. The signage will be in lettering larger than size 14-point type and displayed in a conspicuous place where notices to employees are customarily posted at the job site or where there is employee foot traffic. [...] An exemption to this posting requirement is permitted if the operational time of a project is 7 calendar days or less.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. The verbatim sign text is in 2449(j)(5)(A)-(D).
rules.correction: verbatim_quote re-based on the Final Regulation Order wording ('8 calendar days' and '7 calendar days' where the 15-day text spelled out 'eight' and 'seven'); source_location now cites the Final Regulation Order. The 8-day trigger, 8th-day posting deadline, >14-point lettering, 7-day exemption and sign sections (A)-(D) are unchanged and confirmed.

rules.title: Who is a 'prime contractor' under the off-road rule (homeowner jobs excluded)
rules.plain_english: The prime contractor is whoever holds the contract directly with the project owner or awarding authority to oversee all or part of a project where off-road diesel equipment operates. Work under a contract with a homeowner on their own home (not used for business) is excluded.

parameters.excluded: contract with a homeowner for the personal residence not used for business

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors (and, where stated, public works awarding bodies) on California projects where off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operate
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF pages 4-15, §2449(c)(44) and (b)(2)(E)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF pages 4-14)
