rules.quote: (E) Any prime contractor, as defined in section 2449(c)(44), except for work performed pursuant to a contract with a homeowner on the homeowner’s personal residence where the personal residence is not used for any business purpose. [...] “Prime contractor” means the entity that holds the contract for a project directly with the awarding authority or the owner of the project, to oversee all or part of a project in which vehicles subject to this regulation are operated.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. A 'subcontractor' is anyone with a contract with the prime or another sub, not directly with the owner, for work involving these vehicles (2449(c)(57)).

rules.title: Definition: public works awarding body
rules.plain_english: Any California public agency (state, county, city, school board, water district and so on) that awards contracts to build, alter, repair, remove or improve public structures, roads or property. These agencies must also collect fleet certificates.
rules.applies_to: California public agencies that award public works contracts involving off-road diesel vehicles
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 15, §2449(c)(46)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF pages 14-15)
rules.quote: “Public works awarding body” means any public agency (state, county, city, school board, water district, etc.), or official thereof, in the state of California, that awards or enters into a contract for the erection, construction, alteration, repair, removal, or improvement of any public [...] structure, building, road, or other public lands, property, or improvement of any kind.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared.

rules.title: CARB issues a fleet's Certificate of Reported Compliance after reporting
rules.plain_english: CARB gives a fleet its Certificate of Reported Compliance once its initial or annual report and affirmation show it complies. Fleets download it from their DOORS account; primes and agencies can check it with CARB's public lookup tool.
rules.applies_to: Off-road diesel fleets, prime contractors and public works awarding bodies
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF pages 63-64, §2449(n)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 60); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/2025-07/ORD%202022%20Enforcement%20Advisory_1.pdf (p.3)
rules.quote: if the report and affirmation indicates that the fleet is in compliance with the requirements of the Regulation for In-Use Off-Road Diesel-Fueled Fleets, CARB will provide the fleet with a Certificate of Reported Compliance with the Regulation for In-Use Off-Road Diesel-Fueled Fleets.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. The public lookup URL is from CARB's July 21, 2025 enforcement notice; the DOORS download from CARB's Nov. 2025 booklet ('Fleets may download this Certificate from their DOORS profile').

rules.title: EPA authorized the 2022 off-road amendments on Jan. 10, 2025; CARB enforcement discretion until at least Oct. 21, 2025
rules.plain_english: EPA authorized CARB to enforce all of the 2022 off-road amendments on January 10, 2025. CARB enforced the new adding-vehicle limits from January 11, 2025. For the tier phase-out, low-use and contractor requirements, CARB said it would consider using its discretion to emphasize education and outreach until at least October 21, 2025. No source read says when that ended, so plan on full enforcement.
rules.applies_to: Off-road diesel fleets, prime contractors and public works awarding bodies
rules.citation: CARB Enforcement Notice, July 21, 2025 (2022 ORD amendments)
rules.quote: On January 10, 2025, the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency granted authorization to CARB to enforce all provisions of the 2022 Off-Road Regulation amendments. [...] To facilitate compliance with the tier phase-out, low-Use designations, and contracting and prime contracting requirements, CARB will consider exercising its discretion and emphasizing education and outreach until at least October 21, 2025. [...] Starting January 11, 2025, CARB began enforcement of the expanded adding vehicles requirement on fleets. [...] Prime contractors must report observed non-compliance to CARB within five business days at: https://calepacomplaints.secure.force.com/complaints/Complaint, or by email: diesel.complaints@arb.ca.gov.
rules.notes: Official CARB enforcement notice. No later CARB notice extending the discretion period was found; CARB HTML pages could not be read (rate-limit page).
rules.correction: Title changed: it said enforcement discretion 'ended Oct. 2025', but the notice says CARB 'will consider exercising its discretion ... until at least October 21, 2025'. Nothing read states when discretion ended, and CARB's HTML pages returned HTTP 419. All four date parameters are confirmed against the notice. Review 2026-11-25: added report_email_in_notice: the July 2025 notice gives diesel.complaints@arb.ca.gov, while 2449(j)(3) and the (j)(5) sign text give dieselcomplaints@arb.ca.gov; the web form address is the same in both. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: Zero-emission alternate path (ZETA): 15% ZEV hp by 2030, 50% by 2035
rules.plain_english: A compliant fleet may apply to CARB (Zero-Emission Technology Application) for relief from the phase-out and fleet-average rules if it commits to replacing at least 15% of its total horsepower with zero-emission equipment by January 1, 2030 and 50% by January 1, 2035.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/2024-02/overview_fact_sheet_sept_2023-final.pdf (PDF page 11, p.11 'Alternate Compliance Pathway Zero Emission Technology')
rules.quote: an approved application will require a fleet to, at a minimum, remove from the fleet at least 15 percent of the fleets total hp and replace it with ZEV or technology that creates zero-combustion emissions at the job site by January 1, 2030, and 50 percent by January 1, 2035.
rules.notes: From CARB's official overview fact sheet (rev. January 2024); Confirmed against the adopted text: Final Regulation Order 2449.1(e)(2)(B)1.-2. (at least 15 percent of total horsepower by January 1, 2030 and 50 percent by January 1, 2035), followed instead of 2449.1(a), (b) and (c).

rules.title: Off-road rule violations: civil or criminal penalties under the Health and Safety Code
rules.plain_english: Failing to meet the off-road rule, failing to report, or filing false information can bring civil or criminal penalties under Health and Safety Code sections 39674 and following. CARB weighs willfulness, how long the violation lasted, good-faith effort and size of the violation.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including renters) of self-propelled off-road diesel vehicles of 25 hp or more operated in California; prime contractors; awarding bodies
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/froa-1.pdf (Final Regulation Order, PDF page 63, §2449(m)); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/barcu/regact/2022/off-roaddiesel/ord15dayatta-1.pdf (15-Day Modified Text, PDF page 60)
rules.quote: Any person who fails to comply with the performance requirements of this regulation, who fails to submit any information, report, or statement required by this regulation, or who knowingly submits any false statement or representation in any application, report, statement, or other document filed, maintained, or used for the purposes of compliance with this regulation may be subject to civil or criminal penalties under sections 39674, 39675, 42400, 42400.1, 42400.2, 42400.3.5, 42402, 42402.1, 42402.2, 42402.4, 42403, 43016, 43027, 43028, 43029, and 43030 of the Health and Safety Code.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order for the 2022 Off-Road amendments (Attachment A-1, froa-1.pdf, PDF created Aug. 17, 2023; amendments shown against the prior regulation, struck-out deletions removed). The 15-Day Modified Text (April 10, 2023) carries the same passage. The amendments took effect October 1, 2023 and EPA authorized them January 10, 2025 (CARB enforcement notice, July 21, 2025). The OAL-published CCR edition was not compared. The per-day dollar amounts in those Health and Safety Code sections could not be read (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov blocked), so no amounts are given.

rules.title: Truck and Bus rule covers diesel vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR
rules.plain_english: CARB's Truck and Bus regulation applies to diesel (and dual-fuel or alternative diesel) trucks and buses with a manufacturer's gross vehicle weight rating over 14,000 pounds that run in California, whether owned, leased or rented, and to people selling them. Not covered (2025(c)): emergency and military tactical vehicles, off-road vehicles, dedicated snow-removal vehicles, historic vehicles, motor homes for non-commercial private use, personal-use pickups of 19,500 lb or less, solid waste collection and public transit vehicles under their own rules, municipal vehicles that meet the public agency fleet rule (13 CCR 2022.1) BACT requirements, and two-engine cranes, drill rigs and workover rigs that are under the off-road rule.

excluded: motor homes for non-commercial private use
pickups 19,500 lbs GVWR or less used only for personal use
vehicles owned or operated by a municipality (13 CCR 2020(b)) that comply with the BACT requirements of 13 CCR 2022.1(a)(1)
vehicles subject to the solid waste collection vehicle rule (13 CCR 2021)
vehicles subject to the public transit agency fleet rule (13 CCR 2023)
two-engine on-road vehicles subject to 13 CCR 2449 (cranes, water well drilling rigs, workover rigs), except two-engine sweepers

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of diesel trucks and buses over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California (dump trucks, water trucks, concrete mixers, boom trucks and similar)
rules.quote: Affected vehicles are those that operate on diesel-fuel, dual-fuel, or alternative diesel-fuel that are registered to be driven on public highways, were originally designed to be driven on public highways whether or not they are registered, yard trucks with on-road engines or yard trucks with off-road engines used for agricultural operations, both engines of two-engine sweepers, schoolbuses, and have a manufacturer’s gross vehicle weight rating (GVWR) greater than 14,000 pounds (lbs). [...] (1) Vehicles subject to the solid waste collection vehicle rule commencing with title 13, CCR, section 2021; [...] (2) Vehicles owned or operated by a municipality, as defined in title 13, section 2020(b), that comply with the Best Available Control Technology (BACT) requirements of title 13, CCR, section 2022.1(a)(1); [...] (3) Vehicles subject to the fleet rule for public transit agencies commencing with title 13, CCR, section 2023; [...] (8) Dedicated snow-removal vehicles as defined in section 2025(d)(15); [...] (10) Motor homes for non-commercial private use; [...] (13) Except for two-engine sweepers, other two-engine on-road vehicles that are subject to title 13, CCR, section 2449, including but not limited to, water well drilling rigs, workover rigs, and cranes, in which one engine provides the motive power for the vehicle and a second engine is an auxiliary engine 50 horsepower or greater that is integrated into the design of the vehicle and provides power for the vehicle to perform a specialized function.
rules.notes: Text from CARB's Final Regulation Order PDF for 13 CCR 2025 hosted at ww2.arb.ca.gov (post-2011 amendments, before the voided 2014 amendments). The 2014 amendment attachment and current OAL text could not be read (CARB 419 page).
rules.correction: Review 2026-11-25: the excluded list left out five 2025(c) exemptions that the text states (solid waste (c)(1), municipal vehicles meeting 13 CCR 2022.1(a)(1) BACT (c)(2), public transit (c)(3), dedicated snow-removal (c)(8), two-engine on-road cranes, water well drilling rigs and workover rigs subject to 13 CCR 2449 (c)(13)); added them, quoted 2025(c)(1)-(3), (8), (10), (13) and extended plain_english.

rules.title: Diesel trucks over 14,000 lb must have a 2010 or newer engine (since Jan. 1, 2023)
rules.plain_english: Since January 1, 2023, almost every diesel truck and bus over 14,000 lb GVWR operating in California must have a 2010 or newer model-year engine (or 2010-equivalent emissions). Only low-use (under 1,000 miles a year) and NOx-exempt-area vehicles remain as exceptions.

remaining_flexibility: NOx exempt area with PM filter
compliance_paths: 2010 model year or newer engine (replace the engine or the vehicle)
VDECS retrofit that achieves 2010 model year equivalent emissions

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of diesel trucks and buses over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California (dump trucks, water trucks, concrete mixers, boom trucks and similar)
rules.quote: By January 1, 2023, affected diesel-powered trucks, and buses must have a 2010 or newer model year engine with few exceptions. [...] (1) Except as provided in (3) below, all vehicles with a GVWR 26,000 lbs or less must be equipped with a 2010 model year emission equivalent engine pursuant to the following schedule in Table 1: [...] A fleet may meet the 2010 model year emissions equivalent engine requirement by replacing the engine or vehicle with one with a 2010 model year engine or later, retrofitting the engine with a VDECS that achieves 2010 model year equivalent emissions, or by replacing a vehicle with one that has a future compliance deadline.
rules.notes: CARB Truck and Bus Compliance Overview (last updated March 16, 2023). The phase-in tables (Table 1 for 26,000 lb GVWR or less, Table 2 for over 26,000 lb) are in the regulation order 2025(f)(1) and (g)(1).
rules.correction: Review 2026-11-25: schedule_lighter_26000_or_less keys were bare years ('2015'); Table 1's column is 'Compliance Date as of January 1', so they are now ISO dates ('2015-01-01'). Added compliance_paths from 2025(g): a VDECS achieving 2010 model year equivalent emissions also meets the requirement.

rules.title: Anyone who hires or dispatches diesel trucks must verify Truck and Bus compliance
rules.plain_english: A motor carrier, California broker, or any California resident (including a contractor) who hires or directs a diesel truck over 14,000 lb must check that each hired truck complies, for example by keeping a copy of the fleet's CARB Certificate of Reported Compliance, and keep bills of lading or other records showing who hired or dispatched which vehicle.

who: California resident who operates or directs operation
parameters.proof: copy of Certificate of Reported Compliance with the In-Use On-Road Diesel Vehicle Regulation (at business or in vehicle)
parameters.records: bills of lading and other documents identifying the motor carrier or broker and the vehicle dispatched

rules.applies_to: Contractors, brokers and motor carriers in California who hire or dispatch diesel trucks over 14,000 lb GVWR (e.g., haul and dump trucks)
rules.quote: Any in-state or out-of-state motor carrier, California broker, or any California resident who operates or directs the operation of any vehicle subject to this regulation shall verify that each hired or dispatched vehicle is in compliance with the regulation and comply with the record keeping requirements of section 2025(s)(4). (3) Compliance may be accomplished by keeping at the business location, a copy of the Certificate of Reported Compliance with the In-Use On-Road Diesel Vehicle Regulation for each fleet, or in the vehicle.
rules.notes: Records in 2025(s)(4)(A): 'Bills of lading and other documentation identifying the motor carrier or broker who hired or dispatched the vehicle and the vehicle dispatched.'

rules.title: Truck leases must say who is responsible for Truck and Bus compliance
rules.plain_english: Any truck lease effective January 1, 2010 or later must clearly state whether the leased truck is excluded from the lessor's fleet during the lease; otherwise compliance is the lessee's responsibility.
rules.applies_to: Lessors and lessees of diesel trucks over 14,000 lb GVWR
rules.quote: Any contract that a lessor and lessee enter into that has an effective date of January 1, 2010 or later shall clearly specify whether or not the leased vehicle is to be excluded from the lessor’s fleet for the duration of the lease, or the responsibility will be that of the lessee.

rules.title: Truck bill of sale must carry CARB's on-road diesel disclosure
rules.plain_english: A California seller of a diesel truck over 14,000 lb must give the buyer CARB's written disclosure on the bill of sale, sales contract addendum or invoice. Dealers keep a record of it for three years.

parameters.text: An on-road heavy-duty diesel or alternative-diesel vehicle operated in California may be subject to the California Air Resources Board Regulation to Reduce Particulate Matter and Criteria Pollutant Emissions from In-Use Heavy-Duty Diesel Vehicles. It therefore could be subject to exhaust retrofit or accelerated turnover requirements to reduce emissions of air pollutants. For more information, please visit the California Air Resources Board website at http://www.arb.ca.gov/dieseltruck.

rules.applies_to: California residents selling diesel trucks over 14,000 lb GVWR
rules.quote: Any person residing in California selling a vehicle with an engine subject to this regulation must provide the following disclosure in writing to the buyer on the bill of sale, sales contract addendum, or invoice, “An on-road heavy-duty diesel or alternative-diesel vehicle operated in California may be subject to the California Air Resources Board Regulation to Reduce Particulate Matter and Criteria Pollutant Emissions from In-Use Heavy-Duty Diesel Vehicles.

rules.title: Truck low-use exemption: under 1,000 California miles a year
rules.plain_english: A truck driven less than 1,000 miles a year in California can keep running without the 2010-engine upgrade if it is reported each January (by January 31, or within 30 days of purchase) with odometer readings. If the engine or PTO powers stationary equipment (drill rig, concrete pump), it must also run less than 100 hours a year.

parameters.hour_limit_applies_to: vehicles powering stationary-only equipment (e.g., drill rig, concrete pump)
parameters.report_by: January 31 of the compliance year or within 30 days of purchase

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of diesel trucks and buses over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California (dump trucks, water trucks, concrete mixers, boom trucks and similar)
rules.quote: This option applies to vehicles that operate less than 1,000 miles per calendar year in California. [...] In addition, the engine or power take off must be operated less than 100 hours per year to qualify for the low-use exemption if the vehicle is designed to power other equipment that can only be used while stationary, like a drill rig or a concrete pump. [...] You must report vehicle information, odometer readings, and hour meter readings if applicable by January 31 of the compliance year or within 30 days of purchasing a vehicle.
rules.notes: CARB Truck and Bus Low-Use Vehicle Exemption fact sheet (last updated September 25, 2019). The 100-hour limit does not apply where the engine only loads/unloads cargo (e.g., dump trucks) or the vehicle is mobile while powering equipment (e.g., water trucks).

rules.title: Truck NOx exempt areas: trucks with PM filters that stay in 22 rural counties
rules.plain_english: Trucks that have a diesel particulate filter and operate only in the listed rural counties ('NOx exempt areas') do not need to be replaced. They must be reported each January (or within 30 days of purchase) and marked 'NE' on both doors (3-inch white letters on a 5 x 8 inch black background) unless tracked by GPS. They may leave the NOx exempt areas only for repairs or other service to the vehicle, with a work order from the facility that describes the service and shows its date and the facility's location.

parameters.may_leave_area_only_for: repairs or other services, with a dated work order from the facility

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of diesel trucks and buses over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California (dump trucks, water trucks, concrete mixers, boom trucks and similar)
rules.citation: 13 CCR 2025(d)(46), (p)(1); CARB NOx Exempt Area Extensions fact sheet (2019)
rules.quote: The following counties (shown in the darkly shaded areas) make up the NOx Exempt Areas: Alpine, Colusa, Del Norte, Glenn, Humboldt, Lake, Lassen, Mendocino, Modoc, Monterey, Northern Sonoma, Plumas, San Benito, San Luis Obispo, Santa Barbara, Santa Cruz, Shasta, Sierra, Siskiyou, Tehama, Trinity, and Yuba. [...] vehicles that are designated as NOx Exempt, must have permanently affixed or painted labels on the left and right door with the letters “NE” in three inch white block letters on a five inch by eight inch black background, unless the owner chooses to comply by using a vehicle location tracking system. [...] (D) Vehicles that use the NOx exempt areas exemptions may travel outside of the designated NOx exempt areas only for repairs or other services to the vehicle. The vehicle owner must obtain a work order from the facility that describes the service and it must show the date of the service and the location of the facility.
rules.notes: CARB NOx Exempt Area Extensions fact sheet (last updated June 27, 2019).
rules.correction: Review 2026-11-25: added the travel restriction of 2025(p)(1)(D) (outside the NOx exempt areas only for repairs or service, with a dated work order) and the regulation text as a source; citation now names 2025(d)(46) and (p)(1) (the rule previously cited only 2025(p)). Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: Truck and Bus records: give to CARB within 5 business days
rules.plain_english: Truck fleet owners must keep the required records and give them to CARB within five business days of a request.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of diesel trucks and buses over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California (dump trucks, water trucks, concrete mixers, boom trucks and similar)
rules.quote: The owner shall provide these records to an agent or employee of the ARB within five business days upon request.

rules.title: Truck and Bus violations: civil or criminal penalties
rules.plain_english: Failing to comply, failing to report, or filing false statements under the Truck and Bus rule can bring civil or criminal penalties under Health and Safety Code sections 39674 and following.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of diesel trucks and buses over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California (dump trucks, water trucks, concrete mixers, boom trucks and similar)
rules.quote: Any person who fails to comply with the general requirements of this regulation, who fails to submit any information, report, or statement required by this regulation, or who knowingly submits any false statement or representation in any application, report, statement, or other document filed, maintained, or used for the purposes of compliance with this regulation may be subject to civil or criminal penalties under sections 39674, 39675, 42400, 42400.1, 42400.2, 42402.2, and 43016, of the Health and Safety Code.
rules.notes: Statutory dollar amounts not read (leginfo blocked).

rules.title: DMV checks Truck and Bus compliance before registering diesel vehicles over 14,000 lb (since 2020)
rules.plain_english: Since 2020 the DMV checks that a diesel truck or bus over 14,000 lb GVWR meets CARB's Truck and Bus rule (or is exempt) before it will register it, on a schedule by model year and weight; all 2010-and-older model years were covered by January 1, 2023. CARB can also put a DMV registration hold on a vehicle that is out of compliance.

parameters.statute_unverified: SB 1 (2017) / Vehicle Code 4000.15 (statute text not read)

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of diesel trucks and buses over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California (dump trucks, water trucks, concrete mixers, boom trucks and similar)
rules.citation: CARB FAQ 'CARB Truck Rule Compliance Required for DMV Registration' (2020); 13 CCR 2025; statute (reported as SB 1 of 2017, Vehicle Code 4000.15) not read
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/truckstop/pdfs/sb1_faqeng.pdf (PDF page 1, schedule tables and 'What if I am currently out of compliance')
rules.quote: As of 2020, DMV will check compliance with the regulation in order to register your vehicle based on the following schedule: [...] CARB can place a DMV registration hold on your vehicle now if it does not meet current regulatory requirements.
rules.notes: CARB FAQ PDF on DMV registration (created Feb. 6, 2020), re-fetched 2026-11-25 from ww2.arb.ca.gov. The FAQ does not name the statute. The SB 1 / Vehicle Code 4000.15 attribution comes from search excerpts only, because leginfo.legislature.ca.gov was not used, the CARB SB 1 fact sheet (2019-04) returned HTTP 419, and atrn.assembly.ca.gov is outside the allowed hosts. Schedule rows: lighter vehicles (14,001-26,000 lb GVWR) and heavier vehicles (>26,000 lb GVWR) by vehicle model year.

It is now verified against an official CARB PDF, the FAQ 'CARB Truck Rule Compliance Required for DMV Registration', fetched fresh. source_location, verbatim_quote, read_from_primary_text (false to true), effective (2020-01-01), title, plain_english and citation were updated. Parameters now include the DMV verification schedule from the FAQ tables and the CARB registration hold. The statute name and number (SB 1, Vehicle Code 4000.15) remain unverified and are labelled so.

rules.title: Clean Truck Check covers all non-gasoline vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR
rules.plain_english: California's Clean Truck Check (heavy-duty inspection and maintenance) program applies to every non-gasoline heavy-duty vehicle (over 14,000 lb GVWR) operating in California and its owner and operator, plus freight contractors and brokers who hire them. Zero-emission vehicles, authorized emergency vehicles and military tactical vehicles are excluded.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California
rules.quote: All non-gasoline heavy-duty vehicles operating in California and the owners and operators of such vehicles. [...] “Heavy-duty vehicle” means any motor vehicle having a manufacturer's GVWR greater than 14,000 pounds.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page). Unverified: search excerpts (trade press) report that on January 27, 2026 EPA disapproved applying the program to out-of-state trucks.

rules.title: Clean Truck Check compliance: fee paid, vehicle reported, passing test, no open citations or recalls
rules.plain_english: CARB deems a heavy-duty vehicle compliant (within 72 hours) only when the owner has paid the annual compliance fee, reported owner and vehicle information, submitted a passing emissions test, and has no outstanding enforcement actions or emissions/OBD recalls on the vehicle.

conditions: compliance fee paid
owner and vehicle info reported
passing periodic emissions test
no outstanding enforcement actions
no outstanding emissions/OBD recalls

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California
rules.quote: The Executive Officer shall deem a vehicle compliant within 72 hours with the HD I/M Regulation upon finding all the following conditions are met: [...] (2) The owner has reported to CARB the owner and vehicle information required under section 2197.2(b). (3) The owner has demonstrated compliance with the periodic vehicle emission testing requirements by submitting a passing compliance test as specified in section 2196.2. (4) The owner has no outstanding enforcement actions on the vehicle in question. (5) The owner has no outstanding emissions or OBD-related recalls on the vehicle in question.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page).

rules.title: Clean Truck Check tests: twice a year at first, then 4 times a year for OBD trucks
rules.plain_english: Most heavy-duty vehicles must pass an emissions test twice per compliance year during the first three years of periodic testing. Three years after periodic testing took effect (CARB's fact sheet says 2028), trucks with on-board diagnostics (OBD) move to four tests a year. OBD-equipped means a 2013 or newer diesel or diesel hybrid engine, or a 2018 or newer alternative-fuel or alternative-fuel hybrid engine, with an OBD system. Motor homes and agricultural vehicles test once a year.

parameters.quarterly_start: 3 years after the effective date of 13 CCR 2196.2 (see air-ctc-periodic-testing-start)

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California
rules.quote: (1) Motor homes registered in California and agricultural vehicles shall be subject to an annual compliance deadline. (2) For the first three years of periodic vehicle emission testing requirements specified in section 2196.2, all vehicles other than those specified in (1) shall be subject to semi-annual compliance deadlines. (3) Three years following the effective date of periodic vehicle emission testing requirements specified in section 2196.2, an OBD-equipped vehicle other than those specified in (1) shall be subject to quarterly compliance deadlines. [...] “OBD-equipped vehicle” means a heavy-duty vehicle for the following model years and fuel types equipped with an OBD system: (1) Model year 2013 and newer diesel engines; (2) Model year 2013 and newer diesel hybrid engines; (3) Model year 2018 and newer alternative fuel engines; and (4) Model year 2018 and newer alternative fuel hybrid engines.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page). CARB's Periodic Testing Requirements fact sheet (March 13, 2024; read) says periodic testing is effective October 1, 2024 and that 'Three years after the start of Clean Truck Check periodic emissions testing (2028), on board diagnostics (OBD) equipped vehicles will be required to undergo testing four times per year.' A search excerpt of a later CARB web page gives October 2027 instead (not read). Treat the exact quarterly start as unconfirmed beyond the regulation's 'three years following' rule.
rules.correction: The notes said the fact sheet was not read and estimated a quarterly start of about October 1, 2027. CARB's March 13, 2024 fact sheet (official PDF, now read) confirms the 2024-10-01 effective date and gives '(2028)' for quarterly OBD testing. Added quarterly_start_year_per_carb_fact_sheet = 2028, added the fact sheet to source_location and rewrote the notes. The 2, 3, 4 and 1 tests-per-year values are confirmed in §2196.1(d). Review 2026-11-25: added obd_equipped_from_model_year from the 2195.1 definition of 'OBD-equipped vehicle' (diesel MY2013+, alternative fuel MY2018+), so the quarterly-testing class can be read from the engine model year. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: Clean Truck Check periodic emissions testing took effect Oct. 1, 2024
rules.plain_english: CARB made Clean Truck Check periodic compliance testing effective October 1, 2024 for all vehicles operating in California. A passing test may be submitted no more than 90 days before a compliance deadline; for example, a vehicle with a January 1, 2025 deadline could submit a test from October 1, 2024.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California
rules.citation: 13 CCR 2195(d), 2196.2; CARB Clean Truck Check Periodic Testing Requirements fact sheet (Mar. 13, 2024)
rules.source: https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/2022-11/factsheet_periodic_hdim_testing_requirements.pdf (PDF page 1, 'How will I know when periodic testing begins?'); also https://ww2.arb.ca.gov/sites/default/files/2023-02/a_1_final_regulation_order_hdvip_psip.pdf (PDF page 4, §2195(d))
rules.quote: Clean Truck Check periodic compliance testing requirements for all vehicles that operate in California are effective October 1, 2024. For example, a vehicle with a compliance deadline of January 1, 2025, may submit a passing emissions test as early as October 1, 2024. Vehicles may submit tests no more than 90 days prior to the vehicle’s compliance deadlines.
rules.notes: CARB Clean Truck Check Periodic Testing Requirements fact sheet (dated March 13, 2024; PDF re-fetched 2026-11-25). The regulation (13 CCR 2195(d)) leaves the date to a Notice Register/website notice, no earlier than January 1, 2024. A later CARB FAQ reported in search excerpts says the first deadline was January 1, 2025; the FAQ (HTML) returned HTTP 419 and was not read, so no 'first deadline' parameter is given.
rules.correction: The rule was unverifiable (source not readable). It is now verified against CARB's official Periodic Testing Requirements fact sheet PDF, fetched fresh. periodic_testing_effective 2024-10-01 is confirmed. first_test_deadlines_from 2025-01-01 was removed because the fact sheet gives January 1, 2025 only as an example deadline. It was replaced with early_test_submission_window_days = 90, the example, and the regulation floor from §2195(d). source_location, verbatim_quote, read_from_primary_text (false to true), title, plain_english, citation and notes were updated.

rules.title: Clean Truck Check deadlines follow the DMV registration date
rules.plain_english: For California-registered trucks the compliance year runs from the DMV registration expiration date. Twice-a-year deadlines fall on that day in months 6 and 12; quarterly deadlines in months 3, 6, 9 and 12. For vehicles registered outside California or exempt from DMV registration, the compliance year starts and ends on the last day of a month set by the last digit of the VIN: 0 October, 1 November, 2 December, 3 January, 4 February, 5 March, 6 April, 7 May, 8 June, 9 July.

parameters.compliance_year_anchor: DMV registration expiration day and month (CA-registered)
parameters.short_month_rule: last day of month if the day does not exist
parameters.non_ca_registered: based on last digit of VIN

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California
rules.quote: Semiannual deadlines occur on a vehicle’s compliance year expiration day in months six and twelve of each compliance year with the deadline in month twelve being the final day of a vehicle’s compliance year. [...] Quarterly deadlines occur on a vehicle’s compliance year expiration day in months three, six, nine, and twelve of each compliance year [...] For California-registered vehicles, the start and end date of every compliance year shall align with the day and month of a vehicle’s DMV [...] registration expiration date. [...] The compliance year for a non-California registered vehicle and vehicles exempt from DMV registration shall be determined based on the vehicle’s VIN. The compliance year shall begin and end on the last day of the month specified below based on the last number of a vehicle’s VIN, as shown in the table below. 0 October 1 November 2 December 3 January 4 February 5 March 6 April 7 May 8 June 9 July
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page).
rules.correction: Review 2026-11-25: added the VIN table of 2195.1 'Compliance year' (1) (last VIN digit -> month whose last day starts and ends the compliance year) for vehicles registered outside California or exempt from DMV registration. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: A Clean Truck Check test within 90 days before a deadline counts to the next deadline
rules.plain_english: If you pass the test within 90 days before your upcoming deadline, the truck is compliant through the following deadline. Testing more than 90 days early only covers you up to the upcoming deadline.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California
rules.quote: If a vehicle owner demonstrates vehicle compliance within 90 calendar days or less of the vehicle’s immediate upcoming compliance deadline, the Executive Officer shall deem a vehicle compliant with the HD I/M Regulation up to the vehicle’s subsequent compliance deadline as long as the additional conditions specified in section 2196.1(b) are met.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page).

rules.title: Clean Truck Check annual compliance fee: $30 base, adjusted yearly for inflation
rules.plain_english: Each registered heavy-duty vehicle owes CARB an annual compliance fee before its first compliance for the year. The regulation set it at $30.00 and CARB adjusts it each year by the California Consumer Price Index, publishing the new amount by July 1.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California
rules.quote: The Executive Officer shall assess a compliance fee of $30.00 to the vehicle owner for each registered vehicle prior to the first demonstration of compliance for a vehicle in a given compliance year. The Executive Officer shall adjust the compliance fee annually based on the California Consumer Price Index (CCPI) as updated by the Department of Industrial Relations and shall publish the adjusted compliance fee by July 1st of each year on CARB’s website.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page). Search excerpts of CARB's fee pages report $31.18 for 2025 and $32.13 for deadlines on and after January 1, 2026, with a 2027 update page; those pages could not be read, so the current amount is left null.

rules.title: DMV registration requires Clean Truck Check compliance within 90 days before renewal
rules.plain_english: CARB tells the DMV a heavy-duty vehicle is compliant for registration only if all compliance conditions were met within 90 days before the registration date. Without it, registration can be held.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California
rules.quote: The Executive Officer shall notify the DMV a vehicle has been deemed compliant by CARB with the HD I/M Regulation for registration purposes if compliance with section 2196.1(b)(1) through (b)(5) has been demonstrated for the vehicle within 90 calendar days in advance of the registration date.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page).

rules.title: Buying a used heavy truck: compliance must be within the last 90 days; new trucks 30 days
rules.plain_english: When a heavy-duty vehicle changes owner or registration in California, the new owner must make sure compliance was demonstrated within the 90 days before the transfer. A buyer of a brand-new vehicle has 30 days after purchase to report and pay (no test needed).
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California
rules.quote: Upon a transfer of ownership or registration in California, the new owner shall demonstrate compliance by ensuring the requirements of section 2196.1(b)(1) through (b)(5) have been met for the vehicle within the last 90 calendar days in advance of the transfer date. [...] (2) Upon transfer of ownership of a new motor vehicle as defined in Health and Safety Code section 39042 to an ultimate purchaser, the new owner shall demonstrate compliance within 30 calendar days of the vehicle purchase
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page).

rules.title: Hiring heavy trucks: only use Clean Truck Check-compliant vehicles and keep proof 5 years
rules.plain_english: Anyone (other than a broker) who contracts for heavy-duty vehicles to operate in California, such as a contractor hiring haul trucks, must use only compliant vehicles or fleets, and keep for each hired truck either a copy of its compliance certificate valid at dispatch or the fleet's Affirmation of Fleet Wide Compliance dated within 12 months. Keep records 5 years and produce them within 72 hours.

proof_options: HD I/M compliance certificate valid at time of dispatch
Affirmation of Fleet Wide Compliance dated within 12 months, obtained before contract

rules.applies_to: Freight contractors: any person, other than a broker, who contracts for heavy-duty vehicles to operate in California (including construction firms hiring trucking)
rules.quote: Any freight contractor shall only contract with compliant vehicles or fleets and comply with the recordkeeping requirements specified in section 2197.3(b). [...] (A) A copy of the vehicle’s HD I/M compliance certificate, valid at the time of dispatch, for each vehicle dispatched to, from, or within California; or (B) An Affirmation of Fleet Wide Compliance for the fleet dispatching vehicles to California to which the vehicle belongs. [...] 2. Dated within 12 months of the date the vehicle is contracted by the freight contractor.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page). 'Freight contractor' means 'any person, excluding a broker, who enters into a contract with any party requiring the operation of a heavy-duty vehicle within California.' Section 2197 took effect on a date CARB announced (no earlier than July 1, 2023 per 2195(d)); that date was not read.

rules.title: Clean Truck Check records: keep 5 years, produce within 72 hours
rules.plain_english: Unless a section says otherwise, records required by Clean Truck Check must be kept at least five years and given to CARB staff, inspectors or police within 72 hours of a written or verbal request.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California; freight contractors and brokers
rules.quote: Unless otherwise specified, affected entities shall retain the specified records for a minimum of five years from date of entry, and shall provide them to CARB staff, inspectors, or peace officers within 72 hours of official written or oral request.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page).

rules.title: Clean Truck Check Five-Day Pass: once a year per vehicle, apply 7 business days ahead
rules.plain_english: An owner bringing a noncompliant heavy truck into California for a short job can ask CARB for a Five-Day Pass to operate up to five consecutive days. It is available once per calendar year per vehicle; apply at least seven business days before entry and keep the pass in the truck.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California
rules.quote: Prior to operating in California, a vehicle owner may obtain written approval from the Executive Officer to operate a vehicle for up to five consecutive calendar days without being subject to the requirements of section 2196(a)(1) and (a)(2). [...] Vehicle owners are eligible to apply for a Five-Day Pass prior to travelling to California once per calendar year per vehicle. The vehicle owner shall submit an application for a Five-Day Pass to the Executive Officer at least seven business days prior to the vehicle’s planned travel or entry in California
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page).

rules.title: Do not operate heavy trucks with tampered or defective emission controls
rules.plain_english: Owners may not run a heavy-duty vehicle in California with tampered or defective emission control parts, improperly installed aftermarket parts, or (for 1974 and newer) without meeting the emission standards on its legible emission label.

prohibited: tampered or defective emission control components
improperly installed aftermarket parts
1974+ vehicle not meeting federal standards per legible emission control label

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California
rules.quote: Not operate any vehicle in California with tampered or defective emission control components.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page).

rules.title: Clean Truck Check violations: penalties under the Health and Safety Code
rules.plain_english: Violating Clean Truck Check, misreporting, or filing false statements can bring penalties under Health and Safety Code Division 26, Parts 2 and 5. Blaming the driver, owner or freight contractor does not reduce the penalty.

parameters.statutes: Health and Safety Code Division 26, Parts 2 and 5

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of non-gasoline (diesel and other) heavy-duty vehicles over 14,000 lb GVWR operated in California; freight contractors and brokers
rules.quote: may be subject to penalties under Health and Safety Code, Division 26, Parts 2 and 5. Evidence of fault on the part of the registered owner, vehicle operator, freight contractor, or other entity shall not be considered a mitigating circumstance for assessing penalties.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's Final Regulation Order, Heavy-Duty Vehicle Inspection and Maintenance Program (Attachment A-1, posted February 2023). Later amendments, if any, were not read (CARB HTML pages returned a rate-limit page). Dollar amounts not read (leginfo blocked); search excerpts mention up to $10,000 per day, unverified.

rules.title: Advanced Clean Fleets (as of Sept. 10, 2026) covers only state and local government fleets
rules.plain_english: CARB's amended Advanced Clean Fleets regulation, effective September 10, 2026, applies to state and local government agencies' vehicles over 8,500 lb GVWR (and to anyone hiring those fleets). It no longer contains zero-emission purchase rules for private contractors' truck fleets.

parameters.covered_fleets: state or local government agencies with jurisdiction in California

rules.applies_to: Private construction fleets (status check) and public agencies operating vehicles over 8,500 lb GVWR
rules.quote: Unofficial electronic version of the Advanced Clean Fleets regulation, effective September 10, 2026 [...] This article applies to any state or local government agency with jurisdiction in California that owns, leases, rents, contracts for the operation of, or operates one or more vehicles specified in section 2013(a)(2) in California on or after September 10, 2026. This article does not apply to federal fleets.
rules.notes: CARB's unofficial version of the Final Regulation Order approved by OAL September 10, 2026; it contains only Article 3.2 (state and local government fleets) and Article 8 (2049, hiring compliant fleets). Private fleets remain subject to Truck and Bus and Clean Truck Check.

rules.title: Diesel trucks over 10,000 lb may not idle more than 5 minutes
rules.plain_english: No diesel commercial vehicle over 10,000 lb GVWR may idle more than five minutes in a row anywhere in California, and a diesel auxiliary power unit may not run more than five minutes within 100 feet of homes, schools, hospitals and similar places. This binds owners, drivers and the companies that dispatch them. Pickup trucks as defined in Vehicle Code 471, and zero-emission vehicles, are not commercial motor vehicles under this rule.

not_commercial_motor_vehicles: pickup trucks as defined in Vehicle Code section 471

rules.applies_to: Owners, operators and dispatching motor carriers of diesel commercial vehicles over 10,000 lb GVWR in California
rules.quote: diesel-fueled commercial motor vehicles that operate in the State of California with gross vehicle weight ratings of greater than 10,000 pounds that are or must be licensed for operation on highways. [...] 1. No vehicle subject to this section shall idle for more than 5 consecutive minutes at any location. 2. No diesel-fueled APS subject to this section shall be operated for greater than 5 minutes at any location when within 100 feet of a restricted area. [...] “Commercial Motor Vehicle” means any vehicle or combination of vehicles defined in California Vehicle Code section 15210(b) and any other motor truck or bus with a gross vehicle weight rating of 10,001 pounds or more, except the following: (A) a zero emission vehicle; or (B) a pickup truck as defined in California Vehicle Code section 471.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's posted text of 13 CCR 2485 (dated 09/02/2016). A June 2022 OAL-approved version exists but returned CARB's rate-limit page, so later changes were not read.
rules.correction: Review 2026-11-25: added the 2485(h)(6) definition of 'commercial motor vehicle', which leaves out zero-emission vehicles and pickup trucks as defined in Vehicle Code 471, so the 5-minute limit does not reach them. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: Truck idling exception: power take-off work such as mixers, cranes and pumps
rules.plain_english: The 5-minute truck idling limit does not apply while the engine powers a PTO for the work the truck is built for, such as a crane, pump, drill, hoist, lift or ready-mix concrete drum. Other exceptions include traffic, queuing more than 100 feet from homes or schools, safety inspections, servicing, and adverse weather or breakdowns.
rules.applies_to: Owners, operators and dispatching motor carriers of diesel commercial vehicles over 10,000 lb GVWR in California
rules.quote: (D) idling when the vehicle is queuing that at all times is beyond 100 feet from any restricted area; [...] (H) idling when positioning or providing a power source for equipment or operations, other than transporting passengers or propulsion, which involve a power take off or equivalent mechanism and is powered by the primary diesel engine for: 1. controlling cargo temperature, operating a lift, crane, pump, drill, hoist, mixer (such as a ready mix concrete truck), or other auxiliary equipment;
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's posted text of 13 CCR 2485 (dated 09/02/2016). A June 2022 OAL-approved version exists but returned CARB's rate-limit page, so later changes were not read.

rules.title: Truck idling 'restricted area': property with homes, schools, hotels, hospitals or care facilities
rules.plain_english: A restricted area is any property zoned for houses or apartments, schools, hotels, motels, hospitals, senior care or child care that has at least one such unit. Near these (within 100 feet) even queuing and clean-idle trucks may not idle over 5 minutes.
rules.applies_to: Owners, operators and dispatching motor carriers of diesel commercial vehicles over 10,000 lb GVWR in California
rules.quote: “Restricted area” means any real property zoned for individual or multifamily housing units, schools, hotels, motels, hospitals, senior care facilities or child care facilities, that has one or more of such units on it.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's posted text of 13 CCR 2485 (dated 09/02/2016). A June 2022 OAL-approved version exists but returned CARB's rate-limit page, so later changes were not read.

rules.title: Illegal truck idling fine: up to $1,000 per day for owner and driver
rules.plain_english: CARB's idling fact sheet says air districts, CARB and any law enforcement agency can fine both the owner and the driver of a truck of 10,000 lb or more up to $1,000 per day for illegal idling. The regulation itself (13 CCR 2485(g)) states no dollar amount; it applies the Health and Safety Code penalty sections.

parameters.amount_source: CARB fact sheet (the regulation text states no dollar amount)

rules.applies_to: Owners, operators and dispatching motor carriers of diesel commercial vehicles over 10,000 lb GVWR in California
rules.citation: CARB truck idling fact sheet (Oct. 2021); 13 CCR 2485(g)
rules.quote: Any law enforcement department, including air districts and CARB, can fine a 10,000 pound or greater truck owner and driver up to $1000 per day for illegal idling (13 CCR 2480 & 2485). [...] On or after January 1, 2015, any person who violates any requirement of this section is subject to the penalties set forth in California Health and Safety Code sections 39674, 39675, 42400, 42400.1, 42400.2, 42400.3, 42402, 42402.1, 42402.2, 42402.3, 42402.4, 42403.5, and 42410 and 43704.
rules.notes: CARB fact sheet (October 2021). 2485(g) cites HSC 39674 et seq. for violations on or after January 1, 2015.
rules.correction: Review 2026-11-25: citation was '13 CCR 2480, 2485(g)', which implied the regulation sets $1,000 a day; 2485(g) states no amount and points to HSC 39674 et seq. The $1,000/day figure is CARB's fact sheet statement. Citation, plain_english and parameters now say so; 2480 (school bus idling) dropped.

rules.title: Motor carriers must give dispatched drivers their contact details
rules.plain_english: A company that dispatches a diesel truck over 10,000 lb must give the driver the carrier's business name, address, contact person and phone. On request, the driver must show an enforcement officer their license, the vehicle registration and that carrier information.
rules.applies_to: Owners, operators and dispatching motor carriers of diesel commercial vehicles over 10,000 lb GVWR in California
rules.quote: On or after January 1, 2015, a motor carrier that dispatches a vehicle subject to the requirements of this section must provide the following information to a dispatched driver: 1. motor carrier's business name 2. motor carrier's street address, state, zip code; 3. motor carrier contact person's name; and 4. motor carrier contact person's business phone number.
rules.notes: Quoted from CARB's posted text of 13 CCR 2485 (dated 09/02/2016). A June 2022 OAL-approved version exists but returned CARB's rate-limit page, so later changes were not read.

rules.title: PERP registration is voluntary, but air district permits are mandatory
rules.plain_english: CARB's Portable Equipment Registration Program lets portable equipment such as compressors, generators, concrete pumps, drill rigs and crushers operate statewide without a permit from each of the 35 air districts. Registering is voluntary; if a district requires a permit, you must get it even if the unit is in PERP.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of portable engines and equipment (generators, compressors, pumps, light towers, welders, concrete pumps, crushers, screens) used at California job sites
rules.quote: The Portable Equipment Registration Program (PERP) is a voluntary statewide program to register portable equipment such as air compressors, generators, concrete pumps, tub grinders, woodchippers, water pumps, drill rigs, pile drivers, rock drills, abrasive blasters, aggregate screening and crushing plants, and concrete batch plants. [...] If a district decides something needs a district permit, the owner/operator must obtain the district permit to use it, even if it is registered in PERP.
rules.notes: From CARB's official PERP Frequently Asked Questions (September 29, 2026), staff interpretation of 13 CCR 2450 et seq. and 17 CCR 93116 et seq.; the regulation text controls if they differ. CARB's off-road booklet: 'If you own or operate a portable auxiliary engine 50 hp or greater, you may need a permit or registration to legally operate in California.'

rules.title: Portable means it does not stay at one location more than 12 months
rules.plain_english: Equipment counts as portable (eligible for PERP instead of a stationary permit) only if it can be moved, is not on a foundation, does not stay at the same location more than 12 consecutive months, and is not a seasonal source (one that stays at one location for at least two years and runs at least three months each year). The clock starts when it arrives, not when it first runs, and moving it away and back to reset the clock is not allowed.

parameters.clock_starts: when first brought onto the location

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of portable engines and equipment (generators, compressors, pumps, light towers, welders, concrete pumps, crushers, screens) used at California job sites
rules.quote: It does not reside at the same location for more than 12 consecutive months. [...] The 12-month time period starts when the equipment is first brought onto the location. [...] It does not operate as a seasonal source where it remains in a single location for at least two years and operates at least three months each year.
rules.notes: From CARB's official PERP Frequently Asked Questions (September 29, 2026), staff interpretation of 13 CCR 2450 et seq. and 17 CCR 93116 et seq.; the regulation text controls if they differ.
rules.correction: Review 2026-11-25: added the fourth condition of the 'portable' definition quoted in the FAQ (Q4): not a seasonal source that stays at one location at least two years and operates at least three months each year. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: PERP registration lasts 3 years; send the renewal at least 2 months before expiry
rules.plain_english: A PERP registration usually expires 3 years from the month issued. CARB emails a renewal invoice about 120 days before expiration; return it to PERPrenewals@arb.ca.gov at least 2 months before expiration to avoid late fees. Older-tier engines may get shorter terms.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of portable engines and equipment (generators, compressors, pumps, light towers, welders, concrete pumps, crushers, screens) used at California job sites
rules.quote: You will receive a renewal invoice approximately 120 days before the expiration date. This renewal invoice must be completed and emailed to PERPrenewals@arb.ca.gov at least 2 months prior to expiration to avoid any late renewal fee penalties. [...] In most cases, the registration expires 3 years from the month it was originally issued.
rules.notes: From CARB's official PERP Frequently Asked Questions (September 29, 2026), staff interpretation of 13 CCR 2450 et seq. and 17 CCR 93116 et seq.; the regulation text controls if they differ.

rules.title: PERP fees: $805 per engine, $490 per equipment unit (renewal $735 / $420)
rules.plain_english: Registering a portable engine or pile driver in PERP costs $805 (with placard); an equipment unit costs $490. Renewal is $735 per engine and $420 per equipment unit, plus a penalty fee if late. Fees are not refundable.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of portable engines and equipment (generators, compressors, pumps, light towers, welders, concrete pumps, crushers, screens) used at California job sites
rules.quote: Initial registration: 1. Engine or pile driver: $805 [...] 2. Equipment unit: $490 [...] Renewal registration: 1. Engine or pile driver: $735 [...] 2. Equipment unit: $420
rules.notes: From CARB's official PERP Frequently Asked Questions (September 29, 2026), staff interpretation of 13 CCR 2450 et seq. and 17 CCR 93116 et seq.; the regulation text controls if they differ. Fee amounts as listed in the September 29, 2026 FAQ. Multiple-engine (4+) inspection discount needs a letter of intent to the home district within 45 days of initial registration or by January 30 for renewals.

rules.title: PERP projects over 2,500 bhp in extreme ozone areas: notify the district 14 days ahead
rules.plain_english: If an onshore project in an extreme ozone nonattainment district will have registered portable engines totaling more than 2,500 bhp on site at once, the person responsible must notify the district in writing at least 14 days before startup, or within 72 hours if the total goes over 2,500 bhp after startup. Projects using only Tier 4 engines in remote locations are excused.

parameters.applies_in: districts designated extreme non-attainment for ozone (the FAQ does not list them)
parameters.exempt: only Interim Tier 4/Tier 4 Final engines at locations > 1/2 mile from schools, businesses, hospitals, residences, daycare

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of portable engines and equipment (generators, compressors, pumps, light towers, welders, concrete pumps, crushers, screens) used at California job sites
rules.quote: if an onshore project commences operation in a district designated as extreme non-attainment for ozone and the total maximum rated horsepower of registered engines located simultaneously on the project site exceeds 2,500 brake horsepower (bhp), the person responsible for the project must notify the district in writing at least 14 days prior to startup. If the project exceeds 2,500 bhp after startup, the district must be notified within 72 hours of the exceedance.
rules.notes: From CARB's official PERP Frequently Asked Questions (September 29, 2026), staff interpretation of 13 CCR 2450 et seq. and 17 CCR 93116 et seq.; the regulation text controls if they differ. The district list for 'extreme' ozone nonattainment is not given in the FAQ.
rules.correction: applies_in had an example '(e.g., South Coast, San Joaquin Valley)' that is not in the PERP FAQ or any other source read; the example was removed and the parameter now says the FAQ does not list the districts. The 2,500 bhp, 14-day, 72-hour and remote-Tier-4 exemption values are confirmed.

rules.title: PERP diesel engine eligibility: Tier 4 Final (or flex) only
rules.plain_english: New PERP registrations for diesel engines are limited to current-tier engines: 50-750 bhp must be Tier 4 Final, Tier 4 Interim flex or Tier 3 flex; over 750 bhp must be Tier 4 Final, Tier 4 Interim flex or Tier 2 flex. Tier 3 hazardous-location engines stay eligible until January 1, 2029.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of portable engines and equipment (generators, compressors, pumps, light towers, welders, concrete pumps, crushers, screens) used at California job sites
rules.quote: 2. Engines rated at 50 bhp to 750 bhp, certified to the following federal emission tier levels: • Tier 4 Final, Tier 4 Interim flex, or Tier 3 flex. 3. Engines rated over 750 bhp, certified to the following federal emission tier levels: • Tier 4 Final, Tier 4 Interim flex, or Tier 2 flex.
rules.notes: From CARB's official PERP Frequently Asked Questions (September 29, 2026), staff interpretation of 13 CCR 2450 et seq. and 17 CCR 93116 et seq.; the regulation text controls if they differ.

rules.title: Portable diesel engines 50 bhp and up must meet CARB's Portable Engine ATCM
rules.plain_english: Most portable diesel engines rated 50 bhp or more must meet CARB's Portable Engine Airborne Toxic Control Measure, whether they are PERP-registered, district-permitted or unpermitted. Not covered at all: engines under 50 bhp; engines that propel vehicles or mobile equipment; non-diesel engines; engines on two-engine vehicles, cranes, private street sweepers, water well drilling rigs or snow removal vehicles; engines owned by an agricultural source; engines used only to deal with a public health and safety threat during an emergency; engines approved for hazardous locations that meet Tier 3 standards; military-owned engines in tactical support equipment; and engines used only on harbor craft.

not_subject: engines that propel vehicles or mobile equipment
engines owned by an agricultural source
engines used exclusively to alleviate the threat to public health and safety during an emergency event
engines approved to operate in hazardous locations that meet Tier 3 standards
military-owned engines used in tactical support equipment
engines used exclusively on harbor craft

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of portable engines and equipment (generators, compressors, pumps, light towers, welders, concrete pumps, crushers, screens) used at California job sites
rules.quote: Most portable diesel engines rated 50 bhp or greater are subject to the Portable Engine ATCM. It does not matter if the engine is registered in PERP, permitted with a local air district, or unpermitted. [...] Only the following types of portable engines are not subject to the Portable Engine ATCM at all: [...] Engines owned by an agricultural source; [...] Engines used exclusively to alleviate the threat of public health and safety during an emergency event; [...] Engines approved to operate in hazardous locations and meet Tier 3 emission standards; and [...] Engines owned by the military and used in tactical support equipment. [...] Engines used exclusively on harbor craft;
rules.notes: From CARB's official PERP Frequently Asked Questions (September 29, 2026), staff interpretation of 13 CCR 2450 et seq. and 17 CCR 93116 et seq.; the regulation text controls if they differ.
rules.correction: Review 2026-11-25: not_subject listed 4 of the FAQ Q14 categories; added agricultural-source, emergency-only, Tier 3 hazardous-location, military tactical and harbor craft engines with their quotes. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction (CARB PERP FAQ (Sept. 29, 2026) Q14, verifier's copy of 2026-11-25 re-read on 2026-11-27); no value changed.

rules.title: Portable engine fleets: small 750 bhp or less, large over 750 bhp
rules.plain_english: For the Portable Engine ATCM, a fleet with 750 total bhp or less is small and must follow the tier phase-out schedule; over 750 bhp is large. All companies registering since June 30, 2019 are small fleets. A large fleet may use the fleet average option instead of the tier phase-out only if it opted in by June 30, 2019.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of portable engines and equipment (generators, compressors, pumps, light towers, welders, concrete pumps, crushers, screens) used at California job sites
rules.quote: Large fleets have a total maximum horsepower over 750 bhp and follow either the tier phase out schedule or the fleet average compliance option. [...] Small fleets have a total maximum horsepower of 750 bhp or less. [...] Small fleets must follow the tier phase out schedule. [...] Must have opted into fleet average compliance by June 30, 2019.
rules.notes: From CARB's official PERP Frequently Asked Questions (September 29, 2026), staff interpretation of 13 CCR 2450 et seq. and 17 CCR 93116 et seq.; the regulation text controls if they differ. Engine-specific phase-out dates are printed on each engine's registration certificate (93116.3(c)(1)).
rules.correction: Review 2026-11-25: added fleet_average_opt_in_deadline: a large fleet may use the fleet average option only if it opted in by June 30, 2019 (FAQ Q2, Q16). Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: Low-use portable engines: 200 hours a year; annual report by March 1
rules.plain_english: A low-use portable engine may run no more than 200 hours per calendar year (hours outside California or in emergencies do not count), must have a non-resettable hour meter, and its annual low-use report is due March 1 for the prior year.
rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of portable engines and equipment (generators, compressors, pumps, light towers, welders, concrete pumps, crushers, screens) used at California job sites
rules.quote: May not operate more than 200 hours per calendar year. [...] Annual low-use reports must be submitted by March 1 of each year for operation the prior year as required by section 93116.4(d)(1) of the Portable Engine ATCM.
rules.notes: From CARB's official PERP Frequently Asked Questions (September 29, 2026), staff interpretation of 13 CCR 2450 et seq. and 17 CCR 93116 et seq.; the regulation text controls if they differ.

rules.title: PERP renewal needs an hour meter reading taken within 12 months of expiration
rules.plain_english: To renew a registered portable diesel engine, enter the hour meter reading and the date taken on the renewal invoice; the reading must be within 12 months of the registration's expiration date.

parameters.applies_to: registered diesel engines (not spark-ignition, two-engine cranes, sweepers, water well rigs)

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators of portable engines and equipment (generators, compressors, pumps, light towers, welders, concrete pumps, crushers, screens) used at California job sites
rules.quote: The owner must also list the date the reading was taken, and the reading must be within 12 months of the registration’s expiration date.
rules.notes: From CARB's official PERP Frequently Asked Questions (September 29, 2026), staff interpretation of 13 CCR 2450 et seq. and 17 CCR 93116 et seq.; the regulation text controls if they differ.

rules.title: South Coast: no visible dust beyond the property line
rules.plain_english: In the South Coast AQMD, no person may let dust from a construction site, storage pile or disturbed ground stay visible in the air past the property line, or exceed 20% opacity from vehicle movement.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.quote: No person shall cause or allow the emissions of fugitive dust from any active operation, open storage pile, or disturbed surface area such that: [...] (A) the dust remains visible in the atmosphere beyond the property line of the emission source; or (B) the dust emission exceeds 20 percent opacity (as determined by the appropriate test method included in the Rule 403 Implementation Handbook), if the dust emission is the result of movement of a motorized vehicle.
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF). Does not apply when wind gusts exceed 25 mph if Table 3 contingency measures are used and records kept (403(g)(2)(A)).

rules.title: South Coast: use the Rule 403 Table 1 best available control measures
rules.plain_english: Every active construction operation in the South Coast AQMD must use the applicable best available control measures from Rule 403 Table 1 for each dust source: backfilling, clearing and grubbing, cut and fill, demolition, disturbed soil, earth-moving, hauling bulk materials, staging areas, stockpiles, traffic areas, trenching, truck loading, unpaved roads and others.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.quote: No person shall conduct active operations without utilizing the applicable best available control measures included in Table 1 of this Rule to minimize fugitive dust emissions from each fugitive dust source type within the active operation.
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF). Category 'required_document' is used because the measures are a required checklist; no plan filing is required below the large-operation threshold.

rules.title: South Coast: downwind PM10 may not exceed upwind by more than 50 ug/m3
rules.plain_english: If dust is sampled, the PM10 level downwind of a site may not be more than 50 micrograms per cubic meter above the upwind level.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.quote: No person shall cause or allow PM10 levels to exceed 50 micrograms per cubic meter when determined, by simultaneous sampling, as the difference between upwind and downwind samples collected on high-volume particulate matter samplers or other U.S. EPA-approved equivalent method for PM10 monitoring.
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF). Large operations that routinely use Table 2 measures and keep records are exempt from (d)(3) (403(g)(5)); if SCAQMD monitors, Rule 304.1 fees may apply (403(h)).

rules.title: South Coast: track-out under 25 feet and cleaned up every workday
rules.plain_english: Mud and dirt tracked onto paved roads may not extend 25 feet or more from the site exit, and all track-out must be removed at the end of each workday or evening shift.

parameters.cleanup: end of each workday or evening shift

rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.quote: No person shall allow track-out to extend 25 feet or more in cumulative length from the point of origin from an active operation. Notwithstanding the preceding, all track-out from an active operation shall be removed at the conclusion of each workday or evening shift.
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF).

rules.title: South Coast: sites of 5+ acres or 100+ cy/day need a track-out control at each exit
rules.plain_english: A site with 5 or more acres disturbed, or importing/exporting 100 cubic yards or more of material a day, must have at least one track-out control at every exit to a paved public road: a washed-gravel pad (1-inch rock, 6 inches deep, 30 ft wide by 50 ft long), 100 ft by 20 ft of paving, a 24 by 10 ft wheel shaker, a wheel washer, or an approved equivalent.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.quote: No person shall conduct an active operation with a disturbed surface area of five or more acres, or with a daily import or export of 100 cubic yards or more of bulk material without utilizing at least one of the measures listed in subparagraphs (d)(5)(A) through (d)(5)(E) at each vehicle egress from the site to a paved public road. (A) Install a pad consisting of washed gravel (minimum-size: one inch) maintained in a clean condition to a depth of at least six inches and extending at least 30 feet wide and at least 50 feet long. [...] (B) Pave the surface extending at least 100 feet and at least 20 feet wide. (C) Utilize a wheel shaker/wheel spreading device consisting of raised dividers (rails, pipe, or grates) at least 24 feet long and 10 feet wide to remove bulk material from tires and vehicle undercarriages before vehicles exit the site.
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF).

rules.title: South Coast 'large operation': 50+ acres disturbed or 5,000 cy/day three times a year
rules.plain_english: A large operation is any site with 50 or more acres of disturbed surface, or earth-moving of 3,850 cubic meters (5,000 cubic yards) or more in a day on three days within the last 365 days. Large operations have extra notice, records, signs and supervisor duties. Those extra duties do not apply to public parks and recreation areas, to large operations that must file a dust control plan with a city or county that has a District-approved dust control ordinance, or to Rule 1158 operations whose approved plan covers all their dust sources. A large operation with an unchanged AQMD-approved fugitive dust control plan also skips the Form 403 N notice, operation description and daily records of 403(e)(1)(A)-(C).

subdivision_e_not_applicable_to: officially-designated public parks and recreational areas
large operations required to submit a dust control plan to a city or county government with a District-approved dust control ordinance
large operations subject to Rule 1158 with an approved Rule 1158 dust control plan covering all fugitive dust sources

rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
