rules.quote: (21) LARGE OPERATIONS means any active operations on property which contains 50 or more acres of disturbed surface area; or any earth-moving operation with a daily earth-moving or throughput volume of 3,850 cubic [...] meters (5,000 cubic yards) or more three times during the most recent 365-day period. [...] (7) The provisions of subdivision (e) shall not apply to: [...] (B) any large operation which is required to submit a dust control plan to any city or county government which has adopted a District-approved dust control ordinance. [...] (8) The provisions of subparagraph (e)(1)(A) through (e)(1)(C) shall not apply to any large operation with an AQMD-approved fugitive dust control plan provided that there is no change to the sources and controls as identified in the AQMD-approved fugitive dust control plan.
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF).
rules.correction: Review 2026-11-25: added the large-operation exemptions of 403(g)(7) (all of subdivision (e) does not apply where a city or county with a District-approved dust control ordinance requires the plan, to public parks, or to Rule 1158 plans) and (g)(8) (no Form 403 N, description or daily records under (e)(1)(A)-(C) with an unchanged AQMD-approved fugitive dust control plan). Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction (SCAQMD Rule 403 (g)(7)-(8) and (e)(1) at https://www.aqmd.gov/docs/default-source/rule-book/rule-iv/rule-403.pdf re-read on 2026-11-27); no value changed.

rules.title: South Coast large operations: file Form 403 N within 7 days of qualifying
rules.plain_english: Once a site becomes a large operation, submit a signed Large Operation Notification (Form 403 N) to SCAQMD within 7 days, with the responsible people's names, addresses and phones, a description of the work and a site map.

parameters.trigger: qualifying as a large operation
contents: names, addresses, phone numbers of responsible persons

rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.quote: (A) submit a fully executed Large Operation Notification (Form 403 N) to the Executive Officer within 7 days of qualifying as a large operation; (B) include, as part of the notification, the name(s), address(es), and phone number(s) of the person(s) responsible for the submittal, and a description of the operation(s), including a map depicting the location of the site;
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF).

rules.title: South Coast large operations: daily dust-control records kept 3 years
rules.plain_english: Large operations must keep daily records of the dust control actions taken, keep them at least three years, and show them to SCAQMD on request.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.quote: (C) maintain daily records to document the specific dust control actions taken, maintain such records for a period of not less than three years; and make such records available to the Executive Officer upon request;
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF).

rules.title: South Coast large operations: post project contact signs before earthmoving
rules.plain_english: Before any earthmoving on a large operation, install project signs with contact information meeting the Rule 403 Implementation Handbook standards.

parameters.standard: Rule 403 Implementation Handbook

rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.quote: (D) install and maintain project signage with project contact signage that meets the minimum standards of the Rule 403 Implementation Handbook, prior to initiating any earthmoving activities;
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF). The Implementation Handbook (sign size and content) was not read.

rules.title: South Coast large operations: certified dust control supervisor on call within 30 minutes
rules.plain_english: Large operations must name a dust control supervisor employed or hired by the owner or developer, on site or able to be there within 30 minutes during working hours, with authority to order dust controls, who has completed SCAQMD's Fugitive Dust Control Class.

parameters.training: AQMD Fugitive Dust Control Class certificate
parameters.employer: property owner or developer (employee or contractor)

rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.quote: (E) identify a dust control supervisor that: (i) is employed by or contracted with the property owner or developer; (ii) is on the site or available on-site within 30 minutes during working hours; (iii) has the authority to expeditiously employ sufficient dust mitigation measures to ensure compliance with all Rule requirements; (iv) has completed the AQMD Fugitive Dust Control Class and has been issued a valid Certificate of Completion for the class; and
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF).

rules.title: South Coast: tell SCAQMD within 30 days after a site stops being a large operation
rules.plain_english: Notify SCAQMD in writing within 30 days after the site no longer qualifies as a large operation.

parameters.trigger: site no longer qualifies as a large operation

rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.quote: (F) notify the Executive Officer in writing within 30 days after the site no longer qualifies as a large operation as defined by paragraph (c)(18).
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF). The rule's cross-reference '(c)(18)' is as printed; large operations are defined in (c)(21).

rules.title: South Coast: Form 403 N valid 1 year; resubmit 30 days before it expires
rules.plain_english: An accepted Large Operation Notification is valid one year. Resubmit it at least 30 days before expiration or it lapses; if nothing changed, a short no-change statement (Form 403NC) is enough.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.quote: Any Large Operation Notification submitted to the Executive Officer or AQMD-approved dust control plan shall be valid for a period of one year from the date of written acceptance by the Executive Officer. [...] must be resubmitted annually by the person who conducts or authorizes the conducting of a large operation, at least 30 days prior to the expiration date, or the submittal shall no longer be valid as of the expiration date.
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF).

rules.title: South Coast high winds: gusts over 25 mph trigger Table 3 contingency measures
rules.plain_english: When wind gusts exceed 25 mph, the visible-dust and PM10 limits are excused only if the Table 3 contingency measures are carried out for each dust source and daily records are kept. Contingency options include stopping earth-moving or watering soil within 15 minutes before moving it, and watering disturbed areas 3 to 4 times a day.

earth_moving: water soil not more than 15 minutes before moving

rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.quote: The provisions of paragraphs (d)(1) and (d)(3) shall not apply: (A) When wind gusts exceed 25 miles per hour, provided that: [...] (i) The required Table 3 contingency measures in this Rule are implemented for each applicable fugitive dust source type, and; (ii) records are maintained in accordance with subparagraph (e)(1)(C).
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF).

rules.title: South Coast large operations: 12% soil moisture checks and watering unpaved roads every 2 hours
rules.plain_english: Large operations must follow Table 2: keep earth-moving soil at 12% moisture or more, checking twice in the first three hours and twice every four hours after; water unpaved roads at least every two hours (3 times per 8-hour day), or once a day with a 15 mph limit, or use a chemical stabilizer.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.quote: Maintain soil moisture content at a minimum of 12 percent, as determined by ASTM method [...] Two soil moisture evaluations must be conducted during the first three hours of active operations during a calendar day, and two such evaluations each subsequent four-hour period of active operations; [...] Water all roads used for any vehicular traffic at least once per every two hours of active operations [3 times per normal 8 hour work day]; OR [...] Water all roads used for any vehicular traffic once daily and restrict vehicle speeds to 15 miles per hour; OR
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF). Earth-moving more than 100 ft from all property lines may instead be watered to keep visible dust under 100 ft in any direction (1a-1).

rules.title: South Coast large operations: stabilize completed grading within 5 working days
rules.plain_english: On large operations, completed grading areas must get chemical stabilizer within five working days of finishing grading, or be treated like inactive areas (watering, or vegetative cover started within 21 days).

parameters.vegetation_density: less than 30% unstabilized ground within 90 days of planting

rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.quote: (2c) Apply chemical stabilizers within five working days of grading completion; OR [...] Establish a vegetative ground cover within 21 days after active operations have ceased.
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF).

rules.title: South Coast: stockpiles near occupied buildings max 8 ft; keep 6 inches of freeboard on haul trucks
rules.plain_english: Under Table 1, stockpiles within 100 yards of occupied off-site buildings may be no higher than 8 feet unless a water-truck road or full irrigation system reaches the top, and haul trucks must keep at least six inches of freeboard (per Vehicle Code 23114).
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.quote: Maintain at least six inches of freeboard on haul vehicles; and [...] Stockpiles within 100 yards of off-site occupied [...] buildings must not be greater than eight feet in [...] height; or must have a road bladed to the top to allow [...] water truck access or must have an operational water irrigation system that is capable of complete stockpile coverage.
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF). Table 1 guidance also suggests limiting staging-area vehicle speeds to 15 mph.

rules.title: South Coast: a contractor's Rule 403 duty ends with its contract (grading: 5 days after final inspection)
rules.plain_english: A contractor is no longer covered by Rule 403 after its contract ends if it used the required controls during the contract. A grading contractor's coverage for a phase ends after that phase, provided controls were kept up through five days after the final grading inspection.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, grading and other active operations in the South Coast AQMD (Orange County and the non-desert parts of Los Angeles, Riverside and San Bernardino counties; Coachella Valley under Rule 403.1)
rules.quote: (H) Any contractor subsequent to the time the contract ends, provided that such contractor implemented the required control measures during the contractual period. (I) Any grading contractor, for a phase of active operations, subsequent to the contractual completion of that phase of earth-moving activities, provided that the required control measures have been implemented during the entire phase of earth-moving activities, through and including five days after the final grading inspection.
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403 as amended June 3, 2005 (current rule-book PDF).

rules.title: Coachella Valley: dust control plan approved before earthmoving over 5,000 sq ft
rules.plain_english: In the Coachella Valley, any project disturbing more than 5,000 square feet may not start earthmoving until SCAQMD approves a fugitive dust control plan. SCAQMD acts within 30 days; plans last one year and must be resubmitted at least 30 days before expiry. Keep the plan on site, post contact signs, and for 50+ acres name a dust control supervisor. Where the city or county has a District-approved dust control ordinance, the plan goes to that city or county instead (403.1(i)(4)). Everyone subject to Rule 403.1 keeps written daily records of dust control actions for at least three years.

parameters.plan_to_city_or_county_instead: active operations required to submit a dust control plan to a city or county government that has adopted a District-approved dust control ordinance
parameters.supervisor_class: AQMD Coachella Valley Fugitive Dust Control Class

rules.applies_to: Construction and earthmoving in the Coachella Valley portion of the South Coast AQMD
rules.quote: Any person who conducts or authorizes the conducting of an active operation with a disturbed surface area of more than 5,000 square feet shall not initiate any earth-moving activities unless a fugitive dust control plan is prepared and approved by the Executive Officer in accordance with the requirements of subdivision (f) and the Rule 403.1 Implementation Handbook. [...] Any fugitive dust control plan approved by the Executive Officer shall be valid for a period of one year from the date of approval. Any approved fugitive dust control plan must be resubmitted annually, at least 30 days prior to the expiration date, or the fugitive dust control plan shall expire as of the expiration date. [...] has completed the AQMD Coachella Valley Fugitive Dust Control Class and has been issued a valid Certificate of Completion for the class. [...] A person subject to the provisions of this rule shall compile written daily records to document the specific actions taken to comply with this Rule. Such records shall be retained for not less than three years and shall be made available to the Executive Officer upon request. [...] (4) The provisions of paragraph (e)(1) shall not apply to any active operation which is required to submit a dust control plan to any city or county government that has adopted a District-approved dust control ordinance.
rules.notes: SCAQMD Rule 403.1 as amended April 2, 2004. Exempt where a city/county has a District-approved dust control ordinance (403.1(i)(4)).
rules.correction: Review 2026-11-25: parameters did not carry 403.1(i)(4) (plan filed with a city or county that has a District-approved dust control ordinance instead of SCAQMD), the (h)(1) three-year daily records duty, or the Coachella Valley class named in (e)(4)(D); added all three with their quotes.

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: Dust Control Plan before work on 10+ acres residential, 5+ acres non-residential, or >2,500 cy/day
rules.plain_english: In the San Joaquin Valley, submit a Dust Control Plan before starting any construction on a site with 10 or more acres disturbed (residential), 5 or more acres (commercial, industrial, institutional, public), or moving more than 2,500 cubic yards a day of material on at least three days. Work may not begin until the District approves it, and you must give written notice within 10 days before earthmoving starts.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.quote: An owner/operator shall submit a Dust Control Plan to the APCO prior to the start of any construction activity on any site that will include 10 acres or more of disturbed surface area for residential developments, or 5 acres or more of disturbed surface area for non-residential development, or will include moving, depositing, or relocating more than 2,500 cubic yards per day of bulk materials on at least three days. Construction activities shall not commence until the APCO has approved or conditionally approved the Dust Control Plan. An owner/operator shall provide written notification to the APCO within 10 days prior to the commencement of earthmoving activities via fax or mail.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: District decides on a Dust Control Plan within 30 days (submit 30 days ahead)
rules.plain_english: The District approves, disapproves or conditions a Dust Control Plan within 30 days of submittal; a plan with no District comments after 30 days is automatically approved. The District's guidance is to submit at least 30 days before construction starts. One plan can cover several sites starting within 12 months.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.quote: The APCO shall approve, disapprove, or conditionally approve the Dust Control Plan within 30 days of plan submittal. A Dust Control Plan is deemed automatically approved if, after 30 days following receipt by the District, the District does not provide any comments to the owner/operator regarding the Dust Control Plan.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page). SJVAPCD's 2024 dust control brochure: 'Plans must be submitted to the District at least 30 days prior to commencing construction.'

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: 48-hour notice for 1-10 acre residential and 1-5 acre non-residential sites
rules.plain_english: Smaller construction sites that do not need a full Dust Control Plan still need written notice to the District at least 48 hours before earthmoving: residential sites from 1 to under 10 acres, non-residential sites from 1 to under 5 acres. These sizes are the construction site's area, not the disturbed surface area used for the Dust Control Plan thresholds.

parameters.area_measured: construction site area (the text says 'construction sites ... in area')

rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.quote: On residential development construction sites ranging from 1.0 to less than 10.0 acres in area, an owner/operator shall provide written notification to the District at least 48 hours prior to his/her intent to commence any earthmoving activities. [...] On non-residential development construction sites ranging from 1.0 to less than 5.0 acres in area, an owner/operator shall provide written notification to the District at least 48 hours prior to his/her intent to commence any earthmoving activities.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).
rules.correction: Review 2026-11-25: added area_measured: 6.4.1-6.4.2 key the 48-hour notice to the construction site's area, not the disturbed surface area that the Dust Control Plan thresholds of 6.3.1 use. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction (SJVAPCD Rule 8021 sec. 6.4 at https://ww2.valleyair.org/media/bhfgzedn/rule-8021.pdf re-read on 2026-11-27); no value changed.

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: keep the approved Dust Control Plan on site; one person must take District dust training
rules.plain_english: Keep a copy of the approved Dust Control Plan at the project site; it stays valid until all dust-generating work ends, and breaking it is a rule violation. At least one key person for the owner/operator, or whoever prepares the plan, must complete the District's Dust Control Training Class.

parameters.plan_valid_until: termination of all dust generating activities

rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.quote: An owner/operator shall retain a copy of an approved Dust Control Plan at the project site. The approved Dust Control Plan shall remain valid until the termination of all dust generating activities. [...] At least one key individual representing the owner/operator or any person who prepares a Dust Control Plan must complete a Dust Control Training Class conducted by the District.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: limit visible dust to 20% opacity on construction sites
rules.plain_english: All construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the Valley must use enough controls (pre-watering, phasing, watering or stabilizers during work, wind barriers, stabilizing haul roads) to keep visible dust emissions at or below 20% opacity and keep surfaces stabilized.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.quote: No person shall perform any construction, demolition, excavation, extraction, or other earthmoving activities unless the appropriate requirements in sections 5.1 through 5.5 are sufficiently implemented to limit VDE to 20% opacity and comply with the conditions for a stabilized surface area when applicable.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: stabilize 0.5+ acre areas left unused 7 days or more
rules.plain_english: Any disturbed area of half an acre or more that sits unused for seven or more days must be stabilized (watered, treated, or access restricted) to meet the District's stabilized-surface conditions.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.quote: If an area having 0.5 acres or more of disturbed surface area remains unused for seven or more days, the area must comply with the conditions for a stabilized surface area as defined in section 3.58 of Rule 8011.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: 15 mph on uncontrolled unpaved haul roads, with signs every 500 feet
rules.plain_english: On construction sites, keep vehicles to 15 mph on uncontrolled unpaved access and haul roads, and post DOT-standard speed limit signs at each entrance and at least every 500 feet, readable both directions.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.quote: An owner/operator shall limit the speed of vehicles traveling on uncontrolled unpaved access/haul roads within construction sites to a maximum of 15 miles per hour. [...] At a minimum, speed limit signs shall also be posted at least every 500 feet and shall be readable in both directions of travel along uncontrolled unpaved access/haul roads.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: stop soil-disturbing work when wind dust exceeds 20% opacity
rules.plain_english: Whenever visible dust exceeds 20% opacity, stop outdoor construction and earthmoving that disturbs soil (indoor trades may continue), and keep water trucks running unless unsafe.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.quote: Cease outdoor construction, excavation, extraction, and other earthmoving activities that disturb the soil whenever VDE exceeds 20% opacity. [...] Continue operation of water trucks/devices when outdoor construction excavation, extraction, and other earthmoving activities cease, unless unsafe to do so.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley demolition: water unpaved surfaces within 100 ft within 1 hour
rules.plain_english: When razing buildings, keep visible dust under 20% opacity and apply water within one hour of demolition to unpaved surfaces within 100 feet of the demolished structure.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.quote: Apply water within 1 hour of demolition to unpaved surfaces within 100 feet of the demolished structure.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: Rule 8021 exemptions for small additions and remodels
rules.plain_english: Rule 8021 does not apply to maintenance or remodeling of existing buildings and additions that increase building area by no more than 50% or 10,000 sq ft (whichever is less), all additions to existing single-family homes, or fire-prevention disking under half an acre. Track-out from these jobs must still be cleaned up under Rule 8041. Under Rule 8011, activities at 3,000 feet or more above sea level, and emergency activities to ensure public health and safety, are exempt from all of the Regulation VIII dust rules.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.quote: Maintenance or remodeling of existing buildings and additions to existing buildings where total building area is not increased by more than fifty percent, or 10,000 square feet, whichever is less; but not including ancillary construction such as expanding parking lots. [...] All additions to existing single family residential buildings. [...] In addition to the exemptions established in Rule 8011, the activities listed in Sections 4.1 through 4.5 are exempt from this rule. [...] 4.3 Activities conducted at an elevation of 3,000 feet or higher above sea level. [...] 4.1 Emergency activities performed to ensure public health and safety are exempt from Regulation VIII.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).
rules.correction: Review 2026-11-25: added the Rule 8011 exemptions that Rule 8021 §4.0 incorporates: activities at 3,000 ft or higher elevation (8011 §4.3) and emergency activities (8011 §4.1) are exempt from Regulation VIII. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction (SJVAPCD Rule 8011 sec. 4.1 and 4.3 at https://ww2.valleyair.org/media/xtbcnaht/rule-8011.pdf re-read on 2026-11-27); no value changed.

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley Dust Control Plan fee: $493 (from July 1, 2026); $102 to modify
rules.plain_english: Filing a Rule 8021 Dust Control Plan costs a nonrefundable $493 (effective July 1, 2026), covering any administrative changes. A modification of an approved plan costs $102. Fees unpaid 60 days after submittal incur late charges.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.quote: Every person filing a Dust Control Plan subject to the provisions of Rule 8021, Section 6.3.1, shall pay to the District, upon filing, the nonrefundable fee of $493. [...] Any person submitting a request to modify an existing approved Dust Control Plan, shall pay to the District, a fee of $102.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Rule 3135 as amended May 15, 2025, effective July 1, 2026. Search excerpts show the prior fee was $456 (version effective July 1, 2025); not used.

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: remove all visible track-out at the end of each workday; no blowers or dry brooms
rules.plain_english: Remove all visible carryout and track-out from paved public roads at the end of every workday. Leaf blowers and dry rotary brushes or brooms may not be used to clean it up; use manual sweeping, a wetted rotary broom, a PM10-efficient sweeper, or flushing where allowed.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.quote: The use of blower devices, or dry rotary brushes or brooms, for removal of carryout and trackout on public roads is expressly prohibited. [...] Owners/operators shall remove all visible carryout and trackout at the end of each workday.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: track-out reaching 50 feet must be removed immediately
rules.plain_english: In urban areas (inside city limits or unincorporated islands surrounded by a city), and on rural construction projects of 10 acres or more, prevent track-out or remove it immediately once it extends 50 feet or more from the site exit.

parameters.urban_area: incorporated city or unincorporated area completely surrounded by a city

rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.quote: Within urban areas, an owner/operator shall prevent carryout and trackout, or immediately remove carryout and trackout when it extends 50 feet or more from the nearest unpaved surface exit point of a site. [...] Within rural areas, construction projects 10 acres or more in size, an owner/operator shall prevent carryout and trackout, or immediately remove carryout and trackout when it extends 50 feet or more from the nearest unpaved surface exit point of a site.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: track-out device needed at 150 trips/day, 20 heavy-truck trips/day, Dust Control Plan sites or sites with paved interior roads
rules.plain_english: A site with 150 or more vehicle trips a day, or 20 or more trips a day by vehicles with 3+ axles, or any site under a Dust Control Plan, must install a track-out control device at every exit to a paved public road; if track-out still occurs, it must be removed within half an hour. A site with paved interior roads must also take these Section 5.8 track-out measures.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.quote: An owner/operator of any site with 150 or more vehicle trips per day, or 20 or more vehicle trips per day by vehicles with three or more axles shall take the actions for carryout and trackout as specified in Section 5.8. [...] In the event that measures specified in Section 5.8.1 are insufficient to prevent carryout and trackout, removal of any carryout and trackout must be accomplished within one-half hour of the generation of such carryout and trackout. [...] For sites with paved interior roads, an owner/operator shall prevent and mitigate carryout and trackout as specified in Section 5.8.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).
rules.correction: Review 2026-11-25: added the third trigger of Rule 8041 §5.6 (sites with paved interior roads must also use the §5.8 track-out controls). Rewording 2026-11-27: title and plain_english reworded to match this correction (SJVAPCD Rule 8041 sec. 5.6 at https://ww2.valleyair.org/media/esadqm1u/rule-8041.pdf re-read on 2026-11-27); no value changed.

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley track-out devices: grizzlies 25 ft, gravel pad 50 ft x 3 in deep, or 100 ft of paving
rules.plain_english: An acceptable track-out device is a grizzly or similar rumble device at least 25 feet long across the full exit width, a gravel pad of 1-inch or larger rock at least 3 inches deep and 50 feet long across the full width (clean gravel off the road at least every 24 hours), or paving at least 100 feet long across the full width.
rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.quote: For use of grizzlies or other similar devices designed to removed dirt/mud from tires, the devices shall extend from the intersection with the public paved road surface for a distance of at least 25 feet, and cover the full width of the unpaved exit surface for at least 25 feet. [...] For use of gravel pads, coverage with gravel shall be at least one inch or larger in diameter and at least 3 inches deep, shall extend from the intersection with the public paved road surface for a distance of at least 50 feet, and cover the full width of the unpaved exit surface for at least 50 feet.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page). Paving option (5.9.3): at least 100 feet, full width.

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley: daily dust-control records kept 1 year after the project ends
rules.plain_english: For each day a dust control measure is used, record the measure, where and how much area was covered, and the date, amount and frequency of any dust suppressant (with the product sheet). Keep records one year after the project ends (five years for Title V sources) and show them to the District on request.

contents: date, amount and frequency of suppressant

rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.quote: Such records shall include the type of control measure(s) used, the location and extent of coverage, and the date, amount, and frequency of application of dust suppressant, manufacturer’s dust suppressant product information sheet that identifies the name of the dust suppressant and application instructions. Records shall be kept for one year following project completion that results in the termination of all dust generating activities.
rules.notes: SJVAPCD Regulation VIII rule as amended August 19, 2004 (current PDF linked from the District's Regulation VIII page).

rules.title: San Joaquin Valley APCD counties
rules.plain_english: SJVAPCD covers San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings and Tulare counties and the Valley air basin portion of Kern County. Regulation VIII dust rules apply to projects in these areas.

parameters.partial: Kern (San Joaquin Valley Air Basin portion)

rules.applies_to: Construction, demolition, excavation and earthmoving in the San Joaquin Valley APCD (San Joaquin, Stanislaus, Merced, Madera, Fresno, Kings, Tulare and the Valley portion of Kern counties)
rules.quote: Serving San Joaquin, Stanislaus and Merced counties [...] Serving Madera, Fresno and Kings counties [...] Serving Tulare and Valley air basin portions of Kern counties
rules.notes: From SJVAPCD's official 2024 fugitive dust control brochure.

rules.title: Bay Area CEQA basic dust measures: water twice a day, cover haul trucks, 15 mph, stop work over 20 mph wind
rules.plain_english: Bay Area projects are expected to use all nine basic dust measures: water exposed surfaces twice daily; cover haul trucks; remove track-out daily with wet power vacuum sweepers (no dry power sweeping); 15 mph on unpaved roads; pave and lay pads as soon as possible; suspend excavation, grading and demolition when average wind exceeds 20 mph; wash trucks and equipment before leaving; treat unpaved access roads 100+ ft from pavement with 6-12 inches of wood chips, mulch or gravel; and post a dust complaint sign with a contact who responds within 48 hours.

sign_must_show: lead agency contact name and phone

rules.applies_to: Construction sites in the Bay Area AQMD (Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, southern Sonoma and southwestern Solano counties)
rules.citation: BAAQMD CEQA Guidelines (2022) Table 5-2, BMPs B-1 to B-9
rules.quote: All exposed surfaces (e.g., parking areas, staging areas, soil piles, graded areas, and unpaved access roads) shall be watered two times per day. [...] All haul trucks transporting soil, sand, or other loose material off-site shall be covered. [...] All vehicle speeds on unpaved roads shall be limited to 15 mph. [...] All excavation, grading, and/or demolition activities shall be suspended when average wind speeds [...] exceed 20 mph. [...] This person shall respond and take corrective action within 48 hours.
rules.notes: BAAQMD 2022 CEQA Guidelines, Chapter 5, Table 5-2. The Guidelines are nonbinding advice to CEQA lead agencies, but a project must implement all basic BMPs for construction dust to be found less than significant, so lead agencies commonly impose them as mitigation conditions. The 2022 Guidelines supersede the 2017 version; the exact adoption date was not read.

rules.title: Bay Area CEQA enhanced dust measures near sensitive uses
rules.plain_english: Near schools, homes or other sensitive uses, the Bay Area AQMD strongly encourages enhanced measures: limit simultaneous ground disturbance, wind breaks of at most 50% porosity, early ground cover, sandbags on slopes over 1%, minimal stockpiles, and hydroseed or stabilize areas inactive for 10 or more calendar days.
rules.applies_to: Construction sites in the Bay Area AQMD (Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, southern Sonoma and southwestern Solano counties)
rules.citation: BAAQMD CEQA Guidelines (2022) Table 5-3, BMPs E-1 to E-6
rules.quote: Hydroseed or apply non-toxic soil stabilizers to construction areas, including previously graded areas, that are inactive for at least 10 calendar days.
rules.notes: BAAQMD 2022 CEQA Guidelines, Chapter 5, Table 5-3. The Guidelines are nonbinding advice to CEQA lead agencies, but a project must implement all basic BMPs for construction dust to be found less than significant, so lead agencies commonly impose them as mitigation conditions.

rules.title: Bay Area trackout rule applies to construction sites over 1 acre
rules.plain_english: Bay Area AQMD Rule 6-6 covers large construction, bulk material and disturbed surface sites, meaning sites where the construction, material handling and disturbed area totals more than 1 acre.
rules.applies_to: Construction sites in the Bay Area AQMD (Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, southern Sonoma and southwestern Solano counties)
rules.quote: This Rule does not apply to Bulk Material Sites, Construction Sites and Disturbed Surface Sites less than 1 acre. [...] Large Construction Site: Any Construction Site where the total land area covered by construction activities, bulk material handling operations and disturbed surfaces is greater than 1 acre.
rules.notes: BAAQMD Regulation 6, Rule 6, adopted August 1, 2018, effective July 1, 2019 (the version linked from the District's current Rule 6-6 page; amendments were under development in 2026).

rules.title: Bay Area: clean up track-out over 25 feet within 4 hours; no more than 1 quart left at day's end
rules.plain_english: At each active exit, track-out on the paved public road that exceeds a cumulative 25 linear feet and raises visible dust must be cleaned up within 4 hours of noticing it, and no more than 1 quart of track-out may remain on the road at the end of the workday.
rules.applies_to: Construction sites in the Bay Area AQMD (Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, southern Sonoma and southwestern Solano counties)
rules.quote: The owner/operator of any Large Bulk Material Site, Large Construction Site, or Large Disturbed Surface Site shall not cause or allow trackout at any active exit from such site onto an adjacent paved public roadway or shoulder of a paved public roadway that exceeds cumulative 25 linear feet and creates fugitive dust visible emissions without cleaning up such trackout within 4 hours of when the owner/operator identifies such excessive trackout; and shall not cause or allow more than 1 quart of trackout to remain on the adjacent paved public roadway or the paved shoulder of the paved public roadway at the end of any workday.
rules.notes: BAAQMD Regulation 6, Rule 6, adopted August 1, 2018, effective July 1, 2019 (the version linked from the District's current Rule 6-6 page; amendments were under development in 2026).

rules.title: Bay Area: track-out cleanup may not raise dust over 20% opacity for more than 3 minutes an hour
rules.plain_english: Cleaning up track-out may not create visible dust over 20% opacity (Ringelmann No. 1) for more than 3 minutes in any 60-minute period.
rules.applies_to: Construction sites in the Bay Area AQMD (Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, southern Sonoma and southwestern Solano counties)
rules.quote: shall not cause or allow a fugitive dust visible emission during cleanup of any trackout that exceeds 20 percent opacity as determined by EPA Method 203B (or as dark in shade as that designated as Number 1 on the Ringelmann Chart), for a period or aggregate periods of more than 3 minutes in any 60-minute period.
rules.notes: BAAQMD Regulation 6, Rule 6, adopted August 1, 2018, effective July 1, 2019 (the version linked from the District's current Rule 6-6 page; amendments were under development in 2026).

rules.title: Bay Area: check each exit for track-out twice a workday and keep logs 2 years
rules.plain_english: Large sites that produce track-out must check each active exit at least twice every workday at peak exit times, log which exits were checked, log every time track-out exceeded 25 feet and the cleanup done, and keep the records two years for the District.
rules.applies_to: Construction sites in the Bay Area AQMD (Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, southern Sonoma and southwestern Solano counties)
rules.quote: Monitor the extent of the trackout at each active exit from the site onto a paved public road at least twice during each workday, at times when vehicle traffic exiting the site is most likely to create an accumulation of trackout, or as otherwise specified by the APCO; [...] Maintain the records required by Sections 6-6-501.2 and 501.3 for two years, in electronic, paper hard copy or log book format, and make them available to the APCO upon request.
rules.notes: BAAQMD Regulation 6, Rule 6, adopted August 1, 2018, effective July 1, 2019 (the version linked from the District's current Rule 6-6 page; amendments were under development in 2026).

rules.title: Contractor's license bond: $25,000
rules.plain_english: Every active license must have a $25,000 contractor's bond (or cashier's check) on file with CSLB to be issued, reinstated, reactivated, renewed, or kept active. An inactive license does not need the bond.
rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees with an active license (sole owner, partnership, corporation, LLC, joint venture)
rules.source: PDF page 295 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Contractors/Maintain_License/Bond_Information/Bond_Requirements.aspx
rules.quote: The board shall require as a condition precedent to the issuance, reinstatement, reactivation, renewal, or continued maintenance of a license, that the applicant or licensee file or have on file a contractor's bond in the sum of twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000).
rules.notes: Subdivision (c): bond not required while license is inactive. The $15,000 pre-2023 amount is from general knowledge of the repealed version (repealed 1/1/2023 per the law book history note) and is not needed for calculations. Bond must be from a surety admitted by the CA Department of Insurance, on an Attorney General-approved form (CSLB Bond Requirements page).
rules.correction: The $15,000 pre-2023 amount is not in the law book text; an official-domain search (leginfo SB 607 / CSLB notice) agrees it was $15,000 before 1/1/2023.

rules.title: Bond: $7,500 cap for all claimants except home-improvement homeowners
rules.plain_english: Of the $25,000 contractor's bond, the surety's total liability to everyone EXCEPT homeowners who contracted for home improvement on their own residence (B&P 7071.5(a)) is capped at $7,500. The remaining $17,500 is reserved exclusively for those home-improvement homeowners, who may recover up to the full bond. Single-family-home owners, fraud victims, unpaid employees and fringe-benefit trusts share the $7,500.

parameters.priority_beneficiaries: homeowners contracting for home improvement upon the homeowner's personal family residence (7071.5(a))
capped_nonpriority_beneficiaries: single-family dwelling owners not building for sale (7071.5(b))
persons damaged by willful and deliberate violation or fraud (7071.5(c))
fringe-benefit payees, e.g. union trust funds (7071.5(e))

rules.applies_to: Claims against any contractor's license bond
rules.source: PDF page 295 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: Excluding the claims brought by the beneficiaries specified in subdivision (a) of Section 7071.5, the aggregate liability of a surety on claims brought against a bond required by this section shall not exceed the sum of seven thousand five hundred dollars ($7,500).
rules.notes: 7071.6(b) cross-references "subdivision (a) of Section 7071.5". In 7071.5, subdivision (a) is only home-improvement homeowners. (b)-(e) are separate subdivisions and are not priority. Reserved amount $17,500 derived (25,000 - 7,500).
rules.correction: 7071.6(b) reserves the excess over $7,500 only for beneficiaries in SUBDIVISION (a) of 7071.5, which is just homeowners contracting for home improvement on their own residence. 7071.5(b)-(e) are separate subdivisions (single-family-dwelling owners, willful-violation/fraud victims, unpaid employees, fringe-benefit payees), and they share the $7,500 cap. The extract read the reference as 7071.5(a)-(e) and listed all five groups as priority. Fixed priority_beneficiaries_section, plain_english and notes. Rewording 2026-11-27: title reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: Who the contractor's bond protects
rules.plain_english: The license bond pays: homeowners hurt by license-law violations on their own home, owners building a single-family home not for sale, anyone hurt by willful violations or fraud, unpaid employees, and fringe-benefit funds owed employer payments.
rules.applies_to: All contractor's bonds and qualifying individual's bonds
rules.source: PDF page 294 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); PDF page 300 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: The contractor's bond shall be for the benefit of the following: (a) A homeowner contracting for home improvement upon the homeowner's personal family residence damaged as a result of a violation of this chapter by the licensee.
rules.notes: Bond must be executed by an admitted surety in favor of the State of California and filed with the registrar. Same beneficiary list applies to the qualifying individual's bond (7071.10).

rules.title: Double bond ($50,000) for applicants with unlicensed-contracting history
rules.plain_english: CSLB can make a new applicant post twice the normal bond until first renewal if they were convicted of unlicensed contracting or had a final unlicensed citation that caused substantial public injury.

triggers: citation under B&P 7028.7 reduced to final order

rules.applies_to: License applicants with a prior 7028 conviction or final 7028.7 citation
rules.source: PDF page 295 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: the board may require an applicant to post a contractor's bond in twice the amount required pursuant to subdivision (a) until the time that the license is renewed
rules.notes: Discretionary ('may'). $50,000 derived as 2 x $25,000.

rules.title: LLC employee/worker bond: $100,000
rules.plain_english: An LLC license needs an extra $100,000 surety bond (on top of the $25,000 contractor bond) that protects workers against unpaid wages, interest on wages and fringe benefits. If the LLC is under a union agreement, the bond also covers welfare, pension and apprentice contributions.
rules.applies_to: Limited liability company licensees
rules.source: PDF page 296 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); https://www.cslb.ca.gov/About_Us/LLC.aspx
rules.quote: The board shall require, as a condition precedent to the issuance, reissuance, reinstatement, reactivation, renewal, or continued valid use of a limited liability company license, that the applicant or licensee file or have on file a surety bond in the sum of one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000).
rules.notes: Statute (e) says not applicable while license is inactive; CSLB LLC page sentence first says required for 'both active and inactive licenses' then '(not required for inactive LLC licenses)' - follow the statute (inactive exempt).

rules.title: LLC liability insurance: $1M + $100K per extra person, max $5M
rules.plain_english: An LLC licensee must carry liability insurance for its contracting work with an aggregate limit of at least $1,000,000 if 5 or fewer people are on its personnel of record, plus $100,000 more for each additional person, capped at $5,000,000 per policy period.
rules.applies_to: Limited liability company licensees (issuance, reinstatement, reactivation, continued valid use)
rules.source: PDF page 307 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); PDF page 43 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); https://www.cslb.ca.gov/About_Us/LLC.aspx
rules.quote: (1) For a limited liability company licensee with five or fewer persons listed on the members of the personnel of record, the aggregate limit shall not be less than one million dollars ($1,000,000).
rules.notes: Statute text says '$100,000 ... for each person listed on the personnel of record'; CSLB law book narrative (p.43) and CSLB LLC page read it as each ADDITIONAL person beyond five - formula follows CSLB. Required in addition to bonds. Cap is 'in any one designated period, less amounts paid in defending, settling, or discharging claims'.
rules.correction: Formula follows CSLB reading (each ADDITIONAL person beyond five), which the CSLB LLC page and law book p.43 both state; statute text says "for each person listed" - ambiguity already noted.

rules.title: LLC insurance: policy form, insurer and period rules
rules.plain_english: The LLC policy can be claims-made or occurrence, must cover a 'designated period' of no more than 12 months, and must come from a California-admitted insurer or an eligible surplus line insurer. Deductibles/self-insured retentions are allowed.

insurer_types_allowed: admitted (licensed by CA Dept. of Insurance)

rules.applies_to: LLC licensees
rules.source: PDF page 308 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); https://www.cslb.ca.gov/About_Us/LLC.aspx
rules.quote: For purposes of this section, "designated period" means a policy year or any other period designated in the policy that is not greater than 12 months.
rules.notes: Admitted/surplus line wording effective 1/1/2014 per CSLB LLC page (AB 1236).

rules.title: LLC insurance: restore full limit by next policy period or suspension
rules.plain_english: If claims use up the LLC's aggregate limit, it need not buy more for that period, but the full required limit must be back in place by the start of the next designated period or the license is suspended by law.

parameters.reinstate_by: commencement date of next designated period
parameters.consequence: license suspended by operation of law until compliant

rules.applies_to: LLC licensees whose aggregate limit is impaired or exhausted
rules.source: PDF page 308 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: the aggregate limit of liability coverage (coverage limit) required by this section shall be reinstated by not later than the commencement date of the next designated period, and the license of any licensee that fails to comply with this provision shall be suspended by operation of law

rules.title: LLC dissolution: keep 3-year extended reporting (tail) coverage
rules.plain_english: When an LLC dissolves and winds up, it must keep or buy an extended reporting period endorsement at the full required aggregate limit for at least three years, if reasonably available.

parameters.trigger: dissolution and winding up of the LLC
parameters.limit: maximum total aggregate limit required by 7071.19
parameters.condition: if reasonably available from the insurer

rules.applies_to: Dissolving LLC licensees
rules.source: PDF page 308 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: maintain or obtain an extended reporting period endorsement or equivalent provision in the maximum total aggregate limit of liability required to comply with this section for a minimum of three years if reasonably available from the insurer.

rules.title: LLC insurance: file Certificate of Liability Insurance with CSLB
rules.plain_english: Before an LLC license is issued, reinstated or reactivated, the LLC must prove its liability coverage; a Certificate of Liability Insurance signed by the insurer's authorized agent must be submitted to CSLB, and the insurer reports policy dates, claim payments and cancellations.

parameters.signed_by: authorized agent or employee of the insurer
insurer_reports: date and amount of claim payments

rules.applies_to: LLC applicants/licensees
rules.source: PDF page 308 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-309
rules.quote: For any insurance policy secured by a licensee in satisfaction of this section, a Certificate of Liability Insurance, signed by an authorized agent or employee of the insurer, shall be submitted electronically or otherwise to the registrar.
rules.notes: Registrar may post insurer name, policy numbers and aggregate limits on the public license record.

rules.title: Bond of qualifying individual: $25,000
rules.plain_english: If the license qualifier (RME or RMO etc.) is not the sole owner, a general partner or a joint licensee, that qualifier must file a separate $25,000 qualifying individual's bond in addition to the contractor's bond. Each qualifier on the license needs one.
rules.applies_to: Corporations, LLCs and other licensees qualified by someone other than the owner/general partner
rules.source: PDF page 298 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-299; https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Contractors/Maintain_License/Bond_Information/Bond_Requirements.aspx
rules.quote: the qualifying individual shall file or have on file a qualifying individual's bond as provided in Section 7071.10 in the sum of twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000). This bond is in addition to, and shall not be combined with, any contractor's bond required by Sections 7071.5 to 7071.8, inclusive
rules.notes: CSLB: 'If a license has more than one RME or RMO qualifying the license, each qualifier must comply with the qualifier bonding requirements.' Bond must show business name, license number and qualifier name exactly as on CSLB records.
rules.correction: Note: the $7,500 non-priority cap in 7071.9(b) reserves the excess for the 7071.10 homeowner beneficiaries (home improvement on own residence), same structure as 7071.6(b); exemption also requires the owner certification form.

rules.title: Qualifier bond exemption for 10%+ owners (RMO/LLC qualifier)
rules.plain_english: An RMO who owns at least 10% of the corporation's voting stock, or an LLC qualifier who owns at least 10% of the membership interest, does not need the qualifier bond if they certify ownership on CSLB's form. If ownership drops below 10%, the bond is needed immediately.

parameters.certification_form: Bond of Qualifying Individual Exemption Certification
parameters.on_ownership_drop: bond suspension effective from date ownership requirement no longer exists

rules.applies_to: Corporate RMOs and LLC qualifiers
rules.source: PDF page 299 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Contractors/Maintain_License/Bond_Information/Bond_Suspensions.aspx
rules.quote: The responsible managing officer of a corporation shall not be required to file or have on file a qualifying individual's bond, if the responsible managing officer owns 10 percent or more of the voting stock of the corporation and certifies to that fact on a form prescribed by the registrar.
rules.notes: Changes to the qualifying individual bond exemption must be reported within 90 days (7083). CSLB Bond Suspensions page: suspension when RMO 'no longer owns at least 10 percent'.

rules.title: Bond must reach CSLB within 90 days of its effective date
rules.plain_english: CSLB accepts a bond as of the effective date printed on it only if CSLB receives it within 90 days of that date; then the license is reinstated back to that date. Late bonds are accepted retroactively only if you show circumstances beyond your control (form 13B-31).

parameters.measured_from: effective date shown on the bond

rules.applies_to: All bonded licensees
rules.source: PDF page 296 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Contractors/Maintain_License/Bond_Information/Bond_Suspensions.aspx
rules.quote: the registrar shall accept a bond required by Section 7071.6, 7071.6.5, 7071.8, or 7071.9 as of the effective date shown on the bond, if the bond is received by the registrar within 90 days after that date
rules.notes: CSLB: a surety rescission notice must also be received within 90 days of the bond cancellation date to lift a bond suspension.

rules.title: Bond cancellation: license suspended 30 days after CSLB gets notice
rules.plain_english: When a surety cancels your bond, the cancellation takes effect 30 days after CSLB receives the notice. If no reinstatement or replacement bond reaches CSLB in that window, the license is suspended; work while suspended is unlicensed.

parameters.measured_from: date CSLB receives surety cancellation notice

rules.applies_to: All bonded licensees
rules.citation: B&P 7071.15 (suspension for failure to maintain bond); CSLB Bond Basics
rules.source: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Contractors/Bond_Basics.aspx; PDF page 303 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: A license bond is canceled 30 days from the date that CSLB receives a cancellation notice from a bond company. If a bond reinstatement notice or replacement bond is not received by CSLB before the end of the 30-day period, the license is suspended.
rules.notes: CSLB advises arranging a new bond four weeks before the old one expires and matching the new bond's effective date to the old bond's cancellation date. Bond and license renewal dates usually differ.

rules.title: Bond details must match CSLB records exactly
rules.plain_english: The bond must show the business name and license number exactly as on CSLB's records (plus the qualifier's name on a qualifier bond), be signed by the surety's attorney-in-fact, and be on an Attorney General-approved form. Only one bond can be in effect at a time; bonds are not transferable.

parameters.form: approved by the Attorney General's Office
parameters.surety: licensed by CA Department of Insurance

rules.applies_to: All bonded licensees
rules.quote: The business name and license number on the bond must correspond exactly with the business name and license number on the CSLB's records.
rules.notes: 'Only one bond can be in effect at a time. A second bond filed for the same period cancels out the first bond.'

rules.title: Bond alternative: cashier's check only; held 3 years
rules.plain_english: Instead of a surety bond you may deposit a cashier's or bank-certified check for the full bond amount payable to CSLB. CDs, passbooks and similar deposits are no longer accepted. The deposit cannot be released until 3 years after the license period it covers ends, or 3 years after the license is inactivated, expires, or is canceled or revoked, whichever comes first, and it is held longer if a claim is pending.

parameters.payee_text: Payable to the Contractors State License Board

rules.applies_to: Licensees using a deposit instead of a surety bond
rules.source: PDF page 292 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Contractors/Maintain_License/Bond_Information/Bond_Alternatives.aspx
rules.quote: no other method of deposit, including, but not limited to, a certificate of deposit, shall satisfy a bond requirement under this article.
rules.notes: 3-year hold period is from CSLB's Bond Alternatives page ('three (3) years after the expiration of the license period ... or three (3) years following license inactivation, expiration, cancellation or revocation, whichever occurs first'). 16 CCR 856 in the law book still describes certificates of deposit, which 7071.4 no longer allows.
rules.correction: Release timing is 3 years after expiration of the covered license period or 3 years after inactivation/expiration/cancellation/revocation, whichever occurs FIRST, so it can be earlier than "3 years after the license period ends". Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction (CSLB Bond Alternatives page re-read on 2026-11-27); no value changed.

rules.title: Bond: each wage/fringe claim capped at $4,000
rules.plain_english: A surety's liability on any one claim for wages and fringe benefits against a license bond (other than a disciplinary bond) is capped at $4,000. If the bond cannot pay all claims in full, claimants share it pro rata. On the $25,000 contractor bond, wage claimants are also inside the $7,500 non-priority pool (B&P 7071.6(b)).

parameters.cap_scope: per claim: the statute caps aggregate liability "on a claim for wages and fringe benefits" (wages plus fringe combined); it is not a ceiling on total wage payouts across all claims

rules.applies_to: Claims against contractor and qualifier bonds
rules.source: PDF page 300 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-301
rules.quote: The aggregate liability of a surety on a claim for wages and fringe benefits brought against a bond required by this article, other than a bond required by Section 7071.8, shall not exceed the sum of four thousand dollars ($4,000).
rules.notes: "On a claim" (singular) contrasts with 7071.6(b)'s "on claims" aggregate cap, so the $4,000 is per claim. The LLC $100,000 worker bond (7071.6.5) is in the same article. Whether the $4,000 per-claim cap also limits claims on that bond is not addressed. Verify before relying.
rules.correction: The statute caps the surety's aggregate liability "on a claim" for wages and fringe benefits at $4,000. That is a per-claim cap (wages plus fringe combined), not a $4,000 ceiling on total wage payouts from the bond. Compare 7071.6(b), which uses "on claims" for its aggregate $7,500 cap. Rewrote plain_english and added cap_scope. Wage claimants also fall inside the $7,500 non-priority pool of the $25,000 contractor bond. Rewording 2026-11-27: title reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: Deadlines to sue on a license bond
rules.plain_english: Most bond claims must be filed within 2 years after the end of the license period when the act happened (or 2 years after the license would have expired if it was inactivated/cancelled/revoked). Wage and fringe claims must be brought within 6 months of discovering the shortfall and never more than 2 years after the pay was due.
rules.applies_to: Claimants against license bonds; contractors tracking exposure
rules.source: PDF page 301 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: A claim to recover wages or fringe benefits shall be brought within six months from the date that the wage or fringe benefit delinquencies were discovered, but in no event shall a civil action thereon be brought later than two years from the date the wage or fringe benefit contributions were due.

rules.title: Bond claim: 15 days to protest; 90 days to repay surety
rules.plain_english: Before a surety settles a bond claim in good faith, you get at least 15 days to file a written protest. If you do not protest, you have 90 days from CSLB's notice to prove you repaid the surety (and any excess judgment) or the license is suspended automatically.

parameters.consequence: automatic suspension; disclosed indefinitely as failure to settle outstanding final liabilities

rules.applies_to: Licensees whose bond receives a claim
rules.source: PDF page 301 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-302
rules.quote: Prior to the settlement of a claim through a good faith payment by the surety, a licensee shall have not less than 15 days in which to provide a written protest.
rules.notes: Surety must notify the registrar within 30 days of any payment (7071.11(e)). A notarized accord with the surety may be filed in lieu of full payment; breaking the accord causes automatic suspension.
rules.correction: The 90-day repayment window applies to a licensee that did NOT file a protest (7071.11(f)(2)).

rules.title: Report unsatisfied construction judgments within 90 days; post judgment bond
rules.plain_english: You must tell CSLB in writing within 90 days about any unsatisfied final judgment against you related to construction (including final arbitration awards). Then you must file a bond equal to the unpaid judgments within 90 days of CSLB's notice (or file a notarized accord), or the license is suspended.

parameters.bond_amount: equal to all unsatisfied final judgments
alternatives: notarized copy of accord with judgment creditor
parameters.late_notice_consequence: automatic suspension on date registrar learns of judgment

rules.applies_to: All licensees with unsatisfied final judgments for failing to pay a contractor, sub, consumer, supplier or employee
rules.source: PDF page 304 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-306
rules.quote: all licensees shall notify the registrar in writing of any unsatisfied final judgment imposed on the licensee. If the licensee fails to notify the registrar in writing within 90 days, the license shall be automatically suspended on the date that the registrar is informed, or is made aware of the unsatisfied final judgment.
rules.notes: Personnel of record at the time are barred from serving on any other license until satisfied (7071.17(j)). Judgments discharged in bankruptcy generally excluded (f).
rules.correction: bond_min_on_file_years (1) is stated in 7071.17(a) for applicants; for licensees under (b) the bond stays in force until the debt is satisfied (7071.17(g)).

rules.title: Disciplinary bond: $25,000 to 10x, at least 2 years
rules.plain_english: After a suspension or revocation for discipline, the registrar sets a disciplinary bond of at least $25,000 and at most 10 times the contractor bond ($250,000), kept on file at least 2 years while the license is active and in good standing. It is in addition to all other bonds.
rules.applies_to: Licensees/applicants with disciplined (suspended or revoked) licenses and associated personnel
rules.source: PDF page 298 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Contractors/Maintain_License/Bond_Information/Bond_Requirements.aspx
rules.quote: which sum shall not be less than twenty-five thousand dollars ($25,000) nor more than 10 times that amount required by Section 7071.6.
rules.notes: $250,000 derived as 10 x $25,000. Bond period runs only while license is current, active and in good standing.

rules.title: Do not advertise that you are 'bonded' (license bond)
rules.plain_english: Referring to your license bond (or a disciplinary bond) in ads, solicitations or presentations to the public is grounds for discipline and license suspension.

applies_when_reference_is_to: any bond required by the chapter (7071.13)

rules.applies_to: All licensees' advertising
rules.source: PDF page 303 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); PDF page 243 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/AdvertisingGuidelines.pdf
rules.quote: Any reference by a contractor in his advertising, soliciting, or other presentments to the public to any bond required to be filed pursuant to this chapter is a ground for the suspension of the license of such contractor.
rules.notes: A project-specific performance/payment bond is not a license bond; the prohibition targets license-law bonds. CSLB Advertising Guidelines: 'The law prevents you from noting in your advertising or any presentation to the public that you are bonded.'

rules.title: CGL insurance not required by license law (except LLCs)
rules.plain_english: State license law does not require general liability insurance unless the licensee is an LLC; but you must disclose whether you carry it on home improvement and single-family contracts, and many commercial owners require it.
rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.source: PDF page 43 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: Contractors State License Law does not require contractors to carry CGL insurance unless their business entity is a limited liability company (see below).

rules.title: CGL disclosure statement with every home improvement bid and contract
rules.plain_english: Every home improvement estimate/bid and every home improvement contract must be accompanied by CSLB's 'Information About Commercial General Liability Insurance' statement, checking whether you do or do not carry CGL and, if you do, giving the insurer's name and phone number. Heading 14-point, questions 12-point, comments 11-point italics.

attach_to: every estimate (bid) intended to result in a home improvement contract
parameters.heading_text: Information About Commercial General Liability Insurance Home Improvement
checkbox_options: does not carry Commercial General Liability Insurance
carries Commercial General Liability Insurance (insurer name + telephone)

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors
rules.citation: 16 CCR 872(a); B&P 7159.3 (as cited in the form)
rules.source: PDF page 535 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-536
rules.quote: The following statement, must accompany every estimate (bid) intended to result in a home improvement contract and every home improvement contract. The heading shall be printed in at least 14-point type, the questions in at least 12-point type, and the comments in italics of at least 11-point type.
rules.notes: Full form text (Q&A) on PDF pages 535-536 can be reproduced verbatim by a document generator. Form cites B&P 7159.3, which no longer appears in the 2026 code listing; current contract-level notice is in B&P 7159(e)(1).

rules.title: CGL disclosure statement for single-family home construction contracts
rules.plain_english: Contracts to build a single-family home for an owner who will keep it at least a year must include CSLB's CGL disclosure statement (Single Family Home version), with the same font-size rules, and state whether you carry CGL and the insurer's contact.

parameters.attach_to: every contract described in B&P 7164 (single-family dwelling retained by owner >= 1 year)
parameters.heading_text: Information About Commercial General Liability Insurance Single Family Home

rules.applies_to: Contractors building single-family dwellings for owner-occupants
rules.source: PDF page 536 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-538; PDF page 426 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: Contractors building single-family residences for owners who intend to occupy the home for at least a year are required by law to tell you whether or not they carry Commercial General Liability Insurance. This written statement must accompany the contract.
rules.notes: 7164 also requires the contract and all changes in writing signed by both parties, with name/address/license number, approximate start and completion dates, legal description, and Mechanics Lien Warning.

rules.title: Home improvement contract: CGL notice (4 statement options)
rules.plain_english: Each home improvement contract must include (or attach, with a reference line) a notice headed 'Commercial General Liability Insurance (CGL)' with the one true statement: no CGL; CGL with insurer and phone; self-insured; or LLC carrying insurance/security required by law with phone to verify.

parameters.heading: Commercial General Liability Insurance (CGL)
parameters.attachment_reference_text: A notice concerning commercial general liability insurance is attached to this contract.

options.A: (The name on the license or 'This contractor') does not carry commercial general liability insurance.
options.B: (The name on the license or 'This contractor') carries commercial general liability insurance written by (the insurance company). You may call (the insurance company) at __________ to check the contractor's insurance coverage.
options.C: (The name on the license or 'This contractor') is self-insured.
options.D: (The name on the license or 'This contractor') is a limited liability company that carries liability insurance or maintains other security as required by law. You may call (the insurance company or trust company or bank) at ____ to check on the contractor's insurance coverage or security.

parameters.selection_rule: whichever statement is both relevant and correct

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts (B&P 7151.2)
rules.source: PDF page 401 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: The notice shall include the heading "Commercial General Liability Insurance (CGL)," followed by whichever of the following statements is both relevant and correct: (A) "(The name on the license or 'This contractor') does not carry commercial general liability insurance."
rules.notes: Exception: as provided in 7159.5(a)(8). CSLB LLC page: 'Specific general liability insurance information is required to be included on the LLC's home improvement and service and repair contracts.'
rules.correction: The option texts were stored as predicate fragments without the required subject "(The name on the license or 'This contractor')", and option B paraphrased "(the insurance company)" as "(insurer)". Replaced all four options with the verbatim statutory statements. llc_must_use_option "D" is an inference: the statute says use whichever statement is "both relevant and correct".

rules.title: Home improvement contract: workers' compensation notice
rules.plain_english: Each home improvement contract must include (or attach, with a reference line) a notice headed 'Workers' Compensation Insurance' stating either that the contractor has no employees and is exempt, or carries workers' comp for all employees.

parameters.heading: Workers' Compensation Insurance
parameters.attachment_reference_text: A notice concerning workers' compensation insurance is attached to this contract.

options.A: (The name on the license or 'This contractor') has no employees and is exempt from workers' compensation requirements.
options.B: (The name on the license or 'This contractor') carries workers' compensation insurance for all employees.

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts
rules.source: PDF page 401 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-402
rules.quote: "(The name on the license or 'This contractor') has no employees and is exempt from workers' compensation requirements." (B) "(The name on the license or 'This contractor') carries workers' compensation insurance for all employees."
rules.notes: Option A must not be used by C-8, C-20, C-22, C-39 or D-49 licensees or RME-qualified licenses (they cannot hold an exemption) and, from 1/1/2028, by most licensees (see wc-exemption-ends-2028).
rules.correction: The options were stored without the statutory subject "(The name on the license or 'This contractor')". Replaced them with the full verbatim statements.

rules.title: Service & repair contracts ($750 or less): CGL and WC notices
rules.plain_english: Service and repair contracts (jobs of $750 or less that the buyer asked for, where you sell nothing beyond what is reasonably needed to fix that problem and take no payment until the work is done) must also carry the CGL notice (4 options) and the workers' comp notice (2 options). Use the wording in B&P 7159.10(d)(7)-(8), which differs slightly from the home improvement notices.
rules.applies_to: Service and repair contracts under B&P 7159.10
rules.source: PDF page 414 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-416
