rules.quote: (7) A notice concerning commercial general liability insurance. This notice may be provided as an attachment to the contract if the contract includes the statement, "A notice concerning commercial general liability insurance is attached to this contract."
rules.correction: Wording note: 7159.10(d)(7)(B) reads "You may call the (insurance company) at ___", a trivial variant of 7159(e)(1)(B); generate service/repair notices from 7159.10 text. The (a)(1) definition also requires no upselling and no payment until the work is completed. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction (B&P 7159.10(a)(1) re-read in sources/lawbook.txt on 2026-11-27); no value changed.

rules.title: Advertising 'insured' must name the insurance type
rules.plain_english: If you advertise that you are 'insured,' the ad must say what kind of insurance (for example 'commercial general liability insurance' or 'workers' compensation insurance'); abbreviations are allowed.
rules.applies_to: All licensees' advertising (cards, signs, vehicles, print, web/electronic, directories)
rules.source: PDF page 243 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: It is a cause for discipline for any contractor to advertise that he or she is "insured" or has insurance without identifying in the advertisement the type of insurance, including, for example, "commercial general liability insurance" or "workers' compensation insurance" that is carried by the contractor.

rules.title: Keep a workers' comp certificate (or exemption) on file with CSLB
rules.plain_english: To get, renew, reactivate or keep an active license you must have on file at all times a current Certificate of Workers' Compensation Insurance (filed by your insurer) or DIR Certificate of Self-Insurance in your business name - or, if you truly have no employees and hold no mandatory class, a signed exemption. Inactive licenses need neither.

accepted_documents: Certificate of Workers' Compensation Insurance (filed by CA-licensed WC insurer)
Certification of Self-Insurance (Director of Industrial Relations)
exemption_conditions: no employees subject to CA workers' comp law
no C-8, C-20, C-22, C-39 or D-49 classification

rules.applies_to: All active licensees and applicants for active licenses
rules.source: PDF page 365 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-366; https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Contractors/Maintain_License/Workers_Compensation.aspx
rules.quote: the board shall require as a condition precedent to the issuance, reinstatement, reactivation, renewal, or continued maintenance of a license, that the applicant or licensee have on file at all times a current and valid Certificate of Workers' Compensation Insurance or Certification of Self-Insurance in the applicant's or licensee's business name.
rules.notes: This version is repealed 1/1/2028 (SB 1455, Stats 2024 ch 485). Joint ventures with no employees may also file the statement (7125(c)). B&P 7125.7: CSLB must set up an audit/verification process for no-employee exemptions by 1/1/2027.

rules.title: C-8, C-20, C-22, C-39 and D-49 must carry workers' comp even with no employees
rules.plain_english: Concrete (C-8), HVAC (C-20), Asbestos Abatement (C-22), Roofing (C-39) and Tree Service (C-61/D-49) licensees cannot file a no-employee exemption; they must carry workers' comp or self-insurance. If such a licensee also holds other classes and lacks a certificate, CSLB removes the mandatory class instead of suspending the whole license.

parameters.multi_class_consequence: mandatory classification removed from license unless certificate received (C-39 since 1/1/2013; C-8, C-20, C-22, D-49 after 7/1/2023)

rules.applies_to: Licensees holding any listed classification
rules.source: PDF page 365 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-367; PDF page 45 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: Does not hold a C-8 license, as defined in Section 832.08 of Title 16 of the California Code of Regulations, a C-20 license, ... a C-22 license, ... a C-39 license, ... or a D-49 license, a subcategory of a C-61 license
rules.notes: Quote abbreviated with ellipses (removes the CCR cross-references). Out-of-state licensees with these classes whose employees do not reside in CA use exemption form 13L-50 plus home-state WC certificate (CSLB WC page).

rules.title: From Jan 1, 2028: no-employee exemption ends (except joint ventures)
rules.plain_english: Starting January 1, 2028, the no-employees exemption disappears for ordinary licensees: every active license must have a workers' comp certificate or self-insurance certificate on file. Only a joint-venture license with no employees can still file an exemption statement.

parameters.exemption_remaining_for: joint venture licenses (B&P 7029) with no employees
parameters.required_document: Certificate of Workers' Compensation Insurance or Certification of Self-Insurance

rules.applies_to: All active CSLB licensees (sole owners, partnerships, corporations, LLCs) other than no-employee joint ventures
rules.source: PDF page 367 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-368
rules.quote: This section does not apply to an applicant or licensee organized as a joint venture pursuant to Section 7029 that has no employees, provided that the applicant or licensee files a statement with the board
rules.notes: SB 216 originally made this operative 1/1/2026; SB 1455 (2024) delayed it to 1/1/2028 per the law book history notes. A compliance tool should warn exempt sole owners to budget for a WC policy before 1/1/2028. Watch for further legislative delay.

rules.title: Cannot use the WC exemption if you have employees, an RME, or salespersons
rules.plain_english: You may not file (or keep) a workers' comp exemption if you employ anyone covered by CA workers' comp, if the license is qualified by a Responsible Managing Employee (the RME is an employee), or if you employ home improvement salespersons.

exemption_barred_if: any employee subject to CA workers' comp law

rules.applies_to: Licensees considering or holding a WC exemption
rules.quote: If the license is qualified by a responsible managing employee (RME), CSLB will not accept an exemption certificate because the RME is an employee.
rules.notes: Quote from CSLB 'Get Licensed to Build' guide (Q4 Financial Requirements). The HIS trigger is from the same guide's list of when proof of WC is required ('You employ home improvement salesperson(s)').

rules.title: After hiring your first employee: get WC and file proof
rules.plain_english: An exemption on file becomes invalid the moment you hire someone covered by workers' comp. You must have coverage from that date and CSLB must receive proof within 90 days of the hire. Employing anyone after filing an exemption without first filing a certificate is cause for discipline.
rules.applies_to: Licensees with a WC exemption on file who hire
rules.citation: B&P 7125.1(a); B&P 7125.2(a)(2); B&P 7125.4(a); CSLB Workers' Compensation page
rules.source: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Contractors/Maintain_License/Workers_Compensation.aspx; PDF page 369 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-370
rules.quote: Upon employing anyone in a manner that is subject to the workers' compensation laws of California, the exemption form on file will no longer be valid and you will be required to obtain and submit proof of workers' compensation insurance coverage. This proof must be received at CSLB's Headquarters within 90 days of the hire.
rules.notes: Coverage itself must start before the employee works; 7125.2 suspends the license on the date coverage is required.
rules.correction: The citation omitted B&P 7125.1(a), the statutory source of the 90-day window (a certificate received within 90 days of its effective date is accepted retroactively). 7125.4(a) only supports the discipline sentence. Added 7125.1(a). The parameters were correct.

rules.title: WC certificate accepted retroactively if received within 90 days
rules.plain_english: CSLB accepts a workers' comp certificate as of its effective date (and reinstates the license back to that date) if received within 90 days; later filings are retroactive only for circumstances beyond your control.

parameters.measured_from: effective date shown on the certificate
parameters.late_exception: circumstances beyond licensee's control (form acceptable to registrar)

rules.applies_to: Licensees filing WC certificates
rules.source: PDF page 368 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-370
rules.quote: The registrar shall accept a certificate required by Section 7125 as of the effective date shown on the certificate, if the certificate is received by the registrar within 90 days after that date, and shall reinstate the license to which the certificate pertains, if otherwise eligible, retroactive to the effective date of the certificate.
rules.notes: 7125.3: contractor is considered duly licensed during periods the registrar must accept the certificate.

rules.title: Workers' comp lapse = automatic license suspension
rules.plain_english: If required coverage lapses (or is never obtained when required), the license is automatically suspended as of the lapse date or the date coverage was required, whichever is earlier. CSLB may post a pending suspension up to 45 days before; work while suspended is unlicensed.

parameters.suspension_effective: earlier of coverage lapse date or date coverage required

rules.applies_to: Licensees required to carry WC
rules.source: PDF page 369 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-370
rules.quote: The failure of a licensee to obtain or maintain workers' compensation insurance coverage, if required under this chapter, shall result in the automatic suspension of the license by operation of law

rules.title: False WC exemption / uninsured employees: $10K-$30K CSLB penalties
rules.plain_english: Filing a false exemption, or employing workers without coverage, brings minimum civil penalties of $10,000 per violation for a sole owner and $20,000 for a partnership, corporation, LLC or tribal business, with total penalties up to $30,000 per occurrence. The qualifier can be charged with a misdemeanor, and the license will not be renewed until a valid certificate is filed.
rules.applies_to: Licensees employing workers without WC or with a false exemption
rules.source: PDF page 370 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); PDF page 541 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: (1) A minimum civil penalty of ten thousand dollars ($10,000) per violation for any sole owner licensee found to have employed workers without maintaining workers' compensation coverage. (2) A minimum civil penalty of twenty thousand dollars ($20,000) per violation for any partnership, corporation, limited liability company, or tribal business licensee
rules.notes: B&P 7126: violations of the article are misdemeanors; prosecution within 2 years. DIR/Labor Code penalties (LC 3700.5, 3722) are separate (see labor-hr research file).
rules.correction: Statutory minimums ($10,000 / $20,000) override the $200 regulatory floor in 16 CCR 884.

rules.title: At every renewal: recertify WC exemption or file certificate
rules.plain_english: When renewing, an active licensee with an exemption must recertify it on the renewal form or file a current WC certificate; otherwise the renewal is rejected. If the missing item arrives within 30 days of CSLB's rejection notice, renewal is retroactive.
rules.applies_to: Active licensees with WC exemption
rules.source: PDF page 371 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: The license shall not be renewed unless a licensee with an exemption for workers' compensation insurance on file with the board recertifies the exemption status or provides a current and valid Certificate of Workers' Compensation Insurance or Certificate of Self-Insurance in conjunction with the license renewal.

rules.title: At renewal: report your top 3 WC classification codes
rules.plain_english: Licensees with a WC policy must list on the renewal form the three workers' comp classification codes with the highest estimated payroll on the policy (all codes if fewer than three). CSLB shows them on the public license record and will not renew without them (30-day cure).

parameters.ranking: highest estimated payroll on the policy

rules.applies_to: Active licensees with or required to have WC coverage
rules.source: PDF page 371 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-372
rules.quote: shall certify on the license renewal form for the three workers' compensation classification codes for which the highest estimated payroll is reported on the policy. If the licensee has fewer than three classification codes reported on the policy, the licensee shall provide every classification code reported on the policy.
rules.notes: Added by AB 336 (Stats 2023 ch 323).

rules.title: WC certificate filed with CSLB: required fields
rules.plain_english: The insurer-issued certificate must list CSLB as certificate holder and show your exact business name, license (or application) number, policy number, policy effective and expiration dates, and an authorized insurer signature. Only CA-licensed WC insurers can file.

required_fields: license number (or application fee number if not yet issued)
parameters.filer: insurer licensed by CA Department of Insurance

rules.applies_to: Licensees filing WC certificates
rules.quote: CSLB must be listed as the Certificate Holder.
rules.notes: Common rejection reasons per CSLB: wrong business name, wrong insurer name, wrong policy number, CSLB not listed as holder, invalid signature.

rules.title: Workers' comp required with even one employee
rules.plain_english: Any employer, including a contractor with just one part-time employee, must carry workers' compensation insurance (or be DIR-approved self-insured).
rules.applies_to: All employers (contractors)
rules.source: PDF page 44 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Contractors/Maintain_License/Workers_Compensation.aspx
rules.quote: If the employer has one or more employees, even part-time, they are required to insure for workers' compensation claims.
rules.notes: Labor Code penalties (stop orders, 3722 penalty assessments) are in the labor-hr research file.

rules.title: CSLB stop order for uninsured employers
rules.plain_english: CSLB can serve a stop order barring use of employee labor on an employer (licensed or not) without workers' comp. Affected employees must be paid for lost time up to 10 days. Ignoring the order is a misdemeanor (up to 60 days jail and/or $10,000). Protest within 20 days; hearing within 5 days.
rules.applies_to: Employers subject to licensure without WC (licensed or unlicensed)
rules.source: PDF page 373 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: An employee affected by the work stoppage shall be paid by the employer for his or her time lost, not exceeding 10 days, pending compliance by the employer.
rules.notes: DLSE has a parallel stop order power under Labor Code 3710.1.

rules.title: Building permit applications require a workers' comp declaration
rules.plain_english: When pulling a building permit, the applicant must declare workers' comp status (policy, self-insurance, or no employees) on the permit.

parameters.document: Declaration of Workers' Compensation on building permit application

rules.applies_to: Contractors pulling building permits
rules.citation: Health & Safety Code 19825 (cross-referenced in law book); Labor Code 3800
rules.source: PDF page 373 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: —See also Health and Safety Code Section 19825, Declaration of Worker's Compensation Required on Building Permits, in Appendix
rules.notes: Only the cross-reference title was read in the law book; the HSC 19825 / LC 3800 text itself was not fetched (leginfo blocked). Content of the declaration not verified - do not hard-code wording.

rules.title: Report license record changes to CSLB within 90 days
rules.plain_english: Tell CSLB in writing on its form within 90 days of any change in recorded information - business address, personnel, business name, qualifier bond exemption, or multiple-license qualifier exemption. Late notice makes the change effective only when CSLB receives it and is grounds for discipline.

parameters.late_effect: change effective on date CSLB HQ receives written notice

rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.source: PDF page 323 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); PDF page 540 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: licensees shall notify the registrar, on a form prescribed by the registrar, in writing within 90 days of any change to information recorded under this chapter.
rules.notes: 7083.1: expired/suspended/cancelled licensees must report address changes within 90 days and keep a current address for 5 years. 7083.2: report a valid email at application and renewal.

rules.title: Qualifier leaves: notify and replace within 90 days
rules.plain_english: If the RMO/RME/responsible managing member or manager leaves, notify CSLB within 90 days and replace the qualifier within 90 days of the departure, or the license is automatically suspended (or the class removed). One 90-day extension is possible only if you dispute the disassociation date, the qualifier died, or an agency processing delay outside your control occurred. The petition must be received within 90 days with a replacement application on file. Replacement fee $230.

extension_allowed_only_if: licensee disputes the date of disassociation
processing delay out of the applicant's control attributable to CSLB or another state/federal agency relied on
parameters.late_notice_effect: suspension/classification removal and qualifier removal effective the date CSLB HQ receives written notice; grounds for discipline

rules.applies_to: Corporations, LLCs, and other licensees qualified by an RMO/RME
rules.source: PDF page 288 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); PDF page 451 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: the licensee or the qualifier shall notify the registrar in writing within 90 days after the date of disassociation. The licensee shall have 90 days after the date of disassociation in which to replace the qualifier.
rules.notes: Qualifier remains responsible for construction operations until the later of disassociation or CSLB's receipt of notice (7068.2(d)).
rules.correction: The single 90-day extension is not available for good cause generally. 7068.2(e) allows it only when (A) the licensee disputes the disassociation date, (B) the qualifier died, or (C) a processing delay outside the applicant's control is attributable to CSLB or another agency it relies on. The petition must be received within 90 days and a replacement application must be on file. For (A) and (B) the total is capped at 180 days. Added these conditions to the parameters and plain_english.

rules.title: One qualifier, multiple firms: 20% common ownership, max 3 firms/year
rules.plain_english: A qualifier may qualify an additional firm only if there is at least 20% common ownership, a 20%-owned subsidiary/joint venture, or the same majority of partners/officers/managers - and never more than three firms in any one-year period. The qualifier must actually supervise and control construction operations.

parameters.qualifier_duty: supervision and control of construction operations

rules.applies_to: Qualifying individuals and the firms they qualify
rules.source: PDF page 287 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: Notwithstanding paragraphs (1) to (3), inclusive, of subdivision (a), a qualifying individual may act as the qualifier for no more than three firms in any one-year period.
rules.notes: Violation is a misdemeanor with fine of $3,000-$5,000 and/or up to 6 months jail (7068.1(e), PDF page 288).

rules.title: Corporations/LLCs must stay in good standing with the Secretary of State
rules.plain_english: A corporation or LLC license is automatically suspended 30 days after CSLB's notice if the entity is not registered and in good standing with the Secretary of State (e.g., missed Statement of Information or FTB suspension). During an LLC suspension, each officer/manager/member can be personally liable up to $1,000,000 for damages to third parties.

parameters.reinstatement: proof of SOS registration and good standing

rules.applies_to: Corporation and LLC licensees
rules.source: PDF page 320 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); https://www.cslb.ca.gov/About_Us/LLC.aspx
rules.quote: the licensee shall be suspended 30 days from the date of the notice if the licensee does not provide proof satisfactory to the registrar that it is properly registered and in good standing with the Secretary of State.
rules.notes: Personal liability does not apply where there has been substantial compliance under 7031(e). Not applicable to tribes.

rules.title: Entity events (death, dissolution, merger, partner exit): notify within 90 days
rules.plain_english: Individual licenses cancel on the owner's death (family may request a continuance within 90 days). Partnership licenses cancel when a general partner dies or leaves. Corporation and LLC licenses cancel on dissolution, merger or surrender of the right to do business in California. In each case CSLB must be told in writing within 90 days; continuance requests also within 90 days. If a corporation or LLC never tells CSLB, the license is canceled 60 days after the board discovers it. To dispute a cancellation date, a petition showing good cause must reach CSLB within 90 days of its cancellation notice.

events.individual_death: license canceled; family continuance request within 90 days; bond within 90 days of board notice
events.limited_partner_death_or_disassociation: notify within 90 days; canceled only if sole limited partner not replaced within 90 days

parameters.late_notice_effect: cancellation effective the date written notice is received at CSLB HQ; grounds for discipline

rules.applies_to: All licensee entity types
rules.source: PDF page 316 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-318
rules.quote: The corporation or participating tribe shall notify the registrar in writing within 90 days of the dissolution, merger, or surrender.
rules.notes: LLC subdivision (7076(i), PDF p.319) read: it parallels the corporation rule. If a corporation or LLC never notifies CSLB, the license is canceled 60 days after the board discovers it in SOS records. Continuances are available for individual, partnership and joint-venture licenses, not for corporations or LLCs.
rules.correction: The extract never read the LLC subdivision and only assumed it. It was read now: 7076(i) cancels an LLC license on dissolution, merger or surrender, with written notice due within 90 days. If the corporation or LLC never notifies CSLB, the license is canceled 60 days after the board discovers it (7076(h)-(i)). A cancellation-date dispute petition is due within 90 days of the board's notice (7076(j)). Added these to the parameters and replaced the "verify" note. The citation now reads (a)-(j). Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction (B&P 7076(h)-(j) re-read in sources/lawbook.txt on 2026-11-27); no value changed.

rules.title: License term: 2 years; renew before expiration
rules.plain_english: Contractor licenses expire two years from the last day of the month issued (or two years from last expiration). Renew before the expiration date on CSLB's form with the renewal fee.

parameters.expires: 2 years from last day of month of issuance or last expiration

rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.source: PDF page 383 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: All licenses issued under the provisions of this chapter shall expire two years from the last day of the month in which the license is issued, or two years from the date on which the renewed license last expired.

rules.title: Late renewal: 90-day retroactive window, 5-year limit
rules.plain_english: If you renew within 90 days after expiration (with renewal plus delinquency fee), CSLB renews retroactively with no gap. After that, renewal is effective only on filing and you were unlicensed in the gap; after 5 years you must apply for a new license. Incomplete timely renewals get a 30-day grace on the delinquency fee.
rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.source: PDF page 383 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-385
rules.quote: The registrar shall grant the retroactive renewal of a license if, within 90 days of the expiration of the license, the otherwise eligible licensee submits a completed application for renewal on a form prescribed by the registrar, and pays the appropriate renewal fee and delinquency fee prescribed by this chapter.

rules.title: CSLB fees (application, initial, renewal, HIS)
rules.plain_english: Key CSLB fees: original application $450; initial license $200 (sole owner) / $350 (others); active renewal $450 / $700 (delinquent $675 / $1,050); inactive renewal $300 / $500; additional class $230; replace qualifier $230; add personnel $125; HIS registration and renewal $200 (delinquent $300); business name change $100. C-10 electricians pay $20 more on active renewals.
rules.applies_to: All applicants, licensees and HIS registrants
rules.source: PDF page 451 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-452; https://www.cslb.ca.gov/About_Us/Library/Fees.aspx
rules.quote: (1) The renewal fee for an active license for an individual owner is $450. (2) The renewal fee for an inactive license for an individual owner is $300. (3) The renewal fee for an active license for a partnership, corporation, limited liability company, or joint venture is $700.
rules.notes: Delinquent and C-10 amounts are from CSLB's Fees page (read 2026-11-25), not 16 CCR 811. Fees are tied to postmark date.

rules.title: Inactive license: cannot contract; no bond/WC needed; 4-year validity
rules.plain_english: You may inactivate a license when not contracting. An inactive licensee may not bid or contract until reactivated; no contractor bond, qualifier bond, LLC bond or WC certificate/exemption is required while inactive. Inactive licenses are valid four years from their due date.
rules.applies_to: Licensees not currently contracting
rules.source: PDF page 320 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/GetLicensedToBuild_ENG0525_ADA.pdf (p.30)
rules.quote: The holder of an inactive license shall not be entitled to practice as a contractor until their license is reactivated.
rules.notes: Acting as a contractor under an inactive license is cause for discipline (7117.5(a)).

rules.title: Unpaid EDD, FTB, CDTFA/BOE or DIR debts can block renewal or suspend the license
rules.plain_english: CSLB may refuse to issue, renew or reactivate, or may suspend, a license if the licensee has unresolved final liabilities (taxes, penalties, interest, fees) owed to CSLB, DIR, EDD, FTB or the Board of Equalization (now CDTFA). CSLB must mail a notice at least 60 days before the suspension date. The same personnel cannot serve on other licenses until paid.

agencies: State Board of Equalization (sales/use tax now administered by CDTFA)
parameters.installment_agreement_exception: BOE/CDTFA liabilities under an installment agreement in compliance
parameters.other_licenses_same_personnel: suspended until debt satisfied or personnel disassociate

rules.applies_to: All licensees with final tax or fee liabilities
rules.source: PDF page 386 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-387
rules.quote: may suspend a license for the failure of a licensee to resolve all outstanding final liabilities, which include taxes, additions to tax, penalties, interest, and any fees that may be assessed by the board, the Department of Industrial Relations, the Employment Development Department, the Franchise Tax Board, or the State Board of Equalization.
rules.notes: B&P 494.5 (top-500 tax delinquent list suspension) expressly excludes CSLB (PDF page 205); CSLB uses 7145.5 instead. Personnel may still work as nonsupervising bona fide employees.

rules.title: Provide EIN/SSN/ITIN on the license application
rules.plain_english: CSLB will not process an initial license application without the applicant's federal EIN (partnerships) or SSN/ITIN (others). Licensees who fail to provide it are reported to the FTB and can be penalized under R&TC 19528.

parameters.failure: reported to FTB; penalty under R&TC 19528(b)(2)

rules.applies_to: All license applicants
rules.source: PDF page 103 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: a licensing board shall not process an application for an initial license unless the applicant provides its federal employer identification number, or individual taxpayer identification number or social security number where requested on the application.
rules.notes: CSLB shares this data with FTB/EDD on request (B&P 30(d)).

rules.title: Business name rules: one name per license; no misleading names
rules.plain_english: A licensee may use only one business name per license, and the name cannot suggest classifications the license does not have or be incompatible with the entity type (e.g., an LLC name must end in 'LLC'/'L.L.C.'/'Limited Liability Company' and cannot use 'Inc.' or 'Corp.').

prohibited: name implying classifications not held
name incompatible with entity type

rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.source: PDF page 278 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); https://www.cslb.ca.gov/About_Us/LLC.aspx
rules.quote: (a) A licensee shall not use any business name that indicates the licensee is qualified to perform work in classifications other than those issued for that license, or any business name that is incompatible with the type of business entity licensed. (b) A licensee shall not conduct business under more than one name for each license.
rules.notes: LLC naming rules quoted from CSLB's LLC page summarizing Corp. Code 17701.08 (statute itself not fetched).

rules.title: Commercial vehicles must show business name and license number
rules.plain_english: Every commercially registered vehicle used in the construction business must display the business name and CSLB license number in a clearly visible spot in at least 72-point type (3/4 inch). Plumbing (C-36), sign (C-45) and well-drilling (C-57) contractors must show name, business address and license number on both sides in letters at least 1.5 inches high.
rules.applies_to: All licensees' commercial vehicles
rules.source: PDF page 255 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-256; https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/AdvertisingGuidelines.pdf
rules.quote: every contractor licensed under this chapter shall have displayed, in or on each motor vehicle used in his or her construction business, for which a commercial vehicle registration fee has been paid ... his or her business name and contractors' license number in a clearly visible location in print type of at least 72-point font or three-quarters of an inch in height and width.
rules.notes: Also applies to water-well drill rigs (7029.5). Vehicle lettering is also 'advertising' under 16 CCR 861.

rules.title: Report felony / job-related convictions to CSLB within 90 days
rules.plain_english: A licensee must report in writing to CSLB within 90 days of learning of its conviction of any felony or of any other crime substantially related to contracting.

parameters.measured_from: licensee obtains knowledge of the event
events: conviction substantially related to contractor qualifications/functions/duties

rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.source: PDF page 306 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: a licensee shall report to the registrar in writing the occurrence of any of the following within 90 days after the licensee obtains knowledge of the event: (1) The conviction of the licensee for any felony.

rules.title: Report $1M+ multifamily load-bearing defect judgments/settlements within 90 days
rules.plain_english: Within 90 days of knowing of it, report to CSLB any final judgment, signed settlement or arbitration award of $1,000,000 or more (filed on or after 1/1/2019) in a 'complex case' over construction defects in load-bearing parts of a multifamily rental building. This does not apply to residential construction covered by Civil Code Title 7 (section 895 and following, the SB 800 Right to Repair Act). If several contractors are defendants, each one apportioned liability must report, except one assigned less than $15,000. The signed report gives your license number and the facts, plus the case details if a court was involved. Not reporting is grounds for discipline, but not a crime.

parameters.defect_type: failure or condition creating substantial risk of failure in load-bearing portions
parameters.excluded: residential construction subject to Civil Code Title 7 (sec. 895 et seq., SB 800 Right to Repair Act) (7071.20(b))
parameters.multi_defendant_rule: every contractor apportioned liability must report (7071.20(c))
report_contents: if court action: title of matter, court/agency name, docket number, claim/file number, date of event
parameters.failure_consequence: grounds for discipline; no criminal penalties (7071.20(f))
parameters.threshold_excludes: investigative costs and prior repairs performed by the licensee

rules.applies_to: Licensees named as defendant/cross-defendant in qualifying actions
rules.source: PDF page 309 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: A licensee shall report to the registrar in writing within 90 days after the licensee has knowledge of any civil action resulting in a final judgment, executed settlement agreement, or final arbitration award in which the licensee is named as a defendant or cross-defendant, filed on or after January 1, 2019
rules.notes: Remaining subdivisions read (PDF pp.310-311). Insurers must separately report qualifying payments within 30 days (B&P 7071.21).
rules.correction: The extract never read the later subdivisions. Added: (b) the section does not apply to residential construction subject to Civil Code Title 7 (sec. 895 et seq., the SB 800 Right to Repair Act); (c) when several contractors are defendants, all apportioned liability must report, except one assigned less than $15,000; (f) late or missing reports are grounds for discipline but carry no criminal penalty; (d) required report contents. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction (B&P 7071.20(b)-(f) re-read in sources/lawbook.txt on 2026-11-27); no value changed.

rules.title: License number required on contracts, subcontracts, bids and all advertising
rules.plain_english: Put your CSLB license number on every construction contract, subcontract and call for bids, and on all forms of advertising (cards, signs, vehicles, brochures, contract proposals, print, radio/TV, websites, social media, directories).
rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.source: PDF page 258 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); PDF page 490 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); PDF page 540 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: Every person licensed pursuant to this chapter shall include his license number in: (a) all construction contracts; (b) subcontracts and calls for bid; and (c) all forms of advertising, as prescribed by the registrar of contractors, used by such a person.
rules.notes: CSLB Advertising Guidelines: 'The civil penalty for not complying with this requirement is between $100 and $1,000 for a first offense.'

rules.title: What counts as 'advertising' for the license-number rule
rules.plain_english: For the license-number rule, advertising includes cards, contract proposals, signs, billboards, vehicle lettering (any state), brochures, pamphlets, circulars, newspapers, magazines, airwave or electronic transmissions, and any directory listing under 'Contractor' or similar words.

includes: lettering on vehicles registered in this or any other state
any form of directory under a listing denoting 'Contractor' or similar

rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.source: PDF page 490 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: the term "advertising" includes but is not limited to the following: any card, contract proposal, sign, billboard, lettering on vehicles registered in this or any other state, brochure, pamphlet, circular, newspaper, magazine, airwave or any electronic transmission, and any form of directory under any listing denoting "Contractor"

rules.title: Advertise only for classifications you hold
rules.plain_english: It is a misdemeanor to advertise construction work unless you hold a valid license in the classification advertised; A and B general contractors may advertise as 'general contractor.' Fine $700-$1,000 on top of other punishment; CSLB may cite unlicensed advertisers.

parameters.exception: licensed building (B) or engineering (A) contractor may advertise as general contractor

rules.applies_to: All persons advertising construction work
rules.source: PDF page 241 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-242; https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/AdvertisingGuidelines.pdf
rules.quote: It is a misdemeanor for any person to advertise for construction or work of improvement covered by this chapter unless that person holds a valid license under this chapter in the classification so advertised, except that a licensed building or engineering contractor may advertise as a general contractor.
rules.notes: 7027: anyone who advertises as a contractor is subject to the License Law even if otherwise exempt.

rules.title: Unlicensed handyperson ads: under $1,000 and must say 'not licensed'
rules.plain_english: An unlicensed person may advertise construction work only for projects totaling less than $1,000 (labor, materials, everything) and only if the ad states that the person is not licensed by CSLB.

parameters.required_ad_statement: states that the person is not licensed under the Contractors State License Law

rules.applies_to: Unlicensed persons relying on the minor work exemption
rules.source: PDF page 242 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: a person who is not licensed pursuant to this chapter may advertise for construction work or a work of improvement covered by this chapter only if the aggregate contract price for labor, material, and all other items on a project or undertaking is less than one thousand dollars ($1,000) and the person states in the advertisement that the person is not licensed under this chapter.
rules.notes: Raised from $500 to $1,000 by AB 2622 (Stats 2024 ch 240), effective 1/1/2025, per history note.

rules.title: Using someone else's license number: up to $10,000 fine / prison
rules.plain_english: Willfully using a license number that is not your own currently valid license, with intent to defraud, is punishable by a fine up to $10,000, state prison or up to 1 year county jail, or both.
rules.applies_to: Licensed and unlicensed persons
rules.source: PDF page 242 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: Any person, licensed or unlicensed, who willfully and intentionally uses, with intent to defraud, a contractor's license number that does not correspond to the number on a currently valid contractor's license held by that person, is punishable by a fine not exceeding ten thousand dollars ($10,000)

rules.title: No false, misleading or bait advertising
rules.plain_english: Using false, misleading or deceptive advertising to induce a construction contract, or advertising work/prices you do not intend to honor, is a misdemeanor and cause for discipline (FTC-compliant ads are safe-harbored).
rules.applies_to: All persons and licensees
rules.source: PDF page 421 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-422; PDF page 541 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: (a) Using false, misleading, or deceptive advertising as an inducement to enter into any contract for a work of improvement, including, but not limited to, any home improvement contract, whereby any member of the public may be misled or injured.

rules.title: Prime contracts (non-home-improvement): CSLB jurisdiction notice, 10-pt
rules.plain_english: Every written contract where you are the prime contractor (other than home improvement and service/repair contracts) must include CSLB's statement about licensing and complaint deadlines (4 years patent / 10 years latent structural) in at least 10-point type.

parameters.applies_to: written prime contracts other than home improvement (7151.2) and service and repair (7159.10)
parameters.notice_text: Contractors are required by law to be licensed and regulated by the Contractors State License Board which has jurisdiction to investigate complaints against contractors if a complaint regarding a patent act or omission is filed within four years of the date of the alleged violation. A complaint regarding a latent act or omission pertaining to structural defects must be filed within 10 years of the date of the alleged violation. Any questions concerning a contractor may be referred to the Registrar, Contractors State License Board, P.O. Box 26000, Sacramento, CA 95826.

rules.applies_to: Licensed prime contractors (commercial, new construction, etc.)
rules.source: PDF page 256 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); PDF page 540 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: Contractors are required by law to be licensed and regulated by the Contractors State License Board which has jurisdiction to investigate complaints against contractors if a complaint regarding a patent act or omission is filed within four years of the date of the alleged violation.
rules.notes: Home improvement and service/repair contracts instead use the 12-point 'Information about the Contractors State License Board (CSLB)' notice in 7030(b) (PDF pages 256-257).

rules.title: Licensees suspended/revoked 2+ times in 8 years must disclose before residential contracts
rules.plain_english: If your license was suspended or revoked two or more times within eight years, you must disclose those actions in a document given before contracting on residential property of 1-4 units (10-pt bold caps or 8-pt bold red). Penalties: $1,000, $2,500, then $5,000 plus 1-year suspension, then revocation.

format: contrasting red print at least 8-point roman boldface

rules.applies_to: Licensees with 2+ disciplinary suspensions/revocations in 8 years
rules.source: PDF page 257 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-258
rules.quote: A contractor, who has his or her license suspended or revoked two or more times within an eight-year period, shall disclose either in capital letters in 10-point roman boldface type or in contrasting red print in at least 8-point roman boldface type, in a document provided prior to entering into a contract to perform work on residential property with four or fewer units
rules.notes: May be provided in a bid, estimate or other pre-contract document.

rules.title: Minor work exemption: under $1,000 total, no permit, no employees
rules.plain_english: No license is needed only if the whole project (labor, materials and everything else, by one or more contracts) totals less than $1,000, the work needs no building permit, it is not part of a larger job or split up to evade the law, and the person neither advertises as a contractor nor employs anyone to help.
rules.applies_to: Unlicensed persons doing small jobs; contractors vetting unlicensed subs/handypersons
rules.source: PDF page 268 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/GetLicensedToBuild_ENG0525_ADA.pdf (p.4-5)
rules.quote: This chapter does not apply to a work or operation on one undertaking or project by one or more contracts if the aggregate contract price for labor, materials, and all other items is less than one thousand dollars ($1,000), that work or operation being considered of casual, minor, or inconsequential nature, and the work or operation does not require a building permit.
rules.notes: Amended by AB 2622 (eff. 1/1/2025) and AB 1170 (eff. 1/1/2026) per history note. CSLB guide: materials count 'whether purchased by the contractor or the consumer'. Prior $500 limit is from general knowledge of the pre-2025 statute.
rules.correction: Prior $500 figure is consistent with the AB 2622 amendment history but the old text is not printed in the law book.

rules.title: Unlicensed contracting: criminal penalties (1st, 2nd, 3rd offense)
rules.plain_english: Contracting without a license (or under a license suspended for unpaid penalties/liabilities) is a misdemeanor. 1st: up to $5,000 fine and/or 6 months jail. 2nd: the greater of 20% of the contract price, 20% of payments received, or $5,000, plus at least 90 days jail. 3rd+: $5,000 up to the greater of $10,000 or 20%, and 90 days to 1 year jail. Charges can be filed up to 4 years later.

parameters.sol_measured_from: latest of contract proposal, contract, completion, or abandonment
parameters.hourly_contract_price: cost of materials and labor furnished plus cost of completing the work

rules.applies_to: Unlicensed persons acting as contractors
rules.source: PDF page 245 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-246
rules.quote: A first conviction for the offense described in this section is punishable by a fine not exceeding five thousand dollars ($5,000) or by imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding six months, or by both that fine and imprisonment.
rules.notes: Customers of an unlicensed contractor are crime victims eligible for restitution (7028(h)). Third-offense penalties apply to anyone named on a previously revoked license held responsible (7028(e)).

rules.title: CSLB citation for unlicensed activity: $1,500-$15,000 (from July 1, 2026)
rules.plain_english: CSLB must cite unlicensed contractors and unregistered salespersons. Each citation has an order to stop and a civil penalty of $1,500 to $15,000 (it was $200-$15,000 before July 1, 2026). Citations can be issued up to 4 years after the act (or 18 months after a complaint, if later); appeal within 15 working days.

parameters.service: certified mail to last known business or residence address

rules.applies_to: Unlicensed contractors and unregistered home improvement salespersons
rules.source: PDF page 248 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-250
rules.quote: each citation shall contain an order of abatement and an assessment of a civil penalty in an amount not less than fifteen hundred dollars ($1,500) nor more than fifteen thousand dollars ($15,000).
rules.notes: 16 CCR 884 in the 2026 law book still lists 7028.7 at $200-$15,000 (not yet updated). Failure to comply with a final citation is a misdemeanor (7028.17). Registrar may waive part of the penalty if the person gets licensed (7028.14).

rules.title: Unlicensed contractor cannot collect and must repay all compensation
rules.plain_english: A contractor who was not properly licensed at all times during the work cannot sue to collect payment, and the customer can sue to recover everything already paid. Liens/security interests taken for payment are unenforceable. Substantial compliance helps only someone previously licensed who acted promptly and in good faith.

parameters.proof: verified CSLB certificate of licensure; burden on licensee
substantial_compliance_requirements: was duly licensed in CA before performance
acted reasonably and in good faith to maintain licensure
acted promptly to remedy upon learning of failure

rules.applies_to: Anyone performing work requiring a license (including subs and those with lapsed/suspended licenses)
rules.source: PDF page 258 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-259
rules.quote: a person who utilizes the services of an unlicensed contractor may bring an action in any court of competent jurisdiction in this state to recover all compensation paid to the unlicensed contractor for performance of any act or contract.
rules.notes: Key risk for lapses in bond/WC/SOS status, which cause suspension and therefore unlicensed periods.

rules.title: Unlicensed work on declared-disaster damage: felony-level penalties
rules.plain_english: Contracting without a license to repair damage from a Governor- or President-declared disaster is punishable by up to $10,000 fine and/or 16 months, 2 or 3 years (or up to 1 year county jail and/or $1,000).

parameters.trigger: state of emergency (Gov. Code 8625) or federal emergency/major disaster declaration

rules.applies_to: Unlicensed persons doing disaster repair
rules.source: PDF page 254 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: shall be punished by a fine up to ten thousand dollars ($10,000), or by imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170 of the Penal Code for 16 months, or for two or three years, or by both that fine and imprisonment

rules.title: Bidding public work without a license: misdemeanor; bid rejected; contract void
rules.plain_english: Submitting a bid to a public agency without a license is a misdemeanor (with narrow exceptions); repeat offenders face the greater of 20% of the contract price or $4,500, and/or 10 days to 6 months jail. Unlicensed bids are nonresponsive and contracts awarded to unlicensed contractors are void.
rules.applies_to: Bidders on public agency projects
rules.source: PDF page 252 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-253
rules.quote: If a person has been previously convicted of the offense described in this section, the court shall impose a fine of 20 percent of the price of the contract under which the unlicensed person performed contracting work, or four thousand five hundred dollars ($4,500), whichever is greater
rules.notes: Exceptions: State projects under PCC 10164 and local projects under PCC 20103.5 (license at award).

rules.title: Do not contract with unlicensed contractors (or help them evade the law)
rules.plain_english: Entering into a contract with a contractor who is not licensed is cause for discipline against your license; CSLB citation range $500-$30,000. Aiding or conspiring with an unlicensed person (7114) carries the same range. Verify each sub's license, classification and status before contracting.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and anyone hiring subcontractors
rules.source: PDF page 356 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); PDF page 541 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-542
rules.quote: Entering into a contract with a contractor while such contractor is not licensed as provided in this chapter constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: 7114 text itself was not read (only its title and the CCR 884 penalty row).

rules.title: Do not work under an inactive, suspended or expired license or outside your classes
rules.plain_english: Acting as a contractor under an inactive, suspended or expired (renewable) license, or in a classification you do not hold, or under a name/personnel not on the license, is cause for discipline (CCR 884: $200-$8,000; name/personnel $100-$1,000).
rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.source: PDF page 355 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-356; PDF page 541 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: (b) Acting in the capacity of a contractor under any license that has been suspended for any reason constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: Specialty contractors may do work in other trades only if incidental and supplemental to their licensed craft (7059).

rules.title: Officers/members of a licensed entity need their own license to contract individually
rules.plain_english: Being a partner, officer, director, manager, RME/RMO or other personnel of record of a licensed company does not let you contract on your own; doing so without your own license in good standing is unlawful (CCR 884: $200-$8,000).
rules.applies_to: Personnel of record of licensed entities
rules.source: PDF page 248 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); PDF page 540 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: It is unlawful for a person who is or has been a partner, officer, director, manager, responsible managing employee, responsible managing member, responsible managing manager, or responsible managing officer of ... a licensed partnership, corporation, limited liability company, firm, association or other organization to individually engage in the business

rules.title: Building permit applications: signed statement of license number
rules.plain_english: Cities and counties must require each permit applicant to sign a statement giving their CSLB license number and stating it is in full force, or stating the basis for any exemption. A violation carries a civil penalty of up to $500.

statement_contents: license in full force and effect

rules.applies_to: Contractors (and owner-builders) applying for building permits
rules.source: PDF page 259 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-260
rules.quote: Any violation of this section by any applicant for a permit shall be subject to a civil penalty of not more than five hundred dollars ($500).

rules.title: City business license: file signed CSLB license statement
rules.plain_english: Cities that require a business license for contractors must require each licensee/applicant to file a signed statement that the CSLB license is in full force, or proof of exemption. Most California cities also levy a local business license tax; rates and registration rules vary by city.

statement_contents: licensed under the Contractors License Law
license in full force and effect

rules.applies_to: Contractors doing business in cities requiring a business license
rules.source: PDF page 260 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); PDF page 41 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: shall require that each licensee and each applicant for issuance or renewal of such license shall file, or have on file, with such city or city and county, a signed statement that such licensee or applicant is licensed under the provisions of this chapter and stating that the license is in full force and effect
rules.notes: Local business license tax amounts are set by each city/county ordinance (B&P 16000 et seq. authority); a tool should store per-jurisdiction rules rather than a statewide number. The law book (p.41) also says to determine if city or county permits are required before starting a job.

rules.title: CSLB citation civil penalty ranges and per-citation caps
rules.plain_english: When CSLB cites a licensee, each violated section has a set penalty range (e.g., 7030.5 license number $100-$1,000; 7111 records $100-$1,000; 7118 $500-$30,000; 7125.4 $200-$30,000; 7159 $100-$1,000). Multiple violations on one project are capped at $8,000 per citation, except $15,000 (7028.7) and $30,000 (7110, 7114, 7118, 7125.4). Appeal within 15 working days. For 7028.7 (unlicensed contracting) citations, the statute's $1,500 minimum (operative July 1, 2026) controls over the $200 low end printed in the table.
rules.applies_to: Licensees and unlicensed persons cited by CSLB
rules.source: PDF page 540 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-542
rules.quote: Where a citation lists more than one violation and each of the violations relates to the same construction project, the total penalty assessment in each citation shall not exceed $ 8,000, except as provided for violations of Section 7028.7, in which case the total penalty assessment in each citation shall not exceed $ 15,000
rules.notes: Table lists 7071.1 and 7099.1 twice (as printed). 7028.7 statutory minimum rose to $1,500 on 7/1/2026; regulation not yet updated.
rules.correction: The 7028.7 entry ($200 minimum) is the regulation as printed; B&P 7028.7(c) as operative 7/1/2026 sets a $1,500 statutory minimum that controls (already flagged in notes). Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction (B&P 7028.7(c) re-read in sources/lawbook.txt on 2026-11-27); no value changed.

rules.title: Home improvement salespersons must be registered with CSLB
rules.plain_english: Anyone who solicits, sells, negotiates or signs home improvement contracts (including pools/spas) for a licensed contractor must hold a current CSLB Home Improvement Salesperson (HIS) registration at the time of the sale. Selling without one is a misdemeanor and can be cited.
rules.applies_to: Salespersons for home improvement contractors; contractors employing them
rules.source: PDF page 389 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-391
rules.quote: A home improvement salesperson shall register with the board in order to engage in the business of, or act in the capacity of, a home improvement salesperson.
rules.notes: Employing HIS means the contractor has employees and needs workers' comp (CSLB Get Licensed to Build guide).

rules.title: Who does not need an HIS registration
rules.plain_english: No HIS registration is needed for: corporate officers of record; LLC managers/members/officers of record; general partners on the license; the license qualifier (all only while listed on that licensee's personnel of record); retail-store salespeople where the buyer initiated at a fixed store; appointment setters only; and the contractor's service repair employees handling only the requested repair.

exempt: officer of record of licensed corporation
manager, member, or officer of record of licensed LLC
general partner listed on partnership license
salesperson at general merchandise retail establishment with buyer-initiated negotiation at fixed location
person only scheduling appointments for a registered HIS
bona fide service repairperson employed by licensee limited to requested service/repair
parameters.personnel_exemption_condition: listed as personnel of record of the licensee at time of the sale

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors and their sales staff
rules.source: PDF page 389 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-390
rules.quote: The exemption to registration provided under paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) of subdivision (d) shall apply only to those individuals who, at the time of the sales transaction, are listed as personnel of record for the licensee responsible for soliciting, negotiating, or contracting for a service or improvement

rules.title: Salesperson must identify the contractor's name and license number first
rules.plain_english: Before soliciting or selling, the salesperson must tell the owner or tenant the business name and license number of the contractor they represent for that transaction.

parameters.timing: prior to engaging in any sales activity

rules.applies_to: Home improvement salespersons
rules.source: PDF page 389 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: prior to engaging in any activity described in subdivision (a) of this section, a home improvement salesperson shall identify to the owner or tenant the business name and license number of the contractor they are representing for the purposes of that transaction.

rules.title: Contractor must notify CSLB before an HIS starts and within 90 days after they leave
rules.plain_english: A home improvement contractor must file CSLB's form (name and registration number) before a registered salesperson begins work, and file again within 90 days after the salesperson stops working for it. Using an unregistered salesperson, or not reporting, is cause for discipline.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors employing salespersons
rules.source: PDF page 393 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); PDF page 541 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: The form shall be submitted prior to the home improvement salesperson beginning work for the contractor.
rules.notes: An HIS may not guide an owner to a contractor whose employment notification CSLB has not received (7156(c)). Electronic filing permitted (7156.6).

rules.title: HIS registration: 2-year term; late renewal +50%; 3-year limit
rules.plain_english: HIS registrations expire two years after issuance (end of month). Renew before expiration; late renewals within three years pay a 50% delinquency penalty ($200 renewal -> $300). After three years, apply anew. Incomplete renewal applications are abandoned if not corrected within 90 days.
rules.applies_to: Registered home improvement salespersons
rules.source: PDF page 391 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)-392; https://www.cslb.ca.gov/About_Us/Library/Fees.aspx
rules.quote: A registration may, however, still be renewed at any time within three years after its expiration upon the filing of an application for renewal on a form prescribed by the registrar and the payment of the renewal fee prescribed by this chapter and a delinquent renewal penalty equal to 50 percent of the renewal fee.

rules.title: Contract sold by unregistered salesperson: security interest unenforceable
rules.plain_english: Any security interest (e.g., lien, deed of trust) a contractor takes to secure payment on a home improvement contract is unenforceable if the salesperson who solicited it was neither registered nor exempt when the homeowner signed.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors
rules.source: PDF page 391 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: Any security interest taken by a contractor, to secure any payment for the performance of any act or conduct described in Section 7151 that occurs on or after January 1, 1995, is unenforceable if the person soliciting the act or contract was not a duly registered salesperson or was not exempt from registration

rules.title: Contractor is disciplined for its salesperson's violations
rules.plain_english: A salesperson's violations of the License Law are also grounds for discipline against the contractor employing them, even if the contractor did not know.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors employing salespersons
rules.source: PDF page 394 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: Violations of any provisions of this chapter by a home improvement salesperson likewise constitute cause for disciplinary action against the contractor, by whom he or she was employed at the time the violation occurred, whether or not the contractor had knowledge of or participated in the act or omission constituting violations of this chapter.

rules.title: Salespersons must remit payments; contract forms must name the contractor
rules.plain_english: It is a misdemeanor for a salesperson to fail to account for or remit customer payments to the employing contractor, and for anyone to use a contract form that does not disclose the name of the contractor principal.

prohibited: HIS failing to account for or remit payments to employing contractor
contract form not disclosing name of contractor principal
HIS guiding owner to contractor without CSLB employment notice on file

rules.applies_to: Home improvement salespersons and contractors
rules.source: PDF page 394 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: (b) For any person to use a contract form in connection with any home improvement transaction or any other transaction involving a work of improvement if the form fails to disclose the name of the contractor principal by whom the person is employed.

rules.title: No referral rewards to owners; promotional gifts max $5
rules.plain_english: You may not offer an owner/tenant compensation for referring other home improvement business. Promotional gifts not conditioned on a contract are allowed only up to $5 in value and one per transaction. Salespersons may only be paid by the contractor they represent; contractors may not pay unlicensed persons for work requiring a license.
rules.applies_to: Contractors, agents and salespersons
rules.source: PDF page 395 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); PDF page 541 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: A contractor or his or her agent or salesperson may give tangible items to prospective customers for advertising or sales promotion purposes where the gift is not conditioned upon obtaining a contract for home improvement work if the gift does not exceed a value of five dollars ($5) and only one such gift is given in connection with any one transaction.
rules.notes: Violation is a misdemeanor and cause for discipline.

rules.title: Keep all contracting records 5 years after project completion
rules.plain_english: Keep records of all contracts, documents, receipts and disbursements for every contracting transaction, available for CSLB inspection, for at least five years after the project is completed. Refusing a written CSLB request for records is cause for discipline.

parameters.board_request: must comply with registrar's written request to make records available

rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.source: PDF page 352 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt); PDF page 50 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: failure to have those records available for inspection by the registrar or his or her duly authorized representative for a period of not less than five years after completion of any construction project or operation to which the records refer
rules.notes: B&P 7111.1: failing to respond to a written request to cooperate in a complaint investigation is also cause for discipline. B&P 7159.9 (fire alarm exemption, PDF pp.413-414) separately requires its documents be kept 5 years and produced within 30 days of a written request. Longest-of rule for a retention tool: CSLB 5 yrs after completion; IRS employment tax 4 yrs; EDD payroll 4 yrs (8 yrs if treating workers as non-employees); DIR payroll 3 yrs.

rules.title: Keep federal employment tax records at least 4 years
rules.plain_english: Keep payroll/employment tax records available for IRS inspection for at least four years after the tax due date for the period (or the date paid, if later).

parameters.measured_from: later of due date of the tax for the return period or date tax paid

rules.applies_to: All employers
rules.quote: every person required by the regulations in this part to keep records in respect of a tax (whether or not such person incurs liability for such tax) shall maintain such records for at least four years after the due date of such tax for the return period to which the records relate, or the date such tax is paid, whichever is the later.

rules.title: Keep California payroll records at least 4 years (8 if you claim no employees)
rules.plain_english: EDD requires payroll records for all workers (including former workers and independent contractors) to be kept at least four years; if you believe you are not a subject employer or workers are exempt, keep payment records at least eight years.
rules.applies_to: All California employers
rules.source: https://edd.ca.gov/siteassets/files/pdf_pub_ctr/de44.pdf (not fetched; host blocked - from search excerpt)
rules.quote: Employers must keep payroll records for at least four years.
rules.notes: edd.ca.gov could not be fetched from this environment; quote and 8-year figure come from web search excerpts of EDD DE 44 and DE 40. Verify before relying.

rules.title: Seller's permit for selling tangible property; possible security deposit
rules.plain_english: If the business sells tangible personal property, it needs a California seller's permit, and the tax agency may require a security deposit (the law book says up to six months of estimated sales tax). Collect sales tax from the customer unless tax on the materials was already paid at purchase.

parameters.security_deposit_estimate_basis: estimated sales tax for first six months (per law book)

rules.applies_to: Contractors that sell fixtures, materials over the counter, or otherwise act as retailers
rules.source: PDF page 41 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: California requires a Seller's Permit for businesses that sell tangible personal property. The State Board of Equalization can require a deposit of the estimated sales tax for the first six months. The contractor must collect the required sales tax from the customer unless the tax on materials is already paid at the time of purchase.
rules.notes: Sales and use tax is now administered by CDTFA (not BOE). The law book's summary is simplified; Regulation 1521 controls (materials = consumer, fixtures = retailer). The $50,000 max (R&TC 6701) is from a CDTFA manual search excerpt, not read. CDTFA says permit issuance is not delayed pending deposit.

rules.title: Sales tax: contractor is the consumer of materials it installs
rules.plain_english: On ordinary (non-federal) construction contracts the contractor is the final consumer of 'materials' it furnishes and installs (lumber, drywall, concrete, windows, nails, etc.), so it pays sales tax to its supplier (or use tax) on its cost and does not charge sales tax to the customer on them. It may not buy materials for resale.

parameters.measure: sale price of materials to the contractor (purchase price)

rules.applies_to: Construction contractors (prime and sub) on non-U.S.-government contracts
rules.quote: Construction contractors are consumers of materials which they furnish and install in the performance of construction contracts.
rules.notes: cdtfa.ca.gov could not be fetched from this environment. Quote is from search excerpts of Regulation 1521 and CDTFA annotations. Examples come from CDTFA annotations. Exception: time-and-material contracts meeting title/separate-price test, or 'plus sales tax' billing (see reg1521-time-and-material-retailer).

rules.title: Sales tax: contractor is the retailer of fixtures it installs
rules.plain_english: The contractor is treated as the retailer of 'fixtures' it furnishes and installs (items that keep their identity as accessories, e.g., cabinets, lighting fixtures, plumbing fixtures, alarm systems, plants/trees). Tax applies to the fixture's stated sale price or, if none is stated (lump-sum contract), to the contractor's cost price. Fixtures may be bought for resale with a resale certificate.

parameters.measure_if_not_stated: cost price of fixture to contractor

rules.applies_to: Construction contractors installing fixtures
rules.quote: Construction contractors are retailers of fixtures which they furnish and install in the performance of construction contracts and tax applies to their sales of the fixtures.
rules.notes: From search excerpts only. 5% profit build-up for contractor-manufactured fixtures quoted in excerpt ('shall be deemed to be 5 percent of the sum of the preceding factors'). Regulation's full fixtures/materials definitions not read - verify classification of specific items.

rules.title: Time-and-material contracts: when the contractor becomes retailer of materials
rules.plain_english: On a time-and-material contract the contractor is normally still the consumer of materials. It becomes the retailer (and must collect sales tax on the materials' selling price) if the contract both transfers title to materials before installation and separately states the materials' sale price - or if it bills 'sales tax' on marked-up materials.

retailer_if_all: contract explicitly transfers title to materials before installation
contract separately states sale price of materials exclusive of installation
parameters.retailer_if_billing: bills customer sales tax computed on marked-up materials (time and material plus tax)

rules.applies_to: Contractors using time-and-material contracts
rules.quote: If the contract explicitly provides for the transfer of title to the materials prior to the time the materials are installed, and separately states the sale price of the materials, exclusive of the charge for installation, the contractor will be deemed to be the retailer of the materials.
rules.notes: Search excerpt. CDTFA annotations say both conditions must be met; a title clause alone is not enough.

rules.title: Lump-sum contract: separately stating items on the invoice does not change it
rules.plain_english: A lump-sum contract (one stated price to furnish and install) stays lump-sum even if the invoice separately lists materials, fixtures, labor or tax; the contractor remains consumer of materials and retailer of fixtures (measured by cost price if not stated).

parameters.definition: contract under which contractor for a stated lump sum agrees to furnish and install materials or fixtures, or both

rules.applies_to: Contractors using lump-sum contracts
rules.quote: A lump sum contract does not become a time and material contract when the amounts attributable to materials, fixtures, labor, or tax are separately stated in the invoice.
rules.notes: Subsection number (a)(8) as shown in search excerpt. CDTFA Pub 9 example: $15,000 lump sum with $2,000 materials (tax paid on purchase) and $5,000 fixture cost -> fixture tax measured on $5,000.

rules.title: Subcontractors cannot avoid tax by taking a resale certificate from the prime
rules.plain_english: A contractor (including a sub) cannot escape sales/use tax on materials or fixtures it furnishes and installs by accepting a resale certificate from the prime contractor, designers, decorators or others.
rules.applies_to: Subcontractors and prime contractors
rules.quote: A contractor cannot avoid liability for sales or use tax on materials or fixtures furnished and installed by him or her by taking a resale certificate from the prime contractor, interior decorators, designers, department stores, or others.
rules.notes: Search excerpt only.

rules.title: Federal (U.S. government) jobs: contractor is consumer of materials AND fixtures
rules.plain_english: On contracts with the United States Government, the contractor is the consumer of both materials and fixtures (pays tax on purchase; no sales tax to the government), but is the retailer of machinery and equipment it furnishes.
rules.applies_to: Contractors on U.S. government construction contracts
rules.quote: United States construction contractors are consumers of materials and fixtures which they furnish and install in the performance of contracts with the United States Government.
rules.notes: Search excerpt only.

rules.title: When a contractor needs a CDTFA seller's permit
rules.plain_english: A contractor needs a seller's permit if it sells fixtures, sells materials (e.g., T&M retailer, over-the-counter), machinery/equipment or other tangible property; contractors who only furnish and install materials on lump-sum jobs generally do not, but may need to register for use tax as a qualified purchaser.

permit_required_if: retailer of materials under T&M contract
furnishes and installs solar systems that include fixtures
parameters.generally_not_required: only furnishing and installing materials in lump-sum contracts
parameters.alternate_registration: qualified purchaser / consumer use tax account

rules.applies_to: Construction contractors
rules.quote: If a contractor is a seller or retailer because he or she makes sales of fixtures, materials, or machinery and equipment, or other tangible personal property either in connection with or as part of a construction contract, or otherwise, he or she is required to hold a seller's permit.
rules.notes: Search excerpts of Regulation 1521 and CDTFA Pub 9. Seller's permits are free (general knowledge; not verified here).

rules.title: Use tax on materials bought without CA tax (e.g., out of state)
rules.plain_english: If you buy materials or equipment from an out-of-state seller who does not charge California tax, you owe use tax at the rate where the item is used; if used in a higher-rate district than the rate paid, the difference is due.

parameters.rate_basis: rate in effect where property is used

rules.applies_to: Contractors buying taxable items without CA sales tax
rules.quote: if the property is used in a district with a higher tax rate than the rate paid at the time of purchase, the additional tax is due.
rules.notes: Search excerpt (paraphrase in search summary). Verify reporting method (sales and use tax return or CDTFA use tax account).

rules.title: California statewide base sales/use tax rate 7.25% plus district taxes
rules.plain_english: The statewide base sales and use tax rate is 7.25%; local district taxes (generally 0.10% or more each) are added on top depending on location, so job-site/delivery location determines the total rate. The combined district rate in a county is usually capped at 2.00%, but some laws allow more.
rules.applies_to: Retailers (fixtures/material sales) and consumers owing use tax
rules.citation: R&TC 6051 et seq.; CDTFA rate tables
rules.quote: the total rate for the district (statewide rate + district rate)
rules.notes: Search excerpt; look up current rate per address with CDTFA before filing. Base rate figure from search summary.
rules.correction: Not a correction, but district_tax_each_max_percent (2.0) is really the usual combined county cap, and some statutes authorize more. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: Withhold 7% on CA-source payments over $1,500/yr to nonresident subs
rules.plain_english: If you pay a nonresident (e.g., an out-of-state subcontractor) for services performed in California, you must withhold 7% of payments once the calendar-year total exceeds $1,500, unless the payee gives an exemption (Form 590) or FTB waiver. Report on Form 592 / 592-B.

parameters.applies_to: California-source nonwage payments to nonresidents (services performed in CA)

rules.applies_to: Contractors paying nonresident individuals/entities for CA services
rules.source: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/contractors/Tax_Info.aspx (read: obligation exists); https://www.ftb.ca.gov/pay/withholding/withholding-on-nonresidents.html (not fetched; search excerpt for 7%/$1,500)
rules.quote: If you pay California source income to nonresidents, then you may have withholding responsibilities including those under California Revenue and Taxation Code Section 18662.
