rules.notes: CSLB Tax Info page (read) confirms the obligation and code section; the 7% rate and $1,500 threshold are from FTB search excerpts (ftb.ca.gov blocked). Payer can be liable for tax not withheld.

rules.title: LLC: $800 annual tax + gross-receipts fee at $250,000+
rules.plain_english: Every LLC doing business or organized/registered in California owes an $800 annual tax (Form FTB 3522, due by the 15th day of the 4th month of the tax year) and, if total California income is $250,000 or more, an additional LLC fee estimated by the 15th day of the 6th month (Form FTB 3536).

parameters.annual_tax_due: 15th day of 4th month of taxable year

rules.applies_to: LLCs (including contractor LLCs)
rules.quote: Every LLC that is doing business or organized in California must pay an annual tax of $800.
rules.notes: Search excerpt; fee tier amounts not verified (FTB LLC fee chart not retrieved). Corporations owe an $800 minimum franchise tax (general knowledge - not verified here).

rules.title: LLC Statement of Information: within 90 days, then every 2 years ($20)
rules.plain_english: An LLC must file its Statement of Information with the Secretary of State within 90 days of registering and then every two years during its filing period; fee $20. Updates between periods are free.
rules.applies_to: California and foreign LLCs registered with SOS
rules.citation: Corp. Code 17702.09 (citation from general knowledge; verify)
rules.quote: The filing fee for the initial and required biennial Statement of Information is $20
rules.notes: sos.ca.gov could not be fetched. Missing the filing can lead to SOS/FTB suspension, which triggers CSLB license suspension under B&P 7076.2.

rules.title: Stock corporation Statement of Information: every year ($25)
rules.plain_english: A California stock corporation (and foreign corporation) files a Statement of Information every year during its filing period; fee $25.
rules.applies_to: California stock corporations and foreign corporations
rules.citation: Corp. Code 1502 (citation from general knowledge; verify)
rules.quote: the fee to file the statement is $25 for California stock and foreign corporations
rules.notes: Initial filing within 90 days of incorporation is general knowledge, not confirmed here. Filing period is commonly the month of original registration and the preceding five months (general knowledge - verify).

rules.title: $250 penalty for missing Statement of Information
rules.plain_english: If a corporation or LLC fails to file its Statement of Information, it gets a delinquency notice with 60 more days to file; if still not filed, a $250 penalty is assessed (collected by FTB) and the entity can be suspended.
rules.applies_to: Corporations and LLCs
rules.citation: Corp. Code 2204; Corp. Code 17713.13 (citations from general knowledge; verify)
rules.quote: you may be assessed a $250 penalty for not filing your Statement of Information
rules.notes: Search excerpt. Ties to CSLB: SOS not-in-good-standing -> CSLB suspension 30 days after notice (B&P 7076.2).
rules.correction: Citation unresolved: the FTB penalty chart excerpt cites Corp. Code 2204 and 17653 (a former Beverly-Killea LLC Act section), not 17713.13. Keep the citation flagged "verify".

rules.title: Register with EDD once you pay over $100 in total wages in a quarter
rules.plain_english: A contractor that pays more than $100 in total wages in a calendar quarter must register with EDD, get a state employer account number, and pay state payroll and UI taxes on its employees' wages. The trigger is the employer's total quarterly wages, not each employee's earnings. Also get a federal EIN and pay federal withholding and Social Security taxes on schedule.

parameters.threshold_basis: total wages paid by the employer in a calendar quarter (not each employee's earnings)

rules.applies_to: Contractors with employees
rules.source: PDF page 41 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: The contractor must register with the Employment Development Department, obtain a state EIN, and pay state payroll and unemployment insurance taxes for employees who earn over $100 in a calendar quarter.
rules.notes: The law book (p.41) says "for employees who earn over $100 in a calendar quarter". EDD guidance (search summaries) frames the $100 as the employer's total quarterly wages. See edd-registration-15-days for the deadline.
rules.correction: The law book text "employees who earn over $100 in a calendar quarter" was carried into plain_english as a per-employee test. The EDD trigger is employer-level: an employer that pays more than $100 in total wages in a calendar quarter must register and report, and once subject, all wages are covered (up to the applicable wage bases). Clarified plain_english and added threshold_basis. The $100 figure is unchanged. Rewording 2026-11-27: title reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: EDD employer registration due within 15 days of paying over $100
rules.plain_english: Register with EDD (online via e-Services for Business or Form DE 1) within 15 calendar days after you first pay more than $100 in wages in a calendar quarter. Wages include cash, checks, app payments and the value of meals/lodging.

parameters.trigger: paying more than $100 in wages in a calendar quarter
parameters.form: DE 1 (Commercial Employer Account Registration) or e-Services for Business

rules.applies_to: All employers (contractors) with California employees
rules.quote: Not available verbatim - page not fetched (host blocked). Search excerpt: a business that pays more than $100 in wages in a calendar quarter must register within 15 days.
rules.notes: edd.ca.gov blocked from this environment; the $100 trigger is confirmed by the CSLB law book (p.41, read), the 15-day deadline only by EDD search excerpts.

rules.title: California UI tax: new employer rate 3.4% on first $7,000 per employee
rules.plain_english: Employers pay state Unemployment Insurance tax on the first $7,000 of each employee's wages per year. New employers are assigned a 3.4% rate for two to three years (max $238 per employee per year at 3.4%); later rates come from the annual DE 2088 notice.
rules.applies_to: California employers
rules.quote: New employers are assigned a 3.4 percent UI rate for two to three years.
rules.notes: Search excerpt; $238 derived (7,000 x 3.4%). CUIC 930 citation for wage base from general knowledge - verify.

rules.title: Employment Training Tax (ETT): 0.1% on first $7,000
rules.plain_english: Most employers also pay ETT of 0.1% on the same first $7,000 of each employee's wages ($7 per employee per year). Employers with a negative UI reserve balance pay no ETT (shown as 0.0%).
rules.applies_to: California UI-rated employers
rules.quote: The ETT rate for 2026 is 0.1 percent.
rules.notes: Search excerpt; $7 derived.

rules.title: SDI employee withholding 2026: 1.3% of all wages (no cap)
rules.plain_english: Withhold State Disability Insurance (SDI) from employees' pay at 1.3% for 2026. There is no taxable wage limit or maximum withholding since 2024.
rules.applies_to: California employers withholding from employee wages
rules.citation: CUIC 984 (citation from general knowledge; verify); SB 951 (2022)
rules.quote: The 2026 SDI withholding rate is 1.3 percent (.013).
rules.notes: Search excerpt. 2025 rate 1.2% also from search excerpt.

rules.title: File DE 9 and DE 9C every quarter (even with no payroll)
rules.plain_english: Active employers file the Quarterly Contribution Return (DE 9) and Wage and Withholding report (DE 9C) every quarter, even if no wages were paid. 2026 quarters are due the 1st of the month after quarter end and delinquent if not filed by the last day of that month (Q3 2026 delinquent after Nov 2, 2026; Q4 delinquent after Feb 1, 2027).

parameters.weekend_holiday_rule: delinquent date moves to next business day

rules.applies_to: California employers
rules.citation: CUIC (quarterly returns); EDD Payroll Tax Calendar
rules.quote: Not available verbatim - page not fetched (host blocked). Search excerpt: DE 9 and DE 9C for Jan-Mar due April 1, delinquent after April 30.
rules.notes: Dates from search excerpt of EDD 2026 calendar. PIT/SDI deposits (DE 88) follow federal deposit schedule (not verified here).

rules.title: EDD e-file / e-pay mandate: paper filing penalties
rules.plain_english: All employers must file payroll tax returns/reports and pay deposits electronically. Penalties for noncompliance: $50 per paper DE 9, $20 per wage item on a paper DE 9C, and 15% of a non-electronic payment (credit-card DE 88 payments count as electronic).
rules.applies_to: California employers
rules.citation: CUIC e-file and e-pay mandate (AB 1245, Stats. 2015 - citation from general knowledge)
rules.quote: Not available verbatim - page not fetched (host blocked). Search excerpt: $50 per DE 9 return, $20 per wage item on the DE 9C, 15% of the amount due on DE 88 payments.
rules.notes: Search excerpt only.

rules.title: Report independent contractors (subs) to EDD on DE 542 within 20 days
rules.plain_english: If you must file a federal 1099 for a sole-proprietor independent contractor, report them to EDD on Form DE 542 within 20 calendar days of paying $600 or more in a calendar year or signing a contract for $600 or more, whichever is first. Materials included in the payment count toward $600.

parameters.trigger: earlier of paying >= $600 in calendar year or entering contract >= $600
parameters.report_frequency: once per year per service provider (check Ongoing box)

rules.applies_to: Businesses paying independent contractors (individuals/sole proprietors) for services
rules.quote: You must report independent contractor information to us within 20 calendar days if either of the following applies.
rules.notes: Search excerpt. EDD pages still show $600 even though the federal 1099-NEC threshold became $2,000 for 2026 payments - verify which threshold EDD now applies. $24 penalty from older EDD documents (unverified for 2026). See also labor-hr research file rule independent-contractor-report-de542.

rules.title: Get a federal EIN (Form SS-4) by 7 days after first wages
rules.plain_english: An employer paying wages subject to Social Security/Medicare or income tax withholding must apply for an Employer Identification Number on Form SS-4 no later than the seventh day after the first wage payment, and use it on returns, W-2s and deposits.
rules.applies_to: All employers
rules.quote: The application for an identification number shall be filed on or before the seventh day after the first payment of wages to which reference is made in paragraph (a)(1) of this section.
rules.notes: The CSLB law book (p.41) also says a federal EIN must be requested from the IRS. Partnership license applicants must give their EIN to CSLB (B&P 30).

rules.title: Form 941 due the last day of the month after each quarter
rules.plain_english: File Form 941 (quarterly federal payroll tax return) by the last day of the month after the quarter: April 30, July 31, October 31 and January 31. If all taxes were deposited on time and in full, you get until the 10th of the following month. Weekend/holiday dates roll to the next business day.

parameters.due: last day of first calendar month after quarter
parameters.extended_due_if_timely_deposits: 10th day of second month after quarter

rules.applies_to: All employers filing Form 941
rules.quote: shall be filed on or before the last day of the first calendar month following the period for which it is made. A return may be filed on or before the 10th day of the second calendar month following such period if timely deposits under section 6302(c) of the Code and the regulations have been made in full payment of such taxes due for the period.
rules.notes: 2026 adjusted dates computed: Oct 31, 2026 is a Saturday and Jan 31, 2027 is a Sunday, so they roll to Monday.

rules.title: Federal payroll tax deposits: monthly vs semiweekly ($50,000 lookback)
rules.plain_english: If total employment taxes in the lookback period (12 months ending the prior June 30) were $50,000 or less, deposit monthly by the 15th of the next month; above $50,000, deposit semiweekly (Wed-Fri paydays by next Wednesday; Sat-Tue paydays by next Friday). Deposits must be by electronic funds transfer. A new employer counts as having no employment taxes for any part of the lookback period before it started or acquired the business, so it starts as a monthly depositor.

parameters.safe_harbor_shortfall: greater of $100 or 2% of required deposit, made up by shortfall date

rules.applies_to: All employers
rules.quote: An employer is a monthly depositor for the entire calendar year if the aggregate amount of employment taxes reported for the lookback period is $50,000 or less.
rules.notes: New employers with no lookback history are monthly depositors (general rule; specific new-employer paragraph not extracted).
rules.correction: New employers are treated as having zero liability for any lookback period before they started the business (31.6302-1(b)(4)), so they start as monthly depositors. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction (26 CFR 31.6302-1(b)(4) re-read in the eCFR versioner API, title 26 issue 2026-11-18 on 2026-11-27); no value changed.

rules.title: Federal deposit: $100,000 accumulated = deposit by next day
rules.plain_english: If you accumulate $100,000 or more of employment taxes on any day, deposit by the close of the next business day; a monthly depositor then becomes a semiweekly depositor for the rest of the year and the next year.

parameters.status_change: monthly depositor becomes semiweekly for remainder of year and following year

rules.applies_to: All employers
rules.quote: if on any day within a deposit period (monthly or semi-weekly) an employer has accumulated $100,000 or more of employment taxes, those taxes must be deposited by electronic funds transfer in time to satisfy the tax obligation by the close of the next day.

rules.title: Under $2,500 per quarter: may pay with the timely filed return
rules.plain_english: If total employment taxes for the quarter (or the prior quarter) are under $2,500, you may pay them with a timely filed Form 941 instead of making deposits.

parameters.period: return period (quarter) or immediately preceding quarter
parameters.condition: fully paid with timely filed return; one-day $100,000 rule not triggered

rules.applies_to: Small employers
rules.quote: The total amount of accumulated employment taxes is de minimis if it is less than $2,500 for the return period or if it is de minimis pursuant to paragraph (f)(4)(ii) of this section.

rules.title: Forms W-2: give employees and file with SSA by January 31
rules.plain_english: Furnish each employee's W-2 by January 31 of the following year and file W-2s (with W-3) with the government by January 31. For a terminated employee who asks, you may need to furnish it sooner.
rules.applies_to: All employers
rules.quote: Each statement required by this section for a calendar year and each corrected statement required for the year shall be furnished to the employee on or before January 31 of the year succeeding such calendar year.
rules.notes: Weekend roll-forward per 26 CFR 301.7503-1 (computed).

rules.title: Form 940 (FUTA) due January 31 (10 more days if fully deposited)
rules.plain_english: File the annual federal unemployment (FUTA) return, Form 940, by the last day of the month after the year ends (January 31); you get until February 10 if all FUTA tax was deposited on time.
rules.applies_to: Employers subject to FUTA
rules.quote: Each return of the tax imposed by the Federal Unemployment Tax Act required to be made under § 31.6011(a)-3 shall be filed on or before the last day of the first calendar month following the period for which it is made.
rules.notes: Annual return period from 26 CFR 31.6011(a)-3 (not separately fetched).

rules.title: FUTA: California credit reduction state (2025: 1.2%; 2026: 1.5%)
rules.plain_english: FUTA is 6.0% on the first $7,000 per employee less a normal 5.4% state credit. California employers lose part of the credit because of the state's federal UI loan: an extra 1.2% for 2025 ($84/employee) and 1.5% listed for 2026 ($105/employee), paid with Form 940 Schedule A.
rules.applies_to: California employers
rules.quote: California is 0.015 (1.5%).
rules.notes: From search excerpt of the 2026 Schedule A (Form 940) draft; EDD calls 1.5% a projection pending DOL final notice (after Nov 10, 2026). Effective rates and per-employee amounts derived (0.6% + reduction).

rules.title: Form 1099-NEC: $2,000 threshold for payments made in 2026
rules.plain_english: For nonemployee compensation paid after December 31, 2025, file Form 1099-NEC for each payee (e.g., unincorporated subcontractor) paid at least $2,000 in the year (was $600). The threshold is inflation-adjusted after 2026. Always file if you backup-withheld, regardless of amount.
rules.applies_to: Businesses paying non-corporate service providers (subcontractors)
rules.citation: IRC 6041(a) as amended by P.L. 119-21 (One Big Beautiful Bill Act); 26 CFR 1.6041-1
rules.source: https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i1099mec; https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15 (not fetched; search excerpt); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-26/chapter-I/subchapter-A/part-1/section-1.6041-1 (fetched; still says $600)
rules.quote: You made payments to the payee of at least $2,000 during the year
rules.notes: IRS sites blocked; $2,000 from IRS instructions search excerpt. The eCFR regulation 26 CFR 1.6041-1 (read) still reads 'payments of $600 or more' because Treasury has not updated it - the statute controls. California EDD DE 542 still references $600.

rules.title: Form 1099-NEC due to IRS and recipient by January 31
rules.plain_english: File Form 1099-NEC with the IRS and furnish the recipient copy by January 31 of the year after payment (paper filers include Form 1096). For 2026 payments, January 31, 2027 is a Sunday.
rules.applies_to: Businesses filing 1099-NEC
rules.quote: Section 6071(c) requires you to file Form 1099-NEC on or before January 31, using either paper or electronic filing procedures.
rules.notes: Search excerpt. Weekend roll to Feb 1, 2027 is computed (general IRS weekend rule), not confirmed by IRS text here.

rules.title: No 1099 needed for payments to corporations (except attorneys/medical)
rules.plain_english: Payments to corporations (C or S) generally do not require an information return; exceptions include attorneys' fees and medical/health care service corporations.

exceptions: attorneys' fees (after 1997)
corporations providing medical and health care services or billing for them
parameters.note_llc: LLCs taxed as corporations are corporations for this rule; single-member/partnership LLCs are not (general knowledge)

rules.applies_to: Businesses paying subcontractors and vendors
rules.quote: (p) Payments made to the following persons: (1) A corporation described in § 1.6049-4(c)(1)(ii)(A), except with respect to payments made to a corporation after December 31, 1997 for attorneys' fees, and except a corporation engaged in providing medical and health care services
rules.notes: Collect Form W-9 from every sub to determine entity type and TIN. LLC note is general knowledge.

rules.title: Backup withholding: 24% if a sub gives no TIN (W-9)
rules.plain_english: If a payee does not furnish a taxpayer identification number (e.g., no W-9), withhold 24% from reportable payments such as nonemployee compensation, deposit it, and report it; for 2026 the backup-withholding reporting threshold matches the $2,000 1099 threshold.

parameters.trigger: payee fails to furnish TIN (Form W-9) or IRS notice of incorrect TIN

rules.applies_to: Businesses paying subcontractors and service providers
rules.quote: the backup withholding rate is 24% for reportable payments
rules.notes: Search excerpt.

rules.title: Sole owners and partners must prepay income tax quarterly
rules.plain_english: If the business is a sole ownership or partnership, owners must prepay estimated federal and state income taxes (quarterly). Federal income tax and Social Security withheld from employees must be paid quarterly, monthly or semimonthly as required.
rules.applies_to: Sole proprietors and partners
rules.source: PDF page 41 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (/home/user/Client/sources/lawbook.txt)
rules.quote: If the business is a sole ownership or partnership, estimated federal and state income taxes must be prepaid or paid quarterly.
rules.notes: Specific estimated-tax due dates and safe-harbor percentages not verified here.

rules.title: Multi-employer worksites: four kinds of employer can be cited
rules.plain_english: On a jobsite with more than one employer, Cal/OSHA can cite four kinds of employer for the same hazard: the one whose workers were exposed, the one who created it, the one in control of site safety (usually the GC), and the one whose job it was to fix it.

definitions.exposing: employer whose employees were exposed to the hazard
definitions.creating: employer who actually created the hazard
definitions.controlling: employer responsible, by contract or through actual practice, for safety and health conditions on the worksite (authority to ensure correction)
definitions.correcting: employer who had the responsibility for actually correcting the hazard

rules.applies_to: Every employer on a multi-employer worksite (construction and non-construction): general contractors, construction managers, subcontractors, owners who employ people
rules.quote: On multi-employer worksites, both construction and non-construction, citations may be issued only to the following categories of employers when the Division has evidence that an employee was exposed to a hazard in violation of any requirement enforceable by the Division:
rules.notes: Cal/OSHA Compliance Manual Ch. 14-B notes that one employer may fit more than one category (e.g., creating and controlling). 336.10 history: filed 12/1/97, effective 12/31/97; the Compliance Manual (section III) says 'Beginning in January of 2000, Labor Code Section 6400 and 8 CCR Section 336.10 now permit the Division to cite' creating, controlling and correcting employers. Labor Code 6400 text not readable (leginfo blocked).

rules.title: Controlling employer (usually the GC) can be cited for subs' hazards
rules.plain_english: The employer responsible for site safety, by contract or by how it actually runs the job, is the 'controlling employer'. Cal/OSHA can cite it for a hazard on the site even if none of its own workers were exposed.
rules.applies_to: General contractors, construction managers and any employer with contractual or actual authority over jobsite safety
rules.quote: (c) The employer who was responsible, by contract or through actual practice, for safety and health conditions on the worksite; i.e., the employer who had the authority for ensuring that the hazardous condition is corrected (the controlling employer); or
rules.notes: The three ways to prove control come from the Cal/OSHA Compliance Manual Ch. 14-B, section V.3 (a: explicit contract provisions; b: any contract authority that directly affects worksite safety; c: actual practice). 8 CCR 1951 also defines 'controlling contractor' for confined spaces by reference to 336.10(c).

rules.title: Creating, controlling and correcting employers can be cited without their own workers exposed
rules.plain_english: If you created a hazard, control the site, or were responsible for fixing it, Cal/OSHA can cite you even when only another company's workers were exposed.
rules.applies_to: Every employer on a multi-employer worksite (construction and non-construction): general contractors, construction managers, subcontractors, owners who employ people
rules.quote: Note: The employers listed in subsections (b) through (d) may be cited regardless of whether their own employees were exposed to the hazard.
rules.notes: Penalty amounts themselves are set by 8 CCR 336 (covered in the web_calosha-programs pack). Per the Compliance Manual (section III), citing employers whose own employees were not exposed has been permitted 'Beginning in January of 2000' under Labor Code 6400 and 336.10.

rules.title: Control can be proven by actual practice, regardless of the contract
rules.plain_english: Even if your contract says you are not responsible for safety, Cal/OSHA can treat you as the controlling employer if, in practice, you direct subs to change work practices or fix hazards.

parameters.example: GC routinely orders subcontractors to correct safety hazards and gives direction to sub foremen on site

rules.applies_to: General contractors, construction managers and owners active on the jobsite
rules.citation: 8 CCR 336.10(c); Cal/OSHA Compliance Manual Ch. 14-B, V.3.c
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/DOSHPol/P&PC-1C.pdf (Compliance Manual Chapter 14, PDF p. 47 of 65, section V.3.c 'Actual Practice')
rules.quote: Regardless of whether a contract exists, or if a contract exists, regardless of what provisions it contains, an employer's control over worksite safety can be shown to exist by obtaining evidence of the employer's actual practices at the worksite.
rules.notes: Enforcement policy text (DOSH Compliance Manual, PDF created 2026-10-26 per file metadata), interpreting 336.10. The URL named P&PC-1C now serves Compliance Manual Chapter 14.

rules.title: Controlling the schedule or key information can make you the controlling employer
rules.plain_english: A construction manager or GC that controls scheduling or the flow of safety information can be cited as the controlling employer if it fails to adjust the schedule or pass on information needed to keep workers safe, even when the contract disclaims safety responsibility.

examples: controls scheduling and fails to adjust schedule to prevent a hazard
controls flow of essential information and fails to deliver it

rules.applies_to: Construction managers, general contractors and owners who set schedules or sequencing
rules.citation: 8 CCR 336.10(c); Cal/OSHA Compliance Manual Ch. 14-B, V.3.b
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/DOSHPol/P&PC-1C.pdf (Compliance Manual Chapter 14, PDF pp. 46-47 of 65, section V.3.b)
rules.quote: For example, if an employer controls the scheduling of work and fails to adjust the work schedule when that becomes necessary to prevent a worksite safety hazard, then the employer becomes potentially citable as a controlling employer because of the direct connection between the employer's failure to act and the exposure of employees to the worksite hazard.
rules.notes: Compliance Manual Example 5: a CM whose contract denies safety authority was citable after ignoring a sub's request to resequence work until guardrails were installed.

rules.title: Exposing employer is not cited only if all five defenses are met
rules.plain_english: A sub whose workers were exposed to someone else's hazard avoids a citation only if it did not create the hazard, had no responsibility or authority to fix it, could not fix it, told the responsible employer (or they knew), and took feasible steps to protect and instruct its own workers (including pulling them off the job for an extreme hazard).

parameters.extreme_hazard_step: remove employees from the job if no other way to protect them

rules.applies_to: Subcontractors and other exposing employers on multi-employer worksites
rules.quote: Prior to issuing any citation to an exposing employer, the Division shall first determine whether available information indicates that the employer meets each of the defenses listed below. If the Division concludes that all five defenses have been met, the citation shall not be issued.
rules.notes: Compliance Manual Ch. 14-B, IV says that if the employer appeals a determination that the defense does not apply, 'it is the employer's burden to demonstrate that the defense applies.' Practical takeaway: subs should notify the GC in writing of hazards they did not create.

rules.title: How Cal/OSHA weighs a GC's or sub's responsibility: awareness, foreseeability, reasonable steps
rules.plain_english: Before citing a creating, controlling or correcting employer, inspectors weigh when it knew about the hazard, how foreseeable the hazard was, and what reasonable steps it took. Knowing about a hazard and doing nothing carries the highest responsibility.

parameters.highest_responsibility: aware of violation and took no action

rules.applies_to: Creating, controlling and correcting employers on multi-employer worksites
rules.citation: Cal/OSHA Compliance Manual Ch. 14-B, VI.1.a(6); 8 CCR 336.10
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/DOSHPol/P&PC-1C.pdf (Compliance Manual Chapter 14, PDF pp. 49-50 of 65, section VI.1.a(6)(a)-(c))
rules.quote: An employer who is aware of the violation and takes no action to correct it or prevent employee exposure to it has a high degree of responsibility for the violation.
rules.notes: Enforcement-policy guidance, not a regulation. Useful for a GC daily-inspection and hazard-log feature: documented inspections and corrective orders are the evidence of 'reasonable steps'.

rules.title: Inspectors collect every contract to decide who controlled safety
rules.plain_english: At a multi-employer inspection, Cal/OSHA collects copies of the contracts that set out each company's role. Safety clauses in your prime contract and subcontracts are evidence of who was the controlling employer.

documents_collected: contracts describing roles and obligations of all employers
parameters.controlling_employer_review: all provisions of the written contract between the owner or general contractor and the controlling employer

rules.applies_to: General contractors and subcontractors on multi-employer worksites
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/DOSHPol/P&PC-1C.pdf (Compliance Manual Chapter 14, PDF p. 49 of 65, section VI.1.a(3))
rules.quote: (3) A copy of the contract or contracts describing the respective roles and obligations of all the employers at the worksite.
rules.notes: Enforcement procedure; pairs with a subcontract safety-clause feature.

rules.title: Penalty size counts every exposed worker, whoever employs them
rules.plain_english: When Cal/OSHA sizes a penalty on a multi-employer site, it counts all the workers exposed to the hazard, including other companies' workers.
rules.applies_to: Every employer on a multi-employer worksite (construction and non-construction): general contractors, construction managers, subcontractors, owners who employ people
rules.citation: Cal/OSHA Compliance Manual Ch. 14-B, VII.2.c; 8 CCR 336
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/DOSHPol/P&PC-1C.pdf (Compliance Manual Chapter 14, PDF p. 52 of 65, section VII.2.c 'Penalty Calculations')
rules.quote: When determining "extent" and "likelihood" for the purpose of penalty calculations, the total number of employees exposed to the violative condition, regardless of who is the employer, shall be used.
rules.notes: Enforcement policy. Base penalty tables are in 8 CCR 336 (see web_calosha-programs calosha-penalty-amounts).

rules.title: A sole proprietor exposed alone is not a citable violation
rules.plain_english: A sole proprietor is not an employee. If the only person exposed to a hazard is a sole proprietor working alone, Cal/OSHA has no citable violation for that exposure.
rules.applies_to: Sole proprietors and the GCs that hire them
rules.citation: Cal/OSHA Compliance Manual Ch. 14-B, III (NOTE); Labor Code 3300(c) as cited by DOSH
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/DOSHPol/P&PC-1C.pdf (Compliance Manual Chapter 14, PDF p. 45 of 65, section III NOTE)
rules.quote: NOTE: A sole proprietor is not an employee. Therefore, if a sole proprietor is the only person exposed to a violative condition, there is no citable violation.
rules.notes: Labor Code 3300(c) text not readable (leginfo blocked); relies on DOSH's restatement. Employees of other employers exposed to the same hazard are still counted.

rules.title: Construction confined-space standard (Article 37): what it covers
rules.plain_english: Article 37 covers construction work at any site with a confined space, such as manholes, transformer vaults, pits, tanks, HVAC ducts, storm drains and precast manhole units. It does not apply to excavation work, tunnels, diving or pressurized work, which have their own rules.

exceptions: CSO Article 6 Excavations
Tunnel Safety Orders
GISO Group 26 Diving Operations
GISO Article 154 Pressurized Worksite Operations
example_locations: pits (elevator, escalator, pump, valve or other equipment)
manholes (sewer, storm drain, electrical, communication, or other utility)
tanks (fuel, chemical, water, or other liquid, solid or gas)
precast concrete and other pre-formed manhole units

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (a) This standard sets forth requirements for practices and procedures to protect employees engaged in construction activities at a worksite with one or more confined spaces, subject to the exceptions in subsection (b) of this section.
rules.notes: Article 37 (sections 1950-1962) operative 2015-12-30; 1950 was not changed by the 2026 amendments. The 2026 amendments also struck 'Construction operations regulated by Section 1502' from the GISO 5156(b)(2) list of operations governed by 5158, and struck the 5156 NOTE pointing construction to Article 37; the wider effect on GISO 5156-5158 was not analyzed (5156(a) and 5157 were not read). The example list is from the NOTE to 1950(a) and is not exhaustive; any space meeting the 1951 definition is covered.

rules.title: Definition: confined space (3-part test)
rules.plain_english: A confined space is any space big enough for a worker to get fully inside, with limited or restricted ways in or out, and not designed for people to stay in continuously.

criteria: large enough and configured so an employee can bodily enter
limited or restricted means for entry and exit
not designed for continuous employee occupancy

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: Confined space means a space that: (1) Is large enough and so configured that an employee can bodily enter it; (2) Has limited or restricted means for entry and exit; and (3) Is not designed for continuous employee occupancy.
rules.notes: Definition not changed by the 2026 amendments.

rules.title: Definition: permit-required confined space (any 1 of 4 hazards)
rules.plain_english: A confined space becomes a permit-required space if it has, or could have, a hazardous atmosphere, material that could engulf a worker, a shape that could trap or suffocate someone, or any other serious safety or health hazard.

any_one_of: inwardly converging walls or downward-sloping tapering floor
any other recognized serious safety or health hazard

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: Permit-required confined space (permit space) means a confined space that has one or more of the following characteristics: (1) Contains or has a potential to contain a hazardous atmosphere; (2) Contains a material that has the potential for engulfing an entrant; (3) Has an internal configuration such that an entrant could be trapped or asphyxiated by inwardly converging walls or by a floor which slopes downward and tapers to a smaller cross-section; or (4) Contains any other recognized serious safety or health hazard.
rules.notes: Definition not changed by the 2026 amendments.

rules.title: Hazardous atmosphere: flammable gas or vapor above 10% of LFL
rules.plain_english: Air in a confined space is hazardous if flammable gas, vapor or mist is above 10% of its lower flammable limit (LFL/LEL) on the meter.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (1) Flammable gas, vapor, or mist in excess of 10 percent of its lower flammable limit (LFL);
rules.notes: Item (1) was not changed in 2026. See osha2-cs-no-entry-above-10pct-lfl for the 2026 entry prohibition at this level.

rules.title: Hazardous atmosphere: oxygen below 19.5% or above 23.5%
rules.plain_english: Air in a confined space is hazardous if oxygen is below 19.5% (deficient) or above 23.5% (enriched).
rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.citation: 8 CCR 1951 ('Hazardous atmosphere' (3); 'Oxygen deficient atmosphere'; 'Oxygen enriched atmosphere')
rules.quote: (3) Atmospheric oxygen concentration below 19.5 percent or above 23.5 percent;
rules.notes: Unchanged in 2026.

rules.title: Hazardous atmosphere: combustible dust above 20% of MEC (from 2026)
rules.plain_english: Starting January 1, 2026, airborne combustible dust in a confined space counts as a hazardous atmosphere once it is above 20% of the dust's minimum explosive concentration (MEC). The old 'meets its LFL / can't see 5 feet' test was removed.

parameters.prior_rule_until_2025_12_31: concentration meets or exceeds its LFL (approximated as dust obscuring vision at 5 feet or less)

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.citation: 8 CCR 1951 ('Hazardous atmosphere' (2); 'Minimum explosive concentration (MEC)'), as amended eff. 2026-01-01
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/OSHSB/documents/Confined-Spaces-in-Construction-OAL-Changes-Text.pdf (PDF p. 2 of 11, §1951 'Hazardous atmosphere' (2)); MEC definition p. 3; rulemaking page https://www.dir.ca.gov/OSHSB/Confined-Spaces-in-Construction.html
rules.quote: (2) Airborne combustible dust at a concentration that exceeds 20 percent of the minimum explosive concentration (MEC);
rules.notes: Amended text effective 2026-01-01 (OSHSB 'Confined Spaces in Construction', filed with Secretary of State 2025-11-04). As fetched on 2026-11-25 the dir.ca.gov/title8 section pages still showed only the 2015 history and pre-amendment wording, so the OAL-approved strikeout/underline text is the primary source for this rule. The quote is the clean as-amended reading of the OAL strikeout/underline text (struck words removed, underlined words kept). New definition: 'Minimum explosive concentration (MEC) means the minimum concentration of a combustible dust suspended in air, measured in mass per unit volume that would support (subsonic) combustion.'

rules.title: Hazardous atmosphere: toxic substance that could exceed its PEL (from 2026)
rules.plain_english: A toxic substance in a confined space makes the atmosphere hazardous if it has a Cal/OSHA exposure limit and could expose workers above that limit. The 2026 amendment added the 'could exceed the limit' wording.

parameters.measure: substance with a dose or PEL in CSO Article 4 or GISO Group 16
parameters.hazardous_if: could result in employee exposure in excess of its dose or permissible exposure limit

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (4) Atmospheric concentration of any substance for which a dose or a permissible exposure limit is published in Article 4 of the Construction Safety Orders and Group 16 of the General Industry Safety Orders and which could result in employee exposure in excess of its dose or permissible exposure limit;
rules.notes: Amended text effective 2026-01-01 (OSHSB 'Confined Spaces in Construction', filed with Secretary of State 2025-11-04). As fetched on 2026-11-25 the dir.ca.gov/title8 section pages still showed only the 2015 history and pre-amendment wording, so the OAL-approved strikeout/underline text is the primary source for this rule. The trailing clause beginning 'and which could result' is the underlined new text.

rules.title: Competent person must survey the work area for confined spaces when work begins (2026 wording)
rules.plain_english: Before work starts, each employer must have a competent person survey its work area for every confined space that exists at that time.

parameters.prior_rule_wording: before it begins work at a worksite, identify all confined spaces in which its employees may work

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (1) The employer shall have a competent person conduct an initial survey of its work area for confined spaces existing at the time work begins.
rules.notes: Amended text effective 2026-01-01 (OSHSB 'Confined Spaces in Construction', filed with Secretary of State 2025-11-04). As fetched on 2026-11-25 the dir.ca.gov/title8 section pages still showed only the 2015 history and pre-amendment wording, so the OAL-approved strikeout/underline text is the primary source for this rule. Replaces former 1952(a). 'Competent person' is defined in 8 CCR 1504 (already in the rulebook as competent-person-definition).

rules.title: Competent person must keep inspecting for new confined spaces (2026)
rules.plain_english: As the job changes, the employer must have a competent person inspect the work area often enough to catch new confined spaces created by the work, such as a newly enclosed vault or plenum.

parameters.frequency: with sufficient frequency to effectively identify new confined spaces

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (2) The employer shall have a competent person inspect its work area with sufficient frequency to effectively identify new confined spaces.
rules.notes: Amended text effective 2026-01-01 (OSHSB 'Confined Spaces in Construction', filed with Secretary of State 2025-11-04). As fetched on 2026-11-25 the dir.ca.gov/title8 section pages still showed only the 2015 history and pre-amendment wording, so the OAL-approved strikeout/underline text is the primary source for this rule. The quote is the clean as-amended reading of the OAL strikeout/underline text (struck words removed, underlined words kept). The 45-day proposal said 'periodically'; the adopted text struck it in favor of 'with sufficient frequency'. No fixed day count is set.

rules.title: Tell employees and the GC about each new confined space (2026)
rules.plain_english: Each employer must tell its own workers and the controlling contractor (usually the GC) about every new confined space it finds or creates during construction or demolition.

parameters.trigger: new confined space discovered or created by construction or demolition activity

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (3) The employer shall inform their employees and the controlling contractor of each new confined space discovered or created as a result of construction or demolition activity.
rules.notes: Amended text effective 2026-01-01 (OSHSB 'Confined Spaces in Construction', filed with Secretary of State 2025-11-04). As fetched on 2026-11-25 the dir.ca.gov/title8 section pages still showed only the 2015 history and pre-amendment wording, so the OAL-approved strikeout/underline text is the primary source for this rule. No deadline in days is stated.

rules.title: Competent person decides which spaces are permit spaces, including testing (2026)
rules.plain_english: A competent person must evaluate and test each confined space to decide whether it is a permit-required space. Testing is now part of every evaluation, not just 'as necessary'.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (4) The employer shall have a competent person identify each confined space that is a permit space, through consideration, evaluation and testing of the elements of that space.
rules.notes: Amended text effective 2026-01-01 (OSHSB 'Confined Spaces in Construction', filed with Secretary of State 2025-11-04). As fetched on 2026-11-25 the dir.ca.gov/title8 section pages still showed only the 2015 history and pre-amendment wording, so the OAL-approved strikeout/underline text is the primary source for this rule. The quote is the clean as-amended reading of the OAL strikeout/underline text (struck words removed, underlined words kept). Struck: 'and' after consideration and ', including testing as necessary'.

rules.title: Post DANGER signs (or equal) at each permit space
rules.plain_english: If a permit space exists, the employer who identifies it or is told about it must warn exposed workers, for example with a sign reading 'DANGER -- PERMIT-REQUIRED CONFINED SPACE, DO NOT ENTER'.

parameters.method: danger signs or other equally effective means
parameters.sample_sign_text: DANGER -- PERMIT-REQUIRED CONFINED SPACE, DO NOT ENTER

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (1) Inform exposed employees by posting danger signs or by any other equally effective means, of the existence and location of, and the danger posed by, each permit space; and NOTE to Section 1952(b)(1): A sign reading “DANGER -- PERMIT-REQUIRED CONFINED SPACE, DO NOT ENTER” or using other similar language would satisfy the requirement for a sign.
rules.notes: Unchanged in 2026.

rules.title: Inform union reps and the GC about each permit space (not just by sign)
rules.plain_english: Besides signs, the employer must tell its employees' authorized representatives and the controlling contractor, in a timely way and by a method other than posting, where each permit space is and what danger it poses.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (2) Inform, in a timely manner and in a manner other than posting, its employees' authorized representatives and the controlling contractor of the existence and location of, and the danger posed by, each permit space.
rules.notes: Unchanged in 2026.

rules.title: Keep your workers out of permit spaces they are not authorized to enter
rules.plain_english: An employer that knows about a permit space but has not authorized its workers to enter must take effective steps to keep them out.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (c) Each employer who identifies, or receives notice of, a permit space and has not authorized employees it directs to work in that space shall take effective measures to prevent those employees from entering that permit space, in addition to complying with all other applicable requirements of this standard.
rules.notes: Unchanged in 2026.

rules.title: Entry employers must have a written permit-space program on site
rules.plain_english: Any employer whose workers enter (or will enter) a permit space must have a written permit-space program meeting section 1953, implemented at the site and available to workers and their representatives before and during entry.

parameters.availability: prior to and during entry operations, to employees and authorized representatives

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: Entry employers shall have a written permit space program that complies with Section 1953 implemented at the construction site. The written program shall be made available prior to and during entry operations for inspection by employees and their authorized representatives.
rules.notes: Amended text effective 2026-01-01 (OSHSB 'Confined Spaces in Construction', filed with Secretary of State 2025-11-04). As fetched on 2026-11-25 the dir.ca.gov/title8 section pages still showed only the 2015 history and pre-amendment wording, so the OAL-approved strikeout/underline text is the primary source for this rule. 2026 definition: 'Entry employer means any employer whose employees enter or will enter a permit space.' (the old 'decides that an employee it directs will enter' wording and its NOTE were struck).

rules.title: Alternate (ventilation-only) entry: when it is allowed
rules.plain_english: You may skip the full permit program for a permit space only if the only hazard is the atmosphere, continuous forced-air ventilation alone keeps it safe, you have monitoring data proving it, and you document and share that data. You must still test, ventilate continuously and certify in writing before each entry.

conditions_all_required: all physical hazards eliminated or isolated; only hazard is actual or potential hazardous atmosphere
continuous forced air ventilation alone keeps space safe and entrants can exit safely if it stops
monitoring and inspection data support the above
any initial data-gathering entry done under full 1953-1960 procedures
determinations and data documented and made available to entrants
parameters.job_made_hoist: must be approved in writing by a registered professional engineer before use

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (1) An employer whose employees enter a permit space need not comply with Sections 1953 through 1955 and Sections 1957 through 1960, provided that all of the following conditions are met:
rules.notes: 1952(e)(2)(C) was amended effective 2026-01-01 to allow concurrent multi-gas testing (see osha2-cs-atmospheric-test-order). The rest of (e) is unchanged.

rules.title: Alternate-procedure entry: written pre-entry certification
rules.plain_english: Before each ventilation-only entry, the employer must certify in writing (date, location of the space, signature) that the space is safe and pre-entry steps were taken, and make it available to each entrant.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (I) The employer shall verify that the space is safe for entry and that the pre-entry measures required by Section 1952(e)(2) have been taken, through a written certification that contains the date, the location of the space, and the signature of the person providing the certification.
rules.notes: Unchanged in 2026.

rules.title: Test the air in order: oxygen, then flammables, then toxics (multi-gas OK from 2026)
rules.plain_english: Before and during entry, test the air first for oxygen, then for flammable gases and vapors, then for toxic gases. From 2026 a multi-gas meter that tests all at once is allowed as long as you read the results in that order.

parameters.concurrent_condition: order in which readings are examined is preserved

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (C) When testing for atmospheric hazards, test first for oxygen, then for combustible gases and vapors, and then for toxic gases and vapors. Concurrent testing for atmospheric hazards may be conducted with a multi-gas meter, provided the order in which readings are examined is preserved;
rules.notes: Amended text effective 2026-01-01 (OSHSB 'Confined Spaces in Construction', filed with Secretary of State 2025-11-04). As fetched on 2026-11-25 the dir.ca.gov/title8 section pages still showed only the 2015 history and pre-amendment wording, so the OAL-approved strikeout/underline text is the primary source for this rule. The quote is the clean as-amended reading of the OAL strikeout/underline text (struck words removed, underlined words kept).

rules.title: Reclassifying a permit space as non-permit requires a signed certification
rules.plain_english: A permit space can be treated as a non-permit space only if a competent person finds it has no atmospheric hazard and all other hazards are eliminated or isolated; the basis must be documented in a dated, signed certification. Ventilation alone does not count as eliminating a hazard.

fields: signature of person making the determination
parameters.if_hazard_arises: all employees exit; reevaluate and reclassify

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (3) The entry employer shall document the basis for determining that all hazards in a permit space have been eliminated or isolated, through a certification that contains the date, the location of the space, and the signature of the person making the determination.
rules.notes: Unchanged in 2026. 1952(f) separately requires a competent person to reevaluate a non-permit space when its use or configuration changes.

rules.title: Before entry: owner, GC and entry sub must exchange permit-space information
rules.plain_english: Before any permit-space entry, the property owner (host employer) gives the GC what it knows about each permit space; the GC passes that on to every entering sub and anyone whose work could create a hazard there; and each entry sub tells the GC which permit program it will follow.

host_employer_provides_to_controlling_co: location of each known permit space
hazards or reason it is a permit space
controlling_contractor_provides_to: each entity entering a permit space
any other entity whose activities could foreseeably create a hazard in the space
parameters.entry_employer_provides_to_controlling_c: permit space program it will follow, including hazards likely to be confronted or created
coordination_required_when: more than one entity enters at the same time
entry overlaps activities that could create a hazard in the space

rules.applies_to: Property owners/managers (host employers), general contractors (controlling contractors) and entry subcontractors
rules.quote: (2) Before entry operations begin, the controlling contractor shall:
rules.notes: Unchanged in 2026. Host employer and controlling contractor need not enter a space just to gather the information (NOTE to 1952(h)).

rules.title: After entry: GC debriefs each entry sub and reports back to the owner
rules.plain_english: After permit-space work, the GC must debrief each sub that entered about the program used and hazards found or created; the sub must report this to the GC promptly; and the GC passes it on to the property owner.

parameters.entry_employer: inform controlling contractor in a timely manner of program followed and hazards confronted or created

rules.applies_to: General contractors, entry subcontractors and host employers
rules.quote: (A) The controlling contractor shall debrief each entity that entered a permit space regarding the permit space program followed and any hazards confronted or created in the permit space(s) during entry operations;
rules.notes: Unchanged in 2026.

rules.title: No GC on site: the owner or hiring employer takes the controlling-contractor role
rules.plain_english: If there is no controlling contractor at the site, the property owner (host employer) or the employer who hires another company to do permit-space work must carry out the controlling contractor's duties.

fallback_controlling_contractor: employer who arranges for another employer's employees to perform permit space entry

rules.applies_to: Owner-builders, property owners and employers hiring confined-space subcontractors without a GC
rules.quote: (i) If there is no controlling contractor present at the worksite, the requirements for, and role of, controlling contactors in Section 1952 shall be fulfilled by the host employer or other employer who arranges to have employees of another employer perform work that involves permit space entry.
rules.notes: Unchanged in 2026. 'contactors' is a typo in the official text, quoted as published.

rules.title: What the written permit-space program must include
rules.plain_english: The written program must cover: preventing unauthorized entry; evaluating hazards; safe entry procedures; equipment; testing and monitoring; at least one attendant; designated roles and training; rescue and emergency medical procedures; the permit system; coordination with other employers; closing out entries; and reviews.

elements: prevent unauthorized entry
identify and evaluate hazards before entry
safe entry procedures (acceptable entry conditions, isolation, purging/ventilating, barriers, verifying conditions, entrance covers, ignition-source prohibition, area surveillance)
provide and maintain equipment at no cost
evaluate conditions (testing and monitoring)
at least one attendant
multi-space attendant procedures
designate roles and train
rescue and emergency medical service procedures
permit system
coordinate with controlling contractor when multiple employers
conclude entry procedures
review when program may not protect
review within 1 year after each entry

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/OSHSB/documents/Confined-Spaces-in-Construction-OAL-Changes-Text.pdf (PDF p. 6 of 11, §1953(a) intro); full list at https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/1953.html
rules.quote: A permit space program shall be documented in accordance with Section 1952(d) and as part of the program, each entry employer shall:
rules.notes: Amended text effective 2026-01-01 (OSHSB 'Confined Spaces in Construction', filed with Secretary of State 2025-11-04). As fetched on 2026-11-25 the dir.ca.gov/title8 section pages still showed only the 2015 history and pre-amendment wording, so the OAL-approved strikeout/underline text is the primary source for this rule. Items (1)-(14) are listed in 1953(a); 2026 added (a)(3)(I)-(J) and restructured (a)(9).

rules.title: Confined-space equipment must be provided free and maintained
rules.plain_english: The entry employer must provide at no cost, maintain, and make sure workers properly use: gas monitors, ventilation, communications, PPE, approved lighting, barriers, ladders, and rescue equipment.

equipment: lighting meeting 1523 and approved for the atmosphere

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (4) Provide the following equipment (specified in Section 1953(a)(4)(A) through (a)(4)(I)) at no cost to each employee, maintain that equipment properly, and ensure that each employee uses that equipment properly:
rules.notes: Unchanged in 2026.

rules.title: No entry above 10% LFL unless inerted, IDLH respirators and all hazards isolated (2026)
rules.plain_english: From 2026, nobody may enter a permit space where flammable gas or vapor can't be brought below 10% of the LFL, unless the space is inerted for the whole entry, entrants wear IDLH-rated respiratory protection under section 5144(d)(2), and all other physical hazards are eliminated or isolated.

exception_requires_all: space rendered inert for duration of entry
respiratory protection per 5144(d)(2) for IDLH atmospheres
all additional physical hazards eliminated or isolated

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: 1. Except when the entry employer complies with all of the following, no entry shall be made into a permit space where the entry employer is unable to reduce the concentration of flammable gases, mists, or vapors below 10 percent of the LFL:
rules.notes: Amended text effective 2026-01-01 (OSHSB 'Confined Spaces in Construction', filed with Secretary of State 2025-11-04). As fetched on 2026-11-25 the dir.ca.gov/title8 section pages still showed only the 2015 history and pre-amendment wording, so the OAL-approved strikeout/underline text is the primary source for this rule. Replaces the former NOTE to 1953(a)(3)(D), which allowed entry with inerting plus PPE.

rules.title: No hot work or ignition sources in (or next to) a flammable or oxygen-enriched permit space (2026)
rules.plain_english: From 2026 the permit program must prohibit flame, arc, spark or other ignition sources inside a permit space, or in any space sharing a wall, floor or ceiling with it, that has or could develop a flammable/explosive or oxygen-enriched atmosphere.

prohibited: flame
arc
spark
other source of ignition
locations: adjacent space with common walls, floor or ceiling
atmosphere_conditions: hazardous atmosphere from flammable or explosive substances (present or likely)

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (I) Prohibiting work involving the use of flame, arc, spark, or other source of ignition within a permit space (or any adjacent space having common walls, floor, or ceiling with the permit space) which contains, or is likely to develop, a hazardous atmosphere due to flammable or explosive substances, or contains, or is likely to develop an oxygen enriched atmosphere; and
rules.notes: Amended text effective 2026-01-01 (OSHSB 'Confined Spaces in Construction', filed with Secretary of State 2025-11-04). As fetched on 2026-11-25 the dir.ca.gov/title8 section pages still showed only the 2015 history and pre-amendment wording, so the OAL-approved strikeout/underline text is the primary source for this rule. Any hot work permit issued for a permit space must also be listed on the entry permit (1955(a)(16)).

rules.title: Watch the surrounding area for drifting vapors (2026)
rules.plain_english: From 2026 the permit program must include watching the area around the permit space for hazards such as vapors drifting from tanks, piping and sewers.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (J) Conducting surveillance of the surrounding area(s) to avoid hazards such as drifting vapors from tanks, piping, and sewers.
rules.notes: Amended text effective 2026-01-01 (OSHSB 'Confined Spaces in Construction', filed with Secretary of State 2025-11-04). As fetched on 2026-11-25 the dir.ca.gov/title8 section pages still showed only the 2015 history and pre-amendment wording, so the OAL-approved strikeout/underline text is the primary source for this rule.

rules.title: At least one attendant outside the permit space for the whole entry
rules.plain_english: Someone must stay outside as attendant the entire time anyone is in a permit space. One attendant may cover more than one space only if they can do all attendant duties for each.

parameters.multiple_spaces_condition: duties in 1958 can be effectively performed for each space; program includes emergency procedures

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (6) Provide at least one attendant outside the permit space into which entry is authorized for the duration of entry operations;
rules.notes: Unchanged in 2026.

rules.title: Written procedures for rescue and emergency medical services (2026 wording)
rules.plain_english: The program must have procedures for calling rescue and emergency medical services (including if a non-entry rescue fails), rescuing entrants, getting emergency medical care that meets section 1512(e), and keeping unauthorized people from attempting rescue.

procedures: summon rescue and emergency medical services, including after failed non-entry rescue
obtain emergency medical services specified under 1512(e)
prevent unauthorized personnel from attempting rescue

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (C) Obtaining emergency medical services specified under Section 1512(e) for rescued employees; and
rules.notes: Amended text effective 2026-01-01 (OSHSB 'Confined Spaces in Construction', filed with Secretary of State 2025-11-04). As fetched on 2026-11-25 the dir.ca.gov/title8 section pages still showed only the 2015 history and pre-amendment wording, so the OAL-approved strikeout/underline text is the primary source for this rule. The quote is the clean as-amended reading of the OAL strikeout/underline text (struck words removed, underlined words kept). Section 1512 (emergency medical services) is covered in web_calosha-programs; a 2026 OSHSB first-aid rulemaking for 1512 was noticed 2025-11-28 and is not yet adopted per the OSHSB proposed list.

rules.title: Review the permit program within 1 year after each entry
rules.plain_english: Using the canceled permits, review and fix the permit-space program within one year after each entry. One annual review can cover all entries in a 12-month period; if there were no entries, no review is needed.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (14) Review the permit space program, using the canceled permits retained under Section 1954(f), within 1 year after each entry and revise the program as necessary to ensure that employees participating in entry operations are protected from permit space hazards.
rules.notes: Unchanged in 2026. The period is stated in years ("within 1 year after each entry"); compute the due date by adding one calendar year to the entry date.
rules.correction: The source sets the period as "within 1 year after each entry"; no day count appears in the text. Replaced review_within_days_after_entry = 365 with review_within_years_after_entry = 1, because a 365-day count is one day short of a calendar year whenever a February 29 falls in the period. The single-annual-review rule, the no-entries/no-review rule and the triggers for other reviews are confirmed.

rules.title: Entry permit: prepared, signed by the entry supervisor, posted at the entry
rules.plain_english: Before entry, prepare an entry permit, have the entry supervisor sign it, and post it at the entry portal (or equal) so entrants can see the prep is done. The permit can last no longer than the job it covers.

parameters.availability: posted at entry portal or equally effective means
parameters.max_duration: time required to complete the assigned task or job on the permit

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (b) Before entry begins, the entry supervisor identified on the permit shall sign the entry permit to authorize entry.
rules.notes: Section 1954 was not changed in 2026.

rules.title: Entry supervisor must cancel or suspend the permit when work ends or conditions change
rules.plain_english: The entry supervisor must cancel the permit when the work is done, and suspend or cancel it (and fully reassess the space) if a condition not allowed by the permit arises.

parameters.suspend_or_cancel_when: temporary prohibited condition that does not change configuration or create new hazards

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (1) Cancel the entry permit when the entry operations covered by the entry permit have been completed; or
rules.notes: Unchanged in 2026.

rules.title: Keep canceled entry permits at least 1 year
rules.plain_english: Keep every canceled entry permit for at least one year, and note on it any problems during the entry.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (f) The entry employer shall retain each canceled entry permit for at least 1 year to facilitate the review of the permit-required confined space program required by Section 1953(a)(14).
rules.notes: Unchanged in 2026. The period is stated in years ("at least 1 year"); compute the earliest disposal date by adding one calendar year to the cancellation date. Documents must be produced to the DOSH Chief on request (1962).
rules.correction: The source says "for at least 1 year"; no day count appears in the text. Replaced retention_days_min = 365 with retention_years_min = 1. A 365-day retention is one day short of the legal minimum whenever a February 29 falls in the year. Noting problems on the permit is confirmed.

rules.title: Entry permit: 16 required items
rules.plain_english: The entry permit must list the space, purpose, date and duration, entrants, how a ventilation failure will be detected, attendants and entry supervisor by name, hazards, isolation and control measures, acceptable entry conditions, test results with tester and time, how to summon rescue and emergency medical services, communication method, equipment, other needed information, and any other permits such as hot work.

items: means of detecting increased atmospheric hazard if ventilation stops
entry supervisor by name with signature/initials
test and monitoring results with tester names/initials and times
means to summon rescue services and obtain emergency medical services under 1512(e)
additional permits such as hot work

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/1955.html (subsection (a)); item (12) as amended at https://www.dir.ca.gov/OSHSB/documents/Confined-Spaces-in-Construction-OAL-Changes-Text.pdf (PDF p. 8 of 11)
rules.quote: (a) The entry permit that documents compliance with this section and authorizes entry to a permit space shall identify:
rules.notes: Items (1)-(11) and (13)-(16) unchanged since 2015-12-30. Item (12) as amended 2026-01-01 reads: 'The means (such as the equipment to use and the numbers to call) to summon rescue services and obtain emergency medical services specified under Section 1512(e);' (clean reading of OAL text).

rules.title: Confined-space training: when it must be given
rules.plain_english: Train each affected worker, free and in a language they understand, before their first assignment, before a change in duties, when entry operations change in a way that creates a new hazard, and whenever they deviate from procedures or show gaps in knowledge.

parameters.language: language and vocabulary the employee can understand
triggers: change in operations presenting untrained hazard
evidence of deviation from procedures or inadequate knowledge

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (b) Training required by this section shall be provided to each affected employee:
rules.notes: 1956(b) unchanged in 2026; 1956(a) content was restructured (see osha2-cs-training-content).

rules.title: Confined-space training content: written procedures, hazards, controls, no unauthorized rescue (2026)
rules.plain_english: Training must give workers an understanding of the written procedures, the hazards in the permit space, and the methods used to protect them. Workers not authorized for entry rescue must be trained on the dangers of attempting unauthorized rescues.

content: methods used to isolate, control or otherwise protect employees

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (2) Employees not authorized to perform entry rescues shall be trained in the dangers of attempting unauthorized rescues.
rules.notes: Amended text effective 2026-01-01 (OSHSB 'Confined Spaces in Construction', filed with Secretary of State 2025-11-04). As fetched on 2026-11-25 the dir.ca.gov/title8 section pages still showed only the 2015 history and pre-amendment wording, so the OAL-approved strikeout/underline text is the primary source for this rule. The quote is the clean as-amended reading of the OAL strikeout/underline text (struck words removed, underlined words kept). The 2026 text added '(A) The written procedures' as a required training element.

rules.title: Confined-space training records: name, trainer, date
rules.plain_english: Keep training records showing each employee's name, the trainers' names and the training dates, available to employees and their representatives for as long as the employee works for you.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: The training records shall contain each employee's name, the name of the trainers, and the dates of training. The documentation shall be available for inspection by employees and their authorized representatives, for the period of time the employee is employed by that employer.
rules.notes: Unchanged in 2026.

rules.title: Authorized entrant duties
rules.plain_english: Entrants must know the hazards, use the equipment, keep in contact with the attendant, alert the attendant to warning signs or prohibited conditions, and get out fast when ordered, when an alarm sounds, or when they notice danger.

exit_immediately_when: attendant or entry supervisor orders evacuation
warning sign or symptom of exposure

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (5) Exit from the permit space as quickly as possible whenever:
rules.notes: Unchanged in 2026.

rules.title: Attendant duties: stay outside, keep a count, order evacuation, summon rescue
rules.plain_english: The attendant stays outside until relieved, keeps an accurate count of who is inside, keeps in contact, orders evacuation when conditions require, calls rescue, keeps unauthorized people away, performs non-entry rescue, and does nothing that distracts from protecting entrants.

order_evacuation_when: behavioral effects of exposure in entrant

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (4) Remains outside the permit space during entry operations until relieved by another attendant;
rules.notes: Unchanged in 2026.

rules.title: Entry supervisor duties: verify permit, confirm rescue availability, terminate entry
rules.plain_english: The entry supervisor checks that every test, procedure and piece of equipment on the permit is in place before signing, confirms rescue services are available and reachable, removes unauthorized people, and ends entry and cancels or suspends the permit when required.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (4) Verifies that rescue services are available and that the means for summoning them are operable, and that the employer will be notified as soon as the services become unavailable;
rules.notes: Unchanged in 2026. The entry supervisor must be a qualified person (1951 definition).

rules.title: Rescue services must be trained, immediately available and equipped (2026)
rules.plain_english: From 2026 the entry employer must make sure the rescue service at the site is trained, immediately available, properly equipped, and able to do permit-space rescue and get emergency medical services per section 1512(e).

rescue_service_must_be: capable of obtaining emergency medical services under 1512(e)

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (a) The entry employer shall ensure the rescue services at the site are trained, immediately available, properly equipped, and capable of performing permit space rescue and obtaining emergency medical services specified under Section 1512(e).
rules.notes: Amended text effective 2026-01-01 (OSHSB 'Confined Spaces in Construction', filed with Secretary of State 2025-11-04). As fetched on 2026-11-25 the dir.ca.gov/title8 section pages still showed only the 2015 history and pre-amendment wording, so the OAL-approved strikeout/underline text is the primary source for this rule. New subsection; former 1960(a)-(d) were relettered (b)-(e) and the section retitled 'Permit Space Rescue and Emergency Medical Services.' Relying on a 911 fire department response requires confirming it meets this standard.

rules.title: Evaluate and select an outside rescue service; give it site access
rules.plain_english: If you designate a rescue service, evaluate its response time and proficiency for your spaces, pick one that can reach victims in time, is equipped and proficient, and will tell you immediately if it becomes unavailable; tell it the hazards and let it access the spaces to plan and practice.

evaluate: proficiency with rescue tasks and equipment
selection_criteria: agrees to notify employer immediately if unavailable
provide_to_rescue_service: access to all permit spaces for planning and practice

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (C) Agrees to notify the employer immediately in the event that the rescue service becomes unavailable;
rules.notes: Relettered from (a) to (b) effective 2026-01-01 and 'and emergency' struck from the intro; the subparts quoted are unchanged.

rules.title: In-house rescue team: first aid/CPR and practice rescue every 12 months
rules.plain_english: If your own employees are the rescue team, give them PPE and training at no cost, train them in first aid and CPR with at least one currently certified member available, and have them practice a simulated rescue before any real rescue and at least every 12 months.

parameters.practice_waived_if: properly performed actual rescue in same or similar space within last 12 months

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose own employees are designated to perform permit-space rescue
