rules.quote: (4) Ensure that affected employees practice making permit space rescues before attempting an actual rescue, and at least once every 12 months, by means of simulated rescue operations in which they remove dummies, manikins, or actual persons from the actual permit spaces or from representative permit spaces,
rules.notes: Relettered (b)->(c) effective 2026-01-01; the intro now reads 'permit space rescue and/or emergency medical services'. Subparts (1)-(4) unchanged.

rules.title: Non-entry rescue: harness and retrieval line; mechanical device for vertical spaces over 5 ft deep
rules.plain_english: Non-entry rescue (retrieval from outside) is required unless it would add risk or not help. Entrants wear a chest or full-body harness with a retrieval line, anchored outside; a mechanical retrieval device must be available for vertical spaces more than 5 feet deep. If you don't choose non-entry rescue, you must designate an entry rescue service.

parameters.harness: chest or full body harness (wristlets/anklets only if harness infeasible)
parameters.confirm_before_entry: emergency assistance available if non-entry rescue fails

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: A mechanical device shall be available to retrieve personnel from vertical type permit spaces more than 5 feet (1.52 meters) deep.
rules.notes: Relettered (c)->(d) effective 2026-01-01; text unchanged.

rules.title: Send the SDS with an injured entrant to the medical facility
rules.plain_english: If an injured entrant was exposed to a substance with a Safety Data Sheet at the site, the SDS must be made available to the treating medical facility.

parameters.document: Safety Data Sheet or similar written information
parameters.provide_to: medical facility treating the exposed entrant

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (d) If an injured entrant is exposed to a substance for which a Safety Data Sheet (SDS) or other similar written information is required to be kept at the worksite, that SDS or written information shall be made available to the medical facility treating the exposed entrant.
rules.notes: Relettered (d)->(e) effective 2026-01-01; text unchanged.

rules.title: Consult employees on the program; make all program information available; produce documents to Cal/OSHA
rules.plain_english: Employers must consult affected employees and their representatives in developing and running the permit-space program, give them all information the standard requires, and produce any required document to the Cal/OSHA Chief on request.

parameters.make_available_to_employees: all information required to be developed by this standard
parameters.produce_to: Chief of DOSH or designee, on request

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work at a worksite with one or more confined spaces (not excavations, tunnels, diving or pressurized work)
rules.quote: (a) Employers shall consult with affected employees and their authorized representatives on the development and implementation of all aspects of the permit space program required by Section 1952.
rules.notes: Unchanged in 2026. 1962(a): 'For each document required to be retained in this standard, the retaining employer shall make the document available on request to the Chief of the Division of Occupational Safety and Health or designee.'

rules.title: Definition: high voltage means more than 600 volts
rules.plain_english: Under Cal/OSHA's electrical rules, 'high voltage' means a sustained voltage over 600 volts. Most overhead power distribution lines are high voltage; building wiring at 120/240 or 480 volts is low voltage.
rules.applies_to: All California construction employers
rules.quote: High Voltage. A sustained voltage of more than 600 volts. (See Voltage.)
rules.notes: 8 CCR 2700 was last amended operative 2018-04-01 (history note 11, new definitions); 'effective' is that date. low_voltage_max_volts is derived (anything not over 600 volts is not 'high voltage'); 3638(f) NOTE likewise points to the Low Voltage ESO 'for work below 600 volts'.

rules.title: Construction electrical work must follow the listed Electrical Safety Orders
rules.plain_english: All electrical work on a construction site must follow the Electrical Safety Orders that CSO section 1760 lists, including lockout of de-energized equipment (2320.4), temporary wiring and GFCI rules (2405.x), and the overhead high-voltage line clearances (2946-2947).
rules.applies_to: All California construction employers
rules.quote: All electrical work shall be performed in accordance with the following provisions of the Electrical Safety Orders, Title 8, California Administrative Code, which are hereby expressly incorporated by reference.
rules.notes: Last amendment filed 3-16-83, effective thirtieth day thereafter (date computed). Other ESO sections (e.g., 2320.2, 2320.5, 2320.7, 2948) are not listed in 1760 but the Low-Voltage ESO also apply by their own terms to all places of employment.

rules.title: No work near energized high-voltage lines until contact danger is guarded against
rules.plain_english: Nobody may have employees work, dig, build, demolish, or set up equipment, scaffolds, pile drivers, drill rigs or hoists near energized high-voltage lines until the danger of accidental contact has been effectively guarded against.

activities: erecting/operating/storing tools, machinery, equipment, materials or structures
parameters.condition_to_proceed: danger from accidental contact effectively guarded against

rules.applies_to: Any employer whose employees, equipment, materials or structures (cranes, boom lifts, scaffolds, pumps, excavators, ladders, stored materials) may come near energized overhead high-voltage lines (over 600 volts)
rules.quote: (a) General. No person, firm, or corporation, or agent of same, shall require or permit any employee to perform any function in proximity to energized high-voltage lines; to enter upon any land, building, or other premises and there engage in any excavation, demolition, construction, repair, or other operation; or to erect, install, operate, or store in or upon such premises any tools, machinery, equipment, materials, or structures (including scaffolding, house moving, well drilling, pile driving, or hoisting equipment) unless and until danger from accidental contact with said high-voltage lines has been effectively guarded against.
rules.notes: Section last amended operative 2022-07-26 (new (e)-(f)); subsection (a) wording dates from earlier amendments. Overhead-line clearance rules do not apply where lines are de-energized and visibly grounded.

rules.title: Never handle tools, materials or equipment over energized high-voltage lines
rules.plain_english: Operating, erecting or handling tools, machinery, materials or anything else over energized overhead high-voltage lines is prohibited (limited exceptions for aircraft and limit-switched tower cranes).

parameters.prohibited: operation, erection or handling of tools, machinery, apparatus, supplies or materials over energized overhead high-voltage lines
exceptions: aircraft operating under FAA rules and/or CSO Article 35
tower cranes installed beyond Table 2 clearances with limit switches preventing loads over or within Table 2 distance of lines

rules.applies_to: Any employer whose employees, equipment, materials or structures (cranes, boom lifts, scaffolds, pumps, excavators, ladders, stored materials) may come near energized overhead high-voltage lines (over 600 volts)
rules.quote: (1) Over Lines. The operation, erection, or handling of tools, machinery, apparatus, supplies, or materials, or any part thereof, over energized overhead high-voltage lines shall be prohibited.
rules.notes: Subsection (b) last amended operative 2018-04-01.

rules.title: Overhead lines: minimum clearance for people, tools and materials (Table 1)
rules.plain_english: Keep every part of a worker's body, tools, materials, scaffolds and structures at least 6 feet from energized overhead lines up to 50,000 volts, 10 feet up to 345,000 volts, 16 feet up to 750,000 volts and 20 feet up to 1,000,000 volts (phase to phase). Booms must use the larger Table 2 distances.

applies_to_activities: operation, erection, handling or transportation of tools, machinery, materials, structures, scaffolds
any part of an employee's body
parameters.boom_type_equipment_uses: Table 2 (Table 1 only in transit with boom lowered and no load)

rules.applies_to: Any employer whose employees, equipment, materials or structures (cranes, boom lifts, scaffolds, pumps, excavators, ladders, stored materials) may come near energized overhead high-voltage lines (over 600 volts)
rules.quote: (2) The operation, erection, handling, or transportation of tools, machinery, materials, structures, scaffolds, or the moving of any house or other building, or any other activity where any parts of the above or any part of an employee's body will come closer than the minimum clearances from energized overhead lines as set forth in Table 1 shall be prohibited.
rules.notes: Table 1 rows read from the dir.ca.gov page (the voltage ranges are separated by leader dots in the HTML table). Lookup: use the row where over_volts < nominal_voltage <= up_to_volts; the first row starts at 600 volts. A qualified-person exemption exists under 2949.

rules.title: Table 2 clearances: boom-type equipment (including boom-type lifting or hoisting equipment) and storage near lines
rules.plain_english: Boom-type equipment (for example cranes, boom trucks, concrete pump booms, boom lifts and bucket trucks, and other machines that work with a boom) and any material stored near lines must stay at least 10 feet from lines up to 50,000 volts, rising to 11, 13, 15, 17, 21, 27 and 42 feet for higher voltages up to 1,000,000 volts. Boom-type equipment in transit with the boom lowered and no load uses the smaller Table 1 distances.

applies_to: operation of boom-type equipment (2946(b)(2), last paragraph)
erection, operation or dismantling of boom-type lifting or hoisting equipment (2946(b)(3))
storage of tools, machinery, equipment, supplies, materials or apparatus under, by or near lines (2946(b)(4))
parameters.boom_type_equipment_rule_text: Operation of boom-type equipment shall conform to the minimum clearances set forth in Table 2, except in transit where the boom is lowered and there is no load attached, in which case the distances specified in Table 1 shall apply.

rules.applies_to: Any employer whose employees, equipment, materials or structures (cranes, boom lifts, scaffolds, pumps, excavators, ladders, stored materials) may come near energized overhead high-voltage lines (over 600 volts)
rules.quote: (3) Boom-type lifting or hoisting equipment. The erection, operation or dismantling of any boom-type lifting or hoisting equipment, or any part thereof, closer than the minimum clearances from energized overhead high-voltage lines set forth in Table 2 shall be prohibited.
rules.notes: Table 2 rows read from the dir.ca.gov page. The 10-foot figure for 50,000 volts or less is also the text of the required equipment warning sign (2947). Clearances may not be reduced by line or structure movement (2946(c)). 'Boom-type equipment' is not defined in Article 37; the examples in plain_english are machines that carry a boom (a boom lift's or excavator's arm is its boom). Machines with no boom (scissor lifts, forklift masts, drill-rig masts) are not named by (b)(2)-(3) and fall under Table 1 by the rule text.
rules.correction: The rule limited Table 2 to 'boom-type lifting or hoisting equipment' and storage ((b)(3)-(4)) and missed the last paragraph of (b)(2): 'Operation of boom-type equipment shall conform to the minimum clearances set forth in Table 2, except in transit where the boom is lowered and there is no load attached, in which case the distances specified in Table 1 shall apply.' Table 2 therefore covers all boom-type equipment (boom lifts, excavators, telehandlers), not only lifting or hoisting equipment. Added that provision to title, plain_english, parameters.applies_to and the citation. The 8 table rows, the quote ((b)(3)) and the storage provision are unchanged and confirmed.

rules.title: Do not store material where it could be moved within Table 2 distance of lines
rules.plain_english: Storing tools, equipment or materials under or near energized overhead high-voltage lines is prohibited if handling them could bring any part within the Table 2 clearance.

parameters.prohibited: storage under, by or near energized overhead high-voltage lines
parameters.test: possible during handling to come closer than Table 2 clearance

rules.applies_to: Any employer whose employees, equipment, materials or structures (cranes, boom lifts, scaffolds, pumps, excavators, ladders, stored materials) may come near energized overhead high-voltage lines (over 600 volts)
rules.quote: (4) Storage. The storage of tools, machinery, equipment, supplies, materials, or apparatus under, by, or near energized overhead high-voltage lines is hereby expressly prohibited if at any time during such handling or other manipulation it is possible to bring such tools, machinery, equipment, supplies, materials, or apparatus, or any part thereof, closer than the minimum clearances from such lines as set forth in Table 2.
rules.notes: Typical violations: rebar, pipe, scaffold frames or roofing stock stored under service drops or distribution lines.

rules.title: Treat every overhead line as energized until the utility verifies and visibly grounds it
rules.plain_english: Assume every overhead conductor is live until the line's owner or operator verifies it is not energized and it is visibly grounded at the work site.

assume_energized_until: owner or operator verifies line is not energized
line visibly grounded at the work site

rules.applies_to: Any employer whose employees, equipment, materials or structures (cranes, boom lifts, scaffolds, pumps, excavators, ladders, stored materials) may come near energized overhead high-voltage lines (over 600 volts)
rules.quote: (d) Any overhead conductor shall be considered to be energized unless and until the person owning or operating such line verifies that the line is not energized, and the line is visibly grounded at the work site.
rules.notes: Subsection (d) last amended operative 2018-04-01.

rules.title: Designate a spotter when the operator can't easily judge line clearance
rules.plain_english: When site conditions or crane setup make it hard for the operator to see and keep the required clearance from power lines, a designated person must watch the clearance and give timely warning.

parameters.required_when: site conditions or crane configurations make it difficult for the operator to maintain clearance visually

rules.applies_to: Any employer whose employees, equipment, materials or structures (cranes, boom lifts, scaffolds, pumps, excavators, ladders, stored materials) may come near energized overhead high-voltage lines (over 600 volts)
rules.quote: (e) A person shall be designated to observe clearance of the equipment and give timely warning for all operations where site conditions or crane configurations make it difficult for the operator to maintain the desired clearance by visual means.
rules.notes: Subsections (e)-(f) added operative 2022-07-26.

rules.title: High-voltage warning sign required on cranes, drill rigs, pile drivers and similar equipment
rules.plain_english: Every crane, derrick, power shovel, drilling rig, pile driver or similar machine must carry a durable sign, readable at 12 feet and in view of the operator, stating it is unlawful to operate within 10 feet of high-voltage lines of 50,000 volts or less.

parameters.sign_text: Unlawful To Operate This Equipment Within 10 Feet Of High-Voltage Lines of 50,000 Volts Or Less.
parameters.small_print_text: For Minimum Clearances of High-Voltage Lines In Excess of 50,000 Volts, See California Code of Regulations, Title 8, Article 37, High-Voltage Electrical Safety Orders.
parameters.responsible: owner, agent, or employer responsible for operations of the equipment

rules.applies_to: Owners and employers operating cranes, derricks, drill rigs, pile drivers, boom trucks and similar equipment
rules.quote: The owner, agent, or employer responsible for the operations of equipment shall post and maintain in plain view of the operator and driver on each crane, derrick, power shovel, drilling rig, hay loader, hay stacker, pile driver, or similar apparatus, a durable warning sign legible at 12 feet reading: "Unlawful To Operate This Equipment Within 10 Feet Of High-Voltage Lines of 50,000 Volts Or Less."
rules.notes: Last amended operative 1988-01-09.

rules.title: Notify the power line operator before working within required clearances
rules.plain_english: If work, materials or equipment will come within the required clearances of energized high-voltage lines, the person responsible for the work must promptly notify the line operator (utility) and complete the required safety measures (such as de-energizing and grounding) before work that would reduce clearance.

parameters.timing: promptly, before proceeding with work that would impair clearance
parameters.responsible: person or persons responsible for the work

rules.applies_to: Any employer whose employees, equipment, materials or structures (cranes, boom lifts, scaffolds, pumps, excavators, ladders, stored materials) may come near energized overhead high-voltage lines (over 600 volts)
rules.quote: When any operations are to be performed, tools or materials handled, or equipment is to be moved or operated within the specified clearances of any energized high-voltage lines, the person or persons responsible for the work to be done shall promptly notify the operator of the high-voltage line of the work to be performed and shall be responsible for the completion of the safety measures as required by Section 2946 (b) before proceeding with any work which would impair the aforesaid clearance.
rules.notes: No fixed advance-notice day count is stated in 2948; utility scheduling for de-energizing or covering lines can take time.

rules.title: Overhead-line clearance rules do not apply to utility-authorized qualified electrical workers
rules.plain_english: Sections 2946-2948 do not apply to qualified electrical workers authorized by the line owner who build or maintain the lines, or to qualified persons using approved equipment and procedures under the High-Voltage orders. Everyone else (GCs, framers, roofers, crane and pump operators) must keep the clearances.

exempt: qualified electrical workers authorized by line owner working on the lines or supports
qualified persons using approved equipment and work procedures per Penal Code 385

rules.applies_to: Any employer whose employees, equipment, materials or structures (cranes, boom lifts, scaffolds, pumps, excavators, ladders, stored materials) may come near energized overhead high-voltage lines (over 600 volts)
rules.quote: The provisions of the foregoing Sections 2946 through 2948 shall not apply to the construction, reconstruction, maintenance, or operation of any energized overhead high-voltage lines or their supporting structures or appurtenances by qualified electrical workers, authorized by the owner of such lines, nor to work performed in proximity to energized overhead high-voltage lines by qualified persons using approved equipment and work procedures specified in these orders in accordance with Penal Code Section 385D.
rules.notes: Penal Code 385 text not read (leginfo blocked).

rules.title: Definition: qualified electrical worker needs at least 2 years high-voltage training and experience
rules.plain_english: A 'qualified electrical worker' is a qualified person with at least two years of training and experience on high-voltage circuits and equipment who has shown familiarity with the work and its hazards.
rules.applies_to: Electrical contractors (C-10) and line contractors assigning high-voltage work
rules.quote: Qualified Electrical Worker. A qualified person who by reason of a minimum of two years of training and experience with high-voltage circuits and equipment and who has demonstrated by performance familiarity with the work to be performed and the hazards involved.
rules.notes: Same definition appears in 2300 (Low-Voltage ESO). State electrician certification (Labor Code 108 et seq.) is a separate DLSE requirement not covered here.

rules.title: Only qualified persons may work on electrical equipment
rules.plain_english: Only qualified persons (designated by the employer and trained on the equipment and hazards) may work on electrical equipment or systems, or work near energized overhead conductors unless contact is prevented.

parameters.qualified_person_definition_2300: designated by the employer, trained in and demonstrated skills and knowledge in construction and operation of electric equipment and installations and the hazards involved

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work on or near electrical equipment or systems of 600 volts or less (Low-Voltage Electrical Safety Orders as incorporated by CSO 1760)
rules.quote: (a) Only qualified persons shall work on electrical equipment or systems.
rules.notes: Incorporated into the CSO by 1760.

rules.title: Working on exposed energized parts: required conditions (insulated gloves above 250 V to ground)
rules.plain_english: Live work is allowed only if supervision has decided it must be done energized, workers are instructed, and they use approved insulated gloves or tools, barriers, eye protection and barricades. Insulated gloves are mandatory above 250 volts to ground. Below 50 volts, gloves can be skipped only if a qualified person first confirms no shock, burn or arc risk.

parameters.glove_exception_condition: qualified person makes conclusive determination before work of no shock, burn, explosion or arc exposure
conditions: responsible supervision decided work is to be done energized
personnel instructed on techniques and hazards
suitable PPE and safeguards (approved insulated gloves or insulated tools)
barriers or insulating material
eye protection
barricades, tags or signs where required
non-melting apparel where exposed to flames or arcs

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work on or near electrical equipment or systems of 600 volts or less (Low-Voltage Electrical Safety Orders as incorporated by CSO 1760)
rules.quote: (4) Approved insulated gloves shall be worn for voltages in excess of 250 volts to ground.
rules.notes: Minimum approach distances for low voltage are in a table image in 2320.2(d) served from govt.westlaw.com, which was blocked by the session proxy; the table values were NOT read and are not included.

rules.title: Rubber insulating gloves retested at least every 6 months (sleeves 12 months)
rules.plain_english: Rubber insulating gloves must be electrically retested at least every 6 months and sleeves every 12 months; unused stock may not be issued unless tested within the previous 12 months (per ASTM F496-08, incorporated by 2320.2).

parameters.standard: ASTM F496-08

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees use rubber insulating gloves or sleeves for electrical work
rules.quote: NOTE: The ASTM F 496-08 standard contains provisions regarding the care, inspection, testing and use of insulating gloves and sleeves. Among other requirements, this standard provides that electrical retests shall not exceed 6 months for insulating gloves and 12 months for insulating sleeves and that insulating gloves and sleeves that have been electrically tested but not issued for service shall not be placed into service unless they have been electrically tested within the previous twelve months.
rules.notes: The NOTE summarizes the incorporated ASTM standard; the ASTM text itself was not read.

rules.title: No melting fabrics (acetate, nylon, polyester, rayon) when exposed to flames or arcs
rules.plain_english: Workers exposed to flames or electric arcs must wear clothing that won't make injuries worse; acetate, nylon, polyester and rayon (alone or blended) are prohibited unless treated with flame retardant.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work on or near electrical equipment or systems of 600 volts or less (Low-Voltage Electrical Safety Orders as incorporated by CSO 1760)
rules.quote: This subsection prohibits clothing made from the following types of fabrics, either alone or in blends, unless the employer can demonstrate that the fabric has been treated with flame retardant: acetate, nylon, polyester, and rayon.

rules.title: Lock (or tag) the disconnect before working on de-energized electrical equipment
rules.plain_english: Before work on de-energized electrical equipment, an authorized person must notify everyone involved, lock the disconnect open, tag it, and block or bleed stored energy (capacitors, springs, pneumatics). Tagging alone is allowed only where the disconnect is accessible only to people trained in the tagging procedure.

parameters.tag_only_allowed_when: tagging procedures used and disconnect accessible only to personnel instructed in them
parameters.not_required_if: equipment physically removed from the wiring system

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work on or near electrical equipment or systems of 600 volts or less (Low-Voltage Electrical Safety Orders as incorporated by CSO 1760)
rules.quote: (2) Locking the disconnecting means in the “open” position with the use of lockable devices, such as padlocks, combination locks or disconnecting of the conductor(s) or other positive methods or procedures which will effectively prevent unexpected or inadvertent energizing of a designated circuit, equipment or appliance.
rules.notes: Incorporated into the CSO by 1760. A 2006 change without regulatory effect amended (a)(3).

rules.title: Only the employee who placed a lock or tag may remove it
rules.plain_english: Before re-energizing, confirm everyone is clear. Locks and tags may be removed only by the employee who put them on, unless that employee is gone and the employer authorizes removal under its written procedure.

parameters.exception: employee left premises or unavailable; others authorized by employer under employer's procedure

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work on or near electrical equipment or systems of 600 volts or less (Low-Voltage Electrical Safety Orders as incorporated by CSO 1760)
rules.quote: (A) Locking devices and tags may be removed only by the employee who placed them.
rules.notes: Last amended 8-27-86, effective thirtieth day thereafter (date computed).

rules.title: Accident prevention tags: reason, who placed it and how to reach them, date
rules.plain_english: Each lockout/accident prevention tag must state why it was placed, the name of the person who placed it and how to contact them, and the date.

tag_fields: name of person placing tag and contact method

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work on or near electrical equipment or systems of 600 volts or less (Low-Voltage Electrical Safety Orders as incorporated by CSO 1760)
rules.quote: (a) Suitable accident prevention tags shall be used to control a specific hazard. Such tags shall provide the following minimum information:
rules.notes: Incorporated into the CSO by 1760.

rules.title: No conductive tapes or jewelry near exposed energized parts
rules.plain_english: Don't use conductive measuring tapes or ropes near exposed live parts, don't run metal fish tapes into live enclosures without barriers, and have workers remove rings, watches and chains when working within reach of exposed energized parts.

prohibited_near_exposed_energized_parts: conductive measuring tapes, ropes or similar
conductive fish tapes into enclosures with exposed energized parts (unless barriers)
parameters.barricades_required_when: opened enclosures with exposed energized equipment not under control of an authorized person

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees work on or near electrical equipment or systems of 600 volts or less (Low-Voltage Electrical Safety Orders as incorporated by CSO 1760)
rules.quote: (b) Conductive measuring tapes, ropes or similar measuring devices shall not be used when working on or near exposed energized conductors or parts of equipment.

rules.title: GFCI on all temporary 120 V 15/20 A receptacles (or an assured grounding program)
rules.plain_english: On construction sites, every 120-volt, single-phase, 15- or 20-amp receptacle that is not part of the building's permanent wiring and is used by employees must have GFCI protection, unless the employer runs an assured equipment grounding conductor program instead. Small two-wire generators of 5 kW or less with insulated circuits are exempt.

parameters.applies_to: receptacles not part of permanent wiring and in use by employees
parameters.alternative: assured equipment grounding conductor program (2405.4(d)); employer may use either or both
parameters.generator_exemption_conditions: two-wire single-phase portable or vehicle-mounted; circuit conductors insulated from frame

rules.applies_to: Construction employers (erection, demolition, alteration or excavation sites, other than mining)
rules.quote: All 120-volt, AC, single-phase, 15- and 20-ampere receptacle outlets on construction sites, which are not a part of the permanent wiring of the building or structure and which are in use by employees, shall have approved ground-fault circuit interrupters for personnel protection.
rules.notes: Incorporated into the CSO by 1760.

rules.title: Assured equipment grounding program: written, on site, run by a qualified person
rules.plain_english: If you use an assured equipment grounding conductor program instead of (or in addition to) GFCIs, it must be written, kept at the jobsite for Cal/OSHA and employees, and implemented by one or more designated qualified persons; equipment that passes must be identified (log, color code) with its last test date.

parameters.document: written assured equipment grounding conductor program
parameters.identification_shows: last test date or test interval

rules.applies_to: Construction employers choosing an assured equipment grounding conductor program
rules.quote: (1) A written description of the program, including the specific procedures adopted by the employer shall be available at the job site for inspection and copying by the Division of Occupational Safety and Health and any affected employee.
rules.notes: Equipment that has not met the program's requirements may not be made available or used (2405.4(d)(6)).

rules.title: Cords and tools: daily visual check; continuity tests at least every 3 months
rules.plain_english: Under an assured grounding program, inspect every cord set, plug and cord-connected tool visually before each day's use. Test grounding continuity and terminal connections before first use, after repairs, after suspected damage, and at least every 3 months (6 months for fixed receptacles not exposed to damage).

test_also_before: use after suspected damage (e.g., cord run over)
tests: correct attachment of grounding conductor at each receptacle and plug

rules.applies_to: Construction employers using an assured equipment grounding conductor program
rules.quote: (D) At intervals not to exceed three (3) months, except that cord sets and receptacles which are fixed and not exposed to damage shall be tested at intervals not exceeding 6 months.
rules.notes: Days not specified; months as stated.

rules.title: Before work starts, find out where energized circuits are, mark them and warn workers
rules.plain_english: Before work begins, the employer must find out (by asking, looking or using instruments) whether any energized power circuit, exposed or hidden, could be contacted by people, tools or machines; if so, mark or post warning signs and tell employees where the circuits are and how to stay safe.

if_present: legible marking of location or warning signs per GISO 3340
advise employees of location, hazards and protective measures per 1509

rules.applies_to: All California construction employers
rules.quote: (d) Before work is begun, the employer shall ascertain by inquiry, direct observation, or by instruments, whether any part of an energized electric power circuit, exposed or concealed, is so located that the performance of the work may bring any person, tool or machine into physical or electrical contact with the electric power circuit.
rules.notes: Typical use: wall and ceiling demolition in occupied buildings, core drilling, and saw cutting.

rules.title: Lockout/blockout (3314): when it applies
rules.plain_english: Section 3314 applies whenever workers clean, repair, service, set up, adjust or unjam machines or equipment where unexpected start-up or release of stored energy could hurt someone. Electrical work on energized systems follows the Electrical Safety Orders instead.

parameters.trigger: unexpected energization, start up, or release of stored energy could cause injury

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees clean, repair, service, set up or adjust machinery or equipment (GISO 3314; applies at construction sites through CSO 1502(c) for equipment not covered by the Construction Safety Orders)
rules.quote: (1) This Section applies to the cleaning, repairing, servicing, setting-up and adjusting of machines and equipment in which the unexpected energization or start up of the machines or equipment, or release of stored energy could cause injury to employees.
rules.notes: Construction examples: servicing concrete mixers, pumps, conveyors, saws, hoists and HVAC or process equipment in existing facilities. CSO 1502(c) applies other general orders to equipment not covered by the CSO.

rules.title: Stop, de-energize and block equipment before cleaning, servicing or adjusting; tag the controls
rules.plain_english: Machinery that can move must be stopped and its power shut off or disengaged, with moving parts blocked or locked out if needed, before cleaning, servicing or adjusting, and accident prevention signs or tags placed on the controls. If it must move during the task, use extension tools or other protection and train workers on them.

steps: mechanically block or lock out moveable parts if necessary
place accident prevention signs or tags on controls
parameters.if_movement_required: extension tools or other means plus thorough training

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees clean, repair, service, set up or adjust machinery or equipment (GISO 3314; applies at construction sites through CSO 1502(c) for equipment not covered by the Construction Safety Orders)
rules.quote: Machinery or equipment capable of movement shall be stopped and the power source de-energized or disengaged, and, if necessary, the moveable parts shall be mechanically blocked or locked out to prevent inadvertent movement, or release of stored energy during cleaning, servicing and adjusting operations.

rules.title: Lock out (or positively seal) equipment during repair and set-up
rules.plain_english: During repairs and set-up, equipment with lockable controls must be locked out or sealed in the off position; equipment without lockable controls must be disconnected or otherwise positively prevented from moving. Tags or signs always go on the controls, unless the employer uses a uniform system of personal, identifiable locks.

parameters.lockable_controls: locked out or positively sealed in off position
exceptions: minor routine tool changes during normal production with effective alternative measures
cord-and-plug equipment unplugged with plug under exclusive control of worker
tags not required with uniform system of unique, personally identifiable locks

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees clean, repair, service, set up or adjust machinery or equipment (GISO 3314; applies at construction sites through CSO 1502(c) for equipment not covered by the Construction Safety Orders)
rules.quote: Prime movers, equipment, or power-driven machines equipped with lockable controls or readily adaptable to lockable controls shall be locked out or positively sealed in the “off” position during repair work and setting-up operations.

rules.title: Written hazardous energy control procedures, with steps for each machine
rules.plain_english: The employer must have written hazardous-energy control procedures stating scope, purpose, authorization and rules, the steps to shut down, isolate, block and secure equipment, how locks/tags are placed, removed and transferred, and how to test that the lockout worked, with separate steps for each machine (or for a group of similar machines).

contents: steps for shutting down, isolating, blocking and securing
steps for placement, removal and transfer of lockout/tagout devices and responsibilities
requirements for testing to verify effectiveness
group_procedure_allowed_when: similar controls, identified disconnect points and similar steps
single readily identified energy supply with no stored or residual energy

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees clean, repair, service, set up or adjust machinery or equipment (GISO 3314; applies at construction sites through CSO 1502(c) for equipment not covered by the Construction Safety Orders)
rules.quote: (2) The employer's hazardous energy control procedures shall be documented in writing.

rules.title: Tagout attachments: non-reusable, self-locking, at least 50 lb unlocking strength
rules.plain_english: The employer must supply signs, tags, padlocks and seals. Tag attachment devices must be single-use, attachable by hand, self-locking and non-releasable, with an unlocking strength of at least 50 pounds.
rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees clean, repair, service, set up or adjust machinery or equipment (GISO 3314; applies at construction sites through CSO 1502(c) for equipment not covered by the Construction Safety Orders)
rules.quote: Tagout device attachment means shall be of a non-reusable type, attachable by hand, self-locking, and non-releasable with a minimum unlocking strength of no less than 50 pounds.

rules.title: Group lockout: one responsible authorized employee; each worker adds a personal lock
rules.plain_english: When a crew services equipment together, a group lockout procedure must give the same protection as personal locks: one authorized employee is responsible, the exposure status of each member can be checked, one person coordinates when several crafts are involved, and each worker puts a personal lock on the group lockbox when starting and removes it when done.

parameters.primary_responsibility: authorized employee for a set number of employees

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees clean, repair, service, set up or adjust machinery or equipment (GISO 3314; applies at construction sites through CSO 1502(c) for equipment not covered by the Construction Safety Orders)
rules.quote: (D) Each authorized employee shall affix a personal lockout or tagout device to the group lockout device, group lockbox, or comparable mechanism when he or she begins work and shall remove those devices when he or she stops working on the machine or equipment being serviced or maintained.
rules.notes: Subsections (h)-(i) added operative 2014-10-01.

rules.title: Keep lockout continuous across shift and personnel changes
rules.plain_english: Use specific procedures at shift or crew changes so lockout protection transfers in an orderly way from the off-going to the oncoming workers.
rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees clean, repair, service, set up or adjust machinery or equipment (GISO 3314; applies at construction sites through CSO 1502(c) for equipment not covered by the Construction Safety Orders)
rules.quote: Specific hazardous energy control procedures (i.e. lock-out/tag-out) shall be utilized during shift or personnel changes to ensure the continuity of lockout or tagout protection,

rules.title: Inspect each energy control procedure at least annually and certify it
rules.plain_english: At least once a year, someone other than the people using it must inspect each energy control procedure, review responsibilities with the authorized employees, and the employer must certify the inspection (machine, date, employees included, inspector).

parameters.inspector: authorized employee or person other than those using the procedure

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees clean, repair, service, set up or adjust machinery or equipment (GISO 3314; applies at construction sites through CSO 1502(c) for equipment not covered by the Construction Safety Orders)
rules.quote: The employer shall conduct a periodic inspection of the energy control procedure(s) at least annually to evaluate their continued effectiveness and determine necessity for updating the written procedure(s).
rules.notes: 'At least annually' expressed as 12 months.

rules.title: Contractors servicing equipment at a client's site must follow the site's lockout procedures
rules.plain_english: When outside servicing personnel (such as a contractor's crew) do work covered by 3314 at someone else's facility, the on-site employer's lockout/tagout procedures must be followed.

parameters.procedures_followed: on-site employer's lockout or tagout procedures

rules.applies_to: Contractors performing service, repair or tenant-improvement work on equipment in an operating facility, and the facility employer
rules.quote: (k) Whenever outside servicing personnel are to be engaged in activities covered by this section, the on-site employer's lockout or tagout procedures shall be followed.
rules.notes: Pairs with multi-employer coordination; consider adding to pre-job coordination checklists for work in operating plants, hospitals and campuses.

rules.title: Lockout training: authorized, affected and other employees; documented under the IIPP
rules.plain_english: Train authorized employees on the procedures and hazards, instruct affected employees on the purpose and use of the procedure, tell everyone else working nearby never to restart locked-out equipment, and document the training as the IIPP rule (3203) requires.

parameters.authorized_employees: hazardous energy control procedures and hazards
parameters.affected_employees: purpose and use of the procedure

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees clean, repair, service, set up or adjust machinery or equipment (GISO 3314; applies at construction sites through CSO 1502(c) for equipment not covered by the Construction Safety Orders)
rules.quote: (3) All other employees whose work operations may be in an area where energy control procedures may be utilized, shall be instructed about the prohibition relating to attempts to restart or reenergize machines or equipment which are locked out or tagged out.

rules.title: Scissor lifts are 'elevating work platforms'; boom lifts are 'aerial devices'
rules.plain_english: Cal/OSHA's Article 24 covers lifts that position workers. A scissor lift, vertical tower or mast-climbing platform is an 'elevating work platform'; a vehicle-mounted or self-propelled boom (telescoping or articulating) is an 'aerial device'. Forklifts, mobile scaffolds and material hoists are covered elsewhere.
rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees use elevating work platforms (scissor lifts, vertical towers, mast-climbing platforms) or vehicle-mounted/self-propelled aerial devices (boom lifts, bucket trucks) on construction sites (GISO Article 24 via CSO 1502(c) and 1735(o))
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/3637.html (definitions 'Aerial Device' and 'Elevating Work Platform'); https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/3636.html
rules.quote: Elevating Work Platform. A device designed to elevate a platform in a substantially vertical axis. (Vertical Tower, Scissor Lift, Mast-Climbing Work Platform)
rules.notes: 3637 definitions of Elevating Work Platform amended operative 2006-03-29.

rules.title: Operating and maintenance manual must stay on the lift
rules.plain_english: Each lift must have a manual with maintenance and operating instructions (including capacity in each configuration), kept in a weather-resistant storage spot on the machine.

parameters.document: manual with maintenance and operating instructions
parameters.location: weather resistant storage location on the unit

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees use elevating work platforms (scissor lifts, vertical towers, mast-climbing platforms) or vehicle-mounted/self-propelled aerial devices (boom lifts, bucket trucks) on construction sites (GISO Article 24 via CSO 1502(c) and 1735(o))
rules.quote: (1) The required manual(s) shall be maintained in a weather resistant storage location on the elevating work platform or aerial device.
rules.notes: Rental units: confirm the manual box is not empty at delivery.

rules.title: Lift must carry an ANSI compliance plate with capacity, height and serial data
rules.plain_english: Each lift needs a legible plate showing it was built to the applicable ANSI A92 standard (the edition depends on whether it was placed in service before or after December 23, 1999), plus make, model, serial number, rated capacity at max height, max travel height, and basic cautions and operating instructions.

plate_data: rated capacity at maximum platform height
basic operating instructions or reference to manual

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees use elevating work platforms (scissor lifts, vertical towers, mast-climbing platforms) or vehicle-mounted/self-propelled aerial devices (boom lifts, bucket trucks) on construction sites (GISO Article 24 via CSO 1502(c) and 1735(o))
rules.quote: (2) Each aerial device or elevating work platform placed in service on or after December 23, 1999 shall have a conspicuously displayed legible plate or other legible marking verifying the aerial device or elevating work platform is designed and manufactured in accordance with the following applicable specifications:

rules.title: Instruct lift users; qualified person assembles per manufacturer; HV-line work under Article 37
rules.plain_english: Employees must be instructed in proper platform use per Article 24, the manufacturer's instructions and the IIPP. A qualified person must assemble and erect lifts per the manufacturer (or under a registered PE if the manufacturer is gone). Work near energized high-voltage lines follows the overhead-line rules.

parameters.if_manufacturer_out_of_business: qualified person under direction of a registered professional engineer experienced in EWP/aerial device design

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees use elevating work platforms (scissor lifts, vertical towers, mast-climbing platforms) or vehicle-mounted/self-propelled aerial devices (boom lifts, bucket trucks) on construction sites (GISO Article 24 via CSO 1502(c) and 1735(o))
rules.quote: (d) Employees shall be instructed in the proper use of the platform in accordance with this Article, the manufacturer's operating instructions and Section 3203, Injury and Illness Prevention Program.

rules.title: Keep lift inspection and repair records at least 3 years
rules.plain_english: Inspections, maintenance and repairs must be done by a qualified person per the manufacturer, and records of inspections (date, deficiencies, corrective action, inspector) and repairs (date, work done, who did it) kept at least three years and shown to Cal/OSHA on request.
rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees use elevating work platforms (scissor lifts, vertical towers, mast-climbing platforms) or vehicle-mounted/self-propelled aerial devices (boom lifts, bucket trucks) on construction sites (GISO Article 24 via CSO 1502(c) and 1735(o))
rules.quote: (d) Records. Records of inspections and repairs shall be maintained for at least three years and be made available to the Division upon request.
rules.notes: For rented lifts the owner/rental company typically holds these records; the using employer should be able to obtain them.

rules.title: Lift platform guardrail 42 inches (plus or minus 3) with a midrail; under 39 inches requires fall protection
rules.plain_english: The platform must have a guardrail 42 inches high, plus or minus 3 inches, with a midrail. If the guardrail is under 39 inches, workers must use a personal fall protection system.
rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees use elevating work platforms (scissor lifts, vertical towers, mast-climbing platforms) or vehicle-mounted/self-propelled aerial devices (boom lifts, bucket trucks) on construction sites (GISO Article 24 via CSO 1502(c) and 1735(o))
rules.quote: A guardrail or other structure around its upper periphery that shall be 42 inches high, plus or minus 3 inches, with a midrail.
rules.notes: Mast-climbing work platforms may omit the inboard guardrail if the platform edge is within 7 in (glaziers, bricklayers, stonemasons) or 12 in (others) of the wall, or workers use personal fall protection per 1670.

rules.title: Scissor-lift equipment: toe boards 3.5 in, 16 in minimum width, emergency lowering over 60 in, upper and lower controls
rules.plain_english: Elevating work platforms need toe boards at least 3.5 inches high, a platform at least 16 inches wide, access-ladder rungs no more than 12 inches apart, emergency lowering if the platform goes above 60 inches, marked and guarded upper and lower controls, and an emergency stop at the upper controls.

controls: upper control in or beside platform
lower control able to lower platform

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees use elevating work platforms (scissor lifts, vertical towers, mast-climbing work platforms)
rules.quote: (c) Any elevating work platform equipped with a powered elevating assembly and having a platform height exceeding 60 inches shall be supplied with safe emergency lowering means compatible with the specific elevating assembly employed.
rules.notes: Toe boards may be omitted at access openings.

rules.title: Driving a scissor lift while elevated: 3 ft/sec max, interlocks, level surface
rules.plain_english: Nobody may ride (and no tools or materials may stay) on a moving elevated platform unless travel speed at maximum travel height is 3 feet per second or less, self-propelled units have interlocks preventing driving above the maximum travel height or too fast, and the surface is level with no debris or holes.

parameters.surface: level, no hazardous irregularities or debris

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees use elevating work platforms (scissor lifts, vertical towers, mast-climbing work platforms)
rules.quote: (1) The travel speed at Maximum Travel Height does not exceed 3 feet (0.9m) per second.

rules.title: Inspect scissor lifts before use; never overload; tag out damaged units
rules.plain_english: Assemble and use lifts per the manufacturer, inspect for damaged or defective parts before use, never load above the design working load, and take damaged or weakened units out of service until repaired.
rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees use elevating work platforms (scissor lifts, vertical towers, mast-climbing work platforms)
rules.quote: (c) Units shall be inspected for damaged and defective parts before use.

rules.title: No sitting, standing or climbing on lift guardrails; no planks or ladders to gain height
rules.plain_english: Workers may not sit, stand or climb on a lift's guardrails or basket edge, or use planks, ladders or other devices to reach higher.

prohibited: sit, stand or climb on guardrails or basket edge
planks, ladders or other devices to gain height or reach

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees use elevating work platforms (scissor lifts, vertical towers, mast-climbing platforms) or vehicle-mounted/self-propelled aerial devices (boom lifts, bucket trucks) on construction sites (GISO Article 24 via CSO 1502(c) and 1735(o))
rules.quote: (e) Employees shall not sit, stand or climb on the guardrails of an elevating work platform or use planks, ladders, or other devices to gain greater working height or reach.
rules.notes: Same prohibition for aerial devices in 3648(e). 3646(e) last amended operative 2001-02-22.

rules.title: No lift work in high winds, storms or ice; mark off traffic around the lift
rules.plain_english: Don't work on elevating platforms in high winds, storms, or when covered with ice or snow (unless safety provisions are made). Where vehicles move nearby, mark the work area with flags, rope it off or use other traffic control.

parameters.unless: provisions made to ensure employee safety

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees use elevating work platforms (scissor lifts, vertical towers, mast-climbing work platforms)
rules.quote: (f) Employees shall not work on units when exposed to high winds, storms, or when they are covered with ice or snow (unless provisions have been made to ensure the safety of the employees).
rules.notes: No wind speed number is stated in 3646; check the manufacturer's rated wind speed.

rules.title: Scissor-lift training by a qualified person: required topics
rules.plain_english: A qualified person must train employees who erect, move, operate, use, repair, maintain or inspect elevating work platforms, covering section 3646, their duties, electrical/fall/falling-object hazards, safe operation and material handling, and the platform's maximum load in its configuration.

topics: maximum load capacity for installed configuration

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees use elevating work platforms (scissor lifts, vertical towers, mast-climbing work platforms)
rules.quote: (l) Employees shall be instructed by a qualified person in the safe use of the work platform in accordance with the manufacturer's operating instructions, and Section 3203, Injury and Illness Prevention Program.
rules.notes: No retraining interval is stated in 3646.

rules.title: Mast-climbing work platforms may not be used as personnel or material hoists
rules.plain_english: A mast-climbing work platform may not be used as a construction personnel hoist or material hoist (moving tools and materials at the work location is allowed).

parameters.allowed: transfer of tools, materials and/or workers using personal fall protection at the work location

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees use elevating work platforms (scissor lifts, vertical towers, mast-climbing work platforms)
rules.quote: (k) Mast-climbing work platforms, shall not be used as construction personnel hoists or material hoists.

rules.title: Boom lifts: authorized operators only; test controls before use; ground controls only with permission
rules.plain_english: Only authorized persons may operate an aerial device. Test lift controls before use per the manufacturer, and don't use lower (ground) controls without permission from the worker in the basket except in an emergency.

parameters.lower_controls: only with permission of employee in device, except emergency

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees use aerial devices (boom lifts, articulating and extensible boom platforms, bucket trucks, aerial ladders)
rules.quote: (c) Only authorized persons shall operate an aerial device.

rules.title: Boom lifts: workers must be tied off to the boom or basket
rules.plain_english: Anyone in an elevated aerial device must be secured to the boom, basket or tub with a harness (or belt for restraint/positioning only). Positioning systems must limit free fall to 2 feet; a harness fall-arrest system must limit arresting force to 1,800 pounds and free fall to 6 feet.

parameters.exception: orchard man-lifts made after 1991-09-01 with 42 in+ guardrails

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees use aerial devices (boom lifts, articulating and extensible boom platforms, bucket trucks, aerial ladders)
rules.quote: (o) An employee, while in an elevated aerial device, shall be secured to the boom, basket or tub of the aerial device through the use of a safety belt, body belt or body harness equipped with safety strap or lanyard.
rules.notes: Elevating work platforms (scissor lifts) with compliant guardrails do not carry this tie-off rule; aerial devices (booms) do.

rules.title: Boom lifts: never tie off to, or rest the basket on, adjacent structures
rules.plain_english: Do not belt off to a nearby pole, structure or equipment while working from an aerial device, and do not let the basket be supported by an adjacent structure while workers are in it elevated.

prohibited: belting off to adjacent pole, structure or equipment
basket/platform supported by adjacent structure while occupied and elevated
wearing climbers while working from aerial device

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees use aerial devices (boom lifts, articulating and extensible boom platforms, bucket trucks, aerial ladders)
rules.quote: (d) Belting off to an adjacent pole, structure, or equipment while working from an aerial device shall not be permitted.

rules.title: Boom lifts: set brakes, chock wheels on inclines, outriggers on pads
rules.plain_english: When elevating workers with the vehicle stationary, set the brakes; install wheel chocks on an incline if it can be done safely; put outriggers on pads or a solid surface; and don't exceed manufacturer load limits.

parameters.wheel_chocks_on_incline: if they can be safely installed
parameters.outriggers: on pads or solid surface; hydraulic holding valves or mechanical locks

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees use aerial devices (boom lifts, articulating and extensible boom platforms, bucket trucks, aerial ladders)
rules.quote: (i) When used, outriggers shall be positioned on pads or a solid surface. All outriggers shall be equipped with hydraulic holding valves or mechanical locks at the outriggers.

rules.title: Moving an aerial device truck with someone in the elevated basket: 3 mph, one worker, route survey
rules.plain_english: A truck-mounted aerial device may not be moved with the boom up and a worker in the basket unless it is designed for it, controls are tested, there is constant communication, the route is surveyed just before, speed stays at 3 mph or less, only one worker is in the basket, and both driver and worker are trained for this.

all_required: driver and elevated employee specifically trained

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees use aerial devices (boom lifts, articulating and extensible boom platforms, bucket trucks, aerial ladders)
rules.quote: (5) The speed of the vehicle does not exceed three (3) miles per hour.

rules.title: Forklift operators must complete training and evaluation before operating
rules.plain_english: Before letting an employee operate a forklift (except while training), the employer must make sure the employee completed the required training and a competence evaluation.

parameters.exception: operation for training purposes under direct supervision
parameters.hired_after_2000_07_15: initial training and evaluation before assignment

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees operate powered industrial trucks (forklifts, rough-terrain and telehandler lift trucks) on construction sites (GISO Article 25 via CSO 1502(c)); agricultural operations exempt from 3668
rules.quote: (2) Prior to permitting an employee to operate a powered industrial truck (except for training purposes), the employer shall ensure that each operator has successfully completed the training required by this section, except as permitted in subsection (e).
rules.notes: Section operative 2000-07-15; 2011 change without regulatory effect to (a)(1)-(2). A training card from another employer does not replace the employer's own evaluation and certification (3668(e)-(f)).

rules.title: Forklift training: classroom plus hands-on plus workplace evaluation, by a qualified trainer
rules.plain_english: Training must combine formal instruction (lecture, video, computer or written), practical hands-on training, and evaluation of the operator in the workplace, all delivered by people with the knowledge, training and experience to train and evaluate operators. Trainees may drive only under direct supervision where it is safe.

components: evaluation of operator's performance in the workplace
parameters.trainer_qualification: knowledge, training and experience to train operators and evaluate competence
parameters.trainee_operation: direct supervision; must not endanger trainee or others

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees operate powered industrial trucks (forklifts, rough-terrain and telehandler lift trucks) on construction sites (GISO Article 25 via CSO 1502(c)); agricultural operations exempt from 3668
rules.quote: (3) Training shall consist of a combination of formal instruction (e.g., lecture, discussion, interactive computer learning, video tape, written material), practical training (demonstrations performed by the trainer and practical exercises performed by the trainee) and evaluation of the operator's performance in the workplace.
rules.notes: online_only_sufficient is derived from the required combination of components.

rules.title: Forklift training topics: truck-related and workplace-related
rules.plain_english: Initial training must cover truck topics (controls, steering, visibility, forks and attachments, capacity, stability, inspection, refueling/charging, limits) and workplace topics (surfaces, loads, stacking, pedestrians, narrow aisles, hazardous locations, ramps, carbon monoxide/diesel exhaust in closed areas, other site hazards), except topics shown not to apply.

truck_topics: fork and attachment use and limits

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees operate powered industrial trucks (forklifts, rough-terrain and telehandler lift trucks) on construction sites (GISO Article 25 via CSO 1502(c)); agricultural operations exempt from 3668
rules.quote: (c) Training program content. Powered industrial truck operators shall receive initial training in the following topics, except in topics which the employer can demonstrate are not applicable to the safe operation of the truck in the employer's workplace.
rules.notes: Construction sites: rough terrain, slopes and pedestrians are usually applicable workplace topics.

rules.title: Forklift refresher training: after unsafe operation, accident/near miss, bad evaluation, new truck type or changed conditions
rules.plain_english: Give refresher training (with an evaluation) when an operator is seen driving unsafely, has an accident or near miss, gets a poor evaluation, is assigned a different type of truck, or site conditions change in a way that affects safe operation.

triggers: workplace condition change affecting safe operation

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees operate powered industrial trucks (forklifts, rough-terrain and telehandler lift trucks) on construction sites (GISO Article 25 via CSO 1502(c)); agricultural operations exempt from 3668
rules.quote: (1) Refresher training in relevant topics shall be provided to the operator when:

rules.title: Evaluate each forklift operator at least every 3 years
rules.plain_english: Each forklift operator's performance must be evaluated at least once every three years.
rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees operate powered industrial trucks (forklifts, rough-terrain and telehandler lift trucks) on construction sites (GISO Article 25 via CSO 1502(c)); agricultural operations exempt from 3668
rules.quote: (2) An evaluation of each powered industrial truck operator's performance shall be conducted at least once every three years.
rules.notes: The interval is stated in years; compute the next due date by adding three calendar years to the last evaluation date.
rules.correction: The text says "at least once every three years"; no day count appears. Removed evaluation_interval_days_max = 1095 (3 x 365), because three calendar years are 1,095 or 1,096 days depending on leap years. A tool should compute the due date by adding 3 calendar years. The 3-year interval is confirmed.

rules.title: Forklift training certification: operator name, training date, evaluation date, trainer/evaluator
rules.plain_english: The employer must certify each operator's training and evaluation, listing the operator's name, the training date, the evaluation date, and who did the training or evaluation.
rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees operate powered industrial trucks (forklifts, rough-terrain and telehandler lift trucks) on construction sites (GISO Article 25 via CSO 1502(c)); agricultural operations exempt from 3668
rules.quote: (f) Certification. The employer shall certify that each operator has been trained and evaluated as required by this section. The certification shall include the name of the operator, the date of the training, the date of the evaluation, and the identity of the person(s) performing the training or evaluation.
rules.notes: No retention period is stated in 3668; keeping it at least until the next 3-year evaluation is the practical minimum.

rules.title: Only employer-authorized, trained drivers may operate forklifts; no riders on forks
rules.plain_english: Only drivers authorized by the employer and trained under 3668 may operate industrial trucks. No stunt driving, no riders unless there is a proper seat, nobody rides the forks, and nobody stands or walks under raised forks unless blocked.

parameters.operators: authorized by employer and trained per 3668
prohibited: stunt driving and horseplay
riders without adequate riding facilities
riding on forks
body parts outside running lines or between mast uprights
standing, passing or working under elevated portion unless blocked

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees operate powered industrial trucks (forklifts, rough-terrain and telehandler lift trucks) on construction sites (GISO Article 25 via CSO 1502(c)); agricultural operations exempt from 3668
rules.quote: (1) Only drivers authorized by the employer and trained in the safe operations of industrial trucks or industrial tow tractors pursuant to Section 3668 shall be permitted to operate such vehicles.
rules.notes: 3650 last amended operative 2017-10-01.

rules.title: Forklift pre-shift check: tires, horn, lights, brakes, steering, lift system
rules.plain_english: Drivers must check the truck at the start of each shift (tires, horn, lights, battery, controller, brakes, steering, cooling, and forks/chains/cables/limit switches) and report problems; an unsafe truck stays out of service until fixed. Never run a truck with a fuel leak.

check_items: lift system (forks, chains, cable, limit switches)
parameters.if_unsafe: report to foreman or mechanic; out of service until made safe

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees operate powered industrial trucks (forklifts, rough-terrain and telehandler lift trucks) on construction sites (GISO Article 25 via CSO 1502(c)); agricultural operations exempt from 3668
rules.quote: (7) Drivers shall check the vehicle at the beginning of each shift, and if it is found to be unsafe, the matter shall be reported immediately to a foreman or mechanic, and the vehicle shall not be put in service again until it has been made safe.
rules.notes: No written checklist is mandated by 3650(t)(7); a signed daily checklist is the usual proof.

rules.title: Forklift operating rules: 3-truck-length spacing, loads upgrade on grades over 10%, 25-foot unattended rule
rules.plain_english: Keep about 3 truck lengths (or 3 seconds) behind other trucks; on grades over 10% drive loaded trucks with the load upgrade; a truck is 'unattended' when the operator is more than 25 feet away or out of sight (forks down, mast vertical, brakes set, power off or wheels blocked); within 25 feet and in view, lower the forks, neutral, brakes set (forks may be up to 42 inches for loading if power is off).

unattended_requirements: power off (wheels blocked on incline) or power on with wheels blocked front and rear

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees operate powered industrial trucks (forklifts, rough-terrain and telehandler lift trucks) on construction sites (GISO Article 25 via CSO 1502(c)); agricultural operations exempt from 3668
rules.quote: (16) When leaving a vehicle unattended (the operator is over 25 feet (7.6 meters) from or out of sight of the industrial truck), the brakes are set, the mast is brought to the vertical position, and forks are left in the down position, either:
rules.notes: (t)(17) EXCEPTION amended operative 2017-10-01.

rules.title: Post and enforce forklift operating rules
rules.plain_english: Every employer using industrial trucks must post and enforce a set of operating rules, including the applicable rules from 3650(t).

parameters.post: operating rules including appropriate rules in 3650(t)

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees operate powered industrial trucks (forklifts, rough-terrain and telehandler lift trucks) on construction sites (GISO Article 25 via CSO 1502(c)); agricultural operations exempt from 3668
rules.quote: (a) Every employer using industrial trucks or industrial tow tractors shall post and enforce a set of operating rules including the appropriate rules listed in Section 3650(t).
rules.notes: 3664 last amended operative 2016-01-01 ((b)6 exception); (a) amended by a 2007 change without regulatory effect.

rules.title: Lifting people on a forklift: secured platform at least 2x2 ft, guardrails, operator at controls
rules.plain_english: To lift workers with a forklift, use a securely attached work platform at least 2 feet by 2 feet with guardrails and toeboards and no floor holes over 1 inch; the truck must limit lowering speed to 135 feet per minute on hydraulic failure; an operator must stay at the controls; and the truck must not travel with people on the platform except minor final positioning.

parameters.travel_with_personnel: only minor movements for final positioning

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees operate powered industrial trucks (forklifts, rough-terrain and telehandler lift trucks) on construction sites (GISO Article 25 via CSO 1502(c)); agricultural operations exempt from 3668
rules.quote: (1) The platform shall be of sufficient size to accommodate the personnel and material being elevated but not less than 2 feet by 2 feet.

rules.title: Telehandlers lifting people: stay on the personnel load chart, or one-third of rated capacity
rules.plain_english: When a variable-reach rough-terrain forklift (telehandler) lifts people, follow its personnel load chart; without one, the platform, load and people combined may not exceed one third of the truck's rated capacity at that load center. Set it on firm footing with outriggers on solid surfaces.

parameters.footing: firm; outriggers/stabilizers on solid surface; pads or cribbing if needed

rules.applies_to: Employers using variable reach (boom type) rough-terrain lift trucks (telehandlers) to elevate personnel
rules.quote: (2) If the lift truck is not provided with a load chart for elevating personnel, the combined weight of the work platform, load, and personnel shall not exceed one third of the rated capacity of the rough-terrain lift truck at the load center position as indicated on the load chart for regular loads.
rules.notes: 0.3333 is a rounded 'one third'; for exact limits compute rated capacity x max_fraction_numerator / max_fraction_denominator (= rated capacity / 3).
rules.correction: The text sets the limit at "one third of the rated capacity". The stored 0.3333 is a 4-decimal rounding that does not appear in the text. Added exact fraction fields (max_fraction_numerator = 1, max_fraction_denominator = 3) so a tool can compute rated_capacity / 3 exactly. The decimal is kept for compatibility and is slightly conservative. The load-chart rule, the footing rule and the construction straight-line movement exception are confirmed.

rules.title: Construction PPE: employer must require use, approved and marked, used per manufacturer
rules.plain_english: Construction employers must require workers to use the required PPE, which must be approved for its use, marked with the manufacturer, and used according to the manufacturer's instructions.
rules.applies_to: All California construction employers
rules.quote: (a) The employer shall require employees to use the required personal protective equipment.
rules.notes: Section 1514 last amended operative 2025-10-01 ((e) amended, (f) added).

rules.title: Construction PPE must be selected to fit each worker (from Oct 1, 2025)
rules.plain_english: From October 1, 2025, construction employers must pick PPE that properly fits each affected employee, for example harnesses, gloves and coveralls in sizes that fit women and smaller or larger workers.
rules.applies_to: All California construction employers
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/1514.html (subsection (f)); OSHSB 'Proper Fit of Personal Protective Equipment - HORCHER' (https://www.dir.ca.gov/oshsb/apprvd.html)
rules.quote: (f) All personal protective equipment shall be selected to ensure that it properly fits each affected employee.
rules.notes: Section history: new (f) filed 8-21-2025, operative 10-1-2025. The OSHSB approved list shows 'Aug. 21, 2025' in its effective column; the section history (operative 10-1-2025) is used here.

rules.title: All PPE, even worker-owned, must meet Title 8 and be kept safe and sanitary
rules.plain_english: The employer must make sure all required PPE and safety devices, whether the employer or the worker provides them, meet the applicable Title 8 standards and are kept in safe, sanitary condition.

parameters.condition: safe, sanitary, complying with Title 8

rules.applies_to: All California construction employers
rules.quote: (d) The employer shall assure that all required safety devices and safeguards, whether employer or employee provided, including personal protective equipment for the eyes, face, head, hand, foot, and extremities (limbs), protective clothing, respiratory protection, protective shields and barriers, comply with the applicable Title 8 standards and are maintained in a safe, sanitary condition.
rules.notes: Who pays for PPE is governed by other law (e.g., Labor Code 6401, 2802), not read here (leginfo blocked).

rules.title: Hard hats: required where head injury risk exists; ANSI Z89.1; Class E/G near conductors
rules.plain_english: Workers exposed to falling or flying objects or electric shock must wear approved hard hats (ANSI Z89.1-2009, -2003 or -1997). Class C, E or G is fine for impact only; near conductors under 600 V use Class E or G; near conductors over 600 V use Class E only.

class_rules.exposure: impact only, no electrical contact risk

rules.applies_to: Construction employers (GISO 3381 applies to construction because CSO head protection section 1515 was repealed)
rules.quote: (C) When there is a risk of head injury from contact with conductors greater than 600 volts, protective helmets shall be ANSI-Z89.1 designated Class E.
rules.notes: CSO 1515 (Head Protection) was repealed operative 2000-02-27; the construction requirement now comes from GISO 3381 through CSO 1502(c) and 1514.

rules.title: Eye and face protection: ANSI Z87.1, side shields for angled hazards, prescription options
rules.plain_english: Where flying particles, chemicals or injurious light can injure eyes, the employer must provide and require suitable eye or face protection meeting ANSI Z87.1 (for equipment bought after Jan 12, 1995), with side shields when hazards come from the side. Workers who need vision correction get prescription safety glasses, over-glasses goggles, or goggles with inserts.

parameters.side_shields_when: hazard angular as well as frontal
vision_correction_options: goggles with corrective lenses behind protective lenses

rules.applies_to: Construction employers (GISO 3382 applies to construction because CSO 1516 was repealed)
rules.quote: The employer shall provide and ensure that employees use protection suitable for the exposure.
rules.notes: CSO 1516 (Eye and Face Protection) was repealed operative 2000-02-27.

rules.title: Welding and cutting filter lens shade numbers (Table EP-1)
rules.plain_english: Use at least the listed filter shade: e.g., shade 10 for stick welding with electrodes up to 5/32 in, 12 for 3/16-1/4 in, 14 for 5/16-3/8 in and carbon-arc; 3 or 4 for torch brazing and light cutting; 2 for soldering. Darker shades are allowed.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees weld, cut, braze or solder
rules.quote: Table EP-1 shall be used as a guide for the selection of the proper shade numbers of filter lenses or plates used in welding. Shade more dense than those listed may be used to suit the individual's needs.
rules.notes: Table rows transcribed from the dir.ca.gov text table; atomic hydrogen welding is listed as shade 10-14.

rules.title: Gloves for cut, puncture, chemical, burn and temperature hazards; no gloves near entangling machinery
rules.plain_english: Employers must select, provide and require appropriate hand protection when hands face cuts, punctures, abrasions, chemical or thermal burns, skin absorption or temperature extremes, but gloves must not be worn where they could get caught in moving machinery.

parameters.prohibited_where: danger of entanglement in moving machinery or materials (except momentary contact devices)

rules.applies_to: Construction employers (GISO 3384 applies to construction because CSO 1520 was repealed effective 2014-07-01)
rules.quote: (a) Employers shall select, provide and require employees to use appropriate hand protection when employee's hands are exposed to hazards such as those from skin absorption of harmful substances, cuts or lacerations, abrasions, punctures, chemical burns, thermal burns, radioactive materials, and harmful temperature extremes.
rules.notes: The 3384 exception for infrequent and superficial cut risk depends on a 3380(f) hazard assessment, which 3380(f)(8) says does not apply to CSO-regulated operations.

rules.title: Safety footwear: ASTM F2413 for footwear bought after Jan 26, 2007
rules.plain_english: Workers exposed to foot injuries (falling or rolling objects, punctures, electrical hazards, hot or corrosive substances, abnormally wet locations) must wear appropriate foot protection; protective footwear bought after January 26, 2007 must meet ASTM F2412-05/F2413-05. Defective footwear may not be worn.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers (GISO 3385 applies to construction because CSO 1517 was repealed)
rules.quote: (a) Appropriate foot protection shall be required for employees who are exposed to foot injuries from electrical hazards, hot, corrosive, poisonous substances, falling objects, crushing or penetrating actions, which may cause injuries or who are required to work in abnormally wet locations.

rules.title: Body protection and work clothing: no loose clothing near machinery; remove soaked clothing
rules.plain_english: Provide body protection where work exposes employees to injurious materials. Wear clothing suited to the work; no loose sleeves, ties or cuffs around machinery; promptly remove clothing soaked with flammable, corrosive, irritant or oxidizing substances.
rules.applies_to: All California construction employers
rules.quote: (b) Clothing appropriate for the work being done shall be worn. Loose sleeves, tails, ties, frills, lapels, cuffs, or other loose clothing shall not be worn around machinery in which it might become entangled.
