rules.notes: Last repealed and replaced 9-27-85, effective thirtieth day thereafter (date computed).

rules.title: The GISO written PPE hazard assessment does not apply to construction work
rules.plain_english: The general-industry requirement for a written, certified PPE hazard assessment and certified PPE training (3380(f)) does not apply to operations covered by the Construction Safety Orders. Construction PPE duties come from 1514 and the specific standards instead.
rules.applies_to: All California construction employers
rules.quote: Subsection (f) does not apply to workplace operations regulated by the Construction Safety Orders or the Mine Safety Orders.
rules.notes: Hazard identification is still required by the IIPP (3203/1509). Subsection (f)-(f)(8) added operative 2011-04-13; section last amended operative 2015-04-01 (history notes 4-5).

rules.title: Noise limits: 90 dBA for 8 hours, halving time every 5 dB (Table N-1)
rules.plain_english: Protection is required when noise exceeds Table N-1: 90 dBA for 8 hours, 95 dBA for 4 hours, 100 dBA for 2 hours, 105 dBA for 1 hour, 110 dBA for 30 minutes, 115 dBA for 15 minutes. For mixed levels add up time at each level divided by allowed time; over 1.0 exceeds the limit.

parameters.mixed_exposure_formula: sum(C_n / T_n) > 1 exceeds limit (C = hours at level, T = permitted hours at level)

rules.applies_to: All employers, including construction (5095-5096 and CSO 1521); construction is exempt from 5097-5100
rules.quote: (a) Protection against the effects of noise exposure shall be provided when the sound levels exceed those shown in Table N-1 of this section when measured on the A-scale of a standard sound level meter at slow response.
rules.notes: Table values transcribed from the dir.ca.gov text table (hours column). 5096 history not shown on the page; 'effective' uses the adoption of new Group 15 (Sections 5095-5100) per the 5095 history (filed 6-28-82, effective thirtieth day thereafter = 1982-07-28) and is approximate, because later amendments to 5096 cannot be ruled out. exchange_rate_db is derived from the table (90->8 h, 95->4 h).
rules.correction: effective changed from 1983-11-02 to 1982-07-28. 1983-11-02 is the date of a 5095 amendment ("Amendment filed 10-3-83" in the 5095 history), and nothing shows that it amended 5096. The date that can be seen to cover 5096 is the adoption of new Group 15 (Sections 5095-5100), filed 6-28-82, effective thirtieth day thereafter. 5096 has no history on its page, so later amendments cannot be ruled out; the date stays approximate. Table values, the slow-response A-scale measure, the 90 dBA criterion (5095 definition "Criterion Sound Level") and the mixed-exposure formula are confirmed.

rules.title: Noise over the limit: engineering or administrative controls first, then hearing protection
rules.plain_english: When noise exceeds Table N-1, use feasible engineering or administrative controls; if those don't bring it within the limits, provide and require hearing protection. On construction sites the employer must provide ear protection and require workers to wear it.
rules.applies_to: All employers, including construction (5095-5096 and CSO 1521); construction is exempt from 5097-5100
rules.quote: (b) When employees are subjected to sound levels exceeding those listed in Table N-1 of this section, feasible administrative or engineering controls shall be utilized. If such controls fail to reduce sound levels within the levels of the table, personal protective equipment shall be provided and used to reduce sound levels within the levels of the table.
rules.notes: CSO 1521: 'Where required by Section 5096(b) of the General Industry Safety Orders, ear protection shall be provided by the employer and the employer shall require employees to wear the ear protection.' (1521 last amended 1982).
rules.correction: effective changed from 1983-11-02 to 1982-07-28. 1983-11-02 is the date of a 5095 amendment ("Amendment filed 10-3-83" in the 5095 history), and nothing shows that it amended 5096. The date that can be seen to cover 5096 is the adoption of new Group 15 (Sections 5095-5100), filed 6-28-82, effective thirtieth day thereafter. 5096 has no history on its page, so later amendments cannot be ruled out; the date stays approximate. 1521 was also last amended effective 1982-07-28. The control hierarchy and the construction duty to provide ear protection and require its use are confirmed.

rules.title: Impulse or impact noise should not exceed 140 dB peak
rules.plain_english: Exposure to impulse or impact noise (e.g., powder-actuated tools, pile driving, blasting) should not exceed 140 dB peak sound pressure level.
rules.applies_to: All employers, including construction (5095-5096 and CSO 1521); construction is exempt from 5097-5100
rules.quote: (d) Exposure to impulsive or impact noise should not exceed 140 dB peak sound pressure level.
rules.notes: The regulation uses 'should'.
rules.correction: effective changed from 1983-11-02 to 1982-07-28. 1983-11-02 is the date of a 5095 amendment ("Amendment filed 10-3-83" in the 5095 history), and nothing shows that it amended 5096. The date that can be seen to cover 5096 is the adoption of new Group 15 (Sections 5095-5100), filed 6-28-82, effective thirtieth day thereafter. 5096 has no history on its page, so later amendments cannot be ruled out; the date stays approximate. The 140 dB peak figure and the advisory "should" wording are confirmed.

rules.title: Construction is exempt from the hearing conservation program rules (5097-5100)
rules.plain_english: Construction is exempt from Cal/OSHA's hearing conservation program, hearing protector, training and recordkeeping sections (5097-5100), but the noise limits in 5096 and the construction ear-protection rule (1521) still apply. The 85 dBA 'action level' that triggers a hearing conservation program therefore does not apply to construction work.
rules.applies_to: All employers, including construction (5095-5096 and CSO 1521); construction is exempt from 5097-5100
rules.quote: Agriculture, construction, and oil and gas well drilling and servicing operations are exempt from the provisions of Sections 5097 through 5100.
rules.notes: Contractors with non-construction operations (shop, fabrication yard) are not exempt for that work. 5095 last amended 1997 (group heading only).

rules.title: Wildfire smoke rule applies when AQI for PM2.5 is 151 or higher
rules.plain_english: The wildfire smoke rule kicks in when the current Air Quality Index for PM2.5 (fine particles) is 151 or greater and you should reasonably expect your workers may be exposed to wildfire smoke. Only the PM2.5 AQI counts, not ozone or other pollutants.
rules.applies_to: Employers (including construction) whose employees may reasonably be anticipated to be exposed to wildfire smoke where the current AQI for PM2.5 is 151 or greater
rules.quote: (A) The current Air Quality Index (current AQI) for PM2.5 is 151 or greater, regardless of the AQI for other pollutants; and
rules.notes: 8 CCR 5141.1 made permanent effective 2021-02-01 (Certificate of Compliance filed 2021-02-01). Compliance with 5141.1 counts as compliance with 5141 and 5155 for these exposures (5141.1(a)(3)).

rules.title: Wildfire smoke rule exemptions: filtered buildings and vehicles, measured PM2.5, 1 hour or less per shift
rules.plain_english: The smoke rule does not apply to closed buildings with mechanically filtered air, closed vehicles with cabin air filters, worksites where the employer measures PM2.5 below the AQI-151 level, workers exposed at AQI 151+ for a total of one hour or less in a shift, or wildland firefighters.

exemptions: enclosed buildings with mechanical filtration, openings kept closed
enclosed vehicles with cabin air filter, openings kept closed
employer measures PM2.5 at worksite below AQI 151 per Appendix A
total exposure at AQI 151+ of one hour or less during a shift

rules.applies_to: Employers (including construction) whose employees may reasonably be anticipated to be exposed to wildfire smoke where the current AQI for PM2.5 is 151 or greater
rules.quote: (D) Employees exposed to a current AQI for PM2.5 of 151 or greater for a total of one hour or less during a shift.
rules.notes: 8 CCR 5141.1 made permanent effective 2021-02-01 (Certificate of Compliance filed 2021-02-01). The one-hour exemption is cumulative per shift ('for a total of').

rules.title: Check the PM2.5 AQI at the start of each shift and periodically after
rules.plain_english: On covered worksites, find the PM2.5 AQI at the start of every shift and periodically during it, from AirNow, the Forest Service, CARB, or the local air district (website, phone, text or email), or by measuring PM2.5 on site per Appendix A. You can skip checking only if (1) you assume the AQI is over 500 and protect workers on that basis, or (2) in an emergency operation covered by 5141.1(f)(4), you assume the AQI is 151 or more and provide respirators for voluntary use.

sources: Interagency Wildland Fire Air Quality Response Program
on-site PM2.5 measurement per Appendix A
parameters.exception_emergency_condition: emergency subject to 5141.1(f)(4); employer complies with (f)(3)(A) (voluntary respirators) on that assumption

rules.applies_to: Employers (including construction) whose employees may reasonably be anticipated to be exposed to wildfire smoke where the current AQI for PM2.5 is 151 or greater
rules.quote: (c) Identification of harmful exposures. The employer shall determine employee exposure to PM2.5 for worksites covered by this section at the start of each shift and periodically thereafter, as needed to protect the health of employees, by any of the following methods:
rules.notes: 8 CCR 5141.1 made permanent effective 2021-02-01 (Certificate of Compliance filed 2021-02-01). Platform feature: log the AQI reading, source and time per shift per jobsite.
rules.correction: The plain_english said the AQI check may be skipped "only" if the employer assumes AQI is over 500. 5141.1(c) has a second exception: in an emergency under (f)(4), the employer may assume the current AQI for PM2.5 is 151 or greater and provide respirators for voluntary use under (f)(3)(A). Added that exception to parameters and plain_english. The sources, start-of-shift timing and the over-500 exception are confirmed.

rules.title: Two-way smoke communication: tell workers the AQI and protections; encourage reports without reprisal
rules.plain_english: As part of the IIPP, tell workers the current PM2.5 AQI and the protections available, in a language they understand, and encourage them to report worsening air or symptoms (asthma attacks, trouble breathing, chest pain) without fear of reprisal.

encourage_reports_of: adverse symptoms such as asthma attacks, difficulty breathing, chest pain

rules.applies_to: Employers (including construction) whose employees may reasonably be anticipated to be exposed to wildfire smoke where the current AQI for PM2.5 is 151 or greater
rules.quote: (d) Communication. As required by section 3203, the employer shall establish and implement a system for communicating wildfire smoke hazards in a language and manner readily understandable by employees, including provisions designed to encourage employees to inform the employer of wildfire smoke hazards at the worksite without fear of reprisal.
rules.notes: 8 CCR 5141.1 made permanent effective 2021-02-01 (Certificate of Compliance filed 2021-02-01).

rules.title: Wildfire smoke training must contain at least Appendix B
rules.plain_english: Train workers, in a language they understand, with at least the information in Appendix B: health effects, the right to medical treatment without reprisal, how to get the AQI, the rule's requirements, the communication system, the employer's control methods, and how to use respirators. Appendix B replaces the usual voluntary-respirator handout (5144 Appendix D).

appendix_b_topics: right to medical treatment without reprisal
how to obtain current AQI for PM2.5
importance, limitations and benefits of respirators
how to put on and use respirators

rules.applies_to: Employers (including construction) whose employees may reasonably be anticipated to be exposed to wildfire smoke where the current AQI for PM2.5 is 151 or greater
rules.quote: (e) Training and instruction. As required by section 3203, the employer shall provide employees with effective training and instruction in a language and manner readily understandable by employees. At a minimum, this shall contain the information in Appendix B.
rules.notes: 8 CCR 5141.1 made permanent effective 2021-02-01 (Certificate of Compliance filed 2021-02-01). Appendix B contains blanks the employer fills in for its communication system and control system.

rules.title: Reduce smoke exposure below AQI 151: filtered enclosures first, then schedule/location changes
rules.plain_english: Where feasible, reduce exposure below AQI 151 with engineering controls such as enclosed buildings or vehicles with filtered air. If that isn't feasible or enough, use administrative controls if practicable: move work to cleaner air, change schedules, reduce work intensity, or add rest breaks.

engineering_controls_examples: enclosed buildings, structures or vehicles with filtered air
administrative_controls_examples: relocate work to lower AQI location

rules.applies_to: Employers (including construction) whose employees may reasonably be anticipated to be exposed to wildfire smoke where the current AQI for PM2.5 is 151 or greater
rules.quote: (1) Engineering Controls. The employer shall reduce employee exposure to PM2.5 to less than a current AQI of 151 by engineering controls whenever feasible, for instance by providing enclosed buildings, structures, or vehicles where the air is filtered.
rules.notes: 8 CCR 5141.1 made permanent effective 2021-02-01 (Certificate of Compliance filed 2021-02-01).

rules.title: AQI 151 to 500: provide N95s (or better) for voluntary use and encourage their use
rules.plain_english: When the PM2.5 AQI is 151 to 500, give every worker a NIOSH-approved respirator such as an N95 for voluntary use and encourage them to wear it. Fit testing and medical evaluations are not required for voluntary N95 use. Surgical masks, bandannas and T-shirts don't count.
rules.applies_to: Employers (including construction) whose employees may reasonably be anticipated to be exposed to wildfire smoke where the current AQI for PM2.5 is 151 or greater
rules.quote: (A) Where the current AQI for PM2.5 is equal to or greater than 151, but does not exceed 500, the employer shall provide a sufficient number of respirators to all employees for voluntary use in accordance with section 5144 and encourage employees to use respirators.
rules.notes: 8 CCR 5141.1 made permanent effective 2021-02-01 (Certificate of Compliance filed 2021-02-01). Appendix B(g)(1): 'An N95 filtering facepiece respirator ... is the minimum level of protection for wildfire smoke.'

rules.title: AQI above 500: respirators are mandatory under a full 5144 respiratory program
rules.plain_english: When the PM2.5 AQI exceeds 500, respirator use is required under the full respiratory protection standard (5144: program, medical evaluation, fit testing), with respirators whose protection factor brings the inside level below the AQI-151 equivalent.

parameters.program: 8 CCR 5144 (written program, medical evaluation, fit testing)
parameters.assigned_protection_factor_rule: PM2.5 inside respirator must correspond to AQI less than 151

rules.applies_to: Employers (including construction) whose employees may reasonably be anticipated to be exposed to wildfire smoke where the current AQI for PM2.5 is 151 or greater
rules.quote: (B) Where the current AQI for PM2.5 exceeds 500, respirator use is required. Respirators shall be used in accordance with section 5144. The employer shall provide respirators with an assigned protection factor, as listed in section 5144, such that the PM2.5 levels inside the respirator correspond to an AQI less than 151.
rules.notes: 8 CCR 5141.1 made permanent effective 2021-02-01 (Certificate of Compliance filed 2021-02-01). max_inside_pm25_ug_m3 and the APF formula are derived from Appendix A (55.4 ug/m3 is the top of the AQI 101-150 band, so inside levels must not exceed it). The APF values are in 8 CCR 5144 Table 1 (rule osha2-resp-assigned-protection-factors). An AQI over 500 reported by AirNow means PM2.5 above 325.4 ug/m3 on EPA's current scale (rule osha2-smoke-epa-current-aqi-pm25-breakpoints), so the minimum APF cannot be computed from the AQI alone; it needs a PM2.5 measurement. Emergency operations are exempt from the >500 mandate (5141.1(f)(4)).

rules.title: Respirator assigned protection factors (8 CCR 5144 Table 1): N95/half mask 10, full facepiece 50, PAPR 25-1,000
rules.plain_english: When a respirator is required, choose one whose assigned protection factor (APF) in 5144 Table 1 meets or exceeds the protection needed. Air-purifying respirators: quarter mask 5; half mask, including N95 and other filtering facepieces, 10; full facepiece 50. Powered air-purifying respirators (PAPR): half mask 50; full facepiece 1,000; helmet or hood 25 (1,000 only with the manufacturer's test evidence); loose-fitting facepiece 25. Supplied-air and SCBA respirators have their own rows (up to 10,000 for a pressure-demand SCBA). The APFs count only under a full 5144 program (training, fit testing, maintenance).

apf_table.respirator: air-purifying, half mask (includes N95 and other filtering facepieces, and elastomeric half masks)
supplied-air (airline), continuous flow, helmet or hood
SCBA, demand mode, helmet or hood

parameters.selection_rule: APF meets or exceeds the required level of employee protection

rules.applies_to: Employers whose employees must wear respirators under 8 CCR 5144, including wildfire smoke above AQI 500 under 8 CCR 5141.1(f)(3)(B)
rules.quote: Employers must use the assigned protection factors listed in Table 1 to select a respirator that meets or exceeds the required level of employee protection.
rules.notes: Table 1 and subsection (d)(3)(A)1.-2. came in with the amendment filed 3-6-2007, operative 3-6-2007 (history note 16). Note 3 to Table 1: 'This APF category includes filtering facepieces, and half masks with elastomeric facepieces.' Note 4: PAPRs and SARs with helmets or hoods receive 1,000 only with the manufacturer's WPF or SWPF test evidence, otherwise 25. Note 2: APFs are effective only with a continuing, effective respirator program (training, fit testing, maintenance, use). Note 5: not for escape respirators. For wildfire smoke, 5141.1(f)(3)(B) sets the inside level (AQI under 151, i.e. at most 55.4 ug/m3 per Appendix A), so the highest outside PM2.5 a class covers is APF x 55.4 ug/m3.

rules.title: Emergency, rescue and utility-support work: respirators for voluntary use at any AQI 151+
rules.plain_english: For emergency operations (rescue, evacuation) and utility, communications and medical work directly supporting emergency or firefighting operations, the employer must provide respirators for voluntary use at AQI 151 and above, but the engineering, administrative and mandatory-respirator requirements do not apply.

applies_to: emergency operations incl. rescue and evacuation
utilities, communications and medical operations directly aiding emergency or firefighting operations

rules.applies_to: Employers performing emergency operations or utility/communications/medical work directly aiding emergency or firefighting operations (e.g., utility line crews restoring power in fire areas)
rules.quote: (A) The employer shall comply with subsection (f)(3)(A) for all AQI levels equal to or greater than 151.
rules.notes: 8 CCR 5141.1 made permanent effective 2021-02-01 (Certificate of Compliance filed 2021-02-01). Post-fire debris removal and rebuilding is ordinary construction, not 'emergency operations'.

rules.title: AQI categories for PM2.5 used by the smoke rule
rules.plain_english: The rule uses EPA's six AQI categories: 0-50 Good, 51-100 Moderate, 101-150 Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups, 151-200 Unhealthy, 201-300 Very Unhealthy, 301-500 Hazardous. Current AQI is EPA's 'NowCast'.
rules.applies_to: Employers (including construction) whose employees may reasonably be anticipated to be exposed to wildfire smoke where the current AQI for PM2.5 is 151 or greater
rules.quote: Current AQI is also referred to as the “NowCast,” and represents data collected over time periods of varying length in order to reflect present conditions as accurately as possible.
rules.notes: 8 CCR 5141.1 made permanent effective 2021-02-01 (Certificate of Compliance filed 2021-02-01). The regulation's table is adapted from 40 CFR Part 58 Appendix G Table 2 as it stood when adopted; any later EPA AQI revisions are not reflected in the Title 8 text as fetched 2026-11-25.

rules.title: Measuring PM2.5 on site: monitor requirements and the ug/m3-to-AQI table (Appendix A)
rules.plain_english: If you measure PM2.5 yourself, use a direct-reading monitor that covers particles 0.3 to 2.5 micrometers (or account for its error so exposure isn't underestimated), calibrate and use it per the manufacturer, have a trained person supervise, and convert readings with the table: 55.5-150.4 ug/m3 = AQI 151-200; 150.5-250.4 = 201-300; 250.5-500.4 = 301-500.

parameters.supervisor: person with training or experience to apply section and interpret results

rules.applies_to: Employers that choose to monitor PM2.5 with a direct-reading instrument under 5141.1(a)(2)(C) or (c)(3)
rules.quote: (d) The employer shall use the following table to convert the PM2.5 concentration to the AQI for PM2.5.
rules.notes: 8 CCR 5141.1 made permanent effective 2021-02-01 (Certificate of Compliance filed 2021-02-01). Appendix A is mandatory only if the employer monitors with a direct-reading instrument.

rules.title: EPA's current PM2.5 AQI breakpoints (what AirNow reports): AQI 500 = 325.4 ug/m3
rules.plain_english: 5141.1 defines the current AQI as the method EPA uses to report air quality in real time (AirNow). Since May 6, 2024 EPA's PM2.5 breakpoints are: 0.0-9.0 ug/m3 = AQI 0-50; 9.1-35.4 = 51-100; 35.5-55.4 = 101-150; 55.5-125.4 = 151-200; 125.5-225.4 = 201-300; 225.5 and up = 301 and up, with AQI 500 at 325.4 ug/m3. Above AQI 150 these differ from the older table in 5141.1 Appendix A (which puts AQI 500 at 500.4 ug/m3), but AQI 151 starts at 55.5 ug/m3 on both.

parameters.aqi_above_500: calculated with equation 1 using the concentration specified for AQI 500

rules.applies_to: Employers that rely on a reported current AQI for PM2.5 (AirNow, CARB, air districts) under 8 CCR 5141.1(c)(1)-(2)
rules.citation: 40 CFR Part 58, Appendix G, section 3.4 and Table 2 (the EPA AQI method referenced in 8 CCR 5141.1(b))
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-40/chapter-I/subchapter-C/part-58/appendix-Appendix%20G%20to%20Part%2058 (read through the eCFR versioner API, point in time 2026-11-01: section 3.4.a, Table 2 and its footnote 4)
rules.quote: For AQI values in the hazardous category, AQI values greater than 500 should be calculated using equation 1 and the concentration specified for the AQI value of 500.
rules.notes: Footnote 4 to Table 2 also states 'The AQI value of 500 are as follows: ... PM2.5 24-hour—325.4 µg/m3'. eCFR source note [89 FR 16403, Mar. 6, 2024]; the eCFR version history lists substantive amendments to Appendix G dated 2024-03-06 and 2024-05-06 and none later through 2026-11-01. 5141.1(b) says its category table is 'adapted from Table 2 of Title 40 Code of Federal Regulations, Part 58, Appendix G'; the Title 8 text (operative 2-1-2021) and its Appendix A were not updated for the 2024 breakpoints, and 5141.1 Appendix A(d) still requires its own table for converting on-site readings. Consequence: an AirNow AQI over 500 means PM2.5 above 325.4 ug/m3, while an on-site reading must exceed 500.4 ug/m3 to be over 500 under Appendix A.

rules.title: Workers with smoke symptoms may seek treatment; no punishment; plan for prompt care
rules.plain_english: Employers must let workers with signs of smoke-related illness get medical treatment, may not punish them for it, and must arrange in advance for prompt medical treatment of serious smoke-related illness.

parameters.prohibited: punishing employees for seeking medical treatment for wildfire smoke illness
parameters.required: advance provisions for prompt medical treatment

rules.applies_to: Employers (including construction) whose employees may reasonably be anticipated to be exposed to wildfire smoke where the current AQI for PM2.5 is 151 or greater
rules.quote: Employers shall allow employees who show signs of injury or illness due to wildfire smoke exposure to seek medical treatment, and may not punish affected employees for seeking such treatment.
rules.notes: 8 CCR 5141.1 made permanent effective 2021-02-01 (Certificate of Compliance filed 2021-02-01).

rules.title: Valley Fever training required for construction workers in highly endemic counties
rules.plain_english: Construction employers must train workers on Valley Fever prevention in counties where it is highly endemic, which Cal/OSHA lists as including Fresno, Kern, Kings, Madera, Merced, Monterey, San Joaquin, San Luis Obispo, Santa Barbara, Tulare and Ventura. More counties may be added as case rates change.

training_topics_named_by_dosh: measures used onsite to reduce exposure

rules.applies_to: Construction employers with worksites in counties where Valley Fever is highly endemic
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/dosh/valley-fever-home.html ('Information for Employers' section; page dated July 2025)
rules.quote: Construction employers must train workers on Valley Fever prevention in counties where Valley Fever is highly endemic including but not limited to including, but not limited to, the Counties of Fresno, Kern, Kings, Madera, Merced, Monterey, San Joaquin, San Luis Obispo, Santa Barbara, Tulare, and Ventura.
rules.notes: Primary source read is the official DOSH page (quote reproduces its duplicated 'including but not limited to' wording). The statute (LC 6709) itself could not be read (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov blocked; DOSH links only to leginfo). 'effective' is left blank: the DOSH page is dated July 2025, but that is a page revision date, and the statute's operative date could not be read. DOSH's training-topic list is from its prevention section ('Train workers and supervisors about the risk of Valley Fever, the work activities that may increase the risk, and the measures used onsite to reduce exposure. Also train on how to recognize Valley Fever symptoms.'), which may not match the statute's required topics.
rules.correction: effective changed from 2025-07-01 to "" (unknown). "July 2025" is the revision date in the DOSH page footer, not a date on which any requirement took effect, and "2025-07-01" (a specific day) does not appear on the page. Labor Code 6709 itself could not be read: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov blocks automated access, and the cdph.ca.gov copies the page links to are refused by this session's proxy. Labor Code 6709 is not in the local 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt). The 11 counties, the "including but not limited to" wording (so the list is not exhaustive), the note that other counties may be added, and the training topics named by DOSH are confirmed against the page.

rules.title: Highly endemic = more than 20 Valley Fever cases per 100,000 people per year
rules.plain_english: Cal/OSHA treats an area as highly endemic for Valley Fever when it has more than 20 cases a year per 100,000 people.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers with worksites in counties where Valley Fever is highly endemic
rules.citation: Labor Code 6709 (definition as described by Cal/OSHA)
rules.quote: Populations with more than 20 cases annually of Valley Fever per 100,000 people are considered highly endemic.
rules.notes: Read from the DOSH page; whether LC 6709 uses exactly this test could not be confirmed (statute text blocked). County rates are published by CDPH (cdph.ca.gov was not reachable from this session).
rules.correction: effective changed from 2025-07-01 to "" (unknown). "July 2025" is the revision date in the DOSH page footer, not a date on which any requirement took effect, and "2025-07-01" (a specific day) does not appear on the page. Labor Code 6709 itself could not be read: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov blocks automated access, and the cdph.ca.gov copies the page links to are refused by this session's proxy. Labor Code 6709 is not in the local 2026 CSLB Law Book (sources/lawbook.txt). The threshold "more than 20 cases annually ... per 100,000 people" is confirmed as DOSH's statement. The page does not tie it to Labor Code 6709.

rules.title: Valley Fever training: annually by May 1 and before dust-disturbing work (UNVERIFIED)
rules.plain_english: Reported requirement: construction employers in highly endemic counties must give Valley Fever awareness training each year by May 1, and before an employee starts work expected to cause substantial dust disturbance. This could not be confirmed from the statute text.

parameters.also_before: employee begins work reasonably anticipated to cause substantial dust disturbance

rules.applies_to: Construction employers with worksites in counties where Valley Fever is highly endemic
rules.source: Labor Code 6709 at https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=6709 (blocked); CDPH Occupational Health Branch pages on cdph.ca.gov (not resolvable from this session)
rules.notes: UNVERIFIABLE: statute text not read. Basis is web search excerpts only: a cdph.ca.gov Occupational Health Branch page excerpt stating 'California Labor Code 6709 (2020) requires construction employers who work in counties with high rates of Valley fever to train their employees on minimizing the risk of Valley fever by May 1 of each year,' and unofficial statute reprints stating training is required annually and 'before an employee begins work that is reasonably anticipated to cause exposure to substantial dust disturbance' and 'may be included in the employer's injury and illness prevention program training or as a standalone training program.' 'effective' 2020-01-01 is the assumed operative date of a 2019 statute and is not verified. Verify against the statute before relying on it.

rules.title: Valley Fever dust controls Cal/OSHA expects on endemic sites
rules.plain_english: Cal/OSHA's listed prevention steps: limit soil disturbance; use water or soil stabilizers; tarp spoils piles; closed air-conditioned cabs; stop work in heavy wind; keep workers upwind; clean with HEPA vacuums or wet methods (no compressed air or dry sweeping); and when dust exposure is unavoidable, NIOSH-approved N95-or-better respirators under a written 5144 respiratory protection program.

controls: enclosed air-conditioned cabs with windows and vents closed
keep workers upwind of dust-producing work
HEPA vacuums or wet methods; no compressed air or dry sweeping
clean tools and vehicles before leaving

rules.applies_to: Construction employers with worksites in counties where Valley Fever is highly endemic
rules.citation: 8 CCR 3203, 5141, 5144 (as applied by Cal/OSHA to Valley Fever)
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/dosh/valley-fever-home.html ('How can Valley Fever be Prevented?' section)
rules.quote: When exposure to dust is unavoidable, provide NIOSH-approved respiratory protection with particulate filters rated as N95, N99, N100, P100, or HEPA. Employers must develop and implement a respiratory protection program in accordance with Cal/OSHA's Respiratory Protection standard (8 CCR 5144).
rules.notes: Most listed controls are DOSH guidance ('may include'); the enforceable hooks are the IIPP (3203), control of harmful exposures (5141) and respiratory protection (5144), as cited by DOSH.
rules.correction: effective changed from 2025-07-01 to "" (unknown). "July 2025" is the revision date in the DOSH page footer, not an effective date, and the underlying regulations (3203, 5141, 5144) have their own dates, which were not read for this rule. The controls list, respirator filter classes, 5144 program requirement and face-covering statement are confirmed. Most controls are guidance ("may include"), as the notes say.

rules.title: Valley Fever cases: report hospitalizations/deaths to Cal/OSHA, file Form 5020, record on Log 300
rules.plain_english: If a worker may have work-related Valley Fever: report hospitalized cases and deaths to Cal/OSHA, complete a Form 5020 Employer's Report for each suspected case, send the worker to a workers' comp provider who knows Valley Fever, and record cases on the Log 300.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers with worksites in counties where Valley Fever is highly endemic
rules.citation: 8 CCR 342; 8 CCR 14300 et seq. (as applied by Cal/OSHA to Valley Fever)
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/dosh/valley-fever-home.html ('What should employers do if a worker reports Valley Fever symptoms?' section)
rules.quote: Report all hospitalized cases and deaths to Cal/OSHA.
rules.notes: Reporting deadlines (8 hours for serious illness, 5 days for Form 5020) are in the web_calosha-programs pack (serious-injury-report-8-hours, employer-report-form-5020-5-days).
rules.correction: effective changed from 2025-07-01 to "" (unknown), for the same reason as the other DOSH-page rules: "July 2025" is a page revision date, not an effective date. The four steps (report hospitalized cases and deaths, Form 5020 for each suspected case, Form 5021 by the physician, Log 300) are confirmed.

rules.title: Demolition must always be under immediate supervision of a qualified person
rules.plain_english: Demolition work must at all times be directly supervised by a qualified person who has authority to ensure the crew's safety.

parameters.supervisor: qualified person with authority to secure maximum safety

rules.applies_to: Employers performing demolition of buildings or structures, including partial demolition in alterations (C-21 and B contractors, wrecking and interior demo crews)
rules.quote: (a) Demolition work shall at all times be under the immediate supervision of a qualified person with the authority to secure maximum safety for employees engaged in demolition work.
rules.notes: 'Qualified person' is defined in 8 CCR 1504 (in the rulebook as qualified-person-definition).

rules.title: Written pre-demolition engineering survey, kept on site for the whole project
rules.plain_english: Before any demolition starts, a qualified person must survey the structure (framing, floors, walls) and any exposed adjacent structure for risk of unplanned collapse. The survey must be written, kept on the jobsite for the whole project, and shown to Cal/OSHA on request.

parameters.timing: prior to permitting employees to start demolition
covers: adjacent structures where employees may be exposed

rules.applies_to: Employers performing demolition of buildings or structures, including partial demolition in alterations (C-21 and B contractors, wrecking and interior demo crews)
rules.quote: (2) The survey shall be in written form, kept on the job-site and made available to the Division upon request. The written survey shall be maintained for the duration of the demolition project.
rules.notes: The Cal/OSHA demolition permit (structures over 36 ft) is covered in web_calosha-programs (permit-demolition-36ft).

rules.title: Before demolition: shut off or control utilities; test and purge hazardous substances
rules.plain_english: Notify utility companies and shut off, cap or control all utilities at the building or curb line before demolition (or relocate and protect any you must keep). Find out whether pipes, tanks or equipment held hazardous chemicals, gases, explosives or flammables; if so, test, purge and eliminate the hazard first.

parameters.utilities: notify companies; shut off, capped or controlled at building or curb line before starting
parameters.hazardous_substances: determine; if present or suspected, test and purge before starting

rules.applies_to: Employers performing demolition of buildings or structures, including partial demolition in alterations (C-21 and B contractors, wrecking and interior demo crews)
rules.quote: (a) Utility companies shall be notified and all utility service shut off, capped, or otherwise controlled, at the building or curb line before starting demolition, unless it is necessary to use electricity or water lines during demolition.

rules.title: Survey pipe insulation, fireproofing and ductwork for asbestos before demolition
rules.plain_english: Pipe insulation, steel fireproofing and HVAC ductwork must be surveyed for asbestos; if asbestos is present, the asbestos standard (1529) applies.

survey_items: steel beam and column fire protection

rules.applies_to: Employers performing demolition of buildings or structures, including partial demolition in alterations (C-21 and B contractors, wrecking and interior demo crews)
rules.quote: (c) Pipe-covering insulation, steel beam and column fire protection, and heating, ventilating and air-conditioning duct work shall be surveyed for asbestos. If asbestos is present, the employer shall comply with Section 1529.
rules.notes: Federal NESHAP and air-district asbestos inspection/notice rules are in the rulebook (neshap-asbestos-inspection-before-demo, air-district-demolition-notice-10-working-days).

rules.title: Shore or brace survey deficiencies before starting; keep inspecting as work progresses
rules.plain_english: Before demolition starts, shore, brace or otherwise fix every hazardous structural deficiency the survey found. During demolition, keep inspecting for weakened floors, walls or loose material, and keep workers away from those hazards until corrected.

parameters.before_start: shore, brace or correct deficiencies noted in 1734(b)(1) survey
parameters.retaining_walls: not demolished until moving-ground hazard eliminated

rules.applies_to: Employers performing demolition of buildings or structures, including partial demolition in alterations (C-21 and B contractors, wrecking and interior demo crews)
rules.quote: (1) Prior to starting demolition operations, all structural or other hazardous deficiencies noted during the survey required by Section 1734(b)(1) shall be shored, braced or otherwise corrected as recommended in the survey.

rules.title: Demolish from the top down; floor openings for debris no more than 25% of floor area
rules.plain_english: Exterior walls and floors must be demolished from the top down, one story at a time. Openings cut in a floor to drop debris may total no more than 25% of the floor area unless the lateral supports of the removed flooring stay in place.

parameters.exception: lateral supports of removed flooring remain in place
parameters.storage_space_floors_removed_max: not more than one floor above grade

rules.applies_to: Employers performing demolition of buildings or structures, including partial demolition in alterations (C-21 and B contractors, wrecking and interior demo crews)
rules.quote: (2) Any openings cut in a floor for the disposal of materials shall be no larger in size than 25 percent of the aggregate of the total floor area, unless the lateral supports of the removed flooring remain in place.

rules.title: Demolition entrance canopies: extend 8 ft, 2 ft wider than the opening, 150 psf
rules.plain_english: On multi-story demolition, protect employee entrances from falling material with sidewalk sheds or canopies extending at least 8 feet out from the building, at least 2 feet wider than the entrance (1 foot each side), and able to carry 150 pounds per square foot.

parameters.applies_to: employee entrances to multi-story structures being demolished

rules.applies_to: Employers performing demolition of buildings or structures, including partial demolition in alterations (C-21 and B contractors, wrecking and interior demo crews)
rules.quote: (j) All persons on demolition projects shall be protected from falling material at employee entrances to multi-story structures being demolished, by sidewalk sheds or canopies or both, providing protection extending from the face of the building for a minimum of 8 feet. All such canopies shall be at least two feet wider than the building entrances or openings (one foot wider on each side thereof) and shall be capable of sustaining a load of 150 pounds per square foot.

rules.title: Demolition: guard exterior wall openings to 42 in; remove glass one floor below
rules.plain_english: Protect exterior wall openings on every floor to at least 42 inches high (except the ground floor and the floor being demolished), and where broken glass is a hazard, remove all glazing at least one floor below the working level.
rules.applies_to: Employers performing demolition of buildings or structures, including partial demolition in alterations (C-21 and B contractors, wrecking and interior demo crews)
rules.quote: (k) Exterior wall openings on all floors shall be protected to a height of not less than 42 inches, except on the ground floor and the floor being demolished.

rules.title: Wall sections over one story or 12 ft may not stand alone unbraced (unless a CA civil engineer's data is filed)
rules.plain_english: During demolition, no wall section more than one story or 12 feet tall may stand without lateral bracing unless a California-registered civil engineer has submitted data to Cal/OSHA showing it can stand on its own. All walls must be left stable at the end of each workday.

parameters.exception: California registered civil engineer submits engineering data to DOSH

rules.applies_to: Employers performing demolition of buildings or structures, including partial demolition in alterations (C-21 and B contractors, wrecking and interior demo crews)
rules.quote: (1) No wall section, which is more than one story or 12 feet in height, shall be permitted to stand alone without lateral bracing, unless a civil engineer, currently registered in California, has submitted engineering data to the Division substantiating the capability of the wall to stand without lateral support.

rules.title: Demolition access: stairs clear within 2 floors/24 ft; passenger elevator at 7+ floors or 72+ ft
rules.plain_english: Keep designated access stairways clear up to within two floors or 24 feet of the demolition above (ladders for the last two floors); cover stairwells used for access at least two floors below the work. Provide construction passenger elevators on demolition of buildings 7 or more floors or 72 feet or taller, with landings at least every 4 floors or 48 feet.
rules.applies_to: Employers performing demolition of buildings or structures, including partial demolition in alterations (C-21 and B contractors, wrecking and interior demo crews)
rules.quote: (r)(1) Construction passenger elevators for hoisting employees shall be provided on demolition projects on multi-story buildings seven or more floors or seventy-two feet or more in height.
rules.notes: DOSH may permit alternatives where elevator attachment would jeopardize the structure ((r)(3)).

rules.title: No walking across exposed floor joists, steel beams or girders during demolition
rules.plain_english: Workers may not walk across exposed joists, beams or girders; provide walkways or planks where needed.

parameters.prohibited: walking across exposed floor joists, steel beams, or girders
parameters.provide: walkways meeting 1624 or planks over weakened areas

rules.applies_to: Employers performing demolition of buildings or structures, including partial demolition in alterations (C-21 and B contractors, wrecking and interior demo crews)
rules.quote: (i) Walking across exposed floor joists, steel beams, or girders is prohibited.

rules.title: Wet down demolition debris for dust; qualified person must OK floors for machines
rules.plain_english: Control demolition dust by keeping material wet (or equivalent). Mechanical equipment may be used on floors only after a qualified person confirms they can carry the load, and floor openings need curbs or stop-logs to keep machines from running over the edge.

parameters.dust_control: water to keep material sufficiently wet, or equivalent
parameters.equipment_on_floors: qualified person determines floor strength first

rules.applies_to: Employers performing demolition of buildings or structures, including partial demolition in alterations (C-21 and B contractors, wrecking and interior demo crews)
rules.quote: (u) Mechanical equipment shall not be used on floors or working surfaces unless a qualified person has determined that such floors or surfaces are of sufficient strength to support the imposed load.
rules.notes: Silica (1532.3) and lead (1532.1) rules also apply to demolition dust; see web_calosha-programs.

rules.title: No salvaging during demolition of structures over three stories
rules.plain_english: Salvaging materials is not allowed during demolition of any building, structure, falsework or scaffold more than three stories high (or the equivalent height that requires a Cal/OSHA permit).
rules.applies_to: Employers performing demolition of buildings or structures, including partial demolition in alterations (C-21 and B contractors, wrecking and interior demo crews)
rules.quote: (w) No salvage of materials shall be permitted during demolition operations on any building, structure, falsework or scaffold more than three stories high or the equivalent height for which a permit is required.
rules.notes: The permit height referenced is 36 ft (web_calosha-programs permit-demolition-36ft).

rules.title: Debris dropped without chutes: barricade the drop zone 42 in high, 6 ft back, with signs
rules.plain_english: If debris is dropped outside the walls without an enclosed chute, the area must be barricaded or fenced with warning signs. If debris is dropped through floor holes without chutes, enclose the landing area with barricades at least 42 inches high set at least 6 feet back from the edge of the opening above, post signs on each level, and don't remove debris below until dropping stops.
rules.applies_to: Employers performing demolition of buildings or structures, including partial demolition in alterations (C-21 and B contractors, wrecking and interior demo crews)
rules.quote: (f) When debris is dropped through holes in the floor without the use of chutes, the area onto which the material is dropped shall be completely enclosed with barricades not less than 42 inches high, and not less than six feet back from the projected edge of the opening above.

rules.title: Debris chutes: enclosed over 45 degrees, openings max 48 in, gate at bottom, 6x6 in bumper
rules.plain_english: Chutes steeper than 45 degrees must be fully enclosed except for closable floor-level openings no taller than 48 inches; chutes loading trucks must be enclosed with a gate at the discharge controlled by a qualified person; hand-dump openings need a guardrail; and where wheelbarrows or machines dump into a chute, provide a securely attached bumper at least 6 inches thick and 6 inches high.

parameters.truck_loading_chute: fully enclosed with gate at discharge; qualified person controls gate and truck loading

rules.applies_to: Employers performing demolition of buildings or structures, including partial demolition in alterations (C-21 and B contractors, wrecking and interior demo crews)
rules.quote: (j) All material chutes, or sections thereof, at an angle of more than 45 degrees from the horizontal, shall be entirely enclosed, except for openings equipped with closures at or about floor level for the insertion of materials. The openings shall not exceed 48 inches in height measured along the wall of the chute.

rules.title: Keep solvent waste, oily rags and flammable liquids in covered fire-resistant containers
rules.plain_english: During demolition, keep solvent waste, oily rags and flammable liquids in fire-resistant covered containers until removed, and clear scrap and rubbish from the work area as work progresses.

parameters.housekeeping: remove scrap lumber, waste and rubbish as work progresses

rules.applies_to: Employers performing demolition of buildings or structures, including partial demolition in alterations (C-21 and B contractors, wrecking and interior demo crews)
rules.quote: (h) All solvent waste, oily rags, and flammable liquids shall be kept in fire resistant covered containers until removed from the work site.
rules.notes: CSO 1737 (Fire Prevention in demolition) is repealed; general construction fire rules are in CSO Article 36 (1920-1938).

rules.title: Work in or next to public streets: traffic control per the California MUTCD
rules.plain_english: When traffic or haulage creates a hazard to workers at sites that encroach on public streets or highways, set up traffic controls that conform to the California Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (the January 13, 2012 edition incorporated in Title 8). Sign and device sizes and designs must follow the Manual.

parameters.standard: California MUTCD, January 13, 2012 (as incorporated by reference)
parameters.trigger: hazard to employees from traffic or haulage at work sites encroaching on public streets or highways

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose work encroaches on public streets or highways or whose employees on foot are exposed to vehicular traffic
rules.quote: (a) Where a hazard exists to employees because of traffic or haulage conditions at work sites that encroach upon public streets or highways, a system of traffic controls in conformance with the "California Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices for Streets and Highways, January 13, 2012," which is herein incorporated by reference and referred to as the "Manual", published by the State Department of Transportation, shall be required so as to abate the hazard.
rules.notes: Section last amended operative 2014-07-01. Caltrans may have issued later CA MUTCD revisions, but Title 8 as fetched 2026-11-25 still incorporates the 2012 edition; dot.ca.gov could not be fetched from this session. Encroachment permits may impose their own traffic control plans.

rules.title: Workers on foot exposed to traffic must wear ANSI/ISEA 107 high-visibility garments
rules.plain_english: Any worker on foot exposed to vehicle traffic must wear a warning vest, jacket or shirt meeting ANSI/ISEA 107-2004. The employer picks the right class by consulting the CA MUTCD, the garment maker, ANSI/ISEA 107 Appendix B, or ATSSA.

parameters.standard: ANSI/ISEA 107-2004

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose work encroaches on public streets or highways or whose employees on foot are exposed to vehicular traffic
rules.quote: (c) Employees (on foot) exposed to the hazard of vehicular traffic shall wear warning garments such as vests, jackets, or shirts manufactured in accordance with the requirements of the American National Standards Institute (ANSI)/International Safety Equipment Association (ISEA) 107-2004, High Visibility Safety Apparel and Headwear.
rules.notes: Subsections (c)-(e) last amended operative 2009-08-22.

rules.title: At night, high-visibility garments must be retroreflective, visible at 1,000 feet
rules.plain_english: During darkness, warning garments for workers exposed to traffic (and flaggers) must be retroreflective, meet ANSI/ISEA 107-2004, and be visible from at least 1,000 feet. White outer garments with compliant retroreflective material are allowed at night but not in snow or fog.

parameters.standard: ANSI/ISEA 107-2004

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose work encroaches on public streets or highways or whose employees on foot are exposed to vehicular traffic
rules.quote: The retroreflective material shall be visible at a minimum of 1,000 feet.
rules.notes: 1599(e) contains the same 1,000-foot requirement for flaggers ('visible at a minimum distance of 1,000 feet').

rules.title: Use flaggers where signs and barricades can't control traffic; number and placement per CA MUTCD
rules.plain_english: Flaggers must be used wherever barricades and warning signs can't control moving traffic on a construction site. How many flaggers and where they go follows the CA MUTCD; they must be placed to give effective warning, and warning signs placed per the Manual.

parameters.required_when: barricades and warning signs cannot control moving traffic

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose work encroaches on public streets or highways or whose employees on foot are exposed to vehicular traffic
rules.quote: (a) A flagger or flaggers shall be utilized at locations on a construction site where barricades and warning signs cannot control the moving traffic.
rules.notes: Section last amended operative 2014-07-01.

rules.title: Flaggers: ANSI/ISEA 107 garments; illuminated stations and retroreflective gear at night
rules.plain_english: Flaggers must wear ANSI/ISEA 107-2004 warning garments. At night, the flagger's station must be lit so approaching traffic can clearly see the flagger, and garments must be retroreflective, visible from 1,000 feet.

parameters.standard: ANSI/ISEA 107-2004

rules.applies_to: Construction employers using flaggers
rules.quote: (e) During the hours of darkness, flaggers' stations shall be illuminated such that the flagger will be clearly visible to approaching traffic and flaggers shall be outfitted with reflectorized garments manufactured in accordance with the requirements of the American National Standards Institute (ANSI)/International Safety Equipment Association (ISEA) 107-2004, High Visibility Safety Apparel and Headwear.

rules.title: Flagger training before assignment: 9 required topics including a hands-on demonstration
rules.plain_english: Flaggers must be trained before being assigned, based on the CA MUTCD and site conditions, covering: required equipment, work-zone and station layout, signaling stop/proceed/slow, one-way traffic control, a trainee demonstration, emergency vehicles, emergencies, hostile drivers, and single-flagger procedures where used.

topics: work zone and flagging station layout

rules.applies_to: Construction employers using flaggers
rules.quote: (g) Flaggers shall be trained in the proper fundamentals of flagging moving traffic before being assigned as flaggers.
rules.notes: No retraining interval or certification card is mandated by 1599; some agencies and encroachment permits require certified flaggers.

rules.title: Document flagger training under the IIPP; trainer must be qualified
rules.plain_english: Flagger training must be documented as the IIPP rule (3203) requires, and must be given by someone with the qualifications and experience to teach flagging effectively.

parameters.trainer: qualifications and experience necessary to effectively instruct

rules.applies_to: Construction employers using flaggers
rules.quote: Documentation of the training shall be maintained as required by Section 3203, Injury Illness and Prevention Program of the General Industry Safety Orders.
rules.notes: IIPP training-record retention (at least 1 year) is in web_calosha-programs (iipp-training-records-1-year).

rules.title: Hot work: written-basis fire prevention and suppression procedure per NFPA 51B and ANSI Z49.1
rules.plain_english: Wherever gas or electric welding, cutting, brazing or similar hot work is done, the employer must set up and implement fire prevention and suppression instructions based on ANSI Z49.1-94 (chapters 3 and 6) and NFPA 51B-2009 (chapters 3-7). Welding blankets, curtains and pads must be approved for their use.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees weld, cut, braze, solder or heat metal (GISO 4848 applies through CSO 1502(c))
rules.quote: (a) The employer shall establish a fire prevention and suppression procedure whenever any of the operations and processes covered by Sections 4794(a) and 4850(a) are conducted on its property. The employer shall issue and implement instructions on fire prevention and suppression procedures based upon the requirements contained in American National Standards Institute (ANSI/ASC) Z49.1-94, Safety In Welding, Cutting and Allied Processes, Chapters 3 and 6 and National Fire Protection Association (NFPA) 51B-2009, Standard for Fire Prevention During Welding, Cutting, and Other Hot Work, Chapters 3-7, which are hereby incorporated by reference.
rules.notes: Specific fire-watch durations and clearance distances come from NFPA 51B, whose text was not read; they are therefore not stated here. 4848(a) says 'on its property'; how DOSH applies it to a contractor's hot work at another party's site was not confirmed. Local fire-code hot work permits are outside this pack.

rules.title: Indoor welding: local exhaust with at least 100 ft/min in the welding zone
rules.plain_english: Indoor welding, brazing and cutting needs local exhaust ventilation giving at least 100 linear feet per minute at the welding zone; if not feasible, dilution ventilation keeping fumes under the 5155 limits; if neither is feasible, respirators per 1531.

fallbacks: mechanical dilution ventilation to keep below 5155 limits

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees weld, cut, braze, solder or heat metal
rules.quote: (a) Mechanical Ventilation for Indoor Operations. Local exhaust systems providing a minimum air velocity of 100 lineal feet per minute in the welding zone shall be used except as otherwise specified by this section.
rules.notes: Last amended 12-13-84, effective thirtieth day thereafter (date computed).

rules.title: Welding toxic metals (lead, cadmium, chromium, zinc, beryllium, stainless): local exhaust or supplied air
rules.plain_english: In enclosed spaces, use local exhaust when welding or cutting beryllium, cadmium, chromium, fluorides, lead, mercury, zinc (galvanized) or stainless steel; if that won't control exposure, wear supplied-air respirators. Outdoors, provide respirators for these materials unless ventilation clears fumes (never for beryllium, cadmium, lead or mercury); beryllium always requires supplied-air respirators.

toxic_materials: inert-gas metal-arc welding or oxygen cutting of stainless steel
parameters.enclosed_space: local exhaust; supplied-air respirators if not effective
parameters.open_air: respirators per 1531, except not required when ventilation removes fumes from breathing zone (not allowed for beryllium, cadmium, lead, mercury)

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees weld, cut, braze, solder or heat metal
rules.quote: (1) In operations involving beryllium-containing base or filler metals, only supplied-air respirators shall be used.
rules.notes: Lead and hexavalent chromium have their own construction standards (1532.1, 1532.2).

rules.title: Never use welding gases or oxygen for ventilation, cooling or blowing off dust
rules.plain_english: Compressed gases used for welding and cutting, including oxygen, must never be used for ventilation, cooling, blowing dust off clothing, or cleaning the work area.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees weld, cut, braze, solder or heat metal
rules.quote: (d) Improper Use of Welding Gases. Compressed gases used for welding and cutting shall not be used for ventilation purposes, comfort cooling, blowing dust from clothing, or cleaning the work area.
rules.notes: 1743(i): 'Compressed oxygen shall not be used for ventilation, testing, or similar purposes different from its intended function in welding and burning.'

rules.title: Coated metals: test unknown coatings for flammability; strip toxic coatings 4 inches back
rules.plain_english: Before welding, cutting or heating a surface with a coating of unknown flammability, a qualified person must test it; highly flammable coatings must be stripped. Toxic coatings must be stripped at least 4 inches from the heated area, or workers must use supplied-air respirators (or the 1536 ventilation rules apply).

parameters.highly_flammable_coatings: strip from area to be heated

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees weld, cut, braze, solder or heat metal
rules.quote: (c) All surfaces covered with toxic preservatives, including coatings which generate toxic substances upon heating, shall be stripped for a distance of at least four inches from the area of heat application, or employees shall be required to use supplied-air respirators in accordance with Section 1531, or the provisions of Section 1536(b), (c) shall apply.
rules.notes: Lead paint on steel also triggers the lead standard (1532.1) trigger-task rules.

rules.title: Keep a 10 B:C (or larger) extinguisher near fuel-gas cutting and welding
rules.plain_english: A dry chemical or CO2 fire extinguisher rated at least 10 B:C must be kept near any operation using bottled fuel gases (acetylene, propane, etc.).

parameters.where: near operations using bottled fuel gases

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees weld, cut, braze, solder or heat metal
rules.quote: (j) A dry chemical or carbon dioxide fire extinguisher rated at least 10 B:C shall be kept near operations where bottled fuel gases are being used.
rules.notes: Last amended 1-5-87, effective thirtieth day thereafter (date computed).

rules.title: Shut off cylinders during breaks; remove torch from confined spaces; warn others of hot metal
rules.plain_english: When welding stops for a substantial time (lunch, overnight), shut off the gas cylinders and take the torch and hose out of any confined space. When finished, the welder must warn other workers where hot metal is.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees weld, cut, braze, solder or heat metal
rules.quote: (l) When operations are suspended for any substantial period of time, such as during lunch or overnight, gas cylinders shall be shut off. The torch and hose shall be removed from the confined space. Upon completion or discontinuance of welding operations, the welder shall warn other workers of the location of hot metal.

rules.title: Store oxygen cylinders 20 ft from fuel gas, or behind a 5-ft half-hour fire barrier
rules.plain_english: In storage, oxygen cylinders must be at least 20 feet from fuel-gas cylinders and combustibles (especially oil or grease), or separated by a noncombustible barrier at least 5 feet high with at least a half-hour fire rating.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees weld, cut, braze, solder or heat metal
rules.quote: (g) Oxygen cylinders in storage shall be separated from fuel-gas cylinders or combustible materials (especially oil or grease), a minimum distance of 20 feet or by a noncombustible barrier at least 5 feet high having a fire-resistance rating of at least one-half hour.
rules.notes: Section last amended operative 2007-09-20.

rules.title: Gas cylinders: valve end up, secured upright, caps on to move, never into confined spaces
rules.plain_english: Store and use acetylene and fuel-gas cylinders valve end up; secure all cylinders in use so they can't fall; put valve caps on before moving; don't lift with magnets or slings; never take oxygen, acetylene or fuel-gas cylinders into confined spaces; keep them away from sparks and slag; open fuel-gas valves no more than 1-1/2 turns.

parameters.secured: racks or placed so they cannot fall
parameters.crane_lifting: cradles, nets or skip boxes; never magnet or rope/chain slings

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees weld, cut, braze, solder or heat metal
rules.quote: Cylinders containing oxygen, acetylene or fuel-gases shall not be taken into confined spaces.

rules.title: Construction fire protection program for all phases of work
rules.plain_english: The employer must develop a fire protection program covering all phases of construction and provide the required firefighting equipment without delay as fire hazards arise; keep access to it clear, mark its location, and keep it working. Stricter local fire rules prevail.

parameters.program: fire protection program throughout all phases of construction

rules.applies_to: All California construction employers
rules.quote: (a) The employer shall be responsible for the development of a fire protection program to be followed throughout all phases of the construction work; and he shall provide for the fire fighting equipment as specified in this Article.
rules.notes: Last amended 10-9-86, effective thirtieth day thereafter (date computed). 1920 does not say the program must be written; a written program is the practical way to show one exists.

rules.title: Construction fire extinguishers: one 2A per 3,000 sq ft, within 75 ft travel, one per floor at the stairs
rules.plain_english: Provide at least one 2A-rated extinguisher per 3,000 square feet of floor area (minimum one), with no point more than 75 feet of travel from an extinguisher, at least one on each floor, and one by the stairway on each floor of multi-story buildings. Single-family homes need only one 2A extinguisher on site during work hours.

parameters.multi_story_location: adjacent to stairway on each floor
substitutes_for_2A: 55-gallon open water container with two fire pails
3/4 in garden hose <=75 ft, >=5 gpm, >=30 ft stream
up to 100 ft of 1-1/2 in hose with >=25 gpm nozzle
parameters.formula: extinguishers = max(1, ceil(floor_area_sq_ft / 3000)) per floor area, subject to 75 ft travel

rules.applies_to: All California construction employers
rules.quote: (1) A fire extinguisher, rated not less than 2A, shall be provided for each 3,000 square feet of the floor area, or fraction thereof. Where the floor area is less than 3,000 square feet at least one extinguisher shall be provided. Travel distance from any point of the protected area to the nearest fire extinguisher shall not exceed 75 feet.
rules.notes: Formula derived from 'for each 3,000 square feet of the floor area, or fraction thereof'. Last amended 10-9-86 (effective date computed).

rules.title: 10B extinguisher within 50 ft where over 5 gallons of flammable liquid or 5 lb of flammable gas is used
rules.plain_english: Wherever more than 5 gallons of flammable or combustible liquid or 5 pounds of flammable gas is being used on the site, a 10B-rated extinguisher must be within 50 feet (vehicle fuel tanks don't count).

parameters.excludes: integral fuel tanks of motor vehicles

rules.applies_to: All California construction employers
rules.quote: (3) A fire extinguisher, rated not less than 10B, shall be provided within 50 feet of wherever more than 5 gallons of flammable or combustible liquids or 5 pounds of flammable gas are being used on the job site.

rules.title: Inspect jobsite extinguishers monthly; service annually by a State Fire Marshal licensee
rules.plain_english: Check every portable extinguisher at least monthly (in place, not used or tampered with, no visible damage) and have it serviced at least annually by a person licensed or registered by the State Fire Marshal.

parameters.service_by: person licensed or registered by the State Fire Marshal (H&SC Div. 12, Pt. 2, Ch. 1.5)

rules.applies_to: All California construction employers
rules.quote: (4) Portable fire extinguishers shall be inspected monthly, or at more frequent intervals, and serviced at least annually by a person licensed or registered by the State Fire Marshal as required by the Health and Safety Code, Division 12, Part 2, Chapter 1.5, Articles 2, 3, and 6.
rules.notes: Health and Safety Code text not read (leginfo blocked).

rules.title: Written Injury and Illness Prevention Program (IIPP) required
rules.plain_english: Every employer must have a written IIPP that is actually implemented and kept up to date. Construction employers are required to have one by Construction Safety Order 1509, which points to the general IIPP rule in section 3203.
rules.applies_to: All California employers with employees on construction jobsites (every employer; no size exemption from having a program)
rules.quote: Effective July 1, 1991, every employer shall establish, implement and maintain an effective Injury and Illness Prevention Program (Program). The Program shall be in writing and, shall, at a minimum:
rules.notes: Element (a)(8) employee access was added effective 2020-07-01. 8 CCR 1509(a) separately requires construction employers to maintain an IIPP 'in accordance with section 3203'. A Workplace Violence Prevention Plan may be a separate section of the IIPP (Labor Code 6401.9).

rules.title: Construction employers: IIPP under CSO 1509
rules.plain_english: The Construction Safety Orders independently require every construction employer to establish, implement and maintain an effective IIPP following section 3203.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers
rules.quote: (a) Every employer shall establish, implement and maintain an effective Injury and Illness Prevention Program in accordance with section 3203 of the General Industry Safety Orders.

rules.title: IIPP hazard inspections: when they must happen
rules.plain_english: Your IIPP must include scheduled periodic inspections, and inspections are also required when the program is first set up, when new substances, processes, procedures or equipment bring new hazards, and whenever you learn of a new or previously unrecognized hazard.
rules.applies_to: All California employers with employees on construction jobsites
rules.quote: Include procedures for identifying and evaluating work place hazards including scheduled periodic inspections to identify unsafe conditions and work practices.
rules.notes: The regulation does not fix a numeric inspection interval; the frequency is set by the employer's program. Tool can schedule recurring jobsite inspections and log them (see iipp-inspection-records-1-year).

rules.title: IIPP: correct hazards in a timely manner; remove workers from imminent hazards
rules.plain_english: Unsafe conditions must be corrected in a timely manner based on severity. If an imminent hazard can't be fixed right away, everyone except the people needed to correct it must be removed from the area.
rules.applies_to: All California employers with employees on construction jobsites
rules.quote: When an imminent hazard exists which cannot be immediately abated without endangering employee(s) and/or property, remove all exposed personnel from the area except those necessary to correct the existing condition.

rules.title: IIPP training: when it must be given
rules.plain_english: Safety training must be given when the program starts, to every new employee, to employees given new assignments, when new substances/processes/equipment introduce new hazards, when new hazards are recognized, and to supervisors on the hazards their crews face.
rules.applies_to: All California employers with employees on construction jobsites
rules.quote: (B) To all new employees; (C) To all employees given new job assignments for which training has not previously been received;

rules.title: Employers with fewer than 10 employees may communicate safety orally
rules.plain_english: If you have fewer than 10 employees, you may meet the IIPP communication requirement by instructing employees orally on general safe work practices and job-specific hazards.
rules.applies_to: Employers with fewer than 10 employees
rules.quote: Exception: Employers having fewer than 10 employees shall be permitted to communicate to and instruct employees orally in general safe work practices with specific instructions with respect to hazards unique to the employees' job assignments as compliance with subsection (a)(3).
rules.notes: The program itself must still be in writing; this exception only relaxes the communication element.
rules.correction: None. Quote string-matched against the re-fetched official text and every parameter value checked against it.

rules.title: Give employees a copy of the IIPP within 5 business days
rules.plain_english: When an employee or their designated representative asks for the IIPP, you must provide access no later than 5 business days after the request. The first printed copy is free.

parameters.trigger: request from employee or designated representative
parameters.format_default: printed unless requester agrees to electronic
parameters.alternative: unobstructed electronic access via company server/website

rules.applies_to: All California employers with employees on construction jobsites
rules.quote: Provide access in a reasonable time, place, and manner, but in no event later than five (5) business days after the request for access is received from an employee or designated representative.
rules.notes: Additional copies within 1 year with no updates may carry reasonable reproduction cost. Records of implementation steps need not be included.
rules.correction: None. Quote string-matched against the re-fetched official text and every parameter value checked against it.

rules.title: Keep IIPP inspection records at least 1 year
rules.plain_english: Records of scheduled and periodic inspections (who inspected, what was found, what was done to fix it) must be kept at least one year.
rules.applies_to: All California employers with employees on construction jobsites
rules.quote: These records shall be maintained for at least one (1) year; and Exception: Employers with fewer than 10 employees may elect to maintain the inspection records only until the hazard is corrected.

rules.title: Keep safety training records at least 1 year
rules.plain_english: Document each employee's safety training (name or ID, dates, type of training, trainer) and keep it at least one year.

parameters.lt_10_employees_alternative: log of instructions given at hire/new duties
parameters.short_tenure_exception: employees with < 1 year may receive records at termination instead

rules.applies_to: All California employers with employees on construction jobsites

rules.plain_english: The indoor heat rule applies to indoor work areas at or above 82F while employees are present. It does not apply to brief exposures of 82F or more but below 95F that last less than 15 minutes in any 60-minute period. That exception does not cover vehicles without working air conditioning, or shipping or intermodal containers during loading, unloading or related work.

The old parameter "max_minutes_per_60": 15 and the range [82, 95] did not say which ends are inclusive and read as allowing up to 15 minutes. It is now restated as temperature_f_gte 82 / temperature_f_lt 95 / exposure_minutes_lt 15 per 60-minute period, with the vehicle and container carve-outs. All other values were confirmed. plain_english updated on 2026-11-27 to state the incidental-exposure exception (82F or more and below 95F, less than 15 minutes in any 60-minute period) and its vehicle and container carve-outs.

rules.title: Report serious injury, illness or death to Cal/OSHA within 8 hours

rules.title: Employer's Report of Occupational Injury (Form 5020) within 5 days
rules.plain_english: For every work injury or illness causing lost time beyond the day of injury or needing treatment beyond first aid, file the employer's report with your workers' comp insurer (or DIR/DLSR if uninsured/self-insured) within five days after you learn of it. The report must include the employee's SSN.

parameters.trigger: employer obtains knowledge of injury/illness with lost time beyond date of injury or treatment beyond first aid
parameters.file_with: insurer if insured; otherwise DIR Division of Labor Statistics and Research

rules.applies_to: Employer-contractors with employees
rules.source: PDF page 45-46 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: An employer-contractor MUST file a complete report of every employee occupational injury or occupational illness that results in lost time beyond the date of injury or illness, or which requires medical treatment beyond first aid, with the Department of Industrial Relations through its Division of Labor Statistics and Research or, if an insured employer, with the insurer (Labor Code §6409.1).
rules.notes: Five-day deadline text continues on PDF p.46: '...within five days after the employer obtains knowledge of the injury or illness. Each report ... must indicate the Social Security number of the injured employee'. Form number 5020 is from the DIR WVPP guidance page; the Law Book says 'the form required by the Division of Labor Statistics and Research'. Failure to report to insurer can lead to WCAB order within five days; noncompliance punishable as contempt (Labor Code 3760).
rules.correction: Not refuted. 8 CCR 14001 is the DLSR regulation that implements Labor Code 6409.1(a). It requires a report for lost time beyond the date of injury or treatment beyond first aid, filed on Form 5020 with the insurer, or directly with the Division if self-insured, within five days after the employer learns of it. That matches the parameters and the Law Book quote. Labor Code 6409.1 itself was not seen (leginfo is unreachable).

The older '$1,000' figure in section 340's own text is outdated.

rules.correction: penalty_max_usd_per_violation was 1000. That figure comes from stale text in 8 CCR 340. 8 CCR 334(a) classifies "failure to post ... poster" as a Regulatory violation, and 8 CCR 336(a)(1) (2025 schedule, operative 1-1-2025) sets up to $16,285 per Regulatory violation, with a $500 minimum proposed penalty. 336's history says the (a)(1) amounts are adjusted under Labor Code 6431(b). rules.plain_english: Repeat lead monitoring: below action level - none (unless changes); at/above action level but below 30 ug/m3 - every 12 months; 30-50 ug/m3 - every 6 months; above 50 ug/m3 - quarterly. Stop only after two consecutive results at least 7 days apart fall below the tier.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers with lead exposures
rules.quote: (B) If the initial determination or subsequent determination reveals employee exposure to be at or above the action level but below 30 µg/m³ as an 8-hour TWA, the employer shall perform monitoring at least every 12 months.

rules.title: Lead medical surveillance and blood lead testing
rules.plain_english: Provide medical surveillance for employees exposed at/above the action level (exceptions for fewer than 30 days in 12 months with no day over 10 ug/m3, or fewer than 15 days with no day over 20 ug/m3) and as interim protection for trigger tasks. Blood lead testing every 2 months for the first 6 months, then every 6 months; more often for elevated levels.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers with lead exposures
rules.quote: Exception 1: Medical surveillance is not required for an employee who is not exposed to lead at or above the action level for 30 or more days in any 12 consecutive months, and who is not exposed on any day above 10 µg/m³ as an 8-hour TWA, without regard to respirator use.

rules.title: Lead medical removal at blood lead 30 ug/dl
rules.plain_english: Remove an employee from lead exposure when their last blood lead test is 30 ug/dl or higher. From Jan 1, 2026, also remove them when the last two blood lead tests are 20 ug/dl or higher, or when the average of all blood lead tests in the last 6 months is 20 ug/dl or higher (unless the last test is below 15). Return after two tests at least 30 days apart below 15 ug/dl.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers with lead exposures
rules.quote: 1. The last blood lead test indicates that the employee's blood lead level is at or above 30 µg/dl;
