The field is corrected. The parameters and plain_english were already right. mrp_benefits_max_months: 18 was added from (k)(2)(A). plain_english updated on 2026-11-27 to make clear that both 20 ug/dl triggers (last two tests and 6-month average) start January 1, 2026.

rules.title: Silica in construction: covered unless always below 25 ug/m3
rules.plain_english: The construction silica standard covers all respirable crystalline silica exposures in construction unless exposure will stay below 25 ug/m3 (8-hour TWA) under any foreseeable conditions.

rules.quote: (a) Scope and application. This section applies to all occupational exposures to respirable crystalline silica in construction work, except where employee exposure will remain below 25 micrograms per cubic meter of air (25 μg/m³) as an 8-hour time-weighted average (TWA) under any foreseeable conditions.

rules.title: Silica: follow Table 1 controls or meet PEL of 50 ug/m3
rules.plain_english: For tasks on Table 1, fully implement the listed engineering controls, work practices and respirators. Otherwise, assess exposures and keep them at or below the 50 ug/m3 PEL (8-hour TWA).

compliance_paths: exposure assessment + PEL (performance or scheduled monitoring)

rules.applies_to: Construction employers with silica exposure
rules.quote: (1) Permissible exposure limit (PEL). The employer shall ensure that no employee is exposed to an airborne concentration of respirable crystalline silica in excess of 50 μg/m³, calculated as an 8-hour TWA.

rules.title: Silica: written exposure control plan, reviewed annually

rules.applies_to: Construction employers covered by 1532.3
rules.quote: (2) The employer shall review and evaluate the effectiveness of the written exposure control plan at least annually and update it as necessary.

rules.title: Silica: designate a competent person
rules.plain_english: Designate a competent person to make frequent and regular inspections of jobsites, materials and equipment to implement the silica exposure control plan.

rules.title: Silica medical surveillance for respirator use 30+ days/year
rules.plain_english: Offer free medical exams to employees required to wear a respirator for silica 30 or more days per year: baseline within 30 days of assignment (unless one in last 3 years), then at least every 3 years.

rules.title: Silica: no dry sweeping or compressed-air cleaning

prohibited: dry_sweeping
dry_brushing
compressed_air_cleaning_of_clothing_or_surfaces

rules.quote: (1) The employer shall not allow dry sweeping or dry brushing where such activity could contribute to employee exposure to respirable crystalline silica unless wet sweeping, HEPA-filtered vacuuming or other methods that minimize the likelihood of exposure are not feasible.

rules.title: Fall protection required above 7.5 feet
rules.plain_english: Employees exposed to falls of more than 7 1/2 feet from a structure's perimeter, unprotected sides/edges, leading edges, shaftways/openings, roofs steeper than 7:12, or other surfaces steeper than 40 degrees must wear approved personal fall arrest, restraint or positioning systems unless otherwise adequately protected.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers
rules.quote: (a) Approved personal fall arrest, personal fall restraint or positioning systems shall be worn by those employees whose work exposes them to falling in excess of 7 1/2 feet from the perimeter of a structure, unprotected sides and edges, leading edges, through shaftways and openings, sloped roof surfaces steeper than 7:12,
rules.notes: Trade-specific triggers differ: residential framing/roofing 6 ft (1716.2, 1731); commercial roofing 20 ft (1730).

rules.title: Site-specific written Fall Protection Plan when conventional protection is infeasible
rules.plain_english: If you can show guardrails, fall arrest and nets are infeasible or create a greater hazard, you may use a written, site-specific fall protection plan prepared by a qualified person, kept current and on site, implemented under a competent person, listing reasons, alternative measures, controlled access zones, and the employees allowed in them. Investigate and update after any fall or near miss.

parameters.presumption: conventional fall protection is feasible; employer bears burden

rules.applies_to: Construction employers using a fall protection plan

rules.title: Residential/light commercial framing: fall protection at 6 feet
rules.plain_english: When walking/working on top plates, joists, rafters, trusses or beams 6 feet or more above grade or the floor below, provide scaffolding, guardrails, nets, personal fall protection, or (if conventional methods are infeasible) a fall protection plan with safety monitors and controlled access zones.
rules.applies_to: Residential-type and light commercial framing (joists/trusses on stud walls)
rules.quote: (1) When employees are walking/working on top plates, joists, rafters, trusses, beams or other similar structural members 6 feet or more above the surrounding grade or floor level below, fall protection shall be provided by one or more of the following methods:

rules.title: Residential roofing: fall protection at 6 feet (any height above 7:12)
rules.plain_english: On residential-type roofing with slopes up to 7:12, protect employees when the fall distance is 6 feet or more; on slopes steeper than 7:12, protection is required regardless of height.
rules.applies_to: Residential-type roofing (single-family, townhouses, duplexes)

rules.title: Non-residential roofing: fall protection on roofs over 20 feet
rules.plain_english: For non-residential roofing operations, protect employees from falls from roofs more than 20 feet high (warning lines at least 5 ft from edge on low-slope roofs; any height when using felt-laying machines pulled by an operator walking backwards).
rules.applies_to: Roofing operations other than residential-type (8 CCR 1731)
rules.quote: (1) Employees shall be protected from falls from roofs of a height of more than 20 feet by use of one or a combination of the methods in this section.

rules.title: Cave-in protection for excavations 5 feet or deeper
rules.plain_english: Every employee in an excavation must be protected by an adequate protective system (sloping, benching, shoring, shielding) unless it is entirely in stable rock, or less than 5 feet deep and a competent person finds no sign of potential cave-in.

exceptions: entirely_stable_rock
lt_5ft_and_competent_person_finds_no_cave_in_indication

rules.applies_to: Construction employers with employees in excavations
rules.quote: (B) Excavations are less than 5 feet in depth and examination of the ground by a competent person provides no indication of a potential cave-in.

rules.title: Trench egress within 25 feet when 4 feet or deeper
rules.plain_english: Trenches 4 feet or deeper must have a stairway, ladder, ramp or other safe way out so no employee has to travel more than 25 feet laterally to reach it. Test atmospheres before entry over 4 feet where hazardous atmospheres could exist.

rules.title: Daily competent-person excavation inspections
rules.plain_english: A competent person must inspect excavations, adjacent areas and protective systems daily before work starts, as needed during the shift, and after every rainstorm or other hazard-increasing event; remove employees if cave-in or hazardous conditions are found.

parameters.frequency: daily, prior to start of work, as needed through shift

rules.title: Notify regional notification center (811) at least 2 working days before digging

rules.quote: (1) Every employer working on or furnishing personnel on a construction project, on line crews and on other short duration or transient jobs shall provide at least one first-aid kit in a weatherproof container.

rules.title: Post emergency phone numbers at the job phone
rules.plain_english: Post the phone numbers of a physician (plus an alternate if available), hospitals, ambulance and fire services near the job telephone, or otherwise make them available. Inform all employees of what to do in case of injury or illness and provide transport or communication to get emergency care.

rules.plain_english: Have a written plan describing how you meet the emergency medical service requirements; employers sharing a combined program may use one plan.

rules.plain_english: Provide at least one separate toilet facility per 20 employees (or fraction) of each sex; with fewer than 5 employees one all-gender single-user toilet is enough. Mobile crews with ready transport to nearby toilets are exempt.

rules.title: Written Hazard Communication program (incl. multi-employer sites)
rules.plain_english: Keep a written hazard communication program at the workplace covering labels, safety data sheets and training. On multi-employer sites it must explain how you will inform other employers of hazardous chemicals their workers may be exposed to.

rules.title: Written respiratory protection program; annual fit testing
rules.plain_english: Where respirators are necessary or required (e.g., silica, lead, asbestos), have a written worksite-specific respiratory protection program with a trained administrator, and fit-test tight-fitting respirators before first use, when changing models, and at least annually.

rules.quote: (2) The employer shall ensure that an employee using a tight-fitting facepiece respirator is fit tested prior to initial use of the respirator, whenever a different respirator facepiece (size, style, model or make) is used, and at least annually thereafter.
rules.correction: None. Quote string-matched against the re-fetched official text and every parameter value checked against it.

rules.title: Written Workplace Violence Prevention Plan (SB 553) since July 1, 2024
rules.plain_english: Covered employers must establish, implement and maintain an effective written Workplace Violence Prevention Plan (WVPP), either stand-alone or as a separate section of the IIPP, specific to each work area and operation. Required elements include responsible persons, employee involvement, coordination with other employers, compliance, communication, reporting without retaliation, emergency response, training, hazard identification and correction, post-incident investigation, and periodic review.
rules.applies_to: All California employers, places of employment and employer-provided housing, except Labor Code 6401.9(b)(2) exemptions (construction employers are covered)
rules.quote: On September 30, 2023, California Senate Bill 553 (Cortese) was signed into law and California Labor Code section 6401.9 will be in effect and enforceable on July 1, 2024. Employers that fall within the scope of this law must establish, implement, and maintain an effective written Workplace Violence Prevention Plan
rules.notes: Read from official Cal/OSHA (dir.ca.gov) guidance pages summarizing LC 6401.9; leginfo.legislature.ca.gov statute text was not reachable from this environment. As of the 2026-10-27 DIR rulemaking page, the implementing regulation (proposed 8 CCR 3343) was still a discussion draft (OSHSB deadline to adopt: 2026-12-31). Re-check for an adopted 3343 in 2027.

rules.title: Violent incident log for every workplace violence incident
rules.plain_english: Record every workplace violence incident (including threats) in a violent incident log, with no personal identifying information. On multi-employer sites, the model plan also has you give a copy of the log to the controlling employer.
rules.applies_to: All California employers, places of employment and employer-provided housing, except Labor Code 6401.9(b)(2) exemptions (construction employers are covered)
rules.quote: All workplace violence incidents are required to be documented in the violent incident log.
rules.notes: Cal/OSHA FAQ (official dir.ca.gov). Employers may design their own log if it captures the LC 6401.9(d)(2) fields. Multi-employer provision is from Cal/OSHA's Model WVPP (https://www.dir.ca.gov/dosh/dosh_publications/Model-WPV-Plan-General-Industry.docx).

rules.title: Workplace violence training: initial and annually
rules.plain_english: Provide WVPP training when the plan is first established, annually thereafter, and when new hazards are identified or the plan changes. Training had to be in place by July 1, 2024.
rules.applies_to: All California employers, places of employment and employer-provided housing, except Labor Code 6401.9(b)(2) exemptions (construction employers are covered)
rules.quote: Annually to ensure all employees understand and comply with the plan.
rules.notes: Quote is from Cal/OSHA's official Model WVPP (dir.ca.gov). The statutory 'initial training ... and annually thereafter' wording also appears as baseline LC 6401.9 text in DIR's draft comparison document (https://www.dir.ca.gov/dosh/doshreg/Workplace-Violence-in-General-Industry/WPV-Draft-Revisions-May-13-2025.docx). FAQ Q21 confirms training was enforceable July 1, 2024 with no grace period.
rules.correction: Not refuted. The statutory wording, taken from the unformatted (baseline LC 6401.9) runs of DIR's comparison document, is: "initial training when the plan is first established, and annually thereafter" plus additional training "when a new or previously unrecognized workplace violence hazard has been identified and when changes are made to the plan". FAQ: 6401.9(b)-(g) enforceable July 1, 2024. Caveat: leginfo was not reachable, so the statute was seen only through DIR's verbatim reproduction.

rules.title: Workplace violence records: 5 years (training 1 year)
rules.plain_english: Keep workplace violence hazard identification/evaluation/correction records, violent incident logs, and incident investigation records for at least 5 years; keep WVPP training records for at least 1 year. Records must not contain medical information.
rules.applies_to: All California employers, places of employment and employer-provided housing, except Labor Code 6401.9(b)(2) exemptions (construction employers are covered)
rules.quote: Records of workplace violence hazard identification, evaluation, and correction, for a minimum of five years.
rules.notes: Same DIR page lists, as separate bullets: training records minimum one year; Violence Incident Logs minimum five years; incident investigation records minimum five years. Official Cal/OSHA guidance page summarizing LC 6401.9(f); training records must include dates, contents/summary, trainer names and qualifications, and attendee names and job titles (per DIR draft baseline text and Model WVPP).

rules.title: Give employees WVPP records within 15 calendar days
rules.plain_english: Workplace violence hazard records, training records and violent incident logs must be made available to employees and their representatives on request, free, for examination and copying within 15 calendar days.

parameters.division_access: all WVP records incl. investigations upon request

rules.applies_to: All California employers, places of employment and employer-provided housing, except Labor Code 6401.9(b)(2) exemptions (construction employers are covered)
rules.quote: All records of workplace violence hazard identification, evaluation, and correction, as well as training records and violent incident logs, shall be made available to employees and their authorized representatives, upon request and without cost, for examination and copying within 15 calendar days of a request.
rules.correction: Not refuted. The 15 calendar days and no-cost access match the baseline LC 6401.9 text in DIR's comparison document. Wording note: the statutory baseline reads "employees and their representatives". The quote, from DIR's web page, says "their authorized representatives", and "authorized employee" is a proposed 3343 addition. The quote is accurate to its cited DIR page. Leginfo was not reachable.

rules.title: Review the WVPP at least annually and after incidents
rules.plain_english: Review the Workplace Violence Prevention Plan for effectiveness at least annually, when a deficiency becomes apparent, and after a workplace violence incident.
rules.applies_to: All California employers, places of employment and employer-provided housing, except Labor Code 6401.9(b)(2) exemptions (construction employers are covered)
rules.quote: At least annually. When a deficiency is observed or becomes apparent. After a workplace violence incident.
rules.notes: Read in Cal/OSHA's official Model WVPP; DIR's draft-vs-statute comparison shows the same 'annually, when a deficiency is observed or becomes apparent, and after a workplace incident' review language.
rules.correction: Not refuted. The baseline LC 6401.9 text reads: "The plan shall be reviewed at least: annually, when a deficiency is observed or becomes apparent, and after a workplace incident." The Model WVPP quote matches. Leginfo was not reachable.

rules.title: Workplace crime victim: workers' comp notice within one working day
rules.plain_english: If an employee is the victim of a crime at the workplace (which covers many workplace violence incidents), give them written notice that they may be eligible for workers' compensation, including for psychiatric injuries. Deliver it personally or by first-class mail within one working day of the crime, or of the date the employer reasonably should have known of it. Also log the incident, investigate, report serious injuries within 8 hours, and record it on the Form 300 if recordable.

parameters.trigger: employee is the victim of a crime that occurred at the employee's place of employment
parameters.notice_form: written notice of workers' compensation eligibility, including for psychiatric injuries resulting from the crime
clock_starts_from: date the employer reasonably should have known of the crime

rules.applies_to: All California employers, places of employment and employer-provided housing, except Labor Code 6401.9(b)(2) exemptions (construction employers are covered)
rules.quote: Employers must give employees notice of workers' compensation eligibility within one working day of a workplace violence incident.
rules.notes: The CSLB Law Book (PDF p.47) separately notes the Labor Code 3553 duty to notify workplace-crime victims of workers' comp eligibility.
rules.correction: The 1-working-day deadline is confirmed. The trigger was too loose. Labor Code 3553 applies when an employee is the victim of a crime at the place of employment, not to every workplace violence incident, and the employee need not be injured. The notice must be written, covers workers' comp eligibility including psychiatric injuries, and goes out personally or by first-class mail within one working day of the crime or of the date the employer reasonably should have known of it. The DWC FAQ agrees: 'If the employee is the victim of a crime that happened at work, you must give notice of workers' compensation eligibility within one working day of the crime.' Added parameters: trigger, notice_form, delivery_methods and clock_starts_from. plain_english was reworded. The verbatim_quote (DIR General-Industry page) is unchanged. The statute text was seen only as leginfo search excerpts, not as the full page. title updated on 2026-11-27 to name the trigger (an employee who is the victim of a crime at work) instead of a workplace violence injury.

rules.plain_english: Cal/OSHA penalties: regulatory and general violations up to $16,285 each; serious violations up to $25,000 (base $18,000); repeat violations multiplied x2/x4/x10 up to $162,851; willful violations multiplied x5 with a minimum of $11,632 and maximum of $162,851.

rules.title: CMMC applies to DoD contracts and subcontracts where you will handle FCI or CUI on your own systems
rules.plain_english: The CMMC program covers every DoD prime contractor and subcontractor that will process, store or transmit Federal Contract Information (FCI) or Controlled Unclassified Information (CUI) on its own unclassified information systems while performing the DoD contract, commercial buys included, but not buys only for commercially available off-the-shelf (COTS) items, and not federal systems a contractor runs on the government's behalf. 32 CFR 170.3(c) words the reach as solicitations and contracts 'valued at greater than the micro-purchase threshold' ($2,000 for Davis-Bacon construction, $15,000 otherwise), but the DFARS clause prescription (204.7504) states no dollar limit, so do not treat a small contract as outside CMMC: if the solicitation includes DFARS 252.204-7021, it applies. During Phases 1-3 the phase rules decide which contracts get it, and DoD may waive it for a procurement in advance; a waiver leaves every other cybersecurity requirement in place.

parameters.contract_value_greater_than: micro-purchase threshold (FAR 2.101), as worded in 32 CFR 170.3(c)
parameters.waiver: in advance of the solicitation at DoD's discretion (170.3(c)(2)); by a Service or Component Acquisition Executive in very limited circumstances (170.5(d))

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and subcontractors at every tier on Department of Defense contracts (e.g., USACE, NAVFAC, Air Force, Army, DLA construction and facility work in California) that will process, store or transmit FCI or CUI on their own unclassified information systems

rules.effective: 2024-12-16 (32 CFR part 170 CMMC Program final rule, 89 FR 83214, Oct. 15, 2024; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: FAR 2.101 sets the micro-purchase threshold at $15,000, except $2,000 for construction subject to 40 U.S.C. chapter 31, subchapter IV (Davis-Bacon). DFARS 204.7504, which prescribes the clause, does not restate a dollar threshold; the micro-purchase limit comes from 32 CFR 170.3(c). 170.5(d): with a waiver, contractors 'will remain obligated to comply with all applicable cybersecurity and information security requirements' (e.g., FAR 52.204-21, DFARS 252.204-7012).
rules.correction: The quote and every parameter are confirmed. In 170.3(c) the phrase 'valued at greater than the micro-purchase threshold' follows 'including those for the acquisition of commercial items (except those exclusively for COTS items)', so it can be read as limiting only the commercial-item clause or the whole sentence, and DFARS 204.7504 (the operative clause prescription, re-read) states no dollar threshold. The original plain_english presented the micro-purchase limit as a settled exclusion. plain_english was rewritten to say the limit is worded in 32 CFR 170.3(c) but is not restated in the DFARS prescription and should not be relied on to exclude a contract that carries 252.204-7021; parameters micro_purchase_wording_ambiguous, dfars_prescription_states_dollar_threshold and rely_on_threshold_to_exclude were added. rules.title: CMMC phase-in: Phase 1 from Nov. 10, 2025, Phase 2 from Nov. 10, 2026, Phase 3 from Nov. 10, 2027, full implementation from Nov. 10, 2028
rules.plain_english: DoD is phasing CMMC into solicitations in four one-year steps. Phase 1 began when the DFARS CMMC acquisition rule took effect on November 10, 2025: DoD intends to require Level 1 (Self) or Level 2 (Self) as a condition of award, and may require Level 2 (C3PAO) instead. Phase 2 (from November 10, 2026) adds Level 2 (C3PAO) as a condition of award for applicable contracts (DoD may delay it to an option period) and may add Level 3 (DIBCAC). Phase 3 (from November 10, 2027): Level 2 (C3PAO) for all applicable contracts at award and for options on contracts awarded after the effective date, and Level 3 (DIBCAC) for all applicable contracts. Phase 4 (from November 10, 2028): CMMC in all applicable DoD solicitations and contracts, including option periods on contracts awarded earlier. These are DoD's stated intentions; the level written into your solicitation is the one that binds you.

rules.title: Until Nov. 9, 2028 the CMMC clause goes in only when the program office sets a level; from Nov. 10, 2028 whenever contractor systems will handle FCI or CUI
rules.plain_english: The DFARS CMMC clause (252.204-7021) and its solicitation notice (252.204-7025) go into DoD solicitations, contracts and orders, commercial buys included and COTS-only buys excluded. Until November 9, 2028 they are used only when the program office or requiring activity decides the contractor must have a specific CMMC level. On or after November 10, 2028 they are used whenever the contractor must use its own information systems to process, store or transmit FCI or CUI. rules.title: CMMC Level 1 = the 15 basic safeguarding requirements of FAR 52.204-21(b)(1)
rules.plain_english: Level 1 protects FCI and consists of exactly the 15 basic safeguarding requirements listed in FAR 52.204-21(b)(1)(i)-(xv): access control, identification and authentication, media sanitization, physical protection, boundary protection and system integrity (patching, malware protection and scans). They are self-assessed with the NIST SP 800-171A objectives that 32 CFR 170.15 maps to each one, reading 'FCI' wherever an objective says 'CUI'.

requirements: (i) limit system access to authorized users, processes acting for them, and devices
(ii) limit system access to the transactions and functions authorized users may execute
(iii) verify and control/limit connections to and use of external information systems
(iv) control information posted or processed on publicly accessible systems
(v) identify users, processes acting for users, and devices
(vi) authenticate users, processes or devices before allowing access
(vii) sanitize or destroy media containing FCI before disposal or reuse
(viii) limit physical access to systems, equipment and operating environments to authorized individuals
(ix) escort visitors and monitor visitor activity, keep physical access audit logs, control physical access devices
(x) monitor, control and protect communications at external and key internal boundaries
(xi) put publicly accessible system components on subnetworks separated from internal networks
(xii) identify, report and correct information and system flaws in a timely manner
(xiii) provide protection from malicious code at appropriate locations
(xiv) update malicious code protection when new releases are available
(xv) run periodic system scans and real-time scans of files from external sources

rules.title: Level 2 (Self): self-assess against all 110 requirements every 3 years, post the score in SPRS, affirm yearly
rules.plain_english: For Level 2 (Self) you assess your own CUI systems against all Level 2 requirements with NIST SP 800-171A, score them with the CMMC scoring method and enter the results in SPRS (including the overall score, e.g. 105 out of 110, and any POA&M). A score of 110 gives Final Level 2 (Self); a qualifying POA&M gives Conditional Level 2 (Self). Repeat every three years, have the Affirming Official affirm at each assessment and every year, and keep the evidence for 6 years. Level 2 (Self) also satisfies Level 1 (Self) for the same scope. DoD may still audit you (DCMA DIBCAC), and those results override your self-assessment.

sprs_inputs: all industry CAGE codes in the assessment scope
overall Level 2 self-assessment score (e.g., 105 out of 110)
POA&M usage and compliance status, if applicable
parameters.affirmation: at each assessment and annually thereafter

rules.title: Level 2 (C3PAO): certification assessment by an authorized C3PAO every 3 years; results go to eMASS and SPRS
rules.plain_english: When the solicitation requires Level 2 (C3PAO), an authorized or accredited CMMC Third-Party Assessment Organization must assess your CUI systems against all Level 2 requirements; the C3PAO enters the results in the CMMC instance of eMASS, which feeds SPRS. A NOT MET item can be re-evaluated during the assessment and for 10 business days after it (before the findings report is delivered). Hash your evidence files with a NIST-approved algorithm and keep them 6 years. Repeat every three years and affirm at each assessment and every year. Level 2 (C3PAO) also satisfies Level 1 (Self) and Level 2 (Self).

rules.title: Conditional status: a POA&M is allowed only at Levels 2 and 3, with a score of at least 80%, closed out within 180 days
rules.plain_english: A plan of action and milestones (POA&M) is never allowed at Level 1. At Level 2 you can get a Conditional status only if your score divided by 110 is at least 0.8 (a score of 88 or more), every POA&M item is worth 1 point (except SC.L2-3.13.11 encryption that is not FIPS-validated, worth 3), and none of six listed requirements (external connections, public information, the system security plan, visitor escort, physical access logs, physical access devices) is on the POA&M. At Level 3 the score must be at least 80% of the 24 requirements (20 or more) and seven listed requirements may not be on the POA&M. All NOT MET items must be fixed and confirmed by a closeout assessment within 180 days of the Conditional CMMC Status Date, or the status expires; then contract remedies apply and you cannot win new awards at that level until you get a new status.

parameters.level_2_poam_point_exception: SC.L2-3.13.11 CUI Encryption (3 points) if encryption is employed but not FIPS-validated
parameters.on_expiry: Conditional status expires; standard contractual remedies; ineligible for additional awards at that level for the system until a new CMMC Status is achieved
parameters.award_with_conditional: allowed for Levels 2 and 3; Level 1 requires a Final status (DFARS 204.7502(b)(2))

rules.effective: 2024-12-16 (32 CFR part 170 CMMC Program final rule, 89 FR 83214, Oct. 15, 2024; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: 88 and 20 are derived: 0.8 x 110 = 88 (Level 2 maximum score 110, see cmmc-level2-nist-800-171-r2-110) and 0.8 x 24 = 19.2, so the lowest whole Level 3 score that qualifies is 20 (Level 3 scores 1 point per requirement, 170.24(c)(3)). The CMMC Status Date stays the Conditional date after a successful closeout (170.4, 'CMMC Status Date').

rules.title: Level 2 scoring: start at 110 and subtract 5, 3 or 1 point for each requirement NOT MET; the score can go negative
rules.plain_english: A Level 2 assessment starts at the maximum score (the number of Level 2 requirements, 110) and subtracts each NOT MET requirement's value: 5 points for requirements whose absence could lead to significant exploitation or CUI exfiltration, 3 for a specific and confined effect, 1 for a limited or indirect effect. Multi-factor authentication only for remote and privileged users costs 3 instead of 5; encryption that is not FIPS-validated costs 3 instead of 5. The score can be negative. A requirement that does not apply (N/A) counts as MET. Without an up-to-date system security plan the assessment cannot be completed. At Level 3 each requirement is worth 1 point.

rules.title: A senior Affirming Official must affirm continuing compliance in SPRS after every assessment and every year
rules.plain_english: Each organization assessed, prime or subcontractor, names an Affirming Official: a senior person responsible for CMMC compliance with authority to affirm it. That person enters an affirmation in SPRS (name, title, contact information and a statement that all applicable requirements are implemented and will be maintained) when a Conditional or Final status is reached, after a POA&M closeout, and every year after the Final status date. An affirmation older than one year is not current. Level 3 holders also affirm their Level 2 (C3PAO) status every year.

The prime must comply, require its subcontractors to comply and make them flow the requirement down. A subcontractor that handles only FCI needs Level 1 (Self). One that handles CUI needs at least Level 2 (Self); if the prime contract requires Level 2 (C3PAO) or Level 3 (DIBCAC), the CUI subcontractor needs at least Level 2 (C3PAO). DoD may give contract-specific flowdown guidance.

rules.title: Level 1 scope: every system that processes, stores or transmits FCI; IoT, OT and other specialized assets are outside Level 1 scope
rules.plain_english: Before a Level 1 self-assessment you must define the assessment scope: every information system that processes, stores or transmits FCI is in scope; systems that do not are out of scope and need no documentation. Specialized assets that can handle FCI but cannot be fully secured (IoT and industrial IoT devices, operational technology, government-furnished equipment, restricted information systems, test equipment) are not part of the Level 1 scope. Consider the people, technology, facilities and outside service providers that handle FCI.

rules.title: Cloud services holding CUI must be FedRAMP Moderate (or higher) authorized or FedRAMP Moderate equivalent

Your on-premises systems that connect to it stay in your assessment scope, and the provider's customer responsibility matrix must be documented in your system security plan. Outside IT providers that are not cloud providers are assessed as part of your scope. DFARS 252.204-7012 separately requires any cloud provider holding covered defense information to meet FedRAMP Moderate-equivalent requirements and the clause's incident-reporting, malware, media and forensics paragraphs.

The clause flows down (without the UID-reporting paragraph (e)(1)) to every subcontract that will involve FCI or CUI, commercial ones included, COTS excluded.

rules.plain_english: A CMMC status counts as current only if nothing has changed in your compliance since the status date and your affirmation is current: a Conditional Level 2 or Level 3 status for no more than 180 days, a Final Level 1 (Self) for no more than one year, and a Final Level 2 or Level 3 status for no more than three years, each with an affirmation of continuous compliance no older than one year.

rules.title: CMMC Status Date: the date results go into SPRS or eMASS; a Final status that follows a Conditional keeps the Conditional's date, so the 3-year reassessment counts from it
rules.plain_english: Your CMMC Status Date is the date your assessment results were submitted to SPRS (self-assessments) or to the CMMC instance of eMASS (C3PAO and DIBCAC assessments). If you first got a Conditional status and then closed out the POA&M, the Final status keeps the Conditional's date: no new date is set. The 3-year Level 2 reassessment, the 3-year Level 3 reassessment (counted from the Conditional Level 3 date when there was a POA&M), the 6-year evidence retention and the yearly affirmation after a Final status all run from that date, so use the Conditional date, not the closeout date, when you calendar them.

rules.title: DFARS 252.204-7012: protect covered defense information with NIST SP 800-171; cloud providers must meet FedRAMP Moderate equivalent
rules.plain_english: DFARS 252.204-7012 is in nearly every DoD solicitation and contract (all but COTS-only buys). On your own systems that hold covered defense information you must provide adequate security, at a minimum the NIST SP 800-171 requirements in effect when the solicitation was issued (or as the contracting officer authorizes). Requests to vary from a requirement go in writing to the contracting officer for the DoD CIO to decide. A cloud provider that holds covered defense information must meet FedRAMP Moderate-equivalent requirements and the clause's incident reporting, malware, media and forensic-access paragraphs. CMMC does not replace this clause.

rules.title: Report cyber incidents affecting covered defense information to DoD at dibnet.dod.mil within 72 hours of discovery
rules.plain_english: When you discover a cyber incident that affects a system holding covered defense information (or the information on it), or your ability to perform operationally critical support, review your systems for evidence of compromise and report the incident to DoD at https://dibnet.dod.mil within 72 hours of discovery. You need a DoD-approved medium assurance certificate to file. Subcontractors report directly to DoD and give the DoD-assigned incident report number to the prime (or next higher-tier subcontractor) as soon as practicable.

Malicious software you isolate goes to the DoD Cyber Crime Center (DC3), not to the contracting officer. Give DoD access for forensic analysis when asked.

rules.plain_english: Put DFARS 252.204-7012 without alteration in every subcontract (commercial ones included) whose performance will involve covered defense information or that is for operationally critical support. The prime decides whether the information it passes down is still covered defense information and consults the contracting officer if necessary. Subcontractors must tell the prime (or next higher tier) when they ask to vary from a NIST SP 800-171 requirement and give it the DoD incident report number after reporting an incident.

rules.plain_english: Covered defense information is unclassified controlled technical information or other CUI-Registry information needing safeguarding or dissemination controls that is either marked or identified in the contract and provided by or for DoD, or collected, developed, received, transmitted, used or stored by or for you in performing the contract. Controlled technical information is technical information with military or space application that would carry distribution statements B through F. A covered contractor information system is any unclassified system you own or operate (or that is operated for you) that handles covered defense information.

rules.title: DFARS 252.204-7019: a NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment no more than 3 years old must be in SPRS to be considered for award
rules.plain_english: If you must implement NIST SP 800-171 (DFARS 252.204-7012), you are considered for award only with a current NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment (no more than 3 years old unless the solicitation sets a shorter time) for each covered system, with its summary score posted in SPRS. If you have none, do a Basic (self) Assessment with the DoD Assessment Methodology and send the summary to webptsmh@navy.mil for posting: the standard assessed, who assessed, the CAGE codes per system security plan, the completion date, the summary score (out of 110) and the date you expect to reach 110. The contracting officer checks SPRS before award and before exercising options.

rules.plain_english: Under DFARS 252.204-7020 you must give the Government access to your facilities, systems and people for a Medium or High NIST SP 800-171 DoD Assessment if needed, and you have 14 business days after an assessment to send more information or rebut findings. Flow the clause to all subcontracts except COTS, and do not award a subcontract that requires NIST SP 800-171 under 252.204-7012 unless the subcontractor has completed at least a Basic Assessment within the last 3 years for its covered systems.

It does not include information the government gives the public (such as on public websites) or simple transactional information such as what is needed to process payments.

rules.title: Controlled Unclassified Information: information a law, regulation or government-wide policy requires or permits to be safeguarded
rules.plain_english: CUI is information the government creates or possesses, or that someone creates or possesses for or on behalf of the government, that a law, regulation or government-wide policy requires or permits an agency to handle with safeguarding or dissemination controls. It is not classified information, and not information a private entity keeps in its own systems that did not come from, or was not created for, an executive branch agency.

You must apply the 15 basic safeguarding requirements to those systems and put the clause in subcontracts where the subcontractor may have FCI on its systems. rules.title: No Kaspersky hardware, software or services for the government or in producing contract deliverables; report within 3 business days
rules.plain_english: Every federal solicitation and contract carries FAR 52.204-23. You may not provide any Kaspersky Lab covered article (anything developed or provided by Kaspersky or its affiliates, or containing their hardware or software) that the government will use, and you may not use one to produce data or deliverables first produced under the contract (both since October 1, 2018). If you identify a covered article provided to the government during performance, or a subcontractor or anyone else tells you of one, report it within 3 business days (DoD contracts: at https://dibnet.dod.mil; others: in writing to the contracting officer) and send mitigation details within 10 business days after that report. Flow the clause to all subcontracts.

rules.title: Section 889: no Huawei, ZTE, Hytera, Hikvision or Dahua telecom or video surveillance equipment as a substantial or essential component of what you provide the government or of any system you use; report within 1 business day
rules.plain_english: Every federal solicitation and contract carries FAR 52.204-25. Since August 13, 2019 you may not provide the government any equipment, system or service that uses covered telecommunications equipment or services (Huawei or ZTE telecom equipment; Hytera, Hikvision or Dahua video surveillance and telecom equipment for public safety, government facility security, critical infrastructure surveillance and other national security purposes; their subsidiaries and affiliates; services using that equipment; or entities DoD designates) as a substantial or essential component of any system or as critical technology. Since August 13, 2020 the government may not contract with a company that uses any equipment, system or service that uses covered equipment or services that way, even in work that has nothing to do with the federal contract. Backhaul, roaming and interconnection services and equipment that cannot route or see user data are excepted. If during performance you identify covered equipment or services used as a substantial or essential component of any system (or a subcontractor tells you), report within 1 business day (DoD: https://dibnet.dod.mil; others: the contracting officer) and follow up within 10 business days. Flow the clause to all subcontracts, but without the company-wide 'use' prohibition of paragraph (b)(2).

rules.citation: 40 U.S.C. 3142(a) (as implemented); 29 CFR 5.5(a); 29 CFR 5.2 (Contract); FAR 22.403-1; FAR 1.109(c)(1)(ii); FAR 2.101 (Micro-purchase threshold (1))
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a) introductory text); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-22.403-1; https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-1.109 (paragraph (c)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: in any contract in excess of $2,000 which is entered into for the actual construction, alteration and/or repair, including painting and decorating, of a public building or public work, or building or work financed in whole or in part from Federal funds
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: FAR 1.109(c) says 41 U.S.C. 1908 inflation escalation does not apply to thresholds in 40 U.S.C. chapter 31 subchapter IV (Wage Rate Requirements (Construction)), so the $2,000 stays fixed. 29 CFR 5.2 defines "contract" to include any subcontract of any tier under a covered prime contract. The statute itself (uscode.house.gov) could not be fetched; the threshold is read from 29 CFR 5.5(a) and FAR 22.403-1, which restate it.

rules.title: Pay every laborer and mechanic on site at least the wage determination rate, at least weekly
rules.plain_english: Everyone doing manual or trade work on the site must be paid at least once a week the full basic hourly rate plus fringe benefits (or the same amount in cash) shown in the wage determination for the work they actually do. Their label (employee, owner-operator, "independent contractor") does not matter. Only deductions allowed by the Copeland Act rules may be taken.

parameters.minimum_hourly_pay: wage determination basic hourly rate + fringe benefit rate (or cash equivalent) for each classification actually worked

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a)(1)(i)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: All laborers and mechanics employed or working upon the site of the work (or otherwise working in construction or development of the project under a development statute), will be paid unconditionally and not less often than once a week, and without subsequent deduction or rebate on any account (except such payroll deductions as are permitted by regulations issued by the Secretary of Labor under the Copeland Act (29 CFR part 3)), the full amount of basic hourly wages and bona fide fringe benefits (or cash equivalents thereof) due at time of payment computed at rates not less than those contained in the wage determination of the Secretary of Labor which is attached hereto and made a part hereof, regardless of any contractual relationship which may be alleged to exist between the contractor and such laborers and mechanics.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: Direct federal (FAR) contracts use FAR 52.222-6 (AUG 2018), which has the same weekly-pay rule. California public works law (Labor Code 1771 et seq.) still applies on top when a California awarding body controls the project (see fed-ca-dual-coverage-pay-higher).

rules.title: Post the wage determination and the Davis-Bacon poster (WH-1321) on site
rules.plain_english: Keep the wage determination (including any added classifications) and the federal Davis-Bacon poster WH-1321 posted at the job site the whole time, somewhere workers can easily see them. Each subcontractor must post too.

documents: applicable wage determination(s) incl. conformed classifications
parameters.where: site of the work, prominent and accessible place

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a)(1)(i), last sentence) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The wage determination (including any additional classifications and wage rates conformed under paragraph (a)(1)(iii) of this section) and the Davis-Bacon poster (WH-1321) must be posted at all times by the contractor and its subcontractors at the site of the work in a prominent and accessible place where it can be easily seen by the workers.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: On California public works also post the DIR job site notice and state prevailing wage rates (separate state rules already in the rulebook).

rules.title: Workers in more than one trade may be paid each trade's rate only if payroll shows hours in each
rules.plain_english: If a worker does work in two or more classifications (for example laborer and operator), you may pay the rate for each classification for the hours spent in it, but only if your payroll records accurately show the time in each one. Otherwise expect to owe the highest rate for all hours.

parameters.condition: payroll records accurately set forth time spent in each classification

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a)(1)(i)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: Laborers or mechanics performing work in more than one classification may be compensated at the rate specified for each classification for the time actually worked therein: Provided, That the employer's payroll records accurately set forth the time spent in each classification in which work is performed.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: The "highest rate for all hours" consequence is the practical result of not meeting the stated condition; the regulation states only the condition.

rules.title: Missing trade on the wage determination: request a conformed rate; DOL answers in 30 days
rules.plain_english: If you will use a type of worker that is not listed on the wage determination, the contracting officer must get an added ("conformed") classification and rate. DOL approves, changes or rejects it within 30 days of receipt (or says it needs more time). Once set, the rate must be paid back to the first day anyone worked in that classification, and you must give each affected worker a written copy or post it with the wage determination.

parameters.retroactive_to: first day work performed in the classification
criteria: work not performed by a listed classification
classification used in the area by the construction industry
rate bears a reasonable relationship to wage determination rates
parameters.worker_notice: written copy to each affected worker or post with the wage determination

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a)(1)(iii)(A)-(E)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The Administrator, or an authorized representative, will approve, modify, or disapprove every additional classification action within 30 days of receipt
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: The contracting officer, not the contractor, files the request with DOL. Conformance may not be used to split or subdivide classifications already listed.

rules.title: Davis-Bacon clauses and the correct wage determination apply even if left out of the contract
rules.plain_english: If the agency forgot to put the Davis-Bacon clauses or the right wage determination in your contract, they still apply automatically ("by operation of law"), back to the start. The agency must add them (within 30 days if DOL asks), and the prime contractor must be compensated for any resulting wage increase.

parameters.retroactive_to: contract award or start of construction

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (e)); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.6 (paragraph (a)(1)(ii)(B)-(F)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The contract clauses set forth in this section (or their equivalent under the Federal Acquisition Regulation), along with the correct wage determinations, will be considered to be a part of every prime contract required by the applicable statutes referenced by § 5.1 to include such clauses, and will be effective by operation of law, whether or not they are included or incorporated by reference into such contract, unless the Administrator grants a variance, tolerance, or exemption from the application of this paragraph. Where the clauses and applicable wage determinations are effective by operation of law under this paragraph, the prime contractor must be compensated for any resulting increase in wages in accordance with applicable law.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: New in the 2023 rule. A subcontractor bidding a federal-aid job should price Davis-Bacon even if the subcontract form omits it.

rules.title: Back wages owed under Davis-Bacon carry interest (IRS underpayment rate, compounded daily)
rules.plain_english: If any prevailing wages are underpaid, the contractor must also pay interest from the date of the underpayment. The interest rate is the IRS rate for underpaid taxes (26 U.S.C. 6621), compounded daily.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.10 (paragraph (a)); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a)(1)(vi)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: Interest on any back wages or monetary relief provided for in this part will be calculated using the percentage established for the underpayment of taxes under 26 U.S.C. 6621 and will be compounded daily.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: The current 26 U.S.C. 6621 quarterly rate is published by the IRS (not fetched here); a calculator should take it as an input.

rules.title: Agency can withhold your payments, including on your other federal jobs, to cover unpaid wages
rules.plain_english: If you or any subcontractor underpay prevailing wages, the agency (or the city/Caltrans paying with federal money) may, and must if DOL asks in writing, hold back enough of your contract payments to cover the wages, interest and relief. It can also hold money on any other federal or federally assisted contract held by the same prime contractor, even with a different agency. Failing to pay or to submit payroll records can stop all further payments after written notice.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a)(2)(i)); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.9 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The necessary funds may be withheld from the contractor under this contract, any other Federal contract with the same prime contractor, or any other federally assisted contract that is subject to Davis-Bacon labor standards requirements and is held by the same prime contractor, regardless of whether the other contract was awarded or assisted by the same agency, and such funds may be used to satisfy the contractor liability for which the funds were withheld.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: "Prime contractor" includes controlling shareholders/members, joint venturers and a delegated general contractor (29 CFR 5.2). Cross-withholding from a different legal entity requires that entity's contract to contain the withholding clause in full or by reference (29 CFR 5.9(c)).

rules.title: Withheld wage money goes to workers first, ahead of sureties, banks and bankruptcy trustees
rules.plain_english: Money the agency holds back for Davis-Bacon or CWHSSA violations belongs first to the Department of Labor (for the workers). It comes ahead of claims by your payment or performance bond surety, the agency's reprocurement costs, a bankruptcy trustee, assignees such as lenders, successors, and Prompt Payment Act claims.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California); their sureties and lenders
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a)(2)(ii)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The Department has priority to funds withheld or to be withheld in accordance with paragraph (a)(2)(i) or (b)(3)(i) of this section, or both, over claims to those funds by:
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: New in the 2023 rule. Relevant to assignment-of-proceeds financing and surety takeover on federal jobs.

rules.title: Keep payroll and basic records for 3 years after the whole prime contract is finished
rules.plain_english: Every contractor and subcontractor must keep payrolls and basic records for each worker on site during the job and for at least 3 years after all work on the prime contract is completed. Records must show name, Social Security number, last known address, phone and email, classification(s) actually worked, hourly wage and fringe rates, daily and weekly hours (total and on each covered contract), deductions and actual wages paid.

required_fields: fringe benefit contribution/cost rates or cash equivalents
daily and weekly hours worked in total and on each covered contract
parameters.extra_if_unfunded_plan: proof plan is enforceable, financially responsible, communicated in writing, and its costs
parameters.extra_if_apprentices: written evidence of program and apprentice registration, ratios and wage rates

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a)(3)(i)(A)-(D)); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-3.4 (paragraph (b)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: All regular payrolls and other basic records must be maintained by the contractor and any subcontractor during the course of the work and preserved for all laborers and mechanics working at the site of the work (or otherwise working in construction or development of the project under a development statute) for a period of at least 3 years after all the work on the prime contract is completed.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: Telephone number, email address and "hours on each covered contract" were added by the 2023 rule; FAR 52.222-8 (JUL 2021) on direct federal contracts still lists name, address and SSN. The 3-year clock runs from completion of the whole prime contract, not the subcontract.

rules.title: Submit certified payroll every week work is performed; prime is responsible for subs' payrolls
rules.plain_english: For each week in which any Davis-Bacon work is done, each contractor and subcontractor must submit a certified payroll to the federal agency (or, on federal-aid jobs, to the city, county or Caltrans that holds the records). The prime contractor is responsible for getting every subcontractor's certified payrolls in. Electronic systems are allowed if they use a legally valid e-signature, keep the payrolls accessible for 3 years, and offer another way to submit for contractors who cannot use them.

parameters.frequency: weekly, for each week any covered work is performed
parameters.submit_to: federal agency if party to contract; otherwise applicant/sponsor/owner (e.g., local agency or Caltrans) for transmission to the agency
electronic_system_conditions: contractor, agency and DOL can access for at least 3 years after prime contract work completed
alternative submission method allowed for contractors unable to use it

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a)(3)(ii)(A)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The contractor or subcontractor must submit weekly, for each week in which any DBA- or Related Acts-covered work is performed, certified payrolls
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: Federal weekly certified payroll is separate from California DIR eCPR (see fed-ca-dual-reporting). Copeland Act timing: within 7 days after the regular pay date (fed-copeland-submit-7-days).

rules.title: Weekly certified payroll: same data as your records but only the last 4 of the SSN; WH-347 is optional
rules.plain_english: The weekly certified payroll must contain everything in your payroll records except full Social Security numbers, home addresses, phone numbers and emails, which must not be on the weekly copies. Use an identifying number such as the last four SSN digits. You may use DOL Optional Form WH-347 or any other format. A prime may require subs to give it full SSNs and addresses for its own files.

parameters.worker_identifier: individually identifying number, e.g., last 4 digits of SSN
parameters.form: Optional Form WH-347 or any format with the required information

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a)(3)(ii)(B)); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-3.3 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: except that full Social Security numbers and last known addresses, telephone numbers, and email addresses must not be included on weekly transmittals.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: The WH-347 URL above is the one named in 29 CFR 3.3(b); dol.gov could not be fetched to confirm the current form edition.

rules.title: Each weekly payroll needs a signed Statement of Compliance (back of WH-347)
rules.plain_english: Every weekly certified payroll must come with a signed "Statement of Compliance" certifying that (1) the payroll is complete and correct and records are kept, (2) every worker got full weekly wages with no kickbacks and only allowed deductions, and (3) every worker got at least the wage determination rate and fringes for the work done. The signature on the back of WH-347 (or identical wording) satisfies this. Sign by hand or with a legally valid electronic signature.

certifications: payroll contains required information; records maintained; correct and complete
full weekly wages paid without rebate; only 29 CFR part 3 deductions
not less than wage determination rates and fringe benefits for classifications actually worked
parameters.signer: contractor/subcontractor or agent who pays or supervises payment
parameters.signature: original handwritten or legally valid electronic
parameters.satisfied_by: certification on reverse of Optional Form WH-347 or any form with identical wording

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a)(3)(ii)(C)-(E)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: Each certified payroll submitted must be accompanied by a “Statement of Compliance,” signed by the contractor or subcontractor
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)

rules.title: False certified payroll: civil and criminal prosecution (18 U.S.C. 1001, False Claims Act)
rules.plain_english: Signing a false Statement of Compliance or certified payroll can lead to criminal prosecution for false statements and civil False Claims Act liability.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a)(3)(ii)(F)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The falsification of any of the above certifications may subject the contractor or subcontractor to civil or criminal prosecution under 18 U.S.C. 1001 and 31 U.S.C. 3729.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: Penalty amounts under those statutes were not researched here (uscode.house.gov blocked).

rules.title: Keep the contract, bids, proposals and change orders for 3 years after the prime contract is done
rules.plain_english: Contractors and subcontractors must keep their contract or subcontract and related documents (bids, proposals, amendments, modifications, extensions) during the job and for 3 years after all work on the prime contract is completed. Certified payrolls must also be kept for that 3 years.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a)(3)(iii)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The contractor or subcontractor must maintain this contract or subcontract and related documents including, without limitation, bids, proposals, amendments, modifications, and extensions.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: New in the 2023 rule.

rules.title: Give agency/DOL access to records and let them interview workers on the job; refusal can stop payments
rules.plain_english: You must let the agency and DOL inspect and copy your payroll records and other documents, and interview workers during working hours on the job. If you do not, the agency can suspend payments after written notice, DOL can seek debarment, and records you did not produce in time cannot be used later as evidence in a DOL hearing. You must also keep full SSNs, addresses, phones and emails and hand them over on request.

access_required: worker interviews during working hours on the job
sanctions: suspension of payments after written notice
records not produced on time excluded as evidence in 29 CFR part 6 proceedings

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a)(3)(iv)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: any contractor or other person that fails to submit the required records or make those records available to WHD within the time WHD requests that the records be produced will be precluded from introducing as evidence
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: WHD may grant a reasonable extension request (29 CFR 5.5(a)(3)(iv)(B)).

rules.title: No federal payment after construction starts unless a compliance certification is on file
rules.plain_english: After construction begins, the federal agency may not approve any payment, advance, grant or loan for the project unless the contractor has filed a certification that it and its subcontractors complied with the Davis-Bacon clauses (or that there is a substantial dispute about them). Expect pay applications on federal-aid work to require this.

parameters.trigger: any payment, advance, grant, loan or guarantee approved after beginning of construction
parameters.certification: contractor and subcontractors complied with 29 CFR 5.5 clauses, or a substantial dispute exists

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.6 (paragraph (a)(1)(i)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: no payment, advance, grant, loan, or guarantee of funds will be approved by the Federal agency after the beginning of construction unless there is on file with the Federal agency a certification by the contractor
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: This is an agency obligation that flows to the contractor through pay-application requirements.

rules.title: Apprentice rates only for workers individually registered in a DOL- or state-registered program
rules.plain_english: You may pay less than the journeyworker rate only to apprentices individually registered in a program registered with DOL's Office of Apprenticeship or a recognized State Apprenticeship Agency (in California, DAS). A worker certified as eligible for probationary apprenticeship may be paid the apprentice rate for the first 90 days. Anyone else listed at an apprentice rate must be paid the full rate for the work done. If the program loses approval, apprentice rates stop.

registration_with: State Apprenticeship Agency recognized by OA
parameters.unregistered_worker_pay: full wage determination rate for classification actually performed

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a)(4)(i)(A)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: will be permitted to work at less than the predetermined rate for the work they perform in the first 90 days of probationary employment as an apprentice in such a program.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: Trainees on federal-aid highway projects in programs certified under 23 U.S.C. 113(c) are treated separately (29 CFR 5.2, Apprentice (2)). California DAS is the State Apprenticeship Agency; recognition status was not separately verified here.

rules.title: Apprentice fringe benefits: per the program, or the full wage determination fringe if the program is silent
rules.plain_english: Pay apprentices the fringe benefits their registered program specifies. If the program does not specify fringes, pay the full fringe amount listed on the wage determination for that classification.

parameters.rule: program-specified fringe; if none specified, 100% of wage determination fringe for the classification

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a)(4)(i)(B)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: If the apprenticeship program does not specify fringe benefits, apprentices must be paid the full amount of fringe benefits listed on the wage determination for the applicable classification.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)

rules.title: Apprentice ratio: follow the ratio where the work is done; extra apprentices get journeyworker pay
rules.plain_english: The number of apprentices per journeyworker on the job site in each craft cannot exceed the ratio allowed. When working outside the area where your program is registered, use the ratio and apprentice wage percentages that apply where the work is done (if any). Every apprentice over the ratio must be paid the full journeyworker rate for the work performed.

parameters.ratio_source: locality of the project if one applies, otherwise contractor's registered program
parameters.over_ratio_pay: full wage determination rate for work actually performed

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a)(4)(i)(C)-(D)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: Where a contractor is performing construction on a project in a locality other than the locality in which its program is registered, the ratios and wage rates (expressed in percentages of the journeyworker's hourly rate) applicable within the locality in which the construction is being performed must be observed.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: Locality reciprocity was added by the 2023 rule. California state apprenticeship ratio rules (Labor Code 1777.5) apply separately on state-covered public works.

rules.title: Put the Davis-Bacon clauses and wage determination in every subcontract; prime pays lower-tier back wages
rules.plain_english: Every subcontract (at every tier) must include the Davis-Bacon clauses in 29 CFR 5.5(a)(1)-(11), the wage determination(s), and a clause requiring the sub to pass them down. The prime contractor is responsible for every lower-tier sub's compliance and, with the responsible sub, owes any unpaid wages and interest of lower-tier workers.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a)(6)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: In the event of any violations of these clauses, the prime contractor and any subcontractor(s) responsible will be liable for any unpaid wages and monetary relief, including interest from the date of the underpayment or loss, due to any workers of lower-tier subcontractors, and may be subject to debarment, as appropriate.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: Incorporation by reference is given the same effect as full text (29 CFR 5.5(d)).

rules.title: Direct federal jobs: deliver SF 1413 for each construction subcontract within 14 days
rules.plain_english: On direct federal construction contracts, within 14 days after award the prime must give the contracting officer a completed Standard Form 1413 (Statement and Acknowledgment) for each construction subcontract, signed by the sub acknowledging the labor clauses are in its subcontract. For any subcontract awarded later, deliver an updated SF 1413 within 14 days of that award.

parameters.contents: subcontractor signed and dated acknowledgment that FAR 52.222-11(b) clauses are included

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors on direct federal (FAR) construction contracts performed in the United States
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-52.222-11 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: (d)(1) Within 14 days after award of the contract, the Contractor shall deliver to the Contracting Officer a completed Standard Form (SF) 1413, Statement and Acknowledgment, for each subcontract for construction within the United States
rules.notes: Federal-aid (grant-funded) projects usually use the agency's own subcontract forms instead; check the contract.

rules.title: Disregarding worker obligations: 3-year debarment from all federal and Davis-Bacon work
rules.plain_english: A contractor or sub found to have disregarded its obligations to workers or subcontractors, plus its responsible officers and firms they have an interest in, is barred for 3 years from any federal contract or subcontract and any Davis-Bacon-covered contract. Names are published on SAM.gov.

parameters.standard: disregarded obligations to workers or subcontractors
covers: firms in which they have an interest

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.12 (paragraph (a)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: will be ineligible for a period of 3 years to be awarded any contract or subcontract of the United States or the District of Columbia and any contract or subcontract subject to the labor standards provisions of any of the statutes referenced by § 5.1.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: The 2023 rule applies the single "disregard of obligations" standard to Related Acts too. Breach of the 5.5 clauses can also be grounds for contract termination (5.5(a)(7)).

rules.title: By signing you certify you are not debarred; never subcontract to a debarred firm
