rules.plain_english: Signing a Davis-Bacon contract certifies that neither you nor anyone with an interest in your firm is debarred under 40 U.S.C. 3144(b) or 29 CFR 5.12. No part of the work may be subcontracted to a debarred person or firm. False statements are punishable under 18 U.S.C. 1001.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a)(10)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: No part of this contract shall be subcontracted to any person or firm ineligible for award of a Government contract by virtue of 40 U.S.C. 3144(b) or § 5.12(a).
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)

rules.title: No retaliation against workers who raise Davis-Bacon or CWHSSA issues
rules.plain_english: It is illegal to fire, demote, threaten, blacklist or otherwise punish any worker or job applicant for reporting a suspected violation to the contractor, filing a complaint, cooperating with an investigation, or telling others about their rights. DOL can order reinstatement, back pay with interest, compensatory damages, a neutral reference and a posted notice.

protected_activities: notifying any contractor of a reasonably believed violation
cooperating in an investigation or testifying

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a)(11)); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.18 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: It is unlawful for any person to discharge, demote, intimidate, threaten, restrain, coerce, blacklist, harass, or in any other manner discriminate against, or to cause any person to discharge, demote, intimidate, threaten, restrain, coerce, blacklist, harass, or in any other manner discriminate against, any worker or job applicant for:
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: New contract clause in the 2023 rule.

rules.title: Contest DOL back-wage findings within 30 days or they become final
rules.plain_english: When DOL sends investigation findings (back wages, classification, overtime, retaliation relief), you have 30 days from the date of the notice to request a hearing (stating which findings you dispute and why) or, where only legal issues are involved, to dispute the facts; a petition to the Administrative Review Board on a legal ruling is also due within 30 days. Miss the deadline and the findings become final. Labor-standards disputes do not go through the contract's normal disputes clause.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.11; https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.12 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: A contractor or subcontractor desiring a hearing concerning the Administrator's investigation findings must request such a hearing by letter or by any other means normally assuring delivery, sent within 30 days of the date of the Administrator's notification.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: A firm found to have an "interest" in a debarred firm has 20 days to request a hearing (29 CFR 5.12(c)(2)(iv)(B)).

rules.title: Underpayments of $1,000 or more trigger a formal enforcement report to the agency
rules.plain_english: If an investigation finds underpayments totaling $1,000 or more, reason to believe the contractor disregarded its obligations, or CWHSSA liquidated damages, DOL sends the agency a detailed enforcement report (and agencies must send DOL a report within 60 days of finishing their own investigation). Smaller, corrected underpayments can be closed without a report.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.6 (paragraph (b)(4)); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.7 (paragraph (a)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: Where the underpayments disclosed by such an investigation or other compliance action total $1,000 or more
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)

rules.title: Who is covered: manual and trade workers, plus working forepersons over 20% of the week
rules.plain_english: Davis-Bacon covers workers whose duties are manual or physical, including apprentices and helpers (and guards on CWHSSA contracts). Bona fide executive, administrative or professional employees are not covered. A foreperson who spends more than 20% of a workweek doing laborer or mechanic work is covered for that time.

parameters.excluded: bona fide executive, administrative or professional employees under 29 CFR part 541

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.2 (definition of Laborer or mechanic) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: Forepersons who devote more than 20 percent of their time during a workweek to mechanic or laborer duties, and who do not meet the criteria of part 541, are laborers and mechanics for the time so spent.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)

rules.title: Site of the work includes dedicated nearby yards, batch plants and flagging locations
rules.plain_english: Prevailing wages are owed for work at the "site of the work": where the project will remain; secondary sites where a significant portion (whole modules or rooms) is built specifically for the project; and adjacent or virtually adjacent job headquarters, tool yards, batch plants and borrow pits dedicated (exclusively or nearly so) to the project, plus nearby traffic-control locations. Your permanent shop or yard that runs regardless of this contract is not the site.

includes: secondary construction site(s) building a significant portion for the project
adjacent/virtually adjacent dedicated support sites (job HQ, tool yards, batch plants, borrow pits)
adjacent locations where workers direct traffic around the primary site
excludes: permanent home offices, branch plants, fabrication plants, tool yards operating regardless of the contract
material supplier facilities established before bid opening and not on the site

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.2 (definition of Site of the work) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: Locations adjacent or virtually adjacent to a primary construction site at which workers perform activities associated with directing vehicular or pedestrian traffic around or away from the primary construction site.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: Flagging/traffic-control locations and secondary modular sites were clarified by the 2023 rule. FAR 52.222-6 (AUG 2018) has an older site-of-work definition for direct federal contracts.

rules.title: Truck drivers: on-site time (not de minimis) and hauling between dedicated sites are covered
rules.plain_english: Hauling materials to or from the site is generally not covered, but these are: transport entirely within the site; hauling significant portions of the work from a secondary site; hauling between a dedicated adjacent support site (e.g., a dedicated batch plant) and the site; and a driver's on-site time loading, unloading or waiting, when that time is more than de minimis.

covered_transportation: entirely within site of the work
significant portions between secondary and primary site
between adjacent dedicated support site and primary/secondary site
driver/assistant onsite loading, unloading, waiting when not de minimis
parameters.not_covered: other transportation of materials or supplies to or from the site

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California); trucking subcontractors
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.2 (definition of Construction, prosecution, completion, or repair) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: but only where the driver or driver's assistant's time spent on the site of the work is not de minimis
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: California's own prevailing wage coverage rules for hauling apply separately on state-covered public works; on dual-coverage jobs follow both.

rules.title: Material suppliers (delivery only, from a pre-existing or non-dedicated plant) are not covered subcontractors
rules.plain_english: A company whose only job is delivering (and picking up) materials, with incidental loading, unloading and waiting, from a facility that is not on the site and either existed before bid opening or is not dedicated to the project, is a material supplier and not a covered subcontractor. If it does any other construction work on site, it is not a material supplier.

conditions_all_required: only obligation is delivery/pickup of materials (incl. incidental loading, unloading, waiting)
manufacturing facility not on primary or secondary site
facility established before bid opening OR not dedicated exclusively/nearly so to the project
parameters.loses_status_if: performs other construction work at the site of the work

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.2 (definition of Material supplier) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: If an entity, in addition to being engaged in the activities specified in paragraph (1)(i) of this definition, also engages in other construction, prosecution, completion, or repair work at the site of the work, it is not a material supplier.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)

rules.title: Demolition and removal is covered when it is itself repair/alteration or new construction is planned
rules.plain_english: Demolition or removal is Davis-Bacon work when it is part of altering a building that stays (e.g., asbestos or paint removal), when hazardous-waste or reclamation work involves substantial earth moving, or when covered construction is planned at the site (now or in a later contract). Plans, federal funding applications, bid solicitations and officials' stated intent show that construction is contemplated.

covered_when: demolition itself is alteration/repair of a building or work that remains
hazardous waste removal/land recycling/reclamation with substantial earth moving
later covered construction contemplated at the site
evidence_construction_contemplated: allocation of or application for Federal funds

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California); demolition and abatement contractors
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.2 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: Where subsequent construction covered in whole or in part by the labor standards in this part is contemplated at the site of the demolition or removal, either as part of the same contract or as part of a future contract.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)

rules.title: Covered "building or work" expressly includes solar panels, wind turbines, broadband and EV chargers
rules.plain_english: The 2023 rule lists solar panels, wind turbines, broadband installation and electric car charger installation as construction ("building or work"), alongside roads, sewers, power lines and buildings. Installing equipment into a building or work can also be covered.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California); solar, EV charger and broadband installers on federally funded work
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.2 (definition of Building or work) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: such as bridges, dams, solar panels, wind turbines, broadband installation, installation of electric car chargers
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)

rules.title: Meet the fringe rate by plan contributions, cash, or a mix (DOL example: $21.93 + $6.27 = $28.60)
rules.plain_english: You meet the wage determination by paying at least the basic hourly rate and making bona fide fringe contributions totaling at least the fringe rate, or by paying the fringe amount in cash on top of the basic rate, or by any mix of cash and fringe contributions that adds up to at least the basic rate plus the fringe rate; the cash part has no separate floor of its own. DOL's own example: basic $21.93 plus fringe $6.27; paying $28.60 an hour all in cash, or partly in cash and partly in fringe contributions totaling $28.60, also complies. For federal overtime, the rate used may not be below the wage determination's basic hourly rate (29 CFR 5.32(a)).

parameters.compliance_test: cash_wage + creditable_fringe_per_hour >= basic_hourly_rate + fringe_rate (29 CFR 5.31(a), (b)(3): cash, bona fide fringe payments, or any combination totaling the wage determination amount)
regulation_examples: 5.31(b)(1): at least $21.93 cash + at least $6.27 fringe contributions
5.31(b)(3): any cash/fringe combination totaling at least $28.60
parameters.overtime_note: the basic rate for federal overtime may not be below the wage determination basic hourly rate (29 CFR 5.32(a))

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.31 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: by paying directly to the laborers a straight time hourly rate of not less than $28.60 ($21.93 basic hourly rate plus $6.27 for fringe benefits)
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: Under Davis-Bacon alone the cash/fringe mix can vary as long as the total is met (29 CFR 5.31(b)(3)); DLSE Public Works Manual 4.2.2.2 likewise says Davis-Bacon does not prohibit crediting employer payments toward the hourly rate. California law does not let employer payments reduce the Basic Hourly Rate (see fed-ca-dual-coverage-basic-rate). The test formula restates 29 CFR 5.31(b)(3).
rules.correction: The DOL example of $21.93 + $6.27 = $28.60 and the three payment methods (29 CFR 5.31(b)(1)-(3)) are confirmed. The derived compliance_test also required cash_wage >= basic_hourly_rate. 5.31(a) and (b)(3) allow the obligation to be met 'by a combination thereof' that totals the wage determination amount, with no separate cash floor, and the rule's own notes said fringe credits can shift against the total. The test was corrected to the total-only test of 5.31(b)(3). The three regulation examples and the 5.32 overtime-base floor were added as separate parameters, and the notes were updated. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction (29 CFR 5.31 and 5.32(a) re-read in the eCFR versioner API, title 29 as of 2026-11-23 on 2026-11-27); no value changed.

rules.title: Fringe contributions must be made at least quarterly to be credited for each week
rules.plain_english: Contributions to benefit plans made for periods longer than a week still count for each payroll week, but only if they are made at least quarterly.

parameters.credit: deemed constructively made during each covered weekly period

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a)(1)(i)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: regular contributions made or costs incurred for more than a weekly period (but not less often than quarterly) under plans, funds, or programs which cover the particular weekly period, are deemed to be constructively made or incurred during such weekly period.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: California has a parallel quarterly rule for state public works (rulebook: employer-payments-quarterly).

rules.title: Annualize fringe credit: divide plan cost by ALL hours worked (public and private)
rules.plain_english: To figure how much fringe credit you get per Davis-Bacon hour, divide the total cost of the benefit for the period by the worker's total hours on all work, private and Davis-Bacon, during that period. Defined contribution pension plans with immediate participation and vesting within the first 500 hours are excepted, as are benefits approved by DOL as not continuous and not covering private work.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.25 (paragraph (c)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: To annualize the cost of providing a fringe benefit, a contractor must divide the total cost of the fringe benefit contribution (or the reasonably anticipated costs of an unfunded benefit plan) by the total number of hours worked on both private (non-DBRA) work and work covered by the Davis-Bacon Act and/or Davis-Bacon Related Acts (DBRA-covered work) during the time period to which the cost is attributable to determine the rate of contribution per hour.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: Annualization was codified by the 2023 rule. California applies annualization too (Labor Code 1773.1; rulebook: employer-payments-annualization), per the DLSE Public Works Manual 4.2.6.

rules.title: Fringe contributions must be irrevocable and paid to an unaffiliated trustee or third party
rules.plain_english: To get credit, plan contributions must be irrevocable, paid to a trustee or third person not affiliated with you, and the plan may not let you take the money back or use it yourself (refunds of genuine overpayments are allowed).

requirements: irrevocable
trustee/third person not affiliated with contractor
trustee meets fiduciary duties
no recapture or diversion by contractor

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.26 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: (2) The trustee or third person may not be affiliated with the contractor or subcontractor;
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)

rules.title: Self-funded (unfunded) benefit plans need written DOL approval before you take credit
rules.plain_english: If you provide benefits from company funds rather than paying a trustee or insurer, you may credit the cost only after you request and receive DOL approval showing the plan is enforceable, financially responsible, actuarially sound and communicated to workers in writing.

criteria: reasonably anticipated to provide the benefits
legally enforceable commitment
financially responsible plan
communicated in writing to workers
approved by the Secretary
submit_to: WHD Division of Government Contracts Enforcement, 200 Constitution Ave. NW, Room S-3502, Washington, DC 20210

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.28 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: (5) The contractor or subcontractor requests and receives approval of the plan or program from the Secretary, as described in paragraph (c) of this section.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: Prior approval requirement made explicit by the 2023 rule.

rules.title: No fringe credit for benefits the law already requires (workers' comp, state-mandated benefits), travel or subsistence
rules.plain_english: You cannot count against the Davis-Bacon fringe rate any benefit you must provide anyway under federal, state or local law, such as workers' compensation insurance. Travel, subsistence and industry-promotion payments normally are not fringe benefits either.

not_creditable: benefits required by other Federal, State or local law

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.29 (paragraph (f)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The act excludes fringe benefits which a contractor or subcontractor is obligated to provide under other Federal, State, or local law. No credit may be taken under the act for the payments made for such benefits.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: Applying this to California's statutory paid sick leave is an inference from the regulation's general rule; the DLSE Public Works Manual (Oct. 2023) 4.2.1 says the same for state public works: no credit for statutory paid sick leave, workers' comp, unemployment, Social Security and Medicare.

rules.title: Credit for apprenticeship program costs: registered programs only, per classification
rules.plain_english: You may count apprenticeship training costs toward the fringe rate only for a registered program, only for amounts reasonably related to the training actually provided, only within the same classification, and annualized over the hours of workers in that classification.

parameters.credit_limited_to: costs reasonably related to apprenticeship benefits actually provided
parameters.annualization_denominator: total hours of laborers/mechanics in the apprentice's classification on covered and non-covered work

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.29 (paragraph (g)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: (3) Costs incurred for the apprenticeship for one classification of laborer or mechanic may not be used to offset costs incurred for another classification.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)

rules.title: Your own benefit-administration costs are not fringe credit; third-party plan administration is
rules.plain_english: Premiums and trust contributions that pay for benefits and their administration by the insurer, trust or third-party administrator can be credited. Your own office costs for handling benefits (claim forms, invoices, tracking contributions, new-hire lists), even if you pay an outside firm to do them, cannot be credited.

parameters.creditable: costs of insurer/trust/TPA directly related to administration and delivery of bona fide benefits
parameters.not_creditable: contractor's own administrative and recordkeeping costs, including fees paid to third parties to perform them

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.33 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: A contractor's own administrative expenses incurred in connection with the provision of fringe benefits are considered business expenses of the firm and are therefore not creditable towards the contractor's prevailing wage obligations
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: New section in the 2023 rule.

rules.title: Overtime is figured on the cash basic rate, never below the wage determination basic rate
rules.plain_english: When federal overtime law applies (FLSA or CWHSSA), fringe contributions and cash paid in place of fringes are left out of the overtime rate, but the rate used for time-and-a-half can never be lower than the basic hourly rate on the wage determination. If you actually pay a higher cash base rate, overtime is computed on that higher rate.

parameters.overtime_base: max(actual basic cash rate, wage determination basic hourly rate)
excluded_from_overtime_base: cash paid in lieu of fringe benefits

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.32 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The contractor's contributions or costs for fringe benefits may be excluded in computing such rate so long as the exclusions do not reduce the regular or basic rate below the basic hourly rate contained in the wage determination.
rules.notes: The example overtime figure is derived (time-and-a-half on the basic rate plus straight-time fringe), not stated in the regulation. California public works overtime is daily (over 8 hours) as well as weekly; on dual-coverage jobs pay whichever is higher.

rules.title: Wage determination changes: 10-day rule before bid opening; 90-day award rule
rules.plain_english: For sealed-bid jobs, a revised general wage determination published at least 10 calendar days before bid opening applies to the contract. If published less than 10 days before, it still applies unless the agency finds there is not enough time to tell bidders. If the contract is not awarded within 90 days after bid opening, any revision issued before award applies unless DOL extends the 90 days. Revisions issued after award generally do not apply.

parameters.issue_date_meaning: date revised general WD is published on the DOL-approved website (SAM.gov), or date agency receives written notice of a revised project WD

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California); estimators bidding federal work
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-1.6 (paragraph (c)(2)(ii)(A), (D)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: a revised wage determination issued at least 10 calendar days before the opening of bids is effective with respect to the solicitation and contract.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: Bidders should recheck the wage determination about 10 days before bid opening and again if award slips past 90 days.

rules.title: Project wage determinations expire after 180 days unless incorporated
rules.plain_english: A project-specific wage determination is good for 180 calendar days from its date. If it is not put into a contract (or construction has not started) in that time, it is void and the agency must get a new one.

parameters.general_wd_expiration: none (valid until revised, superseded or canceled)

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-1.6 (paragraph (a)(3)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: “Project wage determinations” initially issued will be effective for 180 calendar days from the date of such determinations.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)

rules.title: New wage rates apply when the contract adds new work, exercises an option, or (for IDIQ) each anniversary
rules.plain_english: Rate revisions issued after award usually do not apply, but the newest wage determination must be added when the contract is changed to add substantial new work or time, or when an option is exercised. For ongoing contracts not tied to one project (IDIQ, job-order, long-term maintenance with construction), the newest rates must be added on each anniversary of award and apply to work started in the next 12 months.

update_triggers: modification adding substantial out-of-scope construction work
modification adding performance time not originally obligated
each contract award anniversary for IDIQ/JOC/long-term O&M type contracts
parameters.not_triggered_by: extra time to complete original scope or merely incidental work

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California); job order (JOC) and IDIQ contractors
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-1.6 (paragraph (c)(2)(iii)(A)-(C)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: the contracting agency must incorporate into the contract the most recent revision(s) of any applicable wage determination(s) on each anniversary date of the contract's award
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: Annual anniversary updating for IDIQ-type contracts is new in the 2023 rule.

rules.title: Non-union wage determination rates can be bumped by the Employment Cost Index every 3 years
rules.plain_english: DOL may raise older non-collectively-bargained wage and fringe rates on general wage determinations using the BLS Employment Cost Index, but no more often than once every 3 years and not sooner than 3 years after the rate was published.

parameters.applies_to: non-collectively bargained prevailing wage and fringe rates on general wage determinations

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-1.6 (paragraph (c)(1)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: Such rates may be adjusted based on ECI data no more frequently than once every 3 years, and no sooner than 3 years after the date of the rate's publication.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)

rules.title: How DOL sets the prevailing rate: majority, else 30% rule, else weighted average
rules.plain_english: The prevailing wage for a classification is the rate paid to more than half of workers on similar projects in the area. If no rate has a majority, it is the rate paid to the largest group, if that group is at least 30%. If no rate reaches 30%, it is the weighted average.

parameters.step3: weighted average of wages paid in classification

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California); contractors submitting wage surveys
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-1.2 (definition of Prevailing wage) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: If the same wage is not paid to a majority of those employed in the classification, the prevailing wage will be the wage paid to the greatest number, provided that such greatest number constitutes at least 30 percent of those employed; or
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: The 2023 rule restored the 30 percent rule (replacing the 1983 straight-majority test).

rules.title: Challenge a wage determination: ask WHD to reconsider (30-day answer), then appeal to the ARB
rules.plain_english: Any interested party may ask DOL's Wage and Hour Division in writing to reconsider a wage determination or how it was applied. WHD answers within 30 days or says it needs more time. If a WHD representative made the decision, you may ask the WHD Administrator for further reconsideration within 30 days. After reconsideration is denied you may appeal to the Administrative Review Board.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-1.8; https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-1.9 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The Administrator will respond within 30 days of receipt thereof, or will notify the requestor within the 30-day period that additional time is necessary.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)

rules.title: The contractor itself must make sure its pay practices comply
rules.plain_english: The agency picks and attaches the wage determination, but each contractor and subcontractor has its own affirmative duty to make sure it pays according to Davis-Bacon labor standards. Questions about which rates apply go to DOL.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-1.6 (paragraph (b)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The contractor or subcontractor has an affirmative obligation to ensure that its pay practices are in compliance with the Davis-Bacon Act labor standards.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)

rules.title: Copeland Act: deliver each weekly certified payroll within 7 days after payday
rules.plain_english: Each weekly certified payroll with its statement of compliance must be delivered within 7 days after the regular payment date for that payroll period, to the agency's representative at the site or, if none, to the agency by mail or other reliable delivery.

parameters.deliver_to: agency representative at site, else agency contracting for or financing the work

rules.applies_to: Contractors and subcontractors on construction of public buildings/works or work financed in whole or in part by federal loans or grants (Copeland Act)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-3.4 (paragraph (a)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: Each certified payroll required under § 3.3 must be delivered by the contractor or subcontractor, within 7 days after the regular payment date of the payroll period
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: Agencies and primes often set earlier internal deadlines; follow the contract if stricter.

rules.title: Weekly Copeland statements are not required on contracts of $2,000 or less
rules.plain_english: The weekly certified payroll and statement of compliance requirement in 29 CFR 3.3 does not apply to any contract of $2,000 or less.
rules.applies_to: Contractors and subcontractors on construction of public buildings/works or work financed in whole or in part by federal loans or grants (Copeland Act)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-3.3 (paragraph (c)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: (c) The requirements of this section do not apply to any contract of $2,000 or less.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: The anti-kickback prohibition itself still applies.

rules.title: Copeland Act: never make workers give back any part of their pay
rules.plain_english: It is a federal crime to make a worker on a federally financed construction job give back any part of the pay they are entitled to, by force, threats of firing or any other means.

parameters.prohibited: inducing any employee to give up any part of compensation

rules.applies_to: Contractors and subcontractors on construction of public buildings/works or work financed in whole or in part by federal loans or grants (Copeland Act)
rules.citation: FAR 22.403-2; 18 U.S.C. 874; 40 U.S.C. 3145; 2 CFR part 200 Appendix II (D)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-22.403-2 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: makes it unlawful to induce, by force, intimidation, threat of procuring dismissal from employment, or otherwise, any person employed in the construction or repair of public buildings or public works
rules.notes: Criminal penalty amounts were not read (uscode.house.gov blocked).

rules.title: Payroll deductions allowed without DOL approval (taxes, garnishments, voluntary benefit, union dues, etc.)
rules.plain_english: Without DOL approval you may deduct only: taxes and other legally required deductions; repayment of a true cash advance (no interest); court-ordered garnishments (not in your favor); voluntary written-consent or union-contract benefit contributions where you get no profit; credit union payments; voluntary Red Cross or 501(c)(3) charity donations; regular union dues under a CBA; reasonable cost of board/lodging; and nominal-value safety gear the worker chose to buy (at no profit to you). Anything else needs DOL approval or is prohibited.

allowed_without_approval: bona fide prepayment of wages without discount or interest
court process (not in favor of contractor/affiliate)
voluntary/CBA benefit fund contributions with no contractor profit
credit union loan repayment or shares
voluntary contributions to governmental/quasi-governmental agencies (e.g., Red Cross)
regular union initiation fees and dues under CBA (not fines or special assessments)
reasonable cost of board, lodging or facilities (FLSA 3(m))
nominal-value safety equipment purchased by worker as own property, voluntary in writing or under CBA
parameters.other_deductions: require Secretary of Labor approval (29 CFR 3.6-3.8); otherwise prohibited (29 CFR 3.9)

rules.applies_to: Contractors and subcontractors on construction of public buildings/works or work financed in whole or in part by federal loans or grants (Copeland Act)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-3.5; https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-3.9 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: Deductions not elsewhere provided for by this part and which are not found to be permissible under § 3.6 are prohibited.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: California wage-deduction limits also apply on California jobs (state rules); follow the stricter rule. Tool or uniform deductions are not on the federal list.

rules.title: Pay wages only by cash or a check payable on demand
rules.plain_english: On Copeland Act work, wages must be paid in cash or negotiable instruments payable on demand (such as a paycheck), plus the deductions the rules allow. No other payment method counts.
rules.applies_to: Contractors and subcontractors on construction of public buildings/works or work financed in whole or in part by federal loans or grants (Copeland Act)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-3.10 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The payment of wages shall be by cash, negotiable instruments payable on demand, or the additional forms of compensation for which deductions are permissible under this part. No other methods of payment shall be recognized on work subject to the Copeland Act.
rules.notes: Whether direct deposit counts is not addressed in the text read; DOL guidance was not reachable (dol.gov blocked).

rules.title: CWHSSA: time-and-a-half after 40 hours a week on federal/federally assisted contracts over $100,000
rules.plain_english: On covered contracts over $100,000 (DOL rule for federally assisted work), no laborer or mechanic (including guards) may work more than 40 hours in a workweek unless paid at least 1.5 times the basic rate for every hour over 40. This applies in addition to Davis-Bacon.

parameters.rate_base: basic rate of pay (may be computed as FLSA regular-rate equivalent, 29 CFR 5.15(c))

rules.applies_to: Contractors and subcontractors employing laborers or mechanics on federal or federally assisted contracts subject to the Contract Work Hours and Safety Standards Act
rules.citation: 40 U.S.C. 3702 (as implemented); 29 CFR 5.5(b)(1); 2 CFR part 200 Appendix II (E); FAR 22.301
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (b) introductory text and (b)(1)); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-200/appendix-Appendix%20II%20to%20Part%20200 (paragraph (E)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: in any contract in an amount in excess of $100,000 and subject to the overtime provisions of the Contract Work Hours and Safety Standards Act.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)
rules.notes: For direct federal FAR contracts the clause is inserted only above $200,000 since 2025-10-01 (see fed-cwhssa-far-clause-200k). California daily overtime (over 8 hours/day) on state public works is separate and stricter. 29 CFR 5.5(b) puts the CWHSSA clauses in contracts over $100,000 'and subject to the overtime provisions of the Contract Work Hours and Safety Standards Act', and says 'These clauses must be inserted in addition to the clauses required by paragraph (a) of this section or 29 CFR 4.6' (the Davis-Bacon or Service Contract clauses); 2 CFR 200 Appendix II(E) says 'Where applicable'. On a federal grant that is not under a Davis-Bacon Related Act, coverage is not settled by the regulation; confirm with the agency.

rules.title: CWHSSA overtime violation: $33 per worker per day in liquidated damages (2025 adjustment, still current)
rules.plain_english: If a worker is made to work over 40 hours in a week without overtime pay, the contractor and responsible sub owe the unpaid wages plus interest, plus liquidated damages to the government of $33 for each worker for each calendar day the worker worked over the 40-hour standard without overtime. The agency head can reduce or waive totals of $500 or less for inadvertent violations; larger amounts need DOL concurrence.

parameters.adjusted_annually_by: DOL inflation adjustment (Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Act)

rules.applies_to: Contractors and subcontractors on CWHSSA-covered contracts
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (b)(2)); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.8 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: in the sum of $33 for each calendar day on which such individual was required or permitted to work in excess of the standard workweek of forty hours without payment of the overtime wages required by the clause set forth in paragraph (b)(1).
rules.notes: eCFR version history shows 29 CFR 5.5/5.8 amounts of $31 (2023), $32 (2024) and $33 (amended 90 FR 1859, Jan. 10, 2025, in eCFR from 2025-01-15); no 2026 amendment appears in eCFR through 2026-11-23, so $33 remains the current amount. FAR 22.302 says DOL adjusts it no later than January 15 each year; recheck in January 2027.

rules.title: Direct federal contracts: CWHSSA overtime clause only above $200,000 (raised from $150,000 on Oct. 1, 2025)
rules.plain_english: Under the FAR, the overtime clause 52.222-4 is left out of contracts valued at or below $200,000 (it was $150,000 before October 1, 2025). It is also left out of commercial-item contracts and a few other categories. Federally assisted (grant) contracts follow the DOL $100,000 figure instead.

other_exclusions: transportation or the transmission of intelligence
work outside the US and listed territories
work done solely in accordance with 41 U.S.C. chapter 65 (Contracts for Materials, Supplies, Articles, and Equipment; FAR subpart 22.6)
supplies that include incidental services that do not require substantial employment of laborers or mechanics

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors (and where flowed down, subcontractors) on direct federal construction contracts under the FAR (e.g., USACE, GSA, VA, Navy, NPS work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-22.305 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API); prior text compared using eCFR point-in-time 2025-09-30 vs 2025-10-01
rules.quote: (a) Valued at or below $200,000;
rules.notes: FAR inflation adjustment (FAR Case 2024-001, 90 FR 41875-41880, Aug. 27, 2025). The DOL rule for assisted contracts (29 CFR 5.5(b)) was not changed and still says $100,000.
rules.correction: FAR 22.305(e) excludes contracts 'For work to be done solely in accordance with 41 U.S.C. chapter 65 (see subpart 22.6)', which is Contracts for Materials, Supplies, Articles, and Equipment (FAR subpart 22.6), not Service Contract Labor Standards (41 U.S.C. chapter 67, subpart 22.10). The other_exclusions entry was corrected and the (f) entry reworded to the text. The $200,000 threshold is confirmed, and so are the prior $150,000 (eCFR copy of 2025-09-30), the 2025-10-01 change date and the $100,000 DOL figure for assisted contracts.

rules.title: CWHSSA-only contracts: keep payroll records 3 years and allow worker interviews
rules.plain_english: On contracts covered only by CWHSSA (no Davis-Bacon), keep regular payrolls during the work and for 3 years after the prime contract is completed, including guards and watchpersons, with name, contact data, SSN, classification, rates, daily and weekly hours, deductions and pay, and let the agency and DOL inspect them and interview workers on the job.
rules.applies_to: Contractors on contracts subject only to CWHSSA (e.g., non-construction service work with laborers or mechanics)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (c)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: must preserve them for a period of 3 years after all the work on the prime contract is completed for all laborers and mechanics, including guards and watchpersons, working on the contract.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)

rules.title: CWHSSA overtime clauses must be flowed down; prime is liable for lower-tier overtime and liquidated damages
rules.plain_english: Put the CWHSSA overtime, liquidated damages, withholding, flow-down and anti-retaliation clauses in every subcontract and require subs to do the same. The prime is responsible for lower-tier compliance and is liable, with the responsible sub, for unpaid overtime, interest and liquidated damages.
rules.applies_to: Contractors and subcontractors on CWHSSA-covered contracts
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (b)(4)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: due to any workers of lower-tier subcontractors, and associated liquidated damages and may be subject to debarment, as appropriate.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (DOL Davis-Bacon final rule, 88 FR 57526/57731, Aug. 23, 2023; eCFR version date)

rules.title: If withheld funds fall short, workers are paid first, then liquidated damages
rules.plain_english: When an agency withholds money for CWHSSA overtime violations and it is not enough to cover everything, the money goes first to the workers for wages owed (pro-rated if needed), and only the remainder to the government's liquidated damages.

payment_order: laborers and mechanics wages (prorated if insufficient)

rules.applies_to: Contractors on CWHSSA-covered contracts
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.15 (paragraph (d)(1)); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-22.302 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: (1) Pay laborers and mechanics the wages they are owed (or prorate available funds if they do not cover the entire amount owed); and

rules.title: CWHSSA safety: no work in unsanitary, hazardous or dangerous conditions (assisted contracts over $100,000)
rules.plain_english: Federally assisted construction contracts over $100,000 must require that no laborer or mechanic be made to work in surroundings or conditions that are unsanitary, hazardous or dangerous (40 U.S.C. 3704). In practice that means federal OSHA construction standards; in California, Cal/OSHA.
rules.applies_to: Contractors and subcontractors on construction paid with federal financial assistance (grants, cooperative agreements) passed through California state or local agencies
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-200/appendix-Appendix%20II%20to%20Part%20200 (paragraph (E)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The requirements of 40 U.S.C. 3704 are applicable to construction work and provide that no laborer or mechanic must be required to work in surroundings or under working conditions which are unsanitary, hazardous or dangerous.
rules.notes: The link to OSHA/Cal-OSHA standards is explanatory; the Appendix text states only the general safety condition.

rules.title: Miller Act: performance and payment bonds (100% each) on federal construction contracts over $150,000
rules.plain_english: Direct federal construction contracts over $150,000 require a performance bond and a payment bond, each normally equal to 100% of the original contract price, plus 100% of any later price increases. This threshold is statutory and was not changed by the 2025 FAR inflation adjustment.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors (and where flowed down, subcontractors) on direct federal construction contracts under the FAR (e.g., USACE, GSA, VA, Navy, NPS work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-28.102-1; https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-28.102-2; https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-1.109 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: 40 U.S.C. chapter 31, subchapter III, Bonds (formerly known as the Miller Act), requires performance and payment bonds for any construction contract exceeding $150,000
rules.effective: In effect 2026 (FAR 28.102-1; eCFR shows no amendment since 2017)
rules.notes: FAR 1.109(c) excludes the Bonds statute from 41 U.S.C. 1908 inflation escalation, and eCFR shows FAR 28.102-1 unchanged across the 2025-10-01 threshold rule. Federally assisted (grant) projects in California use state bonding law (Civil Code 9550: payment bond over $25,000) and 2 CFR 200.326, not the Miller Act. The contracting officer may set a lower performance-bond percentage. Statute text not fetched (uscode.house.gov blocked).

rules.title: Federal construction over $35,000 up to $150,000: payment bond or other payment protection (100%)
rules.plain_english: For direct federal construction contracts over $35,000 but not over $150,000, the contracting officer picks two or more payment protections (payment bond, irrevocable letter of credit, tripartite escrow, certificates of deposit, or other approved security) and the contractor furnishes one, normally for 100% of the contract price. The protection must last for the whole performance period plus one year.

parameters.coverage_period: full contract performance period plus 1 year
options: payment bond
irrevocable letter of credit
tripartite escrow agreement
certificates of deposit
deposit of security under FAR 28.204-1/28.204-2

rules.quote: for construction contracts greater than $35,000, but not greater than $150,000, the contracting officer shall select two or more of the following payment protections

rules.title: Furnish all bonds before the notice to proceed or starting work
rules.plain_english: On direct federal construction, the contractor must deliver all required bonds or alternative payment protections (and any reinsurance agreements) before getting a notice to proceed or being allowed to start work. Under the standard Bid Guarantee provision (FAR 52.228-1) the winning bidder has 10 days after receiving the bond forms to return executed bonds, unless the solicitation sets another period; missing it lets the contracting officer terminate for default.

parameters.must_furnish_before: notice to proceed / start of work
parameters.default_period_source: FAR 52.228-1(d) (SEP 1996); the contracting officer may set a different period (FAR 28.101-2(a)(1))
parameters.if_bonds_not_furnished_in_time: contracting officer may terminate the contract for default (FAR 52.228-1(d))

rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-28.102-1 (paragraph (c)); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-52.228-15 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-52.228-1 (paragraph (d)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25)
rules.quote: (c) The contractor shall furnish all bonds or alternative payment protection, including any necessary reinsurance agreements, before receiving a notice to proceed with the work or being allowed to start work.
rules.notes: The 10-day default is stated in FAR 52.228-1(d): 'fails to execute all contractual documents or furnish executed bond(s) within 10 days after receipt of the forms by the bidder, the Contracting Officer may terminate the contract for default.' FAR 28.101-2(a)(1) lets the CO set a different period. FAR 52.228-15(c) also requires bonds within that period 'but in any event, before starting work.'
rules.correction: The author inferred the 10-day default from FAR 28.101-2(a)(1) and said FAR 52.228-1 was not read. The verifier read FAR 52.228-1(d) (SEP 1996), which states the 10 days after the bidder receives the forms and allows termination for default. The value 10 is unchanged. The parameter was renamed to show it is stated, not inferred, and the source and consequence were added. FAR 52.228-1(d) was added to the citation and source_location, and plain_english and notes were updated. FAR 28.102-1(c) and 52.228-15(c) are confirmed.

rules.title: Federal bid bond: at least 20% of the bid price, capped at $3 million; missing bid bond = rejected bid
rules.plain_english: When performance/payment bonds are required, a federal construction bid must include a bid guarantee in the amount the solicitation states (a percent of the bid price or a dollar figure, whichever is less). The contracting officer must set it at no less than 20% of the bid price and no more than $3 million. In sealed bidding, a missing or deficient bid guarantee means rejection, except in listed cases (e.g., only one bid, amount still covers the gap to the next bid, unsigned or undated bid bond, wrong obligee name).

parameters.formula: required_bid_guarantee = min(P/100 * bid_price, D), where the solicitation fills in P (percent) and D (dollar cap) in FAR 52.228-1(c); FAR 28.101-2(b) requires P >= 20 and an amount not exceeding $3,000,000, so the usual setting P=20, D=3000000 gives min(0.20 * bid_price, 3000000)
parameters.noncompliance_sealed_bid: rejection unless a FAR 28.101-4(c) waiver applies
parameters.governing_amount: the percent/dollar figures stated in the solicitation's FAR 52.228-1(c)

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors (and where flowed down, subcontractors) on direct federal construction contracts under the FAR (e.g., USACE, GSA, VA, Navy, NPS work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-28.101-2 (paragraph (b)); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-28.101-4 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-52.228-1 (paragraph (c)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25)
rules.quote: The bid guarantee amount shall be at least 20 percent of the bid price but shall not exceed $3 million.
rules.notes: Federally assisted (grant) projects use 2 CFR 200.326 (5% bid guarantee) unless the federal agency accepts the local bonding policy; California awarding agencies also apply state bidder-security law (see state rules).
rules.correction: The 20% minimum, the $3 million maximum and the FAR 28.101-4 waivers are confirmed. The original formula min(0.20 * bid_price, 3000000) was presented as the required amount. FAR 28.101-2(b) makes the contracting officer set the amount (at least 20%, not more than $3 million), and FAR 52.228-1(c) states it as '____ percent of the bid price or $____, whichever is less'. The formula was generalized to the solicitation's P and D, with min(0.20 * bid, 3,000,000) kept as the usual setting. solicitation_percent_min and solicitation_dollar_cap_max_usd were added, FAR 52.228-1(c) was added to the citation and source_location, and plain_english was updated.

rules.title: A sub's or supplier's waiver of Miller Act payment bond rights is void unless written and signed after starting work
rules.plain_english: Any waiver of the right to sue on the payment bond is void unless it is in writing, signed by the person giving up the right, and signed only after that person has first furnished labor or material for the contract. Pre-bid or subcontract-form waivers do not work.

waiver_valid_only_if: signed by person whose right is waived
executed after person first furnished labor or material

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors, subcontractors and suppliers on federal construction with a Miller Act payment bond
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-52.228-15 (paragraph (e)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: Any waiver of the right to sue on the payment bond is void unless it is in writing, signed by the person whose right is waived, and executed after such person has first furnished labor or material for use in the performance of the contract.

rules.title: Subs and suppliers can get the surety name, bond amount and a copy of the federal payment bond
rules.plain_english: On a federal job with a Miller Act payment bond, a subcontractor or supplier (or prospective one) can ask the contracting officer for the surety's name and address, the penal amount of the payment bond, and a copy of the bond (a reasonable copy fee may be charged). An unpaid supplier who files an affidavit can get a certified copy of the bond and contract.

parameters.request_form: written or oral to contracting officer
parameters.certified_copy_requires: affidavit of unpaid labor/materials or of being sued on the bond

rules.applies_to: Subcontractors and suppliers on direct federal construction contracts
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-28.106-6 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: Upon the written or oral request of a subcontractor/supplier, or prospective subcontractor/supplier, under a contract with respect to which a payment bond has been furnished pursuant to the Bonds statute, the contracting officer shall promptly provide to the requester
rules.notes: The Miller Act claim deadlines (notice by second-tier claimants and the time limit to sue under 40 U.S.C. 3133(b)) could not be read from an official source in this session and are NOT included; see sources_blocked.

rules.title: Federal bonds must come from a Treasury Circular 570 surety (or approved individual surety/security)
rules.plain_english: Performance and payment bonds on federal construction must be backed by corporate sureties on the U.S. Treasury's Circular 570 list, by acceptable individual sureties, or by other acceptable security such as certified checks, irrevocable letters of credit or U.S. bonds.

acceptable_security: corporate surety listed in Treasury Department Circular 570

rules.notes: Check the surety's Circular 570 underwriting limit against the bond amount (limit lists not fetched).

rules.title: Federally assisted construction over the simplified acquisition threshold (at most $350,000): 5% bid guarantee, 100% performance and 100% payment bonds
rules.plain_english: For grant-funded construction contracts and subcontracts over the simplified acquisition threshold, the federal minimum is a 5% bid guarantee, a 100% performance bond and a 100% payment bond, unless the federal agency or pass-through entity has accepted the local agency's own bonding policy as protecting the federal interest. The threshold is the recipient's own SAT, which can be lower than, but never above, the FAR figure ($350,000 since Oct. 1, 2025), so a city or agency may require these bonds on smaller contracts.

parameters.threshold_name: recipient's or subrecipient's simplified acquisition threshold (2 CFR 200.1), capped at the FAR 2.101 figure
parameters.contract_value_greater_than_usd_is: the maximum trigger; applies when the recipient uses the full FAR SAT

rules.applies_to: Contractors and subcontractors on construction paid with federal financial assistance (grants, cooperative agreements) passed through California state or local agencies
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.326; https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.1 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: (a) A bid guarantee from each bidder equivalent to five percent of the bid price.
rules.notes: 2 CFR 200.1 says the recipient or subrecipient sets an SAT 'less than or equal to' the FAR 2.101 value and 'This threshold must never exceed the dollar value established in the FAR'. The $350,000 figure is the FAR 2.101 SAT as amended 2025-10-01 (it was $250,000 on 2025-09-30). California public works bonding law (e.g., payment bond over $25,000 under Civil Code 9550; rulebook public-payment-bond-required-25000) usually requires more and also applies.
rules.correction: The 5% / 100% / 100% minimums and the acceptance of the recipient's bonding policy in 2 CFR 200.326 are confirmed. The scope was overstated: 2 CFR 200.326 applies to contracts exceeding 'the simplified acquisition threshold', and 2 CFR 200.1 defines that as the recipient's own SAT, 'less than or equal to' the FAR value and never above it. $350,000 is therefore the highest possible trigger, not a fixed one. recipient_may_set_lower_sat and a label for the 350000 value were added, and the title, plain_english and notes were updated. FAR 2.101 SAT $350,000 is confirmed, with $250,000 on 2025-09-30.

rules.title: FAR thresholds from Oct. 1, 2025: micro-purchase $15,000 ($2,000 for Davis-Bacon construction), simplified acquisition $350,000
rules.plain_english: The October 1, 2025 FAR inflation adjustment raised the micro-purchase threshold from $10,000 to $15,000 and the simplified acquisition threshold from $250,000 to $350,000. For construction subject to Davis-Bacon, the micro-purchase threshold stays $2,000.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors (and where flowed down, subcontractors) on direct federal construction contracts under the FAR (e.g., USACE, GSA, VA, Navy, NPS work in California); also used by 2 CFR 200 for federally assisted procurements

rules.quote: Simplified acquisition threshold means $350,000, except for—

rules.title: Miller Act and Davis-Bacon dollar thresholds are never inflation-adjusted
rules.plain_english: The FAR's periodic inflation adjustments do not apply to thresholds set by the Miller Act bond law, the Davis-Bacon Act, the Service Contract Act, or trade-agreement thresholds set by the U.S. Trade Representative. So Davis-Bacon stays at $2,000 and Miller Act bonds at $150,000 / $35,000 until Congress changes them. Adjusted thresholds apply to existing contracts for the rest of their term.

not_escalated: 40 U.S.C. ch. 31 subch. III Bonds (Miller Act)

rules.title: Large-business primes: small business subcontracting plan above $900,000 ($2 million for construction)
rules.plain_english: If you are not a small business and win a federal contract expected to exceed $900,000 ($2 million for construction) that has subcontracting possibilities, you must submit an acceptable small business subcontracting plan or you are ineligible for award. These figures replaced $750,000 / $1.5 million on October 1, 2025. Any federal prime over $350,000 must give small businesses maximum practicable opportunity and pay them on time.
rules.applies_to: Other-than-small prime contractors on direct federal contracts

rules.title: Federal fixed-price construction over $2 million: prime must self-perform a set percentage (usually at least 12%)
rules.plain_english: On federal fixed-price construction contracts expected to exceed $2 million (raised from $1.5 million on Oct. 1, 2025), the contract includes FAR 52.236-1 requiring the prime to perform, on site with its own organization, at least the percentage of the work stated in the contract, ordinarily not less than 12%. Small business set-aside and similar contracts use the limitations-on-subcontracting rules instead.

rules.quote: when a fixed-price construction contract is contemplated and the contract amount is expected to exceed $2 million.

rules.title: E-Verify clause in federal contracts over $150,000 lasting 120 days or more
rules.plain_english: Federal contracts over $150,000 include the E-Verify clause (FAR 52.222-54) unless the work is all outside the U.S., the performance period is under 120 days, or the contract is only for commercially available off-the-shelf items and related services.

exceptions: work only outside the United States
period of performance less than 120 days
only COTS items (and certain related services)

rules.title: E-Verify deadlines: enroll within 30 days of award; verify new hires within 3 business days
rules.plain_english: If not already enrolled as a federal contractor, enroll in E-Verify within 30 calendar days after award. Within 90 days of enrolling, start verifying all new hires company-wide (within 3 business days after each hire date), and verify each existing employee assigned to the contract within 90 days of enrollment or 30 days of assignment, whichever is later. Already-verified employees and those with active security clearances or HSPD-12 credentials need not be re-run.

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors on direct federal contracts containing FAR 52.222-54 and their subcontractors for services or construction over $3,500

rules.quote: Enroll as a Federal Contractor in the E-Verify program within 30 calendar days of contract award;

rules.plain_english: The prime must include the E-Verify clause in every subcontract for services or construction that is over $3,500 and includes work in the United States.

rules.title: Direct federal bids: be registered in SAM.gov (with a UEI) when you bid and at award
rules.plain_english: To bid on a federal contract you must be actively registered in SAM.gov when you submit the offer and at the time of award, and put your Unique Entity Identifier on the cover page of your bid. Registration includes IRS validation of your taxpayer ID and can take time, so register as soon as you see a solicitation.

registration_elements: mandatory data incl. UEI, EFT indicator, CAGE code, FFATA data
Core, Assertions, Representations and Certifications, Points of Contact

rules.title: Keep SAM registration active through final payment and update it at least once a year
rules.plain_english: After award, keep your SAM registration active during the whole contract and through final payment, and review and update it every year from the date of initial registration or last update. If you were allowed to register after award (Alternate I), you must register within 30 days after award or before 3 days prior to your first invoice, whichever is first. Give the contracting officer at least 1 business day's written notice before changing your company name in SAM.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors (and where flowed down, subcontractors) on direct federal construction contracts under the FAR (e.g., USACE, GSA, VA, Navy, NPS work in California)

rules.title: Grant-funded work: subrecipients need a UEI; ordinary contractors under the grant do not need SAM
rules.plain_english: Under federal grants, the grantee and its first-tier subrecipients must have a Unique Entity Identifier (subrecipients do not need full SAM registration). The UEI/SAM rule in 2 CFR part 25 does not apply to second-tier subrecipients or to contractors hired under the federal award, so a typical construction contractor on a city's federally funded job is not required by this rule to register (the awarding agency may still ask).

rules.title: Check SAM.gov exclusions before awarding a federally funded contract or subcontract
rules.plain_english: Contracts under federal grants that are 'covered transactions' may not be awarded to firms listed as debarred, suspended or otherwise excluded in SAM.gov. A contract is covered when it is expected to be $25,000 or more and is awarded by a grant participant, or at any amount when it needs a federal official's consent. Lower-tier subcontracts of $25,000 or more are covered when the agency extends coverage to them. On Federal-aid highway jobs, suspended, debarred or voluntarily excluded contractors may not participate at all. Primes should check subs, and their own status, in SAM Exclusions before award.

rules.correction: Appendix II(H) limits the prohibition to contract awards described in 2 CFR 180.220. The verifier read 180.220. Covered contracts are those expected to equal or exceed $25,000 that a nonprocurement participant awards, any contract that needs a Federal official's consent, and federally required audits. Lower tiers are covered only if the agency extends coverage and the subcontract is $25,000 or more. The original plain_english said all grant-funded contracts and did not give the threshold. Threshold and coverage parameters were added and plain_english and notes were rewritten. 23 CFR 635.110(e) is confirmed with no threshold.

rules.title: Federal jobs: pay subcontractors within 7 days of receiving payment, or owe interest
rules.plain_english: Every subcontract on a federal construction job must require the prime to pay the subcontractor for satisfactory work within 7 days after the prime receives payment from the government, with an interest penalty (Treasury's Contract Disputes Act rate) for late payment, and each sub must flow the same terms down to its own subs and suppliers.
