rules.quote: A payment clause that obligates the Contractor to pay the subcontractor for satisfactory performance under its subcontract not later than 7 days from receipt of payment out of such amounts as are paid to the Contractor under this contract.
rules.notes: California B&P 7108.5 (also 7 days) applies to California-licensed contractors too; the stricter combined result is still 7 days. The Treasury interest rate is published semiannually in the Federal Register (not fetched).

rules.title: Withholding from a sub on a federal job: written notice (amount, reason, fix) with copy to the CO
rules.plain_english: A prime may withhold from a subcontractor only as the subcontract allows and must give the sub a written notice stating the amount withheld, the specific reasons under the subcontract, and what the sub must do to get paid, with a copy to the contracting officer, before the payment is due. After the problem is fixed, pay within 7 days (or 7 days after recovering the money from the government) or owe interest.

parameters.notice_timing: as soon as practicable, before subcontractor payment due date

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and subcontractors (all tiers) on direct federal construction contracts containing FAR 52.232-27
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-52.232-27 (paragraphs (e)-(g)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: (g) Written notice of subcontractor withholding. The Contractor shall issue a written notice of any withholding to a subcontractor (with a copy furnished to the Contracting Officer), specifying— (1) The amount to be withheld; (2) The specific causes for the withholding under the terms of the subcontract; and (3) The remedial actions to be taken by the subcontractor in order to receive payment of the amounts withheld.

rules.title: Holding a sub's money you were already paid: you owe the government interest from day 8
rules.plain_english: If you withhold a sub's payment after the government already paid you for that work, you must tell the contracting officer and pay the government interest on the withheld amount from the 8th day after you received it until the problem is fixed or your next payment request is reduced.

parameters.interest_ends: deficiency corrected or subsequent payment request reduced

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and subcontractors (all tiers) on direct federal construction contracts containing FAR 52.232-27
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-52.232-27 (paragraph (e)(6)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: from the 8th day after receipt of the withheld amounts from the Government until

rules.title: Federal jobs allow retainage on subs if the subcontract says so; you cannot bill retained amounts until the sub is entitled
rules.plain_english: The federal prompt payment clause does not stop a prime and sub from agreeing to retain a percentage of each progress payment without interest. But the prime may not ask the government to pay any amount it withheld or retained from a sub until it certifies the sub is entitled to it.

parameters.prime_may_not_bill_retained_amounts_unti: certified to CO that subcontractor is entitled

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and subcontractors (all tiers) on direct federal construction contracts containing FAR 52.232-27
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-52.232-27 (paragraphs (d)(1), (h)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: (h) Subcontractor payment entitlement. The Contractor may not request payment from the Government of any amount withheld or retained in accordance with paragraph (d) of this clause until such time as the Contractor has determined and certified to the Contracting Officer that the subcontractor is entitled to the payment of such amount.
rules.notes: No federal percentage cap appears in this clause; California private-work and public-work retention caps (5%) may still apply to California contractors (state rules).

rules.title: Government payment due dates on federal construction: progress 14 days, final 30 days, retainage 30 days
rules.plain_english: The government must pay a proper progress payment request within 14 days after the billing office receives it, and final payment by the later of 30 days after a proper invoice or 30 days after acceptance. Retainage the government held is due as the contract says or 30 days after the contracting officer approves its release. An improper invoice must be returned within 7 days with the reasons.

parameters.final_payment_due_rule: later of 30 days after proper invoice receipt or 30 days after acceptance

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors (and where flowed down, subcontractors) on direct federal construction contracts under the FAR (e.g., USACE, GSA, VA, Navy, NPS work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-52.232-27 (paragraph (a)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The due date for making such payments is 14 days after the designated billing office receives a proper payment request.

rules.title: Every federal progress payment request needs the prime's certification that subs have been paid
rules.plain_english: With each progress payment request on a federal fixed-price construction contract, the prime must certify that amounts requested are only for conforming work, that all subs and suppliers were paid from earlier payments and will be paid timely from this one, and that the request excludes amounts the prime intends to withhold or retain from subs. No certification, no payment.

certification_items: amounts only for performance per contract
all prior payments due subs/suppliers made; timely payments will be made (31 U.S.C. ch. 39)
request excludes amounts to be withheld/retained from subs
(optional) not final acceptance of sub performance

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors (and where flowed down, subcontractors) on direct federal construction contracts under the FAR (e.g., USACE, GSA, VA, Navy, NPS work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-52.232-5 (paragraph (c)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: Along with each request for progress payments, the Contractor shall furnish the following certification, or payment shall not be made:

rules.title: Federal construction: government may retain up to 10% only when progress is unsatisfactory
rules.plain_english: If progress is satisfactory, the contracting officer must pay progress payments in full. Only when progress is not satisfactory may the government retain up to 10% of the payment until progress is satisfactory. At substantial completion it keeps only what it needs and releases the rest; separately priced completed buildings or divisions are paid without retention, and bond premium reimbursements are never retained.

parameters.release_at_substantial_completion: all except amount CO considers adequate
no_retainage_on: completed and accepted separately priced divisions

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors (and where flowed down, subcontractors) on direct federal construction contracts under the FAR (e.g., USACE, GSA, VA, Navy, NPS work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-52.232-5 (paragraph (e)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: However, if satisfactory progress has not been made, the Contracting Officer may retain a maximum of 10 percent of the amount of the payment until satisfactory progress is achieved.
rules.notes: The government also reimburses bond premiums on request after proof of payment (52.232-5(g)).

rules.title: Build America, Buy America: all iron, steel, manufactured products and construction materials must be U.S.-made
rules.plain_english: On infrastructure projects paid with federal financial assistance, federal money may not be used unless all iron, steel, manufactured products and construction materials incorporated into the project are produced in the United States. The requirement must be written into every subaward, contract and purchase order, so it reaches subcontractors and suppliers.
rules.applies_to: Contractors and suppliers on infrastructure projects funded by federal financial assistance (e.g., IIJA/BIL-funded roads, transit, water, broadband, EV charging and public buildings in California)
rules.citation: Build America, Buy America Act sec. 70914 (Pub. L. 117-58); 2 CFR 184.1(b); 2 CFR 184.4(a)-(c); 2 CFR 200.322(c)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-184.1; https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-184.4 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The Buy America Preference must be included in all subawards, contracts, and purchase orders for the work performed, or products supplied under the Federal award.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (2 CFR part 184 effective date; Build America, Buy America Act effective 2022-05-14)
rules.notes: Federal-aid highway projects apply FHWA's Buy America regulation (23 CFR 635.410; see fed-fhwa-buy-america-* rules). 2 CFR 184.2(a) exempts pre-November 15, 2021 agency Buy America preferences that meet or exceed section 70914. Agency-specific waivers (e.g., de minimis or small-project waivers) were not researched; check the funding agency.
rules.correction: 2 CFR 184.1(b) and 184.3 ('Buy America Preference') cover items 'incorporated into the project'. The word 'permanently' in the original plain_english is not in 2 CFR part 184; it is the FHWA wording in 23 CFR 635.410. It was removed so the BABA scope is not narrowed. The categories, flow-down (184.4(b)), infrastructure list (184.4(c)) and the 2023-10-23 / 2022-05-14 effective dates (184.2(b)) are confirmed.

rules.title: BABA iron and steel: every step from melting through coating must happen in the U.S.
rules.plain_english: An iron or steel product (more than 50% iron/steel by component cost) counts as U.S.-produced only if all manufacturing processes, from the initial melting stage through applying coatings, occurred in the United States.

parameters.domestic_standard: all manufacturing processes from initial melting through application of coatings in the US

rules.applies_to: Contractors and suppliers on infrastructure projects funded by federal financial assistance (e.g., IIJA/BIL-funded roads, transit, water, broadband, EV charging and public buildings in California)
rules.citation: 2 CFR 184.3 (Produced in the United States (1); Predominantly of iron or steel)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-184.3 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: In the case of iron or steel products, all manufacturing processes, from the initial melting stage through the application of coatings, occurred in the United States.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (2 CFR part 184 effective date; Build America, Buy America Act effective 2022-05-14)

rules.title: BABA manufactured products: made in the U.S. and over 55% U.S. component cost
rules.plain_english: A manufactured product (e.g., pumps, valves, panels, light fixtures) qualifies only if it was manufactured in the United States and the cost of its U.S.-mined, produced or manufactured components is more than 55% of the cost of all its components. Component cost = what the manufacturer paid including freight and duty (or, for components it makes itself, its full cost plus allocable overhead, no profit).

parameters.formula: domestic_pct = sum(cost of US components) / sum(cost of all components) * 100; compliant if final manufacture in US and domestic_pct > 55
parameters.purchased_component_cost: acquisition cost incl. transportation to place of incorporation and any applicable duty
parameters.self_made_component_cost: all manufacturing costs + transportation + allocable overhead, excluding profit
parameters.excludes: costs of manufacturing the final product itself

rules.applies_to: Contractors and suppliers on infrastructure projects funded by federal financial assistance (e.g., IIJA/BIL-funded roads, transit, water, broadband, EV charging and public buildings in California)
rules.citation: 2 CFR 184.3 (Produced in the United States (2)); 2 CFR 184.5
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-184.3; https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-184.5 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The cost of the components of the manufactured product that are mined, produced, or manufactured in the United States is greater than 55 percent of the total cost of all components of the manufactured product
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (2 CFR part 184 effective date; Build America, Buy America Act effective 2022-05-14)

rules.title: BABA construction materials: 8 listed materials must have all manufacturing processes in the U.S.
rules.plain_english: Construction materials covered by BABA are non-ferrous metals, plastic and polymer-based products (including PVC and composites), glass, fiber optic cable, optical fiber, lumber, engineered wood and drywall. Each must have all of its listed manufacturing steps performed in the United States (e.g., lumber from debarking through treatment and planing; drywall from gypsum blending through cutting and drying).

materials_and_standards.non-ferrous metals: initial smelting/melting through final shaping, coating and assembly
materials_and_standards.plastic and polymer-based products: initial combination of inputs until final form
materials_and_standards.glass: batching and melting through annealing, cooling and cutting
materials_and_standards.fiber optic cable: ribboning through buffering, stranding and jacketing (plus glass and optical fiber standards)
materials_and_standards.optical fiber: preform fabrication through completion of draw
materials_and_standards.lumber: initial debarking through treatment and planing
materials_and_standards.drywall: blending gypsum and additives through cutting and drying
materials_and_standards.engineered wood: initial combination of constituent materials until final form

rules.applies_to: Contractors and suppliers on infrastructure projects funded by federal financial assistance (e.g., IIJA/BIL-funded roads, transit, water, broadband, EV charging and public buildings in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-184.6 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: (6) Lumber. All manufacturing processes, from initial debarking through treatment and planing, occurred in the United States.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (2 CFR part 184 effective date; Build America, Buy America Act effective 2022-05-14)

rules.title: Cement, aggregates and binders are excluded from BABA; classify each item once, as delivered to the site
rules.plain_english: Cement and cementitious materials, stone, sand, gravel and aggregate binding agents or additives ("section 70917(c) materials") are not subject to the BABA preference by themselves. Each item falls into only one category (iron/steel, manufactured product, construction material, or excluded), decided by its condition when it arrives at the work site.

excluded_section_70917c_materials: aggregates such as stone, sand or gravel
parameters.classification_time: status when brought to the work site for incorporation

rules.applies_to: Contractors and suppliers on infrastructure projects funded by federal financial assistance (e.g., IIJA/BIL-funded roads, transit, water, broadband, EV charging and public buildings in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-184.4 (paragraph (e)); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-184.3 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The classification of an article, material, or supply as falling into one of the categories listed in paragraph (e)(1) must be made based on its status at the time it is brought to the work site for incorporation into an infrastructure project.
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (2 CFR part 184 effective date; Build America, Buy America Act effective 2022-05-14)
rules.notes: A manufactured product (e.g., precast concrete) may contain excluded materials as components.

rules.title: BABA waivers: public interest, not available, or >25% project cost increase; 15-day public comment
rules.plain_english: The funding agency may waive BABA only if applying it is against the public interest, the U.S. item is not available in enough quantity or quality, or using U.S. items would raise the overall project cost by more than 25%. A recipient (e.g., the city or Caltrans) must request a waiver in writing; proposed waivers are posted for at least 15 days of public comment (30 days to modify or renew general waivers) and reviewed by OMB's Made in America Office.

parameters.requested_by: recipient, in writing to the Federal agency

rules.applies_to: Contractors and suppliers on infrastructure projects funded by federal financial assistance (e.g., IIJA/BIL-funded roads, transit, water, broadband, EV charging and public buildings in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-184.7 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The inclusion of iron, steel, manufactured products, or construction materials produced in the United States will increase the cost of the overall infrastructure project by more than 25 percent (an “unreasonable cost waiver”).
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (2 CFR part 184 effective date; Build America, Buy America Act effective 2022-05-14)
rules.notes: Contractors cannot request waivers directly from the federal agency; they go through the recipient. Plan lead time of at least several weeks.

rules.title: BABA does not apply to Stafford Act disaster and emergency assistance spending
rules.plain_english: Federal disaster and emergency assistance spending under listed sections of the Stafford Act (and related pre- and post-disaster response spending) is exempt from the BABA preference.

parameters.also_exempt: pre and post disaster or emergency response expenditures under other statutes

rules.applies_to: Contractors and suppliers on infrastructure projects funded by federal financial assistance (e.g., IIJA/BIL-funded roads, transit, water, broadband, EV charging and public buildings in California); disaster recovery contractors
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-184.8 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The Buy America Preference does not apply to expenditures for assistance authorized under section 402, 403, 404, 406, 408, or 502 of the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (2 CFR part 184 effective date; Build America, Buy America Act effective 2022-05-14)
rules.notes: Relevant to California wildfire and flood rebuilds funded by FEMA public assistance.

rules.title: Grant-funded purchases: domestic preference clause must be in all contracts and purchase orders
rules.plain_english: Separate from BABA, recipients of federal grants should prefer U.S.-produced goods (iron, aluminum, steel, cement and other manufactured products) to the extent practicable, and this domestic-preference requirement must appear in all subawards, contracts and purchase orders under the grant.

parameters.iron_steel_definition: all manufacturing processes from initial melting through coatings in the US

rules.applies_to: Contractors and subcontractors on construction paid with federal financial assistance (grants, cooperative agreements) passed through California state or local agencies
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.322 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The requirements of this section must be included in all subawards, contracts, and purchase orders under Federal awards.

rules.title: Direct federal construction (Buy American): domestic materials need 65% U.S. content through 2028, 75% from 2029
rules.plain_english: On direct federal construction contracts, use only domestic construction materials. A manufactured construction material is domestic if U.S. components exceed 65% of component cost for items delivered in 2024-2028 (75% from 2029). The content test is waived for COTS items, but COTS items that are mostly iron or steel are still tested on their iron and steel content. Iron/steel materials must have less than 5% foreign iron and steel. The CO may allow foreign material if domestic material costs more than 20% extra (more for listed critical items) or is unavailable. Ask before award, or explain why you could not.

parameters.cots_content_test: waived for COTS construction material that is not wholly or predominantly iron or steel; for COTS material that is wholly or predominantly iron or steel, the test applies only to its iron and steel content, excluding COTS fasteners (FAR 52.225-9(a) 'Domestic construction material', (b)(1))
parameters.critical_items_extra_preference: for critical items or materials with critical components, the 20% differential is increased by the FAR 25.105 preference factor (52.225-9(b)(3)(i)(B))
parameters.trade_agreements_version: FAR 52.225-11: when the contracting officer has determined that the WTO GPA and Free Trade Agreements apply, the Buy American restrictions are waived for designated country construction materials

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors (and where flowed down, subcontractors) on direct federal construction contracts under the FAR (e.g., USACE, GSA, VA, Navy, NPS work in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-52.225-9 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: except that the percentage will be 65 percent for items delivered in calendar years 2024 through 2028 and 75 percent for items delivered starting in calendar year 2029.
rules.notes: Large contracts may use the Trade Agreements versions (FAR 52.225-11) instead; trade agreement thresholds were not researched. Critical-item price preferences in 52.225-9(b)(3) were not summarized.
rules.correction: The 65% (2024-2028) and 75% (2029+) figures, the <5% foreign iron/steel limit, the 20% differential and the post-award explanation rule (52.225-9(c)(1)(iv)) are confirmed. The parameter 'cots_exempt_from_content_test: true' was too broad. 52.225-9(b)(1) waives the content test for COTS material 'except that for construction material that consists wholly or predominantly of iron or steel ... the domestic content test is applied only to the iron and steel content'. It was replaced by cots_content_test. The critical-item preference (b)(3)(i)(B) and the 60% figure for pre-2024 deliveries were added, and plain_english was updated.

rules.title: No Huawei, ZTE, Hikvision, Dahua or Hytera equipment on grant-funded jobs (Section 889)
rules.plain_english: Federal grant or loan money may not be used to buy, extend or renew contracts for telecommunications equipment from Huawei or ZTE, or (for public safety, security and surveillance of critical infrastructure) video surveillance and telecom equipment from Hytera, Hikvision or Dahua, or systems that use them as a substantial or essential component. Contractors installing cameras, radios or network gear on federally funded projects must source other brands.
rules.applies_to: Contractors and subcontractors on construction paid with federal financial assistance (grants, cooperative agreements) passed through California state or local agencies; low-voltage, security, telecom and ITS installers
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.216 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: Telecommunications equipment produced by Huawei Technologies Company or ZTE Corporation (or any subsidiary or affiliate of such entities);
rules.notes: Direct federal contracts have a parallel FAR clause (52.204-25), which was not read for this pack.

rules.title: Federal-aid highway Buy America: steel and iron 100% U.S. incl. coatings; foreign allowed only up to 0.1% of contract or $2,500
rules.plain_english: On Federal-aid highway projects, all permanently incorporated steel and iron must be made in the U.S., including coating. A small amount of foreign steel or iron is allowed if its delivered cost is no more than 0.1% of the total contract cost or $2,500, whichever is greater.

parameters.cost_basis: value of steel and iron products as delivered to the project

rules.applies_to: Contractors on Federal-aid highway construction projects (Caltrans and local agency federal-aid projects in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-23/section-635.410 (paragraph (b)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: if the cost of such materials used does not exceed one-tenth of one percent (0.1 percent) of the total contract cost or $2,500, whichever is greater.
rules.notes: Track foreign steel/iron dollars cumulatively per contract for this calculation.

rules.title: Federal-aid highway manufactured products: U.S.-made from Oct. 1, 2025; plus >55% U.S. components from Oct. 1, 2026
rules.plain_english: For Federal-aid highway projects obligated on or after October 1, 2025, manufactured products permanently incorporated must be manufactured in the United States. For projects obligated on or after October 1, 2026, they must also have more than 55% U.S. component cost. Precast concrete steel components and ITS/electronic cabinets that are mostly steel must meet the steel rule, and their cost counts in the 55% calculation.

special_items.ITS and electronic hardware in right of: iron/steel cabinets and enclosures must meet 635.410(b)

parameters.key_date_driver: date FHWA funds were obligated for the project, not bid date

rules.applies_to: Contractors on Federal-aid highway construction projects (Caltrans and local agency federal-aid projects in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-23/section-635.410 (paragraph (c)(1)(vii), (c)(2)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: (B) For projects obligated on or after October 1, 2026, the product was manufactured in the United States and the cost of the components of the manufactured product that are mined, produced, or manufactured in the United States is greater than 55 percent of the total cost of all components of the manufactured product.
rules.notes: eCFR shows amendments to 635.410 dated 2025-01-14, 2025-03-04 and 2025-03-20; the text above is the version current on 2026-11-23. Ask the agency for the project's federal obligation date.

rules.title: Federal-aid alternate bids for foreign steel: domestic bid wins unless more than 25% higher
rules.plain_english: If a state uses alternate bidding for foreign versus domestic iron or steel on a Federal-aid highway job, every bidder must bid domestic, and the contract goes to the lowest domestic total bid unless it is more than 25% above the lowest foreign-steel total bid.
rules.applies_to: Contractors on Federal-aid highway construction projects (Caltrans and local agency federal-aid projects in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-23/section-635.410 (paragraph (b)(3)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: unless such total bid exceeds the lowest total bid based on furnishing foreign iron or steel products by more than 25 percent.

rules.title: Federal-aid highway primes must self-perform at least 30% of the contract (specialty items excluded)
rules.plain_english: Federal-aid highway contracts must require the prime to perform with its own organization at least 30% of the total original contract price, after subtracting specialty items. Materials the prime buys for its own work count toward its share. The prime must also provide a competent superintendent with full authority. This does not apply to design-build contracts.

parameters.base: total original contract price minus specialty items subcontracted

rules.applies_to: Contractors on Federal-aid highway construction projects (Caltrans and local agency federal-aid projects in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-23/section-635.116 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: This percentage shall be not less than 30 percent of the total original contract price excluding any identified specialty items.
rules.notes: Caltrans contracts set the exact percentage and specialty items in the special provisions.

rules.title: Federal-aid highway: no subcontracting without written state DOT authorization; every subcontract in writing
rules.plain_english: On Federal-aid highway contracts, no work may be subcontracted unless the state DOT has authorized it in writing, and each subcontract must be in writing and contain all the pertinent provisions and requirements of the prime contract.

parameters.must_contain: all pertinent provisions and requirements of the prime contract

rules.applies_to: Contractors on Federal-aid highway construction projects (Caltrans and local agency federal-aid projects in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-23/section-635.116 (paragraph (b)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The State DOT shall not permit any of the contract work to be performed under a subcontract, unless such arrangement has been authorized by the State DOT in writing.

rules.title: Federal-aid highway: no convict labor on site and no in-state labor preference
rules.plain_english: No convict labor may work on a Federal-aid highway project site from award to final acceptance (people on parole, supervised release or probation are allowed). States may not impose rules that discriminate against workers from other states. Bid advertisements must include, or point to, the DOL prevailing wage rates.

parameters.allowed: convicts on parole, supervised release or probation
parameters.bid_call_must_include: DOL minimum wage rates (or state they are in bid documents)

rules.applies_to: Contractors on Federal-aid highway construction projects (Caltrans and local agency federal-aid projects in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-23/section-635.117 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: No procedures or requirement shall be imposed by any State which will operate to discriminate against the employment of labor from any other State, possession or territory of the United States, in the construction of a Federal-aid project.

rules.title: 23 CFR part 633 (Form FHWA-1273 rule) was removed in 2026; Davis-Bacon clauses still apply
rules.plain_english: The regulation that required Form FHWA-1273 ("Required Contract Provisions, Federal-aid Construction Contracts") to be physically attached to every Federal-aid highway contract and subcontract (23 CFR 633 subpart A) no longer appears in the CFR: eCFR shows part 633 as reserved, with subpart A removed effective June 10, 2026. Davis-Bacon, CWHSSA and Copeland clauses still apply by law (29 CFR 5.5(e)), and Caltrans or local contracts may still include FHWA-1273; follow your contract.

parameters.prior_rule: FHWA-1273 physically incorporated in each Federal-aid construction contract and subcontract; not by reference

rules.applies_to: Contractors on Federal-aid highway construction projects (Caltrans and local agency federal-aid projects in California)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-23/part-633 (eCFR shows "PART 633 [RESERVED]" as of 2026-11-23); removal dates from the eCFR versioner API version history for 23 CFR 633.101-633.104 (removed 2026-06-10) and 633.201-633.211 (removed 2026-01-02)
rules.quote: PART 633 [RESERVED]
rules.notes: The Federal Register notice explaining the removal (and whether FHWA still requires FHWA-1273 through other means) could not be read (federalregister.gov and fhwa.dot.gov blocked). Treat FHWA-1273 in a contract as binding. The former 633.102(e) text required primes to insert FHWA-1273 in each subcontract and barred incorporation by reference.

rules.title: USDOT-funded jobs: pay subs within 30 days of each payment received (all tiers)
rules.plain_english: On USDOT-assisted contracts, the agency's DBE program must require primes to pay subcontractors for satisfactory work no later than 30 days after receiving each payment from the agency, and this applies to all lower tiers. Agencies must actively monitor compliance and set penalties; delays need good cause and the agency's prior written approval if the program says so.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and subcontractors on USDOT-assisted contracts (FHWA, FTA, FAA) let by Caltrans, California cities, counties, transit and airport agencies
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/section-26.29 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: a contract clause to require prime contractors to pay subcontractors for satisfactory performance of their contracts no later than 30 days from receipt of each payment you make to the prime contractor.
rules.notes: California law is stricter for California contractors: pay subs within 7 days of receiving a progress payment (B&P 7108.5; rulebook bp-7108-5-pay-subs-7-days). Meeting the 7-day state deadline also satisfies this 30-day federal requirement.

rules.title: USDOT-funded jobs: return sub retainage within 30 days after the sub's work is satisfactorily completed
rules.plain_english: Retainage held from a subcontractor must be paid in full within 30 days after the sub's work is satisfactorily completed (or, where the agency uses incremental acceptance, within 30 days after the agency pays the prime for the accepted work). The agency chooses one method: no retainage at all, prime pays sub retainage within 30 days of completion, or incremental acceptance.

methods: no retainage held by agency or prime
agency holds none; prime returns sub retainage within 30 days of satisfactory completion
agency holds retainage with incremental acceptances; prime pays sub within 30 days after agency payment
parameters.satisfactorily_completed: all subcontract tasks accomplished and documented as required by recipient (or covered by incremental acceptance)

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and subcontractors on USDOT-assisted contracts (FHWA, FTA, FAA) let by Caltrans, California cities, counties, transit and airport agencies
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/section-26.29 (paragraph (b)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: You must ensure prompt and full payment of retainage from the prime contractor to the subcontractor within 30 days after the subcontractor's work is satisfactorily completed.
rules.notes: California public works retention rules (Public Contract Code 7107 and 7200 series, in rulebook) also apply and may be stricter.

rules.title: Every USDOT-assisted contract and subcontract must contain the DBE nondiscrimination assurance
rules.plain_english: Each prime contract and each subcontract on a USDOT-assisted job must include the assurance that the contractor will not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin or sex and will carry out 49 CFR part 26. Breach is material and can lead to withheld progress payments, sanctions, liquidated damages, termination or being found non-responsible for future bids.

remedies_for_breach: disqualification from future bidding as non-responsible

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and subcontractors on USDOT-assisted contracts (FHWA, FTA, FAA) let by Caltrans, California cities, counties, transit and airport agencies
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/section-26.13 (paragraph (b)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The contractor, sub recipient or subcontractor shall not discriminate on the basis of race, color, national origin, or sex in the performance of this contract.
rules.notes: Copy the assurance text verbatim from 26.13(b) into subcontracts.

rules.title: DBE contract goals paused: agencies may not set new DBE goals until their state's DBE re-evaluation is done
rules.plain_english: Since October 3, 2025, USDOT recipients (Caltrans, cities, transit and airport agencies) may not set any DBE contract goals until the Unified Certification Program covering them finishes re-evaluating every certified DBE, and they need not update overall goals until then. Bidders on new federal-aid contracts should not expect DBE goal or good-faith-effort requirements until the agency announces otherwise.

rules.quote: (h) Effective October 3, 2025, you may not set any contract goals until the UCP that covers you has completed the reevaluation process described in § 26.111.
rules.notes: Contracts already awarded with DBE commitments remain governed by their terms and the termination/substitution rules in 26.53(f)-(g). Whether California's UCP has completed its reevaluation was not verified (dot.ca.gov and transportation.gov blocked).

rules.title: DBE re-evaluation: certifiers must finish by Dec. 24, 2026; non-responding DBEs have until March 24, 2027
rules.plain_english: Every Unified Certification Program must re-evaluate all currently certified DBEs under the new rules and finish by December 24, 2026 (one extension of up to 90 days may be granted). A DBE that has not sent its owner's Personal Narrative and personal net worth statement by the time the UCP finishes gets a non-response notice and has until March 24, 2027 (or 90 days after an extended deadline) to submit, or it is automatically disqualified.

parameters.nonresponsive_deadline_if_ucp_extended: 90 days after the UCP's extended deadline

rules.notes: Primes relying on DBE subs or suppliers should confirm each firm's current status in the CUCP directory before counting participation (26.55(f)).

rules.title: DBE certification now requires an individual Personal Narrative; no race or sex presumption
rules.plain_english: Owners seeking or keeping DBE certification must prove social and economic disadvantage with a Personal Narrative showing, by a preponderance of the evidence, specific hardships, barriers or denied opportunities, including at least one objective distinguishing feature and the economic harm caused, plus a current personal net worth statement. Race or sex alone is no longer presumed to show disadvantage.

required_documents: Personal Narrative (PN)
current Personal Net Worth (PNW) statement
parameters.pn_must_identify: at least one objective distinguishing feature (ODF) and type/magnitude of economic harm

rules.title: DBE personal net worth cap: $2,047,000 (excluding home equity and the business); above it, no presumption of economic disadvantage
rules.plain_english: An owner whose personal net worth exceeds $2,047,000 is not presumed economically disadvantaged. Being under the cap does not settle it either: the certifier can still find the owner not economically disadvantaged in fact. Left out of the calculation are the owner's interest in the DBE firm, the owner's share of equity in the primary residence, and qualified retirement accounts (which must still be reported). Assets of more than $20,000 in total transferred to relatives in the prior 2 years are counted. DOT will next adjust the cap by May 9, 2027, and then every 3 years.

excluded: ownership interest in the applicant/DBE firm
owner's share of equity in primary residence
assets in qualified retirement accounts (must be reported)
parameters.effect_of_exceeding_cap: not presumed economically disadvantaged (49 CFR 26.68(a)); the text read does not separately state automatic ineligibility
parameters.below_cap_not_conclusive: certifier may still find the owner not economically disadvantaged in fact (26.67(a)(4), (b))

The original plain_english said an owner over the cap 'is not considered economically disadvantaged'. 26.68(a) says 'is not presumed economically disadvantaged', and under 26.67 no owner is presumed disadvantaged. The title and plain_english were changed to the regulation's wording, and effect_of_exceeding_cap and below_cap_not_conclusive were added.

rules.title: DBE size cap on FHWA/FTA jobs: $30.72 million average gross receipts (as of March 1, 2024, adjusted yearly)
rules.plain_english: Even a firm that is small under SBA rules cannot count as a DBE on FHWA- or FTA-assisted contracts if its affiliated annual gross receipts, averaged over the previous three fiscal years, exceed $30.72 million (figure as of March 1, 2024). USDOT adjusts the cap each year on its website.

rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/section-26.65 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)

rules.title: DBE goal contracts: submit DBE commitments at bid or within 5 days after bid opening
rules.plain_english: When a USDOT-assisted contract has a DBE goal, bidders must submit the names and addresses of DBEs, a description and dollar amount of each DBE's work, written commitments, each DBE's written confirmation, and (if the goal is not met) good-faith-effort evidence including all sub quotes when a non-DBE was chosen over a DBE. The agency decides whether this is due with the bid (responsiveness) or no later than 5 days after bid opening (responsibility).

submission_timing_options: no later than 5 days after bid opening (responsibility)
required_items: DBE names and addresses
description of DBE work (DBE certified in applicable NAICS)
dollar amount of each DBE
written commitment to use DBE
written confirmation from each DBE
good faith efforts documentation if goal not met incl. DBE and non-DBE quotes

rules.title: Replacing a listed DBE needs the agency's written consent and 5 days' written notice to the DBE
rules.plain_english: A prime may not terminate or reduce a DBE listed to meet a goal (including to self-perform) without the agency's prior written consent for good cause. First send the DBE written notice of intent (copy to the agency); the DBE gets 5 days to respond with objections. Good cause includes the DBE refusing to sign, failing to perform to industry standards, failing reasonable bond requirements, insolvency, debarment, withdrawal or ineligibility. The prime is not paid for listed DBE work it performs without consent.

good_cause_excludes: prime wants to substitute another firm after award
good_cause_examples: DBE fails/refuses to execute written contract
DBE fails/refuses to perform to normal industry standards
DBE fails reasonable nondiscriminatory bond requirements
DBE ineligible for credit for the work

rules.title: After a DBE is dropped, make good faith efforts to replace the participation; documents due in 7 days on request
rules.plain_english: If a listed DBE is terminated or cannot finish (or its counted work shrinks), the prime must use good faith efforts to find other DBE participation to meet the goal, document them, and give the documentation to the agency within 7 days of a request (extendable by 7 more days).
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and subcontractors on USDOT-assisted contracts (FHWA, FTA, FAA) let by Caltrans, California cities, counties, transit and airport agencies

rules.title: DBE credit for materials: manufacturer 100%, regular dealer 60%, distributor 40%, broker fees only
rules.plain_english: Materials bought from a DBE count toward DBE goals at 100% if the DBE manufactured them, 60% (including transport) if the DBE is a regular dealer selling at least 51% of the order from its own inventory (or a bulk-items dealer with its own delivery trucks), and 40% if it is a distributor that takes title and risk at the point of origin (FOB origin). Brokers and packagers get credit only for reasonable fees. Note: since October 3, 2025, agencies may not count any DBE participation toward DBE goals until their Unified Certification Program finishes the 26.111 re-evaluation (49 CFR 26.55(i)); these counting rules apply again after that.

parameters.distributor_requires: ownership and risk of loss from point of origin (e.g., FOB origin)
parameters.counting_suspended_until: the UCP covering the recipient completes the 49 CFR 26.111 reevaluation

rules.title: A DBE that does not perform at least 30% of its own contract with its own forces is presumed not to perform a commercially useful function
rules.plain_english: DBE work counts only if the DBE performs a commercially useful function: it runs, manages and supervises its work and handles its own materials (negotiates price, orders, installs and pays). If the DBE does not perform or control at least 30% of the total cost of its contract with its own work force, or subcontracts more than is normal for that trade, the agency presumes it is not performing a CUF (the DBE may rebut). Work a DBE subcontracts to a non-DBE does not count. Note: since October 3, 2025, agencies may not count any DBE participation toward DBE goals until their Unified Certification Program finishes the 26.111 re-evaluation (49 CFR 26.55(i)); these counting rules apply again after that.

rules.title: DBE trucking credit: DBE must own and run at least one truck; non-DBE leased trucks capped
rules.plain_english: A DBE trucking firm must manage the whole trucking operation and own and operate at least one fully licensed, insured truck on the contract. It gets full credit for its own trucks and trucks leased from other DBEs; trucks leased with drivers from non-DBEs get full credit only up to the value provided by DBE trucks (fee-only beyond that, and only with operating administration consent); trucks leased without drivers from a leasing company and driven by DBE employees get full credit. Note: since October 3, 2025, agencies may not count any DBE participation toward DBE goals until their Unified Certification Program finishes the 26.111 re-evaluation (49 CFR 26.55(i)); these counting rules apply again after that.

Agencies keep running tallies of payments to each listed DBE. Note: since October 3, 2025, agencies may not count any DBE participation toward DBE goals until their Unified Certification Program finishes the 26.111 re-evaluation (49 CFR 26.55(i)); these counting rules apply again after that.

rules.title: Grant-funded contracts: required clauses by dollar threshold (2 CFR 200 Appendix II)
rules.plain_english: Contracts paid with federal grant money must include: breach remedies over the simplified acquisition threshold ($350,000); termination for cause and convenience over $10,000; Davis-Bacon and Copeland for prime construction contracts over $2,000 when the program law requires it; CWHSSA over $100,000; Clean Air Act and Clean Water Act compliance over $150,000; and the anti-lobbying certification for bids over $100,000. They also need the equal employment opportunity clause for federally assisted construction (subject to 41 CFR part 60), the debarment check for covered contracts ($25,000 or more), and the procurement-of-recovered-materials, Section 889 telecom and domestic-preference clauses.

rules.citation: 2 CFR part 200 Appendix II (I); 31 U.S.C. 1352; FAR 3.808 (as amended 90 FR 41876, Aug. 27, 2025); FAR 52.203-11; FAR 52.203-12
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/part-200/appendix-Appendix%20II%20to%20Part%20200 (paragraph (I)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-3.808 (paragraphs (a)-(b)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25; compared with eCFR point-in-time 2025-09-30)
rules.quote: Contractors that apply or bid for an award exceeding $100,000 must file the required certification.
rules.notes: The disclosure form (SF-LLL) and civil penalty amounts were not read.
rules.correction: The $100,000 threshold, tier-to-tier certification and disclosure are confirmed in Appendix II(I) for grant-funded contracts. applies_to also named 'direct federal contractors' with the same $100,000 figure. FAR 3.808 puts 52.203-11 and 52.203-12 only in solicitations and contracts 'expected to exceed $200,000', and the eCFR copy of 2025-09-30 shows $150,000 before the 90 FR 41876 adjustment. The FAR threshold and prior value were added, applies_to and plain_english now separate the two regimes, and the citation and source_location were extended. Rewording 2026-11-27: title reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: Federal contractor $15+ minimum wage (EO 14026): revoked March 14, 2025 and not enforced by DOL (UNVERIFIED from primary text)
rules.plain_english: The Biden-era order requiring a higher minimum wage for federal contractors (EO 14026) was revoked on March 14, 2025 by EO 14236, and DOL says it is no longer enforcing EO 14026 or its rule (29 CFR part 23). However, as of November 2026 the rule (29 CFR part 23) and the FAR clause 52.222-55 are still printed in the CFR. The older EO 13658 minimum wage may still apply to some older contracts. Davis-Bacon rates and California minimum wages still apply.

parameters.eo_13658_status: DOL Federal Register notice (Feb. 9, 2026) indicates EO 13658 minimum wage still applies to some existing contracts; 2026 rate not read

rules.applies_to: Contractors on direct federal contracts (FAR) that contained FAR 52.222-55 or 52.222-6 with EO minimum wage terms
rules.citation: Executive Order 14236 (90 FR 13037) sec. 2(d) (as reported by DOL); 29 CFR part 23; FAR 22.403-4; FAR 52.222-55
rules.source: https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/government-contracts/eo14026 (NOT fetched - dol.gov blocked; text seen only in search-result excerpt); https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-23.10 and https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-22.403-4 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: the Department of Labor is no longer enforcing Executive Order 14026 or the implementing rule (29 CFR part 23) and will take steps, including rescinding 29 CFR part 23, to implement and effectuate the revocation of Executive Order 14026.
rules.notes: UNVERIFIABLE from primary text in this session: dol.gov, federalregister.gov and whitehouse.gov could not be fetched, so the revocation and non-enforcement statements come only from search-result excerpts of the DOL EO 14026 page. What WAS read officially: eCFR (current 2026-11-23) still contains 29 CFR part 23 (no changes since 2024) and FAR 22.403-4/52.222-55. The EO 13658 2026 rate was not read; do not compute with it.

rules.title: Federal construction contracts (EO 13706): 1 hour paid sick leave per 30 hours, cap of 56 hours a year allowed
rules.plain_english: Contracts with the federal Davis-Bacon clause (FAR 52.222-6) include the EO 13706 paid sick leave clause. Covered workers earn at least 1 hour of paid sick leave per 30 hours worked on or in connection with the contract (or the employer can front-load 56 hours at the start of the year). The employer may cap accrual at 56 hours per year, must carry over unused leave, must tell workers their balance in writing every pay period (or month), and must reinstate leave if a worker is rehired within 12 months.

parameters.balance_notice: in writing each pay period or month, whichever shorter
parameters.pay_for_leave_used_by: no later than one pay period after the pay period in which leave was taken

rules.applies_to: Contractors on direct federal contracts that include FAR 52.222-6 (construction) or 52.222-41 (services) performed in the United States
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-52.222-62; https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-13.5 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: Permit each employee engaged in performing work on or in connection with this contract to earn not less than 1 hour of paid sick leave for every 30 hours worked;
rules.effective: JAN 2022 clause version (in effect per eCFR 2026-11-23)
rules.notes: Whether EO 13706 itself has been revoked was not verified (no official source reachable); the FAR clause and 29 CFR part 13 remain codified with no changes since 2024. California paid sick leave (Labor Code 245 et seq.) applies independently; meet both. Note that leave required by EO 13706 or state law cannot be credited toward Davis-Bacon fringe (29 CFR 5.29(f)).

rules.title: Federal-aid jobs run by California agencies: pay the higher of the federal Davis-Bacon or state prevailing rate
rules.plain_english: When a federally funded or assisted project is controlled or carried out by any California awarding body (for example a Caltrans or city federal-aid road job), California prevailing wage law applies along with Davis-Bacon, and the state rate must be paid where it is higher (per classification, per hour). State law does not apply to a project under the complete control of the federal government (e.g., a federal agency's own direct contract on federal land).

parameters.rule: pay max(federal Davis-Bacon rate, California DIR prevailing rate) for each classification and hour
parameters.applies_when: federally funded or assisted project controlled or carried out by a California awarding body
parameters.state_law_not_applicable_when: project under complete control of the federal government
parameters.compare_components: compare total and also observe California's rule that employer payments cannot reduce the Basic Hourly Rate (see fed-ca-dual-coverage-basic-rate)

rules.applies_to: Contractors on federally funded or assisted projects in California that are controlled or carried out by a California awarding body (Caltrans, cities, counties, special districts, school districts, transit agencies)
rules.citation: 8 CCR 16001(b); DLSE Public Works Manual (Oct. 2023) sec. 2.5.2 and 4.2.2.2; Southern Cal. Labor Management Committee v. Aubry (1997) 54 Cal.App.4th 873, 886 (cited in Manual)
rules.quote: (b) Federally Funded or Assisted Projects. The application of state prevailing wage rates when higher is required whenever federally funded or assisted projects are controlled or carried out by California awarding bodies of any sort.
rules.effective: In effect (8 CCR 16001(b); 1996 amendment invalidated and prior text reinstated 1999 per HISTORY note)
rules.notes: Caltrans guidance (dot.ca.gov Labor Compliance Manual) could not be fetched, so the Caltrans statement of this rule was not read; the DIR regulation and DLSE manual are the official sources used. Comparing per classification is the practical method; the regulation says "when higher".

rules.title: Dual-coverage jobs: Davis-Bacon lets fringe credits offset the wage rate, California does not - follow the state rule
rules.plain_english: Under Davis-Bacon alone, employer benefit contributions can be credited toward the whole required hourly package. California does not allow employer payments to reduce the Basic Hourly Rate listed in the state determination. On projects covered by both laws (mixed funding, or federal money run by a California agency), contractors must keep meeting the state requirement, so pay at least the state Basic Hourly Rate in cash and the total package that is higher.

parameters.federal_rule: fringe credits may count toward total hourly wage requirement (29 CFR 5.31)
parameters.california_rule: cash wage >= state Basic Hourly Rate; total >= state Total Hourly Rate (Labor Code 1773.1(c); 8 CCR 16200(a)(3)(I))
parameters.dual_coverage_test: cash_wage >= state_basic_hourly_rate AND cash_wage + creditable_fringes >= max(state_total_hourly_rate, federal_basic_hourly_rate + federal_fringe_rate)
parameters.federal_overtime_floor: for federal overtime (CWHSSA/FLSA), the basic rate used may not be below the federal wage determination basic hourly rate (29 CFR 5.32(a))

rules.applies_to: Contractors on federally funded or assisted projects in California that are controlled or carried out by a California awarding body (Caltrans, cities, counties, special districts, school districts, transit agencies)
rules.citation: DLSE Public Works Manual (Oct. 2023) sec. 4.2.2, 4.2.2.1, 4.2.2.2; 8 CCR 16001(b); Labor Code 1773.1(c); 29 CFR 5.31
rules.quote: Contractors performing work on projects which are governed by both the federal Davis-Bacon Act and the California prevailing wage requirements must, however, continue to comply with state requirements in order to be in compliance with California law.
rules.effective: In effect (DLSE Public Works Manual, October 2023 edition)
rules.notes: The dual-coverage test is derived by combining the rules: the state cash floor (DLSE Manual 4.2.2 / 4.2.2.1 example: $25.00 BHR + $15.00 = $40.00), the higher total, and the federal crediting rule (29 CFR 5.31(b)(3); Manual 4.2.2.2: the Davis-Bacon Act 'does not prohibit the crediting of employer payments ... towards fulfilling the hourly wage rate'). Neither source states the formula itself.
rules.correction: The DLSE Manual 4.2.2-4.2.2.2 statements and the $25 + $15 = $40 example are confirmed (PDF pages 54-55). The derived dual_coverage_test also required cash_wage >= federal_basic_hourly_rate. Neither 29 CFR 5.31 nor Manual 4.2.2.2 states a federal cash floor for straight time: 5.31(b)(3) allows any cash/fringe combination that meets the total, and 4.2.2.2 says Davis-Bacon does not bar crediting employer payments toward the hourly rate. The federal basic rate matters as the overtime base (29 CFR 5.32). The test now uses the state BHR as the cash floor and the higher of the two totals, federal_overtime_floor was added and the notes were updated.

rules.title: Dual-coverage jobs: weekly federal certified payroll AND California DIR eCPR (two separate systems)
rules.plain_english: On a federal-aid project run by a California agency, the federal Davis-Bacon rules require a weekly certified payroll with a Statement of Compliance to the agency, while California's prevailing wage law (which also applies) requires electronic certified payroll reporting to DIR. Filing one does not satisfy the other; keep a single payroll that supports both and file both on their own schedules.

federal.what: weekly certified payroll + Statement of Compliance (WH-347 optional)
federal.due: within 7 days after regular payment date (29 CFR 3.4(a))

rules.applies_to: Contractors on federally funded or assisted projects in California that are controlled or carried out by a California awarding body (Caltrans, cities, counties, special districts, school districts, transit agencies)
rules.citation: 29 CFR 5.5(a)(3)(ii); 29 CFR 3.4(a); 8 CCR 16001(b); Labor Code 1771.4 and 1776 (state rules in rulebook)
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-29/section-5.5 (paragraph (a)(3)(ii)); https://www.dir.ca.gov/t8/16001.html (subsection (b)) (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: The contractor or subcontractor must submit weekly, for each week in which any DBA- or Related Acts-covered work is performed, certified payrolls
rules.effective: 2023-10-23 (federal weekly rule); state eCPR per existing rulebook
rules.notes: This rule is a derived combination: the federal weekly requirement is quoted; the state requirement applies because 8 CCR 16001(b) makes state prevailing wage law apply to these projects, and the eCPR obligation itself is covered by existing rulebook rules (ecpr-monthly-submission, cpr-required-contents). No official source read here states the "two systems" point in one place (gaps.md section 23 raises it).

rules.title: Davis-Bacon general wage determinations are published on SAM.gov and take effect on publication
rules.plain_english: General Davis-Bacon wage determinations are posted on the "Wage Determinations" section of SAM.gov. A general wage determination takes effect on the date it is published there (or when the agency receives it, if earlier), has no expiration date, and stays valid until DOL modifies, supersedes or cancels it. Archived determinations are for information only.

parameters.effective_on: earlier of publication date on SAM.gov or receipt by contracting agency
parameters.expiration: none until modified, superseded or canceled

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California); estimators looking up federal rates
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-22.404-1 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: General wage determinations are published on the Wage Determinations at SAM.gov website.
rules.notes: sam.gov itself could not be fetched; the location comes from the FAR text.

rules.title: Which wage schedule applies: building, residential (up to 4 stories), highway or heavy
rules.plain_english: Federal wage determinations have separate rate schedules by type of construction. Building = enclosed walk-in structures (with incidental site work). Residential = single-family homes and apartments no more than 4 stories. Highway = roads, streets, runways, parking areas not incidental to other work. Heavy = everything else (e.g., water and sewer lines, dams, dredging, flood control). The contract must say which schedule applies to which work; ask DOL before bid opening if unclear.

types.building: sheltered enclosures with walk-in access incl. incidental grading, utilities and paving
types.residential: single family houses or apartments of no more than 4 stories
types.highway: roads, streets, highways, runways, taxiways, alleys, parking areas not incidental to other construction
types.heavy: catch-all for projects not building, residential or highway (e.g., dredging, water and sewer lines, dams, flood control)

parameters.resolve_doubt_before: bid opening or receipt of best and final offers

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and all-tier subcontractors on construction paid for by a federal agency or with federal assistance subject to the Davis-Bacon Act or a Related Act (e.g., federal-aid highway, transit, airport, water/wastewater SRF, HUD-assisted work in California); estimators
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-48/section-22.404-2 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: Residential construction is generally the construction, alteration, or repair of single family houses or apartment buildings of no more than four (4) stories in height
rules.notes: Mirrors California's own residential definition (up to four stories) in 8 CCR 16001(d), but federal and state schedules are separate documents.

rules.title: State agencies (Caltrans, DGS, DWR, ...) procure under their own state rules; 2 CFR 200.318-200.326 (including the 200.326 bond minimums) bind local agencies, not the State
rules.plain_english: When a State, or any agency or instrumentality of a State (for example Caltrans, DGS or DWR), buys or contracts under a federal award, it follows the same policies and procedures it uses with its own money. Only if it has none does it fall back on 2 CFR 200.318 through 200.327. It must still comply with 200.321 (small, minority and women's businesses), 200.322 (domestic preferences), 200.323 (recovered materials) and 200.327 (the Appendix II contract clauses). So the federal minimum bonding of 2 CFR 200.326 (5% bid guarantee, 100% performance and payment bonds) does not govern a California state agency's own contract; state law and the bid documents set the bonds. Cities, counties, special districts, school districts and other local governments, including subrecipients of a State, must follow 200.318 through 200.327.

parameters.state_definition: any State of the United States ... and any agency or instrumentality thereof exclusive of local governments (2 CFR 200.1 'State')

rules.applies_to: Contractors on construction paid with federal financial assistance where the awarding body is a California state agency (Caltrans, DGS, DWR and other State agencies or instrumentalities); contrast local agencies, which follow 2 CFR 200.318-200.327
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.317; https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-2/section-200.1 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: When conducting procurement transactions under a Federal award, a State or Indian Tribe must follow the same policies and procedures it uses for procurements with non-Federal funds.
rules.notes: Whether a particular California body is a State instrumentality (for example the University of California or the California State University) was not researched; the tools treat only named State departments as the State. Federal-aid highway contracts are also governed by 23 CFR part 635 (635.110(b): State DOT bonding procedures need FHWA Division Administrator approval).

rules.title: FTA Buy America: iron, steel and manufactured products produced in the U.S.; a manufactured product needs ALL components of U.S. origin
rules.plain_english: FTA may not obligate funds for a project unless all iron, steel and manufactured products used in it are produced in the United States. Steel and iron: all manufacturing processes in the U.S. (except metallurgical processes refining steel additives); this covers construction materials made primarily of steel or iron (structural steel, beams, columns, running and contact rail), not steel or iron used as components of other manufactured products or rolling stock. A manufactured product: all of its manufacturing processes in the U.S. and all of its components of U.S. origin (a component is U.S. origin if it is manufactured in the U.S., wherever its subcomponents come from). That is stricter than the BABA 55% component test. Rolling stock has its own rule (49 CFR 661.11). FTA may waive the requirement for public interest, non-availability, or price: the price-differential waiver is granted when the lowest bid offering the foreign item times 1.25 is less than the lowest bid offering the U.S. item.

parameters.steel_iron_standard: all steel and iron manufacturing processes in the United States, except metallurgical processes involving refinement of steel additives
parameters.steel_iron_scope: construction materials made primarily of steel or iron used in infrastructure projects (e.g. structural steel or iron, beams and columns, running rail and contact rail); not steel or iron used as components or subcomponents of other manufactured products or rolling stock
parameters.component_us_origin_if: manufactured in the United States, regardless of the origin of its subcomponents
parameters.general_waivers: 49 CFR 661.7 Appendix A: items excepted under FAR 25.104; microprocessors, computers and software used solely to process or store data; small purchases

rules.applies_to: Contractors and suppliers on FTA-assisted projects let by California transit agencies (LA Metro, BART, VTA, SFMTA, MTS, OCTA and others)
rules.citation: 49 CFR 661.1; 49 CFR 661.5(a)-(d); 49 CFR 661.7(b)-(d) and Appendix A
rules.source: https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/section-661.5; https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/section-661.7; https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-49/section-661.1 (eCFR text current as of 2026-11-23, retrieved 2026-11-25 via the eCFR versioner API)
rules.quote: (2) All of the components of the product must be of U.S. origin. A component is considered of U.S. origin if it is manufactured in the United States, regardless of the origin of its subcomponents.
rules.effective: In force (49 CFR 661.5 last amended 74 FR 30239, June 25, 2009; unchanged in eCFR through 2026-11-23)
rules.notes: 2 CFR 184.2(a): part 184 (BABA) does not apply to a Buy America Preference meeting or exceeding section 70914 that a Federal agency applied to infrastructure awards before November 15, 2021. Whether FTA also applies the BABA construction-material standards (lumber, glass, drywall, plastics, non-ferrous metals) on its projects was not read from an FTA source; follow the contract's Buy America provisions. The rolling stock domestic-content percentage (661.11) and the 661.13 certification forms were not read. 661.7(d) still refers to 'section 165(b)(4) of the Act'; its 1.25 test is quoted as written.

rules.title: State minimum wage rises to $17.40/hour on January 1, 2027
rules.plain_english: From January 1, 2027, every California employer must pay at least $17.40 an hour for all hours worked, up from $16.90 in 2026. If the city or county where the work is done has a higher minimum wage, pay the higher rate.

parameters.rule: required_rate = max(state_rate, city_or_county_rate_for_work_location)

rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their employees, including construction contractors
rules.citation: Labor Code 1182.12 (annual inflation adjustment); DIR News Release No. 2026-66 (Aug. 13, 2026)
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/DIRNews/2026/2026-66.html (News Release No. 2026-66, dated August 13, 2026, first paragraph); prior 2026 rate: https://www.dir.ca.gov/iwc/MW-2026.pdf (MW-2026: 'Effective January 1, 2026, Minimum Wage: $16.90 per hour')
rules.quote: Beginning January 1, 2027, California’s statewide minimum wage will increase to $17.40 per hour, helping wages keep pace with inflation and providing greater economic support to workers across the state.
rules.notes: The release says DOF certified the increase on July 31, 2026. The DOF certification letter is on dof.ca.gov, which this session cannot reach. The MW-2027 poster (https://www.dir.ca.gov/iwc/MW-2027.pdf) returned 404 on 2026-11-25, so the 2027 posting text and the 2027 meal and lodging credits are not yet published. The increase, day, week and 2x figures are arithmetic, not quotes. The 2x figure is the 2027 test in the existing rule tools-equipment-employer-provides.
rules.correction: source_location now also names MW-2026, which is the official source for prior_rate_usd ($16.90). News Release 2026-66 does not state the 2026 rate. No value changed: $17.40 from 2027-01-01, DOF certification on July 31, 2026 and piece-rate coverage are in the release. The 0.50, 139.20, 696.00 and 34.80 figures were recomputed from 17.40.

rules.title: Exempt (white-collar) employees must earn at least $72,384 a year from January 1, 2027
rules.plain_english: To treat an office manager, estimator or other salaried employee as exempt from overtime in 2027, you must pay at least $72,384 a year ($1,392 a week), and the job must also pass the duties test.

parameters.also_required: duties and other requirements of the specific exemption

rules.applies_to: Employers classifying employees as exempt executive, administrative or professional employees
rules.citation: DIR News Release No. 2026-66 (Aug. 13, 2026); Labor Code 515; IWC Order 16-2001 §1(A) (as cited in the existing rule exempt-salary-threshold-2026)
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/DIRNews/2026/2026-66.html (section 'Minimum salary requirement for exempt employees'); prior 2026 figure: computed from https://www.dir.ca.gov/iwc/MW-2026.pdf ($16.90) and https://www.dir.ca.gov/IWC/IWCArticle16.pdf §1(A) (two times the state minimum wage for full-time employment)
rules.quote: Beginning January 1, 2027, an employee must earn an annual salary of at least $72,384 to meet the salary threshold for exemption. Employees must also satisfy the duties and other requirements applicable to the specific exemption.
rules.notes: The release shows the formula: $17.40 x 2 x 40 hours per week x 52 weeks per year = $72,384. The monthly and weekly figures are arithmetic. This rule updates exempt-salary-threshold-2026 for 2027. The prior 2026 figure ($70,304) is not printed in the release; it is 2 x $16.90 (MW-2026) x 40 x 52 under IWC Order 16 §1(A).
rules.correction: source_location and notes now name the sources of prior_annual_usd. $70,304 is not printed in the release. It is computed as 2 x $16.90 (MW-2026) x 40 x 52 under IWC Order 16 §1(A), which was read. $72,384 and the formula are in the release. Monthly 6,032 and weekly 1,392 were recomputed. No value changed.

rules.title: Construction companies with office staff must also post Wage Order 4
rules.plain_english: Wage Order 16 covers your field crews. If you also employ office staff such as bookkeepers or estimators, post Wage Order 4 as well.

wage_orders_to_post: IWC Order 16 (on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining occupations)
IWC Order 4 (professional, technical, clerical, mechanical and similar occupations)
parameters.trigger: a construction employer that also employs office help

rules.applies_to: Construction employers with office or clerical employees
rules.citation: IWC Order 16-2001 §20 and IWC Order 4-2001 §22 (Posting of Order); DIR workplace postings FAQ Q1
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/FAQworkplacepostings3.htm (Question 1); https://www.dir.ca.gov/IWC/IWCArticle16.pdf (§20 POSTING OF ORDER); https://www.dir.ca.gov/IWC/IWCArticle4.pdf (§22 POSTING OF ORDER)
rules.quote: A construction company (Wage Order 16) employing office help also needs Wage Order 4.

The parameters are unchanged and match FAQ Q1.

rules.title: Postings may be kept in a binder at a jobsite that has only a trailer
rules.plain_english: If a jobsite has no wall to post on, for example only an on-site trailer, you may keep the required postings in a binder. Tell workers where it is and keep it easy to reach without asking.

parameters.binder_allowed_only_when: no room to post (examples: construction site with only an on-site trailer; outdoor agricultural site)
conditions: tell employees where the binder is located
binder available to employees
employees have easy access
employees do not have to walk a long distance
employees do not have to ask to see the material

rules.quote: Some situations where this could be acceptable are a construction site where there is only an on-site trailer, or an agricultural site where the workplace is outdoors. If employers put postings in a binder, they must tell employees where the binder is located, have the binder available for employees, ensure employees have easy access to postings and don't have to walk a long distance or ask to see the material.

rules.title: Post the minimum wage notice in Spanish when workers read only Spanish
rules.plain_english: The wage orders exist only in English. If any of your workers speak and read only Spanish, also post the state minimum wage notice in Spanish.

parameters.trigger: employees who speak and read only Spanish

parameters.english_reading_workforce: the posted IWC order covers minimum wage; separate MW notice not needed

rules.notes: On 2026-11-25 the DIR postings page (https://www.dir.ca.gov/wpnodb.html) listed the Spanish minimum wage notice as '(Spanish Coming Soon)'.

rules.title: Replace a posting only when its content changes; downloaded posters are valid
rules.plain_english: You do not need new posters every year unless the content changes. The wage orders and the minimum wage notice change every year. Free posters downloaded from the agency meet the legal requirement.

changes_annually: IWC wage orders (computer professional exemption rate)
state minimum wage notice (rate changes each January 1)

rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their employees, including construction contractors
