rules.plain_english: If an employee reports to the jobsite as required but is sent home or given less than half the scheduled day, pay half the scheduled day (at least 2, at most 4 hours) at the regular rate, unless the cause was threats, utility failure, or an Act of God or other cause outside the employer's control.

parameters.rate: regular rate, not below minimum wage
exceptions: threats to employees or property, or civil authorities recommend not working
public utilities fail to supply electricity, water or gas, or failure of utilities or sewer
Act of God or other cause not within employer's control
parameters.cba: applies unless CBA expressly provides otherwise

rules.applies_to: Nonexempt employees in on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining occupations (IWC Wage Order 16-2001)
rules.quote: Each workday that an employee is required to report to the work site and does report, but is not put to work or is furnished less than half of his/her usual or scheduled day’s work, the employer shall pay him/her for half the usual or scheduled day’s work, but in no event for less than two (2) hours nor more than four (4) hours at the employee’s regular rate of pay
rules.notes: Weather: rain-outs may fall under 'Act of God' exception - fact specific. WO16 §5 does not contain the separate 'second reporting' 2-hour rule that appears in Orders 1-15 and in the generic DLSE FAQ; do not apply it to WO16 employees without verification. DLSE: not applicable to paid standby or regularly scheduled shifts under 2 hours.

rules.title: Travel after the first required location is paid time
rules.plain_english: Once an employee reaches the first place the employer requires them to be (e.g., the yard or first jobsite), later employer-required travel (yard to jobsite, jobsite to jobsite) must be paid, at overtime rates if it pushes hours over the thresholds.

parameters.trigger: travel occurring after the first location where employee's presence is required by employer
parameters.rate: regular rate or overtime premium where Labor Code 510 / WO16 §3 thresholds are exceeded

rules.applies_to: Nonexempt employees in on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining occupations (IWC Wage Order 16-2001)
rules.quote: All employer-mandated travel that occurs after the first location where the employee’s presence is required by the employer shall be compensated at the employee’s regular rate of pay or, if applicable, the premium rate that may be required by the provisions of Labor Code Section 510 and Section 3, Hours and Days of Work, above.

rules.title: Paid sick leave: at least 40 hours or 5 days per year
rules.plain_english: Employers must let employees use at least 40 hours or 5 days of paid sick leave per year, whichever is more (a worker on 10-hour days gets 50 hours).

parameters.rule: greater of 40 hours or 5 x normal shift length
parameters.year: calendar, fiscal, anniversary, or other 12-month period chosen by employer
parameters.local_ordinance: follow more generous local ordinance except preempted topics (lending, paystubs, calculation, notice, payment timing, termination payout)
purposes_include: own or family member's illness, diagnosis, care, treatment, preventive care
jury duty and court appearance as witness (from 2025-01-01)

rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.quote: Starting on January 1, 2024, an employer must allow an employee to use at least five days or 40 hours, whichever is more (refer to DLSE Opinion Letter 2015.08.07).
rules.notes: DLSE FAQ updated December 31, 2025. Some purposes depend on employer size (25+ employees for certain family-member violence-related uses).

rules.title: Sick leave eligibility: 30 days worked in a year; usable after 90 days
rules.plain_english: An employee who works at least 30 days within a year for the same employer in California is covered (including part-time and temporary). They can start using sick leave after their 90th day of employment.
rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.quote: All employees who work at least 30 days for the same employer within a year in California, including part-time, per diem, in-home supportive services (IHSS) providers, and temporary employees, are covered by this law with some narrow exceptions.
rules.notes: The 90-day employment period before use is stated on the same DLSE page. Employer may advance leave earlier.

rules.title: Sick leave accrual: 1 hour per 30 worked, or 24 hours by day 120 and 40 by day 200
rules.plain_english: Under an accrual plan, employees earn at least 1 hour of sick leave per 30 hours worked. Other schedules are allowed if the employee has 24 hours by the 120th day and 40 hours by the 200th day. Alternatively, frontload 40 hours/5 days each year.

parameters.frontload_option: 40 hours/5 days available at start of each 12-month period; new hires 24h/3 days by day 120 and 40h/5 days by day 200

rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.quote: must earn at least one hour of paid sick leave for each 30 hours of work (the 1:30 schedule). Although employers may adopt or keep other types of accrual schedules (other than 1:30), the schedule must result in an employee having at least 24 hours of accrued sick leave or paid time off by the 120th calendar day of employment and 40 hours by the 200th calendar day of employment.
rules.notes: Exempt employees are deemed to work 40 hours/week for accrual unless normal week is less (statutory detail not read).

rules.title: Sick leave caps: use capped at 40h/5 days; accrual capped at 80h/10 days
rules.plain_english: An employer may limit sick leave use to 40 hours or 5 days a year and may cap total accrued balance at 80 hours or 10 days. Unused accrued leave carries over.

parameters.cap_rule: whichever is more of hours vs. days

rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.quote: the law allows employers to limit an employee’s use of paid sick leave to 40 hours or five days during a year. The law also allows an employer to limit an employee’s total accrued paid sick leave to no more than 80 hours or ten days.

rules.title: Sick leave minimum increment may not exceed 2 hours
rules.plain_english: Employees choose how much sick leave to use; the employer may set a minimum increment of no more than 2 hours. Requests may be oral or written, and leave cannot be conditioned on finding a replacement or solely on a doctor's note.

parameters.notice: advance if foreseeable; as soon as practicable if not

rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.quote: An employer can set a reasonable minimum amount of hours for each time an employee takes paid sick leave, not to exceed two hours.

rules.title: Sick pay due by next regular payday; rate calculation
rules.plain_english: Sick leave taken must be paid no later than the next regular payday. Non-exempt workers are paid their regular non-overtime rate for the week of use, or the 90-day average method.

parameters.pay_deadline: payday for the next regular payroll period after leave was taken
nonexempt_rate_methods: regular non-overtime rate for the workweek the leave was used
total non-OT compensation in prior 90 days / non-OT hours in full pay periods of prior 90 days
parameters.exempt_rate: same as other forms of paid leave

rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.quote: The paid sick leave law requires that an employer provide payment for sick leave taken by an employee no later than the payday for the next regular payroll period after the sick leave was taken.

rules.title: Show sick leave balance on pay stub; keep sick leave records 3 years
rules.plain_english: The available sick leave balance must appear on the pay stub or a document given the same day as pay ('unlimited' is allowed for unlimited plans). Records of sick leave earned and used must be kept for 3 years.

parameters.records: hours (days) accrued and used per employee

rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.quote: Employers must show how many days of sick leave you have available on your pay stub, or on a document issued the same day as your paycheck.
rules.notes: 3-year record retention stated in the next sentence of the same DLSE FAQ answer.

rules.title: No sick leave payout at termination; restore if rehired within 12 months
rules.plain_english: Unused sick leave does not have to be paid out when employment ends (unless policy says so or it is PTO), but it must be reinstated if the employee is rehired within 12 months.

parameters.exception: PTO covering sick leave that was paid out at separation need not be restored

rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.quote: The paid sick leave law requires that your accrued and unused sick leave be restored to you if you return to the same employer within 12 months from the previous separation.
rules.notes: If the employer uses a combined PTO/vacation policy, vested PTO must be paid at separation as vacation (Labor Code 227.3).

rules.title: Construction CBA exemption from paid sick leave law
rules.plain_english: Construction employees covered by a union agreement with specified provisions are fully exempt from the state paid sick leave law. Other qualifying CBAs (paid leave, OT premiums, pay at least 30% above minimum wage) are only partially exempt and must still follow anti-retaliation and use rules.

parameters.construction_cba_fully_exempt: if CBA meets Labor Code 245.5 construction criteria (not read)

must_provide: paid sick days or PTO usable for sick purposes
premium rates for all OT hours

rules.applies_to: Union-represented construction employees
rules.quote: Employees in the construction industry covered by a collective bargaining agreement with specified provisions.
rules.notes: The DLSE FAQ lists this as a full exemption but does not spell out the construction-CBA criteria in Labor Code 245.5(a)(2); the statute could not be read (leginfo blocked). Verify before treating any CBA as exempt.

rules.title: Post the paid sick leave poster; include sick leave terms in 2810.5 notice
rules.plain_english: Display the Labor Commissioner's paid sick leave poster where employees can read it during the workday, and give each nonexempt employee the 2810.5 Notice to Employee that states the sick leave terms.

parameters.poster: Labor Commissioner Paid Sick Leave poster (2026 update)
poster_must_state: right to accrue, request and use paid sick days
right to file complaint with Labor Commissioner

rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.quote: Employers are required to display a poster in an area frequented by employees where it may be easily read during the workday.

rules.title: Paid sick leave violation penalties
rules.plain_english: Unlawfully withholding sick pay can cost the greater of three times the sick pay withheld or $250. If a violation causes other harm, such as firing or other retaliation, the employee can also get $50 for each day or part of a day the violation continues. Separately, if the employer does not comply promptly and the Labor Commissioner must take further enforcement action, the employer owes the State $50 per day for each affected employee. Unpaid amounts carry 10% interest, and willfully failing to post the sick leave poster costs $100. The $4,000 caps reported for these amounts are not confirmed.

parameters.withheld_sick_pay_penalty: greater of 3 x value of sick days withheld or $250
parameters.state_penalty_trigger: prompt compliance not forthcoming and Labor Commissioner must take additional enforcement action, incl. civil action (per DLSE Manual 30.8)
parameters.source_of_restructured_values: DLSE Enforcement Policies and Interpretations Manual 30.7-30.8 (Dec 2017); statute not read

rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.notes: Figures from search-result excerpts (Justia copy of 248.5) and Seyfarth summary; the trigger for the $50/day penalty was not confirmed. Verify the statute before using in calculations.
rules.correction: Status stays unverifiable. The DLSE manual describes the $50/day amount differently from the rule. The $50 per day (or part of a day) is employee damages when a violation causes other harm, such as discharge or retaliation. Separately, a $50 per day, per employee penalty goes to the State when the employer does not comply promptly and the Labor Commissioner must take further enforcement action. The rule merged these into one "administrative_penalty". The manual also gives 10% interest and a $100 penalty for willful posting violations. Its aggregate caps are garbled ("$8,000, $4000 ... and $4,000"), so the $4,000 caps remain unconfirmed. Parameters restructured with per-source labels. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: Itemized wage statement (pay stub): 9 required items
rules.plain_english: Each payday (or semimonthly) give employees a pay stub showing: gross wages, total hours, piece units and rates, all deductions, net pay, pay period dates, employee name and last 4 of SSN (or ID), employer legal name and address, and every hourly rate with hours at each rate. Also show available sick leave.

parameters.frequency: semimonthly or at each payment of wages (check, cash, or otherwise)
required_items: gross wages earned
total hours worked (not for salaried overtime-exempt)
number of piece-rate units earned and applicable piece rates
all deductions (employee-authorized may be aggregated as one item)
net wages earned
inclusive dates of the pay period
employee name and last four digits of SSN or an employee ID number
name and address of the legal entity that is the employer
all applicable hourly rates in effect and hours worked at each rate
parameters.form: detachable part of check or separate writing

rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.quote: Pursuant to Labor Code Section 226(a), semimonthly or every time you are paid your wages, whether by check, in cash, or otherwise, you must be given a detachable part of the check or a separate writing showing required information.
rules.notes: List of items is from the DLSE Paydays FAQ (which also links sample hourly and piece-rate stubs). Labor Code 226(a) also requires the employer to keep copies for at least 3 years (statute not read). Piece-rate employees also need rest/recovery and nonproductive time lines under Labor Code 226.2 (not read).

rules.title: Pay stub violation penalties ($50 / $100 per pay period, max $4,000)
rules.plain_english: An employee injured by a knowing and intentional pay stub violation can recover the greater of actual damages or $50 for the first pay period and $100 for each later pay period, up to $4,000, plus attorney's fees.
rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.notes: Amounts consistent across multiple secondary sources in search results; statute not read. Separate civil penalties under Labor Code 226.3 were reported inconsistently by sources (one: $250 initial / $1,000 subsequent per employee per violation) - not included as a rule.

rules.title: Payroll and time records: required fields, keep 3 years
rules.plain_english: Keep accurate records for every employee (name, address, occupation, SSN, birth date if a minor, daily start/stop times, meal periods, total daily hours, wages and rates, piece-rate details) in English and ink, at the jobsite or a central location, for at least 3 years.

parameters.location: place of employment or central location
parameters.format: English, ink or other indelible form, dated with month/day/year
required_fields: date of birth if under 18 and minor designation
time records of when each work period begins and ends
total wages paid each payroll period incl. value of board/lodging
total hours worked in payroll period and applicable rates
piece rates or incentive plan explanation; accurate production record
need_not_record: meal periods during which operations cease
parameters.public_works: Labor Code 1776 certified payroll requirements also apply

rules.applies_to: Nonexempt employees in on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining occupations (IWC Wage Order 16-2001)
rules.quote: The employer who has control over wages, hours, or working conditions shall also keep said records on file at the place of employment or at a central location for at least three years.
rules.notes: Records must be available to the employee on reasonable request.

rules.title: Produce payroll records within 21 calendar days of request ($750 penalty)
rules.plain_english: When a current or former employee asks (orally or in writing) to inspect or copy their payroll records, the employer must comply within 21 calendar days or owe a $750 penalty.
rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.quote: Your payroll records must be made available to you upon reasonable request, which request must be complied with by your employer as soon as practicable, but no later than 21 calendar days from the date you make such request.

rules.title: Personnel file: inspection/copy within 30 days of written request; keep 3 years after employment ends
rules.plain_english: Keep each employee's personnel records for at least 3 years after their employment ends. When a current or former employee asks in writing, let them inspect the records or give them a copy within 30 calendar days (charge no more than the actual copying cost). You need to honor only one request a year from a former employee. Failure: $750 penalty.

parameters.copy_charge: not more than actual cost of reproduction

rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.quote: The employer must make the employee’s personnel records available within 30 calendar days from the date the employer receives a written request for inspection.
rules.notes: CBA exception exists if CBA meets 30%-above-minimum-wage and inspection-procedure criteria.
rules.correction: The retention period runs from termination. Personnel records must be kept "not less than three years after termination of employment", which the rule's unqualified "retention_years: 3" left ambiguous. Replaced it with retention_years_after_termination = 3 and added the one-request-per-year limit for former employees. The 30-day inspection and copy deadlines, written request, $750 penalty, cost-of-reproduction charge, exclusions and CBA exception are confirmed. Rewording 2026-11-27: title and plain_english reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: Give copies of any signed employment document on request
rules.plain_english: On request, give an employee or job applicant a copy of anything they signed relating to getting or keeping the job.

parameters.trigger: request from employee or applicant
parameters.scope: any instrument signed relating to obtaining or holding employment

rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.quote: Employers are required to give an employee or job applicant, upon request, a copy of any instrument that the employee or applicant has signed relating to the obtaining or holding of employment.

rules.title: Final pay due immediately on discharge or layoff
rules.plain_english: When an employee is fired or laid off (including at the end of a project), all wages, including accrued vacation, are due immediately at the time of termination, at the place of termination.

includes: accrued unused vacation/PTO at final rate

rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.quote: An employee who is discharged must be paid all of his or her wages, including accrued vacation, immediately at the time of termination.
rules.notes: Direct deposit authorization terminates at separation unless employee voluntarily authorizes it for final pay and Labor Code 213(d) is met.

rules.title: Final pay on quitting with 72+ hours' notice: due on last day
rules.plain_english: If an employee gives at least 72 hours' notice and quits on that date, all wages including vacation are due at the time of quitting.
rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.quote: An employee without a written employment contract for a definite period of time who gives at least 72 hours prior notice of his or her intention to quit, and quits on the day given in the notice, must be paid all of his or her wages, including accrued vacation, at the time of quitting.
rules.notes: If the employer cuts the notice short and ends employment earlier, it becomes a discharge: pay immediately.

rules.title: Final pay on quitting without notice: within 72 hours
rules.plain_english: If an employee quits without 72 hours' notice, final wages are due within 72 hours. The employee may ask for the check to be mailed; the mailing date counts as the payment date.

parameters.place_if_not_mailed: employer office in the county where work was performed (Labor Code 208)

rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.quote: An employee without a written employment contract for a definite period of time who quits without giving 72 hours prior notice must be paid all of his or her wages, including accrued vacation, within 72 hours of quitting.

rules.title: Oil drilling layoffs: final pay within 24 hours (excluding weekends/holidays)
rules.plain_english: Oil drilling employees who are laid off must be paid within 24 hours, not counting Saturdays, Sundays and holidays.
rules.applies_to: Employers in the business of oil drilling (drilling occupations under Wage Order 16)
rules.quote: An employee engaged in the business of oil drilling who is laid off must be paid within 24 hours after discharge, excluding Saturdays, Sundays, and holidays.

rules.title: Waiting time penalty: one day's pay per day late, up to 30 days
rules.plain_english: If final wages are willfully paid late, the employer owes the employee's daily rate of pay for each calendar day they are late, up to 30 days.

parameters.day_type: calendar days including weekends and holidays
parameters.daily_rate: regular hours per day x hourly rate; include overtime only if regularly scheduled each week
stops_accruing: filing a court action (a DLSE claim does not stop it)
parameters.defense: good faith dispute that wages are due (8 CCR 13520)

rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.quote: The penalty is measured at the employee's daily rate of pay and is calculated by multiplying the daily wage by the number of days that the employee was not paid, up to a maximum of 30 days.
rules.notes: Unpaid accrued vacation at separation triggers the penalty; unreimbursed expenses do not.

rules.title: Pay all undisputed wages even when some are disputed
rules.plain_english: Even in a dispute, the employer must pay all wages that are not in dispute, with no release or condition. Failing to do so defeats a good-faith defense to waiting time penalties.

parameters.rule: pay undisputed amount unconditionally at the time due

rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.quote: Even if there is a dispute, the employer must pay, without requiring a release, whatever wages are due and not in dispute.

rules.title: Cannot require a release of wage claims before paying; also CSLB discipline
rules.plain_english: An employer cannot require an employee to sign a release of wage claims unless those wages have actually been paid, or require signing a timesheet the employer knows is false as a condition of pay. Doing so is a misdemeanor and a cause for CSLB license discipline.

parameters.includes: requiring a statement of hours worked the employer knows is false as condition of pay

rules.applies_to: All employers; licensed contractors face CSLB discipline
rules.source: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/LawReferenceBook2021.pdf PDF page 892 (Appendix, Labor Code §206.5, 2021 edition); and PDF page 351 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (B&P §7110.1)
rules.quote: An employer shall not require the execution of a release of a claim or right on account of wages due, or to become due, or made as an advance on wages to be earned, unless payment of those wages has been made.
rules.notes: Labor Code 206.5 text read from the 2021 CSLB Law Book appendix (official CSLB publication; 2026 edition omits the appendix). B&P 7110.1 in the 2026 Law Book: requiring a release in violation of LC 206.5 is a cause for disciplinary action.

rules.title: Vacation is wages: no forfeiture; pay out unused vacation at final rate
rules.plain_english: Earned vacation cannot be forfeited ('use it or lose it' is illegal), though a reasonable accrual cap is allowed. All vested, unused vacation must be paid at the final rate when employment ends.

parameters.payout_at_separation: all vested unused vacation at final rate of pay
parameters.cba_exception: unless a CBA provides otherwise (Labor Code 227.3)

rules.applies_to: Employers that offer paid vacation or PTO
rules.quote: a policy that provides for the forfeiture of vacation pay that is not used by a specified date ("use it or lose it") is an illegal policy under California law and will not be recognized by the Labor Commissioner.
rules.notes: Union construction trades often handle vacation through trust funds under CBAs.

rules.title: Pay at least twice a month: 1st-15th by the 26th; 16th-end by the 10th
rules.plain_english: Most employees must be paid at least twice a month on regular paydays. Wages for the 1st-15th are due by the 26th of the same month; wages for the 16th-end of month are due by the 10th of the next month.

parameters.holiday_rule: if payday falls on a holiday the business observes by closing, pay next business day
parameters.exempt_EAP_option: may be paid once a month on or before the 26th if full month's salary (incl. unearned portion) is paid
parameters.timecard_not_submitted: must still pay wages reasonably known to be due on payday

rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.quote: Wages earned between the 1st and 15th days, inclusive, of any calendar month must be paid no later than the 26th day of the month during which the labor was performed, and wages earned between the 16th and last day of the month must be paid by the 10th day of the following month.

rules.title: Weekly/biweekly payroll: pay within 7 calendar days after period ends
rules.plain_english: For weekly, biweekly or other pay periods that are not the 1st-15th / 16th-end split, pay within 7 calendar days after the end of the pay period.
rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.quote: Other payroll periods such as weekly, biweekly (every two weeks) or semimonthly (twice per month) when the earning period is something other than between the 1st and 15th, and 16th and last day of the month, must be paid within seven calendar days of the end of the payroll period within which the wages were earned.

rules.title: Post a payday notice (day, time, place of payment)
rules.plain_english: Post a notice showing the regular paydays and the time and place of payment. An employer-made notice is fine. Not posting it, or not paying on payday, is a misdemeanor.
rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.quote: The employer must establish a regular payday and is required to post a notice that shows the day, time and location of payment.

rules.title: Late or short pay penalty: $100 first, $200 + 25% subsequent/willful
rules.plain_english: Paying wages late (or short) on a regular payday costs $100 per employee per failure for a first violation, and $200 per employee per failure plus 25% of the wages withheld for later or willful violations. This includes late meal/rest premiums.
rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.quote: For any initial violation the penalty is one hundred dollars ($100) for each failure to pay each employee. For each subsequent violation or any willful or intentional violation the penalty is two hundred dollars ($200) for each failure to pay each employee, plus 25% of the amount of wages unlawfully withheld.

rules.title: Register with EDD and pay payroll taxes once wages exceed $100 in a quarter
rules.plain_english: A contractor with employees must register with EDD, get a state employer account number, and pay state payroll and unemployment insurance taxes for employees earning over $100 in a calendar quarter.

parameters.obtain: state employer identification (EDD payroll tax account) number

rules.applies_to: Contractors with one or more employees
rules.citation: Unemployment Insurance Code (EDD registration); 2026 CSLB Law Book Ch. 3
rules.source: PDF page 41 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: The contractor must register with the Employment Development Department, obtain a state EIN, and pay state payroll and unemployment insurance taxes for employees who earn over $100 in a calendar quarter.
rules.notes: See edd-registration-15-day-deadline for the registration deadline (from EDD, not read directly).

rules.title: Register with EDD within 15 days after paying over $100 in a quarter
rules.plain_english: Register as an employer with EDD within 15 days after first paying more than $100 in wages in a calendar quarter.
rules.applies_to: New employers
rules.citation: Unemployment Insurance Code (EDD employer registration; section not verified)
rules.quote: If you operate a business and employ one or more employees, you must register as an employer and set up an EDD payroll tax account within 15 days of paying more than $100 in wages in a calendar quarter.
rules.notes: edd.ca.gov was blocked in this session; quote is from a search-result excerpt of the EDD page. Statute section number not verified.

rules.title: Report new hires, and rehires after a 60-day separation, to EDD (DE 34) within 20 days
rules.plain_english: Report each new employee who works in California to EDD's New Employee Registry within 20 days of hiring. Report a rehire only if they had been separated from your company for at least 60 days in a row. Employers that report electronically submit two transmissions a month, 12 to 16 days apart. Unless there is good cause, EDD may charge $24 for each hire not reported on time, or $490 if the employer and employee conspired not to report it or to file a false or incomplete report.

parameters.start_of_work_date: first day employee performed services for wages
parameters.includes_rehires: only if the employee had been separated from prior employment with this employer for at least 60 consecutive days (UI Code 1088.5(b))
data_fields: employee first name, middle initial, last name
parameters.electronic_or_magnetic_filers: two monthly transmissions not less than 12 and not more than 16 days apart (UI Code 1088.5(d)(2))

rules.applies_to: All California employers
rules.citation: Unemployment Insurance Code 1088.5 (California New Employee Registry)
rules.source: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/LawReferenceBook2021.pdf PDF pages 1160-1161 (Appendix, Unemployment Insurance Code §1088.5); https://edd.ca.gov/en/payroll_taxes/new_hire_reporting/ (not fetched; host blocked)
rules.quote: (d) (1) Employers shall submit a report as described in paragraph (4) within 20 days of hiring any employee whom the employer is required to report pursuant to this section.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the 2021 CSLB Law Book appendix (UI Code 1088.5); check for post-2021 amendments. EDD pages are still blocked, so the EDD e-Services/DE 34 method and the "calendar days" wording come from the original search excerpt.
rules.correction: The statute (UI Code 1088.5) confirms the 20-day deadline but narrows the rehire rule. A rehire must be reported only if the employee had been separated from that employer for at least 60 consecutive days; the rule said all rehires. The rule also marked the penalty as unverified. The statute sets $24 per failure, or $490 if the failure comes from employer-employee conspiracy or a false or incomplete report, unless there is good cause. Electronic and magnetic filers must submit two monthly transmissions 12-16 days apart. Replaced the EDD search-excerpt quote with statute text and updated the source fields. The EDD wording "20 calendar days of start-of-work date" was not seen; the statute says "within 20 days of hiring". Rewording 2026-11-27: title and plain_english reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: Report independent contractors (DE 542) within 20 days of $600 payment or contract
rules.plain_english: If you pay an individual or sole-proprietor contractor $600 or more (or sign a contract for $600+) in a year, report them to EDD on the DE 542 within 20 days of whichever comes first.

parameters.trigger: earlier of paying $600+ or entering a contract for $600+ in a calendar year

rules.applies_to: Service-recipients (businesses) that hire independent contractors
rules.notes: From search summary of EDD pages; an EDD Spanish PDF says 20 business days vs. English 'calendar days' - unresolved. Statute section not verified.

rules.title: EDD pamphlets to give employees (DE 2515, DE 2511, DE 2320)
rules.plain_english: Give new hires the State Disability Insurance (DE 2515) and Paid Family Leave (DE 2511) pamphlets, and give 'For Your Benefit' (DE 2320) to employees who are terminated, laid off or go on leave.

parameters.DE_2515: new hires and employees taking non-work-related disability leave
parameters.DE_2511: new hires and employees taking PFL-covered leave
parameters.DE_2320: employees terminated, laid off, or going on leave of absence
parameters.DE_1857A_poster: post (employers subject to UI, DI and PFL)

rules.applies_to: Employers subject to California UI/SDI/PFL
rules.citation: Unemployment Insurance Code (EDD required notices; sections not verified)
rules.notes: From search summary of the EDD Required Notices and Pamphlets page. Check current revision numbers before generating packets. DE 1857A posting is independently listed on the DIR postings page (read).

rules.title: Required workplace postings checklist (DIR list)
rules.plain_english: Post the required state and federal notices where employees can easily read them during the workday (Wage Order 16, minimum wage, sick leave, payday, Cal/OSHA, workers' comp, whistleblower, discrimination, EDD, voting, federal posters, and others depending on size and work).

postings.posting: Safety and health protection on the job (Cal/OSHA)
Access to medical and exposure records
postings.who: employers using hazardous or toxic substances

postings.posting: Notice to employees - injuries caused by work (workers' comp)
Notice of workers' compensation carrier and coverage
Whistleblower protections (lettering larger than 14-point, AG hotline number)

postings.who: employers with 11 or more employees in previous year

postings.posting: Prevailing wage determinations at each job site
postings.who: public works awarding bodies and contractors

postings.posting: California law prohibits workplace discrimination and harassment (CRD-E07P-ENG)
Family care and medical leave (CFRA) and pregnancy disability leave (CRD-100-21ENG)
EDD Notice to employees - UI benefits (DE 1857D)
postings.who: listed for all employers on DIR page

postings.timing: not less than 10 days before every statewide election

postings.posting: Equal Employment Opportunity is the law (incl. ADA)
Notice of inspection by immigration agencies
postings.who: employer receiving notice of I-9 inspection

parameters.location: area frequented by employees where it may be easily read during the workday

rules.applies_to: All California employers (any size) and their nonexempt employees, including construction contractors
rules.citation: Various (see parameters); DIR Workplace Postings page
rules.quote: The Department of Industrial Relations requires employers to post information related to wages, hours and working conditions in an area frequented by employees where it may be easily read during the workday.
rules.notes: DIR page dated March 2025 (KYR section updated for 2026); the DIR list states it is not all-inclusive. DE 1857D is normally for UI-only employers - DIR lists both as 'All employers'.

rules.title: Post Wage Order 16 (or make it available at remote jobsites)
rules.plain_english: Keep Wage Order 16 posted where employees can easily read it. If the work location makes posting impractical (e.g., a remote jobsite), keep a copy and give it to any employee who asks. Post the MW-2026 minimum wage order next to it.

parameters.if_posting_impractical: keep copy and make available to every employee upon request

rules.applies_to: Nonexempt employees in on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining occupations (IWC Wage Order 16-2001)
rules.quote: Every employer shall keep a copy of this order posted in an area frequented by employees where it may be easily read during the workday. Where the location of work or other conditions make this impractical, every employer shall keep a copy of this order, and make it available to every employee upon request.
rules.notes: Current republished version: IWC Form 1114 (Rev. 11/2025).

rules.title: Annual Workplace Know Your Rights notice by February 1 (SB 294)
rules.plain_english: Every employer must give all employees the state's Workplace Know Your Rights notice on or before February 1 each year (first due February 1, 2026), in the language normally used with them if a template exists. Penalty up to $500 per employee.

content_categories: notice of I-9 inspection by immigration agencies
constitutional rights when interacting with law enforcement at the workplace
new laws affecting workplace rights (as determined by Labor Commissioner)

rules.applies_to: All California employers
rules.citation: Labor Code 1550-1559 (SB 294, Workplace Know Your Rights Act)
rules.quote: On or before February 1, 2026, and each year after that, an employer must provide employees a required workplace rights notice.
rules.notes: Secondary sources also say the notice must go to new hires and that compliance records be kept 3 years - not stated on the DIR pages read; verify against Labor Code 1550-1559.

rules.title: Offer emergency-contact designation and notify contact on arrest/detention at work (SB 294)
rules.plain_english: By March 30, 2026, employers had to let employees name an emergency contact and choose whether that contact is called if they are arrested or detained at work. If so designated, the employer must notify the contact. Penalty up to $500 per day per employee, max $10,000 per employee.

parameters.trigger: employee arrested or detained on worksite, or during work hours off-site when employer has actual knowledge

rules.applies_to: All California employers
rules.quote: By March 30, 2026, an employer must provide employees the opportunity to name emergency contacts and to indicate whether the emergency contact should be notified if the employee is arrested or detained.
rules.notes: Secondary sources say employees hired after March 30, 2026 must be offered designation at hire - not on DIR pages read; verify.

rules.title: Post notice of immigration I-9 inspection within 72 hours
rules.plain_english: If an immigration agency gives notice that it will inspect I-9s or other employment records, post a notice to employees (and inform their union representative if any) within 72 hours.

parameters.trigger: receipt of notice of inspection of I-9 or other employment records by an immigration agency
parameters.template: DIR Notice of Inspection by Immigration Agencies (English/Spanish)

rules.applies_to: All California employers
rules.quote: employers are required to provide notice to employees of any inspection of I-9 Employment Eligibility Verification forms or other employment records by an immigration agency by posting a notice within 72 hours of receiving the notification of inspection.
rules.notes: Employers may not voluntarily consent to immigration agents entering non-public areas without a judicial warrant (per KYR notice).

rules.title: Wage Theft Prevention Act Notice to Employee at hire; update changes within 7 days
rules.plain_english: At hire, give each nonexempt employee a written Notice to Employee with pay rates (including OT), payday, employer names/addresses/phone, workers' comp carrier and policy, and sick leave terms. Give written notice of any change within 7 calendar days unless it appears on the next pay stub.

change_exceptions: all changes shown on timely wage statement (Labor Code 226)
changes provided in another legally required writing within 7 days
required_fields: rate(s) of pay and basis (hour, shift, day, week, salary, piece, commission, other) incl. overtime rates
meal/lodging allowances claimed against minimum wage
employer legal name and any DBA names
physical address of main office and mailing address
workers' comp carrier name, address, phone and policy number (or self-insurance certificate)
staffing agency client entity info (if applicable)
state/federal emergency or disaster declaration issued within 30 days before first day that may affect health/safety
parameters.language: language employer normally uses to communicate employment information
parameters.construction_piece_rates: may attach a sheet listing piece-rate ranges with criteria for each rate
parameters.public_works: must list all known applicable prevailing rates, not just 'prevailing wage'

rules.applies_to: All private employers for nonexempt employees
rules.quote: Workers have to receive the required notice containing specific information at the time of hire: (A) the rate or rates of pay and basis thereof, whether paid by the hour, shift, day, week, salary, piece, commission, or otherwise, including any rates for overtime, as applicable; (B) allowances, if any, claimed as part of the minimum wage, including meal or lodging allowances;
rules.notes: Employee signature only acknowledges receipt.

rules.title: Form I-9: Section 1 on first day; Section 2 within 3 business days
rules.plain_english: New employees complete Section 1 of Form I-9 by their first day of work for pay. The employer must examine documents and complete Section 2 within 3 business days of the hire (same day if the job lasts less than 3 business days).

parameters.section_1_deadline: at time of hire (first day of work for wages)
parameters.short_job_lt_3_business_days: complete Sections 1 and 2 at time of hire; receipts not accepted
parameters.hire_definition: actual commencement of employment for wages or other remuneration
parameters.reverification: no later than the date work authorization expires

rules.applies_to: All U.S. employers, for every new hire
rules.quote: (B) Complete section 2—“Employer Review and Verification”—on the Form I-9 within three business days of the hire and sign the attestation with a handwritten signature or electronic signature in accordance with paragraph (i) of this section.
rules.notes: California: requiring the I-9 within 3 business days is a safe harbor under B&P 494.6(c); don't over-verify (Labor Code 1019.1).

rules.title: Form I-9 retention: later of 3 years after hire or 1 year after termination
rules.plain_english: Keep each employee's I-9 for 3 years after the hire date or 1 year after employment ends, whichever is later.

parameters.document_copies: optional; if made, keep with the I-9

rules.applies_to: All U.S. employers
rules.quote: (A) In the case of an employer, three years after the date of the hire or one year after the date the individual's employment is terminated, whichever is later; or

rules.title: I-9 paperwork penalties $288-$2,861 per form (assessed after July 3, 2025)
rules.plain_english: Federal fines for I-9 paperwork violations are $288 to $2,861 per person; knowingly employing unauthorized workers costs $716-$5,724 per worker for a first order and more for repeat orders.
rules.applies_to: All U.S. employers
rules.quote: (a) For civil penalties assessed after July 3, 2025, whose associated violations occurred after November 2, 2015, the civil monetary penalties provided by law within the jurisdiction of the Department are adjusted as set forth in the fifth column of table 1 to this section.
rules.notes: Amounts are inflation-adjusted roughly annually; refresh from 28 CFR 85.5.

rules.title: CSLB license not at risk for requiring I-9 within 3 business days
rules.plain_english: A licensed business can lose its license for immigration-related retaliation under Labor Code 244(b), but requiring a new or current employee to submit an I-9 within 3 business days of the first day of paid work is not a violation.

parameters.risk: license suspension/revocation for LC 244(b) violations (threatening to report immigration status in retaliation)

rules.applies_to: Licensees regulated by the Business and Professions Code, including contractors
rules.source: PDF page 211 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: An employer shall not be subject to suspension or revocation under this section for requiring a prospective or current employee to submit, within three business days of the first day of work for pay, an I-9 Employment Eligibility Verification form.

rules.title: Prohibited unfair immigration-related practices (I-9 / E-Verify misuse)
rules.plain_english: Employers may not refuse genuine-looking I-9 documents, use E-Verify where not required (e.g., to re-verify current employees or screen only some workers), or threaten to report workers or families to immigration authorities for exercising their rights.

prohibited: refusing I-9 documents that appear genuine
using E-Verify in a way not required or authorized by law (unrequired reverification, selective screening)
reporting or threatening to report employee or family to immigration authorities
filing or threatening false reports to police or agencies

rules.applies_to: All California employers
rules.citation: Labor Code 1019, 1019.1, 1019.2; Immigrant Worker Protection Act (AB 450)
rules.quote: Refusing to accept identification documents during the I-9 process (proof of ID and federal permission to work) that appear to be genuine.
rules.notes: Summarized from the Labor Commissioner's 2026 Know Your Rights notice template; statutes themselves not read.

rules.title: Workers' comp insurance required with even one (part-time) employee
rules.plain_english: Any employer with one or more employees, even part-time or family members, must carry workers' compensation insurance (or be an approved self-insurer). Employees cannot be charged for it.

methods: DIR certificate of consent to self-insure (Labor Code 3700)
CBA alternative dispute resolution program (Labor Code 3201.5)

rules.applies_to: All contractors/employers with employees
rules.source: PDF page 44 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book; https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/FAQ-Workers%20Compensation.pdf; https://www.dir.ca.gov/dwc/FactSheets/Employer_FactSheet.pdf
rules.quote: If the employer has one or more employees, even part-time, they are required to insure for workers’ compensation claims.
rules.notes: DLSE FAQ: limited exceptions where the only workers are partners, or corporate officers who are sole shareholders (coverage by election).

rules.title: C-8, C-20, C-22, C-39, C-61/D-49 must carry workers' comp even with no employees
rules.plain_english: Contractors without employees normally file a workers' comp exemption with CSLB, except holders of Concrete (C-8), HVAC (C-20), Asbestos Abatement (C-22), Roofing (C-39) and Tree Service (C-61/D-49), who must carry workers' comp regardless.

classes_requiring_wc_regardless_of_emplo: C-20 Warm-Air Heating, Ventilating and Air-Conditioning
parameters.other_classes_without_employees: file Certificate of Exemption with CSLB

rules.applies_to: CSLB licensees
rules.source: PDF page 45 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: If you don’t have employees, you must file an exemption from the workers’ compensation requirement unless you hold one of these classifications which requires you to carry workers’ compensation insurance: C-8 Concrete; C-20 Warm-Air Heating, Ventilating and Air-Conditioning; C-22 Asbestos Abatement; C-39 Roofing; C-61/D-49 Tree Service.
rules.notes: Overlaps the CSLB licensing domain; included because it controls whether a WC policy is mandatory.

rules.title: Keep a current workers' comp certificate (or exemption) on file with CSLB
rules.plain_english: A licensee must always have a current Certificate of Workers' Compensation Insurance or Self-Insurance on file with CSLB in the business name; the insurer can file it electronically.

documents: Certificate of Exemption (if no employees and eligible)

rules.applies_to: CSLB licensees and applicants
rules.source: PDF page 45 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: B&P Code section 7125 provides that an applicant or licensee always has on file a current and valid Certificate of Workers’ Compensation Insurance or Certification of Self-Insurance in the licensee’s business name.

rules.title: Give new hires written workers' comp rights notice by end of first pay period
rules.plain_english: Give every new employee a written notice of their workers' compensation rights at hire or by the end of their first pay period, in English and Spanish if there are Spanish-speaking employees.

parameters.deadline: at hire or by end of first pay period

rules.applies_to: All employers subject to workers' compensation law
rules.source: PDF page 46 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Give every new employee, either at the time of hiring or by the end of their first pay period, written notice of the employee’s right to receive workers’ compensation benefits should they be injured on the job while working for the employer.

rules.title: Post the workers' comp Notice to Employees poster
rules.plain_english: Conspicuously post the workers' comp Notice to Employees (showing your carrier) where employees frequent, in English and Spanish if there are Spanish-speaking employees. Not posting it is a misdemeanor.

parameters.content: 8 CCR 9881, or Administrative Director's approved poster (8 CCR 9881.1)

rules.applies_to: All employers subject to workers' compensation law
rules.source: PDF page 46 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book; https://www.dir.ca.gov/wpnodb.html (redirect target of https://www.dir.ca.gov/wp.asp)
rules.quote: Post conspicuously, in a location frequented by employees, a Notice to Employees poster.
rules.notes: Employers may obtain printed copies and the claim form from their claims administrator.

rules.title: Give injured employee a DWC-1 claim form within one working day
rules.plain_english: Within one working day of learning of a work injury or illness, give the employee a workers' comp claim form (DWC 1); when it is returned, complete the employer part, give the employee a copy and send it to the claims administrator.

parameters.from: employer knowledge of injury or illness
next_steps: complete employer portion of returned form

rules.applies_to: All employers
rules.quote: Provide a claim form (DWC form 1) within one working day of finding out about an injury or illness.
rules.notes: Fact sheet dated September 2024; the PDF's two-column layout interleaves a sidebar word in the extracted text.

rules.title: File employer's injury report (DLSR 5020) within 5 days
rules.plain_english: For any work injury or illness causing lost time beyond the day of injury or treatment beyond first aid, file a complete report (Form 5020, including the employee's SSN) with your insurer within 5 days of learning of it.

parameters.form: DLSR 5020 Employer's Report of Occupational Injury or Illness
parameters.trigger: lost time beyond date of injury/illness or medical treatment beyond first aid
parameters.file_with: insurer (insured employers) or DIR Division of Labor Statistics and Research
parameters.failure: WCAB may order report within 5 days; noncompliance punishable as contempt (Labor Code 3760)

rules.applies_to: All employers
rules.source: PDF page 45 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book and PDF page 46 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: five days after the employer obtains knowledge of the injury or illness. Each report of occupational injury or occupational illness must indicate the Social Security number of the injured employee (Labor Code §6409.1).

rules.title: Report serious injury, illness or death to Cal/OSHA immediately
rules.plain_english: For any serious injury or illness or a death, in addition to the 5020 report, report immediately to Cal/OSHA by phone or email.

parameters.to: Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA)

rules.applies_to: All employers
rules.source: PDF page 46 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: In every case involving a serious injury or illness, or death, in addition to the report described above, the employer must report immediately by telephone or email to the Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Labor Code §6409.1).
rules.notes: The Cal/OSHA regulation (8 CCR 342) sets the specific hour limit; see Cal/OSHA domain.

rules.title: Authorize medical treatment within one working day of claim form ($10,000 interim cap)
rules.plain_english: Within one working day after receiving the employee's claim form, authorize medical treatment and keep providing it until the claim is accepted or rejected; liability during that time is limited to $10,000.

parameters.standard: ACOEM guidelines or DWC treatment utilization schedule

rules.applies_to: Employers/insurers
rules.source: PDF page 47 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Within one working day of receiving the employee’s claim form, the employer must authorize treatment for the alleged industrial injury and must continue to provide the treatment until the date that liability for the claim is either accepted or rejected by the employer.
rules.notes: Usually handled by the insurer for insured employers.

rules.title: Notify workplace crime victims of workers' comp eligibility
rules.plain_english: If an employee is the victim of a crime at work, give them written notice that they are eligible for workers' compensation.

parameters.trigger: employee is victim of workplace crime

rules.applies_to: All employers
rules.source: PDF page 47 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Give any employee who is a victim of workplace crime written notification that the employee is eligible for workers’ compensation (Labor Code §3553).

rules.title: Temporary disability: starts after 3rd day at 2/3 of weekly earnings
rules.plain_english: Temporary disability checks begin after the third day of disability at two-thirds of weekly earnings (up to a state maximum). If disability lasts more than 14 days or involves overnight hospitalization, the 3-day wait is eliminated.
rules.applies_to: Employers/insurers of injured employees
rules.source: PDF page 47 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: These weekly payments begin after the third day of disability and are based upon two-thirds of the weekly earnings, up to a legal maximum.
rules.notes: Current min/max TD rates are published annually by DWC (not read).

rules.title: Penalties for no workers' comp: greater of 2x premium or per-employee amount; more after a claim
rules.plain_english: If caught without workers' comp, the penalty is the greater of twice the premium you would have paid or a per-employee amount; if found after an injury claim, $2,000 per employee (non-compensable) or $10,000 per employee (compensable). It is also a misdemeanor and grounds for CSLB license suspension.

parameters.base_penalty: greater of 2 x premiums for uninsured period or per-employee amount
other_consequences: lien on real and personal property (Labor Code 3727)

rules.applies_to: Employers without required coverage
rules.source: PDF page 48 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book and PDF page 49 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book; https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/FAQ-Workers%20Compensation.pdf
rules.quote: (Penalties for an uninsured contractor may be either the greater of twice the amount the contractor would have paid in premiums during the period they were uninsured, or $1,000 per employee employed during that same period.
rules.notes: CONFLICT: the 2026 CSLB Law Book says $1,000 per employee; the DLSE workers' comp FAQ says the per-employee amount has been $1,500 since January 1, 2011. Labor Code 3722 could not be read (leginfo blocked). Use the higher figure for risk estimates and verify.
rules.correction: Not corrected, but the two official sources still conflict on the per-employee base penalty ($1,000 CSLB 2026 book vs $1,500 DLSE FAQ). DLSE is the enforcing agency and its figure is the later-dated change; added per_employee_usd_for_risk_estimates = 1500 pending a read of LC 3722(b).

rules.title: Stop order bars use of employee labor until workers' comp is obtained
rules.plain_english: The Labor Commissioner can issue a stop order prohibiting any use of employee labor until workers' compensation insurance is in place.

parameters.effect: no employee labor may be used until insurance is provided
parameters.issuer: DIR Division of Labor Standards Enforcement

rules.applies_to: Employers without required coverage
rules.source: PDF page 48 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Issuing a “Stop Order,” prohibiting the use of employee labor until insurance is provided (Labor Code §3710.1).
rules.notes: Failure to observe a stop order is also CSLB-disciplinable (B&P 7127, licensing domain).

rules.title: Willfully uninsured employer: benefits + 10% penalty + fees and civil suit
rules.plain_english: If a contractor willfully fails to carry workers' comp and an employee is injured, it must pay disability compensation plus a 10% penalty and attorney fees, provide all medical care, and can be sued with a presumption of negligence.

also: civil damages; presumption of employer negligence; contributory negligence no defense

rules.applies_to: Willfully uninsured employers
rules.source: PDF page 49 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: If a contractor willfully fails to provide compensation insurance for an employee and an injury occurs, the contractor must pay the disability compensation plus a penalty of 10 percent and attorney fees.

rules.title: Serious and willful employer misconduct: compensation increased by one-half (uninsurable)
rules.plain_english: If an employee is hurt because of the employer's (or a manager's/superintendent's) serious and willful misconduct, the compensation is increased by 50% plus up to $250 costs, and insurance cannot cover the increase.
rules.applies_to: All employers
rules.source: PDF page 48 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: The amount of compensation otherwise recoverable can be increased one-half, together with costs and expenses not to exceed $250, where the employee is injured by reason of the serious or willful misconduct of the employer or their managing representative, partner, executive, managing officer, or general superintendent.
rules.notes: Other uninsurable exposures: injury to illegally employed minor under 16 (LC 4557) and LC 132a discrimination.

rules.title: ABC test: worker is an employee unless all three prongs are met
rules.plain_english: A worker is presumed to be an employee. To treat them as an independent contractor, the hiring company must prove (A) no control over how the work is done, (B) the work is outside the company's usual business, and (C) the worker runs an independent business of the same kind.

prongs.A: free from control and direction of hiring entity, under contract and in fact
prongs.B: work outside usual course of hiring entity's business
prongs.C: customarily engaged in independently established trade, occupation or business of same nature

rules.applies_to: All hiring entities in California
rules.quote: Under the ABC test, a worker is considered an employee and not an independent contractor, unless the hiring entity satisfies all three of the following conditions:
rules.notes: Prong B usually fails when a contractor hires a worker to do the same trade it performs. DLSE FAQ revised June 2026.

rules.title: Construction subcontractor exemption: Borello + Labor Code 2750.5 instead of ABC
rules.plain_english: For certain individuals working under a construction subcontract who meet Labor Code 2781's conditions, employee status is decided under the older Borello multifactor test and Labor Code 2750.5 rather than the ABC test.
rules.applies_to: Contractors engaging individuals under construction subcontracts
rules.quote: Certain individuals performing work under a subcontract in the construction industry, including construction trucking (with certain specific conditions applicable to construction trucking only through December 31, 2024). Labor Code section 2750.5 also governs the determination of employee status along with Borello.
rules.notes: See lc-2781-subcontractor-criteria for the list of conditions (not read from primary text).

rules.title: Labor Code 2781 conditions for the construction subcontract exemption
rules.plain_english: To use the construction subcontractor exemption, the contractor must show the subcontract is in writing, the sub holds a CSLB license covering the work, and the sub carries responsibility for errors (insurance, indemnity, bonds or warranties), among other conditions such as running its own independent business.

criteria: (a) subcontract is in writing [confirmed by search excerpt]
(b) subcontractor licensed by CSLB and work within scope of license [confirmed by search excerpt]
(c) subcontractor holds any required business license or business tax registration [secondary/unconfirmed]
(d) subcontractor maintains a business location separate from the contractor's [secondary/unconfirmed]
(e) subcontractor has authority to hire and fire others to provide or assist with services [secondary source]

(f) subcontractor assumes financial responsibility for errors or omissions, evidenced by insurance, legally authorized indemnity obligations, performance bonds, or warranties [confirmed by search excerpt]
(g) subcontractor customarily engaged in an independently established business of the same nature [secondary source]

rules.applies_to: Contractors engaging individuals under construction subcontracts
rules.source: https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=2781 (not fetched; blocked); excerpts via FindLaw/california.public.law search results
rules.quote: employee of the contractor shall be governed by Section 2750.5 and by Borello, if the contractor demonstrates that all the following criteria are satisfied: (a) The subcontract is in writing.
rules.notes: leginfo blocked; the quote is a FindLaw search excerpt. Only (a), (b) and (f) were seen in search excerpts; the remaining items come from secondary summaries and must be verified against the official text before a tool relies on the exact list. A contract-generator can still require: written subcontract, CSLB license number and class matching the scope, proof of insurance/bond/warranty.

rules.title: Business-to-business exception cannot be used for CSLB-licensed work
rules.plain_english: The general business-to-business exception to the ABC test is not available when the service provider is doing work that requires a CSLB contractor license; construction must use the construction-specific exemption instead. The referral-agency exception also excludes construction except minor home repair.

parameters.referral_agency_exception_excludes: construction services other than minor home repair

rules.applies_to: Hiring entities using contractors for construction work
rules.quote: The service provider is not performing the type of work for which a license from the Contractors’ State License Board is required.

rules.title: Unlicensed workers doing licensed work are presumed employees (Labor Code 2750.5)
rules.plain_english: Anyone doing work that requires a CSLB license (or working for someone who must be licensed) is presumed to be an employee, and can be an independent contractor only if they hold a valid contractor's license and meet the independence factors.

rebuttal_factors: right to control manner of performance; result is primary factor bargained for
customarily engaged in independently established business
bona fide status, not a subterfuge (investment, holding out, project pricing, own tools, hiring employees, license, etc.)

rules.applies_to: Contractors and owners hiring workers for work requiring a CSLB license
rules.source: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/LawReferenceBook2021.pdf PDF pages 945-946 (Appendix, Labor Code §2750.5); referenced in PDF page 44 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: There is a rebuttable presumption affecting the burden of proof that a worker performing services for which a license is required pursuant to Chapter 9 (commencing with Section 7000) of Division 3 of the Business and Professions Code, or who is performing such services for a person who is required to obtain such a license is an employee rather than an independent contractor.
rules.notes: Text read from the 2021 CSLB Law Book appendix (last amended 1979 per the book). The 2026 Law Book references §2750.5 on PDF page 44 but omits the appendix.

rules.title: Willful misclassification: $5,000-$15,000 per violation ($10,000-$25,000 pattern)
rules.plain_english: Willfully misclassifying a worker as an independent contractor (or charging them fees/deductions) costs $5,000-$15,000 per violation, or $10,000-$25,000 for a pattern or practice. For licensed contractors, CSLB must start discipline within 30 days of receiving the order, and a public notice must be posted for a year.

parameters.also_unlawful: charging misclassified worker fees or deductions that would be illegal for an employee

rules.applies_to: Any person or employer; licensed contractors referred to CSLB
rules.quote: the person or employer shall be subject to a civil penalty of not less than five thousand dollars ($5,000) and not more than fifteen thousand dollars ($15,000) for each violation, in addition to any other penalties or fines permitted by law.
rules.notes: Text from the 2021 edition of the CSLB Law Book appendix; check for later amendments.

rules.title: Paid advisors who knowingly recommend misclassification are jointly liable
rules.plain_english: Someone paid to knowingly advise an employer to treat a worker as an independent contractor to avoid employee status is jointly and severally liable if the worker is found to be an employee (does not apply to the employer's own employees or to attorneys giving legal advice).
rules.applies_to: Consultants, payroll/HR providers and other paid advisors
rules.quote: A person who, for money or other valuable consideration, knowingly advises an employer to treat an individual as an independent contractor to avoid employee status for that individual shall be jointly and severally liable with the employer if the individual is found not to be an independent contractor.
rules.notes: Relevant to software that recommends classification - keep outputs informational.

rules.title: A 1099, a contract or a label does not make someone an independent contractor
rules.plain_english: Calling someone an independent contractor, having them sign an agreement saying so, or paying them on a 1099 does not decide their status; the ABC (or Borello) test does.
rules.applies_to: All hiring entities
rules.citation: Labor Code 2775 et seq.; DLSE IC FAQ
rules.quote: Being labeled an independent contractor, being required to sign an agreement stating that one is an independent contractor, or being paid as an independent contractor (that is, without payroll deductions and with income reported by an IRS Form 1099 rather than a W-2), does not determine employment status.

rules.title: Specialty contractor may not use more than one sub in its own class unless subs use employees
rules.plain_english: On a single project, a specialty contractor cannot subcontract to more than one subcontractor in its own license classification unless the subcontractor uses workers classified as employees for that work, or the specialty contractor is signatory to a CBA covering the work and subcontracting.

conditions_allowing_more: subcontractor employs persons classified as employees (not independent contractors) to perform that classification's work on the project
specialty contractor is signatory to a bona fide CBA covering the work that addresses subcontracting

rules.applies_to: Specialty (C-class) contractors
rules.source: PDF page 261 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: A specialty contractor shall not enter into a contract for the performance of work on the same single project or undertaking with more than one subcontractor in the same license classification as the specialty contractor offering the contract, unless either of the following requirements are satisfied:

rules.title: Don't sign construction labor contracts without enough money to comply with labor law
rules.plain_english: A person or company may not contract with a construction contractor for labor or services if it knows or should know the price is too low for the contractor to follow labor laws. A contract meeting Labor Code 2810(d) creates a presumption of compliance.

exceptions: party that executes a CBA covering the workers
homeowner contracting for work on own residence where a family member resides at least part of the year
parameters.safe_harbor: rebuttable presumption of no violation if contract meets all 2810(d) requirements
parameters.should_know_includes: failure to request or obtain information required by statute or contract counts as knowledge
parameters.covers: any person acting as a construction contractor, licensed or not

rules.applies_to: Owners, developers and general contractors contracting for construction labor or services
rules.quote: A person or entity may not enter into a contract or agreement for labor or services with a construction, farm labor, garment, janitorial, or security guard contractor, where the person or entity knows or should know that the contract or agreement does not include funds sufficient to allow the contractor to comply with all applicable local, state, and federal laws or regulations
rules.notes: DIR-hosted Word copy of the statute (file dated 2020); verify no later amendments.

rules.title: Labor Code 2810(d) construction labor contract: required written terms
rules.plain_english: To get the safe harbor, the contract with a construction contractor must be one written document containing: parties' names/addresses/phones; work description and start/finish dates; contractor's state employer tax ID; workers' comp policy and carrier; vehicle IDs and auto insurance; worker housing address; number of workers, total wages and pay dates; contractor's fee; number of independent contractors and their license numbers; and signatures and date.

parameters.format: in writing, in a single document
required_terms: name, address and telephone number of the person/entity and of the construction contractor
description of labor or services and when they will commence and be completed
contractor's employer identification number for state tax purposes
workers' compensation policy number and carrier name, address and telephone
VIN of each contractor-owned vehicle used for transportation under the contract, vehicle liability policy number, carrier name/address/phone
address of any real property used to house workers
total number of workers, total amount of all wages to be paid, and date(s) wages will be paid
amount of commission or other payment to the contractor
total number of persons used as independent contractors and their current local, state and federal contractor license numbers
signatures of all parties and date signed
parameters.material_changes: in writing, single document, with all affected provisions

rules.applies_to: Contracts with construction contractors for labor or services (to claim the 2810(b) presumption)
rules.quote: a contract or agreement with a construction, farm labor, garment, janitorial, or security guard contractor for labor or services must be in writing, in a single document, and contain all of the following provisions, in addition to any other provisions that may be required by regulations
rules.notes: DIR-hosted copy (file dated 2020). Good candidate for a contract-generation checklist.

rules.title: Keep the 2810 contract for 4 years after it ends
rules.plain_english: Keep a copy of the written construction labor contract (and written changes) for at least 4 years after the contract ends.
rules.applies_to: Persons/entities contracting with construction contractors
rules.quote: A person or entity who enters into a contract or agreement referred to in subdivisions (d) or (e) shall keep a copy of the written contract or agreement for a period of not less than four years following the termination of the contract or agreement.

rules.title: Labor Code 2810 damages: greater of actual or $250/$1,000 per employee
rules.plain_english: An injured worker can sue the party that signed an underfunded construction labor contract for the greater of actual damages or $250 per employee per violation (first) and $1,000 per employee for later violations, plus attorney's fees.

parameters.requires: employee injured by a labor law violation in performing the contract

rules.applies_to: Persons/entities contracting with construction contractors
rules.quote: may file an action for damages to recover the greater of all of his or her actual damages or two hundred fifty dollars ($250) per employee per violation for an initial violation and one thousand dollars ($1,000) per employee for each subsequent violation

rules.title: Direct contractor liable for subcontractors' unpaid wages (private works)
rules.plain_english: On private construction contracts entered on or after January 1, 2018, the direct (general) contractor is jointly liable for unpaid wages, fringe or other benefit payments or contributions, and interest owed by subcontractors at any tier, but not for penalties or liquidated damages. The Labor Commissioner must file its action within 1 year of the earliest of: recording a notice of completion, recording a notice of cessation, or actual completion of the work. It does not cover work done by employees of the state, a city, a county, a special district or another political subdivision. The direct contractor can demand payroll records from subs.

parameters.liability_scope: unpaid wages, fringe/other benefit payments or contributions, interest; not penalties or liquidated damages (218.7)
parameters.payroll_records_request: subcontractor must provide on direct contractor's request
parameters.withhold_disputed_sums: if sub fails to provide records (unconfirmed)
parameters.labor_commissioner_action_deadline: within 1 year of the earliest of: recordation of notice of completion, recordation of notice of cessation, or actual completion of the work (per DLSE Enforcement Manual 25.3.1)
parameters.not_applicable_to: work performed by employees of the state, a special district, a city, a county or other political subdivision (DLSE Manual 25.3.2)

rules.applies_to: Direct contractors on private works
rules.notes: From search summaries of AB 1701 text and law-firm alerts; Labor Code 218.8 (separate, later contracts) reportedly includes penalties and liquidated damages - not verified. Strong candidate for a subcontractor-payroll-records workflow once statute text is verified.
rules.correction: Status stays unverifiable. The DLSE manual confirms the scope (private works, subcontractor at any tier, unpaid wages, fringe/benefit contributions and interest, no penalties or liquidated damages) and adds a missing limit: a Labor Commissioner action must be filed within one year of the earliest of recording a notice of completion, recording a notice of cessation, or actual completion. The section does not apply to work by public-entity employees. The 30-day pre-suit notice and the withholding right are still unconfirmed. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: Attorney General can sue to discipline a license for unpaid wages
rules.plain_english: The Attorney General can sue to discipline, deny or block renewal of a contractor's license if the contractor failed to pay workers the wages owed, did not satisfy a wage judgment, or violated a wage order or injunction; the AG notifies the Registrar 30 days before filing.

grounds: failure to pay full wages owed under state law
violating injunction/court order on wage payment

rules.applies_to: CSLB licensees and applicants
rules.source: PDF page 262 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: The civil action shall be brought on the grounds that a person has failed to pay its workers the full amount of wages that the workers are entitled to under state law, has not fulfilled a wage judgment, or is in violation of an injunction or court order regarding the payment of wages to its workers.

rules.title: CSLB must start discipline within 18 months of a willful Labor Code violation finding
rules.plain_english: When the Registrar receives a Labor Commissioner finding of a willful Labor Code violation (or Cal/OSHA citations), it must start disciplinary action against the license within 18 months.

parameters.from: registrar's receipt of certified Labor Commissioner finding (LC 98.9) or DOSH citations

rules.applies_to: CSLB licensees
rules.source: PDF page 352 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: the registrar shall initiate disciplinary action against the licensee within 18 months from the date of the registrar’s receipt of the violation.

rules.title: Record and keep cash wage payments for 3 years (license discipline)
rules.plain_english: Licensees must record and keep for at least 3 years every cash transaction used to pay employee wages, and show them to the board on request; investigative costs up to $2,500 can be charged.

parameters.scope: all cash transactions in payment of employee wages
parameters.failure_to_produce: grounds for discipline; unpaid costs may lead to revocation

rules.applies_to: All DCA licensees including contractors who pay wages in cash
rules.source: PDF page 150 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
