rules.quote: the licensee has failed to record and preserve for not less than three years, any and all cash transactions involved in the payment of employee wages by a licensee.
rules.notes: Cash-paid workers still require itemized wage statements (Labor Code 226).

rules.title: LLC licensees need a $100,000 bond for unpaid wages (plus $25,000 license bond)
rules.plain_english: A contractor licensed as an LLC must have a $100,000 surety bond on file, in addition to the $25,000 contractor bond, for employees harmed by the LLC's failure to pay wages, interest on wages or fringe benefits. The bond is required to issue, reissue, reinstate, reactivate or renew the license and for its continued valid use, so keep it in force the whole time the license is active. It is not required while the license is inactive. If the LLC is party to a collective bargaining agreement, the bond also covers welfare fund, pension fund and apprentice program contributions.

required_for: continued valid use of the LLC license

rules.applies_to: Limited liability company licensees
rules.source: PDF page 42 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (summary); PDF page 296 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (B&P 7071.6.5 statute text)
rules.quote: A $100,000 surety bond (in addition to the $25,000 contractor bond) is required for the issuance, reissuance, reinstatement, reactivation, and renewal of an LLC license for the benefit of any employee or worker damaged by the LLC’s failure to pay wages, interest on wages, or fringe benefits, as well as other contributions.
rules.notes: Bond rules overlap the licensing domain; included for wage-claim exposure.
rules.correction: The $100,000 LLC bond and $25,000 license bond are confirmed. The statute also makes the bond a condition of continued valid use of the LLC license, so it must be kept in force continuously, not only at issuance or renewal. It does not apply while the license is inactive, and for an LLC that is party to a CBA it also covers welfare, pension and apprentice fund contributions. Updated required_for and added those parameters. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: Wage claims on the license bond: $4,000 cap; file within 6 months of discovery
rules.plain_english: Employee wage and fringe benefit claims against a contractor's license bond are capped at $4,000 in total, must be brought within 6 months after the delinquency is discovered, and no lawsuit more than 2 years after the payments were due.
rules.applies_to: Employees and employee organizations claiming against contractor license bonds
rules.source: PDF page 300 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book and PDF page 301 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (a) The aggregate liability of a surety on a claim for wages and fringe benefits brought against a bond required by this article, other than a bond required by Section 7071.8, shall not exceed the sum of four thousand dollars ($4,000).
rules.notes: Same 6-month/2-year wage-claim limits apply to deposits given in lieu of a bond (B&P 7071.4(f)(3), PDF page 293).

rules.title: Cal-WARN: 60 days' written notice before mass layoff, relocation or termination
rules.plain_english: A covered employer must give written notice at least 60 days before a mass layoff, relocation or termination at a covered establishment, to affected employees and EDD (and local officials), including the federal WARN notice elements.

recipients_per_EDD_secondary: chief elected official of each city and county affected
parameters.content: notice elements required by federal WARN (29 U.S.C. 2101 et seq.) plus state elements
parameters.exemption_request: Director may grant exemption under Labor Code 1402.5

rules.applies_to: Employers with a covered establishment (see cal-warn-coverage-thresholds)
rules.quote: Generally, “an employer may not order a mass layoff, relocation, or termination at a covered establishment unless, 60 days before the order takes effect, the employer gives written notice of the order” to employees and the Employment Development Department
rules.notes: Secondary sources report SB 617 (2025) added notice content requirements effective 2026 - not verified.

rules.title: Cal-WARN violation: back pay and benefits up to 60 days
rules.plain_english: An employer that fails to give Cal-WARN notice owes each affected employee back pay and benefits for up to 60 days, or half the number of days the employee worked there, whichever is smaller.
rules.applies_to: Covered employers
rules.quote: for back pay and the value of the cost of any benefits the employee may have been entitled to up to a maximum of 60 days or one-half the number of days that the employee was employed by the employer, whichever is smaller.
rules.notes: Secondary sources add 'for the period of violation' (days without notice) as a further limit - not on the DIR page.

rules.title: Cal-WARN coverage: 75+ employees at an establishment; mass layoff = 50+ in 30 days
rules.plain_english: Cal-WARN applies to an establishment that has employed 75 or more full- or part-time employees in the past 12 months. A mass layoff is 50 or more employees laid off within any 30-day period; relocation means moving operations more than 100 miles.
rules.applies_to: Employers with a covered establishment
rules.notes: From search summaries of EDD's WARN page and statute excerpts (one secondary source wrongly states 75 for mass layoff). Courts generally require 75 at a single site.

rules.title: Cal-WARN civil penalty up to $500 per day
rules.plain_english: Failing to give Cal-WARN notice can also bring a civil penalty of up to $500 for each day of the violation, avoided if affected employees are paid what is owed within 3 weeks of the layoff order.
rules.applies_to: Covered employers
rules.notes: From search excerpt of a 2009 code version; verify current text.

rules.title: Cal-WARN exemption for completion of a construction project
rules.plain_english: Cal-WARN does not apply when a layoff results from finishing a particular project of a Wage Order 16 (construction, drilling, logging, mining) employer, if workers were hired with the understanding their job would last only for that project.

exempt_if: layoff/closing results from completion of a particular project or undertaking
employer subject to IWC Wage Order 16 (also 11, 12)
employees hired with understanding employment limited to duration of the project
parameters.documentation_tip: state project-limited duration in offer letters/2810.5 notice

rules.applies_to: Construction employers subject to Wage Order 16
rules.notes: From law-firm summaries (Littler, Seyfarth) and a 2020 Justia code excerpt; section numbering moved in 2022 (AB 1601) per one source. Verify current text before relying on it.

rules.title: Equal Pay Act claims: 3 years to file, up to 6 years of back pay (SB 642)
rules.plain_english: From 2026, an employee can bring an Equal Pay Act claim up to 3 years after the last violation and recover for the whole period of the violation, up to 6 years.

accrual_events: each time wages are paid as a result

rules.applies_to: All California employers
rules.quote: SB 642 establishes that an employee may bring an Equal Pay Act claim up to three years after the last date the cause of action occurs.
rules.notes: Implies keeping pay records well beyond 3 years for pay-equity defense.

rules.title: Employers with 15+ employees must include pay scale in job postings
rules.plain_english: Employers with 15 or more employees must put the pay range (salary or hourly range they reasonably expect to pay) in every job posting, including through third parties; links or QR codes don't count. Keep job title and wage history records.

parameters.pay_scale: salary or hourly wage range employer reasonably expects to pay
parameters.records: job title and wage rate history for duration of employment + 3 years (per secondary source)

rules.applies_to: Employers with 15 or more employees
rules.notes: From search summaries (Labor Commissioner guidance described by law firms). Verify statute.
rules.correction: Not corrected. Before relying on this rule, check the current 432.3 text for 2025 amendments, such as any redefinition of "pay scale".

rules.title: Harassment prevention training for employers with 5+ employees
rules.plain_english: Employers with 5 or more employees must give 2 hours of sexual harassment and abusive conduct prevention training to supervisors and 1 hour to non-supervisors, repeated every 2 years.
rules.applies_to: Employers with 5 or more employees (counting contractors per CRD)
rules.notes: From search summaries of CRD FAQs and releases; the 6-month new hire/new supervisor timing was not confirmed in search results.

rules.title: Wage Order violations: $50 (first) / $100 (subsequent) per employee per pay period
rules.plain_english: Violating Wage Order 16 adds a civil penalty of $50 per underpaid employee per pay period for a first violation and $100 for later violations, on top of the unpaid wages (which go to the employee).
rules.applies_to: Nonexempt employees in on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining occupations (IWC Wage Order 16-2001)
rules.quote: (1) Initial Violation - $50.00 for each underpaid employee for each pay period during which the employee was underpaid in addition to the amount which is sufficient to recover unpaid wages.
rules.notes: Same amounts appear in Labor Code 558 per search results. Labor Code 1197.1 minimum-wage citation amounts were not verified.

rules.title: Child labor violations: $500 to $10,000 civil penalties
rules.plain_english: Violating child labor laws can bring civil penalties of $500 to $10,000 plus criminal penalties. Minors attending school may need work permits.
rules.applies_to: Employers of minors
rules.quote: Any employer or other person acting on behalf of the employer is subject to civil penalties of $500 to $10,000 as well as to criminal penalties for violation of child labor laws.
rules.notes: Hazardous-occupation restrictions for minors in construction are in the Labor Code (not read).

rules.title: Provide elevators when employees work 60+ feet above or below ground
rules.plain_english: Where practicable, provide elevators or similar service when employees work 60 feet or more above or below ground level.

parameters.qualifier: where practicable and consistent with industry-wide standards

rules.applies_to: Nonexempt employees in on-site construction, drilling, logging and mining occupations (IWC Wage Order 16-2001)
rules.quote: adequate elevators, escalators, or similar service consistent with industry-wide standards for the nature of the process and the work performed, shall be provided when employees are employed sixty (60) feet or more above or below ground level.
rules.notes: Does not exceed Cal/OSHA Standards Board regulations.

rules.title: Which employees Wage Order 16 covers
rules.plain_english: Wage Order 16 covers on-site construction work (alteration, demolition, building, excavation, renovation, remodeling, maintenance, improvement, repair, and any work needing a CSLB license), plus drilling, logging and mining. Exempt executives/administrators/professionals, outside salespeople and the owner's immediate family are excluded from most hours provisions.

covered: mining (not covered by LC 750 et seq.)
exclusions: parent, spouse, child or adopted child of employer
parameters.supersedes: any other industry or occupation order for covered occupations
parameters.office_staff: off-site office employees are likely covered by a different IWC order (not verified here)

rules.applies_to: Construction, drilling, logging and mining employers
rules.quote: This order shall apply to all persons employed in the on-site occupations of construction, including but not limited to work involving alteration, demolition, building, excavating, renovation, remodeling, maintenance, improvement, and repair work, and work for which a contractor’s license is required by the Business and Professions Code, Division 3, Chapter 9, Sections 7025 et seq.;

rules.title: Preliminary notice due within 20 days of first furnishing
rules.plain_english: Subcontractors and material suppliers must serve a preliminary notice no later than 20 days after they first furnish labor or materials to the job. One notice covers the whole job no matter how many deliveries are made.

parameters.trigger: claimant first furnishes labor, service, equipment, or material to the work of improvement

rules.applies_to: Subcontractors, sub-subcontractors, material suppliers and equipment lessors on private works of improvement in California (not laborers; see prelim-notice-who-is-exempt)
rules.source: PDF page 75 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Within 20 days from first furnishing labor or materials, serve a "Preliminary 20-day Notice" on the owner, the original contractor, and construction lender. No matter how many deliveries you make, or the time span over which you furnish labor or materials, only one Preliminary Notice is required.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Statutory text per leginfo excerpt of Civ. Code 8204(a): 'A preliminary notice shall be given not later than 20 days after the claimant has first furnished work on the work of improvement.' The law book's '20-day' label is the pre-2012 name; the statute now calls it simply 'preliminary notice'. A claimant furnishing under contracts with more than one subcontractor may need a separate notice per contract (Civ. Code 8206) - not verified against text.
rules.correction: Not refuted. Quote matches Law Book p.75 verbatim, and the 20-day figure matches the CSLB consumer page and the statutory HIC Mechanics Lien Warning ("can be sent up to 20 days after the subcontractor starts work"). None of these is the Civil Code text. The one-notice-per-job parameter is CSLB narrative. The Civ. Code 8206 separate-notice-per-subcontract exception remains unverified.

rules.title: Late preliminary notice only protects last 20 days of work
rules.plain_english: You can still serve a preliminary notice after the 20-day window, but your lien, stop payment notice and bond rights then cover only work furnished within the 20 days before you served it and anything after.

parameters.protected_work: work furnished on or after (service_date - 20 days)

rules.applies_to: Claimants required to give preliminary notice on private works
rules.quote: The Preliminary Notice may be delivered in person or by certified, registered, or first class mail before work begins or supplies are delivered and up to 20 days thereafter. Notice may be given after those 20 days, but payment only is required for work done 20 days before the notice is delivered and anytime thereafter.
rules.notes: CSLB consumer page summary. Leginfo excerpt of 8204: 'The claimant shall, however, be entitled to record a lien, give a stop payment notice, and assert a claim against a payment bond only for work performed within 20 days prior to the service of the preliminary notice, and at any time thereafter.' CSLB's mention of 'first class mail' conflicts with the current Civ. Code 8110 mail methods (registered, certified, express or overnight); see notice-service-methods.
rules.correction: Not refuted. Quote matches the CSLB page verbatim. The CSLB "filed" page and Homeowner's Guide give the same 20-day look-back. Civ. Code 8204 text not seen.

rules.title: Who does not need to give preliminary notice
rules.plain_english: Laborers do not need to give preliminary notice. A direct (prime) contractor that contracts with the owner does not send one to the owner, but must send one to the construction lender if the job has a construction loan.
rules.applies_to: Private works of improvement
rules.quote: NOTE: This notice is not required from laborers or the direct contractor.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Leginfo excerpt of 8200: '(1) A laborer is not required to give preliminary notice. (2) A claimant with a direct contractual relationship with an owner or reputed owner is required to give preliminary notice only to the construction lender or reputed construction lender, if any.' CSLB homeowner guide (https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/HomeownersGuideToPreventingMechanicsLiens.pdf): 'The prime contractor must provide a Preliminary Notice to the construction lender if the contracted project is being financed by a loan.'
rules.correction: Not refuted. Quote matches the CSLB page verbatim. The Guide says the prime must give preliminary notice to the construction lender. The statutory B&P 7159(e)(4) warning says owners get no Preliminary Notices from the prime contractor or laborers. Civ. Code 8200 text not seen.

rules.title: No preliminary notice = no lien / stop notice rights
rules.plain_english: If a subcontractor or supplier who is required to serve a preliminary notice does not do so, it loses the right to record a mechanics lien, serve a stop payment notice, or claim on a payment bond (except as allowed by the bond-notice rules).

parameters.consequence_of_no_notice: lien, stop payment notice and (generally) bond rights unenforceable

rules.applies_to: Subcontractors and suppliers on private works
rules.quote: If subcontractors and suppliers don't provide you with the notice, they lose the right to file a lien.
rules.notes: Leginfo excerpt of 8200 (search snippet): compliance 'is a necessary prerequisite to the validity of a lien claim or stop payment notice'. For payment bonds, a claimant without preliminary notice can still give the 15/75-day bond notice under Civ. Code 8612 (see private-bond-claim-notice).

rules.title: Preliminary notice required contents
rules.plain_english: The preliminary notice must contain the general notice information (owner, direct contractor, lender, site description, who is giving the notice), a general description of the work, an estimate of the total price, and the statutory 'Notice to Property Owner' warning, including wording telling the owner it must notify preliminary-notice givers if it records a notice of completion or cessation.

fields: construction lender name and address (if any)
site description sufficient for identification (street address if any)
name, address and relationship of person giving notice
general description of work to be provided
name of person to or for whom the work is provided
estimate of total price of the work
parameters.owner_warning_type: boldface (point size per statute; not verified)

rules.applies_to: Claimants preparing preliminary notices on private works
rules.source: PDF page 75 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: The notice must include specific wording to inform a property owner of a new responsibility to notify anyone else who served a Preliminary Notice.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Leginfo excerpt of 8202: 'The preliminary notice shall comply with the requirements of Section 8102, and shall also include a general description of the work to be provided' and an estimate of the total price. Leginfo excerpt of 8102: notice shall 'include all of the following information, to the extent known', including 'The name and address of the owner or reputed owner' and 'A description of the site sufficient for identification', and if a sufficient legal description is given, an erroneous or omitted street address does not affect effectiveness. The full statutory owner-warning text (beginning 'EVEN THOUGH YOU HAVE PAID YOUR CONTRACTOR IN FULL...') was NOT obtained verbatim; a document generator must copy it from the current leginfo text of Civ. Code 8202.

rules.title: Optional: file preliminary notice with county recorder
rules.plain_english: A claimant may also file its preliminary notice with the county recorder where the property is located; the recorder will then notify the claimant when a notice of completion or cessation is recorded on that property.

parameters.where: county recorder of county where site is located
parameters.benefit: recorder mails notification of recorded notice of completion/cessation

rules.applies_to: Private-works claimants who gave preliminary notice
rules.citation: Civil Code 8200-8216 (filing with county recorder; exact section not verified)
rules.source: PDF page 75 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: NOTE: You may also file the Preliminary 20-day Notice with the county recorder in the county in which the property is located. The county recorder will then notify you when a Notice of Completion or Notice of Cessation is recorded on the property.
rules.notes: CSLB Law Book narrative; statutory section number for recorder filing not confirmed (believed to be in Civ. Code 8200-8216).

rules.title: Subcontractor discipline for skipping preliminary notice
rules.plain_english: A licensed subcontractor who is required to give preliminary notice and fails to do so on a subcontract over $400 can be disciplined by the CSLB.
rules.applies_to: Licensed subcontractors on private works
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Search excerpt summarized 8216 as making failure to give preliminary notice a disciplinary matter under the Contractors' State License Law 'only where the subcontract pays more than $400'. Exact statutory wording not obtained, so no verbatim quote is given. Some secondary sources describe 8216 as also tying the obligation to work for which a lien could be claimed.
rules.correction: No primary or official secondary text available. The $400 figure and the ">" comparison rest only on the original search excerpt. Keep the existing verify flag.

rules.title: Allowed methods to serve lien-law notices
rules.plain_english: Lien-law notices (preliminary notice, stop payment notice, bond notice, etc.) must be given by personal delivery, by registered or certified mail, express mail, or overnight express carrier, or by leaving the notice and mailing a copy as in CCP 415.20. Plain first-class mail alone is not a listed method.

methods: overnight delivery by express service carrier
leave notice and mail copy per CCP 415.20 (not verified)
parameters.mail_service_complete: when deposited in the mail or with express carrier per CCP 1013

rules.applies_to: All notices under Civil Code Part 6 (private and public works)
rules.quote: notice by mail under this part shall be given by registered or certified mail, express mail, or overnight delivery by an express service carrier
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. 8116 excerpt: mailed notice is complete when 'deposited in the mail or with an express service carrier in the manner provided in Section 1013 of the Code of Civil Procedure'. The 2026 CSLB Law Book narrative (PDF page 75) still says 'first class certified or registered mail, return receipt requested' and the CSLB consumer page mentions 'first class mail' - both appear to reflect pre-2012 law; follow current 8110.

rules.title: Proof of notice declaration and mailing receipts
rules.plain_english: Keep a signed declaration of service for every notice, stating what was served, when, where and how; for mailed notices attach the USPS registered/certified/express receipt or the express carrier's tracking record.

declaration_contents: date, place and manner of notice
facts showing notice was given as required
name and address of person notified
title or capacity of person notified (if any)
parameters.mail_attachment: USPS documentation showing payment for registered/certified/express mail, or express carrier tracking record

rules.applies_to: Anyone giving lien-law notices
rules.quote: documentation provided by the United States Postal Service showing that payment was made to mail the notice using registered or certified mail, or express mail
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Law Book narrative (PDF page 75) advises: 'Be sure to keep post office receipts for later use if you need to file a claim and prove it in court.'

rules.title: When a private work of improvement is 'complete'
rules.plain_english: For lien deadlines, completion happens on the earliest of: actual completion; owner occupation or use plus cessation of labor; cessation of labor for 60 continuous days; or recording a notice of cessation after 30 continuous days of no labor. Public-entity jobs are complete on acceptance.

triggers: owner occupation or use accompanied by cessation of labor
cessation of labor for continuous 60 days
recordation of notice of cessation after cessation of labor for continuous 30 days

rules.applies_to: Private works (Civil Code Title 2)
rules.quote: If a work of improvement is subject to acceptance by a public entity, completion occurs on acceptance.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Search excerpt confirms 'occupation or use by the owner accompanied by cessation of labor' and 'cessation of labor for a continuous period of 60 days'. The 30-day notice-of-cessation trigger was seen in SB 189 bill text and is consistent with the Law Book ('Labor must have ceased for at least 30 days before the owner is entitled to record a Notice of Cessation', PDF page 75) but was not confirmed in the codified excerpt.

rules.title: Notice of completion must be recorded within 15 days of completion
rules.plain_english: An owner who wants the shorter lien deadlines must record a notice of completion with the county recorder within 15 days after the date of completion; a late notice is ineffective.

parameters.trigger: date of completion
parameters.who: owner (signed and verified by owner or owner's agent)
parameters.where: county recorder of county where site is located

rules.applies_to: Owners of private works; direct contractors assisting owners
rules.quote: Filing a Notice of Completion with the county recorder's office after work is completed reduces the amount of time a contractor, subcontractor, laborer, or materials supplier has to record a claim. Homeowners have 15 days from the date of completion to do so.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Leginfo excerpt of 8182: the owner may record 'on or within 15 days after the date of completion'; a noncomplying notice 'is not effective'; an incorrect completion date does not defeat the notice 'if the true date of completion is 15 days or less before the date of recordation of the notice'. CONFLICT: the 2026 CSLB Law Book glossary (PDF page 79) still says 'within 10 days after completion' - that is the pre-2012 rule; use 15 days.
rules.correction: Not refuted. Quote matches the CSLB page verbatim. 15 days also appears in the Guide and Law Book p.76. The stale 10-day figure in the Law Book glossary is on PDF p.79, not p.80: notes corrected. The ineffective-late-notice and 15-day wrong-date tolerance parameters rest only on the original search excerpt of 8182.

rules.title: Notice of completion contents
rules.plain_english: A notice of completion is signed and verified by the owner or its agent and states the completion date, owner name and address, the owner's interest, the site address or description, and the name of the original (direct) contractor.

fields: nature of owner's interest or estate
site street address or description sufficient for identification
name of original/direct contractor for the work completed

rules.applies_to: Owners recording notices of completion on private works
rules.source: PDF page 79 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Notice of Completion is a written notice, signed and verified by the owner or their agent, stating: 1. Date that the job was finished. 2. Name and address of the owner. 3. Nature of the interest or estate of the owner.
rules.notes: Law Book glossary list continues: '4. Street address of the site, if any, or a description of the site sufficient for identification. 5. Name of the original contractor, if any, for the contract covering the portion of the work of improvement completed.' The same glossary's '10 days' recording period is outdated (see noc-recording-15-days).

rules.title: Notice of cessation: 30 days of no labor first
rules.plain_english: An owner may record a notice of cessation only after labor has stopped for at least 30 continuous days; the notice states when labor stopped and that none has been performed since, plus owner, site and contractor details.
rules.applies_to: Owners of private works
rules.citation: Civil Code 8180, 8188 (section number for notice of cessation not verified)
rules.source: PDF page 75 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Labor must have ceased for at least 30 days before the owner is entitled to record a Notice of Cessation.
rules.notes: Contents per Law Book glossary (PDF page 79): 'Notice of Cessation is a written notice, signed and verified by the owner or their agent, stating: 1. Approximate date when labor on the job stopped. 2. Confirmation that no further labor has been performed since the recording of the notice...'.

rules.title: Owner must send copy of recorded NOC/cessation within 10 days
rules.plain_english: An owner who records a notice of completion or cessation must, within 10 days of recording, send a copy to the direct contractor and to every claimant who served it a preliminary notice. If it doesn't, the notice does not shorten that person's lien deadline. Owner-occupants of 1-4 unit residences are excluded.

parameters.trigger: date notice of completion or cessation is recorded
recipients: each claimant that gave the owner preliminary notice
parameters.consequence_of_failure: notice ineffective to shorten that person's time to record under 8412/8414 (stays 90 days)
parameters.exempt: owner occupying the property as a personal residence with four or fewer units

rules.applies_to: Owners of private works recording notices of completion or cessation
rules.source: PDF page 76 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: NOTE: An owner who files a Notice of Cessation or a Notice of Completion must notify any potential lien claimants within 10 days of recording the notices. This notification is designed to let you, the potential lien claimant, know that the time for filing a Claim of Lien has been reduced.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Leginfo excerpt of 8190(a): owner 'shall, within 10 days of the date the notice of completion or cessation is filed for record, give a copy of the notice to all of the following persons: (1) A direct contractor. (2) A claimant that has given the owner preliminary notice.' 8190 excerpt: failure makes the notice 'ineffective to shorten the time within which that person may record a claim of lien under Sections 8412 and 8414'. Law Book adds: 'This provision does not apply to a residential property of four or fewer units.'
rules.correction: Not refuted on the 10-day figure (matches Law Book p.76). FLAG on the exemption: the rule says the exemption covers an "owner occupying the property as a personal residence with four or fewer units". The only official text seen (Law Book p.76) says "does not apply to a residential property of four or fewer units", with no owner-occupancy condition. The two scopes differ and neither is the statute. Verify Civ. Code 8190 before applying the exemption either way.

rules.title: Direct contractor lien recording deadline (60/90 days)
rules.plain_english: A direct (prime) contractor records its lien after it completes its contract and no later than 60 days after the owner records a notice of completion or cessation, or 90 days after completion of the whole job if no valid notice is recorded - whichever is earlier.

parameters.earliest: after completion of the direct contract
parameters.rule: earlier of the two

rules.applies_to: Direct (prime/original) contractors on private works
rules.source: PDF page 77 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: 1. Within 60 days of recording a Notice of Cessation or a Notice of Completion, the contractor must record a Claim of Lien.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Leginfo excerpt of 8412: record 'after the direct contractor completes the direct contract, and before the earlier of' 90 days after completion of the work of improvement or 60 days after the owner records a notice of completion or cessation. If owner fails to send 8190 copy, the 60-day period does not apply to that contractor.
rules.correction: Not refuted. Quote matches Law Book p.77. The 60/90-day figures match the CSLB page and Guide. The "earlier of" structure and the "after completion of the direct contract" start point come only from the original 8412 search excerpt.

rules.title: Subcontractor/supplier lien recording deadline (30/90 days)
rules.plain_english: Subcontractors, suppliers and other non-direct claimants must record their lien no later than 30 days after the owner records a notice of completion or cessation, or 90 days after completion if no valid notice is recorded - whichever is earlier.

parameters.rule: earlier of the two

rules.applies_to: Subcontractors, material suppliers, equipment lessors, laborers on private works
rules.source: PDF page 75-76 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (a) Within 30 days of the owner recording either a Notice of Cessation or Completion, the subcontractor must record a Claim of Lien with the county recorder.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Leginfo excerpt of 8414: claimant other than a direct contractor records after it ceases work and 'before the earlier of' 90 days after completion or 30 days after the owner records a notice of completion or cessation. Law Book (PDF page 79): 'If this notice is not filed in a timely manner, you have a 90-day period within which to record the claim.'
rules.correction: Not refuted. Quote matches Law Book p.75-76; it spans the page break. The 30/90-day figures match the CSLB page and Guide. The note's Law Book cite for the 90-day sentence is PDF p.79, not p.80: corrected. Civ. Code 8414 text not seen.

rules.title: No NOC recorded: 90 days after completion/use/acceptance
rules.plain_english: If no notice of completion or cessation is recorded, any claimant has 90 days after completion - including when labor ceases and the owner uses the improvement, or the owner accepts it - to record its lien.

triggers: labor ceases and owner/agent uses improvement

rules.applies_to: All private-works lien claimants
rules.quote: The potential lien claimant must record the mechanics lien within 90 days of: Completion of work; When the property owner began using the improvement;* or When the property owner accepted the improvement.
rules.notes: CSLB consumer page. Same rule appears in Law Book checklist (PDF page 76-77). Note completion also occurs automatically after 60 continuous days of no labor (Civ. Code 8180).
rules.correction: Quote matches the CSLB page verbatim and the 90-day figure is consistent across CSLB sources. FLAG, not applied because primary text not seen: the "owner/agent accepts improvement" trigger comes only from CSLB consumer narrative and looks like the former Civ. Code 3086 list. As recodified in 2012, Civ. Code 8180 is believed not to list owner acceptance for private works; acceptance is a public-works event under 9200. It is believed instead to include 60 days of continuous cessation and a notice of cessation after 30 days' cessation. The parameters omit the cessation triggers, which appear only in the notes. Verify 8180 before using these triggers.

rules.title: Lien foreclosure suit within 90 days of recording
rules.plain_english: After recording a mechanics lien, the claimant must file a lawsuit to foreclose it within 90 days (and record a lis pendens); otherwise the lien expires and is unenforceable.

parameters.trigger: date claim of lien recorded
parameters.also_record: lis pendens (notice of pendency of action)

rules.applies_to: All private-works lien claimants
rules.source: PDF page 76 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (b) File Lien Foreclosure Action within 90 days of recording a Claim of Lien and record a lis pendens at the same time. You must also file an action on the stop notice at this time, if applicable.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Leginfo excerpt of 8460 states that if no action is commenced the claim of lien 'expires and is unenforceable'. CSLB consumer page: 'The lien claimant must file a lien foreclosure action within 90 days of the date that he or she recorded the mechanics lien.'
rules.correction: Not refuted. Quote matches Law Book p.76. The 90-day period is confirmed by the CSLB page and Guide. "Record a lis pendens at the same time" is Law Book narrative; the statutory lis pendens requirement and its timing were not verified. "Expires and is unenforceable" comes only from the original 8460 excerpt.

rules.title: Credit extension can extend foreclosure deadline (max 1 year after completion)
rules.plain_english: If the owner and claimant agree to extend credit and record notice of the extension, the foreclosure suit is due within 90 days after the credit expires, but never later than one year after completion of the work.

parameters.absolute_limit: 1 year after completion of work of improvement

rules.applies_to: Private-works lien claimants granting credit to owner
rules.quote: the claimant shall commence an action to enforce the lien within 90 days after the expiration of the credit, but in no case later than one year after completion of the work of improvement
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Excerpt also indicates the notice of credit extension may be recorded within 90 days after recording the claim of lien, or later before a good-faith purchaser/encumbrancer acquires an interest.
rules.correction: No official source reachable. The quote and the 90-day/1-year figures rest only on the original search excerpt.

rules.title: Claim of mechanics lien required contents
rules.plain_english: The claim of lien must be signed and verified and state: the amount owed after credits and offsets, the owner's name, the kind of work or materials furnished, who hired you, a site description, and your address, plus the Notice of Mechanics Lien and a proof of service affidavit.

fields: amount of demand after deducting credits and offsets
name of owner or reputed owner, if known
kind of labor, service, equipment or materials furnished
name of person who employed claimant or to whom work was furnished
description of site sufficient for identification
Notice of Mechanics Lien (statutory text, at least 10-point boldface)

rules.applies_to: All private-works lien claimants
rules.source: PDF page 78 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Claim of Lien (mechanics lien) is a written statement signed and verified by the claimant or by the claimant's agent that must state the following: 1. The amount of claimant's demand (after deducting credits and offsets). 2. The name of the owner or reputed owner, if known.
rules.notes: Law Book glossary (PDF page 78) also lists items 3-5 (kind of labor, person who employed claimant, site description). Claimant address, proof-of-service affidavit and Notice of Mechanics Lien come from Civ. Code 8416 per leginfo search excerpt and the CSLB 'If a Mechanics Lien Is Filed' page. Exact statutory Notice of Mechanics Lien text was not obtained verbatim; leginfo excerpt says it must be 'in at least 10-point boldface type' with the final sentence in uppercase except the CSLB web address. Copy text from leginfo Civ. Code 8416(a)(8) before generating.

rules.title: Serve lien + Notice of Mechanics Lien with proof of service affidavit
rules.plain_english: A copy of the recorded lien with the Notice of Mechanics Lien must be served on the owner (or, if the owner can't be served, on the construction lender or direct contractor), and the server must sign a proof of service affidavit. Failure makes the lien unenforceable.

serve_on: fallback: construction lender or original/direct contractor
affidavit_contents: date, place and manner of service
name and address of person served and capacity
parameters.consequence_of_failure: claim of lien unenforceable as a matter of law

rules.applies_to: All private-works lien claimants
rules.source: PDF page 78 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Failure to serve the mechanics lien and confirm a proof of service affidavit will cause the mechanics lien to be unenforceable.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Law Book (PDF page 78) attributes this to 'AB 457, which took effect in 2011'. Leginfo excerpt: failure to serve 'shall cause the claim of mechanics lien to be unenforceable as a matter of law'. Exact service methods (personal service, mail like preliminary notice, CCP 415.20) and timing relative to recording not verified.
rules.correction: Not refuted. Quote matches Law Book p.78. The Guide and CSLB page agree on service, proof of service affidavit and unenforceability. The required wording of the Notice of Mechanics Lien (8416(a)(7)) was not obtained, so do not generate that notice from this rule. Service methods and timing remain unverified.

rules.title: Lien only for work incorporated; supplier's supplier has no lien
rules.plain_english: To have a lien, your labor or materials must be incorporated (installed) in the improvement, and you must have been hired by the owner or someone in charge of the work; a supplier to a material supplier has no statutory lien.
rules.applies_to: Potential lien claimants on private works
rules.citation: Cal. Const. art. XIV, sec. 3; Civil Code 8400, 8404
rules.source: PDF page 73 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: A material supplier is not the agent of the owner and, therefore, a material supplier's supplier is not entitled to a statutory lien. Further, to perfect your lien, the work and/or materials, etc. must be incorporated into the structure. That is to say, it has to be installed.
rules.notes: CSLB Law Book narrative. The statute (8400, 8404) not fetched; incorporation requirement is the Law Book's characterization.
rules.correction: Quote matches Law Book p.73. The constitutional text reproduced there was confirmed, but it contains neither the "incorporated/installed" requirement nor the bar on a supplier's supplier. Both are CSLB narrative. FLAG: "it has to be installed" is CSLB's simplification, and the statutory standard in Civ. Code 8400 et seq. may be broader. Do not use it as a hard eligibility gate until verified.

rules.title: Unlicensed contractor cannot enforce lien over $500
rules.plain_english: Anyone can record a lien, but an unlicensed contractor cannot foreclose a mechanics lien for work valued over $500 (B&P 7031 bars suits for compensation).

parameters.condition: work requiring a license performed while unlicensed

rules.applies_to: Contractors performing work requiring a CSLB license
rules.quote: Although anyone can record a mechanics lien, unlicensed contractors cannot foreclose on a mechanics lien if the work is valued at more than $500.
rules.notes: CSLB consumer page. The $500 figure corresponds to the minor-work exemption (B&P 7048); see license-domain research for 7031/7048 details.

rules.title: Lien release bond = 125% of claim
rules.plain_english: An owner, direct contractor or affected subcontractor can free the property from a recorded lien by recording a release bond from an admitted surety equal to 125% of the lien amount (or of the amount allocated to the property released).
rules.applies_to: Private works with recorded mechanics liens
rules.quote: 125 percent of the amount of the claim of lien or 125 percent of the amount allocated in the claim of lien to the real property to be released
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents.
rules.correction: No official source reachable. The Law Book 1 1/4 figure (p.78, p.81) is for bonded stop notices, not lien release bonds, so it is not corroboration. The 125% figure rests only on the original search excerpt.

rules.title: Release-order petition: 10-day demand first
rules.plain_english: If the claimant has not filed a foreclosure suit within the 90-day period, the owner can petition the court to release the lien, but must first send the claimant a demand to release the lien at least 10 days before filing.

parameters.precondition: no enforcement action within Civ. Code 8460 period
parameters.demand_content: demand that claimant execute and record a release of the claim of lien

rules.applies_to: Owners of private property with expired/unenforced liens
rules.quote: unless at least 10 days before filing the petition the owner gives the claimant notice demanding that the claimant execute and record a release of the claim of lien
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. CSLB consumer page recommends sending the demand by certified, registered, or express mail and keeping proof.

rules.title: Prevailing party attorney fees on lien release petition (no cap)
rules.plain_english: In a court petition to release a lien, the prevailing party gets reasonable attorney's fees; the old $2,000 cap was removed effective July 1, 2012.
rules.applies_to: Owners and lien claimants in release-order proceedings
rules.quote: Civil Code section 8488 provides that if you use an attorney and you prevail, you are entitled to reasonable attorney's fees.
rules.notes: CSLB homeowner guide (PDF columns extracted with pdftotext; quote text read from guide). Leginfo excerpt of 8488: 'The prevailing party is entitled to reasonable attorney's fees.' 8488 also puts the burden of proof as to lien validity on the claimant.
rules.correction: Not refuted. Quote matches the Guide verbatim. Removal of the $2,000 cap effective July 1, 2012 (SB 189, Stats 2010 ch 697) is confirmed by both CSLB sources. Civ. Code 8488 text not seen.

rules.title: Notice of nonresponsibility: post and record within 10 days
rules.plain_english: An owner who did not order the work (e.g., a landlord whose tenant is remodeling) can avoid lien liability only by posting a signed, verified notice of nonresponsibility on the site and recording it within 10 days after learning of the work.

parameters.trigger: person gains knowledge of the work of improvement
actions: post in conspicuous place on site
fields: name and nature of title/interest of person giving notice
name of purchaser under contract or lessee, if known
statement that person is not responsible for claims arising from the work

rules.applies_to: Owners/interest holders who did not cause the work (landlords, vendors under contract of sale)
rules.source: PDF page 80 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Within 10 days of discovering the work of improvement, the person asserting non-responsibility must post this notice in a conspicuous place on the site and must record the notice in the Office of the County Recorder of the county in which the site is located.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Leginfo excerpt of 8444: notice 'is not effective unless, within 10 days after the person giving notice has knowledge of the work of improvement, the person both posts and records the notice'.
rules.correction: Not refuted. Quote and the four content fields match the Law Book glossary (p.79-80), which is CSLB narrative; Civ. Code 8444 text not seen.

rules.title: No mechanics lien on public works - use stop payment notice / bond
rules.plain_english: You cannot record a mechanics lien on public property; on public works your remedies are a stop payment notice to the public entity and a claim on the contractor's payment bond.

public_works_remedies: stop payment notice (Civ. Code 9350 et seq.)
payment bond claim (Civ. Code 9550 et seq.)

rules.applies_to: Subcontractors and suppliers on public works
rules.source: PDF page 74 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: A mechanics lien is a lien on property. A stop notice is a lien on funds. You may use one or the other, or both. However, it should be noted that in public works, you cannot file a mechanics lien; therefore, your only remedy may be a stop notice.
rules.notes: CSLB Law Book narrative; uses pre-2012 term 'stop notice' (now 'stop payment notice').

rules.title: Stop payment notice contents
rules.plain_english: A stop payment notice is signed and verified by the claimant and states the kind of work furnished, who it was furnished to, and the value of work already furnished and of the whole work agreed to be done.

fields: kind of labor, service, equipment or materials furnished or agreed to be furnished
name of person to or for whom furnished
amount/value of work already done or furnished
amount of the whole work agreed to be done

rules.applies_to: Claimants giving stop payment notices (private and public works)
rules.source: PDF page 80 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Stop Notice is a written notice, signed and verified by the claimant or the claimant's agent, that puts a lender or anyone else holding construction funds on notice that there is money due and owed to the claimant.
rules.notes: Law Book glossary (PDF page 80) lists the three required statements. Current statutes call it a 'stop payment notice'; general contents also governed by Civ. Code 8102.

rules.title: Where to deliver a private-works stop payment notice
rules.plain_english: On private works, deliver the stop payment notice to the owner (or the owner's architect), and for a construction lender, to the manager or responsible officer at the office or branch administering the construction funds.

owner_delivery: left at residence/place of business with person in charge
parameters.lender_delivery: manager or other responsible person at office/branch administering or holding construction funds

rules.applies_to: Private-works claimants
rules.source: PDF page 80-81 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: If involving a private work of improvement, the notice must be delivered to the owner personally or left at their residence or place of business with a person in charge or delivered to their architect, if any;
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Leginfo excerpt of 8506: 'A stop payment notice to an owner shall be given to the owner or to the owner's architect, if any' and 'shall comply with the requirements of Chapter 2 (commencing with Section 8100) of Title 1.'

rules.title: Bonded stop payment notice to lender: bond = 125% of claim
rules.plain_english: To bind a construction lender, the stop payment notice must be accompanied by a bond equal to 125% (1.25x) of the claim.
rules.applies_to: Private-works claimants serving construction lenders
rules.source: PDF page 81 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: To bind a construction lender, the stop notice must be bonded. The bond that accompanies a stop notice to any construction lender must be in the sum equal to 1 ¼ times the amount of the claim.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Under 8536 (excerpt), a lender may elect not to withhold on an unbonded notice.

rules.title: Lender objection to stop-notice bond sureties (20/10 days)
rules.plain_english: A lender that objects to the sureties on a bonded stop payment notice must notify the claimant within 20 days; the claimant then has 10 days to substitute a bond from an admitted surety or the lender may release the withheld funds.
rules.applies_to: Construction lenders and claimants on private works
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. rules.title: Holder of funds must withhold on stop payment notice
rules.plain_english: An owner or lender that receives a valid stop payment notice must withhold enough money from the contractor to cover the claim; if it does not, it can become directly liable to the claimant.

parameters.withhold_amount: sufficient to pay claim stated in notice
parameters.liability_if_not_withheld: may be liable to claimant directly

rules.applies_to: Owners and construction lenders on private works
rules.source: PDF page 81 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: The stop notice obligates the person holding construction funds to withhold sufficient funds to satisfy the amount in the stop notice. If the person holding the funds does not withhold sufficient funds to satisfy the stop notice, then the lender or whoever else is holding the funds may be responsible to the claimant directly.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. rules.title: Only non-direct claimants may give owner a stop payment notice
rules.plain_english: On private works, a stop payment notice to the owner may be given by a claimant other than the direct contractor (subcontractors, suppliers, laborers).

parameters.eligible: claimant other than a direct contractor

The search excerpt also referenced forfeiture of lien rights tied to an owner's request for a stop payment notice; that sub-rule was not verified and is omitted.

rules.title: Suit on private stop payment notice: 10 days after / 90 days after window
rules.plain_english: A claimant must sue to enforce a private stop payment notice no earlier than 10 days after giving it and no later than 90 days after the time to give a stop payment notice expires; otherwise the notice lapses and the withheld funds are released.

parameters.notice_period: same as time to record claim of lien (8412/8414) - verify
parameters.consequence: notice ceases to be effective; funds released

rules.applies_to: Private-works claimants who gave stop payment notices

rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. Seen in SB 189 (2010) bill text that enacted the current code; codified subdivision lettering not verified. rules.title: Payment bond recorded: serve notice on surety
rules.plain_english: If no mechanics lien has been recorded and a payment bond has been recorded, the notice must be served on the surety.

parameters.condition: no mechanics lien recorded AND payment bond recorded

rules.applies_to: Private-works claimants
rules.source: PDF page 76 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (b) If no mechanics lien has been recorded, and a surety payment bond has been recorded, then the notice must be served on the surety.

rules.title: Private payment bond claim notice (15/75 days) if no preliminary notice
rules.plain_english: A claimant who did not give preliminary notice can still claim on a private payment bond by giving written notice to the surety and bond principal within 15 days after a notice of completion is recorded, or within 75 days after completion if none is recorded.
rules.applies_to: Claimants on private works with a payment bond
rules.quote: If preliminary notice was not given as provided in Chapter 2 (commencing with Section 8200), a claimant may enforce a claim by giving written notice to the surety and the bond principal within 15 days after recordation of a notice of completion.

Code 8100 et seq.

rules.title: Suit on recorded private payment bond within 6 months after completion

parameters.condition: payment bond recorded before completion

rules.applies_to: Claimants on private works with recorded payment bonds
rules.quote: If a payment bond under this title is recorded before completion of a work of improvement, an action to enforce the liability on the bond may not be commenced later than six months after completion of the work of improvement.
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. rules.title: Public works preliminary notice (20 days) to entity and direct contractor
rules.plain_english: On public works, before giving a stop payment notice or bond claim, a claimant must serve preliminary notice on the public entity and the direct contractor; late notice covers only work within the 20 days before service and after. Laborers are exempt.

parameters.contents: Civ. Code 8102 info + general description of work (9303)

rules.title: Where to file a public-works stop payment notice
rules.plain_english: For a state project, give the stop payment notice to the director of the department that awarded the contract; for other public entities, to the controller, auditor or other disbursing officer, or the awarding body.

rules.quote: fails to make any progress payment within 30 days after receipt of an undisputed and properly submitted payment request from a contractor on a construction contract
rules.notes: Leginfo (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov) is behind a Cloudflare challenge and could not be fetched from this environment; quote is a search-engine excerpt of the official leginfo page, not a fetched copy. Verify exact wording before generating documents. A 7-day return rule for improper requests is believed to also appear in 20104.50(c) but was not confirmed in excerpts; an older AB 1410 bill version used a 2% penalty instead of interest.
rules.correction: No official source reachable.

rules.title: Local agency contracts must include prompt payment article or summary
rules.plain_english: Every local agency construction contract subject to PCC 20104.50 must set out that article, or a summary of it, in the contract terms.

parameters.required_text: PCC 20104-20104.50 article or a summary thereof

rules.applies_to: Local agency construction contracts

rules.title: Home improvement downpayment: lesser of $1,000 or 10%
rules.plain_english: On a home improvement contract, any downpayment may not exceed $1,000 or 10% of the contract amount, whichever is less.

parameters.rule: lesser of

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts (B&P 7151.2) between owner/tenant and licensed or unlicensed contractor
rules.source: PDF page 410 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (3) If a downpayment will be charged, the downpayment shall not exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000) or 10 percent of the contract amount, whichever amount is less.
rules.notes: Contract must also print in 12-point boldface: 'THE DOWNPAYMENT MAY NOT EXCEED $1,000 OR 10 PERCENT OF THE CONTRACT PRICE, WHICHEVER IS LESS.' (B&P 7159(d)(8)(C), Law Book PDF page 400). Exempt if contractor furnishes qualifying bonds/joint control (7159.5(a)(8)).

rules.title: No payment exceeding value of work performed or materials delivered
rules.plain_english: Except for the downpayment, a home improvement contractor may not request or accept payment that exceeds the value of the work performed or materials delivered, including advance payments from a lender.

parameters.max_cumulative_payment: value of work performed + material delivered (+ allowed downpayment)

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors
rules.source: PDF page 410 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (5) Except for a downpayment, the contractor shall neither request nor accept payment that exceeds the value of the work performed or material delivered.
rules.notes: Violation of (a)(1), (3) or (5) is a misdemeanor (see hic-payment-violation-misdemeanor).

rules.title: Schedule of progress payments in dollars and cents
rules.plain_english: If any payments besides the downpayment are due before completion, the home improvement contract must include a 'Schedule of Progress Payments' stating each payment in dollars and cents tied to specific work, materials and equipment, with the statutory 12-point boldface warning.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts with progress payments
rules.source: PDF page 400 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: IT IS AGAINST THE LAW FOR A CONTRACTOR TO COLLECT PAYMENT FOR WORK NOT YET COMPLETED, OR FOR MATERIALS NOT YET DELIVERED. HOWEVER, A CONTRACTOR MAY REQUIRE A DOWNPAYMENT.
rules.notes: Full required statement begins: 'The schedule of progress payments must specifically describe each phase of work, including the type and amount of work or services scheduled to be supplied in each phase, along with the amount of each proposed progress payment.' (Law Book PDF page 400).

rules.title: Furnish unconditional lien releases on payment if requested
rules.plain_english: After each payment by the homeowner, the contractor must, if requested, obtain and give the owner full unconditional lien releases for the work paid for; the owner may withhold all further payments until it gets them.

parameters.trigger: any payment by owner + owner request
parameters.release_type: full and unconditional release (Civ. Code 8134/8138 forms)

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors
rules.source: PDF page 410 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (6) Upon any payment by the person contracting for home improvement, and prior to any further payment being made, the contractor shall, if requested, obtain and furnish to the person a full and unconditional release from any potential lien claimant claim or mechanics lien authorized pursuant to Sections 8400 and 8404 of the Civil Code for any portion of the work for which payment has been made.
rules.notes: Continues: 'The person contracting for home improvement may withhold all further payments until these releases are furnished.'

rules.title: HIC must state contractor will furnish lien releases
rules.plain_english: Every home improvement contract must include a statement that, upon satisfactory payment for any portion of the work, the contractor will furnish a full and unconditional lien release for that portion before any further payment.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement and swimming pool contracts
rules.source: PDF page 398 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (4) The contract shall include a statement that, upon satisfactory payment being made for any portion of the work performed, the contractor, prior to any further payment being made, shall furnish to the person contracting for the home improvement or swimming pool work a full and unconditional release from any potential lien claimant claim or mechanics lien
rules.notes: Quote truncated at 400 chars; statute continues 'authorized pursuant to Sections 8400 and 8404 of the Civil Code for that portion of the work for which payment has been made.'

rules.title: HIC must include the 'Mechanics Lien Warning' notice
rules.plain_english: Home improvement contracts must include the statutory 'Mechanics Lien Warning' explaining liens, preliminary notices, the 20-day timing, and joint checks (unless the contractor furnishes qualifying bonds or joint control).
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts
rules.source: PDF page 402 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Anyone who helps improve your property, but who is not paid, may record what is called a mechanics lien on your property. A mechanics lien is a claim, like a mortgage or home equity loan, made against your property and recorded with the county recorder.
rules.notes: Full text runs on Law Book PDF pages 402-403 (7159(e)(4)); generator should copy the entire warning verbatim from the Law Book including 'BE CAREFUL. The Preliminary Notice can be sent up to 20 days after the subcontractor starts work...' and the CSLB contact line. 7159(e) allows attachment only where a paragraph expressly authorizes it; paragraph (4) does not, so treat the warning as part of the contract form.

rules.title: Bond/joint-control exemption from HIC payment limits
rules.plain_english: A contractor that furnishes a performance and payment bond, lien and completion bond, CSLB-approved bond equivalent, or joint control covering full performance and payment is exempt from the downpayment cap, the payment-schedule and no-advance-payment rules, and need not include the contract's downpayment statement, the progress-payment details/statement, or the Mechanics Lien Warning; it may accept payment before completion. All other contract requirements still apply. A blanket bond application requires 2 years of active licensure.

parameters.still_required: all other 7159(c), (d) and (e) items, including the other 7159(e) notices

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors
rules.source: PDF page 411 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (8) A contractor furnishing a performance and payment bond, lien and completion bond, or a bond equivalent or joint control approved by the registrar covering full performance and payment is exempt from paragraphs (3), (4), and (5), and need not include, as part of the contract, the statement regarding the downpayment specified in subparagraph (C) of paragraph (8) of subdivision (d) of Section 7159, the details and statement regarding progress payments specified in paragraph (9) of subdivision (d) of Section 7159, or the Mechanics Lien Warning specified in paragraph (4) of subdivision (e) of Section 7159.
rules.notes: Contractor furnishing joint control may not have a financial or other interest in the joint control.
rules.correction: Incomplete exemption list. 7159.5(a)(8) also relieves a qualifying bonded or joint-control contractor of two more contract items: the 12-point downpayment statement in 7159(d)(8)(C), and the progress-payment details and 12-point statement in 7159(d)(9). Added both to exempt_from and plain_english. The quote is replaced with the operative exemption sentence. All other 7159(c)-(e) items still apply, including the rest of the 7159(e) notices.

rules.title: HIC payment violations are misdemeanors ($100-$5,000)
rules.plain_english: Violating the written-contract-amount, downpayment cap, or no-payment-ahead-of-work rules is a misdemeanor: fine of $100 to $5,000, up to 1 year in county jail, or both; the maximum fine is mandatory in declared disaster areas.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors and unlicensed persons
rules.source: PDF page 411 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (b) (1) A violation of paragraph (1), (3), or (5) of subdivision (a) by a licensee or a person subject to be licensed under this chapter, or by their agent or salesperson, is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not less than one hundred dollars ($100) nor more than five thousand dollars ($5,000),
rules.notes: Disaster-fraud schemes: full restitution plus fine of $500-$25,000 (7159.5(c)(2)). Limitations periods run from contract date or first payment.

rules.title: HIC notice: owner may require performance and payment bond
rules.plain_english: Near the signatures, the home improvement contract must tell the owner or tenant they have the right to require the contractor to have a performance and payment bond.

parameters.placement: in close proximity to signatures of owner and contractor

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts
rules.source: PDF page 399 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (6) The contract shall contain, in close proximity to the signatures of the owner and contractor, a notice stating that the owner or tenant has the right to require the contractor to have a performance and payment bond.

rules.title: Service & repair contracts: no payment before completion; lien release on request
rules.plain_english: On a service and repair contract (max $750), payment is not due until the job is complete, and on payment the contractor must furnish an unconditional lien release if the buyer asks.
rules.applies_to: Service and repair contracts (B&P 7159.10)
rules.source: PDF page 419 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (7) Payment shall not be due before the project is completed.
rules.notes: (a)(11): 'Upon any payment by the buyer, the contractor shall, if requested, obtain and furnish to the buyer a full and unconditional release...'.

rules.title: No security interest in real property for HIC of $5,000 or less; loan proceeds via joint check/escrow
rules.plain_english: A home improvement goods or services contract of $5,000 or less may not take a security interest in the home (other than a mechanics lien). For larger contracts funded by a mortgage loan, the lender may pay the contractor only by check payable to the borrower (or jointly) or through a third-party escrow the borrower elects.

loan_payment_methods: instrument payable to borrower or jointly to borrower and contractor
parameters.treble_damages: 3x contract price for intentional or pattern violations

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts and lenders funding them
rules.source: PDF page 409 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (a) No home improvement goods or services contract of a value of five thousand dollars ($5,000) or less shall provide for a security interest in real property, except for a mechanic's lien or other interest in property that arises by operation of law.

rules.title: New single-family dwelling contracts must include Mechanics Lien Warning
rules.plain_english: A contract to build a single-family home the owner will keep at least one year must be in writing, signed by both parties, and include the contractor's name/address/license number, approximate start and substantial-completion dates, the legal description, the 7164 version of the "Mechanics Lien Warning", and the CGL insurance statement and check box. Near the signatures it must state, in at least 10-point bold or all caps, that the owner may require a performance and payment bond at the owner's expense. The owner must get a contractor-signed copy before work starts.

fields: approximate start and substantial completion dates
CGL insurance statement and check box
parameters.mechanics_lien_warning_text_source: B&P 7164(b)(4) verbatim (Law Book PDF p.425-426); NOT interchangeable with the 7159(e)(4) HIC text

bond_notice.format: at least 10-point boldface type or all capital letters
bond_notice.content: owner has the right to require the contractor to have a performance and payment bond and the expense of the bond may be borne by the owner

parameters.copy_to_owner_before_work: copy of written agreement signed by the contractor, furnished before commencement (7164(c))
parameters.cgl_statement_operative: 3 months after CSLB adopts the 7164(b)(5)(A) regulation (7164(e))

rules.applies_to: Contracts between owner and contractor to construct a single-family dwelling retained by owner >= 1 year

rules.quote: (a) Notwithstanding Section 7044, every contract and any changes in a contract, between an owner and a contractor, for the construction of a single-family dwelling to be retained by the owner for at least one year shall be evidenced in writing signed by both parties.
rules.notes: The 7164(b)(4) warning differs from the 7159(e)(4) HIC warning: "if he or she is not paid" (7159: "if they are not paid"); "from your prime contractor or other persons you contract with directly or from laborers" (7159 omits the middle phrase); "visit CSLB's Web site at www.cslb.ca.gov or call CSLB at 800-321-CSLB (2752)" (7159: "internet website"). Copy the 7164 text verbatim from Law Book PDF p.425-426 for SFD contracts.
rules.correction: Two gaps where exact wording matters. (1) The 7164(b)(4) Mechanics Lien Warning is not identical to the 7159(e)(4) HIC warning. It says "if he or she is not paid" (7159: "if they are not paid") and "from your prime contractor or other persons you contract with directly or from laborers" (7159 omits the middle phrase). It also says "visit CSLB's Web site at www.cslb.ca.gov or call CSLB at 800-321-CSLB (2752)", where 7159 says "internet website" and splits the line. SFD contracts must use the 7164 text. (2) The rule omitted 7164(d): a notice near the owner and contractor signatures, in at least 10-point boldface or all capitals, that the owner has the right to require a performance and payment bond and that the owner may bear its expense. Also added 7164(c): before work starts the owner gets a copy signed by the contractor. Citation, source_location, parameters, plain_english and notes updated.

rules.title: San Diego: no noisy construction 7 p.m.-7 a.m., on Sundays or City legal holidays without a prior noise permit
rules.plain_english: In the City of San Diego you may not build, demolish, excavate, alter or repair a building between 7 p.m. and 7 a.m. (any day), on Sundays, or on City legal holidays (except Columbus Day and Washington's Birthday) in a way that makes disturbing, excessive or offensive noise, unless you applied for and received a permit from the Noise Abatement Administrator before the work.

parameters.holiday_list_section: Code page (7-2010) cites 'Section 21.04'; the current DSD Construction Noise Permit page cites SDMC §21.0104 for the official holiday list (renumbering date not stated in the sources read)
parameters.permit_issuer: Noise Abatement and Control Administrator (DSD Noise Abatement Administrator)

rules.applies_to: Anyone erecting, constructing, demolishing, excavating for, altering or repairing a building or structure in the City of San Diego, including contractors and subcontractors
rules.source: https://www.sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/appendix_5.7-1_-_noise_0.pdf (City of San Diego, Mission Bay Park Master Plan - Fiesta Island Amendment Draft PEIR, Appendix 5.7-1, Dec. 2018; PDF page 47 reproduces the official SDMC Chapter 5, Article 9.5, Division 4 code page dated (7-2010), Section 59.5.0404(a)). Current official SDMC text at docs.sandiego.gov could not be fetched (host not allowed by the session network policy).
rules.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person, between the hours of 7:00 p.m. of any day and 7:00 a.m. of the following day, or on legal holidays as specified in Section 21.04 of the San Diego Municipal Code, with exception of Columbus Day and Washington’s Birthday, or on Sundays, to erect, construct, demolish, excavate for, alter or repair any building or structure in such a manner as to create disturbing, excessive or offensive noise unless a permit has been applied for and granted beforehand by the Noise Abatement and Control Administrator.
rules.effective: 1984-01-03 (last amendment shown on the 7-2010 code page: O-16100 N.S.)
rules.notes: Code text read from an official City of San Diego code page (7-2010 edition) reproduced in a City EIR appendix. Amendments after July 2010 could not be checked because docs.sandiego.gov is blocked; the City's current DSD noise-permit page still cites SDMC 59.5.0404. The section restricts noisy work only; quiet work in these windows is not prohibited by its words, but DSD requires a Construction Noise Permit for any construction in these windows (see local-sd-noise-permit-required-windows). Whether the City's 'Presidents' Day' holiday is the 'Washington's Birthday' exception could not be confirmed because the text of SDMC 21.0104 (amended 2023 by O-21635) was not readable.
rules.correction: Quote, hours (7 p.m.-7 a.m.), Sunday and holiday ban, the Columbus Day / Washington's Birthday exception and the permit requirement are confirmed on the 7-2010 code page. The code page cites 'Section 21.04' and the current DSD page links 'San Diego Municipal Code §21.0104'. Replaced the unsupported renumbering claim.

rules.title: San Diego: Construction Noise Permit required for work 7 p.m.-7 a.m. weekdays and Saturdays, and all day Sundays and holidays
rules.plain_english: San Diego's Development Services Department requires a Construction Noise Permit for construction work between 7 p.m. and 7 a.m. on weekdays and Saturdays, and at any hour on Sundays and City holidays. Daytime work 7 a.m.-7 p.m. Monday-Saturday needs no noise permit.

rules.source: https://www.sandiego.gov/development-services/permits/noise-permit ('What You Should Know'); also https://www.sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/ds-3073.pdf (instruction 1), https://www.sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/ds269.pdf (page 2, requirement 5) and https://www.sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/2026-06/dsd_independence_day_26.pdf (DSD notice of June 26, 2026)
