Treat all-day Saturday work as unresolved and confirm with NoisePermits@sandiego.gov before scheduling Saturday daytime work without a permit.

rules.title: San Diego: daytime construction noise limit 75 dB average (7 a.m.-7 p.m.) at residential property lines
rules.plain_english: Even during allowed daytime hours, construction in San Diego may not produce an average sound level above 75 decibels over the 12 hours from 7 a.m. to 7 p.m., measured at or beyond the property line of any residentially zoned property. The City itself is bound by this limit.

parameters.measured_at: at or beyond the property lines of any property zoned residential
parameters.exception: construction equipment used for emergency work, if the Administrator is notified within 48 hours (SDMC 59.5.0404(c))

rules.applies_to: Applicants for San Diego Construction Noise Permits
rules.citation: City of San Diego Form DS-3073 (07-23); DSD Construction Noise Permit page
rules.quote: I certify that the I have notified all affected properties of the proposed work, as outlined in the Construction Noise Permit application, within a 500‐foot radius of the construction site.
rules.notes: The certification sentence is quoted as printed (including 'that the I have').

rules.title: San Diego noise permit: post a Notice of Pending Construction at the site
rules.plain_english: When you work under a Construction Noise Permit, you must also post a Notice of Pending Construction at the site in a conspicuous place the public can easily see.

parameters.location: conspicuous, easily viewable place at the site

rules.applies_to: Holders of San Diego Construction Noise Permits
rules.citation: City of San Diego DSD Construction Noise Permit page
rules.quote: A Notice of Pending Construction must also be placed in a conspicuous, easily viewable place at the site for public viewing.

rules.title: San Diego: get an approved Traffic Control Permit before applying for a Construction Noise Permit
rules.plain_english: If the night or holiday work affects the public right-of-way, San Diego requires an approved Traffic Control Permit (with an approved traffic control plan) before you can apply for the Construction Noise Permit. Some work entirely on private property does not need a Traffic Control Permit.

parameters.prerequisite: approved Traffic Control Permit with approved Traffic Control Plan
parameters.private_property_exception: in some cases construction on private property does not require a Traffic Control Permit

rules.applies_to: Applicants for San Diego Construction Noise Permits
rules.citation: City of San Diego DSD Construction Noise Permit page (Apply for a Permit, step 1)
rules.quote: Obtain a Traffic Control Permit with an approved Traffic Control Plan before applying for a Construction Noise Permit.
rules.notes: Because Traffic Control Permits take about 15 business days (local-sd-tcp-processing-15-business-days), night work in the right-of-way needs roughly 4 weeks of lead time.

rules.title: San Diego: submit the noise permit application at least 5 working days ahead (with the approved TCP)
rules.plain_english: For right-of-way work approved for 7 p.m.-7 a.m., Sunday or holiday hours, the Construction Noise Permit application must be submitted in Accela at least five working days ahead, together with the approved Traffic Control Permit.
rules.applies_to: Contractors doing night, Sunday or holiday work in the San Diego public right-of-way
rules.citation: City of San Diego Form DS-269 (06-26), Requirements item 5
rules.quote: Construction Noise Permit Application must be submitted to Accela a minimum of five working days with an approved traffic control permit

rules.title: San Diego: file noise permit applications at least 3 business days before a City holiday closure
rules.plain_english: Before a City holiday office closure, DSD requires Construction Noise Permit applications to be submitted at least three business days before the closure.
rules.applies_to: Contractors needing San Diego noise permits around City holidays
rules.citation: City of San Diego DSD public notice, Independence Day Holiday Office Closure (June 26, 2026)
rules.quote: Applicants must submit a Construction Noise Permit application at least three business days before a holiday closure.
rules.notes: Stated in DSD's holiday-closure notices; the July 3, 2026 notice is the one read.

rules.title: San Diego: request a noise permit extension at least 48 hours before it expires
rules.plain_english: To extend a valid Construction Noise Permit, submit the request at least 48 hours before it expires. Expired permits cannot be extended; you must apply for a new permit, first getting an extended Traffic Control Permit approval letter and submitting the original noise permit approval letter.

extension_steps: approved extended Traffic Control Permit approval letter
submit original noise permit approval letter

rules.applies_to: Holders of San Diego Construction Noise Permits
rules.citation: City of San Diego DSD Construction Noise Permit page (Permit Extensions)
rules.quote: Extension requests for existing (non-expired) Construction Noise Permits may be granted. All requests must be submitted at least 48 hours before a valid permit expires.

rules.title: San Diego: noise permit can be revoked for violations or for SDPD nuisance complaints
rules.plain_english: The Noise Abatement Administrator can deny or revoke a Construction Noise Permit for violations, and the San Diego Police Department can revoke it if people complain to SDPD of excessive noise that is a public nuisance. There are no exemptions from the permit, and all permits are subject to City inspection.

parameters.sdpd_trigger: complaints alleging excessive noise that creates a public nuisance

rules.applies_to: Holders of San Diego Construction Noise Permits
rules.citation: City of San Diego DSD Construction Noise Permit page (Exemptions)
rules.quote: Permits may be revoked or denied by the Noise Abatement Administrator for violations. The San Diego Police Department can also revoke the Construction Noise Permit if complaints are reported to SDPD alleging excessive noise that creates a public nuisance.

rules.title: San Diego: $250 civil penalty for after-hours construction noise, up to $2,500 per incident
rules.plain_english: San Diego code enforcement can issue a $250 civil penalty for excessive construction noise between 7 p.m. and 7 a.m., on Sundays and official City holidays. For severe problems, fines can go up to $2,500 per incident. If you don't pay, a hearing officer can uphold, cancel, lower or raise the fine (up to $2,500).

parameters.usual_precondition: history of noise issues at the location

rules.applies_to: Construction projects and their contractors in the City of San Diego
rules.citation: City of San Diego Neighborhood Code Compliance policy, 'Possible Civil Fines for Construction Noise during Restricted Hours'
rules.quote: This policy could result in the issuance on a $250 civil penalty for excessive construction noise between the hours of 7 PM and 7 AM, Sundays and official City holidays. In general, if such a fine is issued, there will have been a history of noise issues at that location. If the noise issues become severe fines in excess of $250 could be issued up to $2,500 per incident.
rules.effective: undated legacy City document (still hosted on sandiego.gov on 2026-11-25)
rules.notes: The document is an undated legacy Neighborhood Code Compliance flyer (the division is now Building & Land Use Enforcement). The current administrative citation schedule could not be read; treat the amounts as the City's published policy, not a verified current fine schedule.

rules.title: San Diego: projects answer for noisy early deliveries and off-site staging before 7 a.m.
rules.plain_english: A San Diego project is responsible for noise from its contractors on and off the site. Delivery trucks that arrive or wait near homes before 7 a.m. and make excessive noise can lead to penalties for the project.

parameters.condition: delivery trucks arriving at the site or staging in close proximity to residential properties that create excessive noise

rules.applies_to: Construction projects and their delivery suppliers in the City of San Diego
rules.citation: City of San Diego Neighborhood Code Compliance, 'Possible Civil Fines for Construction Noise during Restricted Hours'
rules.quote: Projects will be held responsible for the noise generated by their contractors on and off the site; for example delivery trucks that arrive at the site or stage in close proximity to residential properties prior to 7:00 AM that create excessive noise can result in penalties being assessed.
rules.effective: undated legacy City document (still hosted on sandiego.gov on 2026-11-25)
rules.notes: Same legacy document as local-sd-construction-noise-civil-penalty.
rules.correction: The quote is confirmed. The parameter earliest_delivery_time = 07:00 read as a flat ban on deliveries before 7 a.m. The flyer only penalizes delivery trucks that arrive or stage near residential properties before 7:00 AM and 'create excessive noise'. Replaced it with noisy_arrival_or_staging_before = 07:00 and added the excessive-noise condition.

rules.title: San Diego: no refuse compacting, processing or collection vehicles in residential areas 7 p.m.-6 a.m. without a permit
rules.plain_english: In residential areas of San Diego, refuse compacting, processing or collection vehicles may not operate between 7 p.m. and 6 a.m., and parking-lot sweepers between 7 p.m. and 7 a.m., unless a permit has been applied for and granted by the Noise Abatement Administrator. (Whether a roll-off box swap counts as a 'collection vehicle' is not stated in the code.)
rules.applies_to: Haulers serving construction sites and anyone operating refuse collection vehicles in San Diego residential areas
rules.source: https://www.sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/appendix_5.7-1_-_noise_0.pdf (City of San Diego, Mission Bay Park Master Plan - Fiesta Island Amendment Draft PEIR, Appendix 5.7-1, Dec. 2018; PDF page 47 reproduces the official SDMC Chapter 5, Article 9.5, Division 4 code page dated (7-2010), Section 59.5.0406). Current official SDMC text at docs.sandiego.gov could not be fetched (host not allowed by the session network policy).
rules.quote: No person shall operate or permit to be operated a refuse compacting, processing, or collection vehicle between the hours of 7:00 p.m. to 6:00 a.m. or a parking lot sweeper between the hours of 7:00 p.m. to 7:00 a.m. in any residential area unless a permit has been applied for and granted by the Administrator.
rules.notes: Code text read from an official City of San Diego code page (7-2010 edition) reproduced in a City EIR appendix. Amendments after July 2010 could not be checked because docs.sandiego.gov is blocked; the City's current DSD noise-permit page still cites SDMC 59.5.0404. Relevant to scheduling dumpster swaps at residential jobsites.
rules.correction: The quote, the hours (refuse vehicles 7 p.m.-6 a.m., sweepers 7 p.m.-7 a.m.), the residential-area scope and the permit are confirmed. plain_english said the ban includes 'roll-off and bin service'. The code names only 'a refuse compacting, processing, or collection vehicle', so the roll-off wording is an interpretation. plain_english now uses the code's terms, and the interpretation is flagged in parameters. Rewording 2026-11-27: title reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: San Diego general noise limits by zone (one-hour average dB) for non-construction sources
rules.plain_english: San Diego limits noise from any source, measured at or beyond the property line, by zone and time of day (for example 50/45/40 dB in single-family zones for day/evening/night). Construction noise itself is governed by the separate construction rule (59.5.0404); this table matters for things like stationary equipment left running at a site.

parameters.measured_at: on or beyond the boundaries of the property where the noise is produced
parameters.zone_boundary_rule: arithmetic mean of the two districts' limits

rules.applies_to: Noise sources in the City of San Diego other than construction activity governed by 59.5.0404
rules.source: https://www.sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/appendix_5.7-1_-_noise_0.pdf (City of San Diego, Mission Bay Park Master Plan - Fiesta Island Amendment Draft PEIR, Appendix 5.7-1, Dec. 2018; PDF page 44 reproduces the official SDMC Chapter 5, Article 9.5, Division 4 code page dated (7-2010), Section 59.5.0401). Current official SDMC text at docs.sandiego.gov could not be fetched (host not allowed by the session network policy).
rules.quote: It shall be unlawful for any person to cause noise by any means to the extent that the one–hour average sound level exceeds the applicable limit given in the following table, at any location in the City of San Diego on or beyond the boundaries of the property on which the noise is produced.
rules.notes: Code text read from an official City of San Diego code page (7-2010 edition) reproduced in a City EIR appendix. Amendments after July 2010 could not be checked because docs.sandiego.gov is blocked; the City's current DSD noise-permit page still cites SDMC 59.5.0404. Subsection (b) states that 'Permissible construction noise level limits shall be governed by Sections 59.5.0404 of this article.' Whether a generator or pump serving a construction site counts as 'construction activity' is not stated.

rules.title: San Diego: Traffic Control Permit required for any work encroaching into the public right-of-way
rules.plain_english: In San Diego you need a Traffic Control Permit before any construction or other work that encroaches into the public right-of-way: sidewalks, parking spaces, medians, alleys and streets. It is also required for a dumpster or storage container in the right-of-way and for temporary business use of a street, sidewalk or parking lane.

parameters.permit: Traffic Control Permit (Public Right-of-Way Permit for traffic control)
triggers: construction projects or other work encroaching into the public right of way
temporary dumpster or storage container in the public right of way
temporary use of a street, sidewalk or parking lane for business purposes

rules.applies_to: Contractors, utilities and owners working in or occupying the City of San Diego public right-of-way
rules.citation: SDMC 129.0702 (per IB 177); City of San Diego DSD Traffic Control Permit page
rules.source: https://www.sandiego.gov/development-services/permits/traffic-control-permit ('Traffic Control Permits are required for'); https://www.sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/dsdib177.pdf (section I)
rules.quote: Traffic Control Permits are required for: All public improvement projects, construction projects or other work encroaching into the public right of way, including the sidewalks, parking spaces, medians, alleys and streets.
rules.notes: IB 177 (May 2026) cites SDMC 129.0702 as the authority. The code text itself was not readable (docs.sandiego.gov blocked). [Review 2026-11-25: IB 177 (May 2026) section II, re-fetched from https://www.sandiego.gov/development-services/forms-bulletins/information-bulletin/177 (the dsdib177.pdf link now redirects there), reads 'Complete a Traffic Control Plan/Permit Form DS-269, provide an approved Right-of-Way Permit (where applicable) and submit a traffic control plan.' Added parameter approved_row_permit_with_application.]

rules.title: San Diego: Traffic Control Permits take about 15 business days to process
rules.plain_english: New Traffic Control Permits and extensions take about 15 business days to process in San Diego, so apply early.
rules.applies_to: Applicants for San Diego Traffic Control Permits
rules.citation: City of San Diego DSD Traffic Control Permit page
rules.quote: Please note that it can take about 15 business days to process new Traffic Control Permits or extension requests for existing permits.
rules.notes: This is the City's processing estimate, not a legal deadline. The formal minimum filing lead time is 5 working days (local-sd-tcp-apply-5-working-days).

rules.title: San Diego: file Traffic Control Permit applications and extensions at least 5 working days before work
rules.plain_english: Submit a San Diego Traffic Control Permit application or extension in Accela at least five working days before work in the right-of-way starts. IB 177 also requires at least five working days' notice of the work start date.
rules.applies_to: Contractors working in the San Diego public right-of-way
rules.citation: City of San Diego Form DS-269 (06-26), Requirements item 19; Information Bulletin 177 (May 2026), section III
rules.quote: Traffic control application/extension must be submitted through Accela a minimum of five working days prior to the anticipated start of work within the public right-of-way
rules.notes: IB 177 section III: 'Work start/end dates (A minimum of five working days’ notice is required before the beginning of work.)'

rules.title: San Diego right-of-way work hours: day work Mon-Fri 8:30 a.m.-3:30 p.m.; night work Sun-Thu 9 p.m.-5 a.m.
rules.plain_english: For traffic control in San Diego streets, the standard day work window is Monday-Friday 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. and the standard night work window is Sunday-Thursday nights 9 p.m. to 5 a.m. Your traffic control plan must state the work hours.
rules.applies_to: Contractors working under San Diego Traffic Control Permits
rules.citation: City of San Diego Information Bulletin 177 (May 2026), section III
rules.quote: Work hours: Standard workdays are Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 3:30 p.m. Night work is Sunday through Thursday, 9 p.m. to 5 a.m.
rules.notes: Other hours may be approved on the permit; night hours also need a Construction Noise Permit.

rules.title: San Diego: no right-of-way work on Saturdays, Sundays or holidays unless approved; night permits end 5 a.m.
rules.plain_english: Under a San Diego Traffic Control Permit, day work is Monday-Friday and night work is Sunday-Thursday nights. No work on Saturdays, Sundays or holidays unless the City approves it. Unless the permit says otherwise, a night-work permit expires at 5 a.m. the day after its listed end date.

parameters.night_permit_expires: 05:00 on the day following the permit expiration date

rules.applies_to: Contractors working under San Diego Traffic Control Permits
rules.citation: City of San Diego Form DS-269 (06-26), Requirements item 4
rules.quote: Standard Day Work is Monday through Friday. Standard Night Work is Sunday through Thursday. No work on Saturdays, Sundays or holidays unless otherwise approved. Unless otherwise noted on the permit, Traffic Control Permits with night work hours expire at 5am on the day following the permit expiration date.

rules.title: San Diego Traffic Control Permit fees: $131.52/block initial, $87.68/block/week extension, $87.68 processing
rules.plain_english: San Diego charges a Traffic Control Initial fee of $131.52 per block (covers up to 3 weeks), an extension fee of $87.68 per block per week, and a flat $87.68 processing fee on each request (the initial request, each extension and each modification). Blocked parking meters cost extra ($20 per space per day; $300 to remove a meter post; $600 to remove a pay station).

parameters.modification_fee: processing fee $87.68 + new sheet fee (Traffic Control Initial $131.52) if applicable
parameters.formula: total = 87.68*number_of_requests (initial, each extension request, each modification) + 131.52*blocks + 87.68*blocks*extension_weeks + meter charges
parameters.inspection_fees: hourly per IB 502 when not tied to an approved Right-of-Way permit
parameters.processing_fee_charged_per: each traffic control permit request (initial, extension, modification)

rules.applies_to: Applicants for San Diego Traffic Control Permits
rules.citation: City of San Diego Information Bulletin 177 (May 2026), section V
rules.quote: Traffic Control Initial (Up to 3 weeks) $131.52/block Traffic Control Extension (Per week) $87.68/block Traffic Control Processing Fee (Flat fee) $87.68
rules.notes: Fees are charged 'for each block'. Work or continuous encroachment without a permit is back-billed and added to the next approval.
rules.correction: All dollar amounts, the 3-week initial period, the 6-week extension limit and the per-block basis are confirmed. The formula charged the $87.68 processing fee once per project. IB 177 says the processing fee 'will be applied to all traffic control permit requests, including Traffic Control Initial, Traffic Control Extension and Modification of a previously approved traffic control permit', so it is owed once per request. Corrected the formula and added processing_fee_charged_per. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: San Diego: Traffic Control Permit valid up to 3 weeks; extensions filed 5 working days before expiration
rules.plain_english: A San Diego Traffic Control Permit is valid for up to three weeks at first. Extensions (billed weekly, up to six weeks) need City Engineer approval and must be submitted five working days before the permit expires. After three extensions, a new signed DS-269 is required.
rules.applies_to: Holders of San Diego Traffic Control Permits
rules.citation: City of San Diego Information Bulletin 177 (May 2026), sections V and IX; DSD Traffic Control Permit page
rules.quote: The permit may be extended with approval by the City Engineer and is subjected to additional permit fees. Extensions must be submitted five working days in advance of permit expiration.
rules.notes: The TCP page adds: 'After three extensions, a new filled-out and signed DS-269 form is required.'

rules.title: San Diego: notify police, fire, refuse, transit, signals and USA 5 working days before right-of-way work
rules.plain_english: Before starting work under a San Diego Traffic Control Permit, notify (when applicable) Police Dispatch, Fire Dispatch, refuse collection, San Diego Transit (MTS), Traffic Signals and Underground Service Alert at least five working days ahead, and notify owners or tenants before closing their driveways.

notify: Waste Management - Refuse Collection / Environmental Services (858-694-7000)

rules.applies_to: Contractors working under San Diego Traffic Control Permits
rules.citation: City of San Diego Information Bulletin 177 (May 2026), section VII; Form DS-269 (06-26) page 3
rules.source: https://www.sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/dsdib177.pdf (section VII 'Agency Notifications'); phone list on https://www.sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/ds269.pdf page 3
rules.quote: When applicable, the contractor shall notify all the following agencies five working days before starting work: Police Department Dispatch. Fire Department Dispatch. Waste Management - Refuse Collection. San Diego Transit. Communications and Electrical - Traffic Signals. Underground Service Alert.
rules.notes: The USA 811 ticket itself has its own state deadlines (see the existing usa-* rules).

rules.title: San Diego: post Tow-Away/No Parking signs 72 hours before right-of-way work
rules.plain_english: Post Tow-Away/No Parking signs at least 72 hours before starting work in a San Diego street, and cover or tag parking meters where needed.
rules.applies_to: Contractors working under San Diego Traffic Control Permits
rules.citation: City of San Diego Information Bulletin 177 (May 2026), section VIII; Form DS-269 (06-26) item 13
rules.quote: The contractor shall post Tow-Away/No Parking signs 72 hours before commencing work and cover parking meters (where applicable).

rules.title: San Diego: right-of-way work without a valid Traffic Control Permit brings a stop-work order, NOV and fines
rules.plain_english: Working in a San Diego right-of-way without an approved Traffic Control Permit, or after it expires, results in a stop-work order, a notice of violation and Building and Land Use Enforcement fines. The City also back-bills the permit fees for the unpermitted period.

consequences: Building and Land Use Enforcement fines
back-billed fees added to next approval

rules.applies_to: Anyone working in the San Diego public right-of-way
rules.citation: City of San Diego Information Bulletin 177 (May 2026), section V 'Work Without a Permit'
rules.quote: Any work in the public right-of-way (ROW) requires a traffic control permit. Work without an approved or expired traffic control permit will result in a stop of work, notice of violation (NOV) and subject to Building and Land Use Enforcement fines.
rules.notes: Fine amounts are not stated in IB 177. DS-269 item 9 adds that work creating an undue safety risk or severe congestion may be shut down by City Traffic Engineers, the City Inspector/FIT-RE or the Police Department.

rules.title: San Diego: traffic control plans must follow the 2026 CA MUTCD or the application is canceled
rules.plain_english: San Diego traffic control plans must conform to the 2026 California MUTCD, the Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction with regional and City amendments, and IB 177. Applications that do not are canceled and must be resubmitted.

parameters.standard: California MUTCD 2026
also: Standard Specifications for Public Works Construction (Greenbook) with Regional and City Supplemental Amendments
plan_must_show: plan view with dimensions, parking, curb zones, bus stops, driveways
street, lane, bike lane and sidewalk widths
advance warning sign spacing and taper length

rules.applies_to: Applicants for San Diego Traffic Control Permits
rules.citation: City of San Diego Information Bulletin 177 (May 2026), sections II-III
rules.quote: Applications that do not follow the requirements of the California Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices (CA MUTCD) 2026 and this information bulletin will be canceled.
rules.notes: The CA MUTCD itself (dot.ca.gov) could not be fetched; this rule rests on the City bulletin.

rules.title: San Diego: traffic control workers must be trained by an ATSSA-certified (or equivalent) supervisor
rules.plain_english: Everyone doing traffic control under a San Diego permit must be trained by a supervisor certified by ATSSA (or equivalent), as the MUTCD requires, and the application must list all traffic control subcontractors with contact information.

parameters.training: by a supervisor certified by ATSSA or equivalent

rules.applies_to: Contractors and traffic control subcontractors working under San Diego Traffic Control Permits
rules.citation: City of San Diego Form DS-269 (06-26), Requirements item 2
rules.quote: All traffic control workers are required to be trained, by a supervisor, certified by the American Traffic Safety Services Association (ATSSA), or equivalent, as required by Sections 6D.03 and 6E.01 of the MUTCD. The name and contact information of all Traffic Control subcontractors shall be submitted with this application.
rules.notes: Cal/OSHA flagger rules (8 CCR 1599) also apply; see the osha2- rules.

rules.title: San Diego Traffic Control Permit: $1,000,000 liability insurance naming the City as additional insured
rules.plain_english: To get a San Diego Traffic Control Permit you must declare under penalty of perjury that you carry public liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 combined single limit for the permit term, naming the City as additional insured, and you must agree to defend and indemnify the City.
rules.applies_to: Contractors/permittees applying for San Diego Traffic Control Permits
rules.citation: City of San Diego Form DS-269 (06-26), Insurance, Indemnification and Hold Harmless Agreement
rules.source: https://www.sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/ds269.pdf (page 2, Insurance, Indemnification and Hold Harmless Agreement, declaration 1)
rules.quote: I have and will continue to maintain public liability insurance in the amount of $1,000,000 combined single limit during the term of the permit, naming the City of San Diego an additional insured.
rules.notes: SDMC 82.27 text was not readable.

rules.title: San Diego DS-269: work under a Traffic Control Permit is stated to be subject to prevailing wage (SDMC 310.0105)
rules.plain_english: San Diego's Traffic Control Permit form states that all work under the permit is subject to prevailing wage requirements under SDMC 310.0105. Check with the City whether this applies to your private job before pricing it.

parameters.applies_per_form: all work under the Traffic Control Permit

rules.applies_to: Contractors working under San Diego Traffic Control Permits
rules.citation: City of San Diego Form DS-269 (06-26), Requirements item 3
rules.quote: All work under this Traffic Control Permit is subject to prevailing wage requirements per Chapter 3 Section 310.0105 of the San Diego Municipal Code.
rules.notes: SDMC 310.0105 could not be read, so its actual scope (for example, whether it reaches privately funded work in the right-of-way) is unknown. The form statement is recorded as printed.

rules.title: San Diego: plate or backfill trenches after hours and clean the street daily
rules.plain_english: In San Diego streets, trenches must be backfilled or covered with steel plates (with an asphalt berm on all edges) whenever work stops. All dirt, dust and debris must be removed from the street at the end of each day and at the end of the job, and the street must stay drivable at all times.

trench_after_hours: steel-plated with asphalt concrete berm on all edges
parameters.restoration: contractor restores paving, striping, markings and signal loop detectors per City Whitebook (item 18)

rules.applies_to: Contractors working under San Diego Traffic Control Permits
rules.citation: City of San Diego Form DS-269 (06-26), Requirements items 15 and 18
rules.quote: Trenches shall be backfilled or steel-plated during non-working hours. Steel plates shall have asphalt concrete berm on all edges. All dirt, dust and debris shall be removed from the street at the end of each day and at the end of the job. The street shall be in drivable condition at all times.

rules.title: San Diego: keep an ADA-compliant pedestrian route around sidewalk work
rules.plain_english: When sidewalk concrete is curing after hours, secure the area with reflective or lighted barricades and keep pedestrians moving through an ADA-compliant alternate walkway, a reasonable detour, or by reopening the path in ADA-compliant condition.

pedestrian_options: existing path reopened in ADA-compliant condition

rules.applies_to: Contractors doing sidewalk work under San Diego Traffic Control Permits
rules.citation: City of San Diego Form DS-269 (06-26), Requirements items 6 and 17
rules.quote: During non-working hours of concrete sidewalk cure time, the contractor shall secure the work area with retro-reflective or illuminated barricades and/or barriers. Pedestrian circulation shall be maintained through an ADA-compliant alternative walkway, a reasonable pedestrian detour, or the existing path reopened in ADA-complaint conditions.
rules.notes: Quoted as printed ('ADA-complaint').

rules.title: San Diego: open travel lanes at least 12 ft (14 ft next to bike lanes) during traffic control
rules.plain_english: Lanes kept open past a San Diego work zone must be at least 12 feet wide, or 14 feet next to a bike lane, unless the City Traffic Engineer approves otherwise.
rules.applies_to: Traffic control plans for San Diego streets
rules.citation: City of San Diego Form DS-269 (06-26), Requirements item 11
rules.quote: All travel lanes shall be a minimum of 12 feet wide and 14 feet adjacent to bike lanes unless otherwise approved by the City Traffic Engineer.

rules.title: San Diego: 5 working days' notice to FIT Traffic Field Services for work affecting traffic signals
rules.plain_english: If your San Diego right-of-way work affects traffic signals, contact FIT Traffic Field Services at least five working days in advance (619-446-5242, FIT_Traffic@sandiego.gov).
rules.applies_to: Contractors whose work affects San Diego traffic signals
rules.citation: City of San Diego Form DS-269 (06-26), Requirements item 7
rules.quote: Contractor shall contact FIT Traffic Field Services (see below) for work affecting traffic signals, which requires a minimum of 5 working days advance notice.

rules.title: San Diego: hold the right-of-way pre-construction meeting before any work starts
rules.plain_english: After a San Diego right-of-way or traffic control permit is issued, a pre-construction meeting for Grading and Right-of-Way Inspections must be held before any work can start. For ROW permits, call Construction Management and Field Services (858-627-3200) to schedule it with the Resident Engineer; the permit becomes active only after the meeting.

parameters.schedule_with: Resident Engineer, ECP Construction Management and Field Services 858-627-3200

rules.applies_to: Holders of San Diego Traffic Control and Right-of-Way permits
rules.citation: City of San Diego DSD Traffic Control Permit page; DSD Right-of-Way Permit page (Inspections)
rules.quote: After the permit is issued, a preconstruction meeting for Grading and Right-of-Way Inspections must be held before any work can start.
rules.notes: ROW page: 'Upon completion of the pre-construction meeting, the permit will be considered as "active."'

rules.title: San Diego: permit needed for a dumpster or storage container in the street ($176.57/month dumpster fee)
rules.plain_english: Placing a dumpster or temporary storage container (moving pod) in a San Diego street or sidewalk area needs a Traffic Control Permit. Fees: dumpster $176.57 per month (up to 4 weeks), storage container $87.68 for up to one week, plus a one-time $87.68 processing fee and $20 per blocked meter per day.

parameters.permit: Traffic Control Permit for temporary storage container or dumpster
forms: dumpster or storage container placement plan

rules.applies_to: Contractors, owners and bin companies placing dumpsters or storage containers in the San Diego public right-of-way
rules.citation: SDMC 129.0702 (per IB 718); City of San Diego Information Bulletin 718 (July 2026)
rules.source: https://www.sandiego.gov/development-services/forms-publications/information-bulletin/718 (sections I and V); also https://www.sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/dsdib177.pdf (section V 'Dumpster Permits')
rules.quote: A Traffic Control Permit for a temporary storage container or dumpster is required for containers that encroach into the public right of way, including the sidewalk area
rules.notes: IB 718 lists the dumpster fee as '$176.57 per month'; IB 177 lists 'Traffic Control, Dumpster Fee (Up to 4 weeks) $176.57'.

rules.title: San Diego dumpster placement: no painted curbs; 10 ft, 25 ft and 15 ft-from-hydrant clearances
rules.plain_english: A dumpster or storage container in a San Diego street may not sit in front of red, white or blue curb. Keep at least 10 feet from the dumpster door to the nearest obstruction, 25 feet from the door to an alley or curb return, and 15 feet from the door to a fire hydrant.
rules.applies_to: Dumpster and storage container placements in the San Diego public right-of-way
rules.citation: City of San Diego Information Bulletin 718 (July 2026), section III
rules.quote: They may not be placed in front of a painted curb, such as a no-parking zone (red curb), passenger loading zone (white curb), or accessibility parking zone (blue curb). A minimum of 10 feet of clearance is required from the dumpster door to the nearest obstruction. A minimum of 25 feet of clearance is required from the dumpster door to the alley or curb return. A minimum of 15 feet must be maintained between the dumpster door and the fire hydrant.

rules.title: San Diego: at least 3 working days' notice before placing a dumpster or storage container in the street
rules.plain_english: The San Diego dumpster/storage container permit application needs start and end dates with at least three working days' notice before the container is placed.
rules.applies_to: Dumpster and storage container placements in the San Diego public right-of-way
rules.citation: City of San Diego Information Bulletin 718 (July 2026), section III
rules.quote: Work start/end dates (at least three working days’ notice required before placing storage container or dumpster).

rules.title: San Diego: post No Parking signs 72 hours before placing a dumpster in the street
rules.plain_english: Post Tow-Away/No Parking signs 72 hours before a dumpster or storage container is placed in a San Diego street, and deactivate parking meters where applicable.
rules.applies_to: Holders of San Diego dumpster/storage container permits
rules.citation: City of San Diego Information Bulletin 718 (July 2026), section VII
rules.quote: The permit holder shall post Tow-Away/No Parking signs 72 hours before placing the storage container or dumpster and deactivating parking meters (where applicable).

rules.title: San Diego: storage container permit valid up to 7 days; extensions filed 5 working days ahead
rules.plain_english: A San Diego permit for a storage container in the street lasts up to 7 days. The City Engineer may extend it for extra fees if you apply at least 5 working days before it expires.
rules.applies_to: Holders of San Diego storage container permits
rules.citation: City of San Diego Information Bulletin 718 (July 2026), section VIII
rules.quote: The permit for a storage container is valid for up to 7 days. However, under certain circumstances, a permit may be extended. Upon the City Engineer's approval, extensions will be subject to additional permit fees. Extensions must be submitted at least 5 working days before permit expiration.
rules.notes: Dumpster permits are billed monthly (local-sd-dumpster-in-row-permit-and-fees).

rules.title: San Diego: Public Right-of-Way Permit needed for private improvements, public improvements and construction in the ROW
rules.plain_english: A San Diego Public Right-of-Way (ROW) Permit is needed, unless exempt, to build public improvements as a non-City entity, to build private structures or improvements in the ROW or a public service easement, for any construction activity in the ROW, and to plant anything taller than 30 inches in the ROW (outside a Street Tree Permit). Typical examples: curbs, gutters, sidewalks, driveways, dry utilities and sidewalk cafes.

triggers: construction of public improvements by an entity other than the City
privately owned structures, facilities or improvements in the ROW or a public service easement
any construction activity within a public right-of-way (SDMC 54.0116, 54.0117)
planting over 30 inches tall in the ROW not covered by a Street Tree Permit
exempt: parkway irrigation maintained by fronting owner
parkway landscape under 30 inches maintained by fronting owner

rules.applies_to: Contractors, owners and utilities working in the City of San Diego public right-of-way
rules.citation: SDMC 129.0701-129.0750 (Ch. 12, Art. 9, Div. 7), 54.0116, 54.0117 (as cited by DSD); DSD Right-of-Way Permit page
rules.quote: A Public Right-of-Way Permit is required for the following unless otherwise exempt under §129.0703: The construction of public improvements by an entity other than the City. The construction of privately owned structures, facilities, or improvements in the public right of way or a public service easement. Any construction activity within a public right-of-way, as required by Municipal Code §54.0116 and §54.0117. The planting of any tree, shrub, or plant greater than 30 inches in height in the public right-of-way where not otherwise covered by a Street Tree Permit per Chapter 6, Article 2, Division 6 (Street Planting).
rules.notes: SDMC Chapter 12, Article 9, Division 7 itself could not be read (docs.sandiego.gov blocked). The City Engineer may also require a building permit for private structures in the ROW or waive the ROW permit per the Land Development Manual.

rules.title: San Diego ROW permit: 2-year term, at most two 180-day extensions
rules.plain_english: A San Diego Right-of-Way permit lasts two years from issuance unless conditioned otherwise. You can get at most two extensions of 6 months (180 days) each, with a processing fee.
rules.applies_to: Holders of San Diego Public Right-of-Way permits
rules.citation: SDMC 129.0750 (as summarized by DSD); DSD Right-of-Way Permit page
rules.quote: ROW permits are provided with an initial duration of two years unless otherwise conditioned in the San Diego Municipal Code, starting at the permit issuance. Should extenuating circumstances require additional time to complete the approved scope of work, extensions may be granted. The San Diego Municipal Code allows the consideration of two extensions. Each extension provided is in 6-month (180-day) increments. No additional extensions may be offered.
rules.notes: max_total_days is derived (2 x 365 + 2 x 180).

rules.title: San Diego ROW permit extension: apply within 60 days before expiration; no extension after it expires
rules.plain_english: Apply for a San Diego ROW permit time extension (Form DS-340) no earlier than 60 calendar days before the permit expires, and before it expires. An expired ROW permit cannot be extended.
rules.applies_to: Holders of San Diego Public Right-of-Way permits
rules.citation: SDMC 129.0750 (as summarized by DSD); DSD Right-of-Way Permit page
rules.quote: If a ROW Permit expires before an application for an extension of time is submitted, an extension shall not be granted. The applicant/permittee may submit an application for an extension of time no earlier than 60 calendar days prior to the permit expiration date.

rules.title: San Diego: Encroachment Maintenance and Removal Agreement for private improvements in the ROW
rules.plain_english: Any privately owned or privately maintained improvement in a San Diego street right-of-way or public service easement (for example a private storm drain tie-in, planter boxes or nonstandard parkway features) needs an Encroachment Maintenance and Removal Agreement (EMRA), even when no ROW permit is required.

parameters.document: Encroachment Maintenance and Removal Agreement (EMRA), Form DS-3237
not_encroachments: standard water, sewer or fire services

rules.applies_to: Owners and contractors installing private improvements in the San Diego ROW or public service easements
rules.citation: SDMC 129.0715 and 129.0717 (as cited by DSD); DSD Right-of-Way Permit page; IB 576
rules.quote: An EMRA is required for any privately owned and/or privately maintained encroachment located in the public right-of-way or a public service easement.

rules.title: San Diego: written notice to City field survey at least 7 days before disturbing a vertical control monument
rules.plain_english: If construction will disturb or destroy a vertical control survey monument, notify the City of San Diego field survey section in writing at least 7 days before demolition or construction. The permittee pays to preserve and replace any monuments destroyed.

parameters.notify: City of San Diego field survey section

rules.applies_to: Permittees doing construction or demolition in the San Diego right-of-way
rules.citation: DSD Right-of-Way Permit page (Monument Preservation); Streets & Highways Code 1810.5 and B&P 8771 (cited by DSD)
rules.quote: If a vertical control monument is to be disturbed or destroyed, the City of San Diego field survey section shall be notified in writing at least 7 days prior to demolition/construction.
rules.notes: State statutes cited by the City (S&H Code 1810.5, B&P 8771) were not read (leginfo blocked).

rules.title: San Diego: no excavation in a moratorium street without a City Engineer waiver
rules.plain_english: San Diego does not allow excavation of new pavement in a 'moratorium street' (a recently rebuilt, resurfaced or slurry-sealed street) without a valid moratorium waiver. This applies to public and private street work.

parameters.applies_to: any street disturbance, public or private
parameters.trigger_extent: complete continuous section intersection to intersection and curb to curb (or median to curb); intersections PCR to PCR

rules.applies_to: Contractors and utilities excavating in City of San Diego streets
rules.citation: SDMC 62.1203, 62.1206 (Street Preservation Ordinance) as stated in City Engineer memorandum of Sept. 6, 2016
rules.quote: Per SDMC section 62.1206 - Moratorium Streets, excavations of new pavement areas within these areas shall not be permitted in a moratorium street without a valid moratorium waiver.
rules.notes: Read from an official City Engineer memorandum (2016). The current SDMC Division 12 text could not be read. See local-sd-moratorium-street-definition for the moratorium periods and their uncertainty.

rules.title: San Diego moratorium street: resurfaced/reconstructed within 5 years or slurry sealed within 3 years (2016 text)
rules.plain_english: Under the 2016 City Engineer memo, a San Diego 'moratorium street' is one reconstructed or resurfaced in the last five years, or slurry sealed in the last three years. The current code may use different periods; check the street with the City before bidding trench work.
rules.applies_to: Contractors and utilities planning excavation in City of San Diego streets
rules.citation: SDMC 62.1203 as quoted in City Engineer memorandum of Sept. 6, 2016
rules.quote: SDMC section 62.1203 defines Moratorium Street as any street, or portion thereof, that has been reconstructed or resurfaced in the preceding five year period or slurry sealed in the preceding three year period.
rules.notes: CONFLICT: a search-engine excerpt of the current SDMC Division 12 (docs.sandiego.gov, not readable here) described a three-year period for newly constructed, reconstructed or asphalt-overlaid streets, and City Standard Drawing SDG-107 (2024) speaks of streets 'under moratorium due to new construction, reconstruction, or asphalt overlay'. The periods above are from the 2016 memo and may be outdated.

rules.title: San Diego: asphalt overlay a moratorium street within 180 working days after trench repair approval
rules.plain_english: If you trench in a San Diego street that is under moratorium, you must asphalt overlay it within 180 working days after the City Engineer approves the trench repair.

parameters.clock_starts: Engineer approves the trench repair
parameters.applies_to: moratorium streets (new construction, reconstruction or asphalt overlay)

rules.applies_to: Excavators in City of San Diego moratorium streets
rules.citation: City of San Diego Standard Drawing SDG-107 (Pavement Restoration for AC Surfaced Streets - Major Excavation), note 6
rules.quote: EXCAVATOR SHALL ASPHALT OVERLAY IN MORATORIUM STREETS UNDER MORATORIUM DUE TO NEW CONSTRUCTION,RECONSTRUCTION, OR ASPHALT OVERLAY WITHIN 180 WORKING DAYS AFTER THE ENGINEER APPROVES THE TRENCH REPAIR.

rules.title: San Diego: final street restoration within 180 calendar days of the trench cap
rules.plain_english: On San Diego streets not getting a curb-to-curb overlay, final street restoration must be completed within 180 calendar days of the trench cap. Trench caps must be milled and resurfaced no sooner than 30 calendar days after the first asphalt is placed (where no full-width overlay is done before acceptance).

parameters.clock_starts: trench cap

rules.applies_to: Excavators in City of San Diego AC-surfaced streets
rules.citation: City of San Diego Standard Drawing SDG-107, notes 1-3
rules.quote: IF THE STREET IS NOT SUBJECT TO CURB TO CURB ASPHALT OVERLAY, IT MUST COMPLETE FINAL STREET RESTORATION WITHIN 180 CALENDAR DAYS OF THE TRENCH CAP.
rules.notes: Note 1: any trench 7 feet or wider and longer than 100 feet must be reconstructed with the full pavement section for the street classification (SDG-113).

rules.title: San Diego C&D Debris Deposit Ordinance: most building, combination and demolition permits must divert debris
rules.plain_english: In San Diego most construction, demolition and remodeling projects that need a building, combination or demolition permit must submit a Waste Management Form, pay a refundable recycling deposit, and recycle, reuse or donate their construction and demolition debris instead of landfilling it.

parameters.ordinance: C&D Debris Deposit Ordinance, SDMC Ch. 6, Art. 6, Div. 6
steps: Waste Management Form (WMF I) at permit issuance
submit receipts within 180 days of final inspection

rules.applies_to: Applicants for City of San Diego building, combination and demolition permits
rules.citation: SDMC Chapter 6, Article 6, Division 6 (as described by ESD); City of San Diego ESD C&D Recycling page
rules.quote: requires that the majority of construction, demolition and remodeling projects requiring building, combination and demolition permits divert construction and demolition debris from landfill disposal.
rules.notes: The ordinance text (docs.sandiego.gov) could not be read; this rule rests on the ESD program pages.

rules.title: San Diego C&D recycling deposit: $0.40/sq ft or $0.20/sq ft, or $1,000 flat for residential alterations
rules.plain_english: San Diego's refundable C&D recycling deposit is $0.40 per square foot for residential new construction, non-residential alterations and demolition (1,000-100,000 sq ft: $400-$40,000), $0.20 per square foot for non-residential new construction (1,000-50,000 sq ft: $200-$10,000), and a flat $1,000 for residential alterations of 1,000-6,999 sq ft.

parameters.formula: deposit = rate * min(sq_ft, max_sq_ft_subject) when sq_ft >= 1,000 (flat $1,000 for residential alterations 1,000-6,999 sq ft)
parameters.max_sq_ft_column_label: Maximum Sq. Ft. Subject to Ordinance

rules.applies_to: Applicants for City of San Diego permits subject to the C&D Debris Deposit Ordinance
rules.citation: SDMC Ch. 6, Art. 6, Div. 6 (as described by ESD); ESD 'Application Process - Before the Project Starts' deposit table
rules.quote: Residential New Construction, Non-residential Alterations, Demolition $0.40 1,000 100,000 $400-$40,000 Non-residential New Construction $0.20 1,000 50,000 $200-$10,000
rules.notes: The capped formula is inferred from the published ranges (rate x maximum square feet = top of range). Flat rate row: 'Residential Alterations* $1,000 1,000 6,999 $1,000'; footnote: 'Residential Alterations 7,000 square feet and greater in size, and hotels are considered Non-Residential Alterations.'
rules.correction: All rates, square-foot limits, deposit ranges, the $1,000 flat rate, the 7,000 sq ft/hotel footnote and the $200 floor are confirmed. The capped formula deposit = rate x min(sq_ft, max_sq_ft_subject) does not appear in the table. The column is headed 'Maximum Sq. Ft. Subject to Ordinance', and the cap is inferred from the 'Range of Deposits' column. The inference was noted only in notes. Added formula_is_inferred so tools do not treat the cap above 100,000 or 50,000 sq ft as published.

rules.title: San Diego C&D deposit exemptions: roofing, small single-trade permits, no-plan permits and deposits under $200
rules.plain_english: San Diego's C&D deposit does not apply to roofing, many small replacement or repair items (fences, retaining walls, windows, doors, decks, pools, siding and similar), facade work, re-pipes, foundation repairs, modular or mobile home placement, electrical-only, plumbing-only or mechanical-only permits, permits that need no plans, hazardous-waste-only projects, or projects whose deposit would be under $200.

exempt: pre-fabricated modular building or mobile home
projects not requiring plans for a building permit

rules.applies_to: Applicants for City of San Diego permits
rules.citation: SDMC Ch. 6, Art. 6, Div. 6 (as described by ESD); ESD 'Application Process' page
rules.quote: Projects which require only an electric, only a plumbing permit or only a mechanical permit; Projects which do not require plans for a Building Permit; Projects which are expected to generate only hazardous waste and/or hazardous substances, and Projects for which the construction and demolition debris deposit is less than $200.
rules.notes: CALGreen 65% diversion (calgreen-construction-waste-65-percent) can still apply to exempt projects.

rules.title: San Diego: no permit issued until the Waste Management Form is filed and the C&D deposit is paid
rules.plain_english: For San Diego projects covered by the C&D ordinance, the building or demolition permit will not be issued until you submit Waste Management Form Part I (with debris estimates in tons and the certified facilities you will use) and pay the refundable deposit. Keep a copy of the WMF I for the refund request.

parameters.form: Waste Management Form Part I (WMF I)
must_list: Certified Recycling Facilities to be used

rules.applies_to: Applicants for City of San Diego permits subject to the C&D Debris Deposit Ordinance
rules.citation: SDMC Ch. 6, Art. 6, Div. 6 (as described by ESD); ESD 'Application Process' page
rules.quote: Pay the refundable C&D debris recycling deposit at time of permit issuance. Permits will not be issued unless the WMF - I is submitted and the deposit is paid.

rules.title: San Diego: divert 65% of C&D debris by weight (permits issued on or after July 1, 2016)
rules.plain_english: San Diego projects under the C&D ordinance must recycle or reuse at least 65% by weight of all construction and demolition debris they generate (50% for permits issued through June 30, 2016).
rules.applies_to: City of San Diego projects subject to the C&D Debris Deposit Ordinance
rules.citation: SDMC Ch. 6, Art. 6, Div. 6 (as described by ESD); ESD C&D Recycling page
rules.quote: For projects with permits issued on or after July 1, 2016, the diversion requirement will increase to 65% by weight of the total C&D debris generated by the project. The diversion requirement for projects with permits issued through June 30, 2016, will remain at 50%.
rules.notes: Same percentage as the CALGreen state minimum.

rules.title: San Diego: request the C&D deposit refund within 180 days of final inspection
rules.plain_english: To get your San Diego C&D deposit back, submit WMF Part II, the WMF I copy and all recycling, reuse and disposal receipts (and photos) within 180 days after passing final inspection. Late or incomplete requests get no refund.

parameters.day_type: not specified on the page ('within 180 days'); read as calendar days
submit: WMF II (on back of WMF I copy)
all recycling, reuse and disposal receipts, photos and documentation
parameters.mail_to: City of San Diego Environmental Services Department, Attn: C&D Diversion Coordinator, 9601 Ridgehaven Court, St. 320, San Diego, CA 92123

rules.applies_to: Permit holders who paid a San Diego C&D debris recycling deposit
rules.citation: SDMC Ch. 6, Art. 6, Div. 6 (as described by ESD); ESD 'At the End of the Project' page
rules.quote: Requests submitted after 180 days of passing the final inspection date will not be eligible for a refund. In 180 days, incomplete requests that do not submit additional documentation or proof will not be eligible for the refund.
rules.correction: The 180-day window, the submittals, the mailing address and the no-refund rule for late or incomplete requests are confirmed. day_type = 'calendar' is not printed; the page says only 'within 180 days of passing final inspection'. Relabeled day_type to show the page does not specify it.

rules.title: San Diego: full C&D deposit refund at 65%+ diversion; pro-rated refund below 65%
rules.plain_english: San Diego returns the whole C&D deposit if 65% or more of the project's debris was recycled or reused. If you recycled less, the refund is pro-rated by the recycling rate you achieved; the unrefunded part is lost.
rules.applies_to: Permit holders who paid a San Diego C&D debris recycling deposit
rules.citation: SDMC Ch. 6, Art. 6, Div. 6 (as described by ESD); ESD 'At the End of the Project' page
rules.quote: The total C&D debris recycling deposit paid for the permit may be returned to the applicant if 65% or more of all C&D debris was recycled and/or reused. Refunds for projects recycling less than the required amount will be pro-rated according to the recycling rate achieved by the specific project.
rules.notes: The exact proration formula is not published on the page; do not compute a partial refund without the City's formula.

rules.title: San Diego: use City Certified C&D Recycling Facilities to qualify for the deposit refund
rules.plain_english: Debris must go to City-certified recycling facilities (or be donated with receipts and photos) for it to count toward your San Diego deposit refund. Material taken to a landfill gets no diversion credit, and each receipt must show the project address and permit number. The City publishes the certified facility directory.
rules.applies_to: Permit holders who paid a San Diego C&D debris recycling deposit
rules.citation: SDMC Ch. 6, Art. 6, Div. 6 (as described by ESD); ESD 'Application Process' page
rules.quote: Certified Recycling Facilities must be used in order to be eligible for a deposit refund. Donating reusable goods is also acceptable with appropriate documentation, such as receipts and photos.
rules.correction: The quote and the requirement are confirmed. directory_edition said '2025'. The file at the URL is now the 2026 directory, last updated October 2026; only the link text on the ESD C&D page still reads '2025'. The directory adds that landfill disposal gets no diversion credit and that the project address and permit number must be on the receipt. Updated directory_edition and added those receipt rules. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction (receipt and landfill rules re-read in the 2026 directory, fetched 2026-11-27); no value changed.

rules.title: San Diego C&D deposit program: franchised hauler recommended, not required; contractors may self-haul their own debris
rules.plain_english: For the San Diego C&D deposit program the City recommends (but does not require) using a City franchised hauler, and says you may haul your own project's waste. What matters for the refund is that loads go to certified facilities with receipts. The City's franchise hauler list is published online. Whether a hauler without a City franchise may haul other people's C&D debris for hire was not confirmed.

parameters.third_party_for_hire_hauling_without_fra: not verified (SDMC Chapter 6 franchise provisions not readable)

rules.applies_to: Contractors managing C&D debris on City of San Diego permits
rules.citation: ESD C&D Recycling page and C&D FAQ; ESD Franchise Hauler Directory (REV 8/9/24)
rules.source: https://www.sandiego.gov/environmental-services/recycling/cd (step 3); https://www.sandiego.gov/environmental-services/recycling/cd/cdfaq ('Can I haul the waste from my own project?'); list https://www.sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/esd-franchised-hauler-list.pdf
rules.quote: Can I haul the waste from my own project? Yes. Please note: some recyclers will not accept loads in pick-up trucks. Make sure to clarify that with the Certified Recycling Facilities chosen before planning on bringing your C&D recycling loads to them.
rules.notes: The ESD C&D page lists 'Use Franchised Haulers (recommended to help ensure compliance)'. Whether hauling C&D for others for hire without a City franchise is lawful could not be checked (SDMC Chapter 6 franchise provisions not readable). The franchise directory is dated REV 8/9/24.
rules.correction: The quote, the recommendation, self-hauling your own project and the 21 directory names (REV 8/9/24) are confirmed. 'franchised_hauler_required_for_cd: false' went beyond the text. ESD calls franchised haulers 'recommended' for the deposit program and allows self-hauling your own project, but no source read says a non-franchised third party may haul C&D for hire. Narrowed that parameter to the deposit program and marked for-hire hauling as unverified. Rewording 2026-11-27: title and plain_english reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: San Diego: businesses must get trash, recycling and organics service from one City franchise hauler
rules.plain_english: Under San Diego's Recycling Ordinance, businesses and privately serviced residences must get recycling, organic waste recycling and trash collection from one City franchise hauler of their choice; the City does not assign haulers or set their rates. This covers ongoing service at a business (for example a contractor's yard).
rules.applies_to: Businesses (including contractor offices and yards) and privately serviced residences in the City of San Diego
rules.citation: City of San Diego Recycling Ordinance (as described in the ESD Franchise Hauler Directory)
rules.quote: According to the City’s Recycling Ordinance, all businesses and privately-serviced residences are required to have recycling, organic waste recycling and trash collection from one Franchise Hauler.
rules.notes: Category reflects the service-agreement duty. The ordinance text was not read.

rules.title: Miramar Landfill (San Diego): all loads must be covered; $50 fee per uncovered load
rules.plain_english: Every load brought to the City's Miramar Landfill must be covered. An uncovered load is charged $50, for any vehicle.
rules.applies_to: Contractors and haulers delivering loads to the Miramar Landfill
rules.citation: City of San Diego Miramar Landfill & Greenery Processing Fee Schedule (effective July 1, 2026; updated Oct. 22, 2026); SDMC 66.0124-66.0129
rules.quote: All loads must be covered. Fee for uncovered loads: $50.
rules.notes: Quote is from the ESD Refuse Disposal Fees page; the FY2027 schedule lists 'Uncovered Loads Any vehicle $50 per load'. The 2022 regulations defined an uncovered load as one where 'an item or any part of an item could possibly fall from, bounce out of, or blow from a vehicle or receptacle during the course of transportation.'

rules.title: Miramar Landfill FY2027 C&D debris disposal: $241/ton (City waste), $257/ton (non-City)
rules.plain_english: From July 1, 2026 the City's Miramar Landfill charges $241 per ton for weighed C&D debris generated in the City of San Diego and $257 per ton for C&D from outside the City ($233-$234 per ton for City franchise haulers). Unweighed small loads pay flat rates by vehicle tier ($108/$122 tier 1, $352/$374 tier 2, $1,513/$1,623 tier 3).

included_fees: Refuse Collectors Business Tax $8/ton (standard weighed loads)

rules.applies_to: Contractors and haulers disposing of C&D debris at the Miramar Landfill
rules.citation: City of San Diego Miramar Landfill & Greenery Processing Fee Schedule (effective July 1, 2026), Sections A-C
rules.notes: Quote is the 'City Waste' row of Section B (columns: General Refuse, Special Handling, C&D Debris, Food, Green, Fibrous Greens, Clean Wood). Disposal at the landfill does not count as diversion for the C&D deposit.

rules.title: Miramar Landfill: clean fill dirt only with an approved Clean Fill Dirt Program application before hauling
rules.plain_english: Export soil can go to the Miramar Landfill as clean fill only if the City approved your Clean Fill Dirt Program application before you transport it. Loads must come in approved commercial self-dumping trucks, Saturday-Friday 7 a.m.-4 p.m., and contaminated or unsuitable loads are rejected with fees.

rejected_load_consequences: administrative fees including False Declaration fee
escalating penalties, up to prohibition from the CFDP

rules.applies_to: Contractors exporting soil to the Miramar Landfill
rules.citation: City of San Diego Miramar Landfill & Greenery Processing Fee Schedule (effective July 1, 2026), Section D
rules.quote: An application to use the CFDP must be completed, submitted, and approved by the City prior to transporting CFDP fill material to the Landfill.
rules.notes: Per-load clean fill fees are set by the Mayor's designee and not printed in the schedule.

rules.title: Los Angeles construction/demolition hours: Mon-Fri 7 a.m.-9 p.m., Sat 8 a.m.-6 p.m., no Sunday work
rules.plain_english: In the City of Los Angeles, construction and demolition may only happen Monday to Friday 7 a.m.-9 p.m. and Saturday 8 a.m.-6 p.m. No work is permitted on Sunday. Work outside these hours can be fined. Hillside Construction Regulation districts have stricter hours.

parameters.stricter_districts: Hillside Construction Regulation (HCR) supplemental use districts

rules.applies_to: All construction and demolition work in the City of Los Angeles
rules.citation: LAMC 41.40 (as stated by LADBS); LADBS 'Permitted Construction and Demolition Hours' page
rules.quote: Construction and demolition activities must be performed during the permitted hours described in the table below. Any activity outside of these hours may result in a fine. Monday through Friday 7:00 AM - 9:00 PM Saturday 8:00 AM - 6:00 PM Sunday No Work Permitted
rules.notes: The LADBS hours page does not mention holidays; the LADBS Good Neighbor Construction Practices sheet gives 'Saturday or National Holiday 8 AM - 6 PM' (local-la-national-holiday-hours). The LAMC 41.40 text (codelibrary.amlegal.com) could not be read, so the code's 500-foot residential condition and its exceptions are recorded separately as unverified (local-la-41-40-residential-500ft-unverified).

rules.title: Los Angeles: national holidays follow Saturday hours (8 a.m.-6 p.m.)
rules.plain_english: On national holidays, construction in Los Angeles is limited to 8 a.m.-6 p.m., the same as Saturday.
rules.applies_to: All construction and demolition work in the City of Los Angeles
rules.citation: LAMC 41.40 (as stated by LADBS); LADBS Good Neighbor Construction Practices (Rev. 3/2/15), item 9
rules.quote: Saturday or National Holiday 8 AM – 6 PM
rules.notes: The sheet does not list which days are 'National Holidays'; a federal-holiday calendar is the likely reading but is not stated. The sheet (Rev. 3/2/15) is still posted by LADBS; this line of its text layer is clean and string-matches, although other lines of the PDF duplicate letters.

rules.title: Los Angeles: working outside permitted hours can be a misdemeanor (fine up to $1,000 and/or up to 6 months in jail)
rules.plain_english: Breaking Los Angeles construction-hour rules (citywide or in hillside HCR districts) can be charged as a misdemeanor against the responsible party. LADBS states the penalty as a fine of $1,000 and/or imprisonment; the Code's penalty warning (as printed in a 2017 LADBS notice) sets the maximum at a $1,000 fine and/or six months in County Jail.

parameters.jail_max_source: 2017 LADBS/BBSC HCR notice penalty warning (not restated on the 2026 pages)

rules.applies_to: Contractors and owners working in the City of Los Angeles
rules.citation: LADBS 'Permitted Construction and Demolition Hours' and 'Hillside Construction Regulations (HCR)' pages
rules.quote: Failure to comply with the requirements may result in a misdemeanor charge for the responsible party, punishable by a fine of $1,000 and/or imprisonment.
rules.notes: The underlying LAMC penalty section was not read.
rules.correction: The misdemeanor charge against the responsible party and the $1,000 figure are confirmed on both current LADBS pages ('punishable by a fine of $1,000 and/or imprisonment'). LADBS's 2017 BBSC notice states the Code penalty in full: a fine of 'not more than $1,000.00' or County Jail for 'not more than six months', or both. $1,000 is therefore a maximum, not a fixed fine. Replaced fine_usd with fine_usd_max, added jail_months_max = 6 (from the 2017 notice) and reworded plain_english. Rewording 2026-11-27: title reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: Los Angeles hillside (HCR) districts: weekdays 8 a.m.-6 p.m.; Saturdays interior work only
rules.plain_english: In Los Angeles Hillside Construction Regulation districts (Bel Air-Beverly Crest, Bird Streets/Laurel Canyon, Franklin/Coldwater Canyon/Bowmont-Hazen, Northeast LA), construction is allowed only 8 a.m.-6 p.m. on weekdays, and only interior work on Saturdays.

districts.area: Bel Air - Beverly Crest Community Plan Area
Bird Streets and Laurel Canyon Area
Franklin Canyon, Coldwater Canyon, and Bowmont Hazen Area
Northeast Los Angeles Community Plan Area

parameters.scope: single-family residential developments in HCR supplemental use districts

rules.applies_to: Construction of single-family residential development in Los Angeles HCR supplemental use districts
rules.citation: LA Ordinance No. 184,827 et seq. (HCR Supplemental Use District); LADBS HCR page
rules.quote: In HCR districts, the following permissible working hours apply: During weekdays, work is permitted from 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM. On Saturdays only interior work is allowed.
rules.notes: The page lists Ordinance 184,828 for Bel Air but links the 185,491 document; recorded as shown.

rules.title: Los Angeles HCR districts: no excessive site floodlighting after 6 p.m.
rules.plain_english: In Los Angeles hillside HCR districts, lighting the site with floodlights or similar devices after 6 p.m. on any day is strictly prohibited.
rules.applies_to: Construction sites in Los Angeles HCR supplemental use districts
rules.citation: LA HCR Supplemental Use District ordinances; LADBS HCR page
rules.quote: Excessive exterior illumination of the site using floodlights or similar lighting devices is strictly prohibited after 6:00 PM on any day of the week.

rules.title: Los Angeles: importing or exporting more than 1,000 cubic yards in a hillside grading area needs a BBSC haul route hearing
rules.plain_english: In a Los Angeles Hillside Grading Area, moving more than 1,000 cubic yards of earth onto or off a site requires an approved haul route after a public hearing before the Board of Building and Safety Commissioners.

parameters.approval: public hearing before the Board of Building and Safety Commissioners (BBSC)

rules.applies_to: Grading and building projects importing or exporting earth in Los Angeles Hillside Grading Areas
rules.citation: LAMC 91.7006.7.5 (LABC); LADBS Application for Review of Import-Export (GGI-08, Rev. 7/18); Grading Plan Check Correction Sheet (2026 LABC) item 10
rules.quote: SECTION 91.7006.7.5, REQUIRES A PUBLIC HEARING BEFORE THE BOARD OF BUILDING AND SAFETY COMMISSIONERS (BBSC) FOR ANY IMPORT OR EXPORT OF MORE THAN 1,000 CUBIC YARDS OF EARTH MATERIAL IN A GRADING HILLSIDE AREA.
rules.effective: 2010-05-17 (application form effective date; reaffirmed by the 2026 LABC correction sheet, rev. 01/01/26)
rules.notes: The 2026 LABC correction sheet item 10: 'A Public hearing is required for on-site import or export of earth material in excess of 1,000 cubic yards in a “Hillside Grading Area” (7006.7).' Projects under Mayor's Emergency Executive Order No. 1 get ministerial haul route approval (local-la-eo1-haul-route-ministerial).

rules.title: Los Angeles haul route application: allow at least 8 weeks
rules.plain_english: A Los Angeles hillside haul route application goes to the Building and Safety Commissioners Office and takes at least eight weeks to process.
rules.applies_to: Projects needing a Los Angeles haul route approval
rules.citation: LADBS Grading/Retaining Wall/Shoring Plan Check Correction Sheet (2026 LABC, rev. 01/01/26), item 10
rules.quote: Submit a Haul Route application to the Building and Safety Commissioners Office. Processing time is a minimum of eight weeks.

rules.title: Los Angeles haul route filing fee (2018 form): $529 for the first 1,000 cy + $100 per added 1,000 cy, plus 22% + $10
rules.plain_english: LADBS's 2018 application form sets the Los Angeles import-export (haul route) review filing fee at $529 for the first 1,000 cubic yards plus $100 for each additional 1,000 cubic yards or part of 1,000, plus surcharges of 22% and $10. The form does not say what the 22% is charged on, and the fee was not confirmed as current for 2026, so check the amount with LADBS before relying on it.
rules.applies_to: Applicants for Los Angeles haul route (import-export) review
rules.citation: LADBS Application for Review of Import-Export (GGI-08), item 1
rules.quote: A completed “APPLICATION FOR REVIEW OF TECHNICAL REPORTS AND IMPORT-EXPORT ROUTES” form with a filing fee of $529.00 for the first 1,000 cubic yards and $100.00 additional for each 1,000 cubic yard or portion of 1,000 cubic yards, plus surcharges (22% + $10.00)
rules.notes: The form is a 2018 revision and the fee may have changed; the formula applies the 22% surcharge to the base fee, which is the plain reading but is not spelled out. Confirm the current amount with the Commission Office.
rules.correction: The $529.00 fee for the first 1,000 cy, the $100.00 for each added 1,000 cy or part of 1,000, and the '22% + $10.00' surcharges are confirmed as printed on the 2018 form. The form does not say whether the 22% applies to the base fee alone. The formula is the producer's reading, which was flagged only in notes. Added formula_is_inferred and fee_current_as_of_2026_verified = false, because no 2026 fee source was read. Rewording 2026-11-27: title and plain_english reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: Los Angeles haul route application: what to file (questionnaire, 300-ft radius map, owner labels, route map)
rules.plain_english: A Los Angeles haul route application needs the application and fee, the grading plan with cut/fill and import/export amounts, the soils/geology approval letter, a Haul Route Questionnaire (borrow/dispersal sites, every street on the route, staging area, maximum loaded truck weight), a CEQA questionnaire, a 300-foot radius map, an owner list with three sets of labels, an accuracy certificate and an 8.5x11 haul route map.

items: grading plan with cut/fill and export/import amounts
Department approval letter for soils/engineering/geology reports (if required, LAMC 91.7006.2)
property owner list and three sets of gummed labels
questionnaire_fields: staging area and max trucks staged

rules.applies_to: Applicants for Los Angeles haul route approval
rules.citation: LAMC 91.7006.7.5; LADBS Application for Review of Import-Export (GGI-08) and PC-GRAD.App22 attachments 1-4
rules.quote: A completed Haul Route Questionnaire. The questionnaire shall include the location of borrow and/or dispersal sites, all streets included in the route, the proposed staging area and th maximum gross weight of the trucks when loaded.
rules.notes: Quoted as printed ('th maximum').

rules.title: Los Angeles haul route: the 300-ft owner list must be no older than 6 months
rules.plain_english: The list of property owners within 300 feet that you file with a Los Angeles haul route application must be no more than six months old when you apply.
rules.applies_to: Applicants for Los Angeles haul route approval
rules.citation: LAMC 91.7006.7.5; LADBS PC-GRAD.App22 Attachment 4 (Information Accuracy Statement)
rules.quote: The list must be no older than six months at the time of application.

rules.title: Los Angeles haul route: no application accepted until the CEQA Notice of Determination is filed
rules.plain_english: LADBS will not accept a haul route (import-export) application, and a grading permit cannot be used, until the responsible agency has filed a CEQA Notice of Determination approving the project. The ND, MND or EIR must address the hauling and grading impacts.

parameters.prerequisite: Notice of Determination filed by the appropriate agency
parameters.ceqa_document_must_address: temporary or cumulative impacts of hauling and grading

rules.applies_to: Applicants for Los Angeles haul route approval
rules.citation: LADBS Application for Review of Import-Export (GGI-08), item 5 footnotes
rules.quote: The department shall not accept an application for “import-export” nor shall a grading permit be used until the appropriate agency has filed a “Notice of Determination” approving the project.
rules.notes: If City Planning finds the project categorically exempt, the Notice of Exemption is attached instead (Attachment 2).

rules.title: Los Angeles haul route approval: get the grading permit within 12 months and start hauling within 18 months
rules.plain_english: After the Board approves a Los Angeles haul route, you must obtain the grading permit within 12 months and begin hauling within 18 months of the approval date, or you must file a new haul route application and hearing.

parameters.clock_starts: date of Board approval
parameters.if_missed: new Haul Route application and hearing

rules.applies_to: Holders of Los Angeles haul route approvals
rules.citation: LADBS Application for Review of Import-Export (GGI-08); Grading Plan Check Correction Sheet (2026 LABC) item 11
rules.quote: The associated grading permit must be secured within 12 months from the date of Board approval and hauling must commence within 18 months from the date of Board approval. Otherwise, a new Haul Route application and hearing will be required.
rules.effective: 2018-07 (form revision); repeated on the 2026 LABC correction sheet

rules.title: Los Angeles: mail neighbor notices 10 days before issuing a permit for over 1,000 cy of hillside earthwork
rules.plain_english: For more than 1,000 cubic yards of earthwork in a Los Angeles Hillside Grading Area, notices must be mailed at least 10 days before the permit is issued.
rules.applies_to: Grading projects in Los Angeles Hillside Grading Areas
rules.citation: LAMC 91.106.4.6 (as cited); LADBS Grading Plan Check Correction Sheet (2026 LABC, rev. 01/01/26), item B.2
rules.quote: Comply with Notification requirements for over 1000 CY of earthwork in the “Hillside Grading Area”. Notices must be mailed 10 days prior to permit issuance. (106.4.6)

rules.title: Los Angeles EO 1 wildfire-rebuild projects: haul route approved ministerially (no hearing)
rules.plain_english: For projects eligible under Mayor Bass's Emergency Executive Order No. 1 (rebuilding property substantially damaged or destroyed in the January 2025 Palisades, Hurst, Kenneth, Archer and Sunset fires), the haul route is approved ministerially without a discretionary hearing. LADBS staff still add a Bureau of Street Services and LADOT clearance for transporting more than 1,000 cubic yards of earthwork and check those agencies' conditions before the permit is issued.

parameters.eligible_project: repair, restore, demolish or replace property substantially damaged or destroyed by the Wildfires; same use (no change of use, no increase in primary dwelling units); building permits within 7 years of EO 1 issuance and work completed within 3 years of permits; primary/accessory structures within 110% of prior footprint and height (plus qualifying ADUs and supportive infrastructure)

rules.applies_to: Owners, developers and contractors on Los Angeles EO 1 eligible wildfire-rebuild projects
rules.citation: Implementation Guidelines for Emergency Executive Order No. 1 (version 4.0, June 11, 2026), section III.F
rules.source: https://dbs.lacity.gov/sites/default/files/efs/pdf/publications/EO-1-Implementation-Guidelines.pdf (PDF page 14, 'F. Grading and Haul Route Permits')
rules.quote: A haul route approval for an Eligible Project shall be approved ministerially and exempt from any discretionary approval processes.
rules.notes: Staff add a PCIS clearance for 'Approval to transport earthwork quantities over 1000 cubic yards' from BOSS and LADOT and review their conditions before permit issuance.
rules.correction: The quote, the ministerial approval, the BOSS and LADOT PCIS clearance for 'Approval to transport earthwork quantities over 1000 cubic yards' and version 4.0 (June 11, 2026) are confirmed. The title and plain_english described EO 1 projects as '100% affordable housing', which is wrong. These guidelines implement the wildfire-rebuild order.
