An Eligible Project repairs, restores, demolishes or replaces property substantially damaged or destroyed by the January 2025 Palisades, Hurst, Kenneth, Archer and Sunset fires. It must keep the same use, stay within 110% of the prior footprint and height, get building permits within seven years of EO 1, and finish within three years of the permits. Corrected the title, plain_english and applies_to, and added the eligibility parameters.

rules.title: Los Angeles: projects with approved haul routes must follow BBSC, StreetsLA, LADOT and LADBS conditions
rules.plain_english: If your Los Angeles project has an approved haul route, you must follow the conditions set by the Board of Building and Safety Commissioners, StreetsLA, LADOT and LADBS. LADBS inspectors check haul routes, verify the conditions and refer violations; residents can report violations online.

parameters.enforcement: LADBS Haul Route Monitoring Program task force (LADBS, BOSS, LADOT)

rules.applies_to: Projects with approved Los Angeles haul routes and their trucking contractors
rules.citation: LADBS Good Neighbor Construction Practices (Rev. 3/2/15); LADBS Haul Route Monitoring Program page
rules.quote: In addition to the above Requirements, Projects with Approved Haul Routes shall comply with the conditions required by the Board of Building and Safety Commissioners (BBSC), Public Works, Bureau of Street Services (BOSS), Department of Transportation (DOT) and Department of Building and Safety (LADBS).
rules.notes: The LADBS PDF's text layer duplicates letters where text runs meet (e.g. 'Goodd Neighhbor'); the quote was de-duplicated by hand from the extracted text and checked against the rendered wording, so an exact string match against raw extracted text will fail. Document dated Rev. 3/2/15 and still posted by LADBS in 2026.

rules.title: Los Angeles CD-4 Bird Streets area haul route: requests accepted online Mondays 9:30 a.m.-2:30 p.m. only
rules.plain_english: For hauling in the Bird Streets Area haul route (Council District 4), LADBS accepts online requests only on Mondays between 9:30 a.m. and 2:30 p.m., and publishes a weekly schedule.

parameters.area: Bird Streets Area (bounded by Sunset Blvd, Hillcrest Dr, Crescent Dr, Rising Glen)

rules.applies_to: Haulers and contractors working in the Los Angeles Bird Streets Area
rules.citation: LADBS Haul Route Monitoring Program page (Council District 4 Bird Streets Area Haul Route)
rules.quote: Online requests are only accepted on Mondays between 9:30 AM to 2:30 PM.

rules.title: Los Angeles: provide flaggers when blocking streets for deliveries; no street closures in peak hours
rules.plain_english: When you temporarily block part of a Los Angeles street for material deliveries, provide flag persons for pedestrians and vehicles. Do not close streets during peak traffic hours, and follow the current work area traffic control manual for any street or sidewalk work.

parameters.traffic_control_standard: latest Manual on Work Area Traffic Control

rules.applies_to: Contractors in the City of Los Angeles
rules.citation: LAMC 62.46, 62.107 (as cited); LADBS Good Neighbor Construction Practices (Rev. 3/2/15), items 2-3
rules.quote: When temporarily blocking portions of streets for deliveries of construction materials, please provide flag persons to assist with pedestrian and vehicular traffic. LAMC 62.46 Street closures shall not take place during peak traffic hours. Any street, sidewalk, or other improvement work shall be in conformance with the latest Manual on Work Area Traffic Control. LAMC 62.107
rules.notes: The LADBS PDF's text layer duplicates letters where text runs meet (e.g. 'Goodd Neighhbor'); the quote was de-duplicated by hand from the extracted text and checked against the rendered wording, so an exact string match against raw extracted text will fail. Document dated Rev. 3/2/15 and still posted by LADBS in 2026. 'Peak traffic hours' are not defined on the sheet.

rules.title: Los Angeles: storing building materials in the public right-of-way needs a StreetsLA (BOSS) permit
rules.plain_english: Building materials may be stored in a Los Angeles street or sidewalk only under a permit from the Bureau of Street Services Investigation and Enforcement Division, and the storage must follow its rules.

parameters.permit_from: Department of Public Works, Bureau of Street Services, Investigation and Enforcement Division
parameters.covers: building materials stored in the public right of way

rules.applies_to: Contractors in the City of Los Angeles
rules.citation: LAMC 62.45-62.54 (as cited); LADBS Good Neighbor Construction Practices (Rev. 3/2/15), item 8
rules.quote: If building materials are to be stored in public right of way it shall be by permit from the Department of Public Works, Bureau of Street Services, Investigations and Enforcement Division and shall conform with all applicable rules. LAMC 62.45 through 62.54
rules.notes: The LADBS PDF's text layer duplicates letters where text runs meet (e.g. 'Goodd Neighhbor'); the quote was de-duplicated by hand from the extracted text and checked against the rendered wording, so an exact string match against raw extracted text will fail. Document dated Rev. 3/2/15 and still posted by LADBS in 2026. StreetsLA permit pages (streetsla.lacity.gov, bsspermits.lacity.org) could not be fetched; fees and lead times are not recorded.

rules.title: Los Angeles: keep adjacent streets and sidewalks swept; concrete supplier cleans up spills
rules.plain_english: Streets and sidewalks next to a Los Angeles construction site must be swept and free of construction debris at all times. Don't overfill concrete trucks; if concrete spills, the concrete company must clean it up immediately. Construction vehicles must obey trash-pickup parking restrictions.
rules.applies_to: Contractors and concrete suppliers in the City of Los Angeles
rules.citation: LAMC 62.45-62.54, 62.130, 80.69 (as cited); LADBS Good Neighbor Construction Practices (Rev. 3/2/15), items 4, 6, 7
rules.quote: Streets and sidewalks adjacent to construction sites shall be swept and free of construction debris at all times. LAMC 62.45 through 62.54
rules.notes: The LADBS PDF's text layer duplicates letters where text runs meet (e.g. 'Goodd Neighhbor'); the quote was de-duplicated by hand from the extracted text and checked against the rendered wording, so an exact string match against raw extracted text will fail. Document dated Rev. 3/2/15 and still posted by LADBS in 2026.

rules.title: Los Angeles: all mixed C&D waste must go to City-certified C&D processors
rules.plain_english: All mixed construction and demolition waste generated in the City of Los Angeles must be taken to City-certified C&D waste processing facilities (LA Sanitation runs the program).

parameters.authority: Citywide Construction and Demolition (C & D) Waste Recycling Ordinance, Council File 09-3029 (approved by City Council 2010-03-05)
parameters.lamc_section_unverified: LAMC 66.32 et seq. (search results only; not in any source read)

rules.applies_to: Anyone generating, hauling or disposing of mixed C&D waste in the City of Los Angeles
rules.citation: Citywide Construction and Demolition Waste Recycling Ordinance (CF 09-3029); LADBS Green Building & Sustainability page
rules.quote: that requires ALL mixed C & D waste generated within city limits be taken to City-certified C & D waste processors.
rules.notes: LASAN pages (sanitation.lacity.gov) and the LAMC text could not be read; the certified facility list and any diversion percentage are not recorded here. The 'LAMC 66.32 et seq.' reference is from LADBS green building correction sheets seen in search results.
rules.correction: The quote, CF 09-3029, the March 5, 2010 Council approval and LASAN's role are confirmed. The 'authority' parameter also named 'LAMC 66.32 et seq.', which appears on no page read here (the producer took it from search results). Removed it from authority and recorded it as unverified.

rules.title: Los Angeles: anyone hauling C&D waste needs a LASAN Private Waste Hauler Permit
rules.plain_english: In Los Angeles, every hauler and contractor that collects, hauls or transports C&D waste must first get a Private Waste Hauler Permit from LA Sanitation, and may take the waste only to City-certified C&D processing facilities. This includes contractors hauling their own debris.

parameters.required_before: collecting, hauling and transporting C&D waste
applies_to: contractors responsible for handling C&D waste

rules.applies_to: Haulers and contractors handling C&D waste in the City of Los Angeles
rules.citation: Citywide C&D Waste Recycling Ordinance (CF 09-3029); LADBS Green Building & Sustainability page
rules.quote: All haulers and contractors responsible for handling C & D waste must obtain a Private Waste Hauler Permit from LASAN prior to collecting, hauling and transporting C & D waste, and C & D waste can only be taken to City-certified C &D processing facilities.
rules.notes: The permitted hauler list (srmanagement.lacitysan.org) could not be fetched; permit fees and terms not recorded.

rules.title: Los Angeles: building permit applications must name a hauler on LASAN's Permitted Waste Haulers list
rules.plain_english: When you apply for a Los Angeles building permit you must give your construction waste hauler's name and permit number, and the hauler must be on LASAN's Permitted Waste Haulers list. Mechanical, electrical and plumbing-only permits are exempt.
rules.applies_to: Applicants for City of Los Angeles building permits
rules.citation: LADBS Contractor step-by-step page ('Construction Waste Hauler')
rules.quote: When you apply for Building permits, is required that you supply information about your Construction Waste Hauler. It must be on the Permitted Waste Haulers list . If you are applying for Mechanical, Electrical, or Plumbing permits, this information does not need to be supplied.
rules.notes: Quoted as printed.

rules.title: Los Angeles: buildings over 45 years old need neighbor notice at least 30 days before a demolition permit
rules.plain_english: For a Los Angeles building more than 45 years old, LADBS mails notice of the demolition pre-inspection application to abutting owners and occupants, the Council District office and the Neighborhood Council, and will not issue the demolition permit until at least 30 days after the notice and posting.

parameters.exception: detached garage replaced with an ADU (unless in a historic district)

rules.applies_to: Applicants for City of Los Angeles demolition permits
rules.citation: LAMC 91.106.4.5.1-91.106.4.5.2; LADBS Information Bulletin P/BC 2026-039 'Demolition of Buildings' (eff. 01-01-2026), item A.5
rules.quote: for buildings over 45 years old, as defined below, the department shall not issue a building demolition permit without first having provided the following required notice and taken the following required actions at least 30 days prior to the issuance of the demolition of building or structure permit (LAMC 91.106.4.5.1).
rules.notes: Asbestos/air district notice rules are separate (see air-district-demolition-notice-10-working-days).

rules.title: Los Angeles demolition placard: 11x17 in, within 5 ft of the front line, 4 ft up, 'NOTICE OF DEMOLITION'
rules.plain_english: For a Los Angeles demolition subject to the 45-year notice, post a durable placard at least 11 by 17 inches, within 5 feet of the front property line and at least 4 feet above ground, reading 'NOTICE OF DEMOLITION' in 3-inch letters, with the permit number and phone number in 1.5-inch letters.

parameters.colors: black letters on contrasting white or color background

rules.applies_to: Applicants for City of Los Angeles demolition permits for buildings over 45 years old
rules.citation: LAMC 91.106.4.5.1; LADBS Information Bulletin P/BC 2026-039, item A.5.c
rules.quote: The applicant shall post a placard on the property where the demolition will occur, in a conspicuous, visible place, within 5 feet of the front property line, describing the date of the application for demolition pre-inspection and meeting the following standards:

rules.title: Los Angeles: demolition permits go to C-21 or A contractors (limited owner and B exceptions)
rules.plain_english: In Los Angeles a demolition permit must be obtained by a licensed C-21 wrecking contractor or an A general engineering contractor, with an owner letter or contract. Owners may demolish small one- or two-story wood buildings themselves, and a B contractor may demolish a one-story Type II or V building it will replace.

parameters.proof: notarized owner letter or copy of signed contract
parameters.owner_exception: one- or two-story wood frame, spans <= 25 ft, owner owns building and lot
parameters.b_contractor_exception: one-story Type II or V building, B is contractor for the new building on site, plans filed

rules.applies_to: Contractors pulling City of Los Angeles demolition permits
rules.citation: LADBS Information Bulletin P/BC 2026-039 'Demolition of Buildings', item A.2
rules.quote: Demolition permits must be obtained by a licensed wrecking contractor (Class C-21) or a general engineering contractor (Class A) provided that a notarized letter from the owner or a copy of the signed contract is provided indicating that the contractor has been hired to perform the demolition.

rules.title: Los Angeles demolition: request inspection 24 hours before starting; protection devices approved first
rules.plain_english: Call for a Los Angeles demolition inspection at least 24 hours before work starts. Required protection devices must be inspected and approved before any work, and the Demolition Inspection Record card must be posted and signed for each demolition method.

parameters.field_card: LADBS B-8b Demolition Inspection Record posted on site

rules.applies_to: Contractors performing demolition in the City of Los Angeles
rules.citation: LADBS Information Bulletin P/BC 2026-039, section B
rules.quote: An inspection request must be made at least 24 hours before work is to be started.

rules.title: Los Angeles demolition: sewer cap permit first; BOE approval if demolition removes support of a public way
rules.plain_english: Before a Los Angeles demolition permit is issued for a building with a sewer line, get a sewer cap (plumbing) permit. If the demolition removes lateral support of a street or sidewalk, Bureau of Engineering approval is required first.
rules.applies_to: Applicants for City of Los Angeles demolition permits
rules.citation: LADBS Information Bulletin P/BC 2026-039, item A.8
rules.quote: Approval by the Department of Public Works, Bureau of Engineering, shall be obtained prior to the issuance of a permit for any demolition work which removes the lateral support from a public way.

rules.title: California: vehicles hauling refuse or anything for disposal/recycling must keep the load totally covered (VC 23115)
rules.plain_english: On any California highway or street, a vehicle carrying trash, rubbish or anything being hauled for disposal or recycling (including construction debris) must have the load totally covered so nothing can spill or fall out.

load_types: anything transported for disposal or recycling
parameters.cover_standard: totally covered so that no part of the load can spill or fall from the vehicle

rules.applies_to: Contractors and haulers transporting construction and demolition debris, trash or recyclables on California roads
rules.source: https://www.sandiego.gov/sites/default/files/simplified_fees_q_a_final_2023.pdf (City of San Diego ESD, Miramar Landfill Simplified Fee Schedule Q&A, created 05/09/2023, item on Uncovered Loads, quoting CVC 23115(a)); statute at leginfo.legislature.ca.gov not fetched (blocked)
rules.quote: Per CVC 23115(a) No vehicle transporting garbage, swill, used cans or bottles, wastepapers, waste cardboard, ashes, refuse, trash, or rubbish, or any noisome, nauseous, or offensive matter, or anything being transported for disposal or recycling shall be driven or moved upon any highway unless the load is totally covered in a manner that will prevent the load or any part of the load from spilling or falling from the vehicle.
rules.effective: unknown (statute text and amendment history not read)
rules.notes: The quote matches an official City of San Diego document that quotes the statute; the statute itself was not read. Penalty amounts for VC 23115 violations were not found in any readable source.

rules.title: Los Angeles LAMC 41.40: hours apply to work within 500 ft of residential buildings (UNVERIFIED)
rules.plain_english: Reported: the LAMC 41.40 hour limits (7 a.m.-9 p.m. weekdays, 8 a.m.-6 p.m. Saturdays and national holidays, none on Sundays) cover construction, grading and related job-site deliveries on or within 500 feet of land with residential buildings. Not confirmed from the code text.
rules.applies_to: Construction in the City of Los Angeles near residential uses
rules.source: LAMC 41.40 at https://codelibrary.amlegal.com/codes/los_angeles/ (blocked); restated in City Planning EIR noise sections on planning.lacity.gov (blocked), seen only as search excerpts
rules.quote: Section 41.40 limits construction within 500 feet of residential uses to the hours of 7:00 a.m. to 9:00 p.m. on weekdays and 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. on Saturdays and national holidays, and prohibits construction activity on Sundays.

rules.title: 2025 California Building Standards Code in effect Jan 1, 2026
rules.plain_english: The 2025 edition of the California Building Standards Code (Title 24) was published July 1, 2025 and took effect January 1, 2026. Permit applications submitted on or after January 1, 2026 must comply with the 2025 code; applications submitted earlier stay under the 2022 code.

parameters.exception: Part 1 (California Administrative Code) took effect earlier (reported April 2025)

rules.applies_to: All building permit applications in California (state-regulated occupancies; local amendments may add stricter rules)
rules.citation: Cal. Code Regs. Title 24; Health & Safety Code 18938.5
rules.quote: The 2025 California Building Standards Code (Cal. Code Regs., Title 24) will be published July 1, 2025, with an effective date of January 1, 2026.
rules.notes: Read only via web-search excerpts of dgs.ca.gov (BSC Bulletin 25-01, CALCode Quarterly Summer 2025); dgs.ca.gov is blocked from this environment. Errata carry a January 1, 2026 effective date (BSC IB 26-01). The 2028 next-edition date is an inference from the triennial cycle, not read from a source. Verification 2026-11-25: DGS excerpts state publication July 1, 2025, statewide effective date January 1, 2026, and that all building permit applications submitted on or after January 1, 2026 are subject to the 2025 code; Part 1 (Administrative Code) took effect April 6, 2025. The 2028 next edition remains an inference.

rules.title: Title 24 parts a project must comply with
rules.plain_english: Title 24 has 12 parts. The ones most construction projects touch are Part 2 (CBC building), Part 2.5 (CRC residential), Part 3 (CEC electrical), Part 4 (CMC mechanical), Part 5 (CPC plumbing), Part 6 (Energy Code), Part 9 (Fire Code) and Part 11 (CALGreen).

parts.2: California Building Code (CBC), Vols 1-2, based on 2024 IBC
parts.2.5: California Residential Code (CRC), based on 2024 IRC
parts.7: (no longer published / vacant in recent editions)

rules.applies_to: All construction projects requiring a building permit
rules.notes: Part names for 1, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 5, 6, 11 confirmed in search excerpts (DGS guidebook, ICC collection). Names of Parts 7-10 and 12 are from general knowledge of Title 24 structure, not read from a fetched source in this session; Part 7 status not verified. Model-code bases: CBC on 2024 IBC confirmed in excerpt; CRC/CMC/CPC model-code years not verified.

rules.title: Code edition is set by permit application date
rules.plain_english: The building standards that apply to a project are the ones in effect locally on the date the building permit application is submitted (plan-check submittal), not the date of issuance or construction.

parameters.trigger: date building permit application submitted

rules.applies_to: All permitted construction
rules.quote: (a) Only those building standards approved by the commission, and that are effective at the local level at the time an application for a building permit is submitted, shall apply to the plans and specifications for, and to the construction
rules.notes: Quote is from a 2009 Justia copy surfaced in a search excerpt; statute last amended Stats. 2025 ch. 22 sec. 40 per Counsel Stack - verify current wording. Exception: if the permit later expires (see permit-expiration rule), the new code applies to a re-application. Some building departments treat production-home plan review as the permit application (CALBO).

rules.title: Permit expiration and code lock-in: 12 months / 180 days
rules.plain_english: Under state law (H&S 18938.6, AB 2913) a building permit remains valid if work starts within 12 months after it is issued, unless the work is abandoned; the building official may grant written extensions of up to 180 days each on a written request showing justifiable cause. If work does not start within 12 months or is abandoned, the permit expires and the code edition in effect at application is lost. Locally adopted CBC/CRC Chapter 1 Section 105.5 adds a 180-day suspension/abandonment rule once work has started; check the local ordinance.

parameters.measured_from: permit issuance (18938.6) / permit date (18938.5(b)(2)(B))
parameters.extension_request: written request by permittee showing justifiable cause; building official may grant one or more extensions in writing (H&S 18938.6)
parameters.code_edition_lock_lost_if: work not commenced within 12 months or abandoned

rules.applies_to: All building permits
rules.citation: Health & Safety Code 18938.5(b)(2)(B), 18938.6 (AB 2913, Stats. 2018 ch. 655); CBC (Part 2) Chapter 1 Div. II Sec. 105.5; CRC R105.5
rules.quote: Every permit shall remain valid for purposes of this part if the work on the site authorized by that permit is commenced within 12 months after its issuance, unless the permittee has abandoned the work authorized by the permit.
rules.notes: Statute text seen only through WebSearch excerpts of the DGS "California Building Standards Law" compilation (eff. 2026-01-01) and leginfo; dgs.ca.gov and leginfo cannot be fetched directly. H&S 18938.6(b): "A permittee may request an extension of a permit. The building official may grant, in writing, one or more extensions of time for periods of not more than 180 days per extension. The permittee shall request an extension pursuant to this subdivision in writing and demonstrate justifiable cause for the extension." BSC IB 19-03: AB 2913 "amended HSC Section 18938.5 (b)(2)(B) by changing the exception relative to the permit expiration time period from 180 days to 12 months" and DGS says HSC 18938.5/18938.6 take precedence over the administrative building standards on permit expiration. When work counts as "commenced" is not defined in these excerpts; local amendments still govern suspension/abandonment after start (e.g., 180 days between approved inspections).
rules.correction: 12-month figure confirmed, but the rule misstated the structure. Under H&S 18938.6 (added by AB 2913, eff. 2019-01-01), a permit stays valid if work is commenced within 12 months after issuance unless abandoned, and the building official may grant written extensions of up to 180 days each on a written request showing justifiable cause; under 18938.5(b)(2)(B) the code-edition lock-in is lost if work does not commence within 12 months of the permit date or is abandoned. DGS states that H&S 18938.5 and 18938.6 take precedence over the administrative building standards on permit expiration, so a locally adopted CBC 105.5 cannot impose a 180-day commencement period; the 180-day figure is the CBC 105.5 suspension/abandonment-after-start period and the statutory extension length. Parameters, plain_english and citation updated; effective date 2019-01-01 confirmed.

rules.title: Permit application abandoned after 180 days
rules.plain_english: A permit application that is not pursued in good faith or issued is deemed abandoned 180 days after it was filed (building official may grant extensions). Track plan-check corrections so the application does not lapse.

parameters.extension: building official may extend for justifiable cause (local)

rules.applies_to: Permit applications where CBC/CRC Chapter 1 Div. II is locally adopted
rules.citation: CBC (Part 2) Chapter 1 Div. II Sec. 105.3.2; CRC R105.3.2
rules.quote: An application for a permit for any proposed work shall be deemed to have been abandoned 180 days after the date of filing.
rules.notes: Quote from a city handout reproducing the model code text; section number 105.3.2 is from model-code knowledge, not read. Local amendments vary.
rules.correction: 2025 CBC Section 105.3.2 text was not visible. Model IBC 2021/2024 105.3.2 text matches the quote (180 days after filing unless pursued in good faith or permit issued); IBC 2021 allows extensions of up to 90 days each, IBC 2024 up to 180 days - the 2025 CBC extension length is unconfirmed.

rules.title: Common work exempt from a building permit
rules.plain_english: A building permit is required to construct, alter, repair, move, demolish or change occupancy of a building, but the code exempts minor work such as a one-story detached shed or playhouse up to 120 sq ft, fences up to 7 ft (swimming pool barriers are not exempt), and retaining walls up to 4 ft measured from the bottom of the footing to the top of the wall, unless the wall supports a surcharge or impounds Class I, II or IIIA liquids. Exempt work still has to meet code, and electrical/plumbing/mechanical work may still need its own permit.

parameters.retaining_wall_measurement: bottom of footing to top of wall
retaining_wall_exemption_void_if: impounds Class I, II or IIIA liquids
local_variations: some cities use 6 ft fence limit
some add total-height limits for sheds (e.g., 12-16 ft)

rules.applies_to: Owners and contractors deciding whether a permit is needed
rules.quote: One-story detached accessory structures, used as tool and storage sheds, playhouses, and similar uses, provided the floor area does not exceed 120 square feet
rules.notes: Thresholds from city handouts for the 2025 CBC/CRC (search excerpts), not the official Title 24 text. Many jurisdictions amend Section 105.2 (Atascadero and Fullerton use 6 ft fences). Always confirm with the local building department. The general rule that a permit is required for construct/alter/repair/move/demolish/change occupancy is model-code text not read here. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: 120 sq ft one-story shed, 7 ft fence and 4 ft retaining wall figures confirmed for the 2025 CBC, but the exemption conditions were incomplete: the fence exemption excludes swimming pool barriers, and the retaining-wall exemption is void if the wall supports a surcharge OR impounds Class I, II or IIIA liquids. Parameters updated. CRC R105.2 2025 text not checked. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: Permit applicant must sign license (or exemption) statement
rules.plain_english: Any city or county that requires a building permit must make the applicant sign a statement giving the contractor license number and stating it is in full force, or stating the basis for any exemption. A false or missing statement carries a civil penalty of up to $500.

statement_contents: licensed under Contractors State License Law
license is in full force and effect

rules.applies_to: Every building permit applicant (contractor or owner-builder) for construction, alteration, improvement, demolition or repair
rules.source: PDF page 259-260 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: giving the number of the license and stating that it is in full force and effect, or, if the applicant is exempt from the provisions of this chapter, the basis for the alleged exemption. Any violation of this section by any applicant for a permit shall be subject to a civil penalty of not more than five hundred dollars ($500).
rules.notes: Statute text starts on PDF p. 259 ("Each county or city which requires the issuance of a permit as a condition precedent to the construction, alteration, improvement, demolition or repair of any building or structure shall also require that each applicant for such a permit file ... a statement which he has prepared and") and continues on p. 260.

rules.title: Building department verifies license at permit issuance
rules.plain_english: Building departments are asked to check on the CSLB website that the license number used to pull a permit is valid and in good standing, and that the person signing is the licensee or an authorized agent. Keep license status current and have agent authorization on file before sending staff to pull permits.

parameters.owner_builder_permits: owner-builder verification required; CSLB owner-builder flyer distributed with every owner-builder permit

rules.applies_to: Contractors and agents pulling permits; building departments
rules.quote: As a condition of permit issuance, use the CSLB Web site (www.cslb.ca.gov) to verify that the contractor’s license number being used to pull the permit is valid and in good standing.
rules.notes: Guideline (cooperative CALBO/CSLB agreement), not a statute. The guideline also says owner-builder permits need verification "in accordance with Health and Safety Code Sections 19830, 19831 and 19832"; per search excerpts those sections were repealed by AB 2335 (2008) and the owner-builder notice requirement now sits in H&S 19825 - verify.

rules.title: Cities/counties may require plan approval before construction
rules.plain_english: The contractor license law does not limit a city or county from running its own permit and inspection system or from requiring plans and specifications to be submitted and approved before construction starts. Local building departments can also refer code-violating licensees to CSLB.

parameters.plan_approval_before_construction: may be required by local agency

rules.applies_to: All contractors working under local permits
rules.source: PDF page 260 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Nothing in this chapter shall limit the power of a city or county to adopt any system of permits requiring submission to and approval by the city or county of plans and specifications for an installation prior to the commencement of construction of the installation.

rules.title: Local business tax compliance may be required before permit
rules.plain_english: A city or county may require a contractor to prove it is current on local business tax before issuing any permit, and may deny the permit if it is not. Store each jurisdiction's business tax certificate with the permit packet.

parameters.document: local business tax certificate / proof of compliance
parameters.tax_cap: may not exceed license tax/fee authorized by Gov Code 37101 or B&P 16000

rules.applies_to: Licensed contractors applying for city/county permits
rules.source: PDF page 225 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Nothing in this code shall be interpreted to prohibit cities, counties, and cities and counties from requiring contractors to show proof that they are in compliance with local business tax requirements of the entity prior to issuing any city, county, or city and county permit.

rules.title: $1,000 minor-work exemption is lost if a permit is required
rules.plain_english: The license exemption for jobs under $1,000 (labor, materials and all other items) applies only if the work does not require a building permit. Any job needing a permit requires a licensed contractor, regardless of price, and jobs cannot be split into pieces under $1,000 to evade the law.
rules.applies_to: Handyman-scale work; any person bidding small jobs
rules.source: PDF page 268 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (a) This chapter does not apply to a work or operation on one undertaking or project by one or more contracts if the aggregate contract price for labor, materials, and all other items is less than one thousand dollars ($1,000), that work or operation being considered of casual, minor, or inconsequential nature, and the work or operation does not require a building permit.
rules.notes: CSLB owner-builder pamphlet (13P-060/1025) adds: "Note: Any project needing a permit or workers requires a licensed contractor."

rules.title: Work without a permit is presumed a willful violation
rules.plain_english: CSLB must discipline a license for willful and deliberate violation of state or local building-permit laws, and construction done without a permit is presumed willful. The only carve-out is equipment repair/maintenance/adjustment under $500 in labor or materials, or replacing a mechanical part with an identical part.

parameters.presumption: construction without permit = willful and deliberate (rebuttable)

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees
rules.source: PDF page 334 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: For the purpose of this section, there shall be a rebuttable presumption affecting the burden of proof that construction performed without a permit is a willful and deliberate violation.
rules.notes: Same page: discipline applies where the licensee "has willfully and deliberately violated any state or local law relating to the issuance of building permits, other than failure to obtain a county or city permit for repair, maintenance, and adjustment of equipment where such repair, maintenance, or adjustment is valued at less than five hundred dollars ($500) for labor or materials".

rules.title: Violating building or permit laws is cause for discipline
rules.plain_english: Willfully disregarding state or local building laws, including permit-issuance laws and the 811 dig law, is grounds for CSLB disciplinary action.

causes: building laws of state or political subdivision
any state or local law relating to issuance of building permits (7110(h))
Gov Code 4216 et seq. excavation notification (7110(f))

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees
rules.source: PDF page 351 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Willful or deliberate disregard and violation of the building laws of the state, or of any political subdivision thereof, or of any of the following references to or provisions of law, constitutes a cause for disciplinary action against a licensee:
rules.notes: Subdivision (h) reads "(h) Any state or local law relating to the issuance of building permits." Amended by AB 1747 (Stats 2022 ch 757) effective Jan 1, 2023.

rules.title: Penalty range for failing to obtain permits
rules.plain_english: CSLB's disciplinary guidelines for failure to obtain building permits range from a stayed 60-day suspension with 1 year of probation up to license revocation, and probation may require submitting copies of building permits to the Registrar on demand.

possible_terms: actual suspension of 5 days or more
submit copies of building permits on demand during probation
retake trade exam if not taken within past 5 years

rules.title: Home improvement contract should identify permits and who pays
rules.plain_english: CSLB lists failure to identify the required building permits, or who is paying for them, as a common home improvement contract problem. Contract templates should list each required permit and state whether the contractor or owner obtains and pays for it.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts (residential, including ADUs)
rules.citation: CSLB Law Book Section II guidance (Common Problems with Home Improvement Contracts)
rules.source: PDF page 36 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Failure to identify required building permits or indicate who is paying for them
rules.notes: CSLB guidance, not a specific statutory clause. CSLB ADU Fast Facts also warns owners to confirm permit costs with the building department before paying a contractor for "plans" or "permits".

rules.title: Loan-contingent HIC: only permit work before loan is final
rules.plain_english: When a home improvement contract depends on a loan that the contractor arranges or refers, the contractor may not deliver materials or do any work, other than getting building permits and similar non-lienable preliminary services, until the loan is approved, accepted and past its rescission period. Violating this makes the contract unenforceable.

allowed_before_loan_final: similar services preliminary to commencement for which no mechanics lien can be claimed
conditions: third party agrees to make loan
buyer accepts loan
TILA/Reg Z rescission period expires without rescission
parameters.consequence: contract unenforceable; contractor must return all money/property

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors whose contract is loan-contingent or who arrange/refer financing
rules.source: PDF page 424 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (1) Deliver any property or perform any services other than obtaining building permits or other similar services preliminary to the commencement of the home improvement for which no mechanic’s lien can be claimed.
rules.notes: Subdivision (b): "Until the requirements of paragraphs (1), (2), and (3) of subdivision (a) are satisfied, it shall be unlawful for the contractor to do any of the following:"

rules.title: Workers' comp declaration required on every permit
rules.plain_english: Before a city or county issues a permit for construction, alteration, improvement, demolition or repair, the applicant must sign, under penalty of perjury, a workers' compensation declaration: a certificate of consent to self-insure, or the insurance carrier and policy number, or a statement that no employees will be used. A permit cannot be issued without it.

options: certificate of consent to self-insure (Labor Code 3700)
carrier name + policy number (+ expiration)
exemption: no employees subject to WC

rules.applies_to: All building permit applicants
rules.notes: Content from search excerpts of code-mirror sites and city permit forms; leginfo blocked. AB 2335 (2008, eff. 1/1/2009) rewrote 19825 and folded the former owner-builder notice (old 19830-19832) into it. Lawbook only cross-references "Health and Safety Code Section 19825, Declaration of Worker’s Compensation Required on Building Permits" (appendix removed in 2026 edition).

rules.title: Owner-builder permit responsibilities and limits
rules.plain_english: An owner who signs the permit as owner-builder takes full responsibility for the project: pulling permits, requesting inspections, correcting failed work, paying workers and suppliers, and possibly acting as an employer. Home-improvement owner-builders must have lived in the home 12 months before completion and can use the exemption on no more than two structures in three years; new single-family owner-builders may sell no more than four structures per year unless a B contractor does the work.

parameters.sales_limit_waived_if: owner contracts with General Building (B) contractor
responsibilities: ensure workers and suppliers are paid

rules.applies_to: Property owners pulling owner-builder permits; contractors asked to work "under the owner's permit"
rules.quote: When you sign a building permit application as an owner-builder, you assume full responsibility for all phases of your project and its integrity. You may be considered an employer if you hire unlicensed contractors to do the work.
rules.notes: Owner-builder licensing exemption itself (B&P 7044) is in the lawbook PDF pp. 264-265; covered in more depth by licensing research. Pamphlet: consultants who bid or supervise hiring subcontractors must be licensed.

rules.title: Smoke and CO alarms required when residential permit work exceeds $1,000
rules.plain_english: When a permit is issued for an addition, alteration or repair to a dwelling and the work is valued over $1,000, smoke alarms and carbon monoxide alarms must be installed in the existing dwelling before final. Hard-wiring/interconnection is generally required only where finishes are removed.

devices: carbon monoxide alarms (if fuel-burning appliance or attached garage)

rules.title: Replace noncompliant plumbing fixtures on pre-1994 buildings
rules.plain_english: For buildings built on or before January 1, 1994, a permit for an addition, alteration or improvement triggers replacement of noncompliant (high-flow) plumbing fixtures with water-conserving fixtures before final approval. Single-family: all noncompliant fixtures in the house. Multifamily/commercial: fixtures in the altered area if permit valuation exceeds $150,000, and all fixtures in any altered room.

parameters.multifamily_commercial_scope: fixtures serving altered area; all fixtures in any altered room
parameters.timing: before final permit approval or certificate of occupancy

rules.applies_to: Permitted additions/alterations to residential and commercial buildings built on or before Jan 1, 1994
rules.quote: the permit applicant shall replace all noncompliant plumbing fixtures with water-conserving plumbing fixtures
rules.notes: From search excerpts of city summaries and code-mirror pages. Effective date 2014-01-01 for the permit trigger is from general knowledge of SB 407, not verified. Noncompliant fixture thresholds (toilets >1.6 gpf, urinals >1.0 gpf, showerheads >2.5 gpm, faucets >2.2 gpm) are from general knowledge and omitted from parameters.
rules.correction: Pre-1994 scope, single-family "replace all noncompliant plumbing fixtures" as a condition of final permit approval, and the multifamily/commercial $150,000 estimated-construction-cost trigger (fixtures serving the specific area of the improvement) matched leginfo bill text, but only in bill texts proposing amendments; the current codified wording, the 2014 operative date and the "all fixtures in any altered room" rule were not seen.

rules.title: New/remodeled residential pool: 2 of 7 drowning-prevention features
rules.plain_english: When a building permit is issued for a new pool or spa, or remodel of an existing one, at a private single-family home, it must have at least two of the seven listed drowning-prevention safety features, which the building official checks at final inspection.

example_features: enclosure per H&S 115923 isolating pool from home
removable mesh fencing with self-closing/latching gate
exit alarms on home doors to pool
self-closing, self-latching device on doors to pool
not_counted: exit alarm + self-closing latch on the same door counted as two

rules.applies_to: Pool/spa contractors and owners (private single-family homes)
rules.citation: Health & Safety Code 115922 (Swimming Pool Safety Act, 115920-115929)
rules.quote: spa at a private single-family home, the respective swimming pool or spa shall be equipped with at least two of the following seven drowning prevention safety features
rules.notes: From search excerpts only; full feature wording not read. Lawbook cross-references H&S 115920-115925 (appendix removed) and B&P 7195 requires home inspectors to report which of the 7 features exist (PDF p. 445).
rules.correction: None. Core rule (2 of 7, single-family, building permit trigger, 2018) confirmed. NOT confirmed: the "not_counted" combinations come from SB 552 (2023-24), whose enactment was not shown; AB 1237 (2025-26) would extend coverage to condominium units and its status is unknown.

rules.title: Required inspection sequence; do not cover work before approval
rules.plain_english: The permit holder must call for each required inspection and keep work exposed until it is approved. Typical residential sequence: foundation/footing (after excavation and rebar, before concrete), under-floor/slab, rough plumbing-mechanical-electrical, frame, lath/gypsum board, weather-exposed waterproofing, any special inspections, and final.
rules.applies_to: All permitted residential (CRC) and building (CBC) projects
rules.notes: Third-party code summaries only; official 2025 CRC text not read. Exact California sub-numbering (e.g., R109.1.4 frame, R109.1.6 final per a San Jose handbook) and the order of rough-ins vs. frame vary by jurisdiction. Energy (HERS) and CALGreen verifications are also needed before final.

rules.title: Statement of special inspections required for permit
rules.plain_english: Where special inspections are required (e.g., structural concrete, steel, masonry, high-strength bolting, deep foundations), the applicant must submit a statement of special inspections, prepared by the registered design professional, as a condition of permit issuance. The 2025 CBC removed the exception allowing a non-licensed person to prepare it.

parameters.prepared_by: registered design professional in responsible charge

rules.applies_to: Projects designed under the CBC requiring special inspections (most commercial/multifamily structural work)
rules.quote: The applicant shall submit a statement of special inspections in accordance with Section 107.1 as a condition for permit issuance. This statement shall be in accordance with Section 1704.3.
rules.notes: Quote from a third-party CBC summary. DGS 2025 change summary says the state does not permit the exception allowing non-licensed individuals to prepare the statement - confirm whether that applies to Chapter 17 (local) or only 17A (DSA/state agencies). "Owner hires special inspector" from model-code knowledge (CBC 1704.2), not read.

rules.title: Special inspection reports and final report before occupancy
rules.plain_english: Special inspectors/approved agencies keep records and send interim reports to the building official and the registered design professional; discrepancies must be reported and corrected. A final report documenting required special inspections and correction of discrepancies must be submitted before the certificate of occupancy (or final) is issued.

interim_reports_to: registered design professional in responsible charge
parameters.final_report_timing: before certificate of occupancy / final approval (or as agreed before work starts)
final_report_contents: documentation of required special inspections and tests

rules.applies_to: Projects with special inspections
rules.notes: From local agency forms and summaries; one summary says final report timing is agreed upon before work starts by the owner or owner's agent. Not read from official code text.

rules.title: Building department must inspect within 10 business days of a completion notice (AB 1308)
rules.plain_english: For a project covered by H&S 17970.3 (AB 1308), the city or county building department must inspect the permitted work within 10 business days after it receives notice that the permitted work is complete. The statute says an inspection of the permitted work, not specifically the final inspection. Missing the deadline is a Housing Accountability Act violation. Summaries say the law covers only buildings of up to 10 units and lets the builder use a qualified third-party inspector; neither point was confirmed in the statute text.

parameters.trigger: notice of completion / inspection request for final
remedy_if_missed: builder may retain qualified third-party inspector

rules.applies_to: Builders of housing projects covered by H&S 17970.3 (the 10-unit limit given in summaries is not confirmed)
rules.quote: Within 10 business days of receiving a notice of the completion of the permitted work authorized by a building permit issued for a project subject to this section, the building department of every city or county shall conduct an inspection of the permitted work.
rules.notes: From law-firm and CALBO summaries; statute text not read. Some summaries limit scope to 100-percent residential buildings and mention a 40-ft height limit; confirm scope, height and whether it covers only final or all inspections. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: Deadline confirmed: within 10 business days of receiving notice of completion of permitted work, the building department shall inspect; failure is a disapproval/violation under the Housing Accountability Act. The verbatim_quote was a law-firm paraphrase and was replaced with the statute text. NOT confirmed: the 10-unit scope limit and the third-party-inspector remedy (not in the excerpts); the statute says "an inspection of the permitted work", not only a final inspection. Rewording 2026-11-27: title, plain_english and applies_to reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: Private plan check option when city review is slow (AB 253)
rules.plain_english: Under the California Residential Private Permitting Review Act (AB 253), once a residential permit application is complete the city or county must give an estimated review timeframe. If that estimate exceeds 30 business days, or the agency has not determined compliance within 30 days, the applicant may hire a private professional provider (licensed engineer or architect with a residential plans examiner certification). The agency then has 10 business days to review the provider's report and either issue the permit or give written notice of noncompliance; if it does neither, the plans are deemed compliant. In effect until January 1, 2036.

parameters.provider_qualification: licensed professional engineer or architect with current residential plans examiner certification (e.g., ICC)
parameters.scope: residential projects (unit/height limits per summaries - not confirmed)

rules.applies_to: Residential permit applicants (any unit or height limits are not confirmed)
rules.notes: Summaries say AB 253 was an urgency measure effective immediately on signature (Oct 10, 2025). Whether "30 days" is calendar or business days, the code section number, and the unit/height limits were not verified against bill text. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: Citation was generic: AB 253 adds H&S 17960.3 and amends 17951 and 17960.1. Trigger is broader and the 30-day figure is mixed: the applicant may use a private professional provider if the agency's estimated compliance timeframe exceeds 30 business days or if no determination is made within 30 days of the application being deemed complete. After receiving the provider's report the agency has 10 business days to issue the permit or give written notice of noncompliance; if it does neither, the plans are deemed compliant. Provider = licensed engineer or architect with a current residential plans examiner certification (e.g., ICC). Operative until January 1, 2036. Unit/height scope not confirmed. Rewording 2026-11-27: applies_to reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: Post-entitlement housing permit review deadlines (AB 2234)
rules.plain_english: For housing development projects, a local agency must decide whether a post-entitlement permit application (building, demolition, grading, minor off-site improvements) is complete and give written notice within 15 business days, then approve it or return a full set of comments within 30 business days of completeness (25 units or fewer) or 60 business days (26 or more units). Appeal decisions are due within 60/90 business days under existing law; AB 1621 (2026) shortens these to 30/45 business days.

parameters.tolling: while another public agency must review; notice to applicant within 3 business days

rules.applies_to: Housing development projects with entitlements
rules.quote: A local agency or state agency shall determine whether an application for a postentitlement phase permit is complete and provide written notice of this determination to the applicant not later than 15 business days after the local agency or state agency received the application.
rules.notes: Approval-deadline numbers and the 25-unit split were NOT confirmed in any source read; included only as a flagged lead. Do not compute deadlines from this rule without reading Gov Code 65913.3. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: Completeness determination is 15 BUSINESS days after receipt (written notice). Approval deadlines are now confirmed: 30 business days after the application is deemed complete for projects of 25 units or fewer, 60 business days for 26 or more units (full set of comments or approved permit). Added appeal deadlines: final written appeal determination within 60/90 business days under existing law, which AB 1621 (approved 2026-09-29) cuts to 30/45 business days (assumed operative 2027-01-01 - not confirmed). Timelines are tolled while another agency reviews (notice within 3 business days). AB 1114 scope claim not checked.

rules.title: 2025 Energy Code enforced from Jan 1, 2026
rules.plain_english: The 2025 Building Energy Efficiency Standards (Title 24 Part 6) apply to permit applications submitted on or after January 1, 2026; compliance forms carry the 2025 version and must match the code year of the permit application.
rules.applies_to: All newly constructed buildings, additions and alterations within Part 6 scope
rules.quote: Statewide enforcement of the 2025 Energy Code begins January 1, 2026.
rules.notes: energy.ca.gov blocked; quote from search excerpt. Energy Commission does not enforce directly; local building departments (AHJ) do. Verification 2026-11-25: CEC pages also require approved 2025 compliance software for permit applications on or after 2026-01-01; CEC software transition dates for later CBECC versions conflict between pages (2026-01-07 vs 2026-12-18) - check the software page.

rules.title: CF1R Certificate of Compliance at plan check (registered when HERS required)
rules.plain_english: The energy compliance documentation submitted with plans is the Certificate of Compliance (CF1R residential; NRCC nonresidential). For low-rise/single-family residential work that requires HERS field verification, the CF1R given to the building department must be a copy registered with an approved HERS data registry.

parameters.must_be_registered_if: HERS field verification or diagnostic testing required

rules.applies_to: Residential and nonresidential projects within Energy Code scope (new, additions, many alterations incl. HVAC changeouts)
rules.citation: Title 24 Part 6 Sec. 10-103(a)(1); Reference Joint Appendix JA7; CEC-400-2025-004 Data Registry Requirements Manual
rules.notes: Section 10-103 numbering from general knowledge. Search excerpt: the CF1R sent to the enforcement agency must be a copy registered with an approved HERS data registry for buildings needing field verification. 2025 forms reference an "ECC Registry" (HERS program renamed Energy Code Compliance) - naming not fully verified.

rules.title: CF2R Certificate of Installation by installer
rules.plain_english: The installing contractor completes and signs a Certificate of Installation (CF2R residential; NRCI nonresidential) for each energy feature installed. When HERS verification is required, the CF2R data must be submitted electronically to the same approved data registry, and the signed CF2R must be available at the job site for the building inspector.
rules.applies_to: Installing contractors (HVAC, insulation, windows, water heating, lighting, solar) on permitted work
rules.notes: From energycodeace (CEC-sponsored but third-party) excerpts; section number and job-site availability from general knowledge, not read.

rules.title: CF3R Certificate of Verification by HERS rater before final
rules.plain_english: Where the CF1R calls for field verification (e.g., duct leakage, fan efficacy, airflow, refrigerant charge, ventilation/IAQ, quality insulation), an independent certified HERS rater tests the installation and uploads a CF3R Certificate of Verification to the same registry used for the CF1R and CF2R. The building department should not final the permit until registered CF3Rs are received.
rules.applies_to: Residential new construction, additions and alterations with HERS-verified measures
rules.citation: Title 24 Part 6 Sec. 10-103(a)(5); Reference Residential Appendix RA2/RA3
rules.notes: "Not final until CF3R received" is standard enforcement practice from general knowledge; not read in official text this session.

rules.title: Solar PV required on new single-family homes
rules.plain_english: All newly constructed single-family residential buildings must have a solar PV system sized per Equation 150.1-C (five exceptions apply). If a battery energy storage system is installed with it, the required PV size may be reduced by 25 percent.
rules.applies_to: Builders of new single-family homes (including detached ADUs - check exceptions)
rules.quote: If installed in conjunction with a battery energy storage system (BESS), the solar PV size per Equation 150.1-C may be reduced by 25 percent.
rules.notes: CEC summary documents read only via search excerpt. The five exceptions (e.g., limited solar access, small roof area) not read. CEC FAQ addresses PV for newly constructed detached ADUs; not verified. Verification 2026-11-25: CEC says the 25% reduction applies only if the BESS meets JA12 with a minimum 7.5 kWh cycling capacity.
rules.correction: None. Caveat added to notes: the CEC page conditions the 25% reduction on a JA12-compliant battery (minimum 7.5 kWh cycling capacity). The count of five exceptions was not checked.

rules.title: Heat pumps are the 2025 prescriptive baseline for homes
rules.plain_english: The 2025 Energy Code uses heat pumps for both space heating and water heating as the prescriptive baseline for new single-family homes. Gas equipment is still allowed through the performance path but must make up the difference, and gas appliances trigger electric-ready requirements.

parameters.electric_ready_triggered_by: installation of certain natural gas/propane appliances

rules.applies_to: New single-family residential construction
rules.quote: For homes, use heat pumps for both space heating and water heating, expanding on the single heat pump baselines in the 2022 update.
rules.notes: Gas tankless water heaters removed from prescriptive options for single-family additions (150.2(a)1D) per search excerpt.

rules.title: Battery-storage-ready for new homes with >125 A service
rules.plain_english: Newly constructed one- or two-family dwellings with electrical service over 125 amps must be battery energy storage system (BESS) ready unless a battery is actually installed. Solar-ready rules apply to new single-family homes in subdivisions of 10 or more units.
rules.applies_to: New single-family one- and two-dwelling units
rules.notes: Section number 150.0(s) from general knowledge; requirement wording from CEC summary excerpts only.
rules.correction: None. 125 A trigger, 150.0(s) cite and BESS-installed waiver confirmed. NOT checked: solar-ready 10-unit subdivision figure (110.10(a)1).

rules.title: HVAC replacement triggers permit + HERS verification
rules.plain_english: Replacing or adding a residential space-conditioning system or ducts is an Energy Code alteration that needs a permit, CF1R/CF2R, and HERS-verified tests (e.g., duct leakage and refrigerant charge/airflow) depending on scope. Small duct additions below a length threshold may be exempt from duct testing.

triggers: entirely new or replacement space-conditioning system
parameters.duct_length_threshold_ft: unverified (2025 CF1R-ALT asks about >25 ft of ducts; 2019 form used 40 ft)
parameters.altered_duct_system_definition: <75% of duct system new/replaced (2022 code fact sheet)

rules.applies_to: HVAC (C-20) contractors doing residential changeouts and duct work
rules.notes: Only 2022-code and form excerpts seen; 2025 thresholds and leakage limits NOT verified. Do not compute pass/fail leakage percentages from this rule.

rules.title: Divert at least 65% of construction/demolition waste
rules.plain_english: New construction (and covered additions/alterations) must recycle and/or salvage for reuse at least 65 percent of nonhazardous construction and demolition waste, or meet a stricter local ordinance, and document it (waste management plan / hauler or facility receipts).
rules.applies_to: Residential (4.408.1) and nonresidential (5.408.1) new construction; covered additions/alterations
rules.quote: Recycle and/or salvage for reuse a minimum of 65 percent of the nonhazardous construction and demolition
rules.notes: Quote from a city 2025 CALGreen checklist; official Part 11 text not read. Excavated soil and land-clearing debris are typically excluded (general knowledge). Many cities require a deposit or a C&D plan before permit issuance.
rules.correction: None. Residential 4.408.1 wording and compliance paths (local ordinance, waste management plan, waste management company, waste stream reduction alternative) confirmed for 2025. Nonresidential 5.408.1 2025 text not seen directly (CalRecycle says the 65% applies).

rules.title: CALGreen low-disposal alternative (lbs per sq ft)
rules.plain_english: Instead of documenting 65% diversion, a project can show that the total weight of construction and demolition waste it sends to landfill is at or below a per-square-foot cap: 3.4 lbs/sq ft of building area for low-rise residential, and 2 lbs/sq ft for high-rise residential and nonresidential projects.

parameters.measured_as: total combined weight of C&D waste disposed of in landfills per sq ft of building area

rules.applies_to: CALGreen-covered projects choosing the disposal-rate path
rules.citation: CALGreen (Title 24 Part 11) 4.408.4, 4.408.4.1 (residential); 5.408 waste stream reduction alternative (nonresidential, numbering unverified)
rules.notes: Figures come from city documents based on 2019/2022 CALGreen; not confirmed for the 2025 edition. Verify before use. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: 3.4 lb/sq ft and 2 lb/sq ft figures confirmed for the 2025 residential measures, but the split was wrong: 3.4 lb/sq ft applies to low-rise residential; 2 lb/sq ft applies to high-rise residential and nonresidential (per CalRecycle). Parameters and plain_english updated; exact 2025 5.408 nonresidential wording not seen.

rules.title: Nonresidential additions >=1,000 sq ft or alterations >=$200,000
rules.plain_english: For nonresidential buildings, CALGreen mandatory measures apply to additions of 1,000 sq ft or more and to alterations with a permit valuation of $200,000 or more. The construction waste diversion requirement (65%) is broader: it applies to any nonresidential addition or alteration that requires a permit.

parameters.waste_diversion_5_408_applies_to: all nonresidential additions and alterations requiring a permit (301.3.2)

rules.applies_to: Nonresidential additions and alterations
rules.quote: additions to non-residential buildings or structures of at least 1,000 square feet or alterations with an estimated construction cost of at least $200,000 shall divert from landfills at least 65 percent
rules.notes: Source is based on the 2019 code; thresholds not verified for the 2025 edition. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: The 1,000 sq ft addition / $200,000 alteration-valuation thresholds (Sec. 301.3) are confirmed through the 2025 edition for nonresidential mandatory measures generally, but they do NOT limit waste diversion: CalRecycle and BSC text say the 5.408 65% diversion applies to nonresidential additions and alterations whenever a permit is required (301.3.2). The Vacaville quote reflects the 2013 code. Plain_english and parameters updated; exact 2025 301.3 wording not seen.

rules.title: EV-capable raceway/panel space in new one- and two-family homes
rules.plain_english: New one- and two-family dwellings and townhouses with attached private garages must provide EV infrastructure: a listed raceway for a dedicated 208/240-volt branch circuit and panel capacity and reserved space for a 40-amp 208/240-volt circuit, labeled "EV CAPABLE". The raceway is not needed if a 40-amp circuit is actually installed.

parameters.label: EV CAPABLE
parameters.raceway_waived_if: minimum 40 A 208/240 V dedicated branch circuit installed

rules.applies_to: New one- and two-family dwellings and townhouses with attached private garages
rules.quote: The service panel/subpanel must provide capacity and reserved space to install a 40-ampere 208/240-volt branch circuit.
rules.notes: Secondary summaries; 2025 wording not confirmed. Local reach codes often require EV Ready (installed circuits) instead. Multifamily/nonresidential EV percentages not researched.
rules.correction: None. Raceway for dedicated 208/240 V circuit, panel capacity/reserved space for 40 A, EV CAPABLE labeling and installed-circuit exception confirmed for 2025. The 1-inch trade-size raceway minimum was seen only in the 2022 version.

rules.title: ADU construction is a home improvement contract (down payment max $1,000 or 10%, whichever is less)
rules.plain_english: Building an ADU is a home improvement project under the Contractors State License Law: a written home improvement contract is required, the down payment cannot exceed $1,000 or 10 percent of the contract amount, whichever is less, and progress payments must not get ahead of work completed or materials delivered. The buyer may cancel within 3 business days (5 business days if 65 or older; 7 business days for contracts to repair or restore homes damaged in a declared disaster).

parameters.down_payment_rule: lesser of $1,000 or 10% of contract amount (B&P 7159.5(a)(3))
parameters.disaster_period_applies_to: contracts to repair or restore residential premises damaged by a sudden or catastrophic event with a declared state or local emergency

rules.applies_to: Contractors building ADUs for homeowners
rules.quote: Building an ADU is considered a home improvement project under the Contractors State License Law.
rules.notes: Same page: "A written Home Improvement Contract is required for the construction of an ADU." and "The down payment cannot exceed $1,000." Detailed HIC rules are in the lien/payment and contracts research. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: CSLB Fast Facts quote confirmed, but the statute caps the down payment at $1,000 OR 10% of the contract amount, whichever is less (B&P 7159.5(a)(3)), not a flat $1,000; cancellation periods are business days (3, or 5 for a buyer 65+), and the 7-business-day period applies only to contracts to repair/restore residential premises damaged by a declared state or local emergency, not to all work "in disaster zones". Parameters, plain_english and citation updated. Rewording 2026-11-27: title reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: Who can build an ADU: B general building (or C-47 for manufactured)
rules.plain_english: A B General Building contractor can build or install an ADU and subcontract specialty trades. A C-47 General Manufactured Housing contractor can install an ADU only if it is a manufactured home built off site. Other C-specialty contractors generally cannot manage a full ADU build but can be subcontracted for their trade.
rules.applies_to: ADU projects
rules.quote: C-47 General Manufactured Housing Contractors can install an ADU if it is a manufactured home that is constructed off site and transported to the installation location.

rules.title: ADU permits come from city/county (HCD for manufactured)
rules.plain_english: ADU permits are obtained from the local city or county building department; for a manufactured-home ADU, permits may come from the California Department of Housing and Community Development (HCD). Owners should confirm permit costs directly with the building department before paying a contractor for permits.
rules.applies_to: ADU projects
rules.quote: Permits must be obtained through your local city or county. If the ADU is a manufactured home, permits may come from the California Department of Housing and Community Development.

rules.title: CSLB sample ADU progress payment schedule
rules.plain_english: CSLB publishes a sample ADU progress payment schedule tied to construction milestones (totals 100%). A contract generator can use it as a default, adjusted so payments never exceed work completed.
rules.applies_to: ADU home improvement contracts
rules.quote: 5% Mobilization 10% Demolition, Site Prep 10% Foundation 15% Framing 15% Rough MEP 15% Roof, Exterior Wrap 10% Insulation, Drywall 10% Flooring, Tile, Cabinets 5% Finish MEP and Finish Carpentry 3% Final Inspection 2% Rendering of Keys (Upon completion of punch list)
rules.notes: Sample only ("might be used"); the $1,000 down payment cap still governs the first payment. 5% mobilization on a large contract can exceed $1,000 - generator must cap the deposit at $1,000.

rules.title: ADU permit: act within 60 days or it is deemed approved
rules.plain_english: A local agency must approve or deny a complete ADU/JADU permit application ministerially within 60 days; if it does not, the application is deemed approved. The clock can be tolled at the applicant's request, and is tied to a pending single-family permit if submitted together.

parameters.trigger: receipt of complete application
parameters.tolling: at applicant request; or delayed to act on accompanying new primary dwelling permit

rules.applies_to: ADU and JADU permit applicants
rules.quote: If the local agency has not approved or denied the completed application within 60 days, the application shall be deemed approved.
rules.notes: Statute text seen only via code-mirror search excerpt (marked updated Jan 1, 2026). Gov Code 65852.2 was recodified to 66310-66342 by SB 477 (2024). Denial must include a full set of comments (general knowledge, not verified).
rules.correction: None. Not confirmed: the coastal-zone parallel rule (Gov Code 66329 page appeared in results, AB 462 status unknown).

rules.title: ADU completeness review within 15 business days (SB 543)
rules.plain_english: Beginning January 1, 2026, the permitting agency must determine whether an ADU/JADU application is complete and give the applicant written notice within 15 business days of receiving it; if it misses that deadline, the application is deemed complete. Agencies must also offer an appeal and issue a final written determination within 60 business days of a written appeal.

parameters.notice_form: written notice with list of incomplete items

rules.applies_to: ADU and JADU permit applicants
rules.citation: Gov Code 66317 as amended by SB 543 (Stats. 2025 ch. 520)
rules.quote: A permitting agency shall determine whether an application to create or serve an accessory dwelling unit is complete and provide written notice of this determination to the applicant not later than 15 business days after the permitting agency received the application.
rules.notes: From LA County memo and law-firm summaries; bill text not read. Consequence of missing the 15-day deadline not confirmed. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: 15-business-day completeness determination confirmed. Unconfirmed consequence now resolved: if the agency does not make a timely determination, the application (or resubmitted application) is deemed complete. Appeal decision is 60 BUSINESS days after the written appeal (not 60 days). Parameters updated; exact subdivision not confirmed.

rules.title: ADU size cities must allow (850 / 1,000 sq ft; 800 sq ft guaranteed)
rules.plain_english: A local ADU ordinance cannot set a maximum size below 850 sq ft (1,000 sq ft if more than one bedroom), and cannot use lot coverage, FAR, open space or minimum lot size to block an ADU of at least 800 sq ft with 4-ft side and rear setbacks. Since 2026, ADU square footage is measured as interior livable space.
rules.applies_to: ADU design/permitting on residential lots
rules.notes: Summaries only; pin cites vary across sources. Verify section numbers after SB 543 renumbering.

rules.title: Default ADU size caps: 1,200 sq ft detached; attached 50% of house
rules.plain_english: Absent a local ordinance, a new detached ADU may be up to 1,200 sq ft. An attached ADU may be limited to 50% of the primary dwelling's floor area (but not below the 850/1,000 sq ft floors). Conversions of existing space have no fixed cap.
rules.applies_to: ADU design
rules.notes: Law-firm FAQ excerpt only; verify against statute.
rules.correction: None. Caveat: whether SB 543 (2025) changed "total floor area" to interior livable space in 66314 was not checked.

rules.title: ADU height and setbacks cities must allow
rules.plain_english: Cities must allow detached ADUs at least 16 ft tall, 18 ft within one-half mile walking distance of a major transit stop or high-quality transit corridor or on a lot with a multistory multifamily building, and attached ADUs up to 25 ft (or the primary dwelling's height limit if lower). They cannot require side or rear setbacks over 4 ft for new-construction ADUs; conversions of existing structures need no additional setback.

parameters.detached_near_transit_condition: within one-half mile walking distance of a major transit stop or high-quality transit corridor
parameters.attached_height_ft: 25 ft or primary-dwelling zoning height limit, whichever is lower

rules.applies_to: ADU design
rules.notes: HCD guidance via search excerpt only. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: 16 ft minimum and 4 ft side/rear setback confirmed. The "unverified" higher heights are now confirmed and filled in: 18 ft for a detached ADU within one-half mile walking distance of a major transit stop or high-quality transit corridor; 18 ft for a detached ADU on a lot with an existing or proposed multifamily, multistory dwelling; 25 ft or the primary-dwelling height limit, whichever is lower, for an attached ADU. (Any added roof-pitch allowance was not seen.). Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: No impact fees on ADUs <=750 sq ft or JADUs <=500 sq ft
rules.plain_english: Local agencies, special districts and water corporations may not charge impact fees on an ADU with 750 sq ft or less of interior livable space, or a JADU with 500 sq ft or less. Larger ADUs may only be charged fees proportionate to the primary dwelling.

parameters.over_threshold_formula: fee proportionate to the square footage of the primary dwelling unit, i.e., fee x (ADU sqft / primary dwelling sqft)

rules.applies_to: ADU/JADU owners and builders; fee calculators
rules.citation: Gov Code 66311.5 (renumbered from 66324 by SB 543, Stats. 2025 ch. 520)
rules.quote: A local agency, special district, or water corporation shall not impose any impact fee upon the development of an accessory dwelling unit that has 750 square feet of interior livable space or less or a junior accessory dwelling unit that has 500 square feet of interior livable space or less.
rules.notes: Quote from code-mirror excerpt of 66311.5. The proportional-fee formula for >750 sq ft is described differently in an Assembly analysis (fees only on area over 750 sq ft) - confirm chaptered text before computing. Connection fees/capacity charges have separate proportionality rules (not verified). [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: 750 sq ft ADU / 500 sq ft JADU exemption and quote confirmed. The flagged conflict is resolved: the enacted text requires fees on larger ADUs to be proportionate to the square footage of the primary dwelling (not charged only on area over 750 sq ft); conflict note removed from parameters. FLAG: SB 1117 (2025-26) would further revise 66311.5 (status not checked).

rules.title: ADU/JADU under 500 sq ft exempt from school fees
rules.plain_english: For school impact (developer) fees, an ADU or JADU with less than 500 sq ft of interior livable space is treated like a residential addition that does not add 500 sq ft of assessable space, so no Level 1 school fee applies.
rules.applies_to: ADU/JADU projects
rules.notes: Sources disagree on "less than 500" vs "500 or fewer"; statute text not read.
rules.correction: None. Resolves the noted disagreement: the statute says "less than 500 square feet".

rules.title: JADU owner occupancy only if bathroom is shared
rules.plain_english: From 2026, owner occupancy is required for a JADU only when the JADU shares sanitation facilities (bathroom) with the main house; JADUs may not be used as short-term rentals. JADUs are limited to 500 sq ft.

parameters.owner_occupancy_required_if: JADU shares bathroom with primary dwelling

rules.applies_to: JADU projects
rules.notes: Summaries only; section numbers not verified. Verification 2026-11-25: AB 1154 = Stats. 2025 ch. 507 amending Gov Code 66333; rentals of a JADU must be for a term longer than 30 days; owner occupancy is also waived where the owner is a governmental agency, land trust or housing organization. The 500 sq ft interior-livable-space cap is in SB 543 (ch. 520).
rules.correction: None. Details from the statute: owner occupancy is not required if the JADU has separate sanitation facilities or the owner is a governmental agency, land trust or housing organization; rentals must be for terms longer than 30 days; the 500 sq ft (interior livable space) cap comes from SB 543, not AB 1154.

rules.title: SB 9 urban lot split: 1,200 sq ft minimum resulting lots
rules.plain_english: An SB 9 urban lot split divides a single-family-zoned parcel into two lots ministerially; each new lot must be at least 1,200 sq ft, and the split must be roughly even (each lot at least 40% of the original).
rules.applies_to: Owners/developers of single-family-zoned parcels in urbanized areas
rules.notes: The 1,200 sq ft minimum and "two units on each resulting lot" were in excerpts; the 40% (60/40) figure was referenced but NOT confirmed. Many eligibility exclusions (historic, hazard zones, tenant-occupied in last 3 years, demolition of >25% of exterior walls) were not verified. Verification 2026-11-25: 40% minimum confirmed in leginfo text; AB 1061 (2025-26) text adds "An application for an urban lot split shall be considered and approved or denied within 60 days from the date the local agency receives a completed application. If the local agency has not approved or denied the completed application within 60 days, the application shall be deemed approved." (enactment status not separately confirmed).
rules.correction: None. 40% figure now confirmed. Added note: AB 1061 (2025) adds a 60-day approve/deny clock with deemed approval for urban lot splits. Eligibility exclusions not checked.

rules.title: SB 9 lot split: 3-year owner occupancy affidavit
