rules.plain_english: The applicant for an SB 9 urban lot split must sign an affidavit that they intend to live in one of the units as their principal residence for at least three years from approval (community land trusts and qualified nonprofits excepted).
rules.applies_to: SB 9 urban lot split applicants
rules.quote: An SB 9 urban lot split applicant must sign an affidavit stating that they intend to live in one of the units for three years unless the applicant is a community land trust or qualified nonprofit corporation.
rules.notes: County summary, not statute. A 2022 ABAG overview references a sunset of the owner-occupancy authority in 2027 - check whether this has changed.

rules.title: SB 9 two-unit projects: 800 sq ft units and 4-ft setbacks
rules.plain_english: Under SB 9 a city must ministerially approve up to two units on a single-family lot, cannot apply standards that prevent two units of at least 800 sq ft each, and generally cannot require side/rear setbacks over 4 ft. Local agencies must act within 60 days of a complete application (SB 450).
rules.applies_to: SB 9 two-unit (duplex) projects
rules.notes: NOT confirmed in any source text this session; numbers from general knowledge of SB 9/SB 450. Treat as unverified lead. Verification 2026-11-25: SB 450 text: "An application for a proposed housing development pursuant to this section shall be considered and approved or denied within 60 days from the date the local agency receives a completed application. If the local agency has not approved or denied the completed application within 60 days, the application shall be deemed approved."
rules.correction: None. 800 sq ft, 4 ft side/rear setback and 60-day decision deadline (deemed approved if missed, per SB 450) confirmed. Not checked: 1 parking space per unit.

rules.title: Level 1 school developer fee caps: $5.38 residential / $0.87 commercial per sq ft
rules.plain_english: School districts may collect Level 1 developer fees up to $5.38 per sq ft of assessable residential space and $0.87 per sq ft of commercial/industrial space, as adjusted by the State Allocation Board on January 28, 2026 (previously $5.17 and $0.84). Each district must adopt the increase; new rates typically take effect 60 days after the district board acts.

parameters.self_storage_and_senior_housing_rates: lower commercial rate categories exist (not verified)

rules.applies_to: New residential/commercial construction and residential additions >500 sq ft
rules.notes: Amounts are maximums; actual district rates vary (justification study required; Level 2/3 fees can be higher). Search summary said "about 4.06%". Effective dates in districts vary (e.g., May 18, 2026; LAUSD Aug 11, 2026). Biennial cycle from general knowledge.
rules.correction: None. $5.38 / $0.87, prior $5.17 / $0.84, 4.06% and the two-year cycle (Gov Code 65995(b)(3)) confirmed. Not checked: the 60-day district effective delay.

rules.title: School fees on residential additions only over 500 sq ft
rules.plain_english: A residential addition is subject to Level 1 school fees only if it increases assessable space by more than 500 sq ft; if it does, the fee applies to the entire net increase, not just the excess. Some districts treat the 500 sq ft allowance as cumulative for the life of the structure.

parameters.fee_base_if_over: entire net increase in assessable space

rules.applies_to: Residential additions
rules.quote: Education Code Section 17620 (a)(1)(C)(i) permits school districts to charge Level I Fees on residential additions only if the resulting increase in assessable space exceeds 500 square feet.
rules.notes: Quote is a school district paraphrase, not statute text.
rules.correction: None. Caveat: the clause (ii) exception and the "entire net increase" fee base are district practice not seen in the statute excerpt.

rules.title: School fee certificate required before building permit
rules.plain_english: A city or county may not issue a building permit for a project subject to school fees until the school district certifies the fee has been paid (or the project is exempt). Build the district payment step into the permit schedule.

parameters.gate: school district certificate of compliance / payment receipt

rules.applies_to: Projects subject to school developer fees
rules.quote: The legislation provides that no Building Permit may be issued until the school districts certify that any fees due have been paid. Education Code § 17620(b).
rules.notes: School district paraphrase; statute not read.

rules.title: SMIP (strong motion) fee on every building permit
rules.plain_english: Cities and counties collect a Strong Motion Instrumentation and Seismic Hazard Mapping fee on each building permit: Category 1 (residential up to 3 stories) = valuation x 0.00013 ($13 per $100,000); Category 2 (all other buildings, incl. residential over 3 stories) = valuation x 0.00028 ($28 per $100,000); minimum fee $0.50.

parameters.category_2_scope: all other buildings incl. residential >3 stories

rules.applies_to: All building permits with a valuation
rules.quote: the fee for any valuation up to $1786 is simply $.50
rules.notes: Rates from a CGS-sourced city schedule; statute text not read. Local agency may retain a small percentage for collection (not verified). Rounding conventions vary by jurisdiction. Verification 2026-11-25: PRC 2705 lets a city/county retain up to 5 percent of the total collected.
rules.correction: None. Resolves an unverified note: the city/county may retain up to 5% of fees collected (data utilization and seismic education). The 2014-07-01 rate date was not checked.

rules.title: Building Standards Administration (BSASRF) fee on permits
rules.plain_english: Every building permit with a valuation also carries the state Building Standards Administration Special Revolving Fund fee (the "green fee"): $4 per $100,000 of valuation, collected as $1 per $25,000 or fraction thereof with a $1 minimum. The local agency may keep up to 10 percent for administrative costs and code-enforcement education and sends the rest to the Building Standards Commission.

parameters.local_retention_use: related administrative costs and code enforcement education

rules.applies_to: All building permits with a valuation
rules.quote: Each city, county, or city and county shall collect a fee from any applicant for a building permit, assessed at the rate of four dollars ($4) per one hundred thousand dollars ($100,000) in valuation
rules.notes: The $1 per $25,000 schedule comes from a city fee table; the statutory $4 per $100,000 wording and the 10% local retention were NOT confirmed. Commission may reduce the rate. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: Previously unconfirmed items resolved: statute is $4 per $100,000 of valuation (with fractions); CBSC expresses it as $1 per $25,000 or fraction thereof with a $1 minimum per permit; local retention is up to (not more than) 10% for administrative costs and code-enforcement education; Commission may reduce the rate (18931.6(c)). Quote added. Quarterly remittance not seen.

rules.title: Inspect for asbestos before any demolition or renovation
rules.plain_english: Before starting a demolition or renovation of a regulated facility, the owner or operator must thoroughly inspect the affected part of the facility for asbestos, including Category I and II nonfriable asbestos-containing material.

parameters.timing: before commencement of demolition or renovation
parameters.applies_to_facility_types: institutional, commercial, public, industrial, residential with 5+ units

rules.applies_to: Owners and operators (including demolition contractors) of regulated facilities
rules.quote: prior to the commencement of the demolition or renovation, thoroughly inspect the affected facility or part of the facility where the demolition or renovation operation will occur for the presence of asbestos, including Category I and Category II nonfriable ACM.
rules.notes: In California the NESHAP is enforced by local air districts (e.g., SCAQMD Rule 1403, BAAQMD Reg. 11 Rule 2), which may be stricter. Asbestos survey by a Cal/OSHA Certified Asbestos Consultant is commonly required by districts (not verified here).

rules.title: NESHAP "facility" excludes homes with 4 or fewer units
rules.plain_english: Federal asbestos NESHAP demolition/renovation rules cover institutional, commercial, public, industrial and residential buildings, but exclude residential buildings with four or fewer dwelling units (a building with a dwelling loft is not treated as residential). Local air district rules may still cover single-family demolitions.
rules.applies_to: Demolition/renovation contractors determining applicability
rules.quote: Facility means any institutional, commercial, public, industrial, or residential structure, installation, or building (including any structure, installation, or building containing condominiums or individual dwelling units operated as a residential cooperative, but excluding residential buildings having four or fewer dwelling units);
rules.notes: Bay Area AQMD notification applies to every demolition regardless of asbestos (search excerpt) - California districts often regulate single-family demolitions that the federal rule excludes.

rules.title: Asbestos thresholds: 260 linear ft / 160 sq ft / 35 cu ft
rules.plain_english: Full NESHAP notification and work-practice requirements apply when the combined regulated asbestos-containing material (RACM) is at least 260 linear feet on pipes, 160 square feet on other components, or 35 cubic feet off components. In a renovation, below these amounts the NESHAP does not apply; in a demolition, notification is still required even below them (or with no asbestos).
rules.applies_to: Demolition and renovation of NESHAP facilities
rules.quote: At least 80 linear meters (260 linear feet) on pipes or at least 15 square meters (160 square feet) on other facility components, or
rules.notes: (a)(2): "In a facility being demolished, only the notification requirements of paragraphs (b)(1), (2), (3)(i) and (iv), and (4)(i) through (vii) and (4)(ix) and (xvi) of this section apply, if the combined amount of RACM is" below the thresholds. Cal/OSHA and CSLB use a separate 100 sq ft trigger for asbestos-related work registration/certification.

rules.title: Asbestos demolition/renovation notice: 10 working days before
rules.plain_english: The owner or operator must postmark or deliver written notice to the regulator at least 10 working days before asbestos stripping/removal or any activity that would disturb asbestos begins, and at least 10 working days before any demolition begins (even if little or no asbestos). Working days are Monday-Friday including holidays.

parameters.working_day_definition: Monday through Friday, including holidays that fall on those days
parameters.measured_from: postmark or delivery date
parameters.emergency_or_ordered_demolition: as early as possible, no later than the following working day
parameters.annual_nonscheduled_renovation_notice: at least 10 working days before end of preceding calendar year

rules.applies_to: Owners/operators of NESHAP-regulated demolitions and renovations (in CA, notice goes to the local air district)
rules.quote: If the operation is as described in paragraph (a)(2) of this section, notification is required 10 working days before demolition begins.
rules.notes: (b)(3)(i): "At least 10 working days before asbestos stripping or removal work or any other activity begins (such as site preparation that would break up, dislodge or similarly disturb asbestos material)". Definition (61.141): "Working day means Monday through Friday and includes holidays that fall on any of the days Monday through Friday." Air district fees apply.

rules.title: Update asbestos notice for 20% change or new start date
rules.plain_english: Update the notice when the amount of asbestos affected changes by at least 20 percent. If the start date moves later, phone the regulator before the original date and send written notice no later than the original date; if it moves earlier, give written notice at least 10 working days before the new start. Work may never begin on a date other than the one in the written notice.

later_start: written notice no later than original start date

rules.applies_to: Owners/operators with filed NESHAP notifications
rules.quote: Update notice, as necessary, including when the amount of asbestos affected changes by at least 20 percent.
rules.notes: (b)(3)(iv)(C): "In no event shall an operation covered by this paragraph begin on a date other than the date contained in the written notice of the new start date."

rules.title: Required contents of asbestos demolition/renovation notice
rules.plain_english: The written notice must include: original/revised indicator; names, addresses and phones of facility owner, operator and asbestos removal contractor; demolition vs renovation; facility description (size, floors, age, use); asbestos detection method; estimated RACM and nonfriable ACM amounts; address; asbestos removal and demolition start/end dates; work description and methods; emission controls; waste disposal site; trained-supervisor certification; procedures for unexpected RACM; and waste transporter.

fields: owner/operator and asbestos removal contractor name, address, phone
facility description: size (sq ft), number of floors, age, present and prior use
asbestos detection procedure incl. analytical methods
estimated RACM (linear ft / sq ft / cu ft) and nonfriable ACM remaining
location and street address, city, county, state
scheduled start/completion of demolition or renovation
waste disposal site name and location
parameters.form: similar to EPA Figure 3 (air district forms in CA)

rules.applies_to: Owners/operators filing NESHAP notifications
rules.quote: Name, address, and telephone number of both the facility owner and operator and the asbestos removal contractor owner or operator.

rules.title: Remove all RACM before disturbing activities
rules.plain_english: All regulated asbestos-containing material must be removed from a facility being demolished or renovated before any activity that would break it up or block access to it, with limited exceptions (e.g., intact Category I nonfriable material, material encased in concrete).

parameters.removal_timing: before any activity that would break up, dislodge, disturb, or preclude access

rules.applies_to: Demolition and renovation contractors on NESHAP facilities above thresholds
rules.quote: Remove all RACM from a facility being demolished or renovated before any activity begins that would break up, dislodge, or similarly disturb the material or preclude access to the material for subsequent removal.
rules.notes: Actual removal of 100+ sq ft ACM requires a C-22 or asbestos-certified contractor registered with Cal/OSHA (see asbestos-c22-or-certification-100sqft).

rules.title: Trained asbestos supervisor on site; refresher every 2 years
rules.plain_english: No RACM may be stripped, removed or disturbed unless at least one on-site representative (foreman or management-level person) trained in the NESHAP is present, and that person must get refresher training every 2 years.
rules.applies_to: Asbestos removal/demolition crews on NESHAP facilities
rules.quote: Every 2 years, the trained on-site individual shall receive refresher training in the provisions of this regulation.

rules.title: No demolition permit without asbestos notification copy
rules.plain_english: A city or county may not issue a demolition permit until the applicant provides a copy of the written asbestos notification sent to the air district (or EPA), or declares that notification does not apply to the project. In South Coast AQMD, evidence of Rule 1403 notification satisfies this.

parameters.document: copy of written asbestos notification (NESHAP/air district)
parameters.alternative: applicant declaration that notification is not applicable

rules.applies_to: Demolition permit applicants
rules.source: https://california.public.law/codes/health_and_safety_code_section_19827.5 ; https://www.cityofplacerville.org/media/Building Division Files/2023/Asbestos Notification at Demolition.pdf (search excerpts)
rules.notes: Statute added by AB 2791 (1990) per ARB advisory; text read only via excerpts. Some cities require proof of district receipt despite the statute. Effective date assumed - not verified.

rules.title: Air district demolition notice 10 working days ahead (SCAQMD/BAAQMD)
rules.plain_english: California air districts require asbestos demolition/renovation notifications at least 10 working days before work. South Coast AQMD (Rule 1403) requires notice 10 working days (about 14 calendar days) before any demolition or removal of more than 100 sq ft of asbestos-containing material, with a separate form for owner-occupants demolishing their own house; Bay Area AQMD (Reg. 11-2) requires notice for every demolition, even with no asbestos, and for renovations removing 100 sq ft, 100 linear ft or 35 cubic ft or more of asbestos.

parameters.scaqmd_homeowner_form: owner-occupant personally demolishing own detached single-family house
parameters.emergency_work: waiting period waivable only for qualifying emergency

rules.applies_to: Demolition and renovation contractors in South Coast and Bay Area AQMD (other districts similar)
rules.notes: Air district sites blocked; details partly from archived 2008 BAAQMD pages. 35 local air districts exist; each has its own form and fee. BAAQMD previously allowed a shorter start for 1-4 unit buildings with an extra fee (archived). [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: 10-working-day lead time confirmed for both districts. SCAQMD: the district states notice is due 10 working days (or 14 calendar days) before any demolition or removal of more than 100 sq ft of intact ACM - the 14-calendar-day figure is not a homeowner-only alternative; a separate homeowner form exists for owner-occupants personally demolishing their own detached single-family house. BAAQMD: renovation trigger is 100 sq ft, 100 linear ft OR 35 cubic ft of asbestos; every demolition (load-supporting structure) needs notice regardless of asbestos. Parameters and plain_english updated.

rules.title: C-22 or asbestos certification for 100+ sq ft asbestos work
rules.plain_english: A contractor may not do asbestos-related work involving 100 sq ft or more of asbestos-containing material unless it holds the C-22 Asbestos Abatement classification or its qualifier passed the asbestos certification exam (plus Cal/OSHA registration). Installing/repairing asbestos cement pipe or sheet, vinyl asbestos flooring, or asbestos bituminous/resinous materials is exempt from the exam.

required: or asbestos certification exam by qualifier

rules.applies_to: Demolition, renovation and abatement contractors
rules.source: PDF page 274 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: A contractor shall not engage in asbestos-related work, as defined in Section 6501.8 of the Labor Code, that involves 100 square feet or more of surface area of asbestos containing materials, unless the contractor holds a C-22 Asbestos Abatement classification or the qualifier for the license passes an asbestos certification examination.
rules.notes: Cal/OSHA registration, job notification and safety rules are in the Cal/OSHA research file.

rules.title: Disclose ties to abatement firm when doing permit-required asbestos inspection
rules.plain_english: If a contractor inspects for asbestos knowing the report is required by a lender or by a public entity as a condition of a permit, it must disclose orally and in writing any ownership or financial relationship (including referral fees) with a company that would do the corrective work. Violation is a misdemeanor with a $3,000-$5,000 fine and/or up to 1 year in jail.

parameters.trigger: asbestos inspection report required for loan or permit

rules.applies_to: Contractors performing asbestos inspections tied to permits or loans
rules.source: PDF page 356-357 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (d) A violation of this section is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not less than three thousand dollars ($3,000) and not more than five thousand dollars ($5,000), or by imprisonment in the county jail for not more than one year, or both.

rules.title: Penalty for hiring an uncertified asbestos subcontractor
rules.plain_english: A contractor who knowingly, negligently or by failing to inquire contracts with someone not certified for asbestos-related work faces an infraction fine of $1,000-$3,000 for a first offense, and a misdemeanor with $3,000-$5,000 fine and/or up to 1 year in jail plus license suspension/revocation for a later offense. Verify C-22/certification before subcontracting demo or abatement.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors subcontracting asbestos-related work
rules.source: PDF page 357 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (a) Conviction of a first offense is an infraction punishable by a fine of not less than one thousand dollars ($1,000) or more than three thousand dollars ($3,000), and by possible revocation or suspension of any contractor’s license.

rules.title: Lead RRP rule applies to paid renovation of pre-1978 housing
rules.plain_english: EPA's Renovation, Repair and Painting rule applies to renovations for compensation in "target housing" (built before 1978, except elderly/disabled housing and 0-bedroom units unless a child under 6 lives there) and child-occupied facilities, unless a certified inspector/risk assessor or certified renovator test shows components are lead-free (below 1.0 mg/cm2 or 0.5% by weight).

excluded: housing for elderly or persons with disabilities (unless child <6 resides)
exemption_methods: certified renovator paint chip lab test

rules.applies_to: Contractors doing paid renovation, repair or painting in pre-1978 homes and child-occupied facilities
rules.quote: This subpart applies to all renovations performed for compensation in target housing and child-occupied facilities, except for the following:
rules.notes: California does not have an EPA-authorized RRP program (general knowledge, not verified this session), so the federal rule and EPA certification apply in CA; CA also has separate lead-safe work practice rules (17 CCR / CDPH) not researched here.

rules.title: RRP minor repair exemption: 6 sq ft interior / 20 sq ft exterior
rules.plain_english: Minor repair and maintenance that disturbs 6 sq ft or less of painted surface per room inside, or 20 sq ft or less outside, is not a covered renovation, unless it involves window replacement, demolition of painted surfaces, or prohibited practices. Jobs in the same room within 30 days count as one job.
rules.applies_to: Pre-1978 housing renovation
rules.quote: Jobs, other than emergency renovations, performed in the same room within the same 30 days must be considered the same job for the purpose of determining whether the job is a minor repair and maintenance activity.
rules.notes: Definition text: "...that disrupt 6 square feet or less of painted surface per room for interior activities or 20 square feet or less of painted surface for exterior activities where none of the work practices prohibited or restricted by § 745.85(a)(3) are used and where the work does not involve window replacement or demolition of painted surface areas."

rules.title: Give "Renovate Right" pamphlet no more than 60 days before work
rules.plain_english: No more than 60 days before starting renovation in a pre-1978 dwelling unit, the firm must give the owner the EPA "Renovate Right" pamphlet and get a signed acknowledgment, or a certificate of mailing at least 7 days before the work. If the owner does not live there, an adult occupant must also get it. Common-area work requires notice to each affected unit or posted signs.

recipients: adult occupant if owner does not occupy
parameters.pamphlet: Renovate Right: Important Lead Hazard Information for Families, Child Care Providers and Schools

rules.applies_to: Firms renovating target housing (residential remodelers, painters, window installers, plumbers, electricians, HVAC)
rules.quote: No more than 60 days before beginning renovation activities in any residential dwelling unit of target housing, the firm performing the renovation must: (1) Provide the owner of the unit with the pamphlet, and comply with one of the following: (i) Obtain, from the owner, a written acknowledgment that the owner has received the pamphlet.

rules.title: EPA RRP firm certification and certified renovator
rules.plain_english: A firm may not perform, offer or claim to perform renovations in target housing or child-occupied facilities without EPA firm certification, and every job must be directed by a certified renovator. EPA acts on firm applications within 90 days; certification lasts up to 5 years.
rules.applies_to: Firms doing renovation for compensation in pre-1978 housing
rules.quote: (ii) On or after April 22, 2010, no firm may perform, offer, or claim to perform renovations without certification from EPA under § 745.89 in target housing or child-occupied facilities, unless the renovation qualifies for one of the exceptions identified in § 745.82(a) or (c).

rules.title: RRP prohibited practices on painted surfaces
rules.plain_english: During covered renovations, open-flame burning or torching of painted surfaces is prohibited, and high-speed sanding, grinding, planing, needle-gun or abrasive blasting is prohibited unless the machine has a shroud/containment and HEPA vacuum attachment; heat guns are restricted. Work areas must be posted with warning signs before work begins.

prohibited: open-flame burning or torching
high-speed power removal without shroud + HEPA

rules.applies_to: Covered renovations in pre-1978 housing and child-occupied facilities
rules.quote: (i) Open-flame burning or torching of painted surfaces is prohibited.
rules.notes: Heat gun temperature limit (1100 F) is in 745.85(a)(3)(iii) - truncated in what was read; omitted from parameters.

rules.title: Keep RRP records 3 years after completion
rules.plain_english: Renovation firms must keep all records showing RRP compliance (lead-free determinations, pamphlet acknowledgments, work practice checklists, training certificates) for 3 years after the renovation is complete and provide them to EPA on request.
rules.applies_to: Firms performing covered renovations
rules.quote: (a) Firms performing renovations must retain and, if requested, make available to EPA all records necessary to demonstrate compliance with this subpart for a period of 3 years following completion of the renovation.

rules.title: Construction disturbing 1+ acre needs NPDES stormwater coverage
rules.plain_english: Federal stormwater rules require permit coverage for construction (clearing, grading, excavating) disturbing one acre or more, including smaller sites that are part of a larger common plan of development that will disturb one acre or more. Routine maintenance to keep original line and grade is excluded.

parameters.excluded: routine maintenance of original line, grade, hydraulic capacity or purpose

rules.applies_to: Construction sites (owners as legally responsible persons; contractors as operators)
rules.quote: (15) Storm water discharge associated with small construction activity means the discharge of storm water from: (i) Construction activities including clearing, grading, and excavating that result in land disturbance of equal to or greater than one acre and less than five acres.
rules.notes: In California the State Water Board implements this through the statewide Construction General Permit (see cgp-* rules).

rules.title: Erosivity waiver for 1-5 acre sites (R factor < 5)
rules.plain_english: Sites disturbing less than 5 acres may qualify for a waiver from construction stormwater permit requirements if the rainfall erosivity factor (R in RUSLE) during the construction period is less than 5.

parameters.calculation: RUSLE R factor, USDA Agriculture Handbook 703

rules.applies_to: Small construction sites with short dry-season schedules
rules.quote: The value of the rainfall erosivity factor (“R” in the Revised Universal Soil Loss Equation) is less than five during the period of construction activity.
rules.notes: California's CGP implements an erosivity waiver submitted through SMARTS (state procedure not read). If the schedule extends past the waiver period, full CGP coverage is needed.

rules.title: File CGP NOI in SMARTS and get WDID before work starts
rules.plain_english: Before construction starts on a site disturbing one or more acres, the legally responsible person (usually the owner) must submit a Notice of Intent, permit fee and Permit Registration Documents (risk determination, site map, SWPPP) through the State Water Board SMARTS system and receive a WDID number. The current statewide Construction General Permit is Order WQ 2022-0057-DWQ, effective September 1, 2023.
rules.applies_to: Owners and developers of construction sites disturbing 1+ acre (or part of a larger common plan)
rules.citation: State Water Board Order WQ 2022-0057-DWQ (CGP), Attachment D.2; Water Code 13260
rules.quote: Notice of Intent (NOI) application, permit fees, and all necessary documents via smarts.waterboards.ca.gov (SMARTS) for approval before construction can begin. The State Water Board will issue a unique identification number known as the WDID number once approved.
rules.notes: waterboards.ca.gov blocked; county guide and Caltrans directive excerpts only. Linear underground projects (LUPs) have a separate attachment. Many local agencies require the WDID before issuing grading permits (general knowledge).

rules.title: SWPPP must be prepared by a Qualified SWPPP Developer (QSD)
rules.plain_english: The site-specific Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plan (SWPPP), including drawings and the risk level determination, must be developed by a Qualified SWPPP Developer (QSD) and certified and submitted with the other Permit Registration Documents. The SWPPP must be kept current and implemented on site.
rules.applies_to: CGP-covered construction sites
rules.citation: CGP Order WQ 2022-0057-DWQ, Attachment D.2 (registration requirements)
rules.quote: The SWPPP (including site specific drawings and map) is a site-specific document developed for implementation of this General Permit. The SWPPP shall be developed by a Qualified SWPPP Developer and certified and submitted by each discharger with the other PRDs.
rules.notes: Quote from a July 2022 draft attachment surfaced in search; final wording may differ.

rules.title: Qualified SWPPP Practitioner (QSP) implements and inspects
rules.plain_english: A Qualified SWPPP Practitioner (QSP) implements the SWPPP, conducts required site inspections (weekly and around qualifying precipitation events), and performs sampling; a QSD monthly inspection may count toward the weekly requirement. The QSP also prepares the final inspection report for termination.
rules.applies_to: CGP-covered construction sites (general contractors usually provide the QSP)
rules.notes: Inspection frequencies by risk level not verified. Sampling requirements depend on risk level and TMDLs.

rules.title: CGP Qualifying Precipitation Event (QPE) and inspections
rules.plain_english: Under the 2022 CGP a Qualifying Precipitation Event is a National Weather Service forecast with a 50 percent or greater chance of precipitation and 0.5 inch or more within 24 hours, extended for each following 24-hour period forecasting 0.25 inch or more. Pre-QPE inspections are due within 72 hours before the event (up to 120 hours ahead with extended forecasts), with inspections during the event and a post-QPE inspection within 96 hours if 0.5 inch or more is measured onsite. The old Rain Event Action Plan (REAP) is no longer required.

parameters.qpe_end_rule: FLAG: one subsequent 24-h period forecasting <0.25 in (QPE guidance) vs two consecutive such periods (fact sheet)

rules.applies_to: CGP-covered construction sites
rules.quote: Produce 0.5" of precipitation within a 24-hr period, and are extended for each subsequent 24-hr period of forecast 0.25" or more of precipitation.
rules.notes: From State Water Board QPE fact sheet and FAQ via search excerpts. 120-hour pre-event window reported "in some cases" - confirm. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: 0.5 in/24 h trigger, 0.25 in extension and REAP removal confirmed, but the QPE also requires a 50% or greater probability of precipitation (National Weather Service forecast). Pre-QPE inspection is due within 72 hours before the QPE, or up to 120 hours ahead only where extended forecast data is available; post-QPE inspection within 96 hours if 0.5 in or more is measured onsite. The end-of-event rule conflicts between sources (QPE guidance: one 24-h period under 0.25 in; fact sheet: two consecutive periods) - left as FLAG.

rules.title: Notice of Termination ends CGP coverage and annual fees
rules.plain_english: When the site is complete and finally stabilized (or ownership transferred), the owner files a Notice of Termination in SMARTS with a final site map, photos and a QSP final inspection report. The SWPPP must be implemented and annual fees paid until the NOT is accepted.

parameters.annual_fee_amount: set yearly by State Water Board fee regulation (23 CCR 2200) - not verified
parameters.not_submission_deadline_days: unverified (90 days in older regional guidance)

rules.applies_to: CGP permittees at project completion
rules.citation: CGP Order WQ 2022-0057-DWQ, Section III / Attachment D
rules.quote: Continue to implement the SWPPP, comply with CGP requirements, and pay annual fees until the NOT is accepted in SMARTS.
rules.notes: Final stabilization criteria (e.g., 70% vegetative cover) not verified for the 2022 order.

rules.title: Call 811 at least 2 working days (max 14 calendar days) before digging
rules.plain_english: Anyone planning to excavate must contact the regional notification center (811) at least two working days, but not more than 14 calendar days, before starting, except in emergencies. The day of the call does not count toward the two working days. The call is free.
rules.applies_to: Any person or contractor who disturbs the ground (digging, drilling, boring, grading, trenching, etc.)
rules.source: PDF page 84 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: California Government Code sections 4216-4216.9 require anyone planning to excavate to contact the appropriate regional notification center at least two working days (but not more than 14 calendar days) before beginning excavation. The center will issue an inquiry identification number to the excavator as confirmation of the call.
rules.notes: Also on cslb.ca.gov Appropriate Contacts page (lists older toll-free number 800-227-2600). "The date of the notification shall not count as part of the two-working-day notice" is from a Findlaw excerpt of 4216.2, not primary.

rules.title: Excavation permit invalid without USA ticket number
rules.plain_english: An excavation permit issued by a local agency is not valid unless the excavator has a USA inquiry identification (ticket) number. Record the ticket number on the permit and job file before digging.
rules.applies_to: Excavators working under local excavation/encroachment permits
rules.source: PDF page 84 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: NOTE: An excavation permit is not valid without this identification number.

rules.title: Every excavating contractor and sub needs its own ticket
rules.plain_english: Each general contractor, contractor or subcontractor excavating at a job site must have its own Underground Service Alert ticket number for the excavation work it performs; a sub cannot dig under the GC's ticket.
rules.applies_to: All excavating contractors and subcontractors
rules.source: PDF page 85 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Every contractor or subcontractor excavating at a jobsite must have their own Underground Service Alert (USA) identification (ticket) number for the excavation work they are performing.

rules.title: USA ticket valid 28 calendar days; renew before expiry
rules.plain_english: The USA ticket number is valid for 28 calendar days. If work will continue beyond that, the excavator must renew (revalidate) the ticket with the center before it expires.
rules.applies_to: Excavators on jobs lasting more than 28 days
rules.source: PDF page 85 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Upon notification, the center will issue an identification (ticket) number. The ticket number will be valid for 28 calendar days. If work is to continue past 28 calendar days, the ticket number must be revalidated again by notifying the center before the ticket number expires.
rules.notes: Verification 2026-11-25: leginfo excerpt of 4216.2 says renewal is due "by the end of the 28th day" via the center website or 811; an expired ticket means work must stop and a new ticket be obtained (SB 778 (2024) changed the post-expiration procedure - exact current wording not seen).

rules.title: Mark excavation area in white paint before calling
rules.plain_english: At the site, the excavator must clearly delineate the boundaries of the planned excavation, usually with white paint, so operators know where to mark their lines.
rules.applies_to: Excavators
rules.source: PDF page 86 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: At the site, excavators must clearly mark the boundaries of the work area, usually with white paint.
rules.notes: Ticket request asks whether the excavation has been outlined in white paint.

rules.title: Request re-mark when markings fade (operator has 2 working days)
rules.plain_english: If operator markings are no longer visible during the job, the excavator must contact the regional center to request a re-mark; operators re-mark within two working days. Do not dig on faded marks.

parameters.trigger: markings no longer visible

rules.applies_to: Excavators
rules.source: PDF page 86 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: During the course of the job, if the operator’s markings become no longer visible, the excavator must contact the regional center and request that the operator re-mark the lines within two working days.
rules.notes: Verification 2026-11-25 (leginfo excerpt of 4216.3): "If the field marks are no longer reasonably visible, an excavator shall renotify the regional notification center with a request for remarks ... Excavation shall cease in the area to be remarked. If remarks are requested, the operator shall have two working days, not including the date of request, to remark the subsurface installation." The excavator must also redelineate if the white-paint marks are gone.

rules.title: Locate lines with hand tools or vacuum before power equipment
rules.plain_english: Using the operator's markings, the excavator must find the exact location of underground facilities with hand tools or a vacuum device before any power equipment may be used.

required_methods: vacuum excavation device (if center informed and operator agrees)

rules.applies_to: Excavators
rules.source: PDF page 86 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Using the operator’s markings, an excavator must determine the exact location of underground facilities with hand tools or a vacuum device before any power equipment may be used.
rules.notes: Vacuum use requires telling the center when obtaining the ticket and operator agreement (search excerpt of 4216.4, not primary).

rules.title: Tolerance zone = 24 inches each side of the mark
rules.plain_english: The tolerance zone is 24 inches on each side of the operator's field marking; inside it the excavator must use hand tools (or approved vacuum excavation) to expose the facility.
rules.applies_to: Excavators
rules.citation: Gov Code 4216(u) (definition of tolerance zone; subdivision letter unverified)
rules.notes: Not read from primary text; definition from search excerpt.

rules.title: Report damage to underground facilities within 48 hours
rules.plain_english: An excavator who discovers or causes damage to a subsurface installation must notify the regional notification center within 48 hours (and call 911 immediately if gas or hazardous liquid is escaping).
rules.applies_to: Excavators
rules.source: PDF page 86 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: An excavator must notify the regional notification center within 48 hours of discovering or causing damage.
rules.notes: 911 requirement for escaping gas is general practice, not read here. Verification 2026-11-25: leginfo codified 4216.4 also requires immediate notice to the operator and an immediate 911 call when damage involves specified high-priority/gas or hazardous liquid installations. SB 1345 (2021-22) proposed a 2-hour report to the Dig Safe Board; its enactment was not confirmed, and the codified text and 2026 Law Book still show 48 hours.

rules.title: Information needed to open a USA ticket
rules.plain_english: When calling 811, give the start date/time, caller and company name, mailing address, email, contact phone, nature of work, who the work is for, foreman name, permit name and number, whether the area is outlined in white paint, and a precise site description (address, side of street, intersection, footage/tie-ins, nearest cross street, city, county).
rules.applies_to: Excavators requesting tickets
rules.source: PDF page 86 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Give your name, company’s name, company’s mailing address, email address, telephone number where you can be contacted, nature of work (grading, drilling, etc.), whom the work is being done for, name of the foreman, permit name and number, if excavation has been outlined in white paint, and a description of the excavation site.

rules.title: 811 exemptions (homeowner, rental companies)
rules.plain_english: Exempt from calling 811: (1) a homeowner who is not a licensed contractor, improving their principal residence with hand-tool excavation that needs no permit; (2) equipment rental companies whose signed rental agreement with a licensed contractor contains the statutory responsibility clause. The Law Book also lists a private owner who hires a licensed contractor for non-permit excavation, but that exemption could not be confirmed in current statute text; the contractor must call either way. Licensed contractors themselves are never exempt.

exemptions: homeowner (not a licensed contractor) improving own principal residence with excavation using hand tools that requires no state or local permit (Gov Code 4216.8 as amended by SB 119)
equipment lessor of power-operated excavating/boring equipment to a licensed contractor, with statutory clause in signed rental agreement
FLAG unconfirmed after SB 119: owner of private property hiring a licensed contractor for excavation not requiring an excavation permit (the contractor still must call 811)

rules.applies_to: Owners, rental companies, contractors
rules.citation: Gov Code 4216.8 (as amended by SB 119, Stats. 2015)
rules.source: PDF page 85 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: An owner of private property who contracts with a California state-licensed contractor or subcontractor for an excavation project that does not require an excavation permit.
rules.notes: Section number for exemptions not shown in the law book text. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: The homeowner exemption in current 4216.8 (as amended by SB 119, 2015) is limited to an owner of residential real property, not a licensed contractor, improving the principal residence with excavation using hand tools that needs no state or local permit; the Law Book wording omits the hand-tool condition. SB 119 bill digest says it deleted the prior owner-of-real-property exemptions, so the "owner who hires a licensed contractor" exemption could not be found in post-2015 text (kept as a flagged item; the hired contractor must call 811 in any case). Equipment-lessor exemption confirmed. Exact current wording of 4216.8 not seen in full.

rules.title: Required 811 clause in excavating equipment rental agreements
rules.plain_english: A company renting power excavating or boring equipment to a licensed contractor is exempt from 811 duties only if the signed rental agreement contains the statutory clause placing 811 responsibility on the renter. Rental contract generators should insert it verbatim.

parameters.clause_text: “It is the sole responsibility of the lessee or renter to follow the requirements of the regional notification center law pursuant to Article 2 (commencing with Section 4216) of Chapter 3.1 of Division 5 of Title 1 of the Government Code. By signing this contract, the lessee or renter accepts all liabilities and responsibilities contained in the regional notification center law.”

rules.applies_to: Equipment rental companies; contractors renting excavators/boring rigs
rules.source: PDF page 85 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: “It is the sole responsibility of the lessee or renter to follow the requirements of the regional notification center law pursuant to Article 2 (commencing with Section 4216) of Chapter 3.1 of Division 5 of Title 1 of the Government Code. By signing this contract, the lessee or renter accepts all liabilities and responsibilities contained in the regional notification center law.”
rules.correction: Lessor exemption and the gist of the clause appear in leginfo bill text, but the exact current codified wording of the required rental-agreement provision was not visible (SB 119 is described as rewording it). Use the Law Book text only after checking current 4216.8 on leginfo.

rules.title: Dig-law penalties: $10,000 negligent / $50,000 willful / $100,000 pipeline
rules.plain_english: Negligent violation of the 811 law carries a civil penalty of up to $10,000; knowing and willful violation up to $50,000; knowing and willful violation that damages a gas or hazardous liquid pipeline and releases flammable, toxic or corrosive gas or liquid up to $100,000. Excavators also face third-party damage claims and CSLB discipline.

parameters.enforcing_body: California Underground Facilities Safe Excavation Board (Dig Safe Board) for most persons since 2020-07-01; CSLB may also discipline licensees

rules.applies_to: Excavators and operators
rules.source: PDF page 86-87 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Any operator or excavator who negligently violates any portion of Government Code sections 4216–4216.9 is subject to a fine not to exceed $10,000.
rules.notes: Same section: "Any operator or excavator who knowingly and willfully violates any portion of Government Code sections 4216–4216.9 is subject to a fine not to exceed $50,000." (p. 86) and the $100,000 pipeline penalty (p. 87). Also on cslb.ca.gov Failure to Contact page. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: Amounts confirmed ($10,000 / $50,000 / $100,000), but the statute imposes them as civil penalties ("subject to a civil penalty in an amount not to exceed ..."), not criminal fines; the Dig Safe Board enforces for most excavators (since July 1, 2020). Added penalty_type and reworded plain_english.

rules.title: Which 811 center serves the job (USA North vs DigAlert)
rules.plain_english: USA North 811 (usanorth811.org) serves Northern California and Nevada; USA South / DigAlert (digalert.org) serves Imperial, Inyo, Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino, San Diego, Santa Barbara and Ventura counties. Both are reached by dialing 811.
rules.applies_to: Excavators routing ticket requests
rules.citation: Gov Code 4216(n) (regional notification center); CSLB Law Book Ch. 4
rules.source: PDF page 87 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Underground Service Alert of Southern California: 811 www.digalert.org Serves the following counties in Southern California: Imperial, Inyo, Los Angeles, Orange, Riverside, San Bernardino, San Diego, Santa Barbara, and Ventura
rules.notes: County lists as printed in the 2026 law book (58 counties total).

rules.title: Caltrans encroachment permit for work in state highway right-of-way
rules.plain_english: Anyone other than a Caltrans contractor must get a Caltrans encroachment permit before any work or activity within, under or over the state highway right-of-way (driveways, utility cuts, staging, traffic control, landscaping). Caltrans must approve or deny within 60 days of a complete application (not complete until CEQA and other requirements are met); if it does not notify the applicant of a denial within that period, the permit is deemed approved.

parameters.permit_required_for: any activity within, under, or over state highway right-of-way
parameters.clock_starts: complete application as determined by Caltrans, incl. CEQA compliance

rules.applies_to: Contractors, utilities, developers working in state highway right-of-way
rules.quote: The department shall either approve or deny an application from an applicant for an encroachment permit within 60 days of receiving a completed application, as determined by the department.
rules.notes: dot.ca.gov blocked; text from search excerpts. City/county streets require a separate local encroachment/street-opening permit (rules vary; not researched). USA ticket needed before digging in any right-of-way. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: 60-day approve/deny rule and CEQA-completeness condition confirmed, but the rule omitted the consequence: if Caltrans does not notify the applicant of denial within 60 days, the permit is deemed approved (S&H 671.5(a)). Broadband applications have a separate 30-day completeness notice (deemed complete if not flagged). Parameters and plain_english updated.

rules.title: Human remains found: stop work and call the coroner
rules.plain_english: If human remains are discovered anywhere other than a dedicated cemetery, stop all work at the site and nearby areas immediately and contact the county coroner. The coroner has two working days to examine; if remains are Native American, the coroner notifies the Native American Heritage Commission within 24 hours, which notifies the most likely descendant, who has 24 hours to recommend treatment.

immediate_actions: stop all work at site and nearby area
parameters.dispute_resolution: NAHC mediation; else reinter on property in area not subject to further disturbance

rules.applies_to: All excavating contractors and owners
rules.citation: Health & Safety Code 7050.5; Public Resources Code 5097.9-5097.991
rules.source: PDF page 88 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: The coroner has two working days to examine the remains after being notified by the person responsible for the excavation. If the remains are Native American, the coroner has 24 hours to notify the Native American Heritage Commission.
rules.notes: Step 1 on same page: "Stop all work immediately at that site and any nearby area reasonably suspected to have remains and contact the county coroner."

rules.title: Obtaining or possessing remains or artifacts taken from Native American graves, or removing remains to sell or dissect, or with malice, is a felony
rules.plain_english: Knowingly or willfully obtaining or possessing Native American remains or artifacts taken from a Native American grave or cairn (after 1984), or removing remains from a grave with intent to sell or dissect or with malice, is a felony punishable under Penal Code 1170(h). Stop work and follow the coroner/NAHC procedure on any discovery.

parameters.punishment: imprisonment pursuant to Penal Code 1170(h) (realignment; generally county jail)
covered_conduct: knowingly or willfully obtaining or possessing Native American artifacts or human remains taken from a Native American grave or cairn after 1984-01-01 (PRC 5097.99(b))
removing Native American remains from a grave or cairn with intent to sell or dissect, or with malice or wantonness (PRC 5097.99(c))

rules.applies_to: All persons on construction sites
rules.source: PDF page 89 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book; https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displayText.xhtml?lawCode=PRC&division=5.&chapter=1.75. (Pub. Res. Code 5097.99, via search excerpt of AB 109 (2011) bill text)
rules.quote: is guilty of a felony which is punishable by imprisonment pursuant to subdivision (h) of Section 1170 of the Penal Code
rules.notes: Law Book (CSLB summary) says: "Any person who knowingly or willfully removes, obtains, or possesses any Native American remains or associated burial artifacts, without authority of law, is guilty of a felony, punishable by imprisonment in state prison." That predates 2011 realignment wording. Quote above is the statutory punishment clause as shown in a leginfo search excerpt of AB 109 (2011) amending 5097.99; full current section text not fetched (leginfo HTTP 403).
rules.correction: Not "imprisonment in state prison": since AB 109 (2011) the felony in PRC 5097.99(b)-(c) is punishable by imprisonment pursuant to Penal Code 1170(h) (realignment; generally county jail). Also the statute is narrower than the Law Book summary: (b) covers knowingly or willfully obtaining or possessing Native American artifacts or human remains taken from a Native American grave or cairn after January 1, 1984 (except as allowed by law or a 5097.94/5097.98 agreement); (c) covers removing remains from a grave or cairn with intent to sell or dissect, or with malice or wantonness. Parameters, plain_english and quote updated. Rewording 2026-11-27: title reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: C-57 license required for water, monitoring and geothermal wells
rules.plain_english: Only a person holding a C-57 Water Well Contractor license may dig, bore, drill, deepen, reperforate, abandon or destroy a water well, cathodic protection well, groundwater monitoring well, or geothermal heat exchange well. Many county environmental health departments also require a well permit and fee.

parameters.local_permit: often required by county environmental health

rules.applies_to: Well drilling and geothermal contractors
rules.source: PDF page 90 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: No person shall undertake to dig, bore, or drill a water well, cathodic protection well, groundwater monitoring well, or geothermal heat exchange well, to deepen or reperforate such a well, or to abandon or destroy such a well, unless the person responsible for that construction, alteration, destruction, or abandonment possesses a C-57 Water Well Contractor’s License.
rules.notes: Local well permit statement on PDF p. 91: "Many of these local agencies require permits for any work on a well and charge a fee for that permit."

rules.title: File DWR Well Completion Report within 60 days
rules.plain_english: Whoever constructs, alters or destroys a water, cathodic protection, monitoring or geothermal heat exchange well must file a Well Completion Report (DWR 188) with the Department of Water Resources within 60 days after completing the work, online through OSWCR. Failure to file is a misdemeanor and grounds for CSLB discipline.

parameters.filing_system: OSWCR (Online System of Well Completion Reports)

rules.applies_to: C-57 contractors and others constructing/altering/destroying wells
rules.source: PDF page 90 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: file a report of completion, called the “Well Completion Report, DWR 188,” with the California Department of Water Resources (DWR) within 60 days after completion of the work.

rules.title: HIC: Schedule of Progress Payments required (dollars and cents, tied to work)
rules.plain_english: If a home improvement contract calls for any payment other than the downpayment before the job is done, it must include a 'Schedule of Progress Payments' in which every payment is a dollar-and-cents amount tied to a specific phase of work, services or materials. The schedule section must also carry the required bold warning statement.

parameters.trigger: any payment other than the downpayment is due before project completion
parameters.heading: Schedule of Progress Payments
each_payment_must_reference: amount of work or services to be performed
materials and equipment to be supplied
parameters.required_statement_text: The schedule of progress payments must specifically describe each phase of work, including the type and amount of work or services scheduled to be supplied in each phase, along with the amount of each proposed progress payment. IT IS AGAINST THE LAW FOR A CONTRACTOR TO COLLECT PAYMENT FOR WORK NOT YET COMPLETED, OR FOR MATERIALS NOT YET DELIVERED. HOWEVER, A CONTRACTOR MAY REQUIRE A DOWNPAYMENT.
parameters.exempt_if: contractor furnishes bonds/joint control per B&P 7159.5(a)(8)

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts (aggregate price over $500) between a contractor and a residential owner or tenant
rules.source: PDF page 400 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book; PDF page 410 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (A) A schedule of progress payments shall be preceded by the heading: “Schedule of Progress Payments.” (B) Each progress payment shall be stated in dollars and cents and specifically reference the amount of work or services to be performed and materials and equipment to be supplied.
rules.notes: This is the HIC equivalent of a schedule of values: a tool can generate it from SOV lines but each line must be a dollar amount tied to described work. B&P 7159.5(a)(4) independently requires the schedule in dollars and cents whenever payments precede completion.
rules.correction: None. Quote and required-statement text match PDF p.400 (an automated string match missed only because the page footer "Section VI" splits the sentence).

rules.title: HIC: never request or accept payment exceeding work performed or material delivered
rules.plain_english: Apart from the downpayment, a home improvement contractor may not ask for or take any payment that is more than the value of the work actually done or materials actually delivered. This also applies to advance payments from a lender or financing company.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors (general or specialty), their agents and salespersons
rules.source: PDF page 410 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (5) Except for a downpayment, the contractor shall neither request nor accept payment that exceeds the value of the work performed or material delivered. The prohibition prescribed by this paragraph extends to advance payment in whole or in part from any lender or financier for the performance or sale of home improvement goods or services.
rules.notes: For a pay-app tool: block any HIC billing line where billed-to-date exceeds percent complete x scheduled value, and do not bill AIA-style 'materials presently stored' unless the material has been delivered (interpretation: stored off-site material is not 'delivered'). CSLB's Nov 3, 2026 Legislative Committee packet lists 'unlawful payment provisions that require payments that exceed value of work performed' and up-front lender payments as key current enforcement concerns.

rules.title: HIC downpayment: lesser of $1,000 or 10% of contract price
rules.plain_english: A home improvement downpayment can be no more than $1,000 or 10% of the contract price, whichever is less, and the contract must show it under a 'Downpayment' heading with the required bold statement.

parameters.heading: Downpayment
parameters.required_statement_text: THE DOWNPAYMENT MAY NOT EXCEED $1,000 OR 10 PERCENT OF THE CONTRACT PRICE, WHICHEVER IS LESS.

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts
rules.source: PDF page 410 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book; PDF page 400 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (3) If a downpayment will be charged, the downpayment shall not exceed one thousand dollars ($1,000) or 10 percent of the contract amount, whichever amount is less.
rules.notes: Violation of 7159.5(a)(3) is a misdemeanor (7159.5(b)(1)). Swimming pool contracts have their own rules (B&P 7167) not covered here.
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: HIC contract price in dollars and cents, all-in; finance charge separate
rules.plain_english: The home improvement contract must state the agreed price in dollars and cents under the heading 'Contract Price', and that price must include everything (profit, labor, materials). Any finance charge must be shown separately under 'Finance Charge'.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts
rules.source: PDF page 410 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book; PDF page 399 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book-400
rules.quote: (1) The contract shall be in writing and shall include the agreed contract amount in dollars and cents. The contract amount shall include the entire cost of the contract, including profit, labor, and materials, but excluding finance charges.
rules.notes: Original contract sum on a pay application (G702 line 1) for an HIC should equal this figure. 7159.5(a)(2): a separate finance charge 'shall be set out separately from the contract amount.'
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: HIC progress payments must add up to contract price minus downpayment
rules.plain_english: CSLB's worksheet: take the total contract price, subtract the downpayment, and the sum of all progress payments in the schedule should equal what is left. Each payment is due when its phase of work is complete.

parameters.each_payment_due: on completion of the listed work or service

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors preparing a Schedule of Progress Payments
rules.quote: Amount of Progress Payments = $ (This should equal the figure in Line #3 above)
rules.notes: Official CSLB guide (read in full PDF), not statute text. Line #3 on the worksheet is 'Amount Remaining to be Billed to Customer (Subtract Line #2 from Line #1 above)', i.e., contract price minus downpayment. The guide also says the worksheet 'should NOT be included with the contract.' Guide PDF metadata shows it was last modified in 2020, so it does not reflect 2021+ notice changes (e.g., the LLC CGL option).

rules.title: Allowance overruns/underruns change the price only by written change order
rules.plain_english: If the contract price includes allowances for items not yet selected, and the final cost is more or less than the allowance, the contract price goes up or down through a written change order. CSLB's sample says allowances include overhead, profit and sales tax.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts using allowances (good practice for any contract)
rules.citation: CSLB guidance; ties to B&P 7159.6 (change order contents)
rules.quote: If the final cost of any item covered by the allowance is more or less than the dollar amount listed, the Contract Price will be increased or decreased by a written change order from the Contractor.
rules.notes: Sample contract language from the official CSLB guide, not a statute. The change order must still meet B&P 7159.6 and be signed before the covered work starts.

rules.title: Bonded/joint-control HIC contractors exempt from downpayment and progress-payment limits
rules.plain_english: A home improvement contractor that furnishes a full performance and payment bond, lien and completion bond, registrar-approved bond equivalent, or joint control covering full performance and payment is exempt from the downpayment cap, the schedule-of-payments rule and the no-payment-ahead-of-work rule, and may take payment before completion.

exempt_from: B&P 7159.5(a)(5) no payment ahead of work

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contractors
rules.source: PDF page 411 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (8) A contractor furnishing a performance and payment bond, lien and completion bond, or a bond equivalent or joint control approved by the registrar covering full performance and payment is exempt from paragraphs (3), (4), and (5), and need not include, as part of the contract, the statement regarding the downpayment
rules.notes: Blanket bond application refers to 16 CCR 858.2 as it read on January 1, 2016.
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: HIC salesperson commission paid pro rata with contractor's payments
rules.plain_english: If a salesperson's commission comes out of the contract price, it must be paid out in proportion to the payments the contractor actually receives under the payment schedule, not up front.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts that pay a salesperson's commission from the contract price
rules.source: PDF page 411 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (7) If the contract provides for a payment of a salesperson’s commission out of the contract price, that payment shall be made on a pro rata basis in proportion to the schedule of payments made to the contractor by the disbursing party in accordance with paragraph (4).
rules.notes: Formula is an arithmetic reading of 'pro rata basis in proportion to the schedule of payments'.
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: HIC payment violations are misdemeanors ($100-$5,000 fine, up to 1 year jail)
rules.plain_english: Violating the written-contract/price rule, the downpayment cap, or the no-payment-ahead-of-work rule on a home improvement job is a misdemeanor: a fine of $100 to $5,000, up to a year in county jail, or both. In a declared disaster area the court must impose the maximum fine.

parameters.filing_deadline_trigger: date of contract, or if not in writing, date buyer makes first payment

rules.applies_to: Licensees and persons required to be licensed, their agents and salespersons
rules.source: PDF page 411 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book-412
rules.quote: (b) (1) A violation of paragraph (1), (3), or (5) of subdivision (a) by a licensee or a person subject to be licensed under this chapter, or by their agent or salesperson, is a misdemeanor punishable by a fine of not less than one hundred dollars ($100) nor more than five thousand dollars ($5,000), or by imprisonment in a county jail not exceeding one year, or by both that fine and imprisonment.
rules.notes: Any violation of 7159.5(a) is also cause for CSLB discipline. 7159.5(c): fraud schemes after natural disasters add full restitution and a fine of $500-$25,000.
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: Schedule of values / continuation sheet (G703-style) math
rules.plain_english: Break the contract sum into line items whose scheduled values add up exactly to the contract sum. Each period, for every line: work completed to date = previous + this period + materials presently stored; percent complete = completed to date / scheduled value; balance to finish = scheduled value - completed to date; retainage = retention rate x completed to date (or per line if rates vary).

columns.D: work completed from previous application (D+E of prior app)
columns.F: materials presently stored (not in D or E)
columns.G: total completed and stored to date = D + E + F

checks: G <= C for each line (no overbilling a line)
change orders added as new SOV lines or adjusted lines when approved
ca_overlays: HIC: no billing beyond work performed/material delivered (B&P 7159.5(a)(5))
retention caps: private 5% for contracts on/after 2026-01-01 (Civ. Code 8811), public 5% (PCC 7201)

rules.applies_to: GCs and subcontractors preparing progress billings on any project (AIA, ConsensusDocs or owner forms)
rules.citation: Industry practice (AIA G703-style continuation sheet); no statute prescribes this form
rules.source: Industry practice; no official source fetched
rules.notes: Standard construction-management practice, not a legal requirement; not read from any primary legal text. AIA G702/G703 are copyrighted forms; the column logic above is the widely used structure, described from general knowledge, not copied from the form. Owners and lenders often impose their own SOV rules (e.g., front-loading limits, separate general conditions line).

rules.title: Application for payment (G702-style) summary math
rules.plain_english: The pay application summary rolls up the SOV: original contract sum + net change orders = contract sum to date; total completed and stored to date minus retainage = total earned less retainage; subtract previous certificates for payment to get the current payment due; balance to finish including retainage = contract sum to date - total earned less retainage.

lines.2: net change by change orders (approved only)
lines.4: total completed and stored to date (sum of SOV column G)
lines.5a: retainage on completed work = rate x (D+E)
lines.5b: retainage on stored material = rate x F
lines.7: less previous certificates for payment (line 6 of prior certificate)

parameters.change_order_summary: track additions and deductions approved in previous months vs. this month
attachments_commonly_required: conditional progress lien waivers from GC and paid subs/suppliers
unconditional waivers for the prior payment
parameters.payment_due_trigger: direct contractor's notice demanding payment under the contract (Civ. Code 8800, unless otherwise agreed in writing)

rules.applies_to: GCs, subs, owners, lenders and architects processing progress payments
rules.citation: Industry practice (AIA G702-style); Civil Code 8800 for private-owner payment timing
rules.source: Industry practice; no official source fetched
rules.notes: Standard construction-management practice, not a legal requirement; not read from any primary legal text. leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be fetched from this environment (Cloudflare 403 via curl; host not allowed for WebFetch) and the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted, so the statute text was NOT read. The 30-day Civil Code 8800 figure is taken from companion research (web_lien-payment.json, itself based on a search excerpt) and was not independently verified here. For HIC jobs, line 4 cannot include materials not yet delivered and stored-material retainage generally does not arise.

rules.title: Change order log drives the contract sum to date
rules.plain_english: Keep a numbered change order log (pending, approved, rejected). Only approved, fully signed change orders change the contract sum and the SOV; pending or proposed changes are tracked separately so the pay app never bills unapproved work.

parameters.check: work_start_date of CO >= latest signature date (HIC: B&P 7159(d), 7159.6)

rules.applies_to: All projects
rules.citation: Industry practice; legal content requirements in B&P 7159.6 for home improvement
rules.source: Industry practice; no official source fetched
rules.notes: Standard construction-management practice, not a legal requirement; not read from any primary legal text. Statutory change-order content for home improvement is in hic-change-order-required-contents.

rules.title: Percentage-of-completion revenue; costs vs. billings (WIP)
rules.plain_english: On long jobs, revenue and profit can be recognized by percent complete (e.g., 50% done = 50% of estimated revenue and profit earned). Comparing earned revenue with amounts billed shows over-billing (billings in excess of costs/earnings) or under-billing (costs in excess of billings).

parameters.under_billing: earned_revenue - billings_to_date (if positive; 'costs in excess of billings')
parameters.alternative_method: completed contract method (recognize all at completion)

rules.applies_to: Contractors' job-cost accounting and WIP schedules
rules.citation: Accounting practice described in CSLB Law Book Ch. 3 (no statute)
rules.source: PDF page 51 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: 1) The percentage of completion method will report profits and losses regularly based on work accomplished on each job. For example, if the work performed each year is estimated to represent 50 percent of total performance under contract, then 50 percent of the total estimated revenue and profit is considered earned.
rules.notes: Quote is from the CSLB Law Book's non-binding business-management guidance chapter (official publication, but guidance, not law), so it is marked as a practice item. The cost-to-cost and over/under-billing formulas are standard accounting practice, not from the Law Book (its sample balance sheet on PDF page 53 shows a 'Costs or contracts in excess of billings' line). Tax method elections are governed by IRS rules not covered here.

rules.title: Retention defined (Law Book still says 'usually 10 percent' - outdated for new private contracts)
rules.plain_english: Retention is money held back from each progress payment until the job is completed and accepted; it is earned but unpaid. The Law Book says 'usually 10 percent', but private contracts entered on or after January 1, 2026 are capped at 5% (with exceptions) and public works are capped at 5%.
rules.applies_to: All contractors and owners
rules.citation: CSLB Law Book Ch. 3 guidance; Civil Code 8811 (SB 61, Stats 2025 ch 49); PCC 7201
rules.source: PDF page 54 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book; PDF page 61 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Retention: A specified amount, usually 10 percent, withheld from progress payments to the contractor pending satisfactory completion and final acceptance of the project. You have already earned this amount even though you have not yet been paid.
rules.notes: Quote is from the CSLB Law Book's non-binding business-management guidance chapter (official publication, but guidance, not law), so it is marked as a practice item. CONFLICT: the 2026 Law Book's business chapter (PDF pages 54, 61-62) still describes 10% retention and 'the final 10 percent upon completion and expiration of the lien period'. Do not default a calculator to 10% for private contracts entered on/after 2026-01-01 unless an SB 61 exemption applies (see private-retention-5pct-cap and private-retention-cap-exemptions).

rules.title: Private works retention capped at 5% (contracts entered on/after 1/1/2026)
rules.plain_english: On private jobs under contracts signed on or after January 1, 2026, retention held from any payment (owner to GC, GC to sub, sub to sub-tier) cannot exceed 5% of the payment, total retention cannot exceed 5% of the contract price, and a subcontract cannot use a higher retention percentage than the owner-GC contract. The winner of a lawsuit to enforce this gets attorney's fees.

parameters.attorney_fees: court must award reasonable fees to prevailing party in enforcement action

rules.applies_to: Owners, direct contractors and subcontractors on private works of improvement (see exemptions)
rules.citation: Civil Code 8811(b)(1), (c) (added by SB 61, Stats 2025 ch 49)
rules.source: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/BoardPackets/2025/Sept5Packet_Electronic.pdf (PDF page 109; CSLB Board Packet Sept 5, 2025, bill analysis of SB 61)
rules.quote: 1) Provides that a retention payment withheld from a payment by an owner from the prime or direct contractor (contractor with a contract with the property owner) by the direct contractor from any subcontractor, or from any subcontractor from another subcontractor shall not exceed 5 percent of the payment received;
rules.notes: Read from CSLB's official bill analysis (Chapter 49, Statutes of 2025; 'has been signed into law by the Governor, effective January 1, 2026'), not from the codified Civil Code text, which could not be fetched. Item 2 of the analysis: 'the total retention proceeds withheld shall not exceed 5 percent of the contract price'. The calc formula is an arithmetic reading. Civil Code section number (8811) per companion research; verify. Contracts entered before 2026 keep their agreed retention (subject to other law). [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: Citation fix: SB 61 (Ch. 49, Stats 2025) ADDED Civil Code 8811 (bill title: "An act to add Section 8811 to the Civil Code"); it did not amend an existing section. The leginfo excerpts place the 5% per-payment cap, the 5% total cap and the flow-down limit in 8811(b)(1), and the mandatory prevailing-party fee award in 8811(c). They also state it applies to contracts for a private work of improvement entered into on or after 2026-01-01. The quote and every parameter match the re-fetched CSLB analysis (items 1-3, 6-7). The codified text was seen only as search excerpts.

rules.title: Exemptions from the private 5% retention cap
rules.plain_english: The 5% private retention cap does not apply (1) where the contractor gave the subcontractor written notice, before or when bids were requested, that a performance and payment bond would be required and the subcontractor then fails to furnish one from an admitted surety insurer, or (2) to residential projects that are not mixed-use and are four stories or less.

parameters.exemption_sub_bond_failure: contractor gave written notice, before or at the time the bid was requested, that a performance and payment bond is required, AND the subcontractor fails to furnish a bond issued by an admitted surety insurer
parameters.test: cap_applies = contract_date >= 2026-01-01 and not (residential and not mixed_use and stories <= 4) and not (bond_required_notice_given_before_or_at_bid_request and sub_failed_to_furnish_admitted_surety_bond)

rules.applies_to: Private works retention calculations
rules.citation: Civil Code 8811(b)(2)-(3) (added by SB 61, Stats 2025 ch 49)
rules.source: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/BoardPackets/2025/Sept5Packet_Electronic.pdf (PDF page 109; CSLB Board Packet Sept 5, 2025, bill analysis of SB 61)
rules.quote: 4) Exempts these requirements if the subcontractor fails to comply with contract terms requiring a performance and payment bond issued by an admitted surety insurer. 5) Exempts these requirements from an owner, director, or subcontractor on a residential project if the project is not mixed-use and does not exceed four stories.
rules.notes: 'director' in the CSLB analysis is presumably a typo for 'direct contractor'. Read from CSLB bill analysis, not codified text. Companion research notes secondary sources mention other carve-outs (e.g., contract size) that are NOT confirmed; do not apply them without reading Civil Code 8811. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: The bond exemption is narrower than the CSLB summary. Two leginfo excerpts of the chaptered text, 8811(b)(2), say the cap is lifted only where the contractor gave the subcontractor written notice, before or at the time the bid is requested, that a performance and payment bond would be required, and the subcontractor then fails to furnish a bond from an admitted surety insurer. This mirrors PCC 7201(b)(2). Added that prerequisite, which narrows the exemption. The residential exemption (not mixed-use, four stories or less) is 8811(b)(3) and matches. Codified text seen only as search excerpts; verify the exact wording before encoding.

rules.title: Owner pays retention to direct contractor within 45 days after completion
rules.plain_english: On a private job, an owner that withheld retention must pay it to the direct contractor within 45 days after the work of improvement is completed.

parameters.trigger: completion of the work of improvement
