rules.applies_to: Owners of private works
rules.citation: Civil Code 8812 (pre-existing law; summarized in SB 61 analysis)
rules.source: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/BoardPackets/2025/Sept5Packet_Electronic.pdf (PDF page 109; CSLB Board Packet Sept 5, 2025, bill analysis of SB 61)-110
rules.quote: Existing law requires an owner to pay a retention to a direct contractor within 45 days after completion of the
rules.notes: Read from CSLB's official bill analysis (sentence spans PDF pages 109-110), not codified text. 'Completion' for retention purposes may have its own statutory definition (e.g., actual completion, occupation/use with cessation, acceptance, cessation of labor) - verify in Civ. Code 8180/8800 article. Dispute withholding (up to 150% of disputed amount) per companion research, not verified here.
rules.correction: None. Excerpt of 8812(a): "If an owner withholds a retention from a direct contractor, the owner shall, within 45 days after completion of the work of improvement, pay the retention to the contractor." Codified text seen only as excerpts.

rules.title: Direct contractor passes retention to subs within 10 days
rules.plain_english: On a private job, the direct contractor must pay each subcontractor from whom retention was withheld its share within 10 days after the direct contractor receives all or part of a retention payment. In a good-faith dispute it may withhold no more than 150% of the estimated value of the disputed amount.

parameters.trigger_statute_excerpt: direct contractor's receipt of all or part of a retention payment
parameters.trigger_cslb_summary: completion of the work of improvement (CSLB paraphrase; superseded by statute text)
parameters.payee: each subcontractor from whom retention was withheld
parameters.trigger: direct contractor's receipt of all or part of a retention payment
parameters.max_withhold_good_faith_dispute: 150% of the estimated value of the disputed amount (Civ. Code 8814(c))

rules.applies_to: Direct contractors (and subs paying sub-tiers) on private works
rules.source: https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=CIV&sectionNum=8814 (seen via search excerpts); https://courts.ca.gov/opinions/archive/S231549.PDF; https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/BoardPackets/2025/Sept5Packet_Electronic.pdf (PDF page 110; CSLB Board Packet Sept 5, 2025, bill analysis of SB 61)
rules.quote: The direct contractor shall, within 10 days after receiving all or part of a retention payment, pay to each subcontractor from whom retention has been withheld that subcontractor's share of the payment.
rules.notes: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be fetched from this environment (Cloudflare 403 via curl; host not allowed for WebFetch) and the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted, so the statute text was NOT read. The CSLB analysis (read) says 'for a direct contractor to pay a retention to a subcontractor within 10 days after completion of the work of improvement', but the leginfo search excerpt cited in web_lien-payment.json reads 'within 10 days after receiving all or part of a retention payment'. Trigger therefore unverified; marked false. Public works pass-through is different (PCC 7107(d), 7 days per companion research). [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: The trigger is the direct contractor's receipt of retention, not completion. 8814(a) as quoted: "The direct contractor shall, within 10 days after receiving all or part of a retention payment, pay to each subcontractor from whom retention has been withheld that subcontractor's share of the payment." CSLB's "after completion" wording is a loose paraphrase. The old conservative_calc (min(completion, receipt) + 10 days) could set a due date before the contractor had been paid and is removed. Added the 8814(c) good-faith dispute limit (150% of the estimated value of the disputed amount). Plain_english, quote, source and parameters updated.

rules.title: Retention math on each pay application
rules.plain_english: Compute retention each period as the retention rate times the work completed (and stored materials, if retained) this period, stop when the total hits the contract cap, and release it at completion after deducting no more than the legally allowed amount for genuine disputes.

parameters.waiver_note: statutory progress waivers do not waive retention (exception (1) on the progress waiver forms)

rules.applies_to: All projects with retention
rules.citation: Practice; caps/timelines per Civil Code 8811-8814 and PCC 7107/7201
rules.source: Industry practice; legal figures from other rules in this file
rules.notes: Standard construction-management practice, not a legal requirement; not read from any primary legal text. Public 60-day release and 150% dispute figures come from companion research based on leginfo search excerpts (not verified here). Some owners reduce retention to a lower rate at 50% completion by contract; that is contractual, not statutory.

rules.title: Public works retention capped at 5%
rules.plain_english: On California public works contracts (entered on or after 2012-01-01), retention may not exceed 5% of any payment or 5% of the contract price in total, and subcontract retention may not exceed the prime-contract percentage. Exceptions: (a) a subcontractor that was told in writing before or at the bid request that bonds are required and then cannot or will not furnish an admitted-surety performance and payment bond; (b) a project the agency found "substantially complex" before bid, with the basis and actual retention stated in the bid documents (local agencies: finding approved at a noticed public hearing). No party may require a waiver.

parameters.exception: pre-bid finding that the project is substantially complex, with basis and actual retention amount stated in bid documents (local agencies: finding approved project-by-project at a properly noticed, normally scheduled public hearing)
parameters.exception_sub_bond_failure: contractor gave written notice (PCC 4108(c)) before or at bid request that bonds are required, and subcontractor is unable or refuses to furnish an admitted-surety performance and payment bond
parameters.does_not_limit: withholding 150% of disputed amounts from final payment under PCC 7107(c)

rules.applies_to: Public entities, prime contractors and subcontractors on public works
rules.citation: Public Contract Code 7201(a)-(c) (sunset removed by AB 2173, 2022)
rules.quote: (b) (1) The retention proceeds withheld from any payment by a public entity from the original contractor, by the original contractor from any subcontractor, and by a subcontractor from any subcontractor thereunder shall not exceed 5 percent of the payment. In no event shall the total retention proceeds withheld exceed 5 percent of the contract price.
rules.effective: Contracts entered on or after 2012-01-01; operative indefinitely per AB 2173 (2022)
rules.notes: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be fetched from this environment (Cloudflare 403 via curl; host not allowed for WebFetch) and the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted, so the statute text was NOT read. Figures consistent with CSLB's SB 61 analysis (PDF page 110), which refers to 'the existing 5 percent retention cap for public works projects', and with companion research web_lien-payment.json (search excerpt). Details of exceptions not verified. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: Figures confirmed: 5% of each payment, 5% of the contract price in total, and a flow-down limit to the prime-contract percentage (7201(b)(1)). Corrections: (1) An exception was missing. The cap does not apply if the contractor gave written notice under PCC 4108(c), before or at the bid request, that bonds are required, and the subcontractor is unable or refuses to furnish a performance and payment bond from an admitted surety (7201(b)(2)). (2) The substantially-complex exception needs a pre-bid finding plus bid documents stating the basis and the actual retention amount. Local agencies must approve the finding project by project at a properly noticed, normally scheduled public hearing. The finding must explain why the project is unique (7201(b)(3)-(5)). (3) The 2022 text was due to sunset on 2023-01-01. AB 2173 (2022) made the provisions operative indefinitely, per a leginfo excerpt of its digest. Also: 7201 does not limit the 150% withholding of disputed amounts from final payment under PCC 7107(c), and no party may require a waiver (7201(c)). The current post-AB 2173 text was not read in full.

rules.title: Public entity releases retention within 60 days after completion
rules.plain_english: On public works, the public entity must release retention to the original contractor within 60 days after completion, subject to withholding up to 150% of disputed amounts; the prime then has a short deadline to pass retention through to subs.

parameters.trigger: completion of the work of improvement

rules.applies_to: Public entities and prime contractors on public works
rules.notes: leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be fetched from this environment (Cloudflare 403 via curl; host not allowed for WebFetch) and the session's WebSearch budget was exhausted, so the statute text was NOT read. Figures taken from companion research (web_lien-payment.json rules pcc-7107-*), which relied on search excerpts; verify before use.
rules.correction: None for the encoded figures. Excerpts of 7107 show release within 60 days after completion (c), withholding up to 150% of the disputed amount from final payment (c), pass-through to subs "within seven days from the time that all or any portion of the retention proceeds are received by the original contractor" (d), and a 2% per month charge in lieu of interest (f). FLAG (not applied): one excerpt also describes a 90-day release period for a state agency that retains no more than 125% of the estimated value of work yet to be completed. A deadline tool should not flag a state agency as late between day 61 and day 90 until 7107(c) is read. Statute text seen only as excerpts.

rules.title: Pay subcontractors within 7 days of receiving a progress payment
rules.plain_english: A prime contractor (or sub) must pay each subcontractor its share within 7 days after receiving each progress payment unless otherwise agreed in writing. In a good-faith dispute it may hold back no more than 150% of the disputed amount; late payment costs 2% per month plus attorney's fees.

parameters.trigger: receipt of each progress payment
parameters.scope: all private and public works except where PCC 10262 applies

rules.applies_to: Licensed prime contractors and subcontractors paying subcontractors
rules.source: PDF page 349 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: In the event that there is a good faith dispute over all or any portion of the amount due on a progress payment from the prime contractor or subcontractor to a subcontractor, the prime contractor or subcontractor may withhold no more than 150 percent of the disputed amount.
rules.notes: (a) first sentence: 'A prime contractor or subcontractor shall pay to any subcontractor, not later than seven days after receipt of each progress payment, unless otherwise agreed to in writing, the respective amounts allowed the contractor on account of the work performed by the subcontractors'. (b): violation is cause for discipline and 'a penalty, payable to the subcontractor, of 2 percent of the amount due per month for every month that payment is not made.' Duplicates bp-7108-5-* rules in web_lien-payment.json.
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: Discipline for not paying suppliers/subs after receiving funds
rules.plain_english: A contractor who willfully fails to pay for materials or services when due, while able to pay or after being paid for that work, or who falsely denies the debt to get a discount or delay payment, can be disciplined by CSLB.

elements: willful or deliberate failure to pay money when due
for materials or services on contractor's operations
contractor had capacity to pay OR received sufficient funds for that work
parameters.also_prohibited: false denial of amount due or claim validity to obtain a discount or hinder/delay/defraud

rules.applies_to: All licensees, their agents and officers
rules.source: PDF page 358 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Wilful or deliberate failure by any licensee or agent or officer thereof to pay any moneys, when due for any materials or services rendered in connection with his operations as a contractor, when he has the capacity to pay or when he has received sufficient funds therefor as payment for the particular construction work, project, or operation
rules.notes: A pay-app tool can flag: owner payment received for line items whose subs/suppliers remain unpaid past due dates.

rules.title: Project funds must be applied to that project and accounted for
rules.plain_english: Money received for a specific project (or a specific purpose on a project) must be used for it; diverting it, or failing to substantially account for how it was used, is grounds for CSLB discipline.

parameters.requirement: track receipts and disbursements by project and by purpose
parameters.violation: diversion or failure substantially to account

rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.source: PDF page 349 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Diversion of funds or property received for prosecution or completion of a specific construction project or operation, or for a specified purpose in the prosecution or completion of any construction project or operation, or failure substantially to account for the application or use of such funds or property
rules.notes: Supports job-cost ledgers per project. The Law Book also cross-references Penal Code 484b (wrongful diversion of construction funds), not read.

rules.title: HIC change orders must be in writing and signed before the changed work starts
rules.plain_english: On a home improvement job, the contract must incorporate a change-order form, and a change becomes part of the contract only if it is written and signed by both parties before any of the changed or extra work begins.

parameters.timing: signed before commencement of any work covered by the change order

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts
rules.source: PDF page 398 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book-399
rules.quote: (5) A change-order form for changes or extra work shall be incorporated into the contract and shall become part of the contract only if it is in writing and signed by the parties prior to the commencement of any work covered by a change order.
rules.notes: 7159(d): 'A home improvement contract and any changes to the contract shall be in writing and signed by the parties to the contract prior to the commencement of work covered by the contract or an applicable change order'. CSLB lists 'Change orders not included' among common HIC problems (Law Book PDF page 36).

rules.title: Change order must state scope, price change, and effect on payments/completion
rules.plain_english: An extra work or change order on a home improvement job cannot be enforced against the buyer unless it states (1) the scope of the work, (2) the amount added to or subtracted from the contract, and (3) how it changes the progress payments or the completion date.

required_fields: scope of work encompassed by the order
amount to be added or subtracted from the contract
effect on progress payments or completion date

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts (buyer = owner or tenant)
rules.source: PDF page 412 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book-413
rules.quote: (a) An extra work or change order is not enforceable against a buyer unless the change order sets forth all of the following: (1) The scope of work encompassed by the order. (2) The amount to be added or subtracted from the contract. (3) The effect the order will make in the progress payments or the completion date.
rules.notes: Good template for any project's change order. Deductive (credit) changes are covered: 'added or subtracted'.

rules.title: Buyer cannot require extra/changed work without written authorization
rules.plain_english: A homeowner cannot make the contractor perform extra or change-order work unless the homeowner gives written authorization.
rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts
rules.source: PDF page 413 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (b) The buyer may not require a contractor to perform extra or change-order work without providing written authorization.
rules.notes: The contract notice in B&P 7159(e)(3)(A) adds the timing: authorization must come 'prior to the commencement of work covered by the new change order.'

rules.title: Defective change order does not bar recovery for work performed
rules.plain_english: If a change order does not meet the legal requirements, the contractor may still recover for work actually performed through legal or equitable remedies that prevent unjust enrichment.

parameters.remedy_basis: legal or equitable remedies designed to prevent unjust enrichment

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts
rules.source: PDF page 413 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (c) Failure to comply with the requirements of this section does not preclude the recovery of compensation for work performed based upon legal or equitable remedies designed to prevent unjust enrichment.
rules.notes: Recovery still requires a valid license at all times during performance (B&P 7031). Noncompliance remains cause for discipline under 7159.

rules.title: Required contract text: 'Note About Extra Work and Change Orders'
rules.plain_english: Every home improvement contract must include the heading 'Note About Extra Work and Change Orders' followed by the exact statutory statement about written, signed change orders.

parameters.heading: Note About Extra Work and Change Orders
parameters.statement_text: Extra Work and Change Orders become part of the contract once the order is prepared in writing and signed by the parties prior to the commencement of work covered by the new change order. The order must describe the scope of the extra work or change, the cost to be added or subtracted from the contract, and the effect the order will have on the schedule of progress payments.

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts
rules.source: PDF page 401 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: “Extra Work and Change Orders become part of the contract once the order is prepared in writing and signed by the parties prior to the commencement of work covered by the new change order. The order must describe the scope of the extra work or change, the cost to be added or subtracted from the contract, and the effect the order will have on the schedule of progress payments.”
rules.notes: Generate verbatim. Not required in the bonded form of contract only to the extent 7159.5(a)(8) excuses particular items (it does not list this one).
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: Required notice: performance of extra or change-order work
rules.plain_english: The contract must give the buyer a notice saying (A) the buyer cannot require extra work without written authorization before it starts, (B) a change order is not enforceable unless it states scope, price change and effect on payments or completion date in writing before the work starts, and (C) noncompliance does not bar the contractor's unjust-enrichment recovery.

notice_items: buyer may not require extra/change work without written authorization before commencement
CO not enforceable unless it identifies in writing, before commencement: scope; amount added/subtracted; effect on progress payments or completion date
contractor's noncompliance does not preclude unjust-enrichment recovery

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts
rules.source: PDF page 402 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (A) A statement that the buyer may not require a contractor to perform extra or change-order work without providing written authorization prior to the commencement of work covered by the new change order.
rules.notes: 7159(e) intro says these notices are provided 'as part of the contract form as specified or, if otherwise authorized under this subdivision, may be provided as an attachment'; only the CGL and WC notices are expressly allowed as attachments, so treat this one as in-contract. 'may_be_attachment' is that interpretation.
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: Subcontractor yes/no and disclaimer - repeated on every change order
rules.plain_english: The contract must say, with Yes/No checkboxes, whether subcontractors will be used. If Yes, it must include a disclaimer that a list of subs (names, contact info, license numbers, classifications) will be provided on request, and that same disclaimer must appear on each change order.

parameters.disclaimer_text_if_yes: One or more subcontractors will be used on this project, and the contractor is aware that a list of subcontractors is required to be provided, upon request, along with the names, contact information, license number, and classification of those subcontractors.

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts and their change orders
rules.source: PDF page 399 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (C) If there is a change order during the project, the same disclaimer set forth in subparagraph (B) shall be on each change order.
rules.notes: Change-order generator should auto-insert the disclaimer when the contract box is 'Yes'. Keep a sub list with CSLB license number and classification ready to produce on request.
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: Owner-occupied single-family home construction: contract and changes in writing
rules.plain_english: For building a single-family home the owner will keep for at least a year, the contract and every change must be in writing and signed by both parties, and must show the contractor's name/address/license, approximate start and substantial completion dates, and a legal description of the site.

parameters.scope: construction of a single-family dwelling to be retained by the owner for at least one year
required_contents: approximate dates work will begin and be substantially completed
CGL statement + checkbox (insurer name/phone if carried)
parameters.copy_to_owner: copy signed by contractor before commencement of any work

rules.applies_to: Contractors building single-family dwellings for owners
rules.source: PDF page 425 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book-426
rules.quote: (a) Notwithstanding Section 7044, every contract and any changes in a contract, between an owner and a contractor, for the construction of a single-family dwelling to be retained by the owner for at least one year shall be evidenced in writing signed by both parties.
rules.notes: 7164(b)(2): 'The approximate dates when the work will begin and be substantially completed.' 7164(c): 'Prior to commencement of any work, the owner shall be furnished a copy of the written agreement, signed by the contractor.'

rules.title: Service & repair T&M: actual price may not exceed estimate without written authorization
rules.plain_english: On a qualifying service and repair contract ($750 or less) priced on time and materials, the contract must show an 'Estimated Contract Price', the hourly rate, estimated materials and the time increments, and must say the actual amount may not exceed the estimate without the buyer's written authorization.

parameters.heading: Estimated Contract Price
must_disclose: time increment (e.g., quarter hour, half hour, hour)
parameters.required_statement: The actual contract amount of a time and materials contract may not exceed the estimated contract amount without written authorization from the buyer.
other_conditions: no goods/services beyond those reasonably necessary
no payment due or accepted until work completed

rules.applies_to: Service and repair contracts under B&P 7159.10
rules.source: PDF page 414 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book; PDF page 416 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: The contract must disclose the set rate and the estimated cost of materials. The contract must also disclose how time will be computed, for example, in increments of quarter hours, half hours, or hours, and the statement: “The actual contract amount of a time and materials contract may not exceed the estimated contract amount without written authorization from the buyer.”
rules.notes: If any of the four service-and-repair conditions fails, the full HIC rules of 7159(c)-(e) apply regardless of price (7159.10(b)).
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: Discipline for failing to complete for the contract price (as modified)
rules.plain_english: A contractor who materially fails to finish a job for the price in the contract, or in any written modification (change order), can be disciplined. Price increases must come through valid modifications.

parameters.price_basis: contract price or any modification of the contract
parameters.violation: failure in a material respect to complete for that price

rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.source: PDF page 353 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Failure in a material respect on the part of a licensee to complete any construction project or operation for the price stated in the contract for such construction project or operation or in any modification of such contract constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: Supports a cost-to-complete check: projected final cost to owner must not exceed contract sum to date (original + approved COs).
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: No material departure from plans/specs or trade standards without consent
rules.plain_english: Willfully departing in a material way from good workmanlike trade standards, or from the plans and specifications without the owner's consent, is grounds for discipline. Field changes to plans need owner (and design professional) approval, typically documented by RFI response and change order.

parameters.trade_standard_exception: departure in accordance with plans/specs prepared by or under direct supervision of an architect
plans_specs_change_requires: consent of owner or authorized representative
consent of the person entitled to have the project completed per the plans/specs

rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.source: PDF page 350 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (b) A willful departure from or disregard of plans or specifications in any material respect, which is prejudicial to another, without the consent of the owner or his or her duly authorized representative and without the consent of the person entitled to have the particular construction project or operation completed in accordance with such plans or specifications
rules.notes: 7109(a) is the basis for latent structural-defect complaints (B&P 7091(b)). B&P 7159(a)(5)(B): on HIC jobs the prime/direct contractor is responsible for completing the project per the contract, plans and specifications.

rules.title: Handling changes: document, price cost and time, then both sign
rules.plain_english: When the owner asks for something different from the contract (more or less), write it down, immediately work out the cost and schedule effect, let the customer decide, and have both parties sign the written change order before proceeding.

steps: price cost and time impact immediately
both parties sign written change order

rules.applies_to: All contractors (CSLB business guidance)
rules.citation: CSLB Law Book Ch. 3 guidance (legal minimums for HIC in B&P 7159/7159.6)
rules.source: PDF page 70 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: You should also immediately negotiate the effect of the change, such as cost and time. Tell your customer what is going on and allow the customer to determine if the change is worth it. If you and your customer agree to the change, make sure both parties sign the written change order.
rules.notes: Quote is from the CSLB Law Book's non-binding business-management guidance chapter (official publication, but guidance, not law), so it is marked as a practice item.

rules.title: Estimate labor by classification with full burden
rules.plain_english: Price labor by work classification and include not just the hourly wage but payroll taxes, health and welfare benefits, vacation pay and required insurance.

parameters.labor_cost_per_hour: base_wage + payroll_taxes + health_welfare + vacation + required_insurance (workers' comp, liability as applicable) [+ union fringes]
burden_items_ca: employer FICA (6.2% SS to wage base + 1.45% Medicare)

rules.applies_to: Estimators and contractors bidding work
rules.source: PDF page 64 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Labor costs are calculated according to work classification. These costs include not only the hourly wage rate, but also payroll taxes, health and welfare benefits, vacation pay, and required insurance.
rules.notes: Quote is from the CSLB Law Book's non-binding business-management guidance chapter (official publication, but guidance, not law), so it is marked as a practice item. The CA burden item list is a synthesis of the payroll-tax rules in this file. Prevailing wage jobs must use DIR determinations (see public-works research).

rules.title: Direct labor burden defined
rules.plain_english: Direct labor burden is all payroll taxes, insurance and employee benefits tied to labor payroll; for union labor it includes union benefit assessments and sometimes association fees.
rules.applies_to: Job costing and estimating
rules.source: PDF page 58 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Direct Labor Burden: This includes all payroll taxes, insurance, and employee benefits associated with the labor payroll. If the workers belong to a union, the direct labor burden will include union benefit assessments and, in some cases, association fees.
rules.notes: Quote is from the CSLB Law Book's non-binding business-management guidance chapter (official publication, but guidance, not law), so it is marked as a practice item. Formulas are standard practice, not from the Law Book.

rules.title: Materials: takeoffs priced with sales tax and freight; no cash discounts unless sure
rules.plain_english: Price materials from quantity takeoffs using supplier quotes or price lists, include sales tax and freight, and do not count early-payment cash discounts unless you are sure you will have the cash to pay within the discount period.

parameters.include_cash_discounts: only if payment within discount period is assured

rules.applies_to: Estimators
rules.source: PDF page 64 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Materials required are determined from takeoffs (quantity and measurements taken from plans) that are converted to costs on the estimation form. Prices should be obtained from published price lists and quotes from suppliers and subcontractors. It is important to include sales tax and freight costs.
rules.notes: Quote is from the CSLB Law Book's non-binding business-management guidance chapter (official publication, but guidance, not law), so it is marked as a practice item. Waste factor is standard practice, not in the Law Book. Sales tax rate depends on delivery location (CDTFA district rates; not researched here). The Law Book also says (p. 41) contractors must collect sales tax from customers unless tax on materials was paid at purchase.

rules.title: Add overhead and profit after all costs; estimate becomes the job budget
rules.plain_english: After totaling direct and indirect costs, add overhead (office, advertising, bad debts, storage, admin) and always add profit; the estimate behind the bid becomes the project budget for cost control.
rules.applies_to: Estimators
rules.source: PDF page 64 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book-65
rules.quote: When all the costs have been totaled, the contractor must add profit.
rules.notes: Quote is from the CSLB Law Book's non-binding business-management guidance chapter (official publication, but guidance, not law), so it is marked as a practice item. Law Book PDF page 65: 'The estimate that is the basis for the bid becomes a budget for the project.' Markup vs margin formulas are standard practice.

rules.title: Performance/payment bond cost: typically 1-2% of contract price
rules.plain_english: Project bonds usually cost about 1-2% of the contract price; include that cost in the bid when bonds are required.
rules.applies_to: Estimators on bonded work
rules.source: PDF page 42 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Bonds can be obtained from bonding companies for a percentage of the contract price, usually in the one to two percent range. This requirement is the cost of doing business that should be recognized when the bid is submitted.
rules.notes: Quote is from the CSLB Law Book's non-binding business-management guidance chapter (official publication, but guidance, not law), so it is marked as a practice item. Actual premium depends on surety, contractor financials and contract size.
rules.correction: None. This is CSLB guidance, not law, as the rule already says.

rules.title: Register with EDD once employees earn over $100 in a quarter
rules.plain_english: A contractor must register with the EDD, get a state employer account number and pay state payroll and unemployment insurance taxes for employees who earn more than $100 in a calendar quarter.

obligations: pay state payroll and UI taxes

rules.applies_to: Contractors with employees
rules.citation: California Unemployment Insurance Code (as summarized in CSLB Law Book Ch. 3)
rules.source: PDF page 41 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: The contractor must register with the Employment Development Department, obtain a state EIN, and pay state payroll and unemployment insurance taxes for employees who earn over $100 in a calendar quarter.
rules.notes: Read from the Law Book's narrative summary of the law, not from the Unemployment Insurance Code itself. Federal EIN and federal withholding/Social Security deposits also required (same page).
rules.correction: None. EDD confirms the over-$100-per-calendar-quarter trigger and adds what the rule omits: registration is due within 15 days after paying more than $100 in wages in a calendar quarter (Unemployment Insurance Code 1086, per EDD).

rules.title: CA Unemployment Insurance (UI) 2026: $7,000 wage base; new employers 3.4%
rules.plain_english: California UI tax is employer-paid on the first $7,000 of each employee's wages per year. New employers get a 3.4% rate for their first two to three years; experienced employers get an assigned rate.
rules.applies_to: California employers (estimating labor burden)
rules.citation: Cal. Unemp. Ins. Code (rates published by EDD)
rules.quote: New employers are assigned a 3.4 percent UI rate for two to three years
rules.notes: edd.ca.gov is not reachable from this session (host not allowed) and WebSearch is exhausted; figures and quote come from a search-engine excerpt of EDD's rates page. Max per employee (238.00) is arithmetic: 3.4% x $7,000. Experienced employers' rates vary by reserve account; read the employer's DE 2088 notice.
rules.correction: None. EDD excerpts: 2026 UI taxable wage limit $7,000 per employee per year; new employers pay 3.4% (.034) for two to three years. Page text seen only as excerpts.

rules.title: CA Employment Training Tax (ETT) 2026: 0.1% on first $7,000
rules.plain_english: ETT is an employer-paid tax of 0.1% on the first $7,000 of each employee's wages per year (most for-profit employers).
rules.applies_to: California employers subject to UI (estimating labor burden)
rules.citation: Cal. Unemp. Ins. Code (rates published by EDD)
rules.quote: The ETT taxable wage limit is $7,000 per employee, per calendar year.
rules.notes: From a search-engine excerpt of EDD's rate page ('the ETT rate for 2026 is 0.1 percent'); page not fetched. Some employers (e.g., negative-reserve or certain nonprofits) may differ. Search excerpt also indicated $7,000 UI/ETT limit and 0.1% ETT continue for 2027.
rules.correction: None. EDD excerpts: 2026 ETT 0.1% on the first $7,000 per employee. Employers with a negative UI reserve balance pay no ETT (shown as 0.0% on the rate notice). Page text seen only as excerpts.

rules.title: CA SDI 2026: 1.3% employee withholding, no wage cap
rules.plain_english: State Disability Insurance is withheld from employees' wages at 1.3% for 2026 with no taxable wage limit (all wages subject since 2024). It is an employee deduction the employer must withhold and remit, not an employer labor-burden cost.
rules.applies_to: California employers (payroll setup; not a burden cost)
rules.citation: Cal. Unemp. Ins. Code (rates published by EDD)
rules.quote: all wages are subject to SDI contributions effective January 1, 2024
rules.notes: From search-engine excerpts of EDD pages ('the 2026 rate is 1.3 percent'); page not fetched. The search summary noted an EDD example table labeled 1.1% while computing at 1.3%; rely on 1.3% from the main rate table, but verify.
rules.correction: None. EDD excerpts: "the 2026 rate of 1.3 percent (.013) provides for both State Disability Insurance (SDI) and Paid Family Leave (PFL) benefits"; "There is no taxable wage limit" for SDI. The verbatim quote in the rule was not itself seen.

rules.title: Employer FICA 2026: 6.2% Social Security to $184,500 + 1.45% Medicare (no cap)
rules.plain_english: Employers pay 6.2% Social Security tax on each employee's wages up to $184,500 in 2026 and 1.45% Medicare tax on all wages, matching the employee's share.
rules.applies_to: All employers (labor burden)
rules.citation: 26 U.S.C. 3111 (rates); SSA annual wage base announcement
rules.source: Search results summarizing SSA October 2025 announcement (ssa.gov not reachable)
rules.notes: ssa.gov/irs.gov are not reachable from this session and the statute was not read; figures from WebSearch summaries of secondary sources (Journal of Accountancy, EY, Thomson Reuters) of the SSA announcement. 2025 base was $176,100. The 0.9% Additional Medicare Tax is employee-only (over $200,000) and not an employer burden.
rules.correction: None. SSA: 2026 contribution and benefit base $184,500 (2025: $176,100). OASDI rate 6.2% each for employer and employee. IRS Pub. 15 (2026): no Medicare wage base limit. Pages seen only as excerpts.

rules.title: FUTA: 0.6% net on first $7,000, plus California credit reduction
rules.plain_english: Federal unemployment tax is 6.0% on the first $7,000 of each employee's wages, reduced to a net 0.6% by the state credit. Because California has an outstanding federal loan, its employers lose part of the credit: for 2025 the reduction was 1.2%, for a net 1.8% ($126 per employee). The 2026 reduction is set in November 2026 and was not confirmed here.
rules.applies_to: All employers with California employees (labor burden)
rules.citation: 26 U.S.C. 3301-3302; DOL/IRS annual credit-reduction list (Form 940 Schedule A)
rules.source: Search results (IRS draft 2025 Schedule A; DOL announcement) - irs.gov not reachable
rules.effective: Tax year 2025 (credit reduction paid with 2025 Form 940, due Feb 2, 2026)
rules.notes: Not read from primary text: irs.gov/dol.gov unreachable; figures from WebSearch summaries (IRS draft 2025 Schedule A listing CA at 0.012; Paychex/UHY net 1.8%). Under the general FUTA credit-reduction mechanism the reduction usually grows by about 0.3 percentage points per additional year a loan stays unpaid (general knowledge, not verified); for 2026 budgeting, use the DOL list published after Nov 10, 2026 rather than assuming.
rules.correction: None. 2025 California credit reduction 1.2% confirmed (net 1.8%, $126 per employee). For 2026, EDD projects a 1.5% reduction (net 2.1%, $147 per employee), and the draft 2026 Form 940 instructions name California as the only credit-reduction state. The final 2026 rate is published by DOL after 2026-11-10; it was not found in the search, so ca_credit_reduction_2026_percent stays null.

rules.title: Workers' comp cost estimate: payroll/100 x class rate x experience mod
rules.plain_english: Estimate workers' comp as payroll (in hundreds of dollars) times the insurer's rate for each class code, times the experience modification, plus policy fees/surcharges. The state's average advisory pure premium for policies on or after Sept 1, 2026 is $1.65 per $100 of payroll, but construction classes vary widely and insurers set their own rates.
rules.applies_to: Estimators and employers (labor burden)
rules.citation: Cal. Insurance Code ratemaking (Insurance Commissioner decision July 10, 2026); WCIRB classifications
rules.source: Search results summarizing CDI Decision and Order, July 10, 2026 (insurance.ca.gov and wcirb.com not reachable)
rules.notes: insurance.ca.gov and wcirb.com are blocked in this session; the $1.65 (6.6% above the approved 2025 rate) and $1.551 figures come from WebSearch summaries of CDI press materials, not the decision text. Note: 1.65/1.551 implies about +6.4%, while the search summary described the approved rate as +6.6% over the 2025 approved rate - the exact 2025 base figure is uncertain; verify. Advisory pure premiums exclude insurer expenses, so actual manual rates are higher. Class codes listed are examples to look up (not verified class numbers/descriptions); do not hard-code class rates from this file. Employer cannot charge employees for WC (see wc-employer-pays-no-employee-offset). [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: The $1.65 per $100 average for policies incepting on or after 2026-09-01 is confirmed: 6.6% above the approved 2025-09-01 average; WCIRB had proposed $1.71 (+10.4%); rates are advisory. The prior-year figure was wrong. The 2025-09-01 decision (July 11, 2025) approved an average of $1.52 (+8.7%). CDI's 2026 materials restate it as $1.55 on updated class exposure weights, which is the base for the 6.6%. The unsourced 1.551 is replaced with these two figures. Pages seen only as excerpts.

rules.title: Construction 'dual wage' WC classes split by hourly wage
rules.plain_english: Several California construction trades have two WC class codes: a higher-rated code for workers whose regular hourly wage is below a threshold, and a lower-rated code for workers at or above it. Thresholds change periodically. Effective September 1, 2026 the carpentry (5403/5432) threshold is $46.00 per hour (was $41.00 from September 1, 2024); look up the current figure for every other dual-wage pair.

parameters.concept: class_code = high_wage_code if hourly_wage >= threshold else low_wage_code
parameters.wage_basis: regular hourly wage (5432 assignment subject to verification at final audit; payroll not shown to meet the threshold goes to 5403)

rules.applies_to: Employers with construction trade payroll (WC class assignment and burden)
rules.citation: California Workers' Compensation Uniform Statistical Reporting Plan (WCIRB; approved by Insurance Commissioner)
rules.source: Search results summarizing WCIRB memoranda (wcirb.com not reachable)
rules.notes: Not read from primary text. The $41.00/$39.00 and '16 classifications' figures come from WebSearch summaries of WCIRB documents and may be superseded by the Sept 1, 2026 USRP changes. Must verify current thresholds before assigning class codes. Thresholds use the straight-time hourly wage (exclusive of overtime premium, per USRP practice - verify). [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: The rule's current figure is out of date. Effective 2026-09-01, the carpentry dual-wage threshold (5403/5432) is $46.00 per hour, up from $41.00. WCIRB's 5432 classification reads "employees whose regular hourly wage equals or exceeds $46.00 per hour", and payroll not shown to meet it is classified 5403, subject to verification at final audit. The test is the "regular hourly wage" (the rule's "straight-time" reading is consistent). Other dual-wage thresholds also changed (e.g., the excerpts show 6315/6316 moving from $40 to $45). Look each one up; do not reuse the carpentry figure. The count of 16 dual-wage classifications and the pre-2024 $39 figure were not verified. Pages seen only as excerpts.

rules.title: Workers' comp is required with even one employee; employees cannot be charged
rules.plain_english: California employers must carry workers' comp even with a single part-time employee, and may not make employees pay or offset any of its cost. Failing to carry it is a crime.
rules.applies_to: All California employers
rules.quote: California law requires employers to have workers’ compensation insurance, even if they have just one employee.
rules.notes: Official DWC fact sheet (Sept 2024) also states: 'Employees cannot pay or offset the cost of the policy.' Labor Code section numbers are from general knowledge/Law Book PDF page 48 (3700.5 misdemeanor), not read in the Labor Code itself.

rules.title: C-8, C-20, C-22, C-39, D-49 licensees must carry WC even with no employees
rules.plain_english: Through 2027, a licensee with no employees may file a workers' comp exemption with CSLB, except holders of C-8 Concrete, C-20 HVAC, C-22 Asbestos Abatement, C-39 Roofing or D-49 Tree Service, who must carry workers' comp regardless.

classifications_requiring_wc_regardless: C-20 Warm-Air Heating, Ventilating and Air-Conditioning
parameters.exemption_available_if: no employees AND none of the listed classes (statement filed with CSLB)
parameters.consequence_if_no_wc: listed classification removed (C-39 since 2013; C-8/C-20/C-22/D-49 since 2023-07-01) or license suspended if employees found

rules.applies_to: CSLB licensees; GCs vetting subcontractors in these trades
rules.source: PDF page 45 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book; PDF page 365 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book-367
rules.quote: If you don’t have employees, you must file an exemption from the workers’ compensation requirement unless you hold one of these classifications which requires you to carry workers’ compensation insurance: C-8 Concrete; C-20 Warm-Air Heating, Ventilating and Air-Conditioning; C-22 Asbestos Abatement; C-39 Roofing; C-61/D-49 Tree Service.
rules.notes: Statute text 7125(b)(2) on PDF pages 365-366 lists the same classes by CCR section (832.08, 832.20, 832.22, 832.39, 832.61). Sub-compliance check: a sub holding any of these classes with a WC exemption on file is a red flag.

rules.title: From Jan 1, 2028 all licensees need workers' comp (only no-employee joint ventures exempt)
rules.plain_english: Starting January 1, 2028, every CSLB licensee must keep a workers' comp certificate (or self-insurance certificate) on file; the no-employee exemption survives only for joint-venture licensees with no employees. Inactive licenses are excused while inactive.

parameters.exemption_remaining: joint venture (B&P 7029) with no employees that files statement

rules.applies_to: All CSLB licensees
rules.source: PDF page 367 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book-368
rules.quote: (b) This section does not apply to an applicant or licensee organized as a joint venture pursuant to Section 7029 that has no employees, provided that the applicant or licensee files a statement with the board on a form prescribed by the registrar
rules.notes: 7125(f) of this version: 'This section shall become operative on January 1, 2028.' B&P 7125.7 requires CSLB to set up an exemption-verification process by Jan 1, 2027. Budget WC for owner-operator subs from 2028.
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: Licensee must keep WC certificate on file with CSLB; insurer reports policy dates
rules.plain_english: Every licensee (unless exempt) must always have a current workers' comp certificate or self-insurance certificate on file with CSLB in its business name. The insurer reports the policy number and start, lapse and cancellation dates to CSLB, so a GC can check a sub's WC status on the CSLB license record.

parameters.document: Certificate of Workers' Compensation Insurance or Certification of Self-Insurance
parameters.sub_check: verify sub's WC on CSLB license detail before work starts and before each payment

rules.applies_to: CSLB licensees; GCs vetting subcontractors
rules.source: PDF page 365 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book-366
rules.quote: the board shall require as a condition precedent to the issuance, reinstatement, reactivation, renewal, or continued maintenance of a license, that the applicant or licensee have on file at all times a current and valid Certificate of Workers’ Compensation Insurance or Certification of Self-Insurance in the applicant’s or licensee’s business name.
rules.notes: 7125(e)(1): insurer 'shall report to the registrar the following information for any policy required under this section: name, license number, policy number, dates that coverage is scheduled to commence and lapse, and cancellation date if applicable.'

rules.title: License automatically suspended when required WC lapses
rules.plain_english: If a licensee required to carry workers' comp lets it lapse (or never gets it when required), its license is suspended automatically by law on the lapse date. A sub with a suspended license is unlicensed for that period.

parameters.suspension_effective: earlier of coverage lapse date or date coverage was required

rules.applies_to: CSLB licensees; GCs (unlicensed sub consequences under B&P 7031)
rules.source: PDF page 368 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book-369
rules.quote: (a) The license suspension imposed by this section is effective upon the earlier of either of the following: (1) On the date that the relevant workers’ compensation insurance coverage lapses. (2) On the date that workers’ compensation coverage is required to be obtained.
rules.notes: 7125.1(a): CSLB accepts a certificate as of its effective date if received within 90 days after that date and reinstates retroactively. 7125.3: contractor is considered duly licensed during periods the registrar is required to accept the certificate. Track sub COI expiration dates and re-check CSLB before paying.
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: Employing workers without WC: civil penalty $10,000 (sole owner) / $20,000 (entity) minimum
rules.plain_english: A licensee caught employing workers without workers' comp, or filing a false exemption, faces minimum civil penalties of $10,000 per violation for a sole owner and $20,000 for a partnership, corporation, LLC or tribal business, with added penalties up to $30,000 per occurrence for repeat violations. The license will not be renewed or reinstated until a valid certificate is filed.
rules.applies_to: CSLB licensees and their qualifiers
rules.source: PDF page 370 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (1) A minimum civil penalty of ten thousand dollars ($10,000) per violation for any sole owner licensee found to have employed workers without maintaining workers’ compensation coverage. (2) A minimum civil penalty of twenty thousand dollars ($20,000) per violation for any partnership, corporation, limited liability company, or tribal business licensee
rules.notes: Separate Labor Code penalties also apply (see uninsured-employer-penalties-lc-3722).
rules.correction: None. Quote matches PDF p.370 (an automated string match missed only because the page footer "Section VI" splits the sentence).

rules.title: Labor Code uninsured-employer penalty assessments ($1,500 per employee; $10,000/$2,000 per employee after a claim, $100,000 max)
rules.plain_english: DLSE assesses an uninsured employer the greater of twice the workers' comp premiums it would have paid while uninsured, or $1,500 per employee employed during the uninsured period. If a WCAB judge later finds the employer was uninsured on a claim, it may be assessed $10,000 per employee on the payroll at the time of injury (compensable case) or $2,000 per employee (non-compensable case), up to $100,000. DIR can also issue a stop order barring use of employee labor.

parameters.penalty_after_claim_counted_on: employees on the payroll at the time of injury

rules.applies_to: Employers without workers' comp
rules.citation: Labor Code 3722(b), (d), (f) (as quoted/cited by DIR); Labor Code 3710.1, 3712, 3727
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/dwc/faqs.html; https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/FAQ-Workers%20Compensation.pdf; PDF page 48 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book-49
rules.quote: The Division of Labor Standards Enforcement will also assess a penalty the greater of (1) twice the amount the employer would have paid in workers' compensation premiums during the period the employer was uninsured, determined according to subdivision (c), or (2) the sum of one thousand five hundred dollars ($1,500) per employee employed during the period the employer was uninsured. [ Labor Code section 3722(b) ].
rules.notes: Read from Law Book narrative (PDF page 49 continues: 'If the contractor's uninsured status is discovered following the filing of a claim for compensation, the penalty shall be either $2,000 for each employee employed on the date of injury in non-compensable cases, or $10,000 for each employee in compensable cases (Labor Code §3722).'), not from the Labor Code itself. [Verification 2026-11-25: corrected against official text - see verification.correction; earlier caveats in these notes are superseded where they conflict.]
rules.correction: The per-employee base penalty is $1,500, not $1,000. DIR's DWC FAQ quotes LC 3722(b): "the greater of (1) twice the amount the employer would have paid in workers' compensation premiums during the period the employer was uninsured, determined according to subdivision (c), or (2) the sum of one thousand five hundred dollars ($1,500) per employee employed during the period the employer was uninsured." DLSE says the $1,500 figure has applied since 2011-01-01; the 2026 Law Book narrative (PDF p.49) still says $1,000. The after-claim penalties ($10,000 per employee compensable, $2,000 per employee non-compensable, counted on the payroll at the time of injury) are confirmed by the DWC FAQ, which adds a $100,000 maximum (LC 3722(d), (f)). Parameters, plain_english, citation, source and quote updated. The Labor Code text itself was not read on leginfo.

rules.title: Certify top 3 WC class codes (by payroll) at license renewal
rules.plain_english: At each license renewal, a licensee with (or required to have) workers' comp must certify the three WC classification codes with the highest estimated payroll on its policy (or all codes if fewer than three). CSLB posts them on the public license record, so GCs can see whether a sub's WC class matches the work.

parameters.selection: highest estimated payroll on the policy
parameters.if_fewer_than_three: certify every code on the policy

rules.applies_to: Active licensees with WC on file or required
rules.source: PDF page 371 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book-372
rules.quote: shall certify on the license renewal form for the three workers’ compensation classification codes for which the highest estimated payroll is reported on the policy. If the licensee has fewer than three classification codes reported on the policy, the licensee shall provide every classification code reported on the policy.
rules.notes: Useful sub-vetting check: e.g., a roofing sub whose certified codes are only clerical (8810) is a misclassification red flag.

rules.title: HIC must define substantial commencement and give an approximate start date
rules.plain_english: The home improvement contract must describe what counts as substantial commencement of work, and show an 'Approximate Start Date' heading with the approximate date work will start.

required_items: statement of what constitutes substantial commencement of work
heading 'Approximate Start Date'
approximate start date

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts
rules.source: PDF page 400 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (10) The contract shall address the commencement of work to be performed in substantially the following form: (A) A statement that describes what constitutes substantial commencement of work under the contract. (B) The heading: “Approximate Start Date.” (C) The approximate date on which work will be commenced.
rules.notes: CSLB sample (Contracting for Success PDF page 9) conditions the start date on receipt of required building permits and agreed funds and makes completion 'subject to permissible delays as defined in this contract.'
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: HIC must show an approximate completion date
rules.plain_english: The home improvement contract must include the heading 'Approximate Completion Date' and the approximate date of completion. Change orders must state their effect on the completion date.

parameters.heading: Approximate Completion Date
parameters.updated_by: change orders stating effect on completion date (B&P 7159.6(a)(3))

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts
rules.source: PDF page 401 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (11) The estimated completion date of the work shall be referenced in the contract in substantially the following form: (A) The heading: “Approximate Completion Date.” (B) The approximate date of completion.
rules.notes: A schedule tool can compute revised completion = original + approved change-order days + permissible (excusable) delays defined in the contract.
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: Critical path method (CPM) basics
rules.plain_english: A bar chart shows when each task starts and finishes but ignores how tasks depend on each other. CPM links tasks; the longest chain of dependent tasks is the critical path, and any delay on it delays the whole project.

parameters.forward_pass: ES = max(EF of predecessors); EF = ES + duration
parameters.backward_pass: LF = min(LS of successors); LS = LF - duration
parameters.delay_rule: delay on critical activity extends project by that amount (unless float/mitigation)

rules.applies_to: Project scheduling on any job
rules.citation: CSLB Law Book Ch. 3 guidance; CPM formulas are standard practice
rules.source: PDF page 65 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (Figures 6.A and 6.B on PDF pages 66-67)
rules.quote: The critical path method (Figure 6.B) is a more complex tool that better interrelates the tasks. This technique derives its name from the key path through the network that considers all the tasks to be completed. Any delay in one of these tasks will result in an overall delay of the project.
rules.notes: Quote is from the CSLB Law Book's non-binding business-management guidance chapter (official publication, but guidance, not law), so it is marked as a practice item. Same page on bar charts: 'This scheduling approach is simple but overlooks some interrelated tasks.' The forward/backward pass formulas are standard CPM practice, not from the Law Book.

rules.title: Discipline for willfully failing to prosecute work with reasonable diligence
rules.plain_english: A contractor who willfully and without legal excuse fails to push the job forward with reasonable diligence, causing material injury to someone, can be disciplined.

elements: willful failure or refusal
without legal excuse
to prosecute project with reasonable diligence
causing material injury to another

rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.source: PDF page 358 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Wilful failure or refusal without legal excuse on the part of a licensee as a contractor to prosecute a construction project or operation with reasonable diligence causing material injury to another constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: Daily logs and an updated schedule documenting delays and their causes are the practical defense.
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: Discipline for abandoning a project without legal excuse
rules.plain_english: Walking off a construction project without a legal excuse is grounds for CSLB discipline.

elements: abandonment
without legal excuse

rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.source: PDF page 348 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Abandonment without legal excuse of any construction project or operation engaged in or undertaken by the licensee as a contractor constitutes a cause for disciplinary action.
rules.notes: Document stop-work reasons (e.g., nonpayment notices) in writing. Contract-rights exception on waiver forms preserves claims for 'rescission, abandonment, or breach of contract'.
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: Keep all project records at least 5 years after completion
rules.plain_english: Contractors must keep records of all contracts, documents, records, receipts and disbursements for every job and make them available to CSLB for at least five years after that project is completed. This covers change orders, pay apps, daily logs, RFIs, submittals and lien waivers.
rules.applies_to: All licensees
rules.source: PDF page 352 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (a) Failure to make and keep records showing all contracts, documents, records, receipts, and disbursements by a licensee of all of his or her transactions as a contractor, and failure to have those records available for inspection by the registrar or his or her duly authorized representative for a period of not less than five years after completion of any construction project
rules.notes: The 'practical_scope' list is an interpretation of 'all contracts, documents, records'. Longer retention is prudent given 10-year latent-defect exposure (CCP 337.15; B&P 7091(b)). Other laws impose their own periods (e.g., payroll 3-4 years; Cal/OSHA logs 5 years - see other research files).

rules.title: Daily log (daily report) contents
rules.plain_english: Keep a daily log for each job recording date, weather, crews and hours by trade/sub, work performed by location, equipment, deliveries, visitors and inspections, delays and their causes, safety incidents, instructions received, and photos. It is the main evidence for delay, change and defect disputes.

parameters.frequency: every working day (and non-working days with events)

rules.applies_to: All projects
rules.source: Industry practice; no official source fetched
rules.notes: Standard construction-management practice, not a legal requirement; not read from any primary legal text. CSLB Law Book (PDF page 70) generally advises: 'It is a good idea to document the progress of the project and keep your customer up to date.' Injuries recorded in the log may trigger Cal/OSHA/WC reporting deadlines covered in other research files.

rules.title: Request for Information (RFI) process
rules.plain_english: Use a numbered, logged RFI to ask the designer or owner to clarify conflicts or gaps in the plans and specs before doing the work; record the question, proposed solution, required-by date, response and whether it changes cost or time. If it does, issue a change order.

parameters.aging_metric: days_open = answered_date - sent_date (or today - sent_date if open)
parameters.if_cost_or_time_impact: convert to change order before performing changed work

rules.applies_to: All projects with plans/specs
rules.citation: Industry practice; B&P 7109(b) (no departure from plans without consent)
rules.source: Industry practice; no official source fetched
rules.notes: Standard construction-management practice, not a legal requirement; not read from any primary legal text. Response turnaround times are contractual (e.g., 'within X days' in the general conditions), not statutory in California private work.

rules.title: Submittals (shop drawings, product data, samples) process
rules.plain_english: Before ordering or installing specified items, send shop drawings, product data and samples through a logged submittal process for the design team's review; track required dates against the schedule's lead times and do not install until approved.

parameters.rule: no fabrication/installation before approval

rules.applies_to: All projects with specifications
rules.citation: Industry practice; documents incorporated into HIC per B&P 7159(d)(12)
rules.source: Industry practice; no official source fetched
rules.notes: Standard construction-management practice, not a legal requirement; not read from any primary legal text. Substitutions that change significant materials/equipment described in an HIC (B&P 7159(d)(7)) should be documented by change order.

rules.title: HIC: list every document incorporated into the contract
rules.plain_english: If plans, specifications, bids or other documents are part of a home improvement contract, the contract must include the heading 'List of Documents to be Incorporated into the Contract' followed by the list.

parameters.heading: List of Documents to be Incorporated into the Contract
parameters.condition: if applicable
typical_documents: plans/drawings with dates and revision numbers

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts
rules.source: PDF page 401 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (12) If applicable, the heading: “List of Documents to be Incorporated into the Contract,” followed by the list of documents incorporated into the contract.
rules.notes: 'typical_documents' is practice. B&P 7164(c) similarly requires SFD contracts to 'clearly describe any other document which is to be incorporated into the contract.'
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: HIC: describe the project and significant materials/equipment
rules.plain_english: The contract must have the heading 'Description of the Project and Description of the Significant Materials to be Used and Equipment to be Installed' with an actual description; swimming pools also need a plan and scale drawing with dimensions and specs.

parameters.heading: Description of the Project and Description of the Significant Materials to be Used and Equipment to be Installed
parameters.swimming_pool_extra: plan and scale drawing showing shape, size, dimensions, construction and equipment specifications

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts
rules.source: PDF page 400 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (7) The heading: “Description of the Project and Description of the Significant Materials to be Used and Equipment to be Installed,” followed by a description of the project and a description of the significant materials to be used and equipment to be installed.
rules.notes: This scope description is the baseline for deciding whether later requests are 'extras' requiring a change order. CSLB lists 'Equipment to be used or installed is not detailed, and materials to be used not described specifically' as a common problem (Law Book PDF page 36).
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: CSLB checklist of HIC contract content (incl. permits and permissible delays)
rules.plain_english: CSLB tells contractors a home improvement contract should fully describe the work, materials and equipment, price, payment schedule, start and completion, permits and tests, permissible delays, extra work, required lien-release statements, and the owner's cancellation rights.

checklist: start and completion of work (dates and descriptions)
required release of mechanics' liens statements

rules.applies_to: Home improvement contracts
rules.citation: CSLB Law Book Ch. 2 summary of B&P 7159
rules.source: PDF page 35 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Contract must include full descriptions and information about the following: • Description of work • Description of materials and equipment • The contract price • Payment schedule • Start and completion of work (dates and descriptions) • Permits and tests • Permissible delays • Extra work
rules.notes: CSLB official summary, not statute text; 'permits and tests' and 'permissible delays' are not separately enumerated in the B&P 7159 text read on PDF pages 397-408, so treated as guidance (false). The list continues: 'Required release of mechanics' liens statements; Owner's applicable right to cancellation'.
rules.correction: None. This is a CSLB summary, not statute text, as the rule already says ("permits and tests" and "permissible delays" are not separate items in B&P 7159).

rules.title: Document progress and bill regularly
rules.plain_english: Keep the customer updated on progress in writing and invoice regularly; frequent billing reduces cash strain and keeps the customer informed.
rules.applies_to: All contractors
rules.source: PDF page 70 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book-71
rules.quote: It is a good idea to document the progress of the project and keep your customer up to date.
rules.notes: Quote is from the CSLB Law Book's non-binding business-management guidance chapter (official publication, but guidance, not law), so it is marked as a practice item. PDF page 71 continues: 'Closely allied with the communication of progress is frequent billing. By invoicing regularly, you will minimize your business's cash demands while keeping your customer informed.' On HIC jobs, billing frequency is still limited by work actually performed (B&P 7159.5(a)(5)).

rules.title: Punch lists and a pre-completion walk-through
rules.plain_english: Do frequent punch lists and a walk-through near the end of the job with the customer to list what remains, then fix deficiencies quickly.

parameters.timing: frequent during job + walk-through near end

rules.applies_to: All contractors
rules.source: PDF page 70 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Frequent “punch lists” are a good idea. A walk-through near the end of the job to determine the items that are left to be completed is recommended. Correct any deficiencies quickly.
rules.notes: Quote is from the CSLB Law Book's non-binding business-management guidance chapter (official publication, but guidance, not law), so it is marked as a practice item. Punch item fields are standard practice. Punch status should not be falsely certified as complete (B&P 7158).

rules.title: Using a false completion certificate is a misdemeanor ($500-$5,000)
rules.plain_english: Knowingly accepting and using a false completion certificate (or other proof the job is complete when it is not substantially complete) to assign or collect payment or obtain a loan is a misdemeanor punishable by a $500-$5,000 fine and/or 1 month to 1 year in county jail.

elements: accept/receive completion certificate or other evidence of completion
knowledge document is false and work not substantially completed
use in assignment/negotiation of right to payment or to obtain credit/loan

rules.applies_to: Any person (contractors, owners, lenders, salespersons) handling completion certificates
rules.source: PDF page 396 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: shall be guilty of a misdemeanor and subject to a fine of not less than five hundred dollars ($500) nor more than five thousand dollars ($5,000), or to imprisonment in the county jail for a term of not less than one month nor more than one year, or both.
rules.notes: Closeout tool should require actual punch-list completion/inspection sign-off before generating any completion certificate or lender completion statement. Relevant to solar/financed HIC jobs where lenders pay on completion certificates.
rules.correction: None.

rules.title: Project closeout package
rules.plain_english: Before final payment, assemble: completed punch list signed off, final building inspection/permit final (and certificate of occupancy if applicable), final change order reconciliation and final pay app, conditional then unconditional final lien waivers from the GC and every sub and supplier, warranties and guarantees, O&M manuals, as-built drawings, attic stock and keys, and the notice of completion (owner records). Then release retention per the statutory deadlines.

checklist: final inspection / permit finaled (certificate of occupancy where applicable)
conditional waiver and release on final payment (Civ. Code 8136) from GC and each sub/supplier before final payment
unconditional waiver and release on final payment (Civ. Code 8138) after payment clears
written warranties (contractor and manufacturer), with start dates
recorded notice of completion (owner; Civ. Code 8182 per lien research)

rules.applies_to: GCs and owners at project completion
rules.citation: Industry practice; waiver forms per Civil Code 8132-8138; retention per Civil Code 8812 / PCC 7107
rules.source: Industry practice; legal items cross-referenced to other rules
rules.notes: Standard construction-management practice, not a legal requirement; not read from any primary legal text. Notice of completion recording deadlines and effects on lien periods are in web_lien-payment.json (noc-* rules). Warranty start dates matter for B&P 7091(e) (18 months after warranty expiration).

rules.title: Lien waivers must substantially follow the four statutory forms
rules.plain_english: A waiver and release of lien, stop payment notice and payment bond rights is effective only if it substantially follows one of the four statutory forms: conditional progress, unconditional progress, conditional final, unconditional final.
rules.applies_to: All claimants (GC, subs, suppliers, equipment lessors) and payers on private and public works
rules.quote: To be effective, the waiver and release forms must follow, substantially, one of the forms set forth in Civil Code sections 8132, 8134, 8136, and 8138.
rules.notes: Official CSLB page and the four CSLB form PDFs were read. B&P 7034(b) separately bars contractors from requiring lien waivers in violation of Civ. Code 8122 (see no-unlawful-lien-waiver-demands).

rules.title: Conditional waiver on progress payment - collect with every pay app
rules.plain_english: With each progress billing, get a Conditional Waiver and Release on Progress Payment from the GC and each sub/supplier being paid. It identifies claimant, customer, job, owner, a 'Through Date', and the check (maker, amount, payee), and only takes effect when the claimant is actually paid. It does not waive retentions, unpaid extras, earlier unpaid progress payments, or contract rights.

parameters.when: submitted with each progress pay application, before payment
exceptions_not_waived: extras for which claimant has not received payment
prior progress payments covered by conditional waivers but unpaid (dates and amounts listed)
contract rights incl. rescission, abandonment, breach, and compensation for work not covered by the payment
parameters.effective_on: claimant's receipt of payment from the financial institution on which the check is drawn
parameters.header_notice: NOTICE: THIS DOCUMENT WAIVES THE CLAIMANT'S LIEN, STOP PAYMENT NOTICE, AND PAYMENT BOND RIGHTS EFFECTIVE ON RECEIPT OF PAYMENT. A PERSON SHOULD NOT RELY ON THIS DOCUMENT UNLESS SATISFIED THAT THE CLAIMANT HAS RECEIVED PAYMENT.

rules.applies_to: All claimants and payers on progress payments
rules.quote: This document waives and releases lien, stop payment notice, and payment bond rights the claimant has for labor and service provided, and equipment and material delivered, to the customer on this job through the Through Date of this document.
rules.notes: Form text read from CSLB's PDF (dated 7/1/12). A generator should reproduce the statutory text verbatim; the field list above is the form's 'Identifying Information' and check fields.

rules.title: Unconditional progress waiver - only after payment actually received
rules.plain_english: After a progress payment clears, collect an Unconditional Waiver and Release on Progress Payment stating the amount received. Never sign or demand one before payment: it binds the claimant even if not paid.

parameters.when: after the progress payment has cleared (commonly collected with the next pay app)
exceptions_not_waived: extras for which claimant has not received payment
contract rights incl. rescission, abandonment, breach, and compensation for work not covered by the payment
parameters.header_notice: NOTICE TO CLAIMANT: THIS DOCUMENT WAIVES AND RELEASES LIEN, STOP PAYMENT NOTICE, AND PAYMENT BOND RIGHTS UNCONDITIONALLY AND STATES THAT YOU HAVE BEEN PAID FOR GIVING UP THOSE RIGHTS. THIS DOCUMENT IS ENFORCEABLE AGAINST YOU IF YOU SIGN IT, EVEN IF YOU HAVE NOT BEEN PAID. IF YOU HAVE NOT BEEN PAID, USE A CONDITIONAL WAIVER AND RELEASE FORM.

rules.applies_to: All claimants and payers
rules.quote: THIS DOCUMENT IS ENFORCEABLE AGAINST YOU IF YOU SIGN IT, EVEN IF YOU HAVE NOT BEEN PAID. IF YOU HAVE NOT BEEN PAID, USE A CONDITIONAL WAIVER AND RELEASE FORM.
rules.notes: CSLB consumer guidance (companion research) advises owners they may withhold the next payment until unconditional releases for the previous payment are received.

rules.title: Final waivers: conditional before final payment, unconditional after
rules.plain_english: For the final payment, collect a Conditional Waiver and Release on Final Payment (with check details) before paying, then an Unconditional Waiver and Release on Final Payment stating the claimant has been paid in full. The only exception on the final forms is a stated dollar amount of disputed claims for extras.

sequence: conditional final waiver (Civ. Code 8136) before final payment
unconditional final waiver (Civ. Code 8138) after payment clears
parameters.unconditional_final_statement: The claimant has been paid in full.
parameters.only_exception: Disputed claims for extras in the amount of: $

rules.applies_to: GC, every sub and supplier at closeout; owners/lenders releasing final payment and retention
rules.quote: This document does not affect any of the following: Disputed claims for extras in the amount of: $
rules.notes: Because final forms waive everything except listed disputed extras, a closeout tool should require the claimant to enter any open change-order claims before signing.

rules.title: Waivers release rights on change orders fully signed before the waiver date
rules.plain_english: Every statutory waiver form waives rights for work done under any written change order that was fully signed before the claimant signs the waiver, unless that change order is listed as an exception. Unpaid extras remain protected on progress waivers; on final waivers only the listed disputed-extras amount is preserved.

parameters.rule: rights under change orders fully executed before waiver signature date are waived unless listed as an exception
parameters.progress_waiver_preserves: extras for which the claimant has not received payment
parameters.final_waiver_preserves: only disputed claims for extras in the stated amount
parameters.check: for each CO with executed_date < waiver_signed_date and unpaid: confirm listed as exception or covered by 'extras not paid' exception (progress) / disputed-extras amount (final)

rules.applies_to: Anyone signing or collecting lien waivers on jobs with change orders
rules.quote: Rights based upon labor or service provided, or equipment or material delivered, pursuant to a written change order that has been fully executed by the parties prior to the date that this document is signed by the claimant, are waived and released by this document, unless listed as an Exception below.
rules.notes: Same sentence appears on all four CSLB form PDFs. Ties change-order log to waiver generation.

rules.title: Conditional waiver binds only on evidence of payment
rules.plain_english: A conditional waiver only becomes binding when there is evidence the claimant was paid: the claimant's endorsement on a single or joint check that the bank has paid, or the claimant's written acknowledgment of payment.

evidence_of_payment: claimant's endorsement on a single or joint check paid by the drawee bank
written acknowledgment of payment by claimant

rules.applies_to: Owners, GCs and lenders relying on conditional waivers
rules.quote: In the case of a conditional release, the release is only binding if there is evidence of payment to the claimant.
