rules.title: Apprenticeship violations: up to $100/day; up to $300/day for a knowing repeat within 3 years that denies training; possible debarment
rules.plain_english: A contractor that knowingly violates the apprenticeship requirements (DAS 140, ratio, training funds) faces a civil penalty of up to $100 per full calendar day of noncompliance, and the Labor Commissioner may reduce it if disproportionate. A knowing second or subsequent violation within 3 years carries up to $300 per day when the noncompliance results in apprenticeship training not being provided. For a first-time violation, the Labor Commissioner may instead, with an apprenticeship program's agreement, order the contractor to provide apprentice employment equal to the work hours apprentices would have had during the noncompliance. Debarment is also possible under LC 1777.1(d).

parameters.repeat_trigger: knowing second or subsequent violation within 3 years AND the noncompliance results in apprenticeship training not being provided as required
parameters.first_time_alternative: order equivalent apprentice employment hours (with concurrence of an apprenticeship program) in lieu of the penalty (1777.7(a)(2))

rules.applies_to: Contractors subject to LC 1777.5
rules.source: DIR 'California Prevailing Wage Laws' (rev. Feb. 1, 2025) https://www.dir.ca.gov/public-works/CaliforniaPrevailingWageLaws.pdf PDF p.186 (LC 1777.7); https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/PWManualCombined.pdf (§3.3 and §3.3.1.3, manual pp. 27, 32-33)
rules.quote: If the Labor Commissioner or his or her designee determines after an investigation that a contractor or subcontractor knowingly violated Section 1777.5, the contractor and any subcontractor responsible for the violation shall forfeit, as a civil penalty to the state or political subdivision on whose behalf the contract is made or awarded, not more than one hundred dollars ($100) for each full calendar day of noncompliance. The amount of this penalty may be reduced by the Labor Commissioner if the amount of the penalty would be disproportionate to the severity of the violation. A contractor or subcontractor that knowingly commits a second or subsequent violation within a three-year period, if the noncompliance results in apprenticeship training not being provided as required by this chapter, shall forfeit as a civil penalty the sum of not more than three hundred dollars ($300) for each full calendar day of noncompliance.
rules.notes: LC 1777.7 text read in the DIR compilation (rev. Feb. 1, 2025). SB 909 (Ch. 660, Stats. 2026, chaptered 9/27/2026) amends LC 1725.5, 1771.3, 1775, 1776 and 1777.7 and PCC 2603 per its chaptered title on leginfo (LC 1741 and 1813 appeared only in earlier versions). Final amounts and operative date NOT verified - re-check before 2027.
rules.correction: The $300 tier was overstated. LC 1777.7(a)(1) applies the up-to-$300 per day maximum only to a knowing second or subsequent violation within 3 years where the noncompliance results in apprenticeship training not being provided. The rule said 'two or more violations within 3 years'. Also added: the penalty may be reduced if disproportionate, and (a)(2) allows a first-time alternative of ordering equivalent apprentice employment. The quote was replaced with the statute text. $100 per full calendar day is confirmed. FLAG: SB 909 (Ch. 660, Stats. 2026, chaptered 9/27/2026) amends LC 1725.5, 1771.3, 1775, 1776 and 1777.7 and PCC 2603, per its chaptered title as shown in leginfo search excerpts. The chaptered text and its operative date were not read. The amount here is current law as of 2026-11-25. Re-check it against Ch. 660 before 2027. Rewording 2026-11-27: title and plain_english reworded to match this correction; no value changed.

rules.title: Ratio exemption certificates

(3) There is a showing that the apprenticeable craft or trade is replacing at least one-thirtieth of its journeymen annually through apprenticeship training,

rules.title: Contracts must make the prime responsible for apprenticeship compliance
rules.plain_english: The awarding body must insert contract stipulations implementing LC 1777.5 that fix responsibility for compliance for all apprenticeable occupations on the prime contractor; similarly 1775 and 1776 stipulations must be in the contract.

rules.quote: (n) The body awarding the contract shall cause to be inserted in the contract stipulations to effectuate this section. The stipulations shall fix the responsibility of compliance with this section for all apprenticeable occupations with the prime contractor.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Debarment: fraud (1-3 years) or two willful violations in 3 years (up to 3 years)
rules.plain_english: A contractor found to violate prevailing wage law with intent to defraud is barred from bidding or subcontracting on public works for 1 to 3 years; two or more separate willful violations within 3 years can bring up to 3 years. 'Willful' means it knew or should have known its obligations and deliberately failed or refused to comply.

parameters.extends_to: entities in which contractor has any interest; responsible officers/managers

rules.applies_to: All public works contractors
rules.quote: (e) A willful violation occurs when the contractor or subcontractor knew or reasonably should have known of his or her obligations under the public works law and deliberately fails or deliberately refuses to comply with its provisions.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Debarred list: https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/debar.html (check before listing/hiring subs).

rules.title: Debarment for knowing serious apprenticeship violations (1 yr / 3 yrs)
rules.plain_english: Knowingly committing a serious violation of LC 1777.5 can bar the contractor and its responsible officers for up to 1 year for a first violation and up to 3 years for later violations.
rules.applies_to: Contractors subject to LC 1777.5
rules.quote: the Labor Commissioner may also deny to the contractor or subcontractor, and to its responsible officers, the right to bid on or to be awarded or perform work as a subcontractor on any public works contract for a period of up to one year for the first violation and for a period of up to three years for a second or subsequent violation.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Do not use debarred subcontractors
rules.plain_english: Public works contracts must prohibit the contractor from performing work with a subcontractor ineligible under LC 1777.1 or 1777.7; a subcontract with a debarred sub is reportedly void and public money paid to it must be returned. A listed sub who becomes ineligible may be substituted.
rules.applies_to: Prime and upper-tier contractors
rules.citation: Public Contract Code 6109; PCC 4107(a)(8); Labor Code 1777.1, 1777.7
rules.source: Secondary search snippets of PCC 6109 (leginfo unreachable); PCC 4107(a)(8) read at https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/LawReferenceBook2022.pdf PDF page 1144
rules.notes: PCC 6109 wording differs among third-party reprints; verify. PCC 4107(a)(8) (primary): substitution allowed 'When the listed subcontractor is ineligible to work on a public works project pursuant to Section 1777.1 or 1777.7 of the Labor Code.'

rules.title: Wage assessments must be served within 18 months after notice of completion or acceptance
rules.plain_english: The Labor Commissioner must serve a Civil Wage and Penalty Assessment within 18 months after a valid notice of completion is recorded or the work is accepted, whichever is later; the period is tolled while you fail to produce requested payroll.

parameters.trigger: later of recorded valid notice of completion or acceptance of the public work
tolled_during: awarding body failure to furnish NOC/acceptance

rules.applies_to: Contractors assessing exposure after project close-out
rules.quote: Labor Code § 1741 provides that the CWPA shall be served not later than 18 months after the filing of a valid notice of completion in the office of the county recorder in which the public work was performed, or not later than 18 months after acceptance of the public work, whichever occurs last.
rules.notes: LC 1741(a) text read in the DIR compilation (rev. Feb. 1, 2025) PDF p.143; matches the DLSE Public Works Manual (Oct 2023).

rules.title: Request review of a wage assessment within 60 days or it becomes final
rules.plain_english: If you don't file a written request for a review hearing within 60 days after service of a Civil Wage and Penalty Assessment, it becomes final and can be collected from withheld contract funds or entered as a court judgment.

parameters.if_missed: assessment final; collect from awarding body withholding or court judgment

rules.applies_to: Contractors served with a CWPA
rules.quote: If no hearing is requested “within 60 days after service,” the CWPA becomes final (Labor Code § 1742(a)), and enables the Labor Commissioner to either obtain contract funds withheld by the awarding body or, if insufficient funds have been retained, to enter a court judgment against the contractors served,
rules.notes: LC 1742(a) text read in the DIR compilation (rev. Feb. 1, 2025) PDF p.145; matches the DLSE Public Works Manual.

rules.title: Settlement meeting: request within 30 days of a CWPA
rules.plain_english: Within 30 days after service of a CWPA (or an awarding body's notice of withholding), the contractor may request a settlement meeting, which must be held before the 60-day review deadline; statements made are confidential.
rules.applies_to: Contractors served with a CWPA or notice of withholding
rules.quote: The Labor Commissioner shall, upon receipt of a request from the affected contractor or subcontractor within 30 days following the service of a civil wage and penalty assessment under Section 1741, afford the contractor or subcontractor the opportunity to meet with the Labor Commissioner or his or her designee to attempt to settle a dispute regarding the assessment
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Liquidated damages equal to unpaid wages after 60 days (avoid by escrow deposit)
rules.plain_english: Wages still unpaid 60 days after service of a CWPA or notice of withholding make the contractor, sub and surety liable for liquidated damages equal to those wages. You avoid this by depositing the full assessment (including penalties) with DIR in escrow within the 60 days.

parameters.avoid_by: deposit full assessment incl. penalties with DIR within 60 days

rules.applies_to: Contractors and sureties served with CWPAs
rules.quote: (a) After 60 days following the service of a civil wage and penalty assessment under Section 1741 or a notice of withholding under subdivision (a) of Section 1771.6,, the affected contractor, subcontractor, and surety on a bond or bonds issued to secure the payment of wages covered by the assessment or notice shall be liable for liquidated damages in an amount equal to the wages
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Escrow mail: DIR Attention Cashiering Unit, P.O. Box 420603, San Francisco, CA 94142 (Manual §4.8.4).

rules.title: Joint labor-management committee lawsuits within 18 months
rules.plain_english: A joint labor-management committee may sue an employer that fails to pay prevailing wages or provide payroll records, up to 18 months after the notice of completion or acceptance (whichever is later); courts award back wages, interest and equal liquidated damages.

parameters.trigger: later of recorded notice of completion or acceptance
remedies: liquidated damages equal to unpaid wages

rules.applies_to: Public works employers
rules.quote: This action shall be commenced not later than 18 months after the filing of a valid notice of completion in the office of the county recorder in each county in which the public work or some part thereof was performed, or not later than 18 months after acceptance of the public work, whichever occurs last.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Prop 84-funded projects: CPRs to both DIR and the LCP
rules.plain_english: Projects funded by Proposition 84 still require a DIR-approved labor compliance program; contractors must submit certified payroll to both DIR (eCPR) and the LCP.

parameters.funding_trigger: Proposition 84 (Safe Drinking Water Bond Act of 2006)

rules.applies_to: Contractors on Prop 84 projects
rules.quote: Contractors on these Proposition 84 projects must submit certified payroll records to both the DIR and the LCP.

rules.title: Attorney General action against licenses for unpaid wages; good-faith wage-rate mistake not a violation
rules.plain_english: Effective 2026, the Attorney General may sue to have CSLB suspend, revoke or deny a license when a contractor fails to pay workers wages owed, a wage judgment, or a wage injunction. A good-faith mistake about which wage rate applies (including prevailing wage) is not a violation under this section.

grounds: failure to pay full wages owed

rules.applies_to: CSLB licensees
rules.source: PDF pages 262-263 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (f) A good faith mistake regarding which wage rate applies to a particular category of work, including, but not limited to, for purposes of payment of prevailing wages, shall not constitute a violation under this section.
rules.notes: Added by AB 1002 (Stats 2025 ch 567). B&P 7110 separately makes willful disregard of labor laws grounds for discipline.

rules.title: SB 909 (2026) public works penalty/fee increases - pending verification
rules.plain_english: SB 909 (Ch. 660, Stats. 2026, chaptered 9/27/2026) raises public works penalties. Its chaptered title amends Labor Code 1725.5, 1771.3, 1775, 1776 and 1777.7 and Public Contract Code 2603, and it routes Labor Commissioner penalties to the State Public Works Enforcement Fund. Final amounts and operative dates were not verified; until confirmed, the current amounts in this file apply.

reported_figures_unverified.1813_per_day_usd: 25 -> 35 (Jan 2026 version only; 1813 not in chaptered title)

parameters.operative_date: not verified (2026 non-urgency statutes default to 2027-01-01; LC 1725.5 changes reported operative 2026-07-01)

rules.applies_to: All public works contractors (future amounts)
rules.source: leginfo SB 909 (2025-26) https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billNavClient.xhtml?bill_id=202520260SB909 (search excerpts only); earlier: search-engine summaries of Senate Judiciary/Appropriations analyses
rules.notes: Chaptered title and chaptering confirmed via leginfo search excerpts on 2026-11-25. Section text, amounts and operative dates were not read. Re-verify on leginfo before updating penalty calculators.
rules.correction: Partly wrong section list, now fixed. Leginfo excerpts show the chaptered title amends LC 1725.5, 1771.3, 1775, 1776 and 1777.7 and PCC 2603. LC 1741 and 1813 appeared only in earlier versions, and the rule had omitted 1771.3 and PCC 2603. The chaptered LC 1775 excerpt shows a $56 per day minimum (versus $40 now), which fits the reported 120 -> 168 willful minimum. The $25 -> $35 figure for LC 1813 is from an earlier version and is likely not enacted. Chaptering (Ch. 660, 9/27/2026) is confirmed by the excerpts. The chaptered text and operative dates were not read: the default for a 2026 non-urgency statute is Jan. 1, 2027, and the 1725.5 changes are reported operative July 1, 2026.

rules.title: Skilled & trained workforce (STW) applies only when a statute or the awarding body requires it
rules.plain_english: STW rules (PCC 2600-2603) apply when a specific statute/regulation requires an enforceable STW commitment or the awarding body chooses to require it. They are independent of prevailing wage coverage; bid documents should give notice, but missing notice does not excuse compliance.

triggers: statute or regulation requiring STW commitment (15+ statutes)

rules.applies_to: Contractors/subcontractors (all tiers) on STW-covered projects
rules.quote: Contractors and subcontractors at any tier are required to use a “skilled and trained workforce” to complete a contract or project if required by a statute or regulation, or if an awarding body elects to make it a requirement for a particular project.
rules.notes: DIR STW chart lists the STW statutes: https://www.dir.ca.gov/Public-Works/ADA-Compliant-STW-Chart-without-New-PRC-Provision.pdf

rules.title: STW: every worker in an apprenticeable craft must be a registered apprentice or skilled journeyperson
rules.plain_english: On STW projects, all workers in apprenticeable building trades (programs approved before Jan 1, 2014) must be either DAS-registered apprentices or 'skilled journeypersons' - graduates of an approved apprenticeship program or workers with at least as many on-the-job hours as needed to graduate.

skilled_journeyperson: graduate of CA DAS-approved or out-of-state federally approved program
OJT hours >= hours needed to graduate DAS program
parameters.occupations_covered: apprenticeable occupations with DAS-approved program before 2014-01-01

rules.applies_to: Contractors on STW projects
rules.quote: “Skilled journeypersons,” meaning the worker, in the applicable occupation, either (i) graduated from an in-state, DAS-approved apprenticeship program, or an out-of-state federally-approved apprenticeship program, or (ii) has at least as many hours of on-the-job experience as would be required to graduate from the applicable DAS-approved apprenticeship program.

rules.title: STW minimum graduation requirement: 60% (30% for listed trades; teamsters exempt)
rules.plain_english: At least 60% of skilled journeypersons in each apprenticeable occupation (per contractor, per month) must be apprenticeship graduates; the requirement stays at 30% for acoustical installers, bricklayers, carpenters, cement masons, drywall/lathers, marble masons, modular furniture installers, operating engineers, pile drivers, plasterers, roofers/waterproofers, stone masons, surveyors, terrazzo workers and tile setters; teamsters are excluded. Measure by headcount or hours.

parameters.calc_unit: each contractor/subcontractor, each occupation, each calendar month
calc_methods: % of skilled journeypersons who are graduates
% of skilled-journeyperson hours worked by graduates

rules.applies_to: Contractors on STW projects
rules.quote: The Minimum Graduation Requirements are fixed at 30% for: acoustical installers, bricklayers, carpenters, cement masons, drywall installers or lathers, marble masons, finishers, or setters, modular furniture or systems installers, operating engineers, pile drivers, plasterers, roofers or waterproofers, stone masons, surveyors, terrazzo workers or finishers, and tile layers, setters, and finishers.
rules.notes: Workforces may not be combined across subcontractors. Partial exemption for occupations with no DAS program before 1995 (up to half via pre-program journeypersons).
rules.correction: None. The source FAQ is dated July 2019, and PCC 2601 text was not re-read.

rules.title: STW graduation % does not apply when under 10 hours per month in a craft
rules.plain_english: A contractor is exempt from the graduation percentage for a month and occupation if its skilled journeypersons in that craft work fewer than 10 hours total on the project that month; other STW rules still apply.

parameters.period: calendar month covered by Monthly Compliance Report

rules.applies_to: Contractors/subcontractors on STW projects
rules.quote: A contractor or subcontractor is exempt from the Minimum Percentage Graduation Requirements if, during the calendar month covered by the Monthly Compliance Report, the contractor or subcontractor employs skilled journeypersons who, in total, perform fewer than 10 hours of work in a particular craft on the contract or project.
rules.notes: Example: 9 carpenters x 1 hr = 9 hrs exempt; 4 roofers x 3 hrs = 12 hrs not exempt.
rules.correction: None. The source FAQ is dated July 2019, and PCC 2601 text was not re-read.

rules.title: STW graduation % exemption for small unlisted subs (<= 0.5% of prime contract)
rules.plain_english: A subcontractor is exempt from the graduation percentage while it is not a listed (or substitute-for-listed) subcontractor under PCC 4104 and its subcontract does not exceed one-half of one percent of the prime contract price.
rules.applies_to: Small subcontractors on STW projects
rules.quote: A subcontractor is exempt from meeting the Minimum Graduation Requirements if it meets both of the following: (i) the subcontractor was not a listed subcontractor under Public Contract Code section 4104 or a substitute for a listed subcontractor, and (ii) the subcontract does not exceed one-half of one percent of the price of the prime contract.
rules.correction: None. The source FAQ is dated July 2019, and PCC 2601 text was not re-read.

rules.title: STW Monthly Compliance Report to the awarding body
rules.plain_english: The prime must give the awarding body a Monthly Compliance Report for each month of work showing that it and all subs at every tier met STW requirements; subs must give the prime complete information. Each report covers a calendar month from the start date (e.g., Sept 7 - Oct 7).

parameters.covers: contractor and all subcontractors at every tier
parameters.sub_duty: submit complete STW info to contractor

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and subcontractors on STW projects
rules.quote: The contractor, bidder, or other entity must submit a Monthly Compliance Report to the public entity on a monthly basis for each month while the STW-covered project or contract is being performed. The report covers a calendar month.
rules.notes: Enforceable agreement must commit to PCC 2600-2603 compliance and monthly reports.

rules.title: STW noncompliance: awarding body withholds 150% of monthly billing
rules.plain_english: If a Monthly Compliance Report shows noncompliance, the awarding body withholds 150% of the monthly billing of the noncompliant contractor or sub (all payments if no/incomplete report from the prime); the prime may withhold the same from the offending sub. Payments resume upon a complete report, substitution of the sub with an STW-committed sub, or a Substantial Compliance Plan.

resume_when: offending sub substituted under PCC 4100-4114 with STW commitment
Substantial Compliance Plan submitted (unless timely rejected)

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors and subcontractors on STW projects
rules.quote: Withhold further payments in an amount equal to (1) 150 percent of the value of the monthly billing for the contractor, bidder, or entity that failed to comply with the STW requirements of Public Contract Code sections 2600 – 2603, or (2) 150 percent of the value of the monthly billing for the subcontractor that failed to comply
rules.notes: Awarding body forwards noncompliant reports to the Labor Commissioner.
rules.correction: None. The source FAQ is dated July 2019, and PCC 2602 text was not re-read.

rules.title: STW penalties: up to $5,000/month ($10,000 repeat); debarment up to 3 years
rules.plain_english: STW violations carry civil penalties of up to $5,000 per month of noncompliant work, or up to $10,000 per month for a second or later violation within 3 years; fraud or two willful violations in 3 years can lead to debarment up to 3 years.

debarment_triggers: two or more willful violations within 3 years

rules.applies_to: Contractors/subcontractors on STW projects
rules.quote: The Labor Commissioner can issue a civil penalty of up to $5,000 per month for work performed in violation of Public Contract Code Section 2600-2603. A contractor or subcontractor that commits a second or subsequent violation within a three-year period, may be assessed a civil penalty of up to $10,000 per month.
rules.notes: Penalty factors include whether a Substantial Compliance Plan was submitted and followed.
rules.correction: None. FLAG: SB 909 (Ch. 660, Stats. 2026, chaptered 9/27/2026) amends LC 1725.5, 1771.3, 1775, 1776 and 1777.7 and PCC 2603, per its chaptered title as shown in leginfo search excerpts. The chaptered text and its operative date were not read. The amount here is current law as of 2026-11-25. Re-check it against Ch. 660 before 2027.

rules.title: STW prime safe harbor: include PCC 2600-2603 in subcontracts, monitor, withhold, get declaration
rules.plain_english: A prime avoids liability for a sub's STW penalties only if it: includes a copy of PCC 2600-2603 in the subcontract, periodically monitors the sub's workforce, takes corrective action including retaining 150% of amounts due, and obtains the sub's declaration under penalty of perjury of STW compliance before final payment (and lacked knowledge of the violation).

parameters.subcontract_must_include: copy of Public Contract Code 2600-2603 (Ch. 2.9, Pt. 1, Div. 2)
parameters.declaration_before_final_payment: under penalty of perjury that sub met PCC 2600-2603

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors on STW projects
rules.quote: Include a copy of Chapter 2.9 of Part 1 of Division 2 of the Public Contract Code (sections 2600 - 2603) in contracts executed after January 1, 2019, between the contractor and the subcontractor for work on the STW-covered project;

rules.title: Subcontractor listing: subs over 1/2 of 1% of the bid (streets/highways: greater of 1/2% or $10,000)
rules.plain_english: In a public works bid, the prime must list every subcontractor who will perform work worth more than one-half of 1% of the prime's total bid. For street, highway and bridge bids, list subs over the greater of one-half of 1% or $10,000.

includes: licensed subs who specially fabricate and install per detailed drawings
parameters.formula: list if sub_amount > max(0.005*total_bid, 10000 if streets_highways else 0)

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors bidding public works
rules.quote: in an amount in excess of one-half of 1 percent of the prime contractor’s total bid or, in the case of bids or offers for the construction of streets or highways, including bridges, in excess of one-half of 1 percent of the prime contractor’s total bid or ten thousand dollars ($10,000), whichever is greater.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Listing threshold same 0.5% is used for STW small-sub exemption and PCC 4107(c)/4109.

rules.title: What the subcontractor list must show
rules.plain_english: For each listed sub: name, location of place of business, California contractor license number, DIR public works contractor registration number, and the portion of work it will do. List only one sub for each portion of work.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors bidding public works
rules.quote: (b) The portion of the work that will be done by each subcontractor under this act. The prime contractor shall list only one subcontractor for each portion as is defined by the prime contractor in his or her bid.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Subdivision (a)(1) requires 'The name, the location of the place of business, the California contractor license number, and public works contractor registration number issued pursuant to Section 1725.5 of the Labor Code of each subcontractor'.

rules.title: 24-hour fixes after bid opening for listing errors and extra sub info
rules.plain_english: An inadvertent error in a listed sub's license or DIR registration number is not grounds for protest if the corrected number (matching the listed name and location) is submitted within 24 hours after bid opening. Agencies may also allow other requested sub information (beyond name, location, license and registration numbers) up to 24 hours after the bid deadline.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors bidding public works
rules.quote: (2) An inadvertent error in listing the California contractor license number or public works contractor registration number provided pursuant to paragraph (1) shall not be grounds for filing a bid protest or grounds for considering the bid nonresponsive if the corrected contractor’s license number is submitted to the public entity by the prime contractor within 24 hours after the bid opening
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Unlisted work over 1/2% must be self-performed
rules.plain_english: If the prime doesn't list a sub (or lists more than one) for a portion of work over one-half of 1% of its bid, it is deemed fully qualified and must perform that portion itself; subcontracting it later (except under 4107/4109) triggers 4111 penalties.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors
rules.quote: If a prime contractor fails to specify a subcontractor or if a prime contractor specifies more than one subcontractor for the same portion of work to be performed under the contract in excess of one–half of 1 percent of the prime contractor’s total bid, the prime contractor agrees that he or she is fully qualified to perform that portion himself or herself,
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Allowed grounds to substitute a listed subcontractor
rules.plain_english: After award, a listed sub may be replaced only with the awarding authority's consent for: refusal to sign a subcontract at its bid price/scope; insolvency or bankruptcy; failure/refusal to perform; failure to provide required bonds; inadvertent clerical listing error; no license; substantially unsatisfactory work or delay; debarment under LC 1777.1/1777.7; or not a responsible contractor. Assignment or unauthorized performance by others is also barred.

grounds: fails/refuses to execute written subcontract at bid scope/price
insolvent or bankruptcy order for relief
work substantially unsatisfactory or substantially delaying/disrupting

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors seeking substitution
rules.quote: (a) Substitute a person as subcontractor in place of the subcontractor listed in the original bid, except that the awarding authority, or its duly authorized officer, may, except as otherwise provided in Section 4107.5, consent to the substitution of another person as a subcontractor in any of the following situations:
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Also STW noncompliance can be cured by substitution under 4100-4114.

rules.title: Substitution procedure: notice to listed sub, 5 working days to object, hearing
rules.plain_english: Before approving a substitution, the awarding authority must notify the listed sub in writing by certified or registered mail of the request and reasons. The sub has 5 working days to object in writing (silence = consent); if it objects, the authority gives at least 5 working days' notice of a hearing.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors, listed subs, awarding bodies
rules.quote: The listed subcontractor who has been so notified has five working days within which to submit written objections to the substitution to the awarding authority. Failure to file these written objections constitutes the listed subcontractor’s consent to the substitution.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.
rules.correction: None. Checked against the official 2022 Law Book reprint of the statute (text as of Jan. 1, 2022), which matches. This PCC section is not in the Feb. 2025 DIR compilation, and amendments after 2022 could not be checked because leginfo is not fetchable.

rules.title: Clerical listing error: notice within 2 working days; objections 6; affidavits 8
rules.plain_english: To claim an inadvertent clerical error in listing a sub, the prime must give written notice to the awarding authority, the wrongly listed sub and the intended sub within 2 working days after bid opening. The listed sub has 6 working days from bid opening to object; affidavits from the parties are due within 8 working days.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors
rules.quote: The prime contractor as a condition to assert a claim of inadvertent clerical error in the listing of a subcontractor shall within two working days after the time of the prime bid opening by the awarding authority give written notice to the awarding authority and copies of that notice to both the subcontractor he or she claims to have listed in error and the intended subcontractor
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.
rules.correction: None. Checked against the official 2022 Law Book reprint of the statute (text as of Jan. 1, 2022), which matches. This PCC section is not in the Feb. 2025 DIR compilation, and amendments after 2022 could not be checked because leginfo is not fetchable.

rules.title: No subletting unlisted portions over 1/2% (except change orders or emergencies)
rules.plain_english: Other than for change orders, a prime may not sublet any portion of work over one-half of 1% of its total bid for which no sub was listed; subletting such work is allowed only in a public emergency or necessity with a written public finding. Listed subcontracts may not be assigned or performed by others without consent.

exceptions: change orders
public emergency/necessity with written finding (PCC 4109)

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors
rules.quote: (c) Other than in the performance of “change orders” causing changes or deviations from the original contract, sublet or subcontract any portion of the work in excess of one-half of 1 percent of the prime contractor’s total bid as to which his or her original bid did not designate a subcontractor.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. PCC 4105: listing a contractor who then sublets the majority of the work is circumvention subject to 4110/4111 penalties.

rules.title: Prime may require sub bonds only if specified in the sub-bid request
rules.plain_english: A prime may require a subcontractor's performance and payment bond (from an admitted surety, prime as obligee, at the prime's expense at the standard premium) only if its written or published request for sub-bids clearly states the bond amount and requirements - and whether the sub pays. If the sub then fails to provide it, the prime may reject and substitute.

parameters.sub_fails_to_provide: prime may reject and substitute under 4107

rules.applies_to: Prime contractors soliciting sub-bids; subcontractors
rules.quote: (c)(1) The bond or bonds may be required under this section only if the prime contractor in his or her written or published request for subbids clearly specifies the amount and requirements of the bond or bonds.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. PCC 7201(b)(2) ties sub retention cap exceptions to 4108(c) bond notice.
rules.correction: None. Checked against the official 2022 Law Book reprint of the statute (text as of Jan. 1, 2022), which matches. This PCC section is not in the Feb. 2025 DIR compilation, and amendments after 2022 could not be checked because leginfo is not fetchable.

rules.title: Subletting Act violations: contract cancellation or penalty up to 10% of subcontract; CSLB discipline
rules.plain_english: A prime that violates the Subletting and Subcontracting Fair Practices Act breaches its contract; the awarding authority may cancel the contract or assess a penalty up to 10% of the subcontract involved (after a public hearing with 5 days' notice). It is also grounds for CSLB discipline.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors
rules.source: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/LawReferenceBook2022.pdf PDF page 1148 (Appendix, PCC §§4110-4112); PDF page 351 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (B&P §7110(d))
rules.quote: the awarding authority may exercise the option, in its own discretion, of (1) canceling his or her contract or (2) assessing the prime contractor a penalty in an amount of not more than 10 percent of the amount of the subcontract involved, and this penalty shall be deposited in the fund out of which the prime contract is awarded.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. 2026 Law Book p.351: B&P 7110 lists willful violation of the Subletting Act (PCC 4100 et seq.) as cause for discipline.
rules.correction: None. Checked against the official 2022 Law Book reprint of the statute (text as of Jan. 1, 2022), which matches. This PCC section is not in the Feb. 2025 DIR compilation, and amendments after 2022 could not be checked because leginfo is not fetchable.

rules.title: Late material addenda extend bid closing by at least 72 hours
rules.plain_english: If the agency issues material changes to the bid invitation later than 72 hours before bid closing, the bid deadline must be extended by at least 72 hours. Late bids are returned unopened.

parameters.material_change: substantial cost impact on total bid

rules.applies_to: Bidders and awarding bodies
rules.quote: The date and time shall be extended by no less than 72 hours if the officer, department, board, or commission issues any material changes, additions, or deletions to the invitation later than 72 hours prior to the bid closing. Any bids received after the time specified in the notice or any extension due to material changes shall be returned unopened.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.
rules.correction: None. Checked against the official 2022 Law Book reprint of the statute (text as of Jan. 1, 2022), which matches. This PCC section is not in the Feb. 2025 DIR compilation, and amendments after 2022 could not be checked because leginfo is not fetchable.

rules.title: Noncollusion declaration required with every public works bid
rules.plain_english: Every bid on a public entity's public works contract must include a noncollusion declaration signed under penalty of perjury in the statutory form, stating the bid is genuine and not collusive, with the signer's title, date, city and state.

parameters.required_with: every bid on every public works contract of a public entity
parameters.form_title: NONCOLLUSION DECLARATION TO BE EXECUTED BY BIDDER AND SUBMITTED WITH BID

rules.applies_to: All public works bidders
rules.quote: The bid is not made in the interest of, or on behalf of, any undisclosed person, partnership, company, association, organization, or corporation. The bid is genuine and not collusive or sham. The bidder has not directly or indirectly induced or solicited any other bidder to put in a false or sham bid.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Full statutory form text is on PDF pages 1164-1165 - a tool can generate it verbatim.

rules.title: Bid security on state contracts: at least 10% of the bid
rules.plain_english: Bids on State Contract Act projects must be sealed and include bidder's security of at least 10% of the bid: an admitted surety bid bond (signed or electronic via approved registry), cash, cashier's check or certified check payable to the department director. Bids without security are not considered.

forms: electronic bid bond by admitted surety via approved registry
signed bid bond by admitted surety

rules.applies_to: Bidders on state agency public works
rules.quote: (b) The required bidder’s security shall be in an amount equal to at least 10 percent of the amount bid. A bid shall not be considered unless one of the forms of bidder’s security is enclosed with it.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Bid security is forfeited if the low bidder fails to execute the contract, including for lack of proper license (PCC 10164).
rules.correction: None. Checked against the official 2022 Law Book reprint of the statute (text as of Jan. 1, 2022), which matches. This PCC section is not in the Feb. 2025 DIR compilation, and amendments after 2022 could not be checked because leginfo is not fetchable.

rules.title: Bid security on local agency contracts (commonly 10%)
rules.plain_english: Cities, counties, special districts and school districts generally require bid security (bid bond, cash or check); several city/district statutes set it at 10% of the bid, and school districts set it in the bid documents (commonly 10%). Check each solicitation.
rules.applies_to: Bidders on local agency public works
rules.source: Secondary search snippets (leginfo unreachable); e.g., california.public.law and district bidding guides
rules.notes: Figures from search-engine excerpts only. Bid documents control the required amount and form; verify the statute for each agency type.
rules.correction: Not refuted. The excerpts show PCC 20111 (school districts) lists cash, cashier's check, certified check or admitted-surety bidder's bond with security 'as the board requires' (no fixed %), and unsuccessful bidders' security is returned within 60 days of award. City and Improvement Act sections (e.g., 20413, 20483) set at least 10%. Primary text was not read.

rules.title: CSLB license required to bid public works; unlicensed bids rejected, contracts void
rules.plain_english: Submitting a bid to a public agency without a contractor's license is a misdemeanor (with limited exceptions). Unlicensed bids are nonresponsive and must be rejected; local agencies must verify the license before award; contracts with unlicensed contractors are void. Repeat offenders face a fine of the greater of 20% of the contract price or $4,500, and/or 10 days to 6 months in jail.

exceptions: persons exempt from license law
state projects under PCC 10164 (federal funds)
local projects under PCC 20103.5
joint venture license timing (B&P 7029.1)

rules.applies_to: All bidders on public agency contracts
rules.source: PDF pages 252-253 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (e) Unless one of the foregoing exceptions applies, a bid submitted to a public agency by a contractor who is not licensed in accordance with this chapter shall be considered nonresponsive and shall be rejected by the public agency.
rules.notes: Same section: 'Any contract awarded to, or any purchase order issued to, a contractor who is not licensed pursuant to this chapter is void.'

rules.title: Federal-aid state projects: bid OK without CA license, but must be licensed at award
rules.plain_english: On state projects involving federal funds, a bid isn't invalid because the bidder lacks a California license, but the contractor must be properly licensed in the right classification when the contract is awarded, or it forfeits its bid security.

parameters.failure_consequence: treated as failure to execute contract; forfeiture of bidder's security

rules.applies_to: Bidders on federally funded state projects
rules.quote: In all state projects where federal funds are involved, no bid submitted shall be invalidated by the failure of the bidder to be licensed in accordance with the laws of this state. However, at the time the contract is awarded, the contractor shall be properly licensed in accordance with the laws of this state.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. PCC 20103.5 (local agencies) text exists in the 2022 appendix p.1173 but was not separately excerpted here.

rules.title: Licensees may bid jointly before getting a joint venture license
rules.plain_english: Two or more licensed contractors may submit a joint bid before obtaining a joint venture license, but must have the joint venture license before being awarded the contract and acting jointly; failure to get it doesn't excuse bid-default penalties.
rules.applies_to: Contractors teaming on public bids
rules.source: PDF page 255 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: (b) Prior to obtaining a joint venture license, contractors licensed in accordance with this chapter may jointly bid for the performance of work covered by this section.

rules.title: Public works: awarding authority sets required license class; specialty prime must hold majority class
rules.plain_english: The awarding authority determines the license classification needed to bid and perform a public works project using CSLB's classifications. A specialty contractor may not get the prime contract unless its classification covers a majority of the project, and work outside its specialty (other than incidental and supplemental work) must go to licensed subs per the Subletting Act.

parameters.classification_set_by: awarding authority using CSLB regs (16 CCR Div. 8)
parameters.outside_specialty_work: licensed subcontractor per PCC 4100 et seq.

rules.applies_to: Specialty and general contractors bidding public works
rules.source: PDF page 278 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: In no case shall the awarding authority award a prime contract to a specialty contractor whose classification constitutes less than a majority of the project.
rules.notes: Amended by SB 1455 (Stats 2024 ch 485) eff. 1/1/2025; CSLB Summer 2026 newsletter confirms agencies must use CSLB classification descriptions.

rules.title: State agencies verify license classification before award (every 2 years)
rules.plain_english: Before awarding a contract, a state agency must verify with CSLB that the contractor holds a classification appropriate to the work (once every two years per contractor), or accept the pocket license plus a sworn statement that it is current, valid and in the right classification.

parameters.alternative: pocket license/certificate + statement under penalty of perjury

rules.applies_to: Contractors bidding state agency work
rules.quote: (a) A state agency, as defined in Section 10335.7 that is subject to this code, shall, prior to awarding a contract for work to be performed by a contractor, as defined by Section 7026 of the Business and Professions Code, verify with the Contractors State License Board that the person seeking the contract is licensed in a classification appropriate to the work to be undertaken.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.

rules.title: Public contract delay damages unenforceable unless liquidated
rules.plain_english: In public works contracts entered on or after Jan 1, 2016 (not state departments under PCC 10106), a clause making the contractor liable for delay damages is unenforceable unless the damages are liquidated to a set amount stated in the contract; no delay damages after notice of completion/acceptance.

parameters.must_be: liquidated to a set amount and identified in contract

rules.applies_to: Contractors reviewing public works contracts
rules.quote: (a) A public works contract entered into on or after January 1, 2016, that contains a clause that expressly requires a contractor to be responsible for delay damages is not enforceable unless the delay damages have been liquidated to a set amount and identified in the public works contract.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments.
rules.correction: None. Checked against the official 2022 Law Book reprint of the statute (text as of Jan. 1, 2022), which matches. This PCC section is not in the Feb. 2025 DIR compilation, and amendments after 2022 could not be checked because leginfo is not fetchable.

rules.title: State contracts: pay subs within 7 days of each progress payment (PCC 10262)
rules.plain_english: On state agency contracts, the prime must pay each subcontractor its share within seven days after receiving each progress payment; diversion is grounds for action and CSLB discipline, and subs must notify CSLB and the department in writing of underpayments.
rules.applies_to: Prime contractors on state agency contracts
rules.source: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/LawReferenceBook2022.pdf PDF page 1172 (Appendix, PCC §10262); PDF page 349 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book (B&P §7108.5(e))
rules.quote: The contractor shall pay to his or her subcontractors, within seven days of receipt of each progress payment, the respective amounts allowed the contractor on account of the work performed by his or her subcontractors, to the extent of each subcontractor’s interest therein.
rules.notes: Statute text read from the official CSLB 2022 Law Book appendix (statutes as published Jan. 2022); leginfo.legislature.ca.gov could not be reached to confirm later amendments. Overlaps lien/payment research (bp-7108-5-pay-subs-7-days). B&P 7108.5 applies to all public works 'except where Section 10262 of the Public Contract Code applies.'
rules.correction: None. Checked against the official 2022 Law Book reprint of the statute (text as of Jan. 1, 2022), which matches. This PCC section is not in the Feb. 2025 DIR compilation, and amendments after 2022 could not be checked because leginfo is not fetchable.

rules.title: Payment bond required on public works over $25,000
rules.plain_english: A direct contractor awarded a public works contract over $25,000 must furnish a payment bond (reportedly at least 100% of the contract) before starting work; the agency's bid call must say a payment bond is required, and the agency cannot pay the contractor's claims if no approved bond is given.

parameters.no_bond_consequence: public entity may not pay contractor's claims (CC 9552)

rules.applies_to: Direct (prime) contractors on public works
rules.source: Secondary: search-engine excerpts of leginfo/Justia text (leginfo unreachable)
rules.notes: Overlaps lien/payment research rules public-payment-bond-required-25000 and public-payment-bond-amount-100pct (also unverified). State-entity contracts under PCC 7103 have their own bond rules. The 2026 CSLB Law Book (PDF page 42) only describes bonds generally.
rules.correction: Not refuted. The excerpts report: more than $25,000; bond given before commencing work; 100% of the contract (9554(a)); no payment of the contractor's claims without an approved bond (9552); design professionals exempt; state-entity contracts under PCC 7103 excluded. FLAG: the 'bid_call_must_state' parameter did not appear in the excerpts. Primary text was not read.

rules.title: Performance vs. payment bonds and typical cost (1-2%)
rules.plain_english: A performance bond guarantees the project gets completed per plans and specs; a payment bond assures labor and material claimants get paid. Bonds typically cost about 1-2% of the contract price - include this cost in bids.

parameters.payment_bond: assures payment of labor and material claims
parameters.surety_max_liability: face amount unless surety takes over completion

rules.applies_to: Contractors pricing bonded public work
rules.citation: CSLB Law Book Ch. 3 (Managing a Business) - Bonds
rules.source: PDF page 42 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Bonds can be obtained from bonding companies for a percentage of the contract price, usually in the one to two percent range. This requirement is the cost of doing business that should be recognized when the bid is submitted.
rules.notes: Educational text, not statute. Performance bond amounts/thresholds are set by agency statute or bid documents (not verified here).

rules.title: Government bids may require DVBE/minority/women business participation steps
rules.plain_english: Federal, state and local agencies, utilities and some private owners may require bidders to take specific steps to meet minority, women and disabled veteran business enterprise (DVBE) goals; check the solicitation and DGS's Office of Small Business and DVBE Services.

parameters.contact: DGS Procurement Division, Office of Small Business and DVBE Services (OSDS), (916) 376-5000, OSDSHelp@dgs.ca.gov

rules.applies_to: Contractors bidding government contracts
rules.citation: CSLB Law Book Ch. 3 - Bidding on Government Contracts
rules.source: PDF page 82 of the 2026 CSLB Law Book
rules.quote: Contractors bidding in California should know that there are a variety of federal, state, and local governmental agencies, as well as public utilities and private corporations, which may require a bidder to take specific steps to achieve established minority, women, and disabled veteran business enterprise (DVBE) goals.
rules.notes: Educational text in the official law book.

rules.title: State contracting goals: 3% DVBE participation, 25% small business
rules.plain_english: State agencies must aim to award at least 3% of annual contract dollars to certified DVBEs and at least 25% to certified small businesses (including microbusinesses); state solicitations often include a DVBE participation requirement or incentive that bidders must meet or document good-faith efforts for.

parameters.solicitation_specific_goal: may be above or below 3% (2 CCR 1896.70, reported)

rules.applies_to: Contractors bidding state agency contracts
rules.citation: Military & Veterans Code 999 et seq.; Public Contract Code 10115; Government Code 14838
rules.source: Secondary: search-engine summaries of DGS, LAO and code reprints (dgs.ca.gov, lao.ca.gov not reachable)
rules.notes: Not read from primary text. Certification through DGS OSDS. Verify the solicitation's DVBE requirement, incentive and documentation (e.g., DVBE declarations) per bid.
rules.correction: Not refuted. The excerpts state a minimum 25% small business (incl. microbusiness) participation goal (Gov. Code 14838(a)) and a 3% DVBE goal (M&VC 999.2 / SCM). FLAG: the 'sb_goal_codified_effective: 2023-01-01' date was not confirmed. Primary text was not read.

rules.title: Electricians working for a C-10 contractor must be DIR-certified
rules.plain_english: Anyone who does electrical work as an electrician for a C-10 electrical contractor must hold a state electrician certification (or be a registered apprentice or registered electrician trainee). Uncertified people may not do electrical work that requires certification. The rule follows the employer's license: it covers C-10 contractors only.

alternatives_to_certification: registered electrician trainee under supervision (LC 108.4; 8 CCR 296.3)
parameters.certifying_agency: DIR Labor Commissioner's Office (DLSE) Electrician Certification Unit

rules.applies_to: Workers doing electrical work (connections of 100 volt-amperes or more) for a CSLB class C-10 electrical contractor, and the C-10 contractors who employ them
rules.source: https://www.cslb.ca.gov/Resources/GuidesAndPublications/LawReferenceBook2022.pdf (CSLB Law Book 2022, Appendix - Labor Code Ch. 4.5, PDF pages 919-920, printed pages 886-887)
rules.quote: (b) (1) Certification is required only for those persons who perform work as electricians for contractors licensed as class C-10 electrical contractors under the Contractors' State License Board Rules and Regulations.
rules.notes: Statute text read from CSLB's published Law Book appendix (2022 edition; history line 'Added Stats 2012 ch 46 § 79 (SB 1038), effective June 27, 2012', no later amendment shown). leginfo.legislature.ca.gov was not accessed. DIR's ECU FAQ (revised October 22, 2026) quotes the same subdivision. Subdivision (a): 'Persons who perform work as electricians shall become certified pursuant to Section 108. Uncertified persons shall not perform electrical work for which certification is required.'

rules.title: Who counts as an 'electrician': connections of 100 volt-amperes or more for a C-10
rules.plain_english: 'Electrician' means anyone who connects electrical devices for a C-10 electrical contractor. Connections under 100 volt-amperes are not covered. Also excluded: utility work covered by B&P 7042.5, work normally done by stationary engineers, and temporary or portable equipment run by technicians in theater, film, TV, hotel, exhibition or trade-show work.

excluded_work: public utility work to which B&P 7042.5 applies
electrical work ordinarily and customarily performed by stationary engineers
temporary or portable electrical equipment work by technicians in the theatrical, motion picture production, television, hotel, exhibition or trade show industries

rules.applies_to: Workers doing electrical work (connections of 100 volt-amperes or more) for a CSLB class C-10 electrical contractor, and the C-10 contractors who employ them
rules.citation: Labor Code 108(c) (as quoted by DIR); 8 CCR 290.0
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/ecu/ECU_FAQ.htm ('Who is required to be certified?' - Labor Code section 108 (c)); also https://www.dir.ca.gov/t8/290_0.html
rules.quote: As used in this section, "electricians" includes all persons who engage in the connection of electrical devices for electrical contractors licensed pursuant to Section 7058 of the Business and Professions Code, specifically, contractors classified as electrical contractors in the Contractors' State License Board Rules and Regulations. This section does not apply to electrical connections under 100 volt-amperes.
rules.notes: Labor Code 108(c) text as reproduced on the official DIR ECU FAQ page (leginfo blocked). FAQ short answer: 'All electricians who make connections of greater than 100 volt amps who work for C-10 Contractors.' FAQ also says a foreman who sometimes works with the tools must be certified. A September 2026 CSLB board analysis paraphrases the threshold as 'over 100 volts'; the statute and 8 CCR 290.0 say volt-amperes. Only employees of C-10 licensed contractors are covered; electricians employed directly by a school district or plant are not (FAQ).

rules.title: No electrician certification needed for C-7 or C-45 scope work
rules.plain_english: Workers doing work for a C-7 (low voltage systems) or C-45 (electric sign) contractor do not need electrician certification as long as the work stays within the C-7 or C-45 license scope (including incidental and supplemental work), even if the same company also holds a C-10 license.
rules.applies_to: Workers of C-7 low voltage and C-45 electric sign contractors
rules.quote: (2) Certification is not required for persons performing work for contractors licensed as class C-7 low voltage systems or class C-45 electric sign contractors as long as the work performed is within the scope of the class C-7 or class C-45 license, including incidental and supplemental work as defined in Section 7059 of the Business and Professions Code, and regardless of whether the same contractor is also licensed as a class C-10 contractor.
rules.notes: Same text quoted on DIR ECU FAQ. Work outside the C-7/C-45 scope for a C-10 contractor still needs certification.

rules.title: Utility high-voltage transmission and distribution workers are exempt
rules.plain_english: Workers on high-voltage transmission or distribution systems owned by a utility do not need electrician certification when they are employed by the utility or by a licensed contractor that mainly installs or maintains transmission or distribution systems.

parameters.exempt_system: high-voltage electrical transmission or distribution system owned by a utility (PUC 224.3, 218, 205, 204)
exempt_employers: licensed contractor principally engaged in installing or maintaining transmission or distribution systems

rules.applies_to: Line and transmission/distribution contractors and their workers
rules.quote: (3) Certification is not required for work performed by a worker on a high-voltage electrical transmission or distribution system owned by a local publicly owned electric utility, as defined in Section 224.3 of the Public Utilities Code;
rules.notes: The subdivision continues: 'an electrical corporation, as defined in Section 218 of the Public Utilities Code; a person, as defined in Section 205 ...; or a corporation, as defined in Section 204 ...; when the worker is employed by the utility or a licensed contractor principally engaged in installing or maintaining transmission or distribution systems.'

rules.title: Registered electrical apprentices are exempt; may test in the last year
rules.plain_english: Registered apprentices doing electrical work in a state- or federally-approved apprenticeship program do not need certification. An apprentice within one year of finishing may take the certification exam and becomes certified as soon as the apprenticeship ends. The C-10 contractor must still supervise apprentices properly.

parameters.certified_upon: completion of apprenticeship term after passing exam
approved_programs: state program authorized by federal Office of Apprenticeship

rules.applies_to: Workers doing electrical work (connections of 100 volt-amperes or more) for a CSLB class C-10 electrical contractor, and the C-10 contractors who employ them
rules.quote: An apprentice who is within one year of completion of his or her term of apprenticeship shall be permitted to take the certification examination and, upon passing the examination, shall be certified immediately upon completion of the term of apprenticeship.
rules.notes: Willful failure to supervise apprentices is a separate CSLB discipline ground (LC 108.2(h)(3)). Registered apprentices are not counted as uncertified persons for the trainee supervision ratio (8 CCR 296.3(a)).

rules.title: Only the C-10 qualifying person is exempt; partners, officers and C-10 holders working as employees are not
rules.plain_english: The person who qualifies the C-10 license (the one who passed the CSLB exam) may do electrical work for that company and supervise trainees without state electrician certification. Partners or officers who are not the qualifier must be certified, and a C-10 license holder working as an employee under another C-10 contractor's license must be certified.
rules.applies_to: C-10 contractors, their qualifiers, officers, partners and employees
rules.quote: (g) Notwithstanding subdivision (a), the qualifying person for a class C-10 electrical contractor license issued by the Contractors' State License Board need not also be certified pursuant to Section 108 to perform electrical work for that licensed contractor or to supervise an uncertified person employed by that licensed contractor pursuant to Section 108.4.
rules.notes: DIR FAQ: 'Only the qualifying person, (meaning the person who took the contractor's license examination), may perform electrical work under that license without a state electrician certificate. Partners and officers of the company who did not sit for the licensing exam, must obtain State Electrician Certification to perform work for which certification is required.' and 'Note that if you are a licensed C-10 contractor but working under another C-10 contractor's license as an employee you must be certified.'

rules.title: Five electrician certification types; General covers all
rules.plain_english: DIR issues five certifications: General Electrician, Residential Electrician, Voice Data Video Technician, Fire/Life Safety Technician and Nonresidential Lighting Technician. Each lets the holder do certified work within that category. A General Electrician certification covers work in all categories.
rules.applies_to: Workers doing electrical work (connections of 100 volt-amperes or more) for a CSLB class C-10 electrical contractor, and the C-10 contractors who employ them
rules.quote: (a) An applicant may apply for certification as a General Electrician, a Residential Electrician, a Voice Data Video Technician, a Fire/Life Safety Technician or a Nonresidential Lighting Technician.
rules.notes: 8 CCR 291.0(b): 'Certification as a General Electrician allows one to lawfully perform work for which certification is required in all categories.' Labor Code 108.2(c) requires DIR to maintain these separate certifications. The gap list's 'Voltage Data Signal' label is DIR's 'Voice Data Video Technician'.

rules.title: Residential Electrician scope: dwellings served at 120/208 or 120/240 V
rules.plain_english: A Residential Electrician may work on homes and multifamily buildings (including hotels and motels) whose main use is residential and whose utility service is no more than 3-phase, 4-wire 120/208 or 120/240 volts. They may install panels and feeders for commercial tenant space only if under 50% of the first floor is commercial, may not do the tenant improvements, and may not work in NEC Article 517 (health care) occupancies.
rules.applies_to: Residential Electrician certificate holders and the C-10 contractors who assign them work
rules.quote: performs work for a C-10 electrical contractor installing, constructing, or maintaining any electrical system that is covered by the National Electrical Code in single family homes and multi family units, including hotels and motels, where the primary occupancy of the building is considered residential and the maximum voltage received from a utility company is a 3 phase, 4 wire, 120/208 or 120/240 volts.
rules.notes: 8 CCR 290.1 references the 1999 National Electrical Code for article numbers.

rules.title: Scopes of Fire/Life Safety, Voice Data Video and Nonresidential Lighting technicians
rules.plain_english: Fire/Life Safety Technicians work on NEC Article 760 (fire alarm) systems. Voice Data Video Technicians work on systems under NEC Articles 725, 770 (non-composite cables), 800 (non-hybrid cables), 810 and 820. Nonresidential Lighting Technicians repair, service and maintain existing nonresidential lighting fixtures and install retrofit fixtures; they may not install or alter branch circuits, except reconnecting to existing power within 3 feet.
rules.applies_to: Specialty electrician certificate holders and their C-10 employers
rules.quote: Such work does not include the installation of branch circuits or the alteration of existing branch circuits except a Nonresidential Lighting Technician may reconnect to existing power within 3 feet.
rules.notes: Voice Data Video definition: 'performs work for a C-10 electrical contractor installing, constructing or maintaining any system that falls within the scope of National Electrical Code, Articles 725, 770 (non-composite cables only), 800 (non-hybrid cables only), 810 and 820.' Fire/Life Safety: 'installation, construction or maintenance of systems covered by Article 760 of the National Electrical Code.'

rules.title: On-the-job hours needed to sit for each certification exam
rules.plain_english: To take the exam without an apprenticeship, you need documented work for a C-10 contractor: 8,000 hours (General), 4,800 (Residential), 4,000 (Voice Data Video), 4,000 (Fire/Life Safety) or 2,000 (Nonresidential Lighting). Completing a state- or federally-approved apprenticeship in that classification also qualifies.

parameters.alternative: completion of approved apprenticeship in the classification

rules.applies_to: Applicants for electrician certification
rules.quote: General Electrician: 8000 hours of work for a C-10 electrical contractor installing, constructing or maintaining electrical systems covered by the National Electrical Code.
rules.notes: Residential: 'Residential Electrician: 4800 hours of work for a C-10 electrical contractor ...'. Nonresidential Lighting: '2,000 hours of work installing, repairing and maintaining nonresidential lighting while employed by a C-10 electrical contractor engaged in the business of nonresidential lighting maintenance and retrofit installations.' Same figures on DIR page https://www.dir.ca.gov/DLSE/ECU/EleCat.html.

rules.title: Maximum hours per work area that count toward the experience total
rules.plain_english: Not all hours count equally. For General Electrician, the 8,000 hours must come from at least two work areas, with caps such as 300 hours stock room, 3,000 residential wiring, 6,000 commercial, 6,000 industrial, 1,500 voice/data/video, 750 underground conduit, 1,500 troubleshooting, 600 finish work and 600 fire/life safety. Other types have their own caps.
rules.applies_to: Applicants documenting on-the-job experience
rules.quote: The 8000 hours must consist of work in two or more of the following areas, and the maximum number of hours in a particular area that may be counted toward the 8000 hour total are as follows:
rules.notes: Residential, VDV, FLS and NRLT hours may come from 'one or more' areas.

rules.title: NICET Fire Alarm Level II or higher satisfies Fire/Life Safety experience
rules.plain_english: For the Fire/Life Safety Technician certification, NICET certification in Fire Alarm Systems at Level II or above can be used instead of the 4,000 documented hours.
rules.applies_to: Fire alarm installers working for C-10 contractors
rules.quote: The experience requirement for Fire/Life Safety Technician may also be satisfied by proof of NICET certification in Fire Alarm Systems at Level II or above.
rules.notes: The exam must still be passed.

rules.title: Out-of-state license, military or C-7 experience can count toward eligibility
rules.plain_english: DIR may treat an electrician license from another state as meeting the experience requirement if that state's requirements are comparable. Military experience or relevant work for a C-7 low voltage contractor can be credited toward some or all of the hours on request.
rules.applies_to: Applicants with out-of-state, military or C-7 experience
rules.quote: (b) Where an applicant holds a license as an electrician in another state and it is determined by the Chief DAS that the requirements for experience to hold a license in that state are comparable to the requirements of Section 291.1(a)(1) or Section 291.1(a)(2), the Chief may deem the applicant to have the required experience for certification.
rules.notes: DIR FAQ: 'Your electrician's license acquired from other states will make you eligible to sit for the test.' The regulation still names DAS; the program is now run by DLSE.

rules.title: No grace period: out-of-state electricians must be certified before working
rules.plain_english: An electrician coming from another state must be California-certified before starting work for a C-10 contractor. There is no grace period, even for a short job.
rules.applies_to: C-10 contractors bringing in out-of-state electricians
rules.citation: Labor Code 108.2(a) as applied by DIR ECU FAQ
rules.quote: Yes, out of state electricians need to be certified before they can start working in California, there is no grace period.
rules.notes: FAQ also: 'All electricians working for C-10 licensed contractors should be certified regardless of the length of the project.'

rules.title: Certification application must include a Social Security employment history report
rules.plain_english: When applying for electrician certification you must attach an employment history (earnings) report from the Social Security Administration as proof of experience. You may black out your Social Security number.

parameters.required_attachment: Social Security Administration employment history report

rules.applies_to: Applicants for electrician certification
rules.quote: (4) Individuals desiring to be certified shall submit an application for certification and examination that includes an employment history report from the Social Security Administration.
rules.notes: DIR FAQ: requirement effective 1/1/2012 (AB 1346); choose option #1 on SSA-7050 (detailed earnings with employer names). The FAQ says SSA charges a fee for the report; the dollar amount stated by DIR ($115) is SSA's fee and was not checked on ssa.gov (blocked).

rules.title: Certification application and exam fee: $175 ($75 + $100)
rules.plain_english: Applying for electrician certification costs $75 plus $100 for the exam, $175 total. The fees are not refunded once your application is accepted, and missing your test date forfeits them. If DIR finds the application deficient or short on proof of experience, it returns the application and refunds all fees. Each retake costs another $100.
rules.applies_to: Applicants for electrician certification
rules.quote: (a) The fee for initially applying for certification is $75.00.
rules.notes: 292.0(b): 'The fee for taking or retaking the examination is $100.00.' DIR FAQ: 'The fee is $175 ($100 exam fee and $75 administration fee - NOT REFUNDABLE).' A missed exam date forfeits fees; the applicant then pays both the $75 and $100 again (FAQ).
rules.correction: The $75 application fee, $100 exam fee, $175 total, $100 retake fee and payee are confirmed. The unqualified "refundable": false conflicts with 8 CCR 291.2(e): when an application is deficient or lacks enough proof of experience, DAS returns the application and refunds all fees. The FAQ's 'NOT REFUNDABLE' covers other cases, and missing the test date forfeits the fees. Replaced refundable with refundable_once_accepted = false, refund_if_application_deficient = true and missed_exam_forfeits_fees = true. Added 291.2(e) to the citation. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction (8 CCR 291.2(e) at https://www.dir.ca.gov/t8/291_2.html and the ECU FAQ re-read on 2026-11-27); no value changed.

rules.title: Electrician certification renewal fee: $100 per certificate
rules.plain_english: Renewing an electrician certification costs $100 for each certificate renewed, paid by check or money order to the DIR Electrician Certification Fund.
rules.applies_to: Certified electricians
rules.quote: (c) The fee for renewal of certification is $100.00.
rules.notes: FAQ: 'Submit application along with payment of $100 per Certificate being renewed.'

rules.title: Lapsed (expired) certification: $200 and the exam must be retaken
rules.plain_english: If a certification expires, the electrician must retake and pass the exam; DIR charges $200 (the $100 exam fee plus the $100 renewal fee). The 32 hours of continuing education is not required in that case.
rules.applies_to: Electricians whose certification expired
rules.quote: The fee for renewal for lapsed/expired certification card is $200.00.
rules.notes: DIR fees page revised January 24, 2019 (fee start date not stated). FAQ: 'If you are renewing after your card expired, you do not need to fulfill the 32 hours requirement for continuing education. You must retake the exam and pass or you will be illegally working.'

rules.title: Electrician trainee registration: $25; annual renewal is free
rules.plain_english: Registering as an electrician trainee costs $25 (check or money order to the DIR Electrician Certification Fund). The yearly trainee renewal has no fee. Re-registering after withdrawing from school costs another $25.
rules.applies_to: Electrician trainees
rules.quote: (d) The fee for registering as an Electrician Trainee Registrant is $25.00.
rules.notes: 296.1(e): renewal requirements are the same as registration 'except that no fee is required for renewal'. FAQ: re-applying after withdrawal requires a new registration form and a $25.00 fee with current proof of enrollment.

rules.title: Replacement certification card: $30
rules.plain_english: A lost or damaged electrician certification card can be replaced for $30 (30% of the renewal fee) with a written request including current address and phone.
rules.applies_to: Certified electricians
rules.quote: Such request shall be in writing and accompanied with a current address and phone number and replacement fee in the amount of 30% of the renewal fee specified in Section 292.0(c).
rules.notes: DIR fee page: 'The fee for lost/stolen or replacement card is $30.00.'

rules.title: DIR must answer a certification application within 30 days
rules.plain_english: Within 30 days after receiving an application, DIR must tell the applicant in writing whether they are eligible to take the exam or what is missing. A deficient application is returned with fees refunded.

parameters.trigger: receipt of application

rules.applies_to: Applicants for electrician certification
rules.quote: (e) Within 30 days of the receipt of an application, the DAS shall inform the applicant in writing whether the applicant is eligible to take the certification examination, or whether the application is deficient or the applicant has not submitted sufficient proof of experience to take the certification examination.
rules.notes: FAQ: if no letter within 4-6 weeks, call (510) 286-3900. Applications can now be filed online (ECU page) except trainee registrations, which are still by mail.

rules.title: Take the exam within 1 year of the eligibility notice or reapply
rules.plain_english: After DIR says you are eligible, you have one year to take the exam. Retakes are allowed within that year but at least 60 days apart, paying the exam fee each time. After the year runs out, you must file a new application and pay the fees again.

parameters.window_starts: date of the notification of eligibility to take the examination

rules.applies_to: Applicants for electrician certification
rules.quote: An applicant may take the test as many times as he or she wishes under one application for one year following the date of the notification of eligibility to take the examination so long as there is at least 60 days between each sitting.
rules.notes: 291.2(e): 'If the applicant does not take the examination within one year after being notified by DAS of eligibility to take the examination, the applicant must submit a new application to DAS and pay the required application and testing fee again.' Search results (not an official source) suggest AB 1707 (2026) shortens the retest wait; not verified, so the 60-day rule stays.
rules.correction: The regulation gives 'one year following the date of the notification of eligibility', not 365 days.
