Replaced eligibility_window_days: 365 with eligibility_window_years: 1 and window_starts, so a calculator adds one calendar year (365 days is a day short across a leap day). The 60-day gap between sittings, the $100 fee per sitting and the new-application-plus-$175 rule are confirmed.

rules.title: Exam: multiple choice, open book, 70% to pass
rules.plain_english: The certification exam is a computer-based, open-book, multiple-choice test available in English and Spanish. You need at least 70% to pass. General: 100 questions in 4 hours; Residential: 80 questions in 3 hours; Fire/Life Safety, Voice Data Video and Nonresidential Lighting: 50 questions in 2 hours each. Bring valid state photo ID or you forfeit your fees.
rules.applies_to: Electrician certification exam candidates
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/ecu/ECU_FAQ.htm ('I have questions about the test' and 'What if I fail the test?')
rules.quote: A minimum score of 70% is required to pass the test.
rules.notes: FAQ: exams are administered by CPS HR Consulting via Pearson VUE (new scheduling procedures for exams on or after June 1, 2026 per ECU page). The FAQ elsewhere still mentions PSI for lapsed-card retests, which looks out of date.

rules.title: Renew every 3 years with 32 hours of education and 2,000 hours worked
rules.plain_english: Electrician certification lasts three years. To renew you must show 32 hours of continuing education from an approved provider relevant to your certification and swear you worked 2,000 hours in the industry in the past three years. The same education hours can count for more than one certification.

parameters.ce_must_be_from: DIR-listed continuing education provider or approved apprenticeship program

rules.applies_to: Certified electricians
rules.quote: (a) Certification shall be renewed every three (3) years. To be eligible for renewal an applicant must provide proof under penalty of perjury of 32 hours further electrical education from an Educational Provider or from a state or federally approved apprenticeship program relevant to the type of certification, and must certify under penalty of perjury that he or she has worked in the industry 2000 hours within the previous three years.
rules.notes: FAQ: renewals accepted up to one year before expiration; 'If we do not recognize the continuing education provider on the list, we cannot process your application.' Provider list: https://www.dir.ca.gov/dlse/ECU/continuingeducation.html.
rules.correction: Every 3 years, 32 CE hours, 2,000 industry hours in the previous three years, and CE hours counting toward more than one category are confirmed. The FAQ says renewals are accepted 'up to one year prior to expiration date', not 365 days. Replaced may_renew_up_to_days_before_expiration: 365 with may_renew_up_to_years_before_expiration: 1.

rules.title: File the renewal before the card expires (regulation says 30 days before)
rules.plain_english: To avoid a lapse, file the renewal early. The regulation says a successful renewal must be postmarked or received 30 days before the certification period ends; DIR's FAQ says it must be postmarked on or before the expiration date. Use the earlier date to be safe. DIR must answer a renewal within 30 days.

parameters.dir_faq_deadline: postmarked on or prior to expiration date

rules.applies_to: Certified electricians and their employers
rules.quote: A successful renewal application must be postmarked or received at DAS 30 days before the end of the certification period in order for certification to be renewed without a lapse.
rules.notes: FAQ: 'Your renewal application must be postmarked on or prior to the expiration date on your certification card.' and 'A reminder notice may not be issued, so please refer to your certification card for your expiration date.' The regulation and FAQ differ; a calculator should warn at 30+ days before expiration.

rules.title: A lapsed certification must be re-earned by passing the exam
rules.plain_english: If an electrician lets certification lapse, they must retake the certification exam. Working for a C-10 contractor with an expired card is working uncertified.
rules.applies_to: Certified electricians and their C-10 employers
rules.quote: (c) An individual who allows certification to lapse shall be required to retake the certification examination.
rules.notes: See cert-elec-fee-lapsed-renewal-200 for the $200 fee.

rules.title: Uncertified workers can work only as registered electrician trainees enrolled in approved school
rules.plain_english: Someone without enough experience to test may still do electrical work for a C-10 contractor by registering with DIR as an electrician trainee. They must be enrolled in (or have completed) a state-approved electrician trainee curriculum and send proof of enrollment with the $25 registration. DIR sends a letter with a 'T' number.

parameters.school_enrollment_required: enrolled in or completed DIR-approved curriculum
parameters.filing_method: mail (online trainee registration not yet available per ECU page)
parameters.proof_document: T-number confirmation letter and trainee card

rules.applies_to: Uncertified workers doing certified electrical work for C-10 contractors
rules.citation: Labor Code 108.4 (as described by DIR); 8 CCR 296.1(a)
rules.quote: (a) An individual who is enrolled in or has completed an Approved Curriculum may register with DAS as an Electrician Trainee Registrant by submitting an application as set forth herein.
rules.notes: DIR trainee page (April 2020): 'An electrician trainee must be enrolled in a state approved school and under the supervision of a certified electrician that supervises only one electrician trainee.' Mailing address on the DIR page: DLSE-Electrician Certification Unit, P.O. Box 511286, Los Angeles, CA 90051-7841 (the regulation still shows an old DAS San Francisco P.O. box). Labor Code 108.4 itself was not readable (leginfo blocked).

rules.title: Trainee supervision: one certified electrician per trainee, direct and on site
rules.plain_english: A C-10 contractor using an electrician trainee for certified work must keep the trainee under direct, on-site supervision of a certified electrician who supervises no more than one trainee. That electrician may also supervise registered apprentices, who do not count toward the 1:1 limit. By using a trainee, the employer is promising adequate supervision.
rules.applies_to: C-10 contractors employing electrician trainees
rules.citation: 8 CCR 296.3(a); Labor Code 108.4 (as described by DIR)
rules.quote: (a) An employer who employs an Electrician Trainee to perform work for which certification would otherwise be required must ensure that the trainee is under the direct, on-site supervision of a Certified Electrician who is responsible for supervising no more than one trainee, but who also may be responsible for supervising registered apprentices.
rules.notes: Willfully failing to provide the supervision required by LC 108.4(a)(3) is a CSLB discipline ground (LC 108.2(h)(2)). The C-10 qualifying person may also supervise an uncertified employee (LC 108.2(g)).

rules.title: Employers who fail to supervise trainees can be barred from using them
rules.plain_english: If an employer does not adequately supervise an electrician trainee, the state may bar it from employing trainees in the future. The employer gets written notice and has 30 days to request a hearing; the hearing is set within 90 days and a written ruling follows within 90 days after it.

parameters.notice_served_to: employer address on file with CSLB

rules.applies_to: C-10 contractors employing electrician trainees
rules.quote: (b) An employer that fails to provide adequate supervision to an Electrician Trainee may be barred by the Chief DAS from employing trainees in the future.
rules.notes: 296.3(c): 'The employer may request a hearing with the Director within 30 days of service of the notice.'

rules.title: Electrician trainee registration must be renewed every year
rules.plain_english: Trainee registration lasts one year. Renew annually (no fee) with current proof of enrollment, transcripts of approved classwork completed in the past year, and a list of electrical employers and on-the-job experience for the year. Trainees who finished school renew yearly with a copy of the completion certificate until certified.

renewal_attachments: current proof of enrollment or certificate of completion
list of electrical employers and prior-year on-the-job experience

rules.applies_to: Electrician trainees and their C-10 employers
rules.quote: (e) An Electrician Trainee Registrant must renew his or her registration with DAS on an annual basis, by submitting a renewal application.
rules.notes: 296.1(d) and (f): DIR informs the applicant within 90 days of receiving a registration or renewal application. FAQ: 'Trainee cards have to be renewed every year.' An expired/inactive trainee is not legal to work under a C-10 contractor.

rules.title: Trainees must complete at least 150 classroom hours each year
rules.plain_english: To count as enrolled, a trainee must successfully complete at least 150 hours of approved classroom instruction each year (measured from the date classes start). In the first year the class schedule must be on track for 150 hours. Someone who has signed up but whose classes start later is treated as enrolled for up to 180 days before classes begin.

parameters.final_year_rule: fewer than 150 hours remaining: enrolled while attending remaining classes

rules.applies_to: Electrician trainees
rules.quote: (1) the individual must be successfully completing at least 150 hours of classroom instruction from an approved Educational Provider each year, except that the individual who has fewer than 150 hours of classroom instruction remaining to complete the Approved Curriculum will be deemed enrolled during the final year while attending those classes to complete the Approved Curriculum;
rules.notes: DIR trainee guide (Rev 3/2015): credit is given only for hours actually attended. Approved schools list: https://www.dir.ca.gov/DLSE/ECU/ListOfApprovedSchools.html.

rules.title: Trainee who leaves school must notify DIR; registration is cancelled
rules.plain_english: A trainee who stops attending the approved program without finishing must tell DIR. DIR then cancels the registration, and the person may no longer work as a trainee for a C-10 contractor until re-registered.

parameters.trigger: ceasing enrollment without completing approved curriculum
parameters.result: registration cancelled; status inactive; not legal to work under C-10

rules.applies_to: Electrician trainees and their C-10 employers
rules.quote: (d) An Electrician Trainee Registrant must notify DAS if the registrant ceases to be enrolled in an Approved Curriculum without completing it.
rules.notes: FAQ: "It means you are not active on the Electrician Trainee list and are not legal to work under a C10 Licensed Contractor." Schools may also report non-attendance.

rules.title: Trainees can test after finishing the approved curriculum, but are certified only after the hours
rules.plain_english: An electrician trainee may take the certification exam once they complete the approved curriculum for that classification. They are not certified until they pass and also prove the required work hours; until then they must keep renewing their trainee registration.
rules.applies_to: Electrician trainees
rules.quote: (g) An Electrician Trainee is eligible to test for certification upon completing the Approved Curriculum for the classification for which certification is sought.
rules.notes: FAQ: DIR holds the card until the experience is documented.

rules.title: Nonresidential lighting trainees in an approved OJT program are exempt
rules.plain_english: A nonresidential lighting trainee does not need certification if enrolled in a DAS-approved on-the-job training program and supervised on site by a certified Nonresidential Lighting Technician.

conditions: enrolled in DAS-approved on-the-job instructional training program (LC 3090)
onsite supervision by certified nonresidential lighting technician
parameters.approved_program_listed_by_dir: NALMCO Certified Apprentice Lighting Technician (CALT) program manuals

rules.applies_to: Lighting maintenance and retrofit C-10 contractors
rules.quote: (f) Notwithstanding subdivision (a), certification is not required for a nonresidential lighting trainee (1) who is enrolled in an on-the-job instructional training program approved by the Chief of the Division of Apprenticeship Standards pursuant to Section 3090, and (2) who is under the onsite supervision of a nonresidential lighting technician certified pursuant to Section 108.
rules.notes: DIR page (July 2011) lists the NALMCO CALT manuals as the approved OJT program.

rules.title: CSLB can suspend or revoke a C-10 license for willfully using uncertified electricians
rules.plain_english: It is grounds for CSLB discipline, up to suspension or revocation of the C-10 license, if the contractor willfully employs even one uncertified person as an electrician, willfully fails to supervise uncertified trainees as required, or willfully fails to supervise apprentices.

parameters.max_sanction: suspension or revocation of C-10 license
grounds: willfully employs one or more uncertified persons as electricians
willfully fails to provide adequate supervision of uncertified workers (LC 108.4(a)(3))
willfully fails to provide adequate supervision of apprentices

rules.applies_to: C-10 electrical contractors
rules.quote: (1) The contractor willfully employs one or more uncertified persons to perform work as electricians in violation of this section.
rules.notes: Opening text of 108.2(h): 'The following shall constitute additional grounds for disciplinary proceedings, including suspension or revocation of the license of a class C-10 electrical contractor pursuant to Article 7 (commencing with Section 7090) of Chapter 9 of Division 3 of the Business and Professions Code:'. No per-worker dollar penalty was found in the readable statute or regulations; CSLB citation fines under B&P 7099.2 may apply (see rulebook). DIR FAQ also warns of possible civil suits.

rules.title: CSLB must act within 60 days of a Labor Commissioner referral; no proof of certification is presumed a violation
rules.plain_english: When the Labor Commissioner refers a likely violation, CSLB opens an investigation and must start any disciplinary action within 60 days of the referral. If the employer or worker cannot show proof of certification or trainee status, a violation is presumed (the contractor must then rebut it). Keep copies of every electrician's card or trainee letter on file and at the jobsite.

practical_evidence_examples: DIR electrician certification card or number
electrician trainee T-number letter and trainee card

rules.applies_to: C-10 electrical contractors
rules.quote: Failure of the employer or employee to provide evidence of certification or trainee status shall create a rebuttable presumption of violation of this provision.
rules.notes: 108.2(j): 'Any disciplinary action against the licensee shall be initiated within 60 days of the receipt of the referral.' DIR status search tool: https://www.dir.ca.gov/DLSE/ECU/ElectCert/ElectCertSearch.asp. Recordkeeping practice is a recommendation, not a statutory duty.
rules.correction: The 60-day deadline to start discipline after a referral and the rebuttable presumption are confirmed (both in 108.2(j), which also requires the Registrar to open an investigation on referral). The statute names only 'evidence of certification or trainee status'. The rule's evidence_types list added apprentice registration and named documents the statute does not mention. Replaced it with statutory_evidence = [certification, trainee status] and practical_evidence_examples (DIR card/number, trainee T-number letter and card). Apprentices are exempt separately under 108.2(d), but the presumption wording does not refer to apprentice records.

rules.title: Electrician certification complaints go to DLSE, which forwards verified ones to CSLB
rules.plain_english: Complaints about uncertified electricians are filed with the DIR Electrician Certification Unit on its referral form. DLSE checks them and forwards verified complaints to CSLB. Helpful evidence: the contract, scope, job address, project type, owner and contractor details including CSLB license number, and names and photos of uncertified workers.

parameters.filed_with: DIR Electrician Certification Unit, Attn: ECU Supervisor, 1515 Clay Street, Suite 1902, Oakland, CA 94612
evidence_items: contractor name, address, phone, prime or sub, CSLB license number
list of non-certified employees with names and photographs

rules.applies_to: C-10 contractors (as respondents) and competitors/workers filing complaints
rules.citation: Labor Code 108.2(i); DIR ECU enforcement page
rules.quote: As of July 1, 2009 the Department of Labor Standards Enforcement(DLSE) and the California Contractors State License Board (CSLB) are responsible for enforcing Labor Code 108.2.

rules.title: Falsely claiming to be certified: 7-year bar from testing or trainee registration
rules.plain_english: A person who shows a certificate or claims to be certified when they are not is barred for seven years from taking the certification exam or registering as a trainee.
rules.applies_to: Individuals doing electrical work
rules.quote: Any person who displays a certificate, or otherwise claims to be certified, who is not certified shall be prohibited from taking the test for certification or from registering as an Electrician Trainee Registrant for a period of seven (7) years.

rules.title: Certification can be suspended or revoked; 30 days to request a hearing
rules.plain_english: DIR may suspend or revoke a certification for gross negligence, fraud, repeated negligence, or if it was obtained by mistake or fraud. The electrician has 30 days from service of the notice to request a hearing; otherwise the action takes effect on the 31st day.

grounds: certification obtained through mistake, misrepresentation or fraud

rules.applies_to: Certified electricians
rules.quote: Where no timely request for hearing has been made, the effective date of the suspension or revocation is deemed the 31st day following service of the notice of intention.

rules.title: Appeal a denied certification or trainee registration within 30 days
rules.plain_english: An applicant denied certification, or a trainee denied or cancelled, may appeal in writing within 30 days of service of the denial. Any hearing must start within 90 days after the appeal is received, and the written ruling is due within 90 days of the appeal or the last hearing day, whichever is later.

parameters.appeal_days_run_from: service of the denial (293.0(d)) or of the denial/cancellation notice (296.4(b))
parameters.ruling_deadline_rule: 90 days after DAS receives the appeal or 90 days after the last day of hearing, whichever is later

rules.applies_to: Applicants and trainee registrants
rules.quote: (d) Any applicant may appeal the denial of certification to the Chief DAS. The appeal shall be in writing and made within 30 days of service of the denial.
rules.notes: 296.4(b) sets the same 30-day appeal for trainee registration denial or cancellation.
rules.correction: The 30-day appeal window, 90-day hearing start and applicant's burden are confirmed. The rule's ruling_within_days: 90 had no starting point. Both sections say the ruling is due within 90 days after DAS receives the appeal, or within 90 days after the last day of hearing, whichever is later, and a hearing is at the Chief's discretion. Added ruling_deadline_rule, hearing_discretionary and the trigger for the 30 days.

rules.title: Keep your mailing address current with the Electrician Certification Unit
rules.plain_english: Applicants, certified electricians and trainees must tell DIR when their mailing address changes (online, by form, or by letter). Notices of denial, suspension or revocation are sent to the address on file.

parameters.trigger: change of mailing address

rules.applies_to: Certified electricians, trainees and applicants
rules.quote: (b) Applicants, Electrician Trainee Registrants, and Certified Electricians shall be responsible for notifying DAS of changes in mailing address.
rules.notes: No day count is set by the regulation. 295.0(a): DIR publishes a yearly list of certified electricians and trainees (now on data.ca.gov).

rules.title: AB 1707 (2026): electrician certification program moving to CSLB on July 1, 2028 (enactment not verified)
rules.plain_english: A 2026 bill, AB 1707, moves the electrician certification program from DIR's Labor Commissioner to CSLB effective July 1, 2028, subject to a budget appropriation. CSLB would enforce the existing DIR regulations until it adopts its own. The certification requirement itself does not change. CSLB's board analysis described the bill as pending on the Senate floor as of August 25, 2026; whether it was signed could not be confirmed from an official source.

parameters.from_agency: DIR Division of Labor Standards Enforcement

rules.applies_to: C-10 contractors, certified electricians and trainees
rules.source: https://cslb.ca.gov/Resources/BoardPackets/2026/Sept.2-3_BoardMeetingPacket.pdf (agenda item E1b, PDF pages 154-156, printed pages 140-142)
rules.quote: SUMMARY: AB 1707 transfers the administration of the electrician certification program (ECU) and existing requirements for electrician certification from the Department of Industrial Relations' (DIR) Division of Labor Standards Enforcement (DLSE) to the Contractors State License Board (CSLB), upon appropriation by Legislature, effective July 1, 2028.
rules.notes: UNVERIFIED ENACTMENT. Bill text (leginfo) and the Governor's signing announcement (gov.ca.gov) could not be fetched. Search snippets indicate a September 27, 2026 signing; treat as unconfirmed until the chaptered text is read. Read only the CSLB staff analysis.
rules.correction: Not corrected in substance. Every parameter matches the CSLB staff analysis: July 1, 2028 transfer upon legislative appropriation, Electrician Certification Fund access from July 1, 2027, DLSE transition spending through June 30, 2029, and 'Pending the Senate Floor' as of August 25, 2026. Fixed source_location: the analysis is on PDF pages 154-156, which are printed pages 140-142, not 139-141. Enactment remains unconfirmed.

rules.title: CDPH lead certification required for workers and supervisors exposed at 50 µg/m3 or more in homes and public buildings
rules.plain_english: On lead-related construction work in residential or public buildings, any worker or supervisor shown to be exposed to airborne lead at or above 50 micrograms per cubic meter (8-hour average) must be trained by a CDPH-accredited training provider and hold a California Department of Public Health (CDPH) lead certificate. This is on top of Cal/OSHA's regular lead training.

parameters.calosha_training_program_trigger: exposed at or above the action level on any day (8 CCR 1532.1(l)(1)(C)1.)

rules.applies_to: Construction employers doing lead-related construction work in residential or public buildings
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/1532_1.html (subsection (l)(3) 'Certification of training for residential and public buildings')
rules.quote: The employer shall ensure that all employees and supervisors who are engaged in lead-related construction work as defined in Title 17, California Code of Regulations, section 35040, and have been shown to be exposed to lead at or above 50 µg/m3 as an 8-hour TWA, meet the training requirements of this section, are trained by an accredited training provider and are certified by the California Department of Public Health (CDPH).
rules.notes: CDPH's own pages and 17 CCR 35001 et seq. could not be fetched (cdph.ca.gov and govt.westlaw.com blocked), so the CDPH certificate categories (Inspector/Assessor, Project Monitor, Sampling Technician, Supervisor, Worker), fees, renewal terms and exam rules are not included; see sources_blocked. DOSH fact sheet (Lead in Construction) restates this rule. The (l)(3) certification duty predates the 2025 PEL/action-level amendments; its start date was not determined. (l)(1)(C): the training program in (l)(2) is required '1. For employees who are exposed to lead at or above the action level on any day'.
rules.correction: 2026-11-25 second pass: added calosha_training_program_trigger from (l)(1)(C)1. ('at or above the action level on any day'; the module had said 'above').

rules.title: 'Lead-related construction work' and 'public building' defined
rules.plain_english: Lead-related construction work means any construction, alteration, painting, demolition, salvage, renovation, repair or maintenance of a residential or public building (including prep and cleanup) that disturbs lead-containing material or soil and may significantly expose adults or children. A 'public building' is any building generally open to the public that is not industrial or residential, such as schools, daycare, hospitals, stores, offices and government buildings.
rules.applies_to: Contractors disturbing lead paint or lead-containing soil in homes or public buildings
rules.quote: Lead-related construction work is defined in Title 17 to be any construction, alteration, painting, demolition, salvage, renovation, repair, or maintenance of any residential or public building, including preparation and cleanup, that, by using or disturbing lead containing material or soil, may result in significant exposure of adults or children to lead.
rules.notes: Definition read from Cal/OSHA's restatement in 8 CCR 1532.1; 17 CCR 35040 itself was not readable. Note that California's definition covers public and commercial buildings, unlike EPA RRP (pre-1978 housing and child-occupied facilities only).

rules.title: Where CDPH certification is required, training must come from a CDPH-accredited provider
rules.plain_english: If a worker or supervisor needs CDPH lead certification, their training must be given by a training provider accredited by CDPH under Title 17. Training from an EPA-only provider does not satisfy this.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose workers need CDPH lead certification
rules.quote: (F) Where the certification of employee and supervisor training is required, as described in subsection (l)(3), the training shall be conducted by a training provider accredited by the California Department of Public Health, in accordance with Title 17, California Code of Regulations, Division 1, Chapter 8.
rules.notes: The 'EPA-only provider' statement is an inference from the CDPH-accreditation requirement.

rules.title: Lead 'supervisor' defined; must be CDPH-certified when (l)(3) applies
rules.plain_english: Under Cal/OSHA's lead standard, a supervisor is someone who can spot existing and predictable lead hazards and has authority to fix them promptly. Supervisors must be trained and, when required by the 50 µg/m3 rule, CDPH-certified.

supervisor_must: identify existing and predictable lead hazards
have authorization to take prompt corrective measures

rules.applies_to: Construction employers doing lead work
rules.quote: Supervisors shall be trained, as required by this section, and, when required, be certified consistent with subsection (l)(3).

rules.title: Give lead training and certification materials on request
rules.plain_english: On request, the employer must provide all materials about its lead training program and certification to affected employees, their representatives, Cal/OSHA and NIOSH.

parameters.trigger: upon request

rules.applies_to: Construction employers doing lead work
rules.quote: (B) The employer shall provide, upon request, all materials relating to the employee information training program and certification to affected employees, their designated representatives, the Chief and NIOSH.
rules.notes: No response deadline is stated in (l)(4)(B).

rules.title: Coatings at 0.06% (600 ppm) lead or more are treated as a lead hazard for construction work
rules.plain_english: If test data show a coating or material contains 0.06% lead by dry weight (600 ppm) or more, Cal/OSHA treats it as lead material that may be a health hazard to workers doing lead-related construction. Such objective data cannot replace air monitoring for trigger tasks.
rules.applies_to: Construction employers evaluating coatings before lead work
rules.quote: (C) Objective data for an initial assessment that demonstrate surface coating or material that contain lead at concentrations equal to or exceeding 0.06% lead dry weight (600 ppm) demonstrate the presence of lead surface coatings or material that may constitute a health hazard to employees engaged in lead-related construction work.
rules.notes: Different from the EPA/RRP lead-based paint threshold (1.0 mg/cm2 or 0.5% by weight) and the Cal/OSHA pre-job notification exemption (under 0.5% / 5,000 ppm) already in the rulebook.

rules.title: Worker blood lead of 20 µg/dL or more is reported to Cal/OSHA and treated as a complaint
rules.plain_english: CDPH must notify Cal/OSHA when a worker's blood lead test is 20 micrograms per deciliter or higher. Cal/OSHA treats that report as an official complaint and may inspect the employer's workplace or jobsite.

parameters.treated_as: official complaint from a government representative

rules.applies_to: Employers of lead-exposed construction workers
rules.citation: Health and Safety Code 105185 (AB 35, 2019), as described by Cal/OSHA
rules.quote: California's Department of Public Health (CDPH) must notify Cal/OSHA when a worker's blood lead level tests at or above 20 micrograms per deciliter (μg/dL).
rules.notes: Statute text not read (leginfo blocked); rule taken from Cal/OSHA's official summary page. Effective date of AB 35 not verified.

rules.title: EPA certified renovator: refresher within 5 years (3 years if no hands-on)
rules.plain_english: A certified renovator becomes certified by passing an EPA-accredited renovator course; the course certificate is the proof. To stay certified, take a refresher within 5 years of the initial course. A refresher with hands-on training gives 5 years; one without hands-on gives only 3 years, and the next refresher must include hands-on. Miss the deadline and you must retake the full initial course.
rules.applies_to: Firms and renovators doing paid renovation, repair or painting in pre-1978 target housing and child-occupied facilities
rules.quote: Individuals who take a renovator refresher course that does not include hands-on training will be certified for 3 years from the date they complete the training. Individuals who take a refresher training course that includes hands-on training will be certified for 5 years.
rules.notes: Applies where no EPA-authorized state RRP program exists; the rulebook's rrp-applicability note says California has none (not re-verified: the CFR does not list authorized states and epa.gov was blocked). The 3-year limit for refreshers without hands-on training was added in 2016 (81 FR 7995).

rules.title: Electrical, plumbing and HVAC work in pre-1978 housing is an RRP renovation above 6 / 20 sq ft
rules.plain_english: EPA's minor repair and maintenance exclusion names minor HVAC, electrical and plumbing work: it is exempt only while it disturbs 6 sq ft or less of painted surface per room inside or 20 sq ft or less outside, with no prohibited practices, window replacement or demolition of painted surfaces. When painted components are removed, the whole removed area counts. Trade work that disturbs more (for example cutting into painted walls or ceilings to rewire) is a renovation covered by the RRP rule.

trades_named: minor heating, ventilation or air conditioning work
renovation_examples: removal of building components (e.g., walls, ceilings, plumbing, windows)

rules.applies_to: Electrical, plumbing and HVAC contractors working for compensation in pre-1978 target housing and child-occupied facilities
rules.citation: 40 CFR 745.83 (Minor repair and maintenance activities; Renovation)
rules.quote: are activities, including minor heating, ventilation or air conditioning work, electrical work, and plumbing, that disrupt 6 square feet or less of painted surface per room for interior activities or 20 square feet or less of painted surface for exterior activities
rules.notes: Same definition: 'When removing painted components, or portions of painted components, the entire surface area removed is the amount of painted surface disturbed.' 'Renovation' includes 'the removal of building components (e.g., walls, ceilings, plumbing, windows)' and weatherization such as 'cutting holes in painted surfaces'. Added in the 2026-11-25 second-pass review: the builder never flagged RRP for electrical work in pre-1978 housing.

rules.title: Housing for the elderly or disabled and 0-bedroom dwellings are not target housing unless a child under 6 lives there
rules.plain_english: Target housing is housing built before 1978, except housing for the elderly or persons with disabilities and 0-bedroom dwellings, unless a child under 6 lives or is expected to live there. Housing for the elderly means retirement communities or similar housing reserved for households with at least one person 62 or older at initial occupancy. A 0-bedroom dwelling is one where the living area is not separated from the sleeping area: efficiencies, studio apartments, dormitories, barracks and rented rooms.

zero_bedroom_examples: rentals of individual rooms in residential dwellings

rules.applies_to: Firms renovating senior housing, housing for persons with disabilities, studios, dormitories and rented rooms built before 1978
rules.citation: 40 CFR 745.103 (Target housing; Housing for the elderly; 0-bedroom dwelling); 745.83
rules.quote: means any housing constructed prior to 1978, except housing for the elderly or persons with disabilities or any 0-bedroom dwelling (unless any child who is less than 6 years of age resides or is expected to reside in such housing).
rules.notes: 745.103: 'Housing for the elderly means retirement communities or similar types of housing reserved for households composed of one or more persons 62 years of age or more at the time of initial occupancy.' '0-bedroom dwelling means any residential dwelling in which the living area is not separated from the sleeping area. The term includes efficiencies, studio apartments, dormitory housing, military barracks, and rentals of individual rooms in residential dwellings.' Such a building can still contain a child-occupied facility (745.83). Added in the 2026-11-25 second-pass review: the builder treated senior housing as target housing (RRP 'required').

rules.title: Certified renovator must be on site for signs, containment and cleaning, and reachable at all times
rules.plain_english: The assigned certified renovator must be physically at the job while warning signs are posted, while containment is set up, and while the work area is cleaned. At all other times during the work they must be available on site or by phone. They must carry copies of their initial and latest refresher course certificates at the job.

parameters.availability_otherwise: on-site or by telephone at all times renovation is conducted
documents_at_worksite: most recent refresher course completion certificate

rules.applies_to: Firms and renovators doing paid renovation, repair or painting in pre-1978 target housing and child-occupied facilities
rules.quote: (3) Must be physically present at the work site when the signs required by § 745.85(a)(1) are posted, while the work area containment required by § 745.85(a)(2) is being established, and while the work area cleaning required by § 745.85(a)(5) is performed.
rules.notes: (b)(5): 'Must be available, either on-site or by telephone, at all times that renovations are being conducted.' (b)(7): 'Must have with them at the work site copies of their initial course completion certificate and their most recent refresher course completion certificate.'

rules.title: Every RRP worker must be a certified renovator or trained on the job by one
rules.plain_english: Everyone doing renovation work for the firm must either be a certified renovator or have been trained by the certified renovator on the lead-safe work practices they will use. The firm must document that training (topics for each worker) in the job records.

parameters.documentation_includes: training topics for each worker, certified renovator's training certificate copy

rules.applies_to: Firms and renovators doing paid renovation, repair or painting in pre-1978 target housing and child-occupied facilities
rules.quote: (1) All individuals performing renovation activities on behalf of the firm are either certified renovators or have been trained by a certified renovator in accordance with § 745.90.
rules.notes: 745.86(b)(6)(i): certification by the renovator that 'Training was provided to workers (topics must be identified for each worker).'

rules.title: RRP firm recertification every 5 years; apply at least 90 days before expiration
rules.plain_english: EPA firm certification must be renewed every 5 years. An application filed electronically 90 or more days before expiration is 'timely' and keeps the firm certified while EPA decides. If filed later and not approved in time, the certification expires and the firm may not do renovations until EPA approves it.

parameters.late_and_unapproved_result: certification expires; no renovations until approved

rules.applies_to: EPA-certified renovation firms
rules.quote: (i) An application for re-certification is timely if it is electronically submitted 90 days or more before the date the firm's current certification expires.
rules.notes: 745.89(b): 'To maintain its certification, a firm must be re-certified by EPA every 5 years.' Electronic filing requirement added by 89 FR 89457 (Nov. 12, 2024). Existing rulebook rule rrp-firm-certification covers initial certification.

rules.title: Amend RRP firm certification within 90 days of a change
rules.plain_english: If information in the firm's last EPA application changes (for example name, address or ownership details), the firm must file an amendment within 90 days. If it does not, it may not do renovations until the amendment is made. Amending does not change the expiration date.

parameters.consequence_if_late: no renovations or dust sampling until amended

rules.applies_to: EPA-certified renovation firms
rules.quote: (c) Amendment of certification. A firm must amend its certification within 90 days of the date a change occurs to information included in the firm's most recent application.

rules.title: Supplement an incomplete RRP firm application within 30 days
rules.plain_english: If EPA says the firm application is incomplete, the firm has 30 days from EPA's request to send the missing information or fees, or EPA will not approve it (and keeps the fee).
rules.applies_to: Firms applying for EPA RRP certification
rules.quote: If EPA requests a firm to supplement its application, the firm must submit the requested information or pay the additional fees within 30 days of the date of the request.

rules.title: EPA RRP firm certification fee: $300 (recertification $300)
rules.plain_english: EPA charges a renovation firm $300 for initial certification and $300 for each 5-year recertification. A combined renovation plus lead-based paint activities firm application is $550. Replacing a lost firm certificate costs $15.
rules.applies_to: Renovation firms applying to EPA
rules.quote: (2) Lost certificate. A $15 fee will be charged for the replacement of a firm certificate.
rules.notes: The fee table is rendered as a grid in eCFR (Firm: Certification $300, Re-certification (every 5 years) $300), so the verbatim quote is the replacement-fee sentence; the $300 figures were read from the same table. Training course fees for renovators are set by the private training provider, not EPA.

rules.title: RRP interior containment: cover floor 6 feet beyond the work surfaces
rules.plain_english: Inside, before work starts, remove or cover all objects, close and cover all ducts, close and cover doors, and cover the floor (including carpet) with taped-down plastic at least 6 feet beyond the surfaces being worked on, or farther if needed to contain the dust.

parameters.rule: 6 ft or sufficient distance to contain dust, whichever is greater
other_steps: remove or cover objects with sealed plastic
close windows and doors; cover doors with plastic

rules.applies_to: Firms and renovators doing paid renovation, repair or painting in pre-1978 target housing and child-occupied facilities
rules.quote: (D) Cover the floor surface, including installed carpet, with taped-down plastic sheeting or other impermeable material in the work area 6 feet beyond the perimeter of surfaces undergoing renovation or a sufficient distance to contain the dust, whichever is greater.
rules.notes: Work practices effective July 6, 2010 per 745.81(a)(4).

rules.title: RRP exterior containment: close openings within 20 feet; ground cover 10 feet
rules.plain_english: Outside, close all doors and windows within 20 feet of the work (on multi-story buildings, also those on floors below at the same horizontal distance). Cover the ground with plastic at least 10 feet beyond the surfaces being worked on, unless the property line prevents it. If work is within 10 feet of the property line, put up vertical containment or equal precautions.
rules.applies_to: Firms and renovators doing paid renovation, repair or painting in pre-1978 target housing and child-occupied facilities
rules.quote: (C) Cover the ground with plastic sheeting or other disposable impermeable material extending 10 feet beyond the perimeter of surfaces undergoing renovation or a sufficient distance to collect falling paint debris, whichever is greater, unless the property line prevents 10 feet of such ground covering.
rules.notes: (A): 'Close all doors and windows within 20 feet of the renovation.' (D): 'If the renovation will affect surfaces within 10 feet of the property line, the renovation firm must erect vertical containment or equivalent extra precautions'.

rules.title: RRP cleaning: clean 2 feet beyond the work area; verify with cloths in sections under 40 sq ft
rules.plain_english: After interior work, clean all surfaces in and within 2 feet of the work area (HEPA vacuum, wet wipe, mop). Then the certified renovator checks each window sill and wipes floors and countertops with wet cleaning cloths, in sections under 40 square feet each, comparing each cloth to the EPA verification card. If a section fails twice, wait 1 hour or until the surface is completely dry, whichever is longer, then wipe it with a dry cleaning cloth. After exterior work, the certified renovator checks by visual inspection instead. Remove warning signs only after verification passes.

parameters.wait_after_failed_reclean: 1 hour or until the surface has dried completely, whichever is longer
parameters.after_wait: wipe with a dry disposable cleaning cloth; the surface is then adequately cleaned

rules.applies_to: Firms and renovators doing paid renovation, repair or painting in pre-1978 target housing and child-occupied facilities
rules.quote: If the surface within the work area is greater than 40 square feet, the surface within the work area must be divided into roughly equal sections that are each less than 40 square feet.
rules.notes: (a)(5)(ii): 'The firm must clean all objects and surfaces in the work area and within 2 feet of the work area in the following manner, cleaning from higher to lower'. Exterior jobs require a visual inspection only (745.85(b)(2)).
rules.correction: The 2-foot cleaning band, sections under 40 sq ft, certified renovator, verification card and sign removal are confirmed. wait_after_second_failure_hours: 1 dropped the qualifier in 745.85(b)(1)(ii)(A)(3) and (B)(2): wait '1 hour or until the surface has dried completely, whichever is longer', then wipe with a dry cloth. Replaced it with wait_after_failed_reclean (full rule), wait_min_hours and after_wait, and added the exterior visual-only rule. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction (40 CFR 745.85(b) re-read in the eCFR versioner API, title 40 issue 2026-11-20 on 2026-11-27); no value changed.

rules.title: Optional dust clearance testing: new lower dust-lead action levels from January 12, 2026
rules.plain_english: A firm may skip cleaning verification only if the contract or another law requires dust clearance sampling by a certified inspector, risk assessor or dust sampling technician, with re-cleaning until results are below the action levels. From January 12, 2026 those levels are 5 µg/ft² for floors, 40 µg/ft² for window sills and 100 µg/ft² for window troughs (before: 10, 100 and 400).
rules.applies_to: Firms and renovators doing paid renovation, repair or painting in pre-1978 target housing and child-occupied facilities that use dust clearance testing instead of cleaning verification
rules.quote: On or after January 12, 2026, the action levels for lead in dust are 5 µg/ft2 for floors, 40 µg/ft2 for interior window sills, and 100 µg/ft2 for window troughs.
rules.notes: Amended by 89 FR 89457 (Nov. 12, 2024). Sampling under 745.85(c) must follow 745.227(e)(8). A stricter State, local or Tribal standard can apply (745.85(c)(3)). California CDPH clearance standards for abatement (17 CCR 35036/36000) were not readable.

rules.title: Give the owner the RRP compliance record with the final invoice or within 30 days
rules.plain_english: When the final invoice is delivered or within 30 days after the renovation is finished, whichever is first, the firm must give the building owner (and an adult occupant or child-care representative, if different) the lead-safe compliance information, such as EPA's 'Sample Renovation Recordkeeping Checklist'. For common areas, post it or post how to get it.

parameters.deadline: earlier of final invoice delivery or 30 days after completion
recipients: adult occupant (dwelling) or adult representative (child-occupied facility) if different
parameters.acceptable_form: Sample Renovation Recordkeeping Checklist or similar

rules.applies_to: Firms and renovators doing paid renovation, repair or painting in pre-1978 target housing and child-occupied facilities
rules.quote: (c)(1) When the final invoice for the renovation is delivered or within 30 days of the completion of the renovation, whichever is earlier, the renovation firm must provide information pertaining to compliance with this subpart to the following persons:
rules.notes: Rulebook rule rrp-records-3-years covers the 3-year retention; this is the separate hand-over deadline.

rules.title: Emergency renovations: limited RRP exemption, but cleaning and verification still required
rules.plain_english: Unplanned emergency work (for example a sudden equipment failure that threatens safety or property) is exempt from the pamphlet rule, and from warning signs, containment, waste handling, training and certification only as far as needed to handle the emergency. Interim controls done because a resident child has an elevated blood lead level also count as emergency work, but they are exempt only from the pamphlet rule. Cleaning, cleaning verification by a certified renovator, and the records describing the emergency are still required.

parameters.definition: renovation activities that were not planned but result from a sudden, unexpected event (such as non-routine failures of equipment) that, if not immediately attended to, presents a safety or public health hazard, or threatens equipment and/or property with significant damage
not_exempt_from: cleaning (745.85(a)(5)) by certified renovators or workers trained under 745.90(b)(2)
parameters.must_document: nature of the emergency and the provisions not followed (745.86(b)(6))

rules.applies_to: Firms and renovators doing paid renovation, repair or painting in pre-1978 target housing and child-occupied facilities
rules.quote: Emergency renovations are not exempt from the cleaning requirements of § 745.85(a)(5), which must be performed by certified renovators or individuals trained in accordance with § 745.90(b)(2), the cleaning verification requirements of § 745.85(b), which must be performed by certified renovators, and the recordkeeping requirements of § 745.86(b)(6) and (b)(7).
rules.correction: The cleaning, cleaning verification and recordkeeping duties are confirmed. 745.82(b) gives interim controls done because a resident child has an elevated blood lead level only the pamphlet (745.84) exemption. The warning sign, containment, waste handling, training and certification exemptions apply only to emergency renovations other than interim controls, and only to the extent necessary to respond to the emergency. The rule's parameters implied that interim controls got the full list and limited 'to the extent necessary' to training and certification. Restructured the parameters to match and added the regulatory definition of emergency renovation and the 745.86(b)(6) duty to document the emergency. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction (40 CFR 745.82(b) re-read in the eCFR versioner API, title 40 issue 2026-11-20 on 2026-11-27); no value changed.

rules.title: Child-occupied facility: pre-1978 space a child under 6 uses 2+ days a week, 3+ hours a day, 6+ hours a week, 60+ hours a year
rules.plain_english: RRP also covers 'child-occupied facilities': pre-1978 buildings (or parts) regularly visited by the same child under 6 on at least two days in a week, at least 3 hours each day, at least 6 hours per week and at least 60 hours per year, such as daycares, preschools and kindergarten rooms, even inside commercial buildings.
rules.applies_to: Contractors renovating daycares, preschools, schools and commercial buildings that house child care
rules.quote: Child-occupied facility means a building, or portion of a building, constructed prior to 1978, visited regularly by the same child, under 6 years of age, on at least two different days within any week (Sunday through Saturday period), provided that each day's visit lasts at least 3 hours and the combined weekly visits last at least 6 hours, and the combined annual visits last at least 60 hours.
rules.notes: In public/commercial buildings, only common areas routinely used by children under 6 (restrooms, cafeterias) and the adjacent exterior sides are included; hallways, stairways and garages they only pass through are not.

rules.title: Child-occupied facility jobs: pamphlet to owner and notice to parents within 60 days before work
rules.plain_english: No more than 60 days before starting work in a child-occupied facility, give the building owner the Renovate Right pamphlet (signed receipt, or certificate of mailing at least 7 days before), give it to an adult representative of the facility if not the owner, and inform parents and guardians by mail/hand delivery or posted signs describing the work and completion date. Sign and date a statement of the steps taken.

recipients: adult representative of facility (if not owner)
parents and guardians of children using the facility
parent_notice_methods: mail or hand-deliver pamphlet and renovation info
post informational signs with pamphlet or how to get it

rules.applies_to: Firms renovating child-occupied facilities
rules.quote: (c) Renovations in child-occupied facilities. No more than 60 days before beginning renovation activities in any child-occupied facility, the firm performing the renovation must:
rules.notes: Rulebook rule rrp-renovate-right-pamphlet-60-days covers dwelling units and common areas; this adds the child-occupied facility steps.

rules.title: Pamphlet acknowledgment may be in the renovation contract, in the contract's language
rules.plain_english: The signed pamphlet acknowledgment must state the owner's or occupant's name, acknowledge receiving the pamphlet before work, give the unit address, and be signed and dated. It can be a separate sheet or part of the written contract, and must be in the same language as the contract (or the lease/pamphlet for rentals).

parameters.language: same as contract (or lease/pamphlet for non-owner-occupied housing)

rules.applies_to: Firms renovating target housing and child-occupied facilities
rules.quote: (2) Be either a separate sheet or part of any written contract or service agreement for the renovation.
rules.notes: Pre-Renovation Education Rule provisions in effect since June 1999 (745.81(c)).

rules.title: RRP violations: federal civil penalty up to $49,772 per violation
rules.plain_english: Breaking any RRP rule (certification, work practices, pamphlet, records) violates the Toxic Substances Control Act. EPA can assess civil penalties of up to $49,772 per violation (for penalties assessed on or after January 8, 2025), plus possible criminal sanctions. EPA assumes lead paint is present on covered jobs.
rules.applies_to: Firms and renovators doing paid renovation, repair or painting in pre-1978 target housing and child-occupied facilities
rules.quote: (d) Violators may be subject to civil and criminal sanctions pursuant to TSCA section 16 (15 U.S.C. 2615) for each violation.
rules.notes: 40 CFR 19.4 Table 1 lists 15 U.S.C. 2615(a)(1) TSCA: $49,772 (assessed on/after Jan 8, 2025), $48,512 (Dec 27, 2023 to Jan 8, 2025), $37,500 as enacted. EPA adjusts annually; recheck each January. Whether each day counts as a separate violation is set by the TSCA statute, which was not read.

rules.title: Crane operators: employer must also evaluate and document each operator
rules.plain_english: Certification alone is not enough. The employer must evaluate each crane operator (skills, ability to recognize and avoid risk, the specific equipment size and configuration, and assigned lifts like blind or multi-crane lifts) using a qualified evaluator who is its employee or agent. The written record (operator name, evaluator name and signature, date, make/model/configuration) must be available at the worksite while the operator is employed. Re-evaluate after any retraining.

parameters.evaluator: employee or agent of employer with knowledge, training and experience to assess operators
record_contents: make, model and configuration of equipment

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees operate cranes and derricks (Group 13)
rules.quote: (5) The employer shall document the completion of the evaluation. This document shall provide: The operator's name; the evaluator's name and signature; the date; and the make, model, and configuration of equipment used in the evaluation.
rules.notes: Rulebook rule crane-operator-certification-5-years covers certification validity, 1,000-hour hands-on waiver and exemptions. (f)(2): for operators employed before April 6, 2020 the employer may rely on its previous assessments.

rules.title: Crane operator certificate requires physical exam, drug test, written and hands-on exams
rules.plain_english: An accredited certifying entity may certify a crane operator only after the operator passes a physical exam (ASME B30.5 criteria or DOT 49 CFR 391.41-391.49), a substance abuse test by a recognized lab, a written exam (controls, emergency response, load charts and calculations, power line procedures, ground conditions, Group 13 rules), and a hands-on exam. The certificate must state the equipment type. The employer must provide the certification at no cost to the employee. Certificates are valid for at most 5 years, and operators must re-certify every 5 years; an operator with at least 1,000 hours of documented experience on that crane type in the last certification period who passes the physical, substance abuse and written exams does not have to retake the hands-on exam.
rules.applies_to: Construction crane operators and their employers
rules.quote: (1) Pass a physical examination conducted by a physician or other licensed health care professional (e.g. physician's assistant or nurse practitioner) which at a minimum shall include the examination criteria specified in the American Society of Mechanical Engineers (ASME) B30.5-2000 standard, Chapter 5-3.1.2(a)(1-5, 7, 8) or the U.S. Department of Transportation (US DOT) physical examination requirements contained in 49 CFR Sections 391.41 through 391.49.
rules.notes: (d)(1)(A): an operator is qualified for the certified type, or type and capacity, or higher-capacity equipment of that type. Recertification every 5 years also requires the physical, substance abuse and written exams. (c)(1): 'the employer shall provide the certification or licensure at no cost to employees.' (d)(1): 'Certificates shall be valid for a maximum of five (5) years.'
rules.correction: 2026-11-25 second pass: added option1_certificate_max_validity_years 5 ((d)(1)), recertify_every_years 5 and recertify_hands_on_waiver_hours 1000 ((d)(3)), and employer_provides_at_no_cost_to_employee ((c)(1)); citation widened. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction (8 CCR 5006.2(c)(1), (d)(1), (d)(3) at https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5006_2.html re-read on 2026-11-27); no value changed.

rules.title: Government-issued crane operator license is valid only in that jurisdiction, max 5 years
rules.plain_english: Instead of an accredited certification, a crane operator may hold a license from a government licensing office that meets the Cal/OSHA criteria. That license counts only within the issuing government's jurisdiction and for no more than 5 years. Accredited certifications (Option 1) are portable.

parameters.option: Option 2: licensing by a government entity

rules.applies_to: Construction crane operators and their employers
rules.quote: (A) Meets the operator qualification requirements of this section for operation of equipment only within the jurisdiction of the government entity.
rules.notes: (e)(3)(B): 'Is valid for the period of time stipulated by the licensing department/office, but no longer than 5 years.'

rules.title: Crane operator-in-training: continuous monitoring by a certified trainer with no other duties
rules.plain_english: An uncertified operator may run a crane only as an operator-in-training after formal and practical instruction, continuously monitored on site by a trainer who is the employer's employee or agent, holds a valid certificate for that crane type, stays in the immediate area within sight and communication, and has no other duties while observing. Until certified, a trainee may not operate where any part of the crane, load line or load could get within 20 feet of a power line up to 350 kV (50 feet over 350 kV) at the crane's maximum working radius, hoist personnel, take part in multiple-crane lifts, or work over a shaft, cofferdam or in a tank farm; multiple-lift rigging is allowed only if the trainer decides the trainee's skills are enough.

parameters.communication: direct line of sight plus verbal or hand signals (direct communication for tower cranes)
trainee_prohibited_unless_certified: any part of the equipment, load line or load could get within 20 ft of a power line up to 350 kV, or within 50 ft of a power line over 350 kV
over a shaft, cofferdam, or in a tank farm
multiple-lift rigging operations (unless the trainer determines the trainee's skills are sufficient)

rules.applies_to: Construction employers training crane operators
rules.quote: When performing direct supervision, the supervising operator shall have no other duties other than to observe the operation of the crane by the trainee.
rules.notes: Trainee task restrictions (power line distances, personnel hoisting, multi-crane lifts) are already in rulebook rule crane-operator-certification-5-years. Employer must also retrain when performance shows a need (b)(5). (b)(3)(A)-(E) task restrictions were added to this rule in the 2026-11-25 second-pass review (the rulebook rule crane-operator-certification-5-years that carried part of them is unchecked).
rules.correction: 2026-11-25 second pass: added trainee_prohibited_unless_certified, power_line_clearance_ft and the multiple-lift rigging allowance from 5006.2(b)(3)(A)-(E); citation widened to (b)(2)-(b)(4). Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction (8 CCR 5006.2(b)(3) at https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/5006_2.html re-read on 2026-11-27); no value changed.

rules.title: Mobile and tower cranes outside construction: certified operators too (5006.1)
rules.plain_english: Outside construction (for example yard, shop or plant lifts), mobile and tower crane operators must also hold a certificate of competency from an accredited certifying entity, valid up to 5 years. Exempt: mobile cranes with booms under 25 feet or rated capacity under 15,000 pounds, digger derrick line trucks, and marine terminal work. An operator certified and evaluated under the construction rule (5006.2) is qualified for both construction and general industry.
rules.applies_to: Contractors operating mobile or tower cranes in general industry settings (yards, shops, plants)
rules.quote: (a) Qualifications. The employer shall only permit operators who have a valid certificate of competency (certificate) issued in accordance with this section by an Accredited Certifying Entity for the type of crane to be used to operate a crane covered by this section.
rules.notes: Exceptions to Section 5006.1: '(1) Mobile cranes having a boom length of less than 25 feet or a maximum rated load capacity of less than 15,000 pounds.' 5006.2(h): 'Operators trained, certified under Option 1, evaluated, and certified under this Section 5006.2, are qualified to work on projects in construction and in general industry.'

rules.title: Crane operator certification does not apply to derricks, sideboom cranes, 2,000 lb equipment, small delivery knuckle-booms or digger derricks
rules.plain_english: 8 CCR 5006.2 (operator training, certification and evaluation in construction) does not apply to operators of derricks and sideboom cranes, or of equipment rated to hoist 2,000 pounds or less; the training and qualification rules of 8 CCR 5006 still apply to them. Certification is also not required for articulating/knuckle-boom cranes with a boom under 25 feet or a rated capacity under 15,000 pounds when they deliver material to a construction site, for electric line trucks (digger derricks) regulated by the High Voltage Electrical Safety Orders (but not truck cranes built to ASME B30.5), or for marine terminal operations under Article 14.

parameters.delivery_knuckle_boom_condition: used to deliver material to a construction site
parameters.digger_derrick_exception_excludes: mobile truck cranes designed and built to ASME B30.5

rules.applies_to: Construction employers whose employees operate cranes and derricks (Group 13)
rules.quote: (1) Operators of derricks and sideboom cranes, or equipment with a maximum manufacturer-rated hoisting/lifting capacity of 2,000 pounds or less are not required to comply with this section.
rules.notes: Exception (2): 'Operator qualification or certification under this section is not required for operation of articulating/knuckle-boom cranes having a boom length of less than 25 feet or a maximum rated load capacity of less than 15,000 pounds when used to deliver material to a construction site.' Exception (1) note: 'The training and qualification requirements of Section 5006 will continue to apply in those cases.' Exception (3): electric line trucks (digger derrick trucks) as defined in ESO 2700 and regulated by HVESO 2940.7, not ASME B30.5 truck cranes. Exception (4): marine terminal operations under Article 14. Added in the 2026-11-25 second-pass legal review: the builder's certifications_required said every derrick and knuckle-boom operator needed certification.

rules.title: No elevator may run without a current DOSH permit to operate; post it in the car
rules.plain_english: Every elevator, escalator, lift or dumbwaiter covered by the Elevator Safety Orders needs a valid, current permit to operate from Cal/OSHA's Elevator Unit. For passenger, freight and incline elevators the permit (or a copy) must be posted in the car; for other devices it must be on the premises. Permits last up to 1 year (up to 2 years with a qualifying C-11 maintenance contract). A new building normally cannot open its elevators to use without it.

posting.passenger_freight_incline_elevators: conspicuously and securely in the car

rules.applies_to: Building owners, developers and general contractors delivering buildings with elevators, escalators, lifts or dumbwaiters
rules.citation: 8 CCR 3001(c)(1)-(2); Labor Code 7300 et seq. (not read)
rules.quote: (c) Permit to Operate Required. No elevator shall be operated without a valid, current permit issued by the Division.
rules.notes: Effective date is the operative date of the latest amendment to 8 CCR 3001 (5-1-2008). Elevator Unit FAQ (June 2026): 'The owner/responsible party for any location are responsible for maintaining a current Safety permit for a conveyance.' The certificate-of-occupancy linkage is a practical point from the gap list, not stated in the regulation.

rules.title: Two-year elevator permit: needs a C-11 full maintenance contract with at least monthly service
rules.plain_english: DOSH may issue a 2-year permit if the elevator is safe and covered for the whole term by a full maintenance contract with a C-11 licensed elevator service company. Within 60 days of DOSH's notice, the service company must send its C-11 license and the contract. The contract must cover all repairs and maintenance needed for compliance and require service at least monthly. The company must notify DOSH within 30 days if the contract is ended or changed.
rules.applies_to: C-11 elevator contractors and their mechanics (conveyance companies) and building owners
rules.quote: (6) The elevator service company shall notify the Division within 30 days if a full maintenance service contract is terminated or altered during the period the two-year permit is in effect.
rules.notes: (c)(5)(B): contract must 'Require the elevator service company to service the elevator as frequently as necessary to effect safe operation but not less often than monthly.'

rules.title: New or altered elevators: file plans or notice of intent, then pass DOSH inspection before use
rules.plain_english: Whoever installs a new elevator, escalator, moving walk, dumbwaiter or manlift must submit erection plans to DOSH (or, for a recognized elevator company, a notice of intent to install and a later notice that it is ready for inspection). Each new or altered device must be inspected by DOSH and get a permit to operate before it is put into service, although the inspector may let a safe device run while the permit is processed. The inspection request for new or altered equipment must come from the installing certified company.

submit_before_install: or notice of intent from recognized elevator company
parameters.notify_when: installation complete and ready for inspection

rules.applies_to: C-11 elevator contractors and their mechanics (conveyance companies); general contractors scheduling elevator acceptance
rules.quote: (1) Each new device shall be inspected by an authorized representative of the Division and a permit to operate issued before the device is placed in service.
rules.notes: FAQ: 'If the conveyance is new or altered, the request must be generated by the certified installing company.' All elevator- and building-related life safety items and tests must be complete before DOSH grants an inspection date.

rules.title: Elevators must be reinspected at least once a year (up to 2 years with full maintenance contract)
rules.plain_english: Every elevator must be reinspected at least yearly, or up to every two years if it is safe and under a full maintenance contract. Owners can request the inspection 30 days before the current permit expires. Reinspections may be done by DOSH safety engineers or Certified Competent Conveyance Inspectors.
rules.applies_to: Building owners, developers and general contractors delivering buildings with elevators, escalators, lifts or dumbwaiters
rules.citation: 8 CCR 3001(b)(4); Labor Code 7304 (as cited in the regulation)
rules.quote: (4) Reinspections of the devices covered by these regulations shall be as prescribed in Labor Code section 7304 which requires all elevators to be inspected at least once each year, but permits up to a two-year period if an elevator is in a safe condition for operation and is subject to a full maintenance service contract.
rules.notes: FAQ: 'You can request an inspection 30 days prior to the expiration of the current permit.'

rules.title: Elevator permit renewal: DOSH answers in 15 days, inspects within 30, issues within 15
rules.plain_english: After receiving a renewal application, DOSH has 15 calendar days to say if it is complete, 30 calendar days from filing to inspect, and 15 calendar days after compliance and fee payment to issue the permit. DOSH's historical processing times were 30 days minimum, 60 days median, up to 1 year.
rules.applies_to: Building owners, developers and general contractors delivering buildings with elevators, escalators, lifts or dumbwaiters
rules.quote: (3) After satisfactory compliance with the preliminary order, if one has been issued, and upon notification to the Division's elevator unit that the inspection fee has been paid, the Division shall issue the permit within 15 calendar days.
rules.notes: Schedule the reinspection early: the 1-year maximum time is a realistic risk on a project schedule.

rules.title: Elevator installation permit fees: $225/story (hydraulic), $350/story (traction), escalator $900
rules.plain_english: DOSH's erection/installation permit fee (including plan approval) is $225 per story for the first hydraulic elevator in a building and $350 per story for the first cable, screw or rack-and-pinion elevator, then $225 or $350 per additional similar unit. Escalators and moving walks: $900 for the first, $225 each additional. Dumbwaiters, material lifts, VRCs and sidewalk elevators: $550 each. Wheelchair and stair lifts: $450 each.
rules.applies_to: Building owners, developers and general contractors delivering buildings with elevators, escalators, lifts or dumbwaiters; C-11 elevator contractors and their mechanics (conveyance companies)
rules.quote: (i) The fee for an erection, construction, or installation permit, including the plan approval, is as follows:
rules.notes: Amounts from the table under 344.30(i), current as last amended (Certificate of Compliance filed 4-18-2011; 2017 emergency amendment was reinstated to the prior text).

rules.title: Elevator inspection of new installations and alterations: $225 per hour
rules.plain_english: DOSH charges $225 per hour (or fraction) to inspect a new installation, an alteration or a required component replacement, and for re-inspections when safety orders were not complied with. Field consultations are $450 per hour, with travel time added if the site is more than 50 miles from the district office.
rules.applies_to: Building owners, developers and general contractors delivering buildings with elevators, escalators, lifts or dumbwaiters; C-11 elevator contractors and their mechanics (conveyance companies)
rules.quote: (b) The fee for the inspection of a new installation of any type of conveyance will be $225.00 per hour or any fraction thereof.
rules.notes: Permit processing and mailing fee: actual cost up to $15.00 (344.30(g)).

rules.title: Annual elevator reinspection fees by device type ($120 to $1,800 per unit)
rules.plain_english: Periodic reinspection fees per unit include: hydraulic elevators $225; cable elevators $225 (up to 3 stories), $350 (4-10), $450 (11-20), $550 (21+); escalators and moving walks $675; wheelchair and stairway lifts $125; construction personnel hoists $225; witnessing periodic tests $225. Other listed devices run from $120 (hand dumbwaiters) to $1,800 (automatic guided vehicles), most at $225. A permit processing and mailing fee of actual cost, up to $15, is also charged.
rules.applies_to: Building owners, developers and general contractors delivering buildings with elevators, escalators, lifts or dumbwaiters
rules.quote: (a) Reinspection (periodic inspection) and witnessing of periodic tests of an existing installation shall be:
rules.notes: (f): no more than one charged inspection per permit year except for non-compliance follow-ups, periodic testing or alterations. (a)(4), (6), (16), (19), (20), (23) and (g) added 2026-11-25: '(g) A fee will be charged for processing and mailing a permit. The fee shall reflect the actual cost of processing and mailing up to a maximum of $15.00.'
rules.correction: 2026-11-25 second pass: usd_per_unit lacked 344.30(a)(4) material lifts with automatic transfer devices, (6) hand-powered man platforms, (16) screw type elevator, (19) elevator installed by variance, (20) automatic transfer devices and (23) special purpose personnel elevator (all $225); added them and the (g) permit processing and mailing fee (actual cost, at most $15). Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction (8 CCR 344.30(a), (g) at https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/344_30.html re-read on 2026-11-27); no value changed.

rules.title: Elevator alteration permit fees: $450 (1-2 alterations) or $900 (3+ alterations)
rules.plain_english: An alteration permit (including plan review) costs $450 for one or two alterations to a single unit, or $900 for three or more alterations to a single conveyance, plus $225 per additional similar unit in the same building. Change-order plan review is $225 per hour.
rules.applies_to: C-11 elevator contractors and their mechanics (conveyance companies); owners modernizing elevators
rules.quote: (k) The fee for any change order review of plans shall be $225.00 per hour.
rules.notes: Alteration amounts read from the 344.30(j) table.

rules.title: Unpaid elevator fees after 60 days: 100% penalty; Order Prohibiting Use adds $675
rules.plain_english: Elevator fees not paid within 60 days after notice are doubled (a penalty equal to 100% of the fee). Failure to pay can lead to an Order Prohibiting Use and the elevator being shut down; an inspection that results in an Order Prohibiting Use costs an extra $675.
rules.applies_to: Building owners, developers and general contractors delivering buildings with elevators, escalators, lifts or dumbwaiters
rules.quote: (l) Whenever a person owning or having the custody, management or operation of an elevator fails to pay the fees required under this section within 60 days after notification, he or she shall pay in addition to the fees required by this section, a penalty fee equal to 100 percent of the fee.
rules.notes: FAQ: 'Invoices not paid within 60 days are charged a 100% penalty payment.' and 'Failure to pay either the original fee and/or the penalty can result in an Order Prohibiting Use (OPU) and the State may shut down the conveyance.' Missing Preliminary Order correction deadlines can also lead to shutdown.

rules.title: Only a certified conveyance mechanic working for a certified conveyance company may work on elevators
rules.plain_english: Maintenance, repairs, alterations or replacements on any elevator or other conveyance covered by the Elevator Safety Orders may be done only by a Certified Competent Conveyance Mechanic (CCCM) employed by a Certified Qualified Conveyance Company (CQCC). Other trades (electricians, GC staff) may not work on conveyance equipment.
rules.applies_to: General contractors, C-11 contractors and any trade working near or on conveyances
rules.source: https://www.dir.ca.gov/dosh/elevatorfaq.html ('Who is authorized to perform work on my conveyance?')
rules.quote: In accordance with the California Labor Code, only a Certified Competent Conveyance Mechanic working for a Certified Qualified Conveyance Company is authorized to perform any maintenance, repairs, alterations, or replacements on any conveyance subject to those orders.
rules.notes: Statute (Labor Code 7311.2) not read; DOSH's official FAQ stated the rule. The CCCM application states the certification 'is NOT a license to perform work for which a contractor's license is required'.
rules.correction: Status is unverifiable only because the statute DOSH paraphrases could not be read. Set read_from_primary_text to false to match, as other packs do for rules resting on an agency summary of a statute. No parameter changed.

rules.title: Certified Competent Conveyance Mechanic: 3 years experience plus exam, $210, valid 2 years
rules.plain_english: To be certified as a conveyance (elevator) mechanic you need 3 years of conveyance work experience verified by your current CQCC employer, plus one of: passing the DOSH exam ($100 extra), a NEIEP/CET/CAT certificate, or completion of a registered apprenticeship. You must be employed by a CQCC. The fee is $210 (non-refundable) and the certificate is valid for 2 years. General and limited (device-specific) certifications exist.
rules.applies_to: Elevator/conveyance mechanics and C-11 employers
rules.citation: Labor Code 7311.2, 7311.4 (as cited by DOSH); 8 CCR 344.30(h)(3), (h)(9)
rules.quote: This certification will be valid for 2 years and must be renewed with an application available from the Division.
rules.notes: Form: 'In order to be considered for certification, a person must have at least three (3) years work experience in construction, maintenance, service or repair of conveyances'. Fee confirmed in 8 CCR 344.30(h)(3) ($210.00) and (h)(9) exam $100. Form revised 1/2025; the exam/credential requirement applies to applicants after December 31, 2003.

rules.title: CCCM renewal every 2 years: $140 and 8 hours of continuing education in the prior year
rules.plain_english: Conveyance mechanic certification is renewed every two years for $140. The renewal must include proof of at least 8 hours of approved continuing education taken within the year before renewal, work history for the past two years, and the current CQCC employer's signed verification. Mechanics working on special purpose personnel elevators on cranes that use a rack and pinion system in marine terminals are exempt from the continuing education requirement.

parameters.ce_exempt: mechanics on special purpose personnel elevators on cranes using a rack and pinion system in marine terminals (LC 7311.5(b) per the form)

rules.applies_to: Certified Competent Conveyance Mechanics
rules.citation: 8 CCR 344.30(h)(7); Labor Code 7311.5 (as cited on the DOSH form)
rules.quote: A minimum of 8 hours of instruction from an approved continuing education course provider, covering new and existing provisions of the regulations of the board is required. Continuing education shall occur within one year immediately preceding certificate renewal.
rules.notes: Renewal fee stated on the form as $140.00 per 8 CCR 344.30, matching 344.30(h)(7). Rack-and-pinion marine terminal mechanics are exempt from the CE requirement (LC 7311.5(b) per form).
rules.correction: The biennial renewal, $140 fee, 8 CE hours and attachments are confirmed. The form says CE 'shall occur within one year immediately preceding certificate renewal', not 365 days. Replaced ce_window_days_before_renewal: 365 with ce_window_years_before_renewal: 1, and added the marine-terminal rack-and-pinion CE exemption stated on the form. Rewording 2026-11-27: plain_english reworded to match this correction (DOSH CCCM Renewal form https://www.dir.ca.gov/dosh/elevator/CCCM_Renewal.pdf re-read on 2026-11-27); no value changed.
