rules.title: Certified Qualified Conveyance Company: $700, qualifying person, C-11 license and insurance
rules.plain_english: A company that installs, alters, services or repairs conveyances must be a Certified Qualified Conveyance Company (CQCC). It needs a qualifying individual with 5+ years of journey-level experience (or 2-4 years plus a DOSH exam, $100), a current C-11 license, workers' comp, and general liability insurance of at least $1,000,000 per occurrence for injury/death and $500,000 for property damage. The initial biennial fee is $700; renewal is $140.

required_documents: C-11 license copy
workers' compensation insurance certificate
general liability insurance certificate
8-hour CE certificate for qualifying individual
list of California branch offices

rules.applies_to: C-11 elevator contractors and their mechanics (conveyance companies)
rules.citation: 8 CCR 344.30(h)(1), (h)(7); Labor Code Part 3, Ch. 2 (as cited by DOSH)
rules.quote: Policy or certificate of insurance for general liability coverage of not less than one million dollars ($1,000,000) for injury or death of any one person or persons in any one occurrence, and with coverage of not less than five hundred thousand dollars ($500,000) for property damage in any one occurrence.
rules.notes: Form page 7: 'The application fee for the initial biennial Certification shall be seven hundred dollars ($700.00) per California Code of Regulations, Title 8, Section 344.30.' Sole owners with no employees must qualify as a mechanic but pay only the company fee.

rules.title: Temporary conveyance mechanic (TCCCM): $35, 6 months initially, then monthly
rules.plain_english: When an employer cannot find enough certified mechanics, it may apply for a Temporary Certified Competent Conveyance Mechanic. The candidate needs 1 year of experience as a second-year apprentice, 2 years while enrolled in an approved apprenticeship, or 3 years with proof of competency. The fee is $35; the first certification can be for 6 months, and later ones require a new application and $35 monthly.

qualifying_methods.plus: second year apprentice in approved program
proof of competency determined by DOSH

parameters.precondition: employer personnel needs cannot be met by available CCCM pool

rules.applies_to: C-11 elevator contractors and their mechanics (conveyance companies)
rules.citation: Labor Code 7301.5(c) (as cited by DOSH); 8 CCR 344.30(h)(4)
rules.quote: Initial TCCCM certification may be granted for six months Subsequent certifications require the submittal of a new TCCCM application and $35.00 fee monthly.
rules.notes: DOSH page also notes TCCCM assignments are subject to IUEC Local 8 or Local 18 approval for IUEC members. 344.30(h)(4) and (h)(5) also set $35 per application for TCCCM and Emergency Certified Competent Elevator Mechanic.

rules.title: Elevator mechanic and company certificate holders: report address changes within 30 days
rules.plain_english: CCCMs and CQCCs must report a change of mailing address or other key information to the DOSH Elevator Unit Certification Section within 30 days, using the Address Change Form.

parameters.trigger: change of mailing address or other pertinent information

rules.applies_to: C-11 elevator contractors and their mechanics (conveyance companies)
rules.citation: DOSH CCCM and CQCC application forms (DIR DOSH 002, 003, 003 R)
rules.quote: If you change your mailing address or other pertinent information, please see our website for the Address Change Form and submit that within 30 days of any change.
rules.notes: Requirement appears on the official DOSH forms; the underlying regulation was not located.

rules.title: Elevator Safety Orders do not cover private single-family home elevators or construction elevators
rules.plain_english: The Elevator Safety Orders (and their permits) do not apply to elevators in a single-unit private home not open to the public, or to construction elevators (covered instead by the Construction Safety Orders personnel hoist rules). Elevators in a building with no more than two dwelling units, not open to the public, need only a DOSH inspection when installed or altered, before use.

excluded: single-unit private home elevators not accessible to public
freight platform hoists with travel <= 5 ft

rules.applies_to: Residential builders and contractors installing lifts
rules.quote: (2) Elevators located in a single-unit private home and not accessible to the public.
rules.notes: 3000(d)(11): 'Construction elevators as defined in section 7200 of the Labor Code.' Elevator FAQ: two-unit residential elevators 'shall be inspected by the Division upon completion of installation prior to being placed in service, or after alterations prior to being returned to service.'

rules.title: Construction personnel hoist: DOSH permit to operate before use, posted in the car
rules.plain_english: A new construction personnel hoist must be inspected by DOSH and get a permit to operate before carrying workers (DOSH may let a safe hoist run while the permit is processed). Post the permit in the car. It lasts one year or as long as the hoist stays at the same location, and can be revoked if periodic inspections show it is unsafe. Operating without a valid permit is prohibited.

parameters.permit_term_text: in effect for one year or for the length of time the personnel hoist is at the same location

rules.applies_to: General contractors and hoist subcontractors using personnel hoists on construction sites
rules.quote: No personnel hoist shall be operated without a valid permit except as permitted by Section 1604.29(a).
rules.notes: 1604.29(b) still lists old inspection fees ($25-$40 by number of landings); the current fee schedule in 8 CCR 344.30 lists 'Construction personnel hoist $ 225.00 per unit' for periodic reinspection and $225/hour for new installations. Use 344.30.
rules.correction: 1604.29(c) says the permit 'shall be in effect for one year or for the length of time the personnel hoist is at the same location'. It does not say whichever is shorter, so max_permit_years: 1 overstated the text. Replaced it with the literal term and added the (a) exception (the hoist may run after inspection while the permit is processed if the inspector finds it safe) and the revocation clause. The $225 fees in 344.30(a)(22) and (b) are confirmed. The old 1604.29(b) table ($25/$30/$35/$40 by landings) is still printed and is recorded as a conflict.

rules.title: Personnel hoists: DOSH acceptance inspection, then inspections at least every 3 months
rules.plain_english: A new personnel hoist, one that has had a major alteration, or one moved to a new location must pass a DOSH acceptance inspection and tests before use (tower jumps are not major alterations). After that, a qualified person designated by the employer must inspect and test it at least every 3 months (weekly for bridge construction elevators, and after winds over 35 mph on bridges). Keep a signed certification record of the latest inspection at the jobsite.
rules.applies_to: General contractors and hoist subcontractors using personnel hoists
rules.quote: All existing installations, and all new installations after being placed in service, shall be subjected to periodic inspections and tests at regular intervals of not more than 3 months for construction hoists and not more than one week for bridge construction elevators to determine that the equipment is in safe operating condition and has not been altered.
rules.notes: 1604.26(c): hoists may be operated only by a competent authorized operator in the car or adjacent to the driving machine under stated conditions.

rules.title: Using a building's permanent elevator during construction requires a permit to operate
rules.plain_english: A building's permanent passenger or freight elevator may be used as a construction hoist only if it is set up to meet the personnel hoist rules, and may run on automatic operation on a construction site only after DOSH issues a permit to operate.

parameters.must_meet: CSO Article 14 personnel hoist requirements when used as construction hoist

rules.applies_to: General contractors using permanent elevators before building completion
rules.quote: (b) Permanent passenger or freight elevators may be used on construction sites on automatic operation after a permit to operate has been issued by the Division.

rules.title: Air tanks (compressor receivers) need a DOSH permit to operate; each day without one is a separate misdemeanor
rules.plain_english: No air tank that requires a permit may be operated without a DOSH permit to operate (except while a permit request is pending). Operating one without a permit is a misdemeanor, and each day is a separate offense. Small tanks (1.5 cubic feet or less with safety valve set at 150 psi or less) are exempt.
rules.applies_to: Contractors and equipment owners operating air tanks (compressor receivers) at a place of employment, except tanks of 1.5 cubic feet or less with safety valves set at 150 psi or less and DOT-compliant SCBA tanks of 1 cubic foot or less
rules.quote: Operating an air tank without a permit constitutes a separate offense for each day that it is so operated.
rules.notes: 461(a): 'Except during the time that a request for a permit remains unacted upon or as permitted in Section 461(f), no air tank shall be operated unless a permit to operate has been issued.' DOSH Pressure Vessel page: permits required for 'Air tanks* (over 1.5 Cu. Ft. / 11.2-gallon water capacity)'.
rules.correction: Parameters confirmed. applies_to said 'receivers over 1.5 cubic feet', but the 461(f) exemption needs both 1.5 cubic feet or less and a safety valve set at 150 psi or less. A small tank with a higher valve setting still needs a permit. Rewrote applies_to to match.

rules.title: Air tank permit exemption: 1.5 cubic feet or less with safety valve at 150 psi or less
rules.plain_english: Air tanks with a volume of 1.5 cubic feet (about 11.2 gallons) or less whose safety valves open at no more than 150 psi do not need a permit to operate, but must still meet construction and other rules. SCBA breathing-air tanks of 1 cubic foot or less built and maintained to DOT rules are also exempt.
rules.applies_to: Contractors with portable or stationary air compressors
rules.quote: (f) Air tanks having a volume of 1 1/2 cubic feet or less which have safety valves set to open at not more than 150 psi do not require permits to operate, but shall comply with all other provisions of these Orders, including construction.
rules.notes: The 11.2-gallon equivalent is stated on the DOSH Pressure Vessel page.

rules.title: Air tank permits: portable tanks up to 3 years, others up to 5 years
rules.plain_english: An air tank permit expires no more than 3 years after inspection for portable tanks and 5 years for other tanks, or earlier if the tank or installation is altered or damaged, or (for non-portable tanks) when both ownership and location change. A temporary permit of up to 30 days may be issued to allow repairs.

expires_early_on: change of ownership and location (not for portable tanks)

rules.applies_to: Owners of permitted air tanks
rules.quote: (d) Except as provided in Subsection 461(h), the permit for portable air tanks shall expire not more than three years from the date of inspection and for all other air tanks not more than 5 years from the date of inspection or upon the alteration of, or damage to, the air tank or installation, or upon change of ownership and location, whichever occurs first.
rules.notes: 462(a): internal and external inspections 'at least once every 3 years for portable tanks and once every 5 years for all other tanks by a qualified inspector'. The owner may get an inspection postponed up to 30 days for good cause (462(b)(3)).

rules.title: ASME air tanks up to 25 cubic feet at 150 psi or less: inspected once, indefinite permit
rules.plain_english: An ASME-stamped air tank with a maximum allowable working pressure of 150 psi or less and a volume of 25 cubic feet or less is inspected when placed into service and then gets an indefinite permit. A new inspection and permit are needed if ownership and permanent location change, or the tank is altered in a way that affects safety.

parameters.requires: ASME Code stamp or DOSH-accepted equivalent
reinspection_triggers: change of ownership and permanent location

rules.applies_to: Owners of small and mid-size air receivers
rules.quote: (h) Air tanks subject to a maximum allowable working pressure not exceeding 150 psi., as shown by the required code marking, and having a volume of 25 cubic feet or less shall be inspected when placed into service.

rules.title: Rented air tanks must already have a permit; post permits under glass at the tank
rules.plain_english: No one may rent out an air tank that needs a permit for use at a workplace unless the permit has been issued. The permit must be posted under glass in a conspicuous place on or near the tank, or kept in a weatherproof container on the unit, and shown to inspectors on request.

posting: under glass in conspicuous place on or near tank

rules.applies_to: Equipment rental companies and contractors renting compressors
rules.quote: (g) No person, firm, or company shall rent or offer for rent for use in a place of employment any air tank requiring a permit to operate unless the required permit has been issued by or in behalf of the Division.
rules.notes: 461(c): 'The permit shall be posted under glass in a conspicuous place on or near the air tank or in a weatherproof container secured to the unit, and shall be available at all times to any qualified inspector.'

rules.title: LP-Gas (propane) tanks over 125 gallons need a DOSH permit to operate
rules.plain_english: An LP-Gas tank larger than 125 gallons used for storage or transport at a workplace (for example jobsite propane for heaters or kettles) needs a DOSH permit to operate. DOT cylinders are exempt. Permits for dispensing units, trap tanks and skid tanks last up to 3 years; transportation, mobile fuel and storage tanks up to 5 years. No one may fill a tank that needs a permit unless the permit is issued and posted.

expires_on: change of both ownership and location

rules.applies_to: Contractors and suppliers using LP-Gas tanks over 125 gallons at a place of employment
rules.quote: Exception: No permit to operate shall be required for pressure vessels of 125 gallons capacity or less or for cylinders used, inspected, and maintained in accordance with DOT regulations.
rules.notes: 470(e): 'No person shall charge LP-Gas into any tank requiring a permit to operate unless the permit to operate has been issued and posted, except where a request for a permit remains unacted upon.'

rules.title: Power boilers: annual inspection and a posted permit to operate before use
rules.plain_english: Boilers subject to the Boiler Safety Orders (DOSH lists power boilers above 15 psig steam pressure) must be inspected internally and externally every year and may not be operated until a permit to operate is issued and posted under glass on or near the boiler. The permit expires when the boiler changes both ownership and location. Temporary permits up to 30 days may be issued for repairs.

parameters.permit_expires_on: change of both ownership and location

rules.applies_to: Contractors installing, commissioning or operating steam boilers (e.g. C-4 boiler contractors, owners)
rules.quote: (a) Except during the time that a request for a permit remains unacted upon, no boiler subject to annual inspection by these orders shall be placed in operation until a permit to operate has been issued and posted on or near the boiler.
rules.notes: DOSH page lists 'Power boilers operating at steam pressures exceeding 15 psig*' with the caveat that 'Permit exemptions depend on vessel capacity and operating pressures.' Turboelectric and special-program boilers have longer intervals under 770(b).

rules.title: Small, low-pressure and miniature boilers: no annual inspection or permit
rules.plain_english: Low-pressure boilers, miniature boilers, high-temperature water boilers, and boilers that stay within all of these limits do not need annual inspection or a permit: 100 sq ft of heating surface, 16-inch steam drum, 100 psi working pressure, 35 gallons water, and 400,000 BTU/hr burner input. They must still meet construction, installation and control rules.

still_required: automatic controls per 763(d) for automatically fired boilers

definitions_8_ccr_753.low_pressure_steam_applies_to: steam pressure and steam safety valve setting

rules.applies_to: Mechanical and boiler contractors installing small boilers
rules.quote: (a) The following boilers are not subject to annual inspection and do not require a permit to operate providing they comply with all of the provisions of subsection (b):
rules.notes: Limits from 771(a)(4)(A)-(E). DOSH may still require inspection (771(c)). Section last amended 1966. 8 CCR 753: 'Low--pressure Boiler: A boiler which does not: Operate at steam pressure or with steam safety valve settings exceeding 15 psi (low--pressure steam boiler), or Operate at water pressure exceeding 160 psi or water temperatures exceeding 250° F (hot water heating boiler).' 'Power Boiler: Steam boiler operated at pressure exceeding 15 psi.' 'High Temperature Water Boiler: A fired or unfired pressure vessel used to heat water to temperatures above 212° F. At pressure exceeding 160 psi or to temperatures exceeding 250° F regardless of pressure.' Miniature: 16 in shell ID, 5 cu ft gross volume, 20 sq ft water heating surface, 100 psi MAWP.
rules.correction: 2026-11-25 second pass: added definitions_8_ccr_753 so the exemption can be applied from pressure and temperature (the builder guessed 'likely low-pressure' from steam pressure alone and ignored the safety valve setting).

rules.title: Pressure vessel permit fee $45 and DOSH inspections $150/hour (increase to $55 and $180 proposed Oct 2026)
rules.plain_english: DOSH charges $45 to process each permit to operate for an air tank, LPG tank or boiler, and $150 per hour (including travel, billed in quarter hours) for DOSH field, resale and alteration permit inspections. Fees unpaid after 60 days double. In October 2026 DOSH proposed emergency increases to $55 per permit and $180 per hour, effective on filing with the Secretary of State; whether they have been filed was not confirmed.

proposed_2026.effective: upon filing with Secretary of State (filing not confirmed)

rules.applies_to: Owners and users of permitted air tanks, LPG tanks and boilers
rules.quote: (b) A fee of $45.00 shall be charged to cover the cost of processing each permit to operate.
rules.notes: Notice of Proposed Emergency Action (October 15, 2026): 'Under section 344.2, the Division proposes to increase the fees related to the issuance of a Permit to Operate from $45.00 to $55.00.' Recheck https://www.dir.ca.gov/title8/344_2.html for the filed version. Permit inspections may also be done by a qualified insurance-company inspector.

rules.title: Fix pressure vessel orders within 15 days of the compliance date to avoid follow-up fees
rules.plain_english: If you correct the items on a DOSH preliminary order and notify DOSH within 15 days of the compliance date, there is no charge for the follow-up inspection. Otherwise the follow-up inspection is billed hourly ($150/hour now).
rules.applies_to: Owners and users of permitted air tanks, LPG tanks and boilers
rules.quote: (c) No additional fees shall be assessed for follow-up inspections when safety order requirements have been complied with, and the division is notified of such compliance, within 15 days of the compliance date shown on the preliminary order.

rules.title: Inside the City of Los Angeles, pressure vessel permits come from LADBS
rules.plain_english: For air tanks, LPG tanks and boilers located within the City of Los Angeles, permits to operate are obtained from the LA Department of Building and Safety (Pressure Vessel Code desk), not the state.

parameters.issuer: Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety

rules.applies_to: Contractors with compressors, LPG tanks or boilers at sites in the City of Los Angeles
rules.quote: To obtain permits to operate for items within the City of Los Angeles, please visit https://dbs.lacity.gov/ then click on "Obtain Permit", or contact the City of Los Angeles, Department of Building & Safety, Pressure Vessel Code and Information Desk at phone number (213) 202-9852.
rules.notes: LADBS fees and rules were not researched.

rules.title: Blasting requires a DOSH-licensed blaster physically on site
rules.plain_english: An employer may not allow any blasting unless a blaster holding a current California Blaster's License from Cal/OSHA is physically on site doing or directing the blasting. The blaster must show the license to Cal/OSHA or the local authority on request. Others may work under the blaster's direct supervision to gain experience.
rules.applies_to: Contractors doing blasting, demolition with explosives, quarry or tunnel work
rules.quote: An employer shall not permit a blasting operation, unless a blaster having a current, valid California "Blaster's License" issued by the Division is physically present on the site to accomplish the blasting operation and/or direct and supervise others in such operation.
rules.notes: Local explosives permits (fire authority, H&SC 12000 et seq.) were not researched.

rules.title: Blaster's License: age 21, 3 years experience, exam; classes A-E
rules.plain_english: To get a Blaster's License you must be at least 21, have 3 years of experience in the blasting category you apply for, be physically able, understand and give written and oral orders, and pass DOSH's written or oral exam (field tests may be required). Classes: A Unlimited, B General Above Ground, C General Underground, D Demolition, E Limited.

parameters.exam: written or oral; field tests possible

rules.applies_to: Blasters and contractors employing them
rules.quote: (1) Shall be at least 21 years of age;
rules.notes: 5238(f)(2): 'Shall have at least three years experience in the blasting category being applied for'. Application fee not found in 344.20-344.22.

rules.title: Blaster's License valid 5 years; exam required at each renewal
rules.plain_english: A Blaster's License is good for five years. Renewal is handled like a new application, and the exam must be taken again every five years. A suspended or revoked blaster must wait 6 months before applying for a new license.
rules.applies_to: Licensed blasters
rules.quote: (a) Each Blaster's License issued under this Article shall be valid for a period of five years with renewal privileges.
rules.notes: 344.22(c): 'In the event of suspension or revocation of a blaster's license, the person may not apply for a new license for a period of 6 months'. Grounds: doubt about competency or noncompliance with safety orders (344.22(a)), after notice and hearing.
